Pre-existing bug discovered in 08zd Phase 1. Needs a permanent fix: either fix the readline/FIFO cleanup in the test, or if the test is fundamentally broken, remove it. NOT a prompt workaround — the test itself must be fixed.
close_reason: Fixed: FIFO fd now closed synchronously in finally block. autoClose:false + explicit closeSync. No more batch test hangs.

title: feat: worktree-per-executor isolation — each edit-permission agent runs in its own git worktree
description: Executors touching src/ files must run in isolated git worktrees (branches) to prevent concurrent file corruption and partial-state contamination. Orchestrator manages merge sequence in dependency order. Reviewers/test-runners must cd into the same worktree as the executor they are checking. Parallel executors only allowed if file sets are provably disjoint. This was identified as critical after 08zd Phase 1 had two executors crash/retry on the same files without isolation, producing an unverifiable composite state.
design:
## Refined Design (Overthinker 3 rounds — 2026-04-04)

### Core Model: Two Workspace Primitives

| Flag | Semantics | Creates worktree? |
|------|-----------|-------------------|
| `--worktree` | Provision new isolated workspace | Yes |
| `--job <id>` | Reuse target job's workspace | No |

These are **mutually exclusive**.

### Isolation Policy
- MEDIUM/HIGH specialists **default to worktree isolation**
- Escape hatch: `--shared-checkout` (explicit, auditable, not `--no-worktree`)
- Worktree created via `bd worktree create` — hard dependency, no silent git fallback

### --job Semantics
- Inherits **cwd only**, not bead context — caller's `--bead` stays authoritative
- Injects target job metadata as variables (target_job_id, target_specialist, target_bead_id, target_worktree_path)
- Concurrency guard: READ_ONLY allowed while target is running; MEDIUM/HIGH rejected
- Missing worktree: hard fail with actionable error

### Central Job Registry
- All jobs live in **main/common-root `.specialists/jobs/`** (resolved via `git --git-common-dir`)
- `worktree_path` + `branch` persisted in status.json
- Execution cwd is the worktree; metadata stays central

### Pi Bootstrap (MVP-blocking)
- Symlink `.pi` → main repo `.pi`
- Symlink `.pi/npm` → main repo `.pi/npm`
- Minimal preflight for extension correctness

### Cleanup
- Minimal GC command (not full worktree list/remove CLI)
- On terminal job completion, mark worktree ownership in status
- Future: clean orphaned worktrees whose owning jobs are terminal

### MVP Scope (ordered)
1. Central job-root resolution via git common-dir
2. `run --worktree` with hard `bd worktree create`
3. Minimal Pi bootstrap (.pi + .pi/npm symlinks)
4. Persist `worktree_path` + `branch` in central status.json
5. `resume`/`steer`/`status` use central metadata
6. `run --job <id>` workspace reuse
7. Minimal cleanup/GC

### NOT in MVP
- Full `specialists worktree create/remove/list` CLI
- xt attach/session metadata parity
- SQLite worktree_column (ships after fqxo)
- Search-based worktree recovery
- `--shared-checkout` escape hatch (add after MVP proves stable)
notes: UPDATE 2026-04-04: Pi extensions going global (~/.pi/). Pi bootstrap step removed from hgpu.2 — no longer MVP-blocking. worktree-bootstrap.ts dropped from scope.
close_reason: Worktree isolation MVP merged to master. 5 impl beads complete, reviewer PASS 82/100, docs committed (worktrees.md, cli-reference, ARCHITECTURE, features, SKILL.md v4.0). Remaining: test regeneration (post-FIFO fix), resolveCommonRoot dedup.

title: Review feed follow-mode fix for correctness (potential regression)
description: The feed -f follow-mode fix landed this session (unitAI-3j2b) with 21/21 unit tests passing, but the fix was complex enough to warrant a second pass. Key changes to review: (1) trackedJobs set built from non-terminal jobs at follow-start — verify the exit condition (completedJobs.size === trackedJobs.size) correctly handles jobs that start AFTER follow begins; (2) makeJobMetaReader with useCache:false — verify fresh reads via openSync/closeSync actually bypass OS fd cache on Linux; (3) the early-exit path when trackedJobs.size === 0 — should this exit immediately or wait for new jobs to appear? (4) race condition: files written synchronously before first poll fires — confirmed in tests but verify in real tmux-backed runs where timing differs. Run: specialists feed -f on a live background job and verify it tails correctly to completion.
notes:
The investigation is complete. Here's the TL;DR of what I found:

**Two real bugs, two non-issues:**

| | Finding | Action |
|---|---------|--------|
| 🐛 | Silent exit when all jobs complete during the seed pass (before first 500ms poll fires) | Add `stderr.write('All jobs complete.\n')` to the second early-exit guard — 1 line fix |
| 🐛 | "All jobs complete." printed when jobs directory is empty (no jobs ever ran) | Check `listMatchingJobIds().length > 0` to distinguish "no jobs" vs "all done" |
| ✅ | `readFileFresh` / `useCache:false` — doesn't bypass OS page cache | Not needed — page cache is always coherent with writes on Linux. **Rename to `useAppCache` for clarity** |
| ✅ | Race condition (events written before first poll) | Correctly handled — `lastSeenT` is seeded from the initial snapshot, so poll only picks up events with `t > lastT` |

The short-lived new-job gap (start+complete within 500ms) is a known design trade-off: events still stream, it just doesn't affect the exit condition.

title: Design: centralized specialists manifest for permission policies and global defaults
description:
PROBLEM: Specialists runtime has hardcoded tier→tool mappings in
`src/pi/session.ts::mapPermissionToTools` (constants at lines 156-219, mapping
at lines 225-243). The hotfix `unitAI-2s7y8` exposed Serena/GitNexus tool
names per tier but did not solve the deeper problem: native tools (grep,
find, ls, read, edit, write, bash) and extension tools coexist with no
preference signal, so explorer still picks `grep` over `gitnexus_query`
(observed in smoke `unitAI-zuun0`). Specialists cannot override tier policy
without forking YAML or hacking `excludeExtensions`. There is no debug
surface to inspect what a specialist actually receives at runtime.

SUCCESS: A documented, evidence-based design that:
1. Defines a tool catalog schema (native + extension) with capability tags
   (read / search.text / search.symbol / analyze.graph / shell / write.* /
   mutate.* / admin / memory / meta).
2. Defines tier policy as capability sets + deny rules (including
   "denied_natives_when_extension"), not concrete tool lists.
3. Extends the existing manifest overlay schema (in current bead description)
   with capabilities, denied natives, denied-mode, fallback semantics.
4. Specifies `sp config show <specialist> --resolved` output exhaustively:
   effective manifest, tier policy file, extension availability, final
   `--tools` string, native tools denied with reason, per-layer attribution.
5. Defines fallback behavior when an extension is loaded but unhealthy
   (gitnexus index missing/stale; serena LSP offline; package not installed).
6. Provides a migration plan from current hardcoded arrays to manifest-driven
   resolution without behavior change on first land.

SCOPE: This bead is the DESIGN phase only. Implementation is a follow-up
bead. Output lives in `docs/design/gzrx-tool-catalog.md` (skeleton already
exists with FILL markers). The in-pi agent populates evidence sections
(§1.1-§1.6, §3.3, §7) and refines proposed sections (§2, §3.1, §3.2, §4-§6,
§8). Bead description gets a final summary block pointing at the doc.

Files for evidence (read-only, source archaeology):
- src/pi/session.ts — `mapPermissionToTools` (lines 225-243), tool constants
  (lines 156-219), extension wiring (lines 657-672 — gitnexusPackageName,
  serenaPackageName, excludedExtensions).
- src/specialist/runner.ts:880-905 — where `excludeExtensions` is computed
  from `execution.extensions.{serena,gitnexus} === false` and
  `permissionLevel` is resolved.
- src/specialist/schema.ts — current YAML schema (will need ManifestSchema
  alongside).
- src/cli/config.ts — `sp config get/set` (need `show --resolved` adjacent).
- config/mandatory-rules/ — context for how rules constrain specialists today.
- .specialists/default/*.specialist.json — current specialist YAMLs to see
  which tier each uses and whether any need overrides.
- docs/observability-metrics.md, docs/cli-reference.md — doc pattern to
  match for docs/manifest.md.

Files for behavioral evidence (in-pi runtime introspection — the whole
point of running this in pi directly):
- The agent's own toolbox at READ_ONLY / LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH tiers (set via
  pi --tools or by launching from a specialist YAML). Enumerate, categorize.
- Tool-call behavior: does explorer prefer gitnexus_query over grep when
  both are available? Does Serena's hook block native tools? Are denied
  tools visible to the agent or silently dropped?
- Extension health probes: what happens when `.gitnexus/` is absent? When
  Serena LSP isn't running? When package is missing from npm global?

NON_GOALS:
- No code changes. Design only.
- No change to specialist YAML schema for model/prompt/output_schema.
- No new CLI commands beyond `sp config show --resolved` (spec only, not
  implementation).
- No reshuffling of mandatory-rules system.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Layer on top of YAML, don't replace it. Per-YAML wins (highest precedence).
- Backward compat: with no manifest file, runtime behavior must match today's
  hardcoded mapping byte-for-byte.
- Catalog files are hand-editable JSON — no codegen.
- Do not break the existing overthinker design (manifest overlay schema in
  the current bead description). Extend it.

VALIDATION:
1. `docs/design/gzrx-tool-catalog.md` has every FILL marker resolved with
   either evidence or a stated open question.
2. The doc cross-references concrete file:line for each "current state"
   claim.
3. Migration plan in §7 is concrete enough that a follow-up implementation
   bead can be filed with file-level scope.
4. Bead description final block summarises the design and points at the doc.

OUTPUT: Updated `docs/design/gzrx-tool-catalog.md`. Bead-description summary
block (3-5 sentences) added via `bd update unitAI-gzrx --notes` referencing
the doc. Optional: filed follow-up implementation bead `unitAI-gzrx.impl`
with file-level scope.

EXECUTION CONTEXT: This bead is being driven by an interactive pi coding-
agent session launched outside the orchestrator's control. The agent has
firsthand visibility into its own toolbox (the whole reason for this
approach over a self-report-via-bead-instruction explorer). Proceed slowly:
gather evidence first, then design on top of it. The existing manifest
overlay schema in the prior overthinker pass is the transport — fill in
the catalog/capability/tier-policy content.
notes: DESIGN COMPLETE (2026-05-03). docs/design/gzrx-tool-catalog.md is final draft: tool catalog schema (§4) classifies tools by capability tags rather than package; tier policy (§3.1) is capability sets + denied-natives rules with soft/hard modes (§3.2); extension health states (§3.3) distinguish not_installed/disabled/loaded_healthy/loaded_unhealthy with explicit fallback semantics. Manifest overlay schema (§5) extends the prior overthinker pass with capabilities, denied_natives_when_extension, denied_natives_mode, and fallback_on_extension_failure. §6 specifies sp config show --resolved output with per-layer attribution. §7 lays out a 10-step migration that preserves byte-equivalent default behavior via snapshot tests before enabling soft/hard denies. §1.2.1 source-tier cross-reference flags ⚠ where capability grouping differs from current source policy and forces memory→{read,write} and admin.serena→{read,write} splits. Ready for implementation bead with file-level scope (src/specialist/manifest.ts, src/pi/session.ts threading, sp config show --resolved, .specialists/catalog/*.json).
close_reason: Design complete. docs/design/gzrx-tool-catalog.md final; summary block added to bead notes; impl follow-up filed as unitAI-8vb65.

title: Test: Phase 0 core — event mapping fidelity (tool args, isError, run_complete, tool_call_id)
description:
Layer: core
Strategy: unit + example-based (pure event mapping, no I/O)
Covers: z0mq.1 (P0 event fidelity), z0mq.10 (tool_call_id + dedup)

## What to test

The event mapping pipeline from raw pi callback events to TimelineEvent objects. These are pure transform functions — no I/O, no mocking needed.

### Assertions required

**z0mq.1 — tool args + isError + run_complete output:**
- [ ] mapCallbackEventToTimelineEvent: tool_execution_start with args produces TimelineEventTool with args field populated
- [ ] mapCallbackEventToTimelineEvent: tool_execution_start without args produces TimelineEventTool with args undefined (no crash)
- [ ] mapCallbackEventToTimelineEvent: tool_execution_end with isError=true produces TimelineEventTool with is_error=true
- [ ] mapCallbackEventToTimelineEvent: tool_execution_end with isError=false produces is_error=false
- [ ] createRunCompleteEvent: when output string provided, event.output contains the full text
- [ ] createRunCompleteEvent: when output is undefined/empty, event.output is undefined (no empty string)
- [ ] onToolStart callback receives (tool, args) — verify supervisor wiring passes args through
- [ ] onToolEnd callback receives (tool, isError) — verify supervisor wiring passes isError through

**z0mq.10 — tool_call_id + dedup:**
- [ ] tool_execution_start with toolCallId produces TimelineEventTool with tool_call_id populated
- [ ] tool_execution_start without toolCallId produces tool_call_id as undefined (graceful)
- [ ] Only one tool:start event emitted per tool call (no duplicate from toolcall + tool_execution_start)
- [ ] getToolActivity correctly pairs start/end by tool_call_id when available
- [ ] getToolActivity falls back to tool name when tool_call_id missing (backward compat)

### Edge cases
- [ ] Empty args object {} on tool_execution_start (valid but empty)
- [ ] Very large args payload (>10KB) — no truncation at this layer
- [ ] Two sequential tool calls with same tool name but different tool_call_ids — correctly distinguished
- [ ] tool_execution_end arriving without a preceding start — no crash, event still recorded

### Fixture policy
- [ ] No shared mutable state between tests
- [ ] Each test constructs its own callback event input independently
- [ ] Use real TimelineEvent type assertions (not just "truthy")

### Test file structure
- `tests/unit/specialist/timeline-events.test.ts` — extend existing or create
- `tests/unit/specialist/timeline-query.test.ts` — getToolActivity pairing tests

### Critical paths covered
- Tool args visible in timeline events — risk: agents cannot observe what specialists do
- isError distinguishes failed from successful tools — risk: misleading feed output
- run_complete self-contained with output — risk: consumers need extra file read
- tool_call_id correlation for multi-tool runs — risk: ambiguous start/end pairing

### Known deferred paths
- Feed rendering of args (human format) → tested in shell layer test issue
- Supervisor integration wiring of new callback fields → tested in boundary layer test issue

Gates: z0mq.2 (Phase 1), z0mq.4 (Phase 3a), z0mq.7 (Phase 5a)
Do not start Phase 1 implementation until these core mapping tests pass.

Done when: all assertions pass, event mapping is fully covered for the 3 new fields + dedup fix.
close_reason: Added 2 missing edge-case tests: empty args {} in mapCallbackEventToTimelineEvent and tool:end without matching start in getToolActivity. All 54 tests pass.

title: P0: Forward tool args and isError through session.ts event pipeline
description:
## Context

Three P0 event fidelity gaps identified in jcvu.3 block all downstream consumers (feed, poll, MCP tools) from seeing meaningful tool activity. This is the highest priority fix — without it, "tool visibility" in the output pipeline is tool-name-only, not tool-action visibility.

## What to build

Fix the session.ts → supervisor.ts → timeline event pipeline to preserve critical tool event fields:

1. **tool_use.input on tool_execution_start**: In `PiAgentSession._handleEvent`, when `type === 'tool_execution_start'`, forward `event.args` (the tool_use.input payload) to the `onToolStart` callback. Extend `onToolStart` signature from `(tool: string) => void` to `(tool: string, args?: Record<string, unknown>) => void`.

2. **isError on tool_execution_end**: In `_handleEvent` when `type === 'tool_execution_end'`, forward `event.isError` to `onToolEnd`. Extend `onToolEnd` from `(tool: string) => void` to `(tool: string, isError: boolean) => void`.

3. **output on run_complete**: In `supervisor.ts`, at the point where `result.output` is available (~line 356), pass output into `createRunCompleteEvent`. Add `output?: string` field to `TimelineEventRunComplete` interface in `timeline-events.ts`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `events.jsonl` tool:start events include `args` field with tool input data
- [ ] `events.jsonl` tool:end events include `is_error` boolean
- [ ] `events.jsonl` run_complete events include `output` text (final assistant output)
- [ ] feed.ts renders tool args in human-readable format
- [ ] Existing tests pass; new unit tests cover the 3 field additions
- [ ] No breaking changes to existing callback signatures (args/isError are additive params)

## Approach notes

- `src/pi/session.ts:_handleEvent` — tool_execution_start and tool_execution_end branches
- `src/specialist/supervisor.ts` — onToolStart/onToolEnd callback wiring, createRunCompleteEvent call (~line 370)
- `src/specialist/timeline-events.ts` — `TimelineEventTool` interface (add `args`, `is_error`), `TimelineEventRunComplete` (add `output`), `mapCallbackEventToTimelineEvent` function
- `src/cli/feed.ts:getHumanEventKey` and `formatEventLine` — render args in human mode
- Reference: jcvu.3 priority ranking, jcvu.8 target contracts section
close_reason: Implemented: forwarded tool.args via onToolStart at tool_execution_start, isError via onToolEnd, output in run_complete. Extended session.ts signatures, wired through runner.ts and supervisor.ts, added args rendering in format-helpers.ts. 5 new unit tests added. 324/324 tests pass.

title: Fix current test and TypeScript regressions blocking ship readiness
description: Current codebase health check on 2026-03-27 shows bun --bun vitest run failing (33 tests across feed CLI, edit CLI, command-help, runner script execution, permission mapping, run CLI, and use_specialist tool) and tsc --noEmit failing in src/specialist/schema.ts with duplicate type exports and invalid Zod issue handling. This is a direct ship-stability blocker and should take precedence over non-essential feature work.
close_reason: Fixed TS schema errors and aligned CLI/runtime tests; vitest + tsc now passing

title: Schema validation not wired: should run on specialist creation and on run
description: src/specialist/schema.ts contains the canonical schema for .specialist.yaml but it is only used internally. Two gaps: (1) No schema validation fires when a new specialist is created (via CLI or manually). A user can write an invalid YAML and only find out at runtime. (2) No schema validation fires when 'specialists run' loads a specialist — malformed fields (wrong model format, invalid permission_required, etc.) are silently ignored or cause cryptic runtime errors. Fix: expose schema validation as a standalone command ('specialists validate <name>') and wire it into both the creation flow and the run command's loading step.
close_reason: Done: Added validateSpecialist() with friendly error messages, specialists validate CLI command, and wired validation into run command

title: installer bundles stale skill: specialists-usage-workspace should be removed
description: The npm package config/skills/ contains: specialists-creator, specialists-usage-workspace, using-specialists. It should contain only: specialists-creator, using-specialists. Fix: remove specialists-usage-workspace from config/skills/ — it is stale and superseded.
notes: On closer inspection: 'using-specialists' in the package appears to be the renamed/published version of 'specialists-usage' in the project (same description). So these may not be missing — they may be intentional renames. Needs verification: is specialist-author intentionally excluded (project-internal only), and is specialists-usage superseded by using-specialists? If so, this issue may be invalid.
close_reason: Fixed: removed stale specialists-usage-workspace skill; fixed installation paths: skills to ~/.pi/skills/, hooks to .claude/hooks/ with correct settings.json wiring

title: quickstart references removed flags and deprecated install command
description: 'specialists quickstart' (Section 1 and Section 4) contains outdated content: (1) lists 'specialists install' as the setup command instead of 'specialists init', (2) shows '--background' and '--follow' flags on 'specialists run' which were removed, (3) the fire-and-forget workflow in Section 10 uses '--background'. Any user following the quickstart guide will hit broken commands immediately.
close_reason: Fixed: quickstart now uses 'specialists init' and removed deprecated --background/--follow flags

title: run prints specialist header before validating specialist name
description: When running 'specialists run nonexistent --prompt "..."', the CLI prints 'Running nonexistent' before checking if the specialist exists, then errors with 'Specialist not found: nonexistent'. Validation should happen before any output is printed.
close_reason: Added validation to check specialist exists before printing the 'Running' header. Now 'specialists run nonexistent' will fail immediately without printing the header.

title: --scope default rejected by edit command but used internally
description: The loader uses 'default' as a valid scope name (shown as [default] in 'specialists list' output), but 'specialists edit --scope default' returns: 'Error: --scope must be "project" or "user", got: "default"'. The CLI only accepts 'project' or 'user' scopes for edit, creating an inconsistency: the user can see default-scoped specialists but cannot edit them by scope name.
close_reason: Changed --scope validation from 'project' to 'default' to match the loader's scope names. Fixed in edit.ts, index.ts help text, and type definitions.

title: edit --dry-run diff is full of YAML reformatting noise
description: When running 'specialists edit <name> --model <value> --dry-run', the diff output shows the entire file reformatted (bracket spacing, line reflows, indentation) alongside the actual field change. The real change is buried and hard to spot. The edit command should produce a minimal diff showing only the changed field, not reformat the whole YAML.
close_reason: In progress: fixing edit --dry-run diff noise

title: specialists feed with no args replays all jobs instead of showing usage
description: Running 'specialists feed' with no arguments silently enters global replay mode and dumps all job history. It should either show usage (like 'specialists poll' does) or require an explicit -f flag for global mode. Current behavior is surprising and can flood output unexpectedly.
close_reason: Added validation to require either job-id or -f flag. Running 'specialists feed' with no arguments now shows usage instead of dumping all job history.

title: specialists version exits with code 1
description: Running 'specialists version' prints the version string correctly but exits with code 1 instead of 0. Any script or CI check using 'specialists version' as a health check will incorrectly report failure.
close_reason: Fixed: deprecated commands now show warning and redirect to init; version exits with code 0

title: Deprecated setup/install commands still write files with outdated content
description: specialists setup and specialists install are marked deprecated but still execute fully, mutating CLAUDE.md and other project files without any deprecation warning before running. Worse, the content they inject is outdated: references --background and --follow flags (removed), old MCP tool names, and lists specialists install as the setup command instead of specialists init. A deprecated command that silently writes stale content to user files is dangerous.
close_reason: Fixed: deprecated commands now show warning and redirect to init; version exits with code 0

title: sp alias not installed
description: The sp shortcut is advertised throughout help, quickstart, status, and all documentation as a valid alias for specialists, but the symlink does not exist in PATH. Every mention of 'sp run', 'sp list', etc. is currently broken for users who follow the docs.
close_reason: Added sp alias check to specialists doctor. The sp alias is defined in package.json bin field; users who installed before this entry was added need to reinstall: npm install -g @jaggerxtrm/specialists@latest

title: Run command should create job files for poll command
description: After removing --background, the Supervisor integration was lost entirely. Foreground runs don't create .specialists/jobs/ files, making poll command useless. Supervisor should be used for ALL runs to create job files.
close_reason: Fixed: run command now uses Supervisor for all runs, creating job files. poll command works correctly. Fixed hanging by: (1) skipping FIFO creation for foreground runs, (2) proper session close with process exit wait, (3) process.exit(0) at end of run.

title: npm package missing config/ directory - specialists init fails to copy assets
description: The package.json files array references non-existent directories (specialists/, hooks/) at root level, but the actual content lives in config/ which is not included. This causes specialists init to fail copying hooks, skills, and specialists when installed from npm.
close_reason: Fixed: Added config/ to package.json files array. The npm package now includes all hooks, skills, and specialists from config/ directory.

title: Fix session.ts _handleEvent nested RPC protocol parsing
description:
## Context

\`PiAgentSession._handleEvent\` in \`src/pi/session.ts\` misreads the Pi RPC event hierarchy.
Three categories of event are looked up at the wrong level — they never fire.
This is the core fix that unblocks consumers (unitAI-4rn.2) and tests (unitAI-4rn.3).

## What to build

Edit \`src/pi/session.ts\` \`_handleEvent\` (lines 181–259):

### Remove broken top-level handlers

Delete the \`thinking_start/delta/end\` block (lines 220–227) — these are not top-level events.
Delete the \`toolcall_start/end\` block (lines 229–235) — same.

### Expand message_update nested dispatch

Replace the current 2-branch \`message_update\` handler with a full switch on \`ae.type\`:

\`\`\`
case 'thinking_start' → onEvent('thinking')
case 'thinking_delta' → onThinking(ae.delta) + onEvent('thinking')
case 'thinking_end'  → (no-op)
case 'toolcall_start' → onToolStart(ae.name ?? ae.toolName ?? 'tool') + onEvent('toolcall')
case 'toolcall_delta' → (no-op)
case 'toolcall_end'   → onEvent('toolcall')
case 'done'           → onEvent('message_done')  [message-level, not run-level]
case 'text_delta'     → onToken(ae.delta) + onEvent('text')  [existing, keep]
\`\`\`

### Fix agent_end callback name

Change \`onEvent?.('done')\` in the \`agent_end\` handler to \`onEvent?.('agent_end')\`.

### Remove duplicate onToolStart from tool_execution_start

\`onToolStart\` now fires from nested \`toolcall_start\` (when LLM emits the call).
Remove the \`onToolStart\` call from the \`tool_execution_start\` top-level handler.
Keep \`onToolEnd\` in \`tool_execution_end\` (execution completion is still the right trigger).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] \`thinking_delta\` inside \`message_update.assistantMessageEvent\` calls \`onThinking\`
- [ ] \`toolcall_start\` inside \`message_update.assistantMessageEvent\` calls \`onEvent('toolcall')\` and \`onToolStart\`
- [ ] Top-level \`thinking_delta\` / \`toolcall_start\` events do NOT trigger any callback
- [ ] \`agent_end\` fires \`onEvent('agent_end')\`, not \`onEvent('done')\`
- [ ] \`assistantMessageEvent.done\` fires \`onEvent('message_done')\`
- [ ] TypeScript compiles clean, existing tests pass

## Approach notes

Relevant file: \`src/pi/session.ts:181\`
Docs reference: \`docs/pi-rpc.md\` section "message_update (Streaming)" — table of \`assistantMessageEvent\` types
Tool name for \`toolcall_start\`: \`ae.name ?? ae.toolName ?? 'tool'\` (toolcall_end has \`ae.toolCall?.name\`)
close_reason: Implemented in worktree-fix-4rn-rpc-nesting (8751862). All 3 tasks: session.ts protocol fix, timeline-events.ts consumer update, 7 regression tests. 20/20 tests pass.

title: PiAgentSession: align RPC event parsing with documented nested toolcall/message_update semantics
description:
## Context

Exploration for unitAI-4pq found a protocol-level mismatch between specialists and Pi RPC reality.

Confirmed by both live \`pi --mode rpc\` traces and \`docs/pi-rpc.md\`.

## Pi RPC nesting model

Per the docs:
- \`toolcall_start\`, \`toolcall_delta\`, \`toolcall_end\`, \`text_*\`, \`thinking_*\`, \`done\`, \`error\` are nested under \`message_update.assistantMessageEvent\`
- \`tool_execution_start\`, \`tool_execution_update\`, \`tool_execution_end\` are top-level
- \`agent_end\` is run-level completion containing all generated messages

## Current bugs in session.ts

1. \`thinking_start/delta/end\` handled as top-level events → \`onThinking\` NEVER fires
2. \`toolcall_start/end\` handled as top-level events → \`onEvent('toolcall')\` NEVER fires (tool-start phase in timeline always missing)
3. \`agent_end\` fires \`onEvent('done')\` — blurs run-level completion with message-level \`assistantMessageEvent.done\`

## Blast radius (GitNexus confirmed)

- \`src/pi/session.ts\` — bug location
- \`src/specialist/runner.ts\` — direct callback consumer
- \`src/specialist/supervisor.ts\` — maps callbacks to timeline events
- \`src/specialist/timeline-events.ts\` — \`mapCallbackEventToTimelineEvent\` already annotated with unitAI-4rn
- \`src/tools/specialist/poll_specialist.tool.ts\` — reads status/timeline downstream

## Goals

- Align \`PiAgentSession._handleEvent\` with the documented RPC nesting model
- Fix thinking and tool-call lifecycle events so they actually fire
- Separate message-level vs run-level completion semantics
- Protect the protocol mapping with regression tests

## Success criteria

- [ ] \`onThinking\` fires on \`message_update.assistantMessageEvent.thinking_delta\`
- [ ] \`onEvent('toolcall')\` fires on \`message_update.assistantMessageEvent.toolcall_start\`
- [ ] \`onEvent('agent_end')\` replaces \`onEvent('done')\` for run-level completion
- [ ] Timeline tool-start events (phase: start) actually appear in runs
- [ ] Downstream consumers updated/confirmed correct
- [ ] Regression tests cover protocol boundary

## Tasks

1. unitAI-4rn.1 — Fix session.ts _handleEvent nested protocol parsing
2. unitAI-4rn.2 — Audit and update downstream consumers after protocol fix
3. unitAI-4rn.3 — Regression test suite for Pi RPC event parsing

title: A settled Specialist does not wake its coordinator, so completion still requires polling
description:
PROBLEM
A settled Specialist does not wake its coordinator. ASK_EVENTS in the Pi extension maps exactly two forensic events to the wake — clarification_requested and escalation_raised. Nothing maps activation_settled, activation_completed or activation_failed, so a coordinator that dispatches and waits cannot learn the child finished except by calling specialist_status again.

Observed live 2026-09-08 by the pi-specialists coordinator against READY bead unitAI-v29bw: the ask path woke the session into a new turn with no polling and the child resumed and settled correctly — but settlement produced no notification and no follow-up turn. The coordinator only discovered the activation had completed because the OPERATOR asked 'is he settled?'.

THIS IS THE OPERATOR'S ORIGINAL COMPLAINT 3, still live. From the pane-757 report that opened this work: 'third, he started polling for results.' unitAI-rrdnt.45 built the ask wake and I recorded that complaint as addressed. It was addressed only for asks. The .46 Fleet widget also does not close it: the widget repaints for an OPERATOR watching the TUI, and never wakes the coordinator MODEL. A coordinator running headless, or one simply not being watched, is exactly as blind as before.

PRD REFERENCE: 5.3 item 7, the finalize step's typed Channels/handoff notification, does not reach a coordinator.

SUCCESS
A coordinator that dispatches a Specialist and does nothing learns, without polling, that the activation settled — completed, failed or refused — and can read the result.

SCRUTINY
MEDIUM

SCOPE
The wake observer in config/pi-extensions/specialist-subagents/index.mjs. The seam already exists: createAskObserverSink wraps the forensic sink and the wake rides pi.sendMessage with deliverAs followUp and triggerTurn.

NON_GOALS
Does not change what the host emits — the producer side already emits every terminal event. Does not add a second notification channel; this rides the wake that .45 built.

CONSTRAINTS
Terminal events are NOISIER than asks. Every activation settles exactly once, but a coordinator running several will get one wake each, and a wake carries a turn. Decide deliberately whether settlement wakes always, only when nothing else is pending, or is batched — and say which in the flag description, because the --no-specialist-wake flag currently reads as covering everything.
A failed or REFUSED activation must wake too. Waking only on success would make the silent case the failure case, which is the shape this epic has repeatedly got wrong.
The wake must not become authoritative: like the ask wake, it reports and never mutates DeliveryState. specialist_status stays the correlation authority.

VALIDATION
1. Dispatch, do nothing, and observe the coordinator take a turn on settlement naming the activation and its status.
2. The same for a failed activation and for one refused at admission.
3. With --no-specialist-wake, no settlement turn fires and the result stays readable through specialist_status.

OUTPUT
The settlement wake, its tests, and a live transcript of a coordinator that dispatched and did nothing.

REFERENCES
Reported by the pi-specialists coordinator 2026-09-08 from a live smoke test. Related: unitAI-rrdnt.45 (the ask wake, which this extends), unitAI-rrdnt.46 (the Fleet widget, which serves operators rather than the coordinator model).
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-09-08 to this bead's CONSTRAINTS, from the pi-specialists coordinator. I wrote 'a failed or REFUSED activation must wake too'. The REFUSED half is wrong and the bead should not be built to it.

ADMISSION REFUSAL NEEDS NO WAKE, and it is not a second instance of this defect. A refusal happens SYNCHRONOUSLY inside the specialist_dispatch call the coordinator is already awaiting: start() throws DispatchRejectedError and the tool catches it and returns { status: 'rejected', reason, detail } as the tool RESULT (index.mjs:614-622, activation.tool.ts:270-273). The coordinator is mid-turn, blocked on that exact call, and cannot miss it. There is no asynchronous window for silence to hide in, so a wake would be redundant rather than absent. Refusal emits activation_rejected, which is not a terminal event.

WHERE THE POINT ACTUALLY BITES is RUNTIME failure AFTER admission. activation_failed fires on a RUNNING activation when a turn ends with stopReason 'error' or 'aborted' — provider 429, auth, abort (native-host.ts:586-605) — or when runToSettled throws (636-639). That is asynchronous, post-dispatch, and not in ASK_EVENTS. An unattended coordinator is as blind to it as to settlement, and given how many 429s this provider produced today it is not a rare path.

SO THE HOLE IS BOUNDED, and stating the boundary is more useful than the general claim: the silent cases are the POST-ADMISSION asynchronous ones — activation_settled, activation_completed, activation_failed. Admission refusal is correctly synchronous. Build the wake for the first set and leave refusal alone.

The 'waking only on success makes silence mean failure' constraint still holds in full, but it applies to runtime failure rather than to refusal.
close_reason:
Merged at d150c0f3 and PROVEN LIVE.

The coordinator was instructed to dispatch and stop completely — no polling, no status calls. It went idle, then woke itself:

  [specialist_settled]
  Specialist explorer finished and is no longer running.
  activation_id: act:8dd59a44-5c6
  bead: unitAI-dkfxi
  Call specialist_status to read its validated result...

It then called specialist_status unprompted and disposed the activation. That is the operator's original complaint 3 — 'he started polling for results' — actually closed, rather than closed for asks only.

WHAT SHIPPED: wakes on activation_completed and activation_failed. Runtime failure counts as much as success; activation_failed fires when a turn ends with stopReason error or aborted, which this provider produced continuously today.

THREE DELIBERATE EXCLUSIONS. activation_settled precedes output validation and activation_completed follows it, so waking on both double-fires for one activation. Admission refusal is excluded because it is the synchronous return value of the dispatch call the coordinator is already blocked on — no asynchronous window, so a wake would be redundant rather than missing. That boundary came from the pi-specialists coordinator correcting my 'a failed or REFUSED activation must wake too', which was wrong on the refused half.

Always wakes rather than batching: each activation terminates exactly once, so volume is bounded by dispatches the coordinator itself made, and batching would trade the defect for a smaller version of itself.

The --no-specialist-wake flag description and the first-dispatch announcement both said 'asks or escalates' and now say what they cover.

description:
PROBLEM
The MCP server uses StdioServerTransport (src/server.ts:244) and owns NativeActivationHost as an in-process field (src/server.ts:135). Stdio is connection-scoped: when the client disconnects the process exits, the host goes with it, and EVERY live native Specialist dies mid-flight.

That contradicts properties the PRD states explicitly. Section 1 requires a Specialist to be 'persistent' and 'resumable'. native-host.ts's own docstring says 'Session lifetime deliberately exceeds turn lifetime: reaching agent_settled makes a Specialist waiting and resumable, never disposed. Disposal is an explicit act.' Under stdio, disposal is NOT an explicit act — a dropped client disposes everything, silently, with no forensic settle and no lease release.

TO BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THE PRD DOES AND DOES NOT SAY: it never names a transport. 'streamable', 'http', 'sse' and 'stdio' each appear ZERO times. So this is not a violation of a named-transport requirement; it is a violation of the persistence and resumability requirements the PRD does state, which stdio plus an in-process host cannot satisfy. The stronger argument is the property one, and it does not depend on which protocol revision is current.

HOW THIS GOT MISSED: unitAI-rrdnt.33 (Phase 13) validated that the tools WORK over MCP — a real stdio client against the built dist server reaching state 'running' with a real pi_session_id. It never tested that an activation SURVIVES the client going away. Phase 13 was closed on tool reachability, not on lifetime. I closed it; this is my miss.

SUCCESS
A native activation survives the MCP client disconnecting and reconnecting, and remains resumable — or the coupling is documented as intended with its consequence stated wherever persistence is claimed.

SCRUTINY
HIGH

SCOPE
src/server.ts transport selection and host ownership. The decision about whether the host outlives the connection belongs in this bead.

NON_GOALS
Does not change the Pi extension, which is unaffected — its host lives in the pi process and has no MCP connection to lose. Does not change tool semantics.

CONSTRAINTS
The SDK in tree is @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.29.0, whose LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION is 2025-11-25 and which also speaks 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26, 2024-11-05 and 2024-10-07. Our server pins nothing and takes the SDK default. Streamable HTTP with a session id is the transport that permits reconnection and parallel clients; moving to it is necessary but NOT sufficient — if the host stays a field on the server object, a process restart still kills every activation. The lifetime question is separate from the transport question and must be answered explicitly.
Do not treat 'the connection came back' as 'the activation survived'. That is the same inference-from-absence the uncertain-workspace design refuses everywhere else.

VALIDATION
1. Dispatch a native activation over MCP, drop the client, reconnect, and observe the activation still present and resumable.
2. A dropped client that DOES kill activations produces forensic settle events and releases workspace leases, rather than vanishing silently.

OUTPUT
Either a transport plus host-lifetime change that satisfies (1), or a documented decision with the consequence stated wherever the PRD's persistence claim is repeated.

REFERENCES
Raised by the operator 2026-09-08. Related: unitAI-rrdnt.33 (Phase 13, closed on tool reachability), unitAI-rrdnt.10 (which already demoted MCP as the Claude push transport after finding Claude Code's MCP client lacks the needed surfaces).
notes:
TRANSPORT AVAILABILITY CHECKED 2026-09-08, against the packages rather than from memory. The target is MCP spec 2026-07-28 (stateless connections), per the operator.

  installed:  @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.29.0
              LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION = '2025-11-25'
              SUPPORTED = ['2025-11-25','2025-06-18','2025-03-26','2024-11-05','2024-10-07']
  latest published: 1.30.0 — fetched and unpacked to check
              LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION = '2025-11-25'  (unchanged)
              '2026-07-28' appears ZERO times in its types.js

So the official TypeScript SDK does NOT yet speak 2026-07-28, even at head. Upgrading 1.29.0 -> 1.30.0 buys nothing for this bead. That reorders the work:

  1. The HOST LIFETIME fix is available NOW and is the larger half of the defect. Decoupling NativeActivationHost from the server object means a dropped client stops killing activations regardless of which transport is underneath. This bead's SUCCESS can be met on the current transport.
  2. The TRANSPORT move is blocked on the SDK, not on us. Options when it matters: wait for SDK support, implement 2026-07-28 outside the SDK, or move to Streamable HTTP on 2025-11-25 — which already permits reconnection and parallel clients and is a strict improvement on stdio even though it is not the target spec.

Do NOT do (2) before (1). A stateless transport in front of a host that still dies with its process just relocates the failure.

Re-check the SDK before starting: this reading is from 2026-09-08 and a version bump is exactly the kind of fact that goes stale.
DEFERRED by operator decision 2026-09-08 — the transport migration is a large piece of work in its own right and MCP is not the Pi coordinator's path.

CARRIED FORWARD, so the deferral is not read as 'no problem here': the HOST LIFETIME half is independent of the transport and is the larger half of the defect. NativeActivationHost is a field on the MCP server object, so process exit disposes every live Specialist with no forensic settle and no lease release. That is fixable on stdio today and does not wait for the SDK.

If MCP is picked up again for Claude and non-pi agents, do the lifetime decoupling FIRST. A stateless transport in front of a host that still dies with its process only relocates the failure.

title: Acceptance U: the coordinator is not fenced, and half of U is unachievable on Pi 0.85.1
description:
PROBLEM
PRD acceptance U says the coordinator is fenced from a workspace a Specialist holds. workspace-lease.ts opens by claiming 'exactly one writer per mutable workspace, coordinator included'. Neither is true today, and one half of it cannot be made true on the current platform.

MEASURED 2026-09-08:
  1. NOTHING ACQUIRES A LEASE FOR THE COORDINATOR. acquireLease is called from exactly two places, both in native-host.ts and both for a Specialist activation (admission at :336, resume at :877). The coordinator never takes a lease, so there is nothing for another writer to contend with and nothing to refuse the coordinator itself.
  2. THE MODULE ALREADY STATES THE PLATFORM LIMIT. H3 (pi.exec inside an extension handler) and H4 (direct node:fs / child_process inside extension code) are documented as 'not satisfiable on Pi 0.85.1 — no exec or filesystem interposition layer exists'. A coordinator writing through those paths cannot be fenced by any lease we build.

So U splits into a part that is achievable and a part that is not, and the bead conflates them:
  - ACHIEVABLE: fence the coordinator's LLM-INITIATED mutations, the same class the lease already covers for Specialists. This is interposable — it is a tool-call hook on the coordinator's own session, the same seam the ask-observer and the wake already ride.
  - NOT ACHIEVABLE on Pi 0.85.1: fence extension code and pi.exec. The module is explicit that this is a trusted-extension threat rather than a delegated-agent threat, and that 'a lease that claims total enforcement is more dangerous than one that documents its boundary'.

SUCCESS
Either the coordinator acquires and respects the workspace lease for its own LLM-initiated writes, with the H3/H4 boundary stated wherever the guarantee is described — or acceptance U is formally narrowed to that scope, with the reason recorded.

SCRUTINY
HIGH

SCOPE
Coordinator-side lease acquisition and the tool-call hook that would enforce it, plus the wording of the guarantee in workspace-lease.ts and both frontends.

NON_GOALS
Does not attempt to close H3/H4 — the platform does not permit it and pretending otherwise is the specific danger the module names. Does not change Specialist-side admission, which is proven.

CONSTRAINTS
Do NOT describe the coordinator as 'fenced' without the qualifier. The lease covers every mutation an LLM can initiate; it does not cover trusted extension code. That distinction is the whole of the module's honesty and it must survive into the operator-facing text.
A coordinator that takes a lease must also release it, or it will fence every Specialist it dispatches — which is worse than the current state.

VALIDATION
1. With a Specialist holding a workspace, a coordinator LLM write to that workspace is refused, and the refusal names the holder.
2. The coordinator releases such that a subsequent Specialist dispatch is admitted.
3. The H3/H4 boundary is stated in the operator-facing description, not only in the module docstring.

OUTPUT
Either the coordinator-side fence plus the narrowed guarantee, or a recorded decision that U is narrowed with its reason.

REFERENCES
unitAI-rrdnt.36 acceptance U; unitAI-rrdnt.6 (the pi.exec/executeBash veto bypass, unclosed). Blocks unitAI-rrdnt.36 from closing.
notes:
MECHANISM FOUND 2026-09-08. This is no longer an open design question — the achievable half is buildable and the hook is named. Read from the installed SDK typings at node_modules/@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts, not inferred.

  on(event: 'tool_call', handler: ExtensionHandler<ToolCallEvent, ToolCallEventResult>): void;
  // 'Fired before a tool executes. Can block.'
  interface ToolCallEventResult { block?: boolean; reason?: string }

So an extension CAN intercept and refuse the coordinator's own mutating tool calls, per call, which is precisely the shape workspace-lease.ts §5.9 requires and explicitly distinguishes from setActiveToolsByName. ToolCallEvent is a union with concrete members for bash, read, edit, write, grep, find, ls plus CustomToolCallEvent, so the mutating set is addressable by name.

THE BUILD, in one sentence: register a tool_call handler in config/pi-extensions/specialist-subagents/index.mjs that, for the mutating tool names, calls the SAME admitToolCall the Specialist side uses against the coordinator's workspace and returns { block: true, reason } when a Specialist holds the lease. Shared function, not a second implementation — a second admission check would let the coordinator and the Specialists disagree about who holds the workspace, which is the failure mode this epic has spent the day removing.

THIS ALSO CORRECTS THE MODULE'S OWN H-ANALYSIS. workspace-lease.ts records H2 (the operator user_bash path) as 'satisfiable by our own discipline'. It is stronger than that: pi exposes on('user_bash', ...) with a UserBashEventResult, so H2 is ENFORCEABLE, not merely avoidable by convention. H3 (pi.exec) and H4 (direct node:fs in extension code) remain unhookable and the module's verdict on them stands.

WHY I AM NOT BUILDING IT IN THIS SESSION, deliberately. A tool_call handler that returns block:true on the COORDINATOR's session has the largest blast radius of anything in this epic — a bug there stops the operator writing anything at all, in their own session, with the failure appearing as an unexplained refusal. That is a HIGH-scrutiny change (this bead is marked HIGH for exactly this reason) and it needs a live run to validate, on a provider that has been rate-limiting all session. Shipping it on unit tests would repeat the mistake I made twice today with unitAI-rrdnt.59.

The next session starts with the hook named, the result shape known, the shared function identified, and the H2 correction recorded. That is the expensive part and it is done.
CORRECTION to my own note above, found while starting the build. 'Call the SAME admitToolCall the Specialist side uses' IS WRONG and would have been a serious defect.

admitToolCall's decision table (workspace-lease.ts:443-467) is:
  not a mutating tool                 -> allow
  held by THIS activationId           -> allow
  held by another                     -> refuse
  uncertain                           -> refuse
  FREE / not leased by this activation-> REFUSE

The default for an UNLEASED workspace is REFUSE, because a Specialist must hold a lease to mutate. The coordinator never holds one. So reusing this predicate for the coordinator would block EVERY coordinator write whenever no Specialist happened to be running — which is almost always. That is not a fence, it is a coordinator that cannot edit its own repo.

The coordinator needs a DIFFERENT predicate: refuse only when the workspace is held by another activation, or is uncertain; allow when free. Same underlying inspect(), different rule, and the difference is the default case.

That makes .61 a genuine design decision rather than wiring, which is what its HIGH scrutiny was for. Whoever builds it must:
  - add a coordinator-facing admission function beside admitToolCall, sharing inspect() so the two cannot disagree about who holds the lease, but NOT sharing the verdict rule
  - state in both docstrings why the defaults differ, because two admission functions over one lease is exactly the shape that drifts (see unitAI-kv8ac)
  - fail OPEN on any error: a bug in a coordinator tool_call handler must never be able to stop an operator writing in their own session

Also required and not yet present: admitToolCall (or its coordinator sibling) is NOT exported through src/lib.ts, and the extension has no workspace-identity resolver. Both are prerequisites.

I stopped here rather than building it. Finding that the obvious reuse is wrong is worth more to the next attempt than a fence that would have refused every coordinator edit.
close_reason:
Coordinator fence built. PRD acceptance U is satisfied for every mutation the coordinator's MODEL can initiate, with the platform boundary documented rather than implied away — which is the second of the two resolutions this bead's SUCCESS permitted.

MECHANISM: pi.on('tool_call') fires before a tool executes and can block (ToolCallEventResult { block, reason }), read from the installed SDK typings. That is the per-call hook workspace-lease.ts §5.9 requires and that setActiveToolsByName cannot provide.

THE PREDICATE IS NEW, NOT REUSED, and that is the whole finding. admitCoordinatorToolCall sits beside admitToolCall and shares inspect(), so the two can never disagree about who holds the lease — but its DEFAULT differs: a free workspace is allowed. The Specialist rule refuses an unleased workspace because a Specialist must hold a lease to mutate; applying it to the coordinator would have refused every coordinator write whenever no Specialist was running. 'Just share the function' was what I wrote on this bead an hour before building it, and it was wrong.

FAILS OPEN, without exception. This handler runs on the operator's own session; a bug that threw or refused wrongly would stop them editing their own repository and would surface as an unexplained refusal. A fence that misses a block is recoverable, one that wrongly blocks the operator is not.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE REAL FILE-BACKED LEASE, not a stub:
  free      + write -> allow
  free      + read  -> allow
  HELD      + write -> REFUSED, 'held by executor act:spec pid 1814477'
  HELD      + read  -> allow (non-mutating is never gated)
  released  + write -> allow again
Plus four extension tests, including the free-workspace case that exists specifically to catch the reuse trap, and the fail-open case.

BOUNDARY, stated in the code and not only here: H3 (pi.exec) and H4 (direct node:fs inside extension code) are not interposable on Pi 0.85.1, so this fences every mutation the coordinator's model can initiate and no more. The lease module's claim that H2 (user_bash) is merely 'satisfiable by our own discipline' is understated — pi exposes on('user_bash') with a result type, so H2 is enforceable; that remains unbuilt and is the obvious follow-up.

Suite 2347 passed, 193 files.

title: Lease events never reach forensics, so a blocked write leaves no trace
description:
PROBLEM
Workspace-lease events never reach the forensic store. `bd`-verified 2026-09-08: `SELECT event_name, count(*) FROM specialist_forensic_events WHERE event_name LIKE '%lease%'` returns NOTHING for the entire history of the database. native-host.ts emits lease_acquired (line 343) and lease_denied (334, 434), and Phase 7's projection deliberately drops all three with a documented rationale in native-activation-observability.ts lines 59-62: 'Workspace-lease contention has no legacy runner concept.'

That reasoning is half right and the conclusion does not follow. There is genuinely no legacy EQUIVALENT to compare a lease event against. It does not follow that the event should not be RECORDED. Parity means a native activation answers the same queries a legacy one does; it does not mean native may only emit events legacy also emits. An event with no counterpart is uncomparable, not unimportant.

The concrete consequence: PRD acceptance V, carried by unitAI-rrdnt.36 VALIDATION 2, requires that a BLOCKED WRITE emits a forensic event. It cannot be satisfied while lease_denied is unmapped. A write refused for lease contention currently leaves no durable trace at all — the refusal reaches the caller and vanishes.

This is also the one event class an operator most needs after the fact. A writer that was refused, or a lease left uncertain, is exactly the situation reconstructed from forensics hours later, and it is the situation with no rows.

SUCCESS
lease_acquired, lease_denied and lease_uncertain are durable in specialist_forensic_events, queryable by job_id alongside every other event for that activation. PRD acceptance V is satisfiable.

SCRUTINY
MEDIUM

SCOPE
src/specialist/native-activation-observability.ts, where the three events are currently mapped to rationale strings instead of rows.

NON_GOALS
Does not change what the host emits — the producer side is correct. Does not re-add a parallel event vocabulary for anything else; this is three named events with a stated reason, not a reopening of Phase 7.

CONSTRAINTS
Phase 7's rule stands: no second forensic model, and native rows keep the v15 identity lineage. These events must go through the same writers as everything else, carrying job_id, attempt_id and participant_id, so the joint query still finds them.
Choose the family deliberately and write down why. These are admission-control events, not job lifecycle events, and calling them 'job' to make them look legacy-shaped would be the same mistake in reverse.

VALIDATION
1. A live write dispatch produces a lease_acquired row queryable by job_id.
2. A second concurrent write dispatch is refused and produces a lease_denied row.
3. The Phase 7 joint query still returns matching families for native and legacy.

OUTPUT
The mapping, its tests, and a live two-writer transcript showing the denial row.

REFERENCES
Found by the coordinator's live Phase 10 writer proof, act:f644288a-b64 (executor, admitted [write], wrote its file, 742 forensic rows, ZERO lease rows). Blocks unitAI-rrdnt.36 VALIDATION 2.
close_reason:
Lease and tool-guard events now persist as control_signal — family 'control', severity 'warn' — a shared timeline type the legacy runner also uses, so the rows return without reopening a native-only vocabulary. Deliberately NOT the 'job' family: these are admission decisions, not run lifecycle, and dressing them as job events would be the same mistake in reverse.

VALIDATION 1 and 2, both LIVE, two concurrent writers against one workspace:
  act:8a8b1840-e33 (granted)  -> control.lease_acquired.recorded, carrying bead_id unitAI-schwn and the workspace path
  act:76e4bf99-c59 (refused)  -> control.lease_denied.recorded, carrying bead_id unitAI-9exji, the workspace, and reason workspace_held_by_another_writer

Before this change the store contained ZERO lease rows across its entire history. It now contains both.

The refusal envelope the operator saw is also worth recording, because it is what PRD acceptance S asks for and it names the holder: 'exactly one writer holds a mutable workspace at a time', holder 'executor act:8a8b1840-e33 pid 489654', AgentSession not created.

VALIDATION 3: the Phase 7 joint query is unaffected — control_signal is a shared type and the rows carry the same identity columns. Full suite 2336 passed, 193 files.

The Phase 7 lane's pinned gap-table assertion was UPDATED, not loosened: the four names were removed from the table and from the assertion, with a comment saying why. lease_released and lease_reconciled remain gaps — teardown of a granted lease is implied by the activation's terminal event.

title: Contract gate rejects same-line 'PROBLEM: text' sections and reports them all missing
description:
PROBLEM
src/activation/bead-gate.ts headingOf() recognises a section only as a bare word on its own line (markdown marks, bold and a TRAILING colon are stripped). A contract written as 'PROBLEM: the thing is broken' normalises to 'PROBLEM:_THE_THING_IS_BROKEN', which is not in ALL_HEADINGS, so extractSections returns an EMPTY map and the gate refuses with every section listed as missing — while all eight sections are in fact present. Measured: extractSections on a full inline-form contract returns [].

The refusal reason is actively misleading. An operator or model reading 'missing: PROBLEM, SUCCESS, ...' about a description that visibly contains PROBLEM and SUCCESS has no path to the real cause.

SUCCESS
A contract using same-line 'SECTION: body' headers is parsed with the text after the colon as the first line of that section's body, and dispatches. The bare-heading form keeps working unchanged.

SCRUTINY
HIGH

SCOPE
headingOf and extractSections in src/activation/bead-gate.ts, and the 'contract' parameter teaching text on BOTH frontends (config/pi-extensions/specialist-subagents/index.mjs and src/tools/specialist/activation.tool.ts).

NON_GOALS
Does not change which sections are required. Does not change the refusal shape or the DispatchRejectedError rendering.

CONSTRAINTS
extractSections is the SINGLE parser for the contract — the gate decides admission with it and the StepContract compiler reads section bodies with it. A second parser would let the two disagree, which the file's own docstring calls worse than either being wrong alone. Fix it in headingOf, not at a call site.
The inline body text must be CAPTURED, not discarded: dropping it turns 'missing' into 'declared but empty', which the parser deliberately distinguishes.
Only treat a line as a heading when the section name is at the START of the line followed immediately by a colon — a section name inside prose is still not a heading.

VALIDATION
1. extractSections on an inline-form contract returns all eight sections with non-empty bodies.
2. extractSections on the bare-heading form is byte-identical to today's output.
3. A live specialist_dispatch with an inline-form contract is admitted rather than refused.

OUTPUT
The parser fix, its regression tests, and teaching text on both frontends that states the accepted format rather than only the section names.
notes:
VALIDATION 3 MET, 2026-09-08, live in a FRESH pi session (the freshness is the point — see unitAI-rrdnt.55).

Dispatch with an inline same-line contract and NO bead_id: admitted on first try.
  activation: act:b5d298b2-ed8 / att:b5d298b2-ed8:1, specialist explorer
  bead created from the contract: unitAI-jrlmj, title derived from PROBLEM's first line, description stored in the same-line form verbatim
  11 forensic rows: activation_requested -> ... -> output_validation_passed -> activation_completed
  admitted body: tier READ_ONLY, tools 'read,grep,find,ls', custom_tools 'ask_coordinator,escalate_to_coordinator'

This proves .48 and .54 together: the gate ran BEFORE any bead existed, passed on the same-line form, and only then was the bead created — a refusal would have left the board unchanged.

Two independent confirmations, and they failed differently, which is why both were needed. The pi-specialists session ran evaluateBeadReadiness directly against the rebuilt dist and got ok:true on the identical sections, but its LIVE retry still refused — its extension held the pre-fix module in memory from before the rebuild. It diagnosed that from a property of the running process rather than the code: the loaded tool's contract-parameter description lacked a sentence the on-disk index.mjs carries. Filed as unitAI-rrdnt.55, because that refusal is byte-identical to a genuinely incomplete contract and every future extension change inherits it.
close_reason:
Fixed in headingOf(), the single parser both the gate and the StepContract compiler read through — not at a call site.

VALIDATION 1: extractSections on a full inline-form contract returns all eight sections with non-empty bodies (was: an empty map). VALIDATION 2: the bare-heading form is byte-identical, asserted directly. VALIDATION 3 (live inline dispatch) delegated to the pi-specialists session that found this, which had two dispatches refused by it.

Kept the guard the old docstring promised: a section name inside prose is still not a heading. The name must START the line with the colon immediately after, so 'we must decide whether to log OUTPUT: below or above the fold' stays inside PROBLEM's body. Test asserts it.

The inline body text is captured as the section's first body line rather than discarded — dropping it would have converted 'missing' into 'declared but empty', a distinction the parser deliberately keeps.

Teaching text on BOTH frontends now states the accepted FORMAT, not only the section names. That omission is what made this reachable: .44 taught which sections and never how to write them, so a model following the tool description exactly would produce the form the parser rejected.

Full unit suite 2310 passed, 188 files. Reported by the pi-specialists session; root cause independently reproduced here before any edit.

title: Acceptance AX cannot pass: the probe bead instructs the opposite of the asking specialist
description:
PROBLEM
The acceptance AX live case dispatches live-smoke-asker against the SHARED reader probe bead. That bead's SCOPE says "Reply with one short sentence confirming you are running, then stop", its NON_GOALS say "No further work", its CONSTRAINTS say "One sentence". The specialist's system prompt says the child must call ask_coordinator and cannot finish otherwise. The bead is the prompt in the native runtime, so the bead outranks the system prompt: the child replies once and stops, and never asks.

Observed 2026-09-07 on the first run in which the case executed at all (it had been dying on a nonexistent host.snapshot() before reaching any assertion):
  the child never asked.
    activation state: settled
    tools the session actually resolved: ["read","grep","find","ls","ask_coordinator","escalate_to_coordinator"]
    ask tool present: true
    child result so far: completed: I'm running natively in-process as the activation host's live smoke probe, and this sentence completes the required turn.
The child's answer is verbatim the reader probe's answer. The ask tool was present, so this is not the unitAI-rrdnt.43 tool-filter defect; it is the probe design.

askingSpecialistSpec carries a comment saying it "makes asking the ONLY way to finish", precisely so the case does not turn on model temperament. The shared bead defeats that.

SUCCESS
Acceptance AX exercises a real ask/answer/resume cycle, and it can only be satisfied by calling the ask tool.

SCOPE
tests/integration/activation/native-activation.live.test.ts: a second probe bead created in beforeAll for the asking case, and closed in afterAll alongside the existing one.

NON_GOALS
No change to askingSpecialistSpec's system prompt, to the host, to the ask tool, or to the reader probe bead used by acceptance B, A, C, D and F.

CONSTRAINTS
The withheld value must be unguessable and must exist nowhere on disk — generate it at run time. A guessable value turns a green test back into a fixture assertion, which is the failure shape this epic has hit four times. The bead text is read by the child, so it must state the requirement without carrying the value. The ask bead must still be a complete 7-section contract with SCRUTINY, or the Phase 3 gate refuses it.

VALIDATION
1. The AX case reaches exactly one pending ask and the child's final output contains the run-time-generated value.
2. pi_session_id is unchanged across the answer, which is what distinguishes a resume from a restart.
3. Live, not stubbed.

OUTPUT
An asking-probe bead that makes the ask mandatory, and a passing acceptance AX.

SCRUTINY
MEDIUM. A probe that can pass without asking gives false assurance about the clarification path.
close_reason: Acceptance AX has its own probe bead with a per-run unguessable token; it passes live against zai/glm-5.3-flash with a real ask, a real answer and an unchanged pi_session_id. Uncovered a second defect: InteractionTransport.attemptDelivery returned true with no deliver hook, marking every ask delivered with nothing to deliver it — fixed, with the missing test. Commit aeccb792 on xt/phase11-model.

title: Pi extension: specialist_list as the sp-list awareness surface (implemented, merged 48fd3452)
description:
PROBLEM
The operator asked for an sp-list equivalent inside the Pi extension (awareness, not surface area). The specialist_list tool was implemented and merged (48fd3452) but never tracked as a bead, so the decision behind its shape is invisible to later readers.

SUCCESS
unitAI-rrdnt.49 is tracked with the shape decision recorded; the tool continues to work as merged.

SCOPE
Tracking + contract only. The implementation is already on master (specialist_list in config/pi-extensions/specialist-subagents/index.mjs).

NON_GOALS
Explicitly NOT a replacement for the specialists CLI: sp run/feed/result/steer/resume/stop and the rest of sp help are deliberately not reproduced as tools. The listing is awareness — one read of the resolved registry with native dispatchability markers — and its description points at sp help for the full surface. No scheduler, no workflow engine, no second SpecialistLoader resolution (it uses the SAME loader and the SAME admission checks the host runs via the lib seam).

CONSTRAINTS
Keep the dispatchable/undispatchable distinction (model chain, tool contract, preflight) derived from the same functions the host admits with, never a reimplementation. Repo + user layer overrides must be visible (scope/source per row).

VALIDATION
specialist_list returns rows with name/category/scope/source/permission_required/access/dispatchable (+reason when undispatchable) and a 'Full CLI surface: sp help' note; unit test covers the projection (26/26 suite green on the merged tree).

OUTPUT
This bead closed with notes citing the merged implementation and this contract.

SCRUTINY LOW
notes:
PROGRESSIVE DISCLOSURE ADDED 2026-09-08 after an operator reported the tool dumping ~300 lines.

MEASURED before: 32 specialists x 9 fields = 16,161 bytes over 357 lines, of which 7,156 bytes (44%) was 'description' prose — a field a coordinator needs when choosing ONE specialist and never when scanning all of them.

NOW:
  default            compact line per specialist: name, tier, access, category, dispatchable, and reason only where dispatchable is false
  name=<specialist>  the full record for one, description included; an unknown name returns the list of known names rather than a bare error
  detail='full'      the previous dump, kept so nothing is lost

dispatchable stays on EVERY row even though omitting it when true would save more. Absence would then mean 'dispatchable', which is indistinguishable from the field going missing through a bug — and dispatchability is the single thing this tool exists to report. Only 'reason' is conditional, because there is no reason when nothing is wrong. An existing .49 assertion caught me trying the byte-saving version, correctly.

A test asserts the compact form is under a third of the full form, so the reduction cannot silently regress.
close_reason: Closed — specialist_list (the .49 work) was implemented and merged at 48fd3452; this bead exists to record the shape decision: awareness-not-surface-area, NON_GOALS explicit, sp help pointer, same loader/admission checks via the seam.

title: Pi extension: specialist_list tool is the sp-list awareness surface (implemented, merged 48fd3452)
description:
