title: Native activations are invisible to the CLI: sp ps and sp feed do not show them
description:
PROBLEM
Operator-observed live on 2026-09-08: with an activation running, the operator reached for sp ps and for an sp feed equivalent and neither showed it. Native activations live in an in-process FleetRegistry inside whichever process hosts them, so a separate CLI process cannot see them at all — and the forensic rows that WOULD make them visible are not being written (unitAI-rrdnt.37.1).

SUCCESS
An operator can see a native activation and its progress from the CLI, or the CLI states plainly that native activations are only visible in their host session and points at where they ARE visible.

SCOPE
sp ps and the feed surfaces. Deciding whether native activations become CLI-visible at all, and by what mechanism.

NON_GOALS
Does not put the Fleet in a shared store for its own sake. Does not create a second telemetry database (acceptance AP).

CONSTRAINTS
Depends on unitAI-rrdnt.37.1: without forensic rows there is nothing for a separate process to read. Fix that first or this bead has no data source.
An in-process Fleet is not a defect — session lifetime deliberately exceeds turn lifetime — so the honest answer may be that the CLI reports from forensics rather than from the registry, and shows last-known state rather than live state. If so, say which it is in the output, because 'last known' shown as 'current' is worse than absent.

VALIDATION
With an activation live in a pi session, an operator in a separate shell learns it exists and what state it reached.

OUTPUT
Either the CLI surface, or a documented decision that it is host-local with the reason.
notes: Coordinator 2026-09-08: assignee corrected to pi/cli-visibility. 'xt pi --bead' warned 'pi did not signal readiness within 30s' at launch, so the stamp never applied and the bead read as held by the shared actor jaggerxtrm. That made the coordinator's commit gate fire on a bead it does not own.
close_reason: Landed answer 1: sp ps 'Native activations' section + sp feed act:* forensic trail, both labeled LAST-KNOWN. Validated live against real DB rows (feed trail + ps human + ps JSON). Commit 74855783 on xt/cli-visibility, not pushed. Not proven: true liveness; follow-mode for act ids not built.

title: The Pi extension registers no UI: no slash commands, no Fleet view, nothing rendered in the TUI
description:
PROBLEM
Operator-observed live on 2026-09-08: the extension surfaces nothing in the TUI. No slash commands are offered, and the Fleet is not displayed anywhere — the coordinator's tool calls are the only evidence an activation exists. The operator reached for sp ps and for an sp feed equivalent and found neither applies to native activations.

PRD SS(viewport) says the Specialists extension should own a custom child viewport. It owns none.

SUCCESS
An operator in an interactive xt pi session can see the Fleet and any pending asks without asking the model to call a tool, and can act on them through slash commands.

SCOPE
config/pi-extensions/specialist-subagents/index.mjs: extension-registered commands and whatever view surface pi 0.85.1 exposes to an extension.

NON_GOALS
Does not build a second workflow engine (PRD line 222). Does not duplicate sp ps for legacy jobs.

CONSTRAINTS
Measure what pi 0.85.1 actually gives an extension before designing: other loaded extensions register commands and docks (pi-processes has processes-dock and processes-logs), so the capability exists — read one of them rather than guessing.
The view is a PROJECTION of the host Fleet, never a second source of state.

VALIDATION
Live in an interactive TUI: the operator sees a dispatched activation and a pending ask without prompting the model, and invokes at least one slash command against it.

OUTPUT
The registered commands and view, plus a live transcript or screenshot description.
close_reason: Operator surface added to the Pi extension: /fleet, /fleet:reply, /fleet:stop (all with live argument completion) plus an aboveEditor Fleet widget and a footer status, projected from host.list()/pendingAsks() by a 1s poll. Shared session_start ctx capture with generation + session-id guard, agreed verbatim with the unitAI-rrdnt.45 lane. 21/21 unit tests; live-verified in a real pi 0.85.1 TUI (widget paints with no model turn, reply and stop both act and repaint). Host untouched: no emitter added.

title: Extension-dispatched activations write NO forensics: the Pi extension constructs NativeActivationHost with no sink
description:
PROBLEM
config/pi-extensions/specialist-subagents/index.mjs:107 constructs `new NativeActivationHost()` with no deps, so `forensics` defaults to NULL_FORENSIC_SINK. src/server.ts:146-149 does the opposite — it passes `createActivationForensicSink(this.observability)`. So an activation dispatched from the MCP surface is answerable from observability.db and the identical activation dispatched from the Pi extension is forensically invisible.

Measured 2026-09-08 on a real interactive xt pi TUI run: activation act:36a8720f-f30 dispatched from the extension reached settled/completed with a validated result, and `SELECT ... FROM specialist_forensic_events WHERE job_id LIKE 'act:36a8720f%'` returns 0 rows. The worktree has no .specialists directory at all, so the rows did not go elsewhere — they were never written.

This contradicts PRD acceptance AJ (native observability) for the surface the PRD calls PRIMARY, and it is the same class of gap as the epic's recurring one: the sink exists, is correct, is tested, and the frontend most likely to be used does not wire it.

SUCCESS
An activation dispatched from the Pi extension produces the same forensic rows, under the same job_id, as the identical activation dispatched over MCP.

SCOPE
The host construction in config/pi-extensions/specialist-subagents/index.mjs, and whichever observability client the extension can reach from an ESM extension without a build step.

NON_GOALS
Does not change the sink, the schema, or the event vocabulary. Does not create a second telemetry store — acceptance AP forbids it.

CONSTRAINTS
The extension is .mjs with no build step, so it must reach the sink through the src/lib.ts seam rather than by importing internals. If the observability client cannot be constructed from that seam, say so with the measurement rather than adding a parallel store — an honest 'the seam does not expose this' is a usable result and unitAI-rrdnt.37 can gain the export.
The store must resolve to the SAME database the CLI reads, or the parity claim is false in a new way.

VALIDATION
1. Dispatch from the extension in a live pi session, then query specialist_forensic_events by that job_id and observe activation_admitted, activation_started and activation_completed.
2. Compare the row set against an MCP-dispatched activation of the same specialist and bead; the event_name sequences must match.
3. findDatabases-style check: no second .db file is created anywhere in the workspace (acceptance AP).

OUTPUT
The wiring, and the two row sets side by side as evidence.
close_reason: Closed on merge 48fd3452 — the extension now constructs its host with the canonical forensic sink (createCoordinatorHost + lib seam), live rows under node-pi proven (10 events for act:198ce538-0c7).

title: The per-call mutation guard has no caller: admitToolCall is host surface nothing invokes
description:
PROBLEM
67be44b1 wired the workspace writer lease into admission and release. It did not close the
in-turn half. NativeActivationHost.admitToolCall(activationId, toolName) is a public method
that returns the per-call verdict, emits tool_blocked on a refusal, and fails closed on an
unknown activation. Nothing calls it: `grep -rn admitToolCall src/ tests/` finds only
workspace-lease.ts (the underlying function), the method definition itself, and the lease
module's own unit tests. The host registers no blocking tool_call handler —
session.subscribe (native-host.ts:448) is an observation listener with no veto.

The only frontend that could call it is the Pi extension (unitAI-rrdnt.37), which is
unmerged; the MCP frontend has no agent-loop hook and structurally cannot. Leaving the
enforcement point to be invoked by a frontend is how enforcement becomes optional: the next
frontend forgets, and nothing goes red.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ENFORCED, stated precisely, because "the lease does nothing" is false and
dismissible:
- Two activations cannot both hold one worktree. Admission refuses the second, names the
  holder, and never steals an uncertain lease. That part works.
- The block DURING a turn is absent. A writer whose lease turns uncertain mid-turn is not
  stopped.
- A reader is not refused mutating calls by the lease. It is still constrained, but by its
  fail-closed tool allowlist — a different mechanism with a different failure mode. That
  distinction is exactly what gets flattened when someone summarises this later.

This is the same shape as the defect three lanes found independently earlier the same day:
a module complete, tested, correct, and reachable by nothing. One level up.

SUCCESS
Every mutating tool call made by a native activation passes through admitToolCall before it
executes, invoked by the host rather than by a frontend. A frontend that forgets to wire
anything cannot produce an unguarded activation.

SCOPE
src/activation/native-host.ts — the session hook that invokes the existing admitToolCall.
The verdict logic in workspace-lease.ts is correct and unchanged.

NON_GOALS
Does not change the lease record format, acquisition, release, or reconciliation. Does not
attempt to close the H1-H4 bypasses (executeBash, user_bash, pi.exec, direct node:fs), which
are not closable on pi 0.85.1 and are a trusted-extension threat rather than a
delegated-agent one. Does not move enforcement into a frontend.

CONSTRAINTS
Must be a per-CALL block and NOT setActiveToolsByName. Within a turn the agent loop runs
against a tool snapshot taken at turn start, so revoking a tool cannot cancel a call that is
already planned; every handler in a batch fires before any execution, so a block is
enforceable exactly where a tool-set change is not (unitAI-rrdnt.7).
If pi 0.85.1 exposes no in-process blocking hook to a session's own creator — as opposed to
an extension — say so with the measurement rather than moving the responsibility to the
frontend. An honest "the host cannot hook this on 0.85.1" is a usable result; a guard that
depends on each frontend remembering is not.

VALIDATION
1. A live probe drives a write-capable activation whose lease is made uncertain mid-turn and
   observes the next mutating call blocked, with a tool_blocked row in observability.db.
   A unit test over admitToolCall's return value does not satisfy this: the function was
   always correct and the defect is that nothing calls it.
2. A check fails if the host creates a session without registering the guard, so a future
   refactor cannot silently unhook it.
3. docs/native-activation.md: the "per-call mutation guard has no caller" holes row is
   removed and the lease banner stops saying "partly in force".

OUTPUT
The guard invoked from the host, the live evidence, the anti-unhook check, and the docs row
retired.

SCRUTINY
HIGH. This is a workspace mutation authority boundary. The failure mode is silent: nothing
errors, nothing goes red, and the gap is only visible by grepping for a caller.
notes:
MECHANISM MEASURED 2026-09-08 (coordinator lane), so this bead does not start from 'is it possible'. The answer to the CONSTRAINTS escape hatch is: pi 0.85.1 DOES give a session's own creator a way in, three of them, and they are not equally good.
(1) sdk.wrapRegisteredTool(registeredTool, runner) / wrapRegisteredTools — exported. Its own source shows it returning { ...tool, execute: async (toolCallId, params, signal, onUpdate) => ... }, which both confirms the real execute signature and shows the wrapping shape to copy.
(2) The individual builtin factories are exported: createEditTool, createWriteTool, createBashTool, createPowerShellTool, createReadTool, createGrepTool, createFindTool, createLsTool, plus their *Definition variants and createCodingTools/createReadOnlyTools. So the host can CONSTRUCT the mutating builtins itself, wrap each execute with a call to admitToolCall, and pass them as customTools rather than naming them in tools[] and getting pi's unguarded originals. This is the shape I would build: the guard is then structurally impossible to skip, because the only mutating tool the child can reach IS the wrapped one. It also satisfies the SUCCESS criterion literally — a frontend that wires nothing cannot produce an unguarded activation, because the frontend is not involved.
(3) AgentSession exposes bindExtensions, extensionRunner and hasExtensionHandlers, so the host could bind an in-process extension carrying a tool_call handler. Rejected as the primary: it reintroduces the extension seam this bead exists to get away from, and unitAI-rrdnt.6 already measured that extension vetoes do NOT cover AgentSession.executeBash() or pi.exec().
CAUTION: whichever is chosen, remember tools[] is a hard filter that also applies to customTools (unitAI-rrdnt.43.1) — a wrapped tool must be named in tools[] as well as supplied, or it is silently dropped and the child ends up with no mutating tool at all, which will look like the guard working.
close_reason: Guarded mutating tools: the host reconstructs pi's four mutating builtins (edit, write, bash, powershell) via the exported factories, wraps each execute with a live admitToolCall verdict, and passes them as customTools. The only mutating tool a child can reach is the guarded one, so a frontend that wires nothing cannot produce an unguarded activation. A mutating name the runtime cannot reconstruct refuses the dispatch rather than passing through unwrapped. 31 tests green.

title: Wire the workspace lease into admission, per-call mutation gating, and teardown
description:
PROBLEM
src/activation/workspace-lease.ts was complete, mutation-tested and closed on the board, and imported by nothing in src/. native-host.ts refused every write-capable activation with writer_not_supported_in_phase_1, so nothing was fenced because nothing wrote. Three lanes found this independently.

SUCCESS
A write-capable Specialist is admitted by TAKING the lease; contention refuses with the holder named; a reader is refused every mutating call; teardown releases, and an unreleasable lease becomes evidence rather than a silent free.

SCOPE
src/activation/native-host.ts: acquire after workspace resolution, admitToolCall as a per-call verdict, release on stop. The lease forensic events. Test isolation for every host built on a real cwd.

NON_GOALS
Does not prove acceptance S-Z with live dispatches — that stays on the parent unitAI-rrdnt.36 and is deliberately not claimed here. Does not close the pi.exec/executeBash veto hole (unitAI-rrdnt.6), which no 0.85.1 option closes.

CONSTRAINTS
The guard must be a per-call verdict and never setActiveToolsByName: within a turn the agent loop runs against a snapshot taken at turn start, so revoking a tool cannot cancel an already-planned call. release() THROWS on an uncertain lease and that throw must become a lease_uncertain event, never be swallowed — swallowing it silently frees a workspace that may still be under mutation. Teardown is never failed by a release problem.

VALIDATION
1. A writer is admitted and emits lease_acquired; a second writer on the same workspace is refused with workspace_held_by_another_writer and emits lease_denied.
2. The holder may mutate; a reader in the same workspace is refused a mutating call and emits tool_blocked, while its reads are untouched.
3. An unknown activation fails closed.
4. No unit test leaves a lease in the repository: ls .specialists/leases/ is empty after a suite run.

OUTPUT
The wiring, its forensic events, its tests, and the test isolation.
close_reason: Lease acquired on admission, per-call admitToolCall gate, release on teardown with the uncertain throw converted to lease_uncertain evidence. 18 host tests, 178 activation tests green, tsc clean, no lease leaked into the repo. Live S-Z proof remains open on the parent.

title: Dispatch refusals silently drop their explanation: reject() passes detail:, DispatchRejectedError renders note:
description:
PROBLEM
Four call sites in src/activation/native-host.ts (lines 235, 259, 281, 298) call reject(reason, { detail: <explanation> }). DispatchRejectedError's detail object has no 'detail' field — its only free-text field is 'note' (src/activation/types.ts:167-176), and the rendered block is built from note/missing/requestedModel/workspace/holder. Every explanation passed this way is discarded. reject()'s parameter is typed Record<string, unknown>, so the compiler never objected and four sites drifted the same way.

Operator-visible consequence: dispatch a bead marked contract=draft and the refusal reads 'reason: bead_contract_incomplete' with no missing sections and no mention of the word draft, for a bead whose seven sections are all present and correct. evaluateBeadReadiness returns the draft reason with missing: [], reject swallows the reason, and the renderer has nothing to print. That is the least actionable form the gate can take, and the gate exists to make refusals cheap and informative.

Found by the unitAI-rrdnt.32 documentation lane while tracing the refusal path end to end; relayed from unitAI-rrdnt.33, then independently verified in the tree rather than accepted on report.

SUCCESS
A refused dispatch renders its explanation. A draft-contract refusal names the draft state.

SCOPE
The four call sites in src/activation/native-host.ts and a regression test over the rendered message.

NON_GOALS
Does not change DispatchRejectedError's field set or the rendering order. Does not tighten reject()'s parameter type — that is a separate call with its own blast radius.

CONSTRAINTS
The test must assert on the RENDERED message, not on the detail object. A test that checks the object passed to reject would have passed against this defect for as long as it existed, since the object was always correct — it was the rendering that dropped it.

VALIDATION
1. Each of the four refusal paths renders its explanation in the message.
2. A contract=draft bead's refusal message contains the word draft.
3. tsc clean, activation suite green.

OUTPUT
The fix and its regression test.
close_reason: Four call sites moved from detail: to note:. Two regression tests over the RENDERED message, both verified to fail against the reintroduced defect. tsc clean, 16 host tests green.

title: State enforcement status on the epic: closed lease and reconciliation beads are not in force
description:
PROBLEM
The board shows unitAI-rrdnt.21 (workspace writer lease) and unitAI-rrdnt.31 (uncertain workspace reconciliation) both closed and green. A reasonable reader concludes that leasing and reconciliation are in force. Neither is. Verified on the merged tree at 696d3f49: acquire(), release() and admitToolCall() have zero callers in src/; reconcile() has zero callers in src/. Both are harmless only because write-capable activations are refused at admission in src/activation/native-host.ts:199 (writer_not_supported_in_phase_1). A closed bead is the strongest signal this project emits, and two of them currently say something false by implication.

One correction to the framing this bead was requested under, because it changes what the statement must say. workspace-reconcile.ts IS imported by src/tools/specialist/specialist_status.tool.ts, so the READ path is live: projectUncertainWorkspaces() runs on every specialist_status call and would report a genuinely uncertain workspace today. What is unwired is the ENFORCEMENT path — nothing acquires a lease, nothing checks one before a mutation, and nothing calls reconcile(). The statement must distinguish these, or it will read as false to anyone who greps and finds the import.

SUCCESS
A reader arriving at the epic learns, without reading code, that lease enforcement and reconciliation exist, are tested, and are called by nothing; that this is currently safe because writers are refused at admission; and which bead changes it.

SCRUTINY
MEDIUM

Rationale: this is an audit of whether closed enforcement beads are actually in force, so its output is a set of claims about guarantees the system does or does not make. Getting it wrong in the optimistic direction reports a guarantee that is not enforced, which is worse than reporting nothing. It changes no runtime behaviour itself, which is why this is MEDIUM rather than HIGH.

SCOPE
The unitAI-rrdnt epic description, which is the surface people actually read, and docs/design/native-activation-reconciliation.md as the second surface. The statement names: what exists (workspace-lease.ts, workspace-reconcile.ts), what calls it (nothing on the enforcement path; specialist_status calls the read-only projection), why that is currently safe (native-host.ts:199 refuses write-capable activations), and the bead that changes it (unitAI-rrdnt.36, Phase 10).

Add the pattern, not just the incident. Three modules in this epic have reached complete, tested, closed and called by nothing: the workspace lease, reconciliation, and per the coordinator the interaction transport, which had no deliver hook wired and so could not carry a question to a coordinator until it was found. All three passed their own suites. The method that caught every one was grepping for the import, not reading the code. A lane that internalises green does not mean reachable will find the fourth faster than any process will.

NON_GOALS
Does not wire anything. Does not reopen .21 or .31 — both are correctly closed for what they contracted to deliver. Does not add a lint rule, a CI check, or an unused-export detector; if that is wanted it is a separate bead with its own false-positive budget. Does not edit the closed beads' notes.

CONSTRAINTS
The statement must be accurate at the granularity above: enforcement unwired, read projection live. A statement that says reconciliation is entirely uncalled is falsifiable by one grep and will be dismissed along with the warning it carries.
Cite native-host.ts:199 by symbol (writer_not_supported_in_phase_1) as well as line, because the line will move.

VALIDATION
1. The epic description carries the statement; bd show unitAI-rrdnt displays it without opening a file.
2. docs/design/native-activation-reconciliation.md carries the same statement.
3. Each claim in the statement is re-verified against the tree at the time of writing, not copied from this bead: grep for callers of acquire, release, admitToolCall and reconcile in src/, and confirm the admission refusal is still present.
4. unitAI-rrdnt.36 gains a VALIDATION line requiring this statement to be retired when Phase 10 lands, so the warning does not outlive the gap. Same rule the docs lane applied to the .38 holes-table row.

OUTPUT
The enforcement-status statement on both surfaces, and the retirement requirement recorded on unitAI-rrdnt.36.

title: Wire the participant transport to the peer channel so an ask can reach a coordinator
description:
PROBLEM
NativeActivationHost constructed InteractionTransport with no options, so its deliver hook was never supplied and no question a Specialist asked could reach a coordinator over the peer channel. The ask/escalate path (unitAI-rrdnt.22) and the peer transport (unitAI-rrdnt.12/.25) were both complete and both green, and were not joined. Nothing tested the seam because there was none.

SUCCESS
An ask sent through the host's transport is pushed to the configured coordinator, and a reply written to the durable interaction store resolves the blocked request so the Specialist resumes in the same session.

SCOPE
A new src/activation/peer-bridge.ts, the optional peer configuration on NativeActivationHost, and the peerTransportEvent hook on ActivationForensicSink.

NON_GOALS
Not the live end-to-end proof — that is the parent unitAI-rrdnt.30 and it is deliberately not satisfied by this work. Does not change the four delivery-confirmation boundaries. Does not wire the workspace lease.

CONSTRAINTS
The reply must be awaited on the durable store, never on the socket, or a pushed question and a polled question stop being indistinguishable to the Specialist. Delivery must not be claimed without a receipt. The peer channel stays a serialisation of InteractionMessage and never becomes a second vocabulary.

VALIDATION
1. An ask is pushed with the canonical message and the pending ask reads pending, not delivered.
2. An adapter reporting no route at all still resolves the ask from a store reply.
3. finding and completion are pushed but create no outstanding ask.
4. An in-process reply winning the race against a store reply does not produce an unhandled rejection.

OUTPUT
peer-bridge.ts, the host wiring, and its tests.
close_reason: peer-bridge.ts joins InteractionTransport to PeerAdapter; host takes optional peer config. 4 bridge tests, 147 activation tests, tsc clean. Live end-to-end proof remains open on the parent.

title: Phase 14 — Specialist to Claude asynchronous runtime events
description:
PROBLEM
A Specialist can ask its coordinator and block on the answer (Phase 6), and the peer transport can carry a message to a live Claude session (unitAI-rrdnt.12/.25). Nothing yet pushes runtime events — progress, findings, completion — to Claude asynchronously. A coordinator must poll to learn anything, so a long activation is silent until it ends.

SUCCESS
PRD acceptance AY: Claude receives a structured completion notification tied to a validated ActivationResult, and AM/AI lineage holds on every pushed event.

SCOPE
The async event push path on top of the existing PeerAdapter, and the projection of runtime events into InteractionMessage form.

NON_GOALS
Does not change the four delivery-confirmation boundaries. Does not make push authoritative.

CONSTRAINTS
A completion notification is a PROJECTION of a validated ActivationResult, never a substitute for it: a coordinator that received a push and one that polled must reach the same result object. finding and completion have NO confirmation available on this transport and stay sent_unconfirmed permanently by design — do not add a mechanism to 'fix' that. Nothing is lost on undeliverable: durable pending state is written before any send is attempted.

VALIDATION
1. A completion push carries the same ActivationResult the polling path returns, compared field by field, not by summary.
2. With the peer channel unavailable, the completion is still readable through specialist_status and the record does NOT reach delivered.
3. Pushed events carry participant_id, activation_id, attempt_id and pi_session_id.
4. A push attempted before the result is validated is refused.

OUTPUT
The async push path, its tests, and the AY evidence.
notes: Phase 14 complete on xt/phase14-async. RuntimeEventPusher (src/activation/async-events.ts) + MCP wiring (specialist_dispatch tracks route and attaches settle-then-push; specialist_status projects activation_results[]; src/server.ts owns the pusher). native-host.ts unmodified. Live evidence in .xtrm/reports/2026-09-08-unitAI-rrdnt.34-async-events.md: a real completion pushed over the real roster ARRIVED in the target session carrying the serialised ActivationResult, while the record read sent_unconfirmed with no receipt — sent_unconfirmed means unconfirmable, not lost. 8 new tests, one of which asserts the dispatch path actually reaches the push. NOT DONE: no finding/progress push — the only progress source is onSessionEvent inside native-host.ts (not this lane's file); the wakeup lane (unitAI-rrdnt.45) confirmed its forensic sink is the Pi-side seam when a caller appears. title: Phase 12 — documentation for the native activation runtime
description:
PROBLEM
The native activation runtime has no operator-facing or developer-facing documentation. /using-specialists documents the sp CLI path only. A coordinator cannot currently learn from the docs when a native activation is the right tool, what a Bead must contain before dispatch, what the writer lease means for them, or how a clarification differs from a restart.

SUCCESS
PRD acceptance AR, AS, AT and AU. AR: an operator can run a native Specialist from the documentation alone. AS: lease behaviour is understood from the docs without reading the source. AT: the docs make clear when a worktree is NOT needed. AU: the difference between a validated ActivationResult and a message is stated, because conflating them is the failure this runtime was built to prevent.

SCOPE
The /using-specialists skill, tool descriptions on the specialist_* MCP tools, docstrings on the public activation surface, and operator and developer docs under docs/.

NON_GOALS
Does not restate the PRD. Does not document unshipped phases as though they shipped. Does not duplicate what a docstring already says into prose.

CONSTRAINTS
Every documented behaviour must be verified against the current tree, not against the PRD. Several PRD statements have already been falsified by measurement (procStart formats, receipt premise, the executeBash veto hole) — documentation that repeats a design intention the code does not implement is worse than no documentation. Where a hole is known and unclosed, say so plainly and name the bead.

VALIDATION
1. A reader following the docs alone dispatches a native Specialist successfully.
2. Every command and flag in the docs is executed and its output matches what is written.
3. The lease section states what happens on contention, on uncertainty, and on the known bypass, with bead references.
4. No documented claim contradicts a test in the repo.

OUTPUT
Updated skill, tool descriptions, docstrings and docs, with the verification transcript recorded on the bead.

title: Phase 13 — expose the native activation runtime through MCP, no CLI shell-out
description:
PROBLEM
Claude Code can only obtain a Specialist today by shelling out to sp run in a terminal or an xt session. The native activation runtime exists in-process but is not reachable over MCP, so the coordinator that is best placed to use it is the one that cannot.

SUCCESS
PRD acceptance AV and AW. AV: Claude Code launches a real Pi Specialist without sp run. AW: it does so without needing a separate terminal or xt session.

SCOPE
src/tools/specialist/** and src/server.ts. The MCP tool surface for dispatch, status and reply, backed by NativeActivationHost.

NON_GOALS
Does not implement the async push channel (Phase 14) or the roster adapter (Phase 15, largely landed as unitAI-rrdnt.12/.25). Does not add a second message vocabulary — MCP is a serialisation of InteractionMessage (PRD invariant BH), never a parallel protocol.

CONSTRAINTS
No shelling out to the CLI, including internally: a subprocess that runs sp satisfies the letter and defeats the purpose. The Bead gate, the StepContract compilation and the writer lease apply identically to an MCP-dispatched activation — a second dispatch path that skips a gate is how gates die. src/activation/native-host.ts is owned by the coordinator session; propose changes there rather than making them.

VALIDATION
1. A Specialist is dispatched from Claude Code over MCP with no sp process spawned; assert on the process table, not on intent.
2. A draft-contract Bead is REFUSED by the MCP path exactly as by the CLI path.
3. An MCP-dispatched writer takes the same lease and is fenced by the same rules (acceptance BA).

title: Phase 9 — uncertain workspace recovery and reconciliation
description:
PROBLEM
The workspace writer lease (unitAI-rrdnt.21) already produces the uncertain state and four uncertainReason values, and release THROWS rather than guessing when a lease is uncertain. Nothing yet reconciles an uncertain workspace. A writer that disappears mid-mutation therefore leaves a workspace that is correctly not-silently-free but also permanently unusable, which converts a safety property into a liveness bug.

SUCCESS
PRD acceptance AB and AC. AB: a writer disappearing during an unresolved mutation leaves the workspace uncertain, never silently free. AC: an uncertain workspace can be reconciled from durable evidence, and reconciliation is a decision an operator or the runtime records, never an inference from absence.

SCOPE
src/activation/workspace-lease.ts and a new reconciliation path beside it. The forensic evidence a reconciliation reads and the evidence it writes. Surfacing uncertain workspaces through specialist_status.

NON_GOALS
Does not change lease acquisition or the linkSync publish. Does not close the pi.exec/executeBash veto hole (unitAI-rrdnt.6) — reconciliation must work in a world where that hole exists.

CONSTRAINTS
Absence of a process is NOT evidence a mutation completed or did not. Liveness is /proc/<pid> plus procStart, never a self-reported status and never socket existence. Reconciliation must distinguish the four uncertainReason values rather than collapsing them: they were separated because they have different safe actions. A reconciliation that can silently free a workspace reintroduces exactly the failure the uncertain state exists to prevent.

VALIDATION
1. A writer killed with SIGKILL mid-mutation leaves state uncertain with the correct uncertainReason; assert the reason, not just the state.
2. Reconciliation of that workspace succeeds and records durable forensic evidence naming what it decided and on what basis.
3. Reconciliation REFUSES when evidence is insufficient, and the refusal is readable through specialist_status rather than thrown away.
4. A live writer's workspace can never be reconciled out from under it.

OUTPUT
The reconciliation path, its forensic events, its tests, and the specialist_status surface for uncertain workspaces.
notes:
PHASE 9 COMPLETE — library + status surface. Branch xt/phase9-recovery, not pushed, no PR (coordinator dawid-0b merges).

DELIVERED
- src/activation/workspace-reconcile.ts (new). reconcile() validates a proposed outcome against the live lease re-inspected at decision time. PRD 59 outcomes verbatim: safe_free | recovered_holder | superseded | manual_attention_required.
- src/activation/workspace-lease.ts: leasePath() exported. No other change; acquisition and the linkSync publish are untouched per NON_GOALS.
- src/tools/specialist/specialist_status.tool.ts: new top-level uncertain_workspaces key.
- tests/unit/specialist/activation-workspace-reconcile.test.ts: 19 tests, all passing.

DECISION MODEL
Reconciliation is a proposal, not an inference. Caller supplies {outcome, decidedBy, basis[]}. Empty basis[] is insufficient evidence for every outcome. recovered_holder is computed, never proposed, so a caller cannot assert that a holder came back. Permitted outcomes per uncertainReason, deliberately not collapsed: holder_process_gone and holder_start_mismatch -> safe_free/superseded/manual; unreadable_record -> superseded/manual only; liveness_unverifiable -> manual ONLY. safe_free and superseded both free the lease file and differ in what is asserted; neither publishes a successor lease.

EVIDENCE
Durable: append-only <key>.reconcile.jsonl beside the lease, one line per attempt including refusals. Forensic: lease_reconciled on an applied decision, lease_uncertain on a refusal, through the existing ActivationForensicSink. A sink that throws never changes an outcome.

VALIDATION AS RUN
1. Real SIGKILL, real /proc probe: a bun child acquired a real lease, was asserted held while alive, was SIGKILLed, /proc entry confirmed absent, and inspect() then returned uncertain with uncertainReason holder_process_gone. The reason is asserted, not just the state.
2. Reconciliation of that same real crash applied safe_free and wrote the durable record.
3. Refusals asserted for empty basis, for liveness_unverifiable, and for safe_free on unreadable_record; each refusal is readable through projectUncertainWorkspaces.
4. A live holder yields recovered_holder and the lease file is untouched.
Live probe beyond the suite: createSpecialistStatusTool(...).execute({}) run in a real git repo after a real killed holder returned the uncertain_workspaces row. Keys observed: loaded_count, pending_interactions, uncertain_workspaces, backends_health, specialists, background_jobs.
bun run lint clean. 44 tests pass across the three activation lease/status files. dist rebuilt and committed.

SCOPE HONESTY — READ THIS BEFORE ASSUMING RECONCILIATION IS IN FORCE
workspace-lease.ts is imported by nothing in src/ except this new module and its own test. Writers are refused outright at native-host.ts:196-198, so no workspace is leased and therefore none can become uncertain in production today. This bead's reconciliation is correct and unwired, exactly like the lease it resolves. Wiring is unitAI-rrdnt.36 (Phase 10). Closing this bead does not mean uncertain workspaces are being reconciled at runtime.

HOST CALL SITES REQUESTED FROM THE COORDINATOR (native-host.ts is not mine)
None are required for this bead. reconcile() is operator/runtime-initiated and deliberately has no automatic trigger: an automatic call on teardown would be the inference from absence this module exists to prevent. If Phase 10 wants a trigger, the correct one is to emit lease_uncertain when release() throws, and to leave the resolution to an operator reading specialist_status.

GITNEXUS detect_changes: risk_level high, driven by name-collision fan-out on the generic symbol execute across 11 unrelated flows. The actual edit to specialist_status.tool.ts adds one key and changes no existing behaviour.
close_reason: Phase 9 uncertain workspace reconciliation: reconcile() as a validated proposal, four uncertainReason values with distinct permitted outcomes, append-only durable evidence, lease_reconciled/lease_uncertain forensics, and an uncertain_workspaces surface on specialist_status. 19 tests including a real SIGKILL against the real /proc probe. Correct and unwired — the lease itself is not yet called from src/, wiring is unitAI-rrdnt.36.

title: Prove AX end to end: a real Specialist push confirmed by a real reply
description:
PROBLEM
The reply-based delivery criterion is implemented and unit-tested, and the inbound path is confirmed by a live coordinator, but no Specialist has yet asked a question over the peer channel and been resumed by a real reply. unitAI-rrdnt.22 (Phase 6 ask/escalate) and unitAI-rrdnt.25 (registration and reply-as-delivery) are both closed, so nothing open tracks the end-to-end proof. Marking the criterion superseded was correct; marking it met is not, and the gap between those two is exactly the finding that produced the fourth boundary.

SUCCESS
A Specialist running under NativeActivationHost pushes a question to a busy Claude coordinator, that coordinator replies, the reply is correlated by inReplyTo, the pending record moves from sent_unconfirmed to delivered, and the child resumes in the same session. Acceptance AX, observed rather than inferred.

SCRUTINY
HIGH

Rationale: this bead's own CONSTRAINTS record that THREE separate claims about this transport were falsified by live probes after passing on inspection — the procStart format, the receipt premise, and the prior-state boundary on reply confirmation. The receipt premise has since failed a fourth time (unitAI-rrdnt.45: attemptDelivery returned true with no deliver hook, so a pending record reached 'delivered' with no receiver). A path with that record does not get a routine review.

SCOPE
Wiring the existing pieces and running the observation. All parts exist: PeerAdapter.ask() and the reply-as-delivery boundaries (src/activation/transport/), registration (peer-registration.ts), and the ask/escalate path on a live AgentSession (ask-tool.ts, native-host.ts).

NON_GOALS
No new transport. No change to the four confirmation boundaries without evidence that one of them is wrong.

CONSTRAINTS
The proof must be a live coordinator, not a fixture. Three separate claims about this transport have now been falsified by live probes after passing on inspection or on a reading of pi-claude-link: the procStart format, the receipt premise, and the prior-state boundary on reply confirmation. pi-claude-link is evidence of what pi-claude-link sends, never a specification of what Claude Code sends. Do not close on a green unit test.

VALIDATION
1. A pending record for a question reaches delivered against a reply carrying inReplyTo equal to its message id.
2. The Specialist resumes on that reply in the same session.
3. AY: a completion notification tied to a validated ActivationResult.
4. With the peer channel unavailable, the same question is still answerable through specialist_status and the record does NOT reach delivered.

OUTPUT
Observed evidence of AX and AY, and whichever of the four boundaries the observation changes, if any.
notes:
Coordinator note 2026-09-08: NOT satisfied by the pi-extension lane's AX proof. That proof ran over the Pi extension with a pi coordinator and the in-process ask tool; .30 requires the PEER channel with a live Claude coordinator and the inReplyTo correlation. Different path, different evidence.

Now blocked on .45 for a concrete reason: the wakeup lane measured that InteractionTransport.attemptDelivery returned true whenever no deliver hook was wired, so a pending record went straight to 'delivered' without any receipt. .30's VALIDATION 1 asks for a record that reaches delivered AGAINST a reply carrying inReplyTo — which cannot be distinguished from the bug's behaviour until the fix lands. Proving .30 on the current code would prove nothing.

This is the fourth falsified-claim entry for this transport, and it fits the bead's own CONSTRAINTS: three prior claims passed on inspection and failed live. The receipt premise has now failed twice.

title: Add ActivationForensicSink.sessionEvent hook for raw Pi session events
description:
PROBLEM
The Phase 7 observability parity lane (unitAI-rrdnt.20) needs raw Pi AgentSession events to reach the shared forensic pipeline so that turn, message, tool, retry and compaction timeline rows are produced by the same mappers the legacy sp run path uses. NativeActivationHost.onSessionEvent currently translates a handful of event types into hand-written forensic names and discards the rest, so the raw stream never reaches mapCallbackEventToTimelineEvent. That lane owns src/specialist/** and forensic-sink.ts but not native-host.ts, so it cannot add the seam itself and is blocked.

SUCCESS
Every raw Pi session event is offered to the forensic sink, so the Phase 7 mapper can produce timeline rows at parity with the legacy runner, while the existing translated events continue to be produced exactly as before.

SCOPE
src/activation/native-host.ts only: add an optional sessionEvent method to ActivationForensicSink and call it at the top of onSessionEvent for every raw event, carrying activation identity, pi session id, workspace path and the event itself.

NON_GOALS
Does not implement the mapping -- that is unitAI-rrdnt.20 and belongs to the Phase 7 lane. Does not change the existing translated emit() calls or their names. Does not add a callback through NativeActivationHostDeps; the hook is a method on the sink that already exists.

CONSTRAINTS
sessionEvent must be OPTIONAL so every existing sink, including the null sink and all test doubles, keeps compiling and working untouched. The sink swallows its own errors, so the host must not wrap the call in try/catch and must not let a forensic concern alter activation behaviour. The raw hook must not duplicate what the translated path already emits: raw events feed the timeline mappers, while the existing emit() names remain the sole producers of their own rows.

VALIDATION
1. Every raw session event reaches sessionEvent, including types the switch does not translate.
2. A sink without sessionEvent still works -- no crash, no behaviour change.
3. Existing native host tests pass unchanged.

OUTPUT
Hook plus tests.

SCRUTINY
LOW -- additive seam on an existing interface, but it unblocks a HIGH-scrutiny lane.
close_reason: ActivationForensicSink gained an optional sessionEvent(input) offering every RAW Pi session event with full activation identity, fired at the top of onSessionEvent before any translation. Unblocks the Phase 7 parity lane, which owns the mapping but not native-host.ts. Optional so the null sink and every test double keep working; not wrapped in try/catch because the sink swallows its own errors and a forensic concern must not alter activation behaviour nor be hidden by a catch. Tested that an untranslated event type still reaches the hook, that identity is carried, and that a sink without the method is unaffected.

title: Register the activation runtime as a Claude peer so pushes can be confirmed — needs a user ruling
description:
PROBLEM
Measured on 2026-09-07 during unitAI-rrdnt.12: the Claude cross-session peer channel DELIVERS a frame to a live coordinator without any sender registration, but returns no peer_message_status receipt to an unregistered sender. A frame written from the adapter to pid 3574376 arrived and rendered normally in that session (confirmed by asking the coordinator), and no receipt naming the message id came back within 15s to a correctly colocated /run/user/1000/cc-socks socket. pi-claude-link always calls registerPeer() before sending. Without a receipt the adapter can never mark a push delivered, so acceptance AX cannot be satisfied over the peer channel.

SUCCESS
Either the runtime registers itself as a peer and receipts are observed end to end, or the user declines and AX is formally reassigned to the polling path. Both are acceptable outcomes; an unrecorded decision is not.

SCOPE
Whether the activation runtime may write ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json and bind a colocated socket, its lifecycle (deregistration on exit, orphan cleanup), and the resulting update to docs/design/claude-transport-decision.md.

NON_GOALS
Does not change the adapter's degraded behaviour, which is already correct and tested.

CONSTRAINTS
Registration writes a file into the user's home directory and adds an entry to every other session's roster. That is a side effect on the user's environment and is the user's call, not an implementation detail an agent decides. The measured facts in claude-transport-decision.md section 4 apply to any entry this runtime writes: procStart is mandatory and both formats are in use.

VALIDATION
A push from the runtime to a live coordinator records delivery state 'delivered' against a receipt naming its own message id.

OUTPUT
A ruling, and either the registration path or a documented reassignment of AX.
notes:
FINDING 2026-09-07, peeradapter lane: the premise this ruling was granted on is FALSIFIED. Registration was implemented exactly as approved (numeric procStart, peerProtocol 1, colocated 0600 socket, from: uds:<sock> matching pi-claude-link byte for byte) and a push to a live coordinator was held open for 180s. No peer_message_status frame ever arrived. Registered produced the identical result to unregistered. Root cause: receiptFrame is referenced in exactly one place in pi-claude-link's index.ts (line 100), where it SENDS a receipt to an inbound sender; nothing in that codebase ever receives or awaits one. The receipt is what a non-Claude peer emits so a Claude sender's own delivered-UI resolves — it is not something Claude Code emits to us. The protocol header comment claiming 'Claude sends us delivery/hold receipts' was never exercised by the code it sits in. VALIDATION CRITERION AS WRITTEN IS NOT SATISFIABLE on Claude Code 2.1.263. Conditions 1 and 2 of the approval ARE met and proven independently: deregistration verified against real processes on normal exit and SIGTERM with nothing left on disk, and cleanup scoped to our own version marker (skipped all 19 foreign entries on the real roster, refused to remove a live entry of ours). PROPOSED REDIRECTION, needs the operator: registration's real value is addressability — the inbound path by which a coordinator sends TO the runtime, i.e. the reply path. A reply carrying inReplyTo is a STRICTLY STRONGER proof of delivery than a receipt: a receipt says the wire accepted the frame, a reply proves a coordinator read and answered it. AX is defined as 'Specialist asks, busy coordinator receives, replies, child resumes', so the reply is the acceptance criterion and the receipt was only ever a proxy for it. Recommend marking delivered on a correlated reply as well as on a receipt. An inbound-frame probe was run but no peer sent to it inside the window, so the inbound path is UNCONFIRMED and must be proven before this redirection is accepted.
RULING 2026-09-07 (RESTORED — I overwrote this with --notes; original text recovered from the bead as read earlier this session): the operator APPROVED peer registration, verbatim: 'yes it can, i do approve.' This is genuine user input recorded at the time of the decision, not an agent inference. Approved scope: the activation runtime may write ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json and bind a colocated socket so receipts return and a push can honestly be marked delivered. Approval was given ON THE CONDITIONS raised by the peeradapter lane and both are binding: (1) deregistration on exit, including abnormal exit as far as reasonably coverable; (2) orphan cleanup, because the measured baseline is 128 socket files for 20 registrations and approval was given on the understanding this does not worsen that ratio. Implementation assigned to the peeradapter lane, which owns src/activation/transport/**. The doc update to claude-transport-decision.md section 5 is the coordinator's. NOTE: the approval's stated purpose (receipts) is falsified by the finding recorded above this line; the conditions attached to it are met regardless.
INBOUND CONFIRMED 2026-09-07: a real SendMessage from a live Claude coordinator arrived on a registered 0600 colocated socket as a type:'user' frame wrapping the standard cross-session-message envelope (which additionally carries a hop-chain attribute that pi-claude-link's buildEnvelope does not emit). Registration therefore delivers addressability and the reply path, which is what it is worth keeping for. title: Correct claude-transport-decision.md: procStart has two formats, and steer is receiver-side
description:
PROBLEM
docs/design/claude-transport-decision.md carries three statements that live measurement has since contradicted or extended, and an adapter built literally to the current text fails.

1. Section 4 documents procStart as the ps-style string form ("Mon Sep  7 11:10:29 2026"). Measured across all 18 registrations on this host, 13 of them -- every one written by Claude Code itself (2.1.257 / 2.1.263) -- carry procStart as a NUMBER, raw field 22 of /proc/<pid>/stat, ticks since boot, verified by exact equality for pids 1100092, 2176609, 3574376 and 404065. Only the 5 pi-claude-link entries use the string. The section generalised from a sample that excluded every registration Claude Code writes. An implementation following it literally rejected 13 of 18 live sessions as missing_proc_start, which would have refused to route to every native Claude coordinator and looked like "the peer channel does not work" rather than "the liveness check is wrong".

2. Section 3 lists "idle sendUserMessage versus busy steer" as adapter behaviour. It is not a sender-side choice. pi-claude-link/index.ts:91 picks deliverAs steer for its OWN agent when IT is busy -- the RECEIVER injecting an inbound message into its current turn. Every outbound frame carries the default priority next. A sender that tried to choose would have to branch on the registration's self-reported status, which section 4 itself measures as unreliable.

3. Delivery and receipt are separable and were not distinguished. A live probe sent by a non-SendMessage adapter frame ARRIVED in the coordinator session, while no peer_message_status receipt returned to the sender's own colocated socket within 15s. So raw delivery works without registration, but confirmation does not.

SUCCESS
The decision record states what was measured rather than what was inferred from a partial sample, and an implementer following it does not build a liveness check that rejects most live sessions.

SCOPE
docs/design/claude-transport-decision.md sections 3, 4 and 5. Record both procStart forms with the numeric one as the stronger exact-integer check; move the steer behaviour to the receiver and say why a sender cannot choose; and separate delivery from receipt, recording that confirmation appears to require the sender to hold a registration.

NON_GOALS
Does not decide whether the runtime should register itself as a peer -- that writes to the user's environment and is the operator's call. Does not change the transport assignment, which stands. Does not touch src/activation/transport/**, which the peeradapter lane owns.

CONSTRAINTS
Every corrected claim must name how it was measured, including counts, so the next reader can tell measurement from inference -- that distinction is what the original section 4 lost. Do not weaken the liveness rule itself: /proc plus a start-time guard stays mandatory, and the registration's self-reported status stays banned as a liveness signal.

VALIDATION
1. Section 4 documents both procStart forms and the count behind each.
2. Section 3 attributes steer to the receiver.
3. The delivery-versus-receipt distinction is stated with the probe result behind it.

OUTPUT
Corrected decision record.

SCRUTINY
MEDIUM -- a design document that reads as measured when it was partly inferred is how the next lane builds the wrong thing confidently.
close_reason: Corrected claude-transport-decision.md sections 3, 4 and 5 from live measurement. Section 4 documents both procStart formats with counts (13 numeric from Claude Code itself, 5 string from pi-claude-link) and prefers the numeric exact-integer check; the prior text generalised from a sample excluding every registration Claude Code writes, and an adapter following it rejected 13 of 18 live sessions. Section 3 attributes steer to the receiver. Section 5 separates delivery from confirmation: a frame from an unregistered sender arrived in my session while no receipt returned, so acceptance AX requires peer self-registration -- a side effect on the user's environment, left explicitly as the operator's decision.

title: Phase 6 — clarification and escalation on a live AgentSession
description:
PROBLEM
PRD Phase 5 landed InteractionMessage and the participant transport (src/activation/interaction.ts, unitAI-rrdnt.19), but nothing connects it to a running Specialist. A child cannot actually ask its parent anything: NativeActivationHost has no tool the model can call to raise a question, no path from an answer back into the same AgentSession, and no state transition when an ask is outstanding. PRD Phase 6 requires both flows proven end to end -- child asks, child waits, parent replies, the SAME AgentSession resumes; and child escalates, remains alive, someone resolves it, the child resumes.

SUCCESS
A running Specialist raises a question through a tool, its activation moves to needs_reply and the session is not disposed, the parent answers, and the SAME AgentSession continues with the answer in context. The escalation flow behaves identically except the activation moves to escalated.

SCOPE
PRD Phase 6. Wire src/activation/interaction.ts into NativeActivationHost: a custom tool the child calls to ask or escalate, the state transition onto ActivationState, answer delivery back into the live session, and the forensic events for ask, answer and resume. Reuse InteractionTransport.impliedState for the state mapping rather than deriving state a second time.

NON_GOALS
Does NOT implement any out-of-process transport -- the parent here is in-process, and MCP/peer delivery is unitAI-rrdnt.12. Does not add message kinds beyond the existing InteractionKind enum. Does not implement the writer lease or uncertain recovery. Does not build a UI.

CONSTRAINTS
Asking must NOT kill the child (PRD invariant 7): the session stays alive and resumable while a question is outstanding, and answering continues the SAME AgentSession rather than starting a new one -- a new session would lose the child's context and turn a clarification into a restart. Correlation stays by inReplyTo, never positional. The custom tool must be admitted through the existing fail-closed tool contract, not by widening the allowlist for everyone: a read-only Specialist gains the ask tool without gaining any mutation capability. Reuse the existing forensic sink; no new event vocabulary and no second store.

VALIDATION
1. Child asks, activation reads needs_reply, session is NOT disposed, parent replies, the same pi session id continues and the answer reaches the model.
2. Child escalates, activation reads escalated, the child stays alive, resolution resumes it.
3. Two outstanding asks from one child are answered out of order and each answer reaches the request that asked it.
4. A read-only Specialist can ask without gaining any mutation tool.

OUTPUT
Ask/escalate tool, host wiring, state transitions, forensics, tests.

SCRUTINY
HIGH -- the failure mode is a clarification that silently restarts the child instead of resuming it, which looks like success and destroys the child's context.
close_reason: PRD Phase 6 landed. src/activation/ask-tool.ts provides ask_coordinator and escalate_to_coordinator as CUSTOM tools wired into NativeActivationHost, plus host-side answer(messageId, body) and pendingAsks(). The child asks from inside a blocking tool call and the answer returns as that call's result, so the SAME AgentSession continues with its context intact rather than being restarted. Validation: the child suspends inside the call and is neither finished nor disposed; escalation moves the activation to escalated and resolving resumes it; two outstanding asks answered OUT OF ORDER each resolve to the request that asked them, so correlation cannot be positional; attempt_id is read at call time so a resumed activation attributes correctly; a read-only Specialist gains the ask tools without any mutation capability; an empty question is refused rather than asked. 17 tests across the clarification and host suites. Acceptances AX and AY are now testable against the peer adapter's ask()/push() seams -- not yet run end to end with a live model, which is the remaining gap.

title: Phase 8 — workspace writer lease store and mutation admission
description:
PROBLEM
NativeActivationHost refuses every write-capable Specialist with writer_not_supported_in_phase_1 because no lease exists. Nothing in this codebase implements workspace exclusion: src/cli/console previously displayed a lease that was a hardcoded placeholder (removed in unitAI-rrdnt.4), and worktree_owner_job_id is chain provenance for --job reuse, not an exclusion primitive. Until a lease exists, no native Specialist can mutate a workspace, which blocks PRD Phase 10 writer parity and leaves the coordinator itself unfenced.

SUCCESS
Exactly one writer holds a given mutable workspace at a time, the coordinator included. A second writer is refused with a structured rejection naming the holder. A crashed holder leaves the lease uncertain rather than free. A resumed activation reacquires its own lease rather than colliding with itself.

SCOPE
PRD Phase 8: workspace identity, mutation classification, the lease store, atomic acquire, release, parent fencing, second-writer failure and resume reacquisition. Deliver as a self-contained module under src/activation/ (suggested src/activation/workspace-lease.ts) plus tests. Workspace identity already exists as WorkspaceIdentity in src/activation/types.ts and mutation authority as WorkspaceAccess derived from the resolved capability grant -- reuse both, do not redefine them.

NON_GOALS
Does NOT wire the lease into NativeActivationHost. src/activation/native-host.ts is owned by the coordinator this round and the wiring is a separate step; deliver the module and a written description of the wiring you need. Does not implement uncertain recovery (PRD Phase 9) beyond producing the uncertain state. Does not implement writer Specialist parity (Phase 10). Does not auto-provision worktrees -- the PRD is explicit that a writer does not get a new one.

CONSTRAINTS
The worktree path is the mutation domain: two linked git worktrees sharing one common repo are DISTINCT mutable workspaces even though they share history and one observability database. Acquisition must be atomic against a concurrent acquirer in another process, so it cannot be a plain read-then-write on a JSON file. A crashed holder must yield uncertain, never a blind free -- releasing a lease whose holder's liveness is unknown is how two writers end up in one worktree. Liveness must be established by process existence plus a start-time guard, never by the holder's own self-reported status and never by the presence of a file; this is the same lesson recorded in the claude-peer-transport-liveness memory, where 10 of 20 registrations advertised status idle while naming dead PIDs. A resume reacquires the SAME lease for the same activation_id rather than contending with itself. observability.db stays the single store; a lease state file is acceptable but must not become a second forensic database.

REFERENCES
Read docs/design/native-activation-reconciliation.md section 5.8 before designing the guard. It is now re-verified against Pi 0.85.1 (unitAI-rrdnt.17) and the finding is decisive: the tool_call veto covers all LLM-initiated tool paths, but AgentSession.executeBash() and pi.exec() bypass it entirely with the handler firing ZERO times, and no 0.85.1 option closes this. The lease is therefore enforceable against the model but NOT against a trusted extension or against our own host code calling executeBash. Design to that reality and state the residual hole explicitly rather than implying total enforcement. Related beads: unitAI-rrdnt.6 (the bypass) and unitAI-rrdnt.7 (the guard must be a per-tool-call block, not setActiveTools -- confirmed, because all tool_call handlers in a batch fire before any execution, so a mid-batch block IS enforceable, whereas revoking active tools cannot cancel an already-planned call).

VALIDATION
1. Two concurrent acquirers on one workspace: exactly one succeeds, the loser is refused with the holder named.
2. Two linked worktrees of one repository are independently leasable.
3. A holder whose process is gone leaves the lease uncertain, not free, and a test proves the uncertain state is reachable without killing a real process.
4. Resume by the same activation_id reacquires rather than being refused.
5. The residual enforcement hole is documented in the module, not merely known.

OUTPUT
Lease module, tests, and a written wiring note for the coordinator.

SCRUTINY
HIGH -- this primitive is what makes concurrent writers safe. A lease that frees on uncertainty is worse than no lease, because it grants confidence that is not warranted.
close_reason:
Workspace writer lease delivered as src/activation/workspace-lease.ts plus tests and an in-module wiring note. All five validation criteria met.

1. Two concurrent acquirers: exactly one succeeds, the loser gets a DispatchRejectedError naming the holder. Proven by eight real processes contending under a tight file-existence barrier, repeated over four rounds.
2. Two linked worktrees of one repository are independently leasable; the key is the resolved worktree path, so they share a lease directory but not a lease.
3. A holder whose process is gone yields uncertain, not free, and the uncertain state is reachable in a test through an injected probe without killing a real process. Four distinct uncertain causes are distinguished: holder_process_gone, holder_start_mismatch, liveness_unverifiable, unreadable_record. Acquiring or releasing an uncertain lease is refused outright.
4. Resume by the same activation_id reacquires, advancing only the attempt.
5. The residual enforcement hole (H1-H4 from reconciliation section 5.8) is stated in the module header, including that H3 and H4 are unsatisfiable on Pi 0.85.1.

Atomicity is link(), which publishes a fully written record or fails EEXIST — not a read-then-write. Liveness is process existence plus a /proc stat field 22 start-time guard, never a self-reported status and never file presence. Mutation admission is a per-call block with a non-mutating allowlist, so an unrecognised tool is treated as mutating (fail closed, per PRD section 54); setActiveToolsByName is explicitly rejected as the fence per section 5.9.

Testing note worth carrying: the first version of the concurrency test used a wall-clock barrier and passed identically against a deliberately broken read-then-write implementation. It was rebuilt after mutation-testing it; the measured numbers are in the test comment so it is not simplified back into something meaningless. Memory key concurrency-test-barrier-must-discriminate.

NOT DONE, by contract: no wiring into native-host.ts (coordinator lane owns it; the four call sites are documented in the module header), no Phase 9 uncertain recovery, no Phase 10 writer parity, no worktree auto-provisioning.

118 activation tests green; tsc clean.

title: Phase 7 — observability parity for native activations
description:
PROBLEM
Native activations emit a small hand-written event set from NativeActivationHost via src/activation/forensic-sink.ts, while legacy sp run activations flow through the full shared pipeline -- mapCallbackEventToTimelineEvent, the timeline factories, appendEvent and the forensic writers. The two are not at parity: a native activation produces fewer event kinds, does not populate the timeline tables the console and sp log read, and now that unitAI-rrdnt.2 has landed it does not populate attempt_id, pi_session_id or workspace_id on its rows. The consequence is that the same question asked of a native child and a legacy child returns different answers.

SUCCESS
A native activation is answerable by exactly the same queries as a legacy one. Its AgentSession events flow through the shared forensic pipeline rather than a parallel hand-written path, and its rows carry the full v15 identity lineage.

SCOPE

Populate the v15 identity columns from the activation's own identity. Verify against observability.db that native and legacy rows are queryable together.

NON_GOALS
Does not change the legacy sp run path. Does not add event kinds beyond parity. Does not create a telemetry side database -- observability.db stays the single store. Does not alter the v15 schema; that landed in unitAI-rrdnt.2.

Reuse createForensicEvent, appendForensicEvent, appendEvent and the existing timeline factories -- a second forensic model is the specific thing this bead removes. Native rows must carry attempt_id, pi_session_id and workspace_id per the v15 identity model, and participant_id must use the canonical specialist::<role> derivation. Tests must not touch the repository's own observability.db; isolation is enforced centrally by tests/setup/isolate-observability.ts and must not be bypassed.

2. Native rows carry attempt_id, pi_session_id and workspace_id.
3. The event kinds a native activation produces match the legacy set where the concepts correspond, and every intentional gap is named.

Pipeline wiring, identity population, parity tests.
