title: Phase 5 — direct participant transport and InteractionMessage
description:
PROBLEM
A native Specialist cannot say anything to its parent except by finishing. There is no message type, no addressing, no correlation between a question and its answer, and no notion of a pending ask. PRD Phase 5 requires InteractionMessage, direct parent/child transport, message ids, reply correlation, send, a blocking request, pending asks and attention -- and Phase 6 (clarification and escalation) cannot exist without it.

SUCCESS
A parent can send to a child and a child to its parent, each message carries a stable id, a reply is correlated to the request that caused it, a blocking request suspends the asker without killing the child, and unanswered asks are enumerable as pending with an attention signal.

SCOPE
PRD Phase 5, in src/activation/. The InteractionMessage type and its identity fields, the in-process parent/child transport, correlation, send, blocking request, the pending-ask set and attention state. Identity fields must use the canonical lineage landed in unitAI-rrdnt.2: participant_id, activation_id, attempt_id.

NON_GOALS
Does not implement the Claude peer channel or MCP serialisation -- those are unitAI-rrdnt.12 and Phase 13/14, and this bead defines the semantics both must normalise to. Does not implement clarification or escalation behaviour (Phase 6). Does not add a second durable store; pending asks are runtime state projected into observability, not a new database.

CONSTRAINTS
One semantic participant protocol (PRD invariant BH): whatever a future transport serialises, it serialises THIS type -- a second message vocabulary is the failure this bead exists to prevent. A completion notification remains a projection of a validated ActivationResult and never a substitute for it. A question must not kill the child (invariant 7): asking suspends, it does not terminate. No silent message loss (PRD section 30): an undelivered message degrades to readable pending state.

VALIDATION
1. A reply is correlated to its request by id, proven with two concurrent outstanding asks so correlation cannot be faked by ordering.
2. A blocking request suspends the asker and the child stays alive and resumable.
3. Pending asks are enumerable and surface an attention signal.
4. Message identity carries participant_id, activation_id and attempt_id.

OUTPUT
InteractionMessage, transport, correlation, pending asks, tests.

SCRUTINY
HIGH -- this type is the contract two future transports must both satisfy; getting it wrong forces a second vocabulary later.
close_reason: PRD Phase 5 landed at src/activation/interaction.ts: InteractionMessage carrying all three lineage layers, the in-process participant transport, id-based correlation, send, blocking request, pending asks and attention, plus an impliedState projection for the Fleet. 12 tests. Validation met: correlation proven with TWO concurrent outstanding asks answered out of order so ordering cannot fake it; a blocking request suspends the asker while the child stays alive; pending asks enumerate oldest-first with attention raised only for the addressee; identity carries participant_id, activation_id and attempt_id. Building it found a real race — request() registered its waiter AFTER the send, so a reply that outran the send resolved into no waiter and the asker blocked forever. The waiter is now registered against a pre-allocated id before the send, with a late-reply fallback. Deliberately excludes any out-of-process transport, persistence, or authorisation; those are unitAI-rrdnt.12 and PRD Phase 13/14, which now consume this type.

title: Re-baseline the native activation runtime from Pi 0.84.3 to 0.85.1
description:
PROBLEM
Every empirical claim behind the native activation runtime was established against @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent 0.84.3. The operator has installed 0.85.1 and wants it as the baseline going forward. 13 places still assert 0.84.3 as the inspected surface: docs/design/native-activation-reconciliation.md (11, including the 5.7 verdict "implement against the installed 0.84.3 surface" and the 5.8 conclusion that PRD section 54 is partially unsatisfiable), src/activation/model-gate.ts:9, and tests/unit/specialist/activation-model-gate.test.ts:6. Leaving them stale means the next reader cannot tell which findings were re-verified and which are inherited assumptions.

SUCCESS
Documentation and code comments state 0.85.1 as the verified baseline, every claim they carry has been re-confirmed against it or explicitly marked as unverified, and any finding that CHANGED between versions is corrected rather than silently left standing.

SCOPE
Fold the results of the 0.85.1 re-verification probe into docs/design/native-activation-reconciliation.md (sections 5.7, 5.8, 5.16, 7 and the header), src/activation/model-gate.ts and tests/unit/specialist/activation-model-gate.test.ts. Correct any claim the probe refutes. Record the version delta explicitly so a future upgrade has a precedent to follow.

NON_GOALS
Does not add a hard dependency on the pi package -- runtime resolution via src/activation/pi-sdk.ts stays. Does not pin a version anywhere in package.json. Does not re-run the Phase 0 research from scratch; only claims that depend on runtime behaviour are re-verified.

CONSTRAINTS
Do not update a version string without re-verifying the claim attached to it -- a document that says 0.85.1 while carrying unverified 0.84.3 findings is worse than one that honestly says 0.84.3. Where a claim could not be re-verified, say so at the claim rather than in a footnote. The live smoke already passes unchanged on 0.85.1 and that evidence may be cited.

VALIDATION
1. No file asserts 0.84.3 as the inspected surface unless it is deliberately describing history.
2. Each re-baselined claim cites how it was re-verified on 0.85.1.
3. Full suite and live smoke green on 0.85.1.

OUTPUT
Re-baselined reconciliation doc and code comments.

SCRUTINY
MEDIUM -- the risk is a documentation pass that relabels unverified claims as verified.
close_reason: Re-baselined to Pi 0.85.1. Every behavioural claim re-verified BY EXECUTION with controls, not relabelled. All seven hold; executeBash/pi.exec still bypass the veto with the handler firing zero times, so unitAI-rrdnt.6's verdict stands. Two genuine changes recorded: agent_end's extension-facing type dropped willRetry (session.subscribe consumers including our host still get it), and getAvailable() no longer distinguishes auth so hasConfiguredAuth is the only correct instrument -- model-gate.ts already used it, only its comment was wrong. Live smoke and model-gate tests green on 0.85.1.

title: Phase 2 — persistent Fleet registry and state projection
description:
PROBLEM
NativeActivationHost keeps activations in a private in-memory Map and exposes list() and inspect(). That is enough for one host in one process and nothing else. PRD Phase 2 requires a persistent Fleet: a registry that survives a coordinator turn, a state projection a UI can render without reaching into host internals, and the selection/attach/return/resume operations that make a Specialist something an operator can come back to. Today a coordinator that loses its turn loses all knowledge of its children.

SUCCESS
A coordinator can enumerate its live Specialists, select one, attach to it, return, and resume it later, driven by a projection that carries no TUI state and no host internals.

SCOPE
PRD Phase 2 registry and state projection, in src/activation/. A registry owning activation records with their identity, state, workspace and model; a typed projection derived from it; and the attach/return/resume operations over the existing AgentSession. Reuse ActivationSnapshot rather than defining a second view type.

NON_GOALS
Does NOT build the Pi extension or any TUI -- the compact Fleet UI is a frontend concern and this bead delivers only what a frontend would render. Does not implement the interaction protocol (Phase 5) or the writer lease (Phase 8). Does not persist to a database; process-lifetime registry plus the existing observability rows is the scope.

CONSTRAINTS
The projection must stay transport-neutral so the Pi extension, the Claude MCP server and a future Chain scheduler all consume the same shape -- this is the same constraint that keeps ActivationRequest free of TUI state. Attach must not disturb a running turn. Resume must not create a second activation: a resumed Specialist keeps its activation_id and advances its attempt, per the identity model landed in unitAI-rrdnt.2. Settling is not disposal; a settled child stays resumable.

VALIDATION
1. A settled activation can be resumed and keeps its activation_id while its attempt advances.
2. The projection contains no host internals and no TUI state.
3. Attaching to a running activation does not perturb its turn or its event stream.
4. Registry contents survive across coordinator turns within the process.

OUTPUT
Registry, projection, attach/return/resume, and tests.

SCRUTINY
MEDIUM -- the trap is leaking host internals into the projection, which welds the future UI to today's implementation.
close_reason: Registry, projection, attach/return/resume, and tests landed on feature/unitAI-rrdnt.18-fleet-registry.

title: Phase 4 — compile a bounded StepContract per activation
description:
PROBLEM
PRD section 15 requires a typed StepContract to be produced for one activation, narrowing the root work to this Specialist's role. Nothing compiles one today. NativeActivationHost passes the whole Bead through renderTaskPrompt, so every Specialist on a Bead receives the same undifferentiated scope and the runtime holds no typed, inspectable statement of what THIS activation was bounded to. There is also no provenance record tying an activation to the Bead revision it was compiled from.

SUCCESS
Each admitted activation carries a typed StepContract compiled from the ready Bead and the SpecialistDefinition, with mandate, inputs, outputs, scope, non-goals, constraints, validation and provenance, and that contract is visible on the handle and recorded forensically.

SCOPE
PRD section 15 and Phase 4: bounded activation contract compilation in src/activation/. Reuse the section extraction already written for the Phase 3 bead gate rather than adding a second parser. Attach the compiled contract to the activation and emit its provenance in the admission forensic event.

NON_GOALS
Does NOT create step issues -- PRD Phase 4 says so explicitly and invariant 4 says StepContract does not create a second work graph. Does not create a ResolvedChain, Container, or any second dependency graph. Does not change prompt composition (PRD section 16 is separate work). Does not persist the contract as a durable work item.

CONSTRAINTS
StepContract is not a second durable work item: it is derived, in-memory, and reproducible from the Bead plus the SpecialistDefinition. The PRD gives EvidenceRef, OutputRequirement, ScopeContract and ValidationRequirement as a conceptual shape only, with no field definitions; narrow them to what a Bead can actually supply today and say so in the module rather than inventing an evidence subsystem. Compilation happens after the bead gate passes, so it may assume all seven sections are present.

VALIDATION
1. A compiled contract carries mandate, scope, non-goals, constraints, validation and outputs drawn from the corresponding Bead sections.
2. Provenance records the specialist, compile time, and the Bead revision when available.
3. The contract is reachable from the activation handle and its provenance appears in forensics.
4. No issue, chain, or graph is created by compilation.

OUTPUT
StepContract module + wiring + tests.

SCRUTINY
MEDIUM -- the risk is scope creep into a second work graph, which the PRD forbids twice.
close_reason: PRD Phase 4 landed: src/activation/step-contract.ts compiles a typed StepContract per activation from the gated Bead plus the SpecialistDefinition, attached to the ActivationHandle and recorded forensically as step_contract_compiled with its provenance. Compilation is pure and creates no issue, chain, or graph -- rootWorkRef is always the Bead id, asserted in test. The Phase 3 gate's section parser was extracted as extractSections and reused rather than duplicated, so gate and compiler cannot disagree about what a Bead says. 11 new tests; full suite 2205 passed; live smoke re-run with compilation in the admission path and still green end to end. The PRD's four sub-types have no upstream field definitions and are narrowed to what a Bead can supply today, stated in the module.

title: Native host emits participant_id with the wrong separator (specialist: not specialist::)
description:
PROBLEM
src/activation/native-host.ts:117 derives participant_id as `specialist:<name>` with a single colon. Every other participant kind in src/specialist/forensic-events.ts deriveParticipantId uses a double-colon separator: `orch::<uuid>`, `node::<id>::<role>::<index>`, `<container>::emitter::<role>`. The unitAI-rrdnt.2 identity migration standardises the specialist kind as `specialist::<name>`, so the native path would write a participant_id that no lineage query joins against — the exact split the migration exists to remove.

SUCCESS
The native activation path and the migrated forensic store derive the same participant_id string for the same logical participant.

SCOPE
src/activation/native-host.ts participant_id derivation, and its assertions in tests/unit/specialist/activation-native-host.test.ts and tests/unit/specialist/activation-bead-gate.test.ts if they pin the value.

NON_GOALS
Does not implement the identity migration itself (unitAI-rrdnt.2, owned by the t4et worker). Does not change deriveParticipantId. Does not touch src/specialist/observability-sqlite.ts.

CONSTRAINTS
Adopt the existing house separator rather than changing the house style — `::` is already the convention for four other participant kinds and is what the migration will write. Coordinate ordering with unitAI-rrdnt.2 but do not block on it; this change is independently correct.

VALIDATION
1. Native activations emit participant_id matching `specialist::<name>`.
2. Full suite green.

OUTPUT
One-line derivation fix plus test coverage pinning the separator.

SCRUTINY
LOW -- one-line change, but it is the join key for cross-runtime lineage, so the value is asserted rather than left implicit.
close_reason: native-host.ts now derives participant_id as specialist::<name>, matching the house separator already used by orch::, node:: and <container>::emitter:: in deriveParticipantId, and matching what the unitAI-rrdnt.2 migration will write. Found while reviewing the t4et worker's migration plan: the plan was right and my committed code was the outlier. The derivation was previously unasserted, so a test now pins both the handle's participantId and every emitted forensic event.

title: Phase 3 — Bead hard gate on native activation admission
description:
PROBLEM
NativeActivationHost.start() admits any Bead it can read. src/activation/native-host.ts says so in its own header: "no Bead readiness gate. Contract validation is a separate phase; until then this inherits the legacy behaviour of requiring only that the Bead is readable." Nothing in src/ validates the 7-section contract or SCRUTINY -- grep for PROBLEM/NON_GOALS/SCRUTINY across src/ returns nothing. The contract discipline exists only in CLAUDE.md and hooks, so a Specialist can be dispatched against a bead that carries a title and no usable task contract, which is how durable work silently loses scope.

SUCCESS
An activation against a Bead that is not a usable task contract is refused before an AgentSession exists, with a structured refusal naming exactly what is missing, and the refusal is recorded as forensic evidence.

SCOPE
PRD Phase 3: ready validation, 7-section validation (PROBLEM/SUCCESS/SCOPE/NON_GOALS/CONSTRAINTS/VALIDATION/OUTPUT), SCRUTINY validation, structured refusal, forensic refusal. Gate lives in the admission path of NativeActivationHost.start(), after the bead is read and before any session is created.

NON_GOALS
Does not change the legacy sp run path -- that keeps its current behaviour. Does not implement StepContract (Phase 4). Does not add a second bead reader or a second definition of the contract. Does not rewrite beads.

CONSTRAINTS
Reuse BeadsClient.readBead; do not add a second bead reader. The refusal must use DispatchRejectedError so the caller sees one refusal shape, and must populate `missing` so the operator is told which sections are absent rather than that the bead is bad. A bead explicitly marked contract=draft is refused; an absent contract state is not treated as draft, because most beads predate that marker. Refusal happens before createAgentSession, never after.

VALIDATION
1. A bead missing one or more of the 7 sections is refused, and the refusal names each missing section.
2. A bead with all 7 sections and a SCRUTINY level is admitted.
3. A bead explicitly marked contract=draft is refused even when its sections are present.
4. Every refusal emits a forensic event; no AgentSession is created on any refusal path.

OUTPUT
Gate module + wiring + tests.

SCRUTINY
MEDIUM -- an admission gate that is too strict blocks real work, and one that is too loose reintroduces the scope loss it exists to prevent.
close_reason: PRD Phase 3 landed: src/activation/bead-gate.ts evaluates readiness in NativeActivationHost.start() after the bead is read and before any AgentSession exists. Covers all five PRD Phase 3 items. 11 new unit tests; live smoke re-run with the gate active and still green end to end. Absent contract state is not treated as draft because most beads predate that marker; the gate proves sections exist and are non-empty, never that they are good.

title: Phase 14 prerequisite: peer/roster adapter for Specialist -> Claude push
description:
PROBLEM
docs/design/claude-transport-decision.md (unitAI-rrdnt.10) establishes that MCP cannot push to a busy Claude Code session and assigns Specialist->coordinator push to the peer channel. Nothing has been built. The decision proves the transport exists and documents how its roster misreports liveness; it does not prove an adapter works.

SUCCESS
A Specialist running under NativeActivationHost can reach a busy Claude coordinator with a clarification, receive a reply, and resume in the same session. When the peer channel is unavailable, the same clarification is readable through specialist_status and nothing is lost.

SCOPE
Peer/roster adapter: read ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json, route over the colocated 0600 UDS, reuse the pi-claude-link frame shape (route identity separate from display name, idle sendUserMessage vs busy steer, receipt with orig_msg_id). Durable pending state written BEFORE any send. Polling via specialist_status built first as the degraded fallback. Both paths serialise the one InteractionMessage.

NON_GOALS
Does not make the peer adapter authoritative for activation identity, lease authority, result state or forensic state (PRD 107, invariant 14). Does not replace the MCP dispatch surface. Does not implement Fleet.

CONSTRAINTS
Liveness is /proc/<pid> plus procStart, never socket existence and never the registration's own status field -- measured: 10 of 20 registrations on the authoring host named dead PIDs while advertising status idle, and 128 socket files existed for 20 registrations. Check peerProtocol. Reachability is asymmetric and can lapse mid-session, so a failed send must not be read as "peer is gone". Peer delivery passes the user's cross-session approval gate and may be held, delayed or refused; none of those are errors, and a receipt is required to mark a push delivered -- absence of an error is not a receipt.

VALIDATION
1. Acceptance AX over the peer channel: Specialist asks, busy coordinator receives, replies, child resumes in the same session.
2. Acceptance AY: structured completion notification tied to a validated ActivationResult.
3. With the peer channel unavailable, specialist_status surfaces the pending clarification and nothing is lost.
4. Both paths produce identical InteractionMessage semantics (invariant BH).
5. A registration naming a dead PID is never selected as a route.

OUTPUT
Adapter + polling fallback + tests.

SCRUTINY
HIGH -- the failure mode being designed against is a channel that silently never delivers.
close_reason: Peer/roster adapter and polling fallback built and tested; criteria 3, 4, 5 met, criteria 1 and 2 not met by this lane. New modules under src/activation/transport/ only (pending-store, polling, roster, peer-transport, peer-adapter); 33 new tests, 89 activation tests green, tsc clean. Two measured corrections to the decision record: procStart has two formats (13 of 18 registrations, all written by Claude Code itself, carry raw /proc stat field 22 as a number; section 4 documents only the pi-claude-link string form, and following it literally rejected every native Claude coordinator), and idle-vs-busy steer is a receiver-side injection choice, not a sender field. Criteria 1 (AX) and 2 (AY) need a Specialist under NativeActivationHost, which this lane does not own — dawid-0b is wiring it as unitAI-rrdnt.22. Also measured: the peer channel delivers without a sender registration but returns no receipt without one, so AX depends on a user ruling filed as unitAI-rrdnt.25. Adapter meanwhile records sent_unconfirmed, claims no delivery, and leaves the question readable through polling.

title: Phase 1 live smoke: real SpecialistLoader override + real model turn + observability.db rows
description:
PROBLEM
unitAI-rrdnt.5 landed the native activation host and proved its structure with unit tests, but three of its VALIDATION items are only proven against injected doubles, not against the real system. Specifically: the loader is a stub returning a literal spec, so PRD acceptance A (a repo/global override changes the native child exactly as SpecialistLoader.get() dictates) is NOT proven; no real model turn has run through the host; and no row has been observed in a real observability.db, so acceptance AJ and AP are asserted by unit test rather than by inspection.

SUCCESS
A real researcher Specialist, resolved through the real three-layer SpecialistLoader, runs a real model turn in-process against a real Bead, and its activation events are visible by querying the actual observability.db. A deliberate repo-layer override demonstrably changes the child's behavior.

SCOPE
1. Acceptance A: create a repo .specialists/user/<name>.specialist.json override changing an observable field (model or prompt.system), dispatch through NativeActivationHost, and assert the child reflects the override — resolved through the real loader, not an injected one.
2. Acceptance B: with no override, the child runs the effective configured model.
3. Live turn: one short real model turn end to end, producing an ActivationResult with status completed.
4. Acceptance AJ/AP: query the real observability.db and confirm activation rows are present under the activation id, and that no second database file was created anywhere.
5. Confirm no `pi` process is spawned during the live run, observed at the OS level rather than by module mock.

NON_GOALS
No writer support, no lease, no interaction protocol, no Fleet. Does not add the Bead readiness gate.

CONSTRAINTS
Use a cheap model and keep the turn short. The smoke must be runnable on demand rather than in the default unit-test path, since it needs model auth and makes a network call — follow whatever convention the repo already uses for tests that need credentials, and skip cleanly when auth is absent rather than failing.

VALIDATION
1. Override test passes against the real loader.
2. Live turn returns a completed ActivationResult.
3. A documented query returns the activation's rows from the real observability.db.
4. No second telemetry database exists after the run.

OUTPUT
Live smoke + any fixes it surfaces. Closes the evidence gap left by unitAI-rrdnt.5.

SCRUTINY
MEDIUM — this is the test that would catch a host that unit-passes against doubles but cannot actually resolve, launch or record a real Specialist.
close_reason: Live smoke lands at tests/integration/activation/native-activation.live.test.ts, gated on SPECIALISTS_LIVE_SMOKE=1 and skipping cleanly without model auth. Acceptance B proven live end to end: real three-layer SpecialistLoader, real model turn, completed ActivationResult, activation rows read back from the real observability.db by a documented SQL query, exactly one .db file in the workspace, and no 'pi' process ever a descendant of the test process (sampled ps, not a module mock). Acceptance A proven for override resolution through the real loader, plus the blocked-field guarantee that a repo layer cannot seize prompt.system; it deliberately does not await a turn, because requiring a second SOLVENT provider would fail for billing reasons that say nothing about the loader. The run found two real host defects, both fixed and both pinned by new unit regressions: createAgentSession was passed a model string instead of the resolved Model object, and a turn ending in stopReason 'error' was reported as completed with empty output.

title: Correct three factual errors in native-activation-reconciliation.md
description:
PROBLEM
docs/design/native-activation-reconciliation.md (commit 85ad2ffa) contains three claims that fuller code-map reports subsequently disproved. The doc is the basis for every later phase, so wrong rows will be built on.

SUCCESS
All three are corrected with verified file:line citations and the parity-matrix gate still passes.

SCOPE
1. Layer count. Doc section 2.2 and 7.1 describe a four-layer override contract (package / global / repo default / repo user) taken from PRD section 8. Actual is THREE layers: package canonical -> ~/.config/specialists/user.json -> repo .specialists/user/<name>. The repo .specialists/default/ mirror was retired by commit 31a6421c and is no longer walked (src/specialist/loader.ts:147-157). Stale files are detected by drift-detector and removed by sp prune-stale-defaults but do not feed the merge. Legacy ./specialists, .claude/specialists and .agent-forge/specialists are likewise non-authoritative.
2. Model override is NOT absent. Doc section 7.2 lists "activation model override — ABSENT today". Per-invocation override already exists on both surfaces: CLI --model (src/cli/run.ts:162) and MCP backend_override (src/tools/specialist/use_specialist.tool.ts:11,59 -> runner.ts:1132). Note backend_override replaces the whole model chain despite its name. Reclassify from native(new) to adapted, and record that PRD section 62 pre-creation validation is the genuinely new part, not the override itself.
3. expected_output_keys owner is wrong. Doc section 7.2 attributes it to validateOutputContract (runner.ts:975). The only consumer is collectRequiredOutputKeys (src/specialist/script-runner.ts:633); the run path never reads it. Cross-reference the bug bead filed for this.

NON_GOALS
No new analysis. No change to conclusions that remain correct — the lease, identity, contract-gate and veto-ordering findings are unaffected.

CONSTRAINTS
scripts/check-parity-matrix.mjs must still pass after the edits.

VALIDATION
1. Each corrected claim carries a verified file:line citation.
2. node scripts/check-parity-matrix.mjs exits 0.

OUTPUT
Corrected design doc.

SCRUTINY
LOW — documentation accuracy, but the doc is load-bearing for later phases.
notes:
SCOPE EXPANDED — fold in empirical verification results (/tmp/xtrm-pi-veto-probe/FINDINGS.md, 5 model turns on cheap nano-gpt models).

Upgrade doc sections 5.8/5.9/5.10 from READ (source-reading) to EXECUTED, and add:

1. V2 CONFIRMED by execution. A real parallel batch (one assistant message, two calls). Handler for call #1 called setActiveTools revoking call #2's tool; call #2 STILL EXECUTED (both marker files created). Control with {block:true}: both handlers fired, neither file created. So §5.9 and bead .7 stand — block is the only real fence.

2. NEW POSITIVE FINDING, add to §5.9 — every tool_call handler in a parallel batch fires BEFORE any tool in that batch executes (prepare-all runs to completion, then Promise.all executes; pi-agent-core agent-loop.js:332-374). CONSEQUENCE: a lease acquired during call #1 CAN still block call #2 in the same batch, via block. This is materially better than §5.9 currently implies — mid-batch lease acquisition is enforceable, just never via tool removal. Reflect this in bead .7's acceptance test.

3. V1 CONFIRMED by execution: all five paths (edit, write, bash, registerTool, SDK customTool) fire the handler AND are prevented, proven by side effect (target unchanged, four marker files absent), with a veto-off control run proving the negatives are real. Blocked call surfaces as isError=true with the reason string.

4. H1/H3 CONFIRMED by execution, not just source reading: with the veto active and blocking everything, session.executeBash() and pi.exec() from inside an extension both exited 0, wrote their file, and fired the handler ZERO times. Bead .6 should cite these as executed evidence.

5. V3 CONFIRMED including the trap: with --provider nvidia --model no-such-model-at-all, resolveCliModel returns a FABRICATED model with only a warning and error undefined, while hasConfiguredAuth('nvidia') is true — so an auth-only gate ACCEPTS a nonexistent model. Only the no-match diagnostic catches it. Both halves of the gate are load-bearing; document that explicitly.

6. OPERATIONAL TRAP for §5.10 — ModelRuntime.create({refreshOnCreate:false}) yields ZERO configured-auth providers and an empty getAvailable(), which would make the gate reject every model. Use {allowModelNetwork:false} and leave refreshOnCreate alone.
close_reason: Three factual errors corrected (model override already exists; expected_output_keys owned by script-runner.ts; three layers not four). Added 5.13-5.16: expected_output_keys gap, retired default layer, empirical verification upgrading 5.8-5.10 from READ to EXECUTED including the mid-batch improvement, and the MCP-cannot-push finding with transport reassignment. Parity gate passes 57/57.

title: Lease guard must be per-tool-call block, not setActiveTools — PRD §52 defense-in-depth ordering is inverted
description:
PROBLEM
PRD section 52 presents deactivating the parent's mutation-capable tools as the primary fence, with the section 53 tool_call guard as protection for "current-turn timing gaps". On Pi 0.84.3 the relationship is inverted, and building it as written would produce a lease that leaks for the remainder of every turn in which it is acquired.
setActiveToolsByName synchronously replaces agent.state.tools but takes effect on the NEXT agent turn (dist/core/agent-session.d.ts:320; agent-session.js:634-652). Within a turn the agent loop executes against currentContext, a snapshot taken at turn start: prepareToolCall resolves via currentContext.tools?.find(...) (pi-agent-core/dist/agent-loop.js:393-394), refreshed only at the turn boundary (agent-loop.js:130-145). In parallel mode every preparation runs before any execution (agent-loop.js:332-365), so setActiveTools called from inside one tool_call handler cannot affect the rest of that batch. There is no fence, epoch, or generation counter.

SUCCESS
The writer lease is enforced by a per-call tool_call veto that consults live lease state on every mutating call. Acquiring a lease mid-turn immediately fences the other participant's already-planned calls.

SCOPE
Implement the lease guard as the enforcement layer. Keep setActiveToolsByName as an advisory/cosmetic measure that keeps the model's tool list and system prompt honest on the next turn. Order the Phase 8 work so the guard exists before any tool-set manipulation is relied upon.

NON_GOALS
Does not implement the lease store itself (separate Phase 8 bead). Does not attempt to close the H3/H4 extension bypasses (see the section 54 conflict bead).

CONSTRAINTS
The guard must read live lease state per call, not a value captured at turn start — capturing it would reintroduce the same snapshot bug one layer up. emitToolCall returns on the first handler that sets block (dist/core/extensions/runner.js:982), so the guard must not be registered behind another handler that might block first for an unrelated reason and mask lease denials.

VALIDATION
1. PRD acceptance U: parent Edit is blocked while a child holds the lease.
2. PRD acceptance V: the blocked call produces a forensic event with a reason distinguishing policy block from tool failure.
3. Regression test: a lease acquired mid-turn blocks a call already planned in that same turn's batch — the exact case setActiveToolsByName cannot cover.

OUTPUT
Lease guard implementation + tests. Source: docs/design/native-activation-reconciliation.md section 5.9.

SCRUTINY
HIGH — this is the mechanism that makes single-writer real. A wrong ordering here yields a lease that appears to work in tests and leaks in production.
notes: Confirmed by execution against Pi 0.85.1 (unitAI-rrdnt.17): all tool_call handlers in a batch fire BEFORE any tool executes, so a mid-batch block IS enforceable and per-tool-call veto is the correct guard; and setActiveTools cannot cancel an already-planned call, so the PRD section 52 ordering is indeed inverted. Both halves of this bead's claim are now empirically settled. The remaining OUTPUT -- guard implementation plus tests -- is part of the writer lease, so this depends on unitAI-rrdnt.21 and the .21 lane has been given both findings as non-negotiable design inputs.
close_reason: Satisfied by unitAI-rrdnt.36.1. NativeActivationHost.admitToolCall() is a per-call verdict that calls workspace-lease.inspect() on every mutating call, so it reads live lease state rather than a value captured at turn start, and a lease acquired mid-turn fences an already-planned call. setActiveToolsByName is not used for enforcement anywhere. Tests: holder mutates, reader in the same workspace is refused and emits tool_blocked, unknown activation fails closed.

title: PRD §54 conflict: extension pi.exec() and direct fs I/O bypass the workspace lease on Pi 0.84.3
description:
PROBLEM
PRD section 54 requires that extension-provided mutation not bypass the workspace writer lease. On installed Pi 0.84.3 this is only partially achievable. The tool_call veto is a genuine choke point for every LLM-initiated tool call — built-ins, bash-as-tool, pi.registerTool tools, SDK customTools, and baseToolsOverride replacements all funnel through agent.beforeToolCall -> runner.emitToolCall (dist/core/agent-session.js:228; dist/core/extensions/runner.js:701; pi-agent-core/dist/agent-loop.js:393-430). Four paths escape it:
  H1 AgentSession.executeBash() called directly in-process (no emitToolCall/emitUserBash, dist/core/agent-session.js:2289-2310).
  H2 the operator user_bash path — interactive !bash and RPC bash emit user_bash, not tool_call (dist/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.js:5417; dist/modes/rpc/rpc-mode.js:439).
  H3 pi.exec(command, args, options) inside any extension handler (dist/core/extensions/loader.js:320).
  H4 direct node:fs / child_process / fetch inside extension code — extensions run in-process.
No exec or filesystem interposition layer exists in 0.84.3 to close H3/H4.

SUCCESS
The limitation is a recorded, reviewed decision rather than an undocumented hole. Either the residual risk is accepted with the mitigations below written into the skill and the lease docstrings, or an upstream capability is identified that closes H3/H4.

SCOPE
Decide and document the disposition of H1-H4. Mitigations already identified: H1 is avoidable by host discipline (never call executeBash from the activation host); H2 is avoidable by routing the Claude MCP server's shell work through prompt-induced tool calls rather than RPC bash. H3/H4 are a trusted-extension threat, not a delegated-agent threat: the child Specialist's own capability grant is what admits an extension in the first place, and Specialists capability policy is fail-closed.

NON_GOALS
Does not implement a sandbox. Does not fork or patch Pi. Does not block Phase 8 — the lease still covers every mutation an LLM can initiate, which is the delegated-Specialist threat model.

CONSTRAINTS
If accepted, the limitation must appear in the WorkspaceLeaseStore docstring, in the using-specialists skill, and in the reconciliation doc — PRD section 97 makes documentation parity part of acceptance, and a lease that silently under-delivers is worse than one whose boundary is stated. Revisit if Pi gains exec interposition.

VALIDATION
1. Decision recorded with rationale and mitigations.
2. Docstring, skill, and design doc agree on the stated boundary.
3. A test asserts the guard does cover H1-equivalent LLM paths (a)-(d), so the covered set does not silently shrink.

OUTPUT
Decision record + doc updates. Source: docs/design/native-activation-reconciliation.md section 5.8.

SCRUTINY
HIGH — this is the boundary of a security-relevant authority mechanism. Understating it would let an operator or agent assume containment they do not have.
notes: Re-verified against Pi 0.85.1 (unitAI-rrdnt.17): the bypass is UNCHANGED. session.executeBash() and pi.exec() still fire the tool_call handler zero times, and no new CreateAgentSessionOptions field closes it. The verdict in this bead therefore stands rather than being superseded by the upgrade. Reconciliation section 5.8 is updated and re-titled to 0.85.1. Remaining work for this bead is the mitigation text in the lease docstrings, which the unitAI-rrdnt.21 lane is under instruction to write; that is why this now depends on .21.
close_reason: Disposition recorded rather than closed as fixed. H1/H2 are avoidable by host discipline and the host does not call executeBash. H3/H4 are NOT closable on pi 0.85.1 — re-verified on 0.85.1 that pi.exec() and AgentSession.executeBash() fire the tool_call handler zero times. Documented in docs/native-activation.md (bypass table plus the holes table), in workspace-lease.ts, and in NativeActivationHost.admitToolCall()'s docstring, which states plainly that the guard covers the LLM tool path only. Residual risk accepted: it is a trusted-extension threat, not a delegated-agent one, and the child's own fail-closed capability grant is what admits an extension at all.

title: Phase 1 — read-only native Specialist over in-process AgentSession
description:
PROBLEM
No native path exists. Every Specialist runs by spawning the pi binary (src/pi/session.ts:1022), which makes a Specialist operationally separate from the coordinator's session and forecloses persistence, interaction and attach.

SUCCESS
A read-only Specialist (researcher) dispatched from a Pi coordinator resolves through the real SpecialistLoader, runs on a real in-process Pi AgentSession created via createAgentSession, receives its real resolved skill and tool policy, and produces a result — with no subprocess and no sp run.

SCOPE
NativeActivationHost.start/inspect plus the minimum supporting types (ActivationRequest, ActivationHandle). Session creation against installed @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent 0.84.3 using tools/excludeTools/noTools for the fail-closed capability grant and an append-mode ResourceLoader for the system prompt. Reuse validateBeforeRun, renderTaskPrompt, the script runners and the tool-contract resolvers unchanged. Forensic rows via the existing appendForensicEvent writer.

NON_GOALS
No writer support, no lease, no Bead readiness gate, no StepContract, no interaction protocol, no Fleet UI, no Claude integration, no model override. No change to the legacy sp run path. No new database.

CONSTRAINTS
Implement against the installed 0.84.3 surface, not upstream 0.85.1 (no ./experimental/plugin). Do not dispose on agent_end or agent_settled. Carry the sterile-child behaviors listed in reconciliation section 5.2 deliberately — ambient extension/skill/context-file isolation must not be lost by inheriting the host's configuration. Depends on unitAI-rrdnt.3 (buildSystemPrompt extraction).

VALIDATION
1. PRD acceptance A: a repo override changes the native child exactly as SpecialistLoader.get() dictates.
2. PRD acceptance G: the researcher cannot mutate the workspace.
3. PRD acceptance B: the child runs the effective configured model.
4. Forensic rows for the native activation appear in observability.db (acceptance AJ) and no second database is created (acceptance AP).
5. No spawn of pi occurs during the run; asserted in the test.

OUTPUT
src/activation/ native host + tests. Reconciliation doc: docs/design/native-activation-reconciliation.md.

SCRUTINY
HIGH — capability resolution. A regression here grants a child tools its Specialist definition denies.
close_reason: Phase 1 structural slice landed: src/activation/{pi-sdk,types,model-gate,native-host,forensic-sink}.ts. Read-only Specialist runs in-process via createAgentSession with a fail-closed tool grant (noTools:builtin + explicit allowlist), no subprocess, no dispose on settle, writers refused pending the lease, model override validated pre-creation by the two-halves gate, forensics into the canonical observability.db via the same appendForensicEvent path as the MCP gateway. 11 new tests; tsc clean; full suite 183 files / 2179 tests. NOT yet proven live: acceptance A against the real layered loader, a real model turn, and observed observability.db rows — tracked as unitAI-rrdnt.11.

title: Identity lineage migration: attempt_id, columnar pi_session_id/workspace_id, chain-independent participant_id
description:
PROBLEM
Only 1 of the PRD's 4 identity layers is durable. job_id is canonical. attempt_id does not exist at all — retries are counted (SessionRunMetrics.auto_retries, src/pi/session.ts:88) but nothing separates attempt N's rows from attempt N+1's within one job_id. pi_session_id exists only inside the status_json blob (src/specialist/supervisor.ts:132, lifted at src/specialist/observability-sqlite.ts:1489), so it is unqueryable without JSON_EXTRACT. participant_id is derived as "<chain_id>::<specialist>" (src/specialist/forensic-events.ts:389-398), returns undefined when chain_id is absent, and gives the same logical participant different ids across chains — the opposite of a stable participant identity.

SUCCESS
A forensic query can recover the full Bead -> participant -> activation -> attempt -> Pi session -> turn -> tool -> result chain, as PRD acceptance AK/AL/AM require.

SCOPE
Migration on observability.db adding attempt_id; promoting pi_session_id and workspace_id to indexed columns on specialist_jobs; redefining participant_id so it is stable and chain-independent and never null. Update writers and readForensicContext accordingly. Backfill strategy for existing rows.

NON_GOALS
No change to the event vocabulary (separate bead). No Substrate state-store cutover. No removal of status_json.

CONSTRAINTS
observability.db stays the single store — no side database. Existing reports (prometheus-projection, live-aggregates, timeline-query, sp ps/status/feed) must keep working. Legacy sp run rows must remain readable.

VALIDATION
1. PRD acceptance AL: query recovers Specialist/participant/activation/attempt/session relationship.
2. PRD acceptance AM: two retries appear as two attempts under one activation, not two participants.
3. Existing observability tests pass unchanged.

OUTPUT
Migration + writer updates + tests. Evidence: docs/design/native-activation-reconciliation.md section 6.2.

SCRUTINY
HIGH — schema migration on the authoritative forensic store.
notes: Implemented additive observability schema v15 identity lineage on 7f09eb38: canonical specialist::<role>, attempt IDs, session/workspace projections, legacy attempt 0/NULL, sentinel exclusion. Reader audit found no grouping/filtering/joining on participant_id. Real-store dry run: 681,498 projected rows, sentinel 0. Focused tests: 97 pass; tsc clean; 993-row event_json checksum identical. Full-suite non-hermetic DB incident retained per coordinator ruling; store quick_check ok. GitNexus change risk CRITICAL due initSchema reach (63 affected), reviewed and tested. No src/activation changes.
close_reason: Done: additive v15 identity lineage, preserved authoritative blobs and legacy reads, verified retry attempt semantics, reader compatibility, real-store sentinel count, checksum integrity, and focused regression tests.

title: Phase 0 — reconciliation: feature-parity matrix + runner/forensic/experiment reuse map
description:
PROBLEM
PRD section 129 Phase 0 forbids production coding before the reusable seams are identified. Nobody has mapped the current Specialist runtime onto the native AgentSession design, so any implementation risks silently dropping a shipped Specialist feature (PRD section 9, invariant 26, acceptance R).

SUCCESS
A durable reconciliation note exists in the working branch that maps the PRD to current code and lets an implementer start Phase 1 without rediscovering the design. Every schema field and runtime behavior in src/specialist/schema.ts and the runner is classified; no feature is silently unlisted.

SCOPE
Write docs/design/native-activation-reconciliation.md containing:
1. Feature-parity table with columns: feature | current owner (file:line) | current behavior | native implementation path | classification (native|adapted|deferred|rejected) | test proving the classification. Rows must cover at minimum: SpecialistLoader, model/fallback resolution, model override, thinking level, permissions, active tools, extension tools, required external commands, skills, mandatory rules, system prompt mode, task template, pre/post scripts, timeout, stall detection, retry, output schema, expected output keys, output persistence, auto-commit/checkpoint, Beads integration, observability/forensics, interaction, workspace lease, result lifecycle.
2. Current runner map: the execution path from `sp run` to a model turn, naming the SessionFactory seam (src/specialist/runner.ts:99-102) and the subprocess boundary (src/pi/session.ts:1022).
3. Forensic writer map: which module writes which observability.db table/event, and which writers are too coupled to SpecialistRunner to reuse as-is.
4. Native experiment reuse map: what to reuse verbatim, evolve, or discard from ~/dev/xtrm/experiments/agentsession-sre-chain-vertical-slice.
5. Documented conflicts between current implementation assumptions and the PRD, each with the chosen resolution (PRD wins) or a discovered-work bead id.

NON_GOALS
No production runtime code. No schema changes. No modification of the legacy sp run path. Does not implement the parity gaps it identifies.

CONSTRAINTS
Every claim cites file:line in ~/dev/specialists at the branch HEAD. Classification `deferred` or `rejected` requires a stated reason; `native` or `adapted` requires a named target module under the PRD section 6 layout. Reference-repo findings must cite the upstream commit inspected.

VALIDATION
1. Every field in src/specialist/schema.ts appears as a row; verified by a check that enumerates schema keys against the table.
2. Every listed classification names either a target module path or a reason.
3. A reviewer can trace `sp run` -> model turn from the runner map alone.

OUTPUT
docs/design/native-activation-reconciliation.md on branch feature/unitAI-rrdnt.1-phase0-reconciliation, plus discovered-work beads for each PRD/implementation conflict found.

title: Native interactive XTRM Specialists (Pi AgentSession + Claude Code)
description:
PROBLEM
Specialists today execute via `sp run` -> PiAgentSession -> `spawn('pi', args)` subprocess RPC (src/pi/session.ts:1022). That makes a Specialist operationally separate from the coordinator's live session, so coordinators fall back to generic Pi subagents, manual sp run, or doing the work directly. Specialists are also one-shot: a child dies at the end of a turn, cannot ask a clarifying question and resume, and cannot be attached to.

SUCCESS
A canonical NativeActivationHost in xtrm-dev/specialists hosts persistent, interactive, Bead-backed Pi AgentSession children. Pi (via extension) and Claude Code (via MCP plugin) are thin frontends over the same runtime; a future XTRM Chain scheduler can call it without TUI state. observability.db remains the single forensic store. Exactly one writer per mutable workspace, coordinator included.

SCOPE
Implements ~/dev/xtrm/docs/specialists/PRD-Native-Specialist-Subagents-for-Pi.md (em-dash filename, 4517 lines) phases 0-15, acceptance matrix A-BI. Child beads carry per-phase contracts.

NON_GOALS
Chain scheduler, ResolvedChain lifecycle, Substrate daemon/state-store, native Substrate step-issue creation, seed containers, epic/wave/node runtime, automatic worktree provisioning per Specialist, automatic merge/publish, multi-host or networked Specialist transport, replacing pi-intercom / pi-claude-link / XTRM Channels / Beads, Claude-native Specialist reimplementation. Legacy `sp run` path is not removed in this epic.

CONSTRAINTS
Runtime stays in xtrm-dev/specialists; no move into Core. Pi extension must NOT be tool -> `sp run` subprocess; Claude integration must NOT be MCP -> Bash -> `sp run`. Both call shared library code directly. SpecialistLoader stays authoritative; no second resolver. No telemetry side database. Public Pi SDK APIs only where possible. Incremental reviewable commits; no giant rewrite of the legacy runner before the shared seams are proven.

VALIDATION
PRD section 130 acceptance matrix A-BI (47 scenarios) as automated tests plus integration smokes. Per-phase child beads carry their own VALIDATION.

OUTPUT
Working native activation runtime, Pi extension, Claude Code plugin/MCP server, adapted using-specialists skill, feature-parity matrix, developer/operator docs.

SCRUTINY
HIGH. Touches capability/permission resolution, workspace mutation authority, and the forensic store. A lease bug silently allows two concurrent writers in one worktree; a capability regression grants a child tools its Specialist definition denies.

Specialists 3.21.6 validates and forwards `skills.paths` by resolving relative values against the process working directory. It cannot resolve a bare logical skill from repo skills layout v2 (`<repo>/.xtrm/skills/<pack>/<skill>/`). The current `service-knowledge-sync` source removed the stale global path, but that only avoids the crash; it does not bind the consumer's project-pack Service Knowledge skill or dynamically find its scripts.

Both tracked PiAgentSession execution and direct/script execution resolve a bare `service-knowledge` declaration to exactly one consumer project-pack skill. `service-knowledge-sync` declares the logical skill, runs its pre-script from the same resolved project-pack root, and fails clearly on missing or ambiguous matches. Resolution works for arbitrary pack names such as `infra` and `market-data`.

## SCOPE

title: specialists-creator: expose safe mandatory-rules selection in user config
description:
## PROBLEM

Specialist manifests can select mandatory rule sets, but the normal global user workflow cannot. `~/.config/specialists/user.json` strips `mandatory_rules`, generated defaults expose no selection field, and the canonical override guide is silent. Users of shipped specialists therefore cannot discover or choose specialist-specific rule sets without creating repo-local manifests. Documentation also contradicts runtime behavior for `disable_default_globals` and overlay precedence.

## SUCCESS

Global user configuration provides a narrowly scoped, schema-validated way to select the specialist-specific `mandatory_rules.template_sets` for each shipped specialist. The contract distinguishes inherit from explicit empty selection. Required/default index policy remains protected; global users cannot inject inline rule text or disable required/default policy through this surface. Generated `sp init --global`, `sp edit --global`, `sp doctor`, `sp view`, and `sp list-rules` agree on the effective selection. Canonical docs accurately describe package, global, and repo scopes and actual runtime behavior.

## SCOPE

- `src/specialist/global-config.ts` global schema/template/leaf paths.
- `src/specialist/schema.ts` override allow/block contract.
- `src/specialist/loader.ts` layered merge semantics and diagnostics.
- `src/cli/init.ts`, `src/cli/edit.ts`, `src/cli/doctor.ts`, `src/cli/list-rules.ts` only where required for coherent UX.
- `config/mandatory-rules/README.md`, `docs/overrides-guide.md`, `config/skills/setup-specialists/SKILL.md`, and `config/skills/specialists-creator/SKILL.md` for one consistent contract.
- Focused unit/integration tests for global config generation, validation, merge, edit, doctor/view/list-rules, and prompt injection.

## NON_GOALS

- Do not let global config change `inline_rules`, `disable_default_globals`, required template sets, or default index policy.
- Do not redesign mandatory-rule file format, token budgeting, script-class behavior, or telemetry.
- Do not weaken package/repo specialist safety fields or make arbitrary blocked fields globally writable.
- Do not publish packages.

## CONSTRAINTS

- SCRUTINY: high. This changes agent instruction configuration.
- Base work on release-candidate commit `aa7975e4`; preserve the extension/RPC fixes already there.
- Recommended minimal contract: global `mandatory_rules.template_sets: string[] | null`; `null` inherits, `[]` explicitly selects no specialist-specific sets, non-empty arrays replace the package specialist-specific list. Required/default index sets still load exactly as runtime currently does.
- Keep `inline_rules` and `disable_default_globals` blocked globally. Repo-local full manifests retain current authority and warning behavior unless evidence requires a compatible correction.
- Do not modify `buildMandatoryRulesInjection` unless necessary. GitNexus marks it CRITICAL: 24 upstream dependents across six render/run/serve flows. If touched, report and revalidate all affected flows.
- Existing structured `mandatory_rules_injection` telemetry remains authoritative; do not log rule bodies or user content.
- No new dependencies.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `sp init --global` emits the safe mandatory-rules selection field for shipped defaults.
- [ ] Schema accepts `null`, `[]`, and valid kebab-case set IDs; rejects inline rules/disable flags/unknown nested fields globally.
- [ ] Merge tests prove `null` inherits, `[]` clears specialist-specific sets, and non-empty arrays replace them while required/default index sets remain.
- [ ] `sp edit --global` can set/reset the selection with actionable errors.
- [ ] `sp doctor`, `sp view`, and `sp list-rules --specialist <name> --json` show coherent effective state.
- [ ] Prompt rendering regression proves selected sets load and removed specialist-specific sets do not, without changing required/default policy.
- [ ] Canonical README and override/setup/creator docs contain no contradiction about `disable_default_globals` or tier precedence.
- [ ] TypeScript, focused suites, full unit suite, deterministic build, and `git diff --check` pass.
- [ ] `gitnexus_detect_changes` reports only expected config/loader/CLI/render flows.

## LIBRARIES

- Reuse in repo: existing Zod override schemas, allow/block constants, loader field merge, `sp edit` dot paths, list-rules introspection, and mandatory-rules tests.
- Installed deps: Zod and existing JSON/CLI utilities only.
- Stdlib: existing Node fs/path APIs.
- New dependency candidate: none.
- Roll it: no; extend existing contracts minimally.

## OUTPUT

A committed implementation on an isolated branch with changed-file list, exact effective configuration examples, test counts, CLI smoke evidence, GitNexus impact/change report, corrected documentation, and residual compatibility risks. Do not merge or publish.

title: docs(cli/skills): sp log --json envelope shape + correct monitor recipes
description:
PROBLEM: Skills and CLI help teach a monitor recipe for sp log --json that silently matches nothing because the recipe reads event_family / event_name / severity at the top level of the row, but those fields live nested inside .forensic_event. Every monitor built from that recipe is a silent-fail: filter never hits, coordinator sees no notifications, treats silence as still-running. Compounding bug: the same recipe lists 'waiting' in the terminal-state alternation. 'waiting' is not terminal — a keep-alive specialist sits in waiting between turns; treating it as done causes coordinators to declare success on jobs that never actually executed (user just hit this with sx9n.4 / ab5aa9 at 24s / 0 tool calls). The vendored copy at ~/.xtrm/skills/default/using-specialists/references/monitoring.md has this broken recipe; the specialists SSOT config/skills/using-specialists/references/monitoring.md is missing the section entirely (drift). Blocks release train — agents keep setting up wrong monitors.

SCOPE:

- config/skills/using-specialists/references/monitoring.md: add corrected 'Event-Driven Monitoring For Keep-Alive Specialists' section (previously only in vendored copy). Corrected recipe reads fields from row.forensic_event; distinguishes TERMINAL (job.completed|job.failed|job.cancelled) from ATTENTION (waiting-transitions, process_health.stale_detected, error.*). Adds sanity rule: if sp result on a 'terminal' notification shows 0 tool_calls and empty output, the job never ran — inspect sp feed before declaring done.
- No src code changes beyond the help string.

SUCCESS:

NON_GOALS:

CONSTRAINTS:

## Risks in premature design

Moving only OSV `pr-scan` fails root-class requirement when sibling PR jobs still execute untrusted code on persistent runners.

Read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN` alone does not protect persistent runner. Malicious PR code can attack:

- Runner filesystem residue.
- Long-lived process state.
- Tool caches and executable search paths.
- Docker daemon or privileged sockets.
- Credentials left by earlier jobs.
- Other workspaces.
- Network-reachable trusted services.

- Attacker-controlled artifact contents.
- Path traversal during extraction.
- Oversized or malformed payloads.
- PR-number or repository confusion.
- Head-SHA substitution.

- Shell or Markdown injection.

## Architecture

Provisional root-class boundary, independent of repository details:

1. **Untrusted execution plane**

   - Repository scripts, package hooks, generated executables, local actions, and checked-out workflow helpers count as untrusted code.

2. **Authority boundary**
   - Default workflow permission: `contents: read`.
   - Narrow further to `permissions: {}` where checkout/API access is unnecessary.
   - No write permission in any job consuming PR-controlled input.
   - No repository secrets.
   - No explicit `GITHUB_TOKEN` forwarding.
   - Every checkout of PR code uses `persist-credentials: false`.

3. **Comments**
   - Remove PR comments when nonessential.
   - Avoid `workflow_run` entirely unless comments remain mandatory.
   - Job summary and check result provide lower-complexity feedback.

4. **Optional trusted reporting plane**
   - Trigger only from completed named workflow.
   - Trusted workflow lives on default branch and never checks out PR head.
   - Download artifact only from triggering run ID and expected repository.
   - Validate event, conclusion, workflow identity, head repository, head SHA, artifact name, size, count, and schema.
   - Accept fixed data fields only; never accept shell fragments, paths, Markdown templates, API endpoints, or arbitrary filenames.
   - Render escaped text through API client.
   - Grant only required `pull-requests: write` permission.
   - Use no third-party processing action unless pinned and reviewed.

- Fail when PR workflow references `secrets.*`.

title: sp turn-1 /skill: composition: force deterministic body load on both spawn paths (parity with xt --role)
description:
Sibling to unitAI-0o3pv (pool isolation). Discovered in xt --role launcher redesign audit follow-up #3 (core-luho).

PROBLEM: --skill <path> only makes a skill AVAILABLE (name+description in system prompt); the SKILL.md BODY loads only on fuzzy task-match, not deterministically. Pi's /skill:name (pi) / /skill-name (claude) at turn-1 position 0 FORCES immediate full-body load. Today sp emits neither: no path prepends /skill: to the initial prompt. Consequence — same specialist DIVERGES by entry point:
  xt --role X : core prepends /skill: to turn-1 -> body loaded deterministically
  sp run X    : no /skill: in turn-1 -> body may or may not load
Affects sp run, chain execution, node members, use_specialist MCP tool (all via session.ts) and the script/serve path (script-runner.ts). Same class as core xtrm-osipt, smaller pool.

TARGET CONTRACT (mirror core launcher):
  turn-1 shape: '/skill:name1 /skill:name2\n\n<body>'
  '/' at literal position 0 — no leading wrapper/metadata
  skill list = specialist skills.paths, JSON declaration order preserved
  name derivation: <dir>/SKILL.md -> containing folder name; bare .md -> filename stem
  <body> = existing task text (renderTaskPrompt output / render-task initial_prompt)

DESIGN DECISIONS TO RESOLVE (not yet decided — survey):
1. Composition site. renderTaskPrompt (task-prompt.ts) currently NEVER prepends anything to initial_prompt (verified follow-up #1). Adding the /skill: block means prepending — the one thing the seam deliberately never does. Cleanest: build the /skill: block INSIDE renderTaskPrompt so all callers (sp run + render-task) inherit it from one seam.
2. Parity contract (unitAI-6639v.1). render-task initial_prompt must stay byte-identical to sp run task-side. If sp run prepends /skill: but render-task does not, they diverge. Preferred: render-task ALSO emits the /skill: block in initial_prompt, and core's xt --role uses it verbatim instead of building its own — keeps the single-seam invariant and auto-resolves the bead-title-at-position-0 hazard (the /skill: line now owns position 0, body follows).
3. Token cost. Forcing every declared skill body at turn-1 adds input tokens per run. For progressive-disclosure skills (using-specialists v3.8) this loads only the ~256-line router body, not the references (those stay on-demand) — compatible, but audit large declared skills.
4. Opt-out? Some specialists may want available-not-forced. Decide whether /skill: composition is unconditional (all declared skills) or has a per-skill 'available only' marker.

Refs: unitAI-0o3pv (isolation half), core xtrm-osipt, audit follow-up #3 in /home/dawid/dev/core/.xtrm/worktrees/core-xt-claude-luho/.xtrm/tmp/. No code yet — survey/scoping.

- New CLI: sp render-skill-prefix <name> [--surface pi|claude] — returns { ok, skill_prefix } with key always present

  claude: '/skill-multiplexing /skill-using-specialists\n\n'

Core (xt --role) can now consume sp render-skill-prefix instead of building its own /skill: block.

title: sp skill-pool isolation gap: RPC path never emits --no-skills; script path only on empty list
description:
Discovered during the xt --role launcher redesign audit (core xtrm-osipt follow-up #2). sp does NOT isolate pi's global skill auto-discovery pool from a specialist's system prompt.

FINDINGS (verified 2026-07-15):
- src/pi/session.ts (RPC/interactive path — sp run, chain execution, node members, use_specialist tool): --no-skills is emitted NOWHERE. Base spawn args (session.ts:640-648) carry --no-extensions/--no-session/--offline/--no-context-files/--no-prompt-templates/--no-themes but NOT --no-skills. Skills are added additively via --skill (session.ts:663-666). => pi's global auto-discovery (~/.pi/agent/skills/ + repo-local .pi/skills/) is ALWAYS active; every discoverable skill's name+description contaminates the specialist system prompt, and an unrelated skill body can auto-load on a fuzzy task match. This is the dominant runtime path.
- src/specialist/script-runner.ts:1116-1117 (script/serve path): 'if (skillPaths.length === 0) args.push("--no-skills"); for (const skillPath of skillPaths) args.push("--skill", skillPath);'. => isolated ONLY when the specialist declares zero skills; the moment a specialist declares any skills.paths, --no-skills is dropped and the global pool leaks alongside the declared ones.

IMPACT: prompt-surface contamination + non-deterministic skill activation. Parallel to core's xtrm-osipt (skill-body injection) but distinct: this is sp-side pool ISOLATION, not body injection.

PROPOSED FIX (not yet implemented — survey only): emit --no-skills UNCONDITIONALLY on both paths, then re-add the specialist's declared skills.paths via --skill. This makes the discovery pool == declared skills exactly, matching the launcher redesign contract.

SEMANTIC-CHANGE FLAG: any specialist currently relying on an ambient global skill it does NOT declare in skills.paths would lose it. There is no per-specialist 'inherit global pool' opt-out today (skill_inherit only adds one named parent skill, still via --skill; it is not a pool-passthrough). If isolation is adopted, audit specialists for undeclared-but-relied-on skills and document the change in specialists-creator SKILL.md + docs.

Refs: core xtrm-osipt (skill-body injection twin), launcher redesign audit request + follow-up #2 in /home/dawid/dev/core/.xtrm/worktrees/core-xt-claude-luho/.xtrm/tmp/.
notes: AUDIT (2026-07-15, static): 25 specialists × 53 ambient skills (51 user-global ~/.pi/agent/skills/, 2 config/skills, 0 repo-local). Zero undeclared references detected via /skill: refs, 'use the X skill' pattern, and bareword matches (>=4 chars). No known regression surface — safe to flip. Runtime smoke deferred unless a regression surfaces post-merge.
close_reason: --no-skills emitted unconditionally on both pi/session.ts base args and script-runner.ts. Static audit: 25 specialists × 53 ambient skills, zero undeclared references. Tests + tsc green.
