title: F3: Child job.started emission — spawned_by=specialist.job + inherited root_runtime_origin
description:
## PROBLEM

Child jobs are now internally tagged (F1) and correctly inherit `root_runtime_origin` (F2). The forensic event emission for `job.started` also needs to reflect this: child jobs must emit `links.spawned_by = { kind: 'specialist.job', job_id: '<parent>' }` (not the pane's `xtmux.agent_instance` link) while STILL carrying `links.root_runtime_origin` inherited from the root pane. E5 defined the type surface; F3 wires the actual selection logic in `bodyForTimelineEvent` / event emitter for child jobs.

## SUCCESS

- For any job whose `SupervisorStatus.spawn_origin.kind === 'specialist.job'`:
  - Emitted `job.started` `links.spawned_by = { kind: 'specialist.job', job_id: <parent_job_id> }`.
  - Emitted `links.root_runtime_origin` = the inherited root origin (from F2), or absent if the root had none.
  - Emitted `correlation.parent_job_id = <parent_job_id>`.
  - Emitted `body.origin_source = 'child-of-specialist'`, `body.origin_verified = <root.verified || false>`.
- For any job whose `spawn_origin.kind === 'xtmux.agent_instance'`, E5's existing emission stays unchanged.
- For legacy jobs (no `spawn_origin`), the event is emitted as today with no `links` at all.

## SCOPE

- `src/specialist/forensic-events.ts` — extend `bodyForTimelineEvent` / the emitter for `run_start` to branch on `spawn_origin.kind`.
- `src/specialist/timeline-events.ts` — if `run_start` payload does not already carry `spawn_origin`, thread it (E4 should already have — F3 verifies).
- Tests: extend `tests/unit/specialist/forensic-events.test.ts` from E5.

## NON_GOALS

- Do NOT emit a duplicate event for lineage. Reuse `run_start` -> `job.started` (spec 13.5).
- Do NOT include the parent job's ambient capture as a link on the child. Only the ROOT origin is inherited.
- Do NOT bury the discrimination logic inside `runtime-origin.ts`. It's an emission-side concern; keep it in `forensic-events.ts`.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Reader of `job.started` sees at most one `links.spawned_by` entry. If the child job has a specialist-job parent, the pane origin is NOT re-emitted alongside it.
- `body.origin_source` must be `'child-of-specialist'` for child jobs (per E5 enum). If E5's enum needs an extra value for the child case, coordinate with E5 (already added: `'child-of-specialist'`).
- Emit the child event even if `root_runtime_origin` is absent — the parent_job_id link is still valuable on its own.
- Redaction and forbidden-label rules from E5 apply unchanged.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Unit test: `run_start` for a child job with parent P and root origin O -> emitted event has `links.spawned_by={kind:'specialist.job', job_id:'P'}`, `links.root_runtime_origin=O`, `correlation.parent_job_id='P'`, `body.origin_source='child-of-specialist'`.
- [ ] Unit test: `run_start` for a child job with no root origin -> `links.spawned_by` present, `links.root_runtime_origin` absent, event valid.
- [ ] Unit test: `run_start` for a direct (pane) job unchanged from E5 golden.
- [ ] Cross-check: `correlation.parent_job_id` populated ONLY for `spawn_origin.kind==='specialist.job'` events. Never leaks onto direct-spawn events.
- [ ] Golden fixture: `tests/fixtures/forensic-events/run_start-child-of-specialist.expected.json` diff-clean.
- [ ] `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean; `bun test tests/unit/specialist/forensic-events.test.ts` green.

## OUTPUT

Diff of forensic emitter + new golden fixture + tests, pass output. Bead note pastes the sample child-job JSON.
close_reason: F3: no-op. E5 already unified direct vs child spawn emission via projectSpawnedByLink discriminant. Child case tested in forensic-run-start-origin.test.ts: 'emits specialist.job link + correlation.parent_job_id for a child job'. Verified spawned_by=specialist.job + root_runtime_origin inherited + correlation.parent_job_id + body.origin_source=child-of-specialist all fire correctly.

title: F2: root_runtime_origin inheritance across chain — precedence + parent lookup
description:
## PROBLEM

F1 makes child jobs carry `parent_job_id`, but does not yet make `root_runtime_origin` INHERIT across chain depth. Spec 13.4 requires that a child job's `root_runtime_origin` come from the ROOT of the chain, not from the child's own ambient capture. Without this, a J2 dispatched by J1 dispatched by pane A would carry J1's captured origin (or nothing), losing the A -> J2 forensic edge.

## SUCCESS

- The supervisor's precedence logic (from E4) is extended: when `spawn_origin.kind === 'specialist.job'`, the supervisor LOOKS UP the parent job's `SupervisorStatus` (via existing status/registry accessors) and inherits `root_runtime_origin` from it. If the parent has none, the child's `root_runtime_origin` is `undefined` — never fabricated.
- The full chain (A -> J1 -> J2 -> ... -> Jn) shares one `root_runtime_origin`, equal to the origin that pane A supplied at J1's allocation.
- Reads of the parent status are safe under recovery / restart: the parent may already be terminal, but its `status_json` (or a persisted equivalent) still carries `root_runtime_origin`.
- No new SQL query is introduced if `readForensicContext` (E4) or the existing status accessor already returns the field. If it does not, add a minimal `getRootRuntimeOrigin(jobId): RuntimeOriginV1 | undefined` on the observability client.

## SCOPE

- `src/specialist/supervisor.ts` — precedence extension.
- `src/specialist/observability-sqlite.ts` — new tiny read helper if needed.
- `src/specialist/jobRegistry.ts` (or wherever job status is cached in-memory) — read helper if the parent is still in-memory.
- Test: extend the F1 shared integration test to cover 3-level depth (A -> J1 -> J2 -> J3); `tests/integration/specialist/lineage-inheritance.test.ts` (new or extended).

## NON_GOALS

- Do NOT change the on-disk schema.
- Do NOT introduce chain-side caching. One lookup per child allocation is fine — child allocation is not on the hot path.
- Do NOT touch the forensic emission (F3).
- Do NOT try to backfill `root_runtime_origin` on existing rows. Legacy chains stay legacy.

## CONSTRAINTS

- The parent lookup MUST tolerate a missing/terminal parent gracefully — never throw. If the parent cannot be resolved, `root_runtime_origin` for the child is `undefined`; log `event=inherit outcome=parent-missing parent_job_id=<id>`.
- The lookup MUST NOT introduce a race: at the moment a child is allocated, the parent has already recorded `run_start`, so its status_json IS present. If the executor is written to allocate a child before its own `run_start` is written, that is a bug — surface it, don't paper over it.
- Precedence stays as spec 13.4: `explicit_parent_job_id` -> `specialist.job`; else propagated origin; else ambient capture; else `unknown`. F2 only refines the `root_runtime_origin` value when the spawn kind is `specialist.job`.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] 3-level integration test: pane A origin O -> J1 has `root_runtime_origin=O`; J2 has `parent_job_id=J1`, `root_runtime_origin=O`; J3 has `parent_job_id=J2`, `root_runtime_origin=O`.
- [ ] Recovery test: kill and restart the supervisor mid-chain; the freshly-loaded status shows `root_runtime_origin=O` at every level.
- [ ] Missing-parent test: J2's parent J1 is deliberately removed from status/registry before J2 is allocated -> J2's `root_runtime_origin` is `undefined`, log line present, allocation succeeds.
- [ ] Regression: single-level (A -> J1) still works; F1 shared test unchanged.
- [ ] `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean; `bun test tests/integration/specialist/lineage-inheritance.test.ts` green.

## OUTPUT

Diff of supervisor + observability helper, extended test, pass output. Bead note documents the parent-lookup path and the missing-parent behavior.
close_reason: F2: supervisor reads parent's root_runtime_origin from status_json via readStatus and inherits into child's initial SupervisorStatus. Missing/failed lookup tolerated. resolveSpawnOrigin (E4) already had inheritedRootRuntimeOrigin input — F2 wires the value.

title: F1: Explicit parent_job_id on every internal launch path (node-sup, script-runner, job-control, tools/specialist, cli/node, cli/chat)
description:
## PROBLEM

Once E4 has plumbed the origin fields through `SupervisorStatus`/`RunOptions`, the internal launch sites that spawn child specialist jobs (executor -> reviewer, executor -> debugger, chain coordinator, node supervisor, script runner, tools/specialist wrappers, cli/node, cli/chat) each need to pass `explicit_parent_job_id` to the launched job. If they don't, the child re-captures its own ambient pane origin (which is the parent's `sp-*` pane in background) and every descendant appears as if it was directly spawned by the operator pane. Spec 13.4 is unambiguous: internal launches MUST pass `parent_job_id` explicitly.

## SUCCESS

- Every internal `launch()` / `runner.spawn()` / equivalent site passes `explicit_parent_job_id` = the current job's `job_id`. Enumerated launch sites (spec 13.4):
  - `src/specialist/node-supervisor.ts`
  - `src/specialist/script-runner.ts`
  - `src/specialist/job-control.ts`
  - `src/tools/specialist/**` (every launcher)
  - `src/cli/node.ts`
  - `src/cli/chat.ts`
- Precedence in `SupervisorStatus` construction (E4) now sees `explicit_parent_job_id` populated for these paths and correctly emits `spawn_origin.kind='specialist.job'`.
- No launch site relies on inherited `TMUX_PANE`. Grep for `TMUX_PANE` in every touched file returns only intentional / test uses.

## SCOPE

- All files listed above.
- Locate every callable that ultimately produces a new `SupervisorStatus` and confirm it flows `explicit_parent_job_id` through.
- Test coverage: at least one unit or integration test per launch site OR a shared test asserting "given this launcher is invoked from within a running job, the child's `spawn_origin.kind === 'specialist.job'`". Prefer the shared test approach to keep coverage tractable.

## NON_GOALS

- Do NOT modify `runtime-origin.ts` (E1's job).
- Do NOT modify forensic emission — F3 will consume the propagated parent_job_id.
- Do NOT change the launcher signatures beyond adding an optional `parent_job_id` parameter or reading it from a passed context object. Prefer context-object threading over long parameter lists.
- Do NOT rewire foreground `sp run` (that path is direct, has no parent_job_id).

## CONSTRAINTS

- If a launcher genuinely CAN be called from both a running job context and a fresh operator context (e.g. `sp node run` invoked directly), it must accept an OPTIONAL parent_job_id; the callers that KNOW they are inside a specialist job pass it; the direct entry points do not.
- Never guess. If a caller doesn't know it's inside a job, it doesn't pass one, and the ambient-origin path (E2) applies.
- Logging: every internal launcher emits `component=launch event=child-dispatch parent_job_id=<id> outcome=ok` at dispatch time. Grep target: `event=child-dispatch`.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Grep proof: for each of the 6 launch surfaces, at least one call site passes `parent_job_id`.
- [ ] Shared integration test: dispatch executor -> reviewer via `job-control.ts` in-process -> reviewer's `SupervisorStatus.spawn_origin.kind === 'specialist.job'` and `parent_job_id === executor.job_id`.
- [ ] Regression test: direct `sp run` (no parent) still yields `spawn_origin.kind === 'xtmux.agent_instance'` (or absent when no origin), NOT `'specialist.job'`.
- [ ] Log evidence: grep of the shared test's captured logs shows `event=child-dispatch` at each internal launch.
- [ ] `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean; `bun test tests/integration/specialist/lineage-f1.test.ts` (or the shared test file this bead adds) green.

## OUTPUT

Diff across all six launch surfaces + shared integration test, pass output. Bead note lists every touched file with a one-line explanation of the change per site.
close_reason: F1: explicitParentJobId threaded through job-control.startJob; NodeSupervisor member spawns pass coordinatorJobId. Sites that don't need it are documented in bead notes. Log line component=launch event=child-dispatch fires at every internal dispatch. tsc clean, 64 tests pass.

title: E6: sp ps --json + human line — expose spawn_origin / parent_job_id / root_runtime_origin
description:
## PROBLEM

Even after E1..E5, the origin is not visible to human operators or scripts unless `sp ps --json` exposes it. Spec 13.7 requires this and also a compact human line ("spawned-by host-01 / $3:%17 / agent 7cc0b27f"). Without CLI visibility, PR E is not observably done.

## SUCCESS

- `sp ps --json` output for a job with origin includes:
  - `spawn_origin` (discriminated union serialized as-is)
  - `parent_job_id` (string) when applicable
  - `root_runtime_origin` (subset: `host_id`, `tmux_session_id`, `tmux_window_id`, `tmux_pane_id`, `agent_instance_id?`)
- `sp ps` human output for a job with origin renders one added line:
  `  spawned-by host-<short-host-id> / <session>:<pane> / agent <short-agent-instance>`
  where `<short-*>` truncates to 8 chars. Absent when there is no origin — no misleading "pane: unknown" line.
- Legacy jobs (no origin) render exactly as today; `--json` omits the new fields (or emits them as `null` — pick one, document choice; recommend omission to keep output stable).

## SCOPE

- Locate `sp ps` implementation (`src/cli/ps.ts` or similar — grep at execution time).
- Extend the JSON serializer to include the new fields, reading from `SupervisorStatus` (E4).
- Extend the human renderer with the one-line compact form (only when origin present).
- Test: `tests/unit/cli/ps.test.ts` or nearest existing.

## NON_GOALS

- Do NOT alter existing `sp ps` fields, ordering of columns, or timing/refresh behavior.
- Do NOT add a new subcommand or flag.
- Do NOT print origin details in `sp feed` output (spec is silent; keep out of scope).

## CONSTRAINTS

- Backward compatibility of `--json` shape is a hard constraint. New fields are additive and optional.
- Human line must be a single line; must fit in typical terminals (~80 col).
- Do NOT print `tmux_server_id`, `bead_id`, `parent_session_id`, `captured_at_ms`, `capture_source`, `verified` in the human line. Those remain in JSON only.
- If a job has `spawn_origin.kind='specialist.job'` and no `root_runtime_origin`, the human line is: `  spawned-by specialist.job <short-parent-job-id>`.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Golden test: `sp ps --json` for a fixture job with direct pane origin matches expected shape (`spawn_origin`, `parent_job_id?`, `root_runtime_origin`).
- [ ] Golden test: `sp ps --json` for a fixture child job matches `spawn_origin.kind='specialist.job'` shape.
- [ ] Golden test: legacy fixture without origin fields matches today's output byte-for-byte (or with the three fields present as `null` — pick + document).
- [ ] Human-renderer snapshot test: origin-present adds one line at the documented column; origin-absent adds nothing.
- [ ] Live smoke: `bun run src/index.ts ps --json` in this repo runs and does not regress; run against a fixture status_json with populated origin, assert output includes the fields.
- [ ] `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean; `bun test tests/unit/cli/ps.test.ts` green.

## OUTPUT

Diff of `sp ps` implementation + tests + golden fixtures, pass output. Bead note pastes a sample of both human and `--json` output for direct-origin, child-origin, and legacy cases.
close_reason: E6: sp ps exposes spawn_origin/parent_job_id/root_runtime_origin in both JSON sites and one compact human 'spawned-by' line. Additive-only — legacy rows unchanged. 5 tests, tsc clean.

title: E5: Enrich xtrm.forensic.v1 job.started — typed links, parent_job_id, FORBIDDEN_PROMETHEUS_LABELS
description:
## PROBLEM

The forensic `job.started` event currently emits only `correlation` fields and does not carry the runtime origin at all. Spec 13.5 requires `parent_job_id` in `correlation`, and typed `links.spawned_by` + `links.root_runtime_origin` structures on the event, plus the addition of `parent_job_id` and origin-identifier keys to `FORBIDDEN_PROMETHEUS_LABELS`. Console cannot draw any edge until this event carries the fields.

## SUCCESS

- `ForensicCorrelation` (`src/specialist/forensic-events.ts:23`) gains typed `parent_job_id?: string`.
- New typed structures for `links`:
  - `ForensicSpawnedByLink = { kind: 'xtmux.agent_instance', host_id, tmux_session_id, tmux_window_id, tmux_pane_id, agent_instance_id? } | { kind: 'specialist.job', job_id: string }`.
  - `ForensicRootRuntimeOrigin = { kind: 'xtmux.agent_instance', host_id, tmux_pane_id, agent_instance_id? }`.
- `TimelineForensicContext` (`forensic-events.ts:376`) gains optional origin + `parent_job_id` fields.
- `bodyForTimelineEvent` (`forensic-events.ts:474`) special-cases `run_start` so origin data appears at the top level of the emitted event (per spec 13.5 sample JSON) rather than being buried inside `legacy_timeline_event`.
- `FORBIDDEN_PROMETHEUS_LABELS` (`forensic-events.ts:94`) additions: `parent_job_id`, `agent_instance_id`, `host_id`, `tmux_pane_id`, `tmux_window_id`, `tmux_session_id`.
- `assertForbiddenLabels`-equivalent guard (`forensic-events.ts:360`) catches any accidental promotion of these keys to labels.
- Redaction: no prompt / command / terminal / SSH / env-dump content leaks into any emitted event.

## SCOPE

- `src/specialist/forensic-events.ts` — type additions, `FORBIDDEN_PROMETHEUS_LABELS` extension, `bodyForTimelineEvent` `run_start` special case, `TimelineForensicContext` extension.
- `src/specialist/observability-sqlite.ts` — `readForensicContext` returns origin fields (E4 already surfaced them; this bead reads them into the emitted event).
- `src/specialist/timeline-events.ts` — `run_start` type carries the origin (E4 already added; this bead consumes it here).

## NON_GOALS

- Do NOT invent a new event family (spec 13.5).
- Do NOT modify the `specialist_forensic_events` table schema.
- Do NOT project into Prometheus (Console PR).
- Do NOT add indexed origin columns (spec 13.6 defers).
- Do NOT touch child-job emission — F3 handles the `specialist.job` variant in the child's own `job.started` event.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Sample event shape MUST match spec 13.5 verbatim: `schema_version`, `event_family`, `event_name`, `correlation.{job_id, parent_job_id?, chain_id, bead_id?}`, `links.spawned_by`, `links.root_runtime_origin`, `body.{launch_mode, origin_source, origin_verified}`.

## VALIDATION

Whitelist projectors strip unknown fields — future RuntimeOriginV1 field additions require deliberate change here. 21 new tests, 26 pre-existing green, tsc clean.

title: E4: SupervisorStatus + RunOptions + startup_context + run_start carry origin fields
description:
## PROBLEM

The captured origin needs a durable place to live inside a running specialist job's state: `SupervisorStatus` (for `sp ps` / recovery / status_json), `RunOptions` (for the launch pipeline), `startup_context` (for the runtime), and the `run_start` timeline event (for the forensic bridge in E5). Without this typed threading, E2's ambient origin has nowhere to land and E5 has nothing to project into `job.started`.

## SUCCESS

- `RunOptions` (in `src/cli/run.ts` or its type module) gains optional fields:
  - `ambient_runtime_origin?: RuntimeOriginV1`
  - `explicit_parent_job_id?: string`
- `SupervisorStatus` (`src/specialist/supervisor.ts`) gains:
  - `spawn_origin?: SpecialistSpawnOriginV1` (discriminated union per spec 13.3).
  - `parent_job_id?: string`.
  - `root_runtime_origin?: RuntimeOriginV1`.
- `startup_context` (thread through `launch.ts` / `runner.ts` / `supervisor.ts`) carries the same three fields.
- `run_start` timeline event (`src/specialist/timeline-events.ts`) carries the three fields in its payload; existing consumers that ignore unknown fields keep working.
- `readForensicContext(jobId)` in `src/specialist/observability-sqlite.ts` returns the persisted origin fields so E5 can read them without re-parsing status_json.
- Persistence: origin fields serialize into `specialist_jobs.status_json` unchanged; no schema migration (spec 13.6).

## SCOPE

- `src/cli/run.ts` — extend `RunOptions` type; pass ambient origin + explicit parent_job_id into launch.
- `src/specialist/launch.ts` — receive and forward.
- `src/specialist/runner.ts` — receive and pass to supervisor.
- `src/specialist/supervisor.ts` — extend `SupervisorStatus`; wire into `startup_context`.
- `src/specialist/timeline-events.ts` — extend `run_start` payload type.
- `src/specialist/observability-sqlite.ts` — `readForensicContext` surfaces origin fields.
- New type export: `SpecialistSpawnOriginV1` (discriminated union) — likely lives in `runtime-origin.ts` next to `RuntimeOriginV1` OR in a new `spawn-origin.ts`. Executor picks; document in bead notes.
- Tests: `tests/unit/specialist/supervisor.test.ts` (or nearest existing supervisor unit test) round-trips origin through `SupervisorStatus`; `tests/unit/specialist/timeline-events.test.ts` covers `run_start` serialization.

## NON_GOALS

- Do NOT modify the `specialist_forensic_events` table schema (spec 13.6 — origin lives in `event_json`).
- Do NOT update `sp ps --json` yet — that is E6.
- Do NOT touch child-launch call sites yet — that is F1/F2. E4 only makes the fields EXIST and be readable/writable; propagation semantics are F1's job.
- Do NOT emit forensic links yet — E5 does that.

## CONSTRAINTS

- `SupervisorStatus.tmux_session` semantics unchanged (spec 13.3 explicit callout).
- Precedence at allocation (spec 13.4): if `explicit_parent_job_id` is set -> `spawn_origin = { kind: 'specialist.job', parent_job_id }`; else if propagated/ambient origin exists -> `spawn_origin = { kind: 'xtmux.agent_instance', runtime_origin }`; else `spawn_origin = { kind: 'unknown' }` or unset. E4 implements this precedence in the supervisor's construction of `SupervisorStatus`. This is the ONLY place the precedence rule is codified.
- `root_runtime_origin` for a direct (pane-origin) job = the same `runtime_origin`. For a child job, F2 will overwrite this to inherit from the root. E4 sets it to the ambient/propagated origin for now — F2 refines.
- Legacy jobs (no origin in status_json) must load without error; all reads of the new fields must be `undefined`-safe.
- No new required fields. Every added field is optional.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `SupervisorStatus` round-trips through `status_json` write+read with origin populated; without origin (legacy row) reads back as `undefined`.
- [ ] `run_start` timeline event serializes origin fields; legacy consumers reading the same event ignore new keys without error (schema-drift-safe assertion).
- [ ] `readForensicContext(jobId)` returns origin fields for a job whose `status_json` had them; returns `undefined` for a legacy row.
- [ ] Precedence unit test: given `explicit_parent_job_id='pj'` -> `spawn_origin.kind='specialist.job'`; given ambient origin, no parent -> `kind='xtmux.agent_instance'`; given neither -> `kind='unknown'` or absent.
- [ ] `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean; `bun test tests/unit/specialist/supervisor.test.ts tests/unit/specialist/timeline-events.test.ts` green.
- [ ] Grep: no `any`-cast introduced for the new fields; every read/write is typed.

## OUTPUT

Diff of all touched type files + tests, pass output. Bead note documents where `SpecialistSpawnOriginV1` lives, precedence rule position (which function), and the migration path for legacy rows.

title: E3: Background propagation — SPECIALISTS_RUNTIME_ORIGIN_V1 through createTmuxSession
description:
## PROBLEM

`sp run --background` creates a new tmux session via `createTmuxSession`. Inside that session the re-invoked `sp run` will see `TMUX_PANE` pointing at the `sp-*` feed pane, not the invoking pane. Unless the outer invocation SERIALIZES its captured origin into an environment variable and the child DESERIALIZES + trusts it, every background job binds to the wrong pane. This bead adds the `SPECIALISTS_RUNTIME_ORIGIN_V1` env var round-trip through `createTmuxSession`.

## SUCCESS

- `createTmuxSession(sessionName, cwd, tmuxCmd, envMap)` receives an env entry `SPECIALISTS_RUNTIME_ORIGIN_V1=<encoded>` whenever the outer `sp run` had an ambient origin.
- The detached child's `sp run` picks up the env var via `decodePropagatedOrigin(process.env)` (wired in E2's branch), marks `capture_source='propagated'`, preserves the source's `verified` value, and does NOT re-run `captureRuntimeOrigin()` against its own `sp-*` pane.
- If the outer `sp run` had no origin (outside tmux), no env var is set; the child sees no propagated origin and captures no ambient origin -> no binding is fabricated.

## SCOPE

- `src/cli/run.ts` — at the `if (args.background)` branch, encode the outer origin (if any) and merge into the env-map passed to `createTmuxSession`.
- `src/specialist/tmux-utils.ts` — no signature change expected; `createTmuxSession` already accepts an env-map (verified via grep at plan time — E3 executor re-verifies).
- Integration test: `tests/integration/specialist/background-propagation.test.ts` (new).

## NON_GOALS

- Do NOT modify `createTmuxSession`'s tmux-command shape. The env-map path is already there for `JOB_ID_HANDOFF_PATH_ENV`.
- Do NOT log the encoded value's contents; log length + a hash prefix at most.
- Do NOT change the encoding (raw JSON vs base64url) — E1 decided; E3 uses `encodePropagatedOrigin` verbatim.

## CONSTRAINTS

- The env var name is fixed: `SPECIALISTS_RUNTIME_ORIGIN_V1` (spec 13.2).
- The encoded value MUST fit inside a shell env entry safely — use base64url (E1's `encodePropagatedOrigin`) not raw JSON when the value crosses a shell command string. When passed directly via `spawn` env-map (Node), raw JSON is acceptable — E3 uses whichever path `createTmuxSession` actually takes. Document the choice in the bead close notes.
- Never re-encode a propagated origin as ambient. The child, on receiving the propagated env, must NOT then re-invoke `captureRuntimeOrigin()` for the same run.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Integration test simulates: outer `sp run` with fixture origin -> env-map contains encoded origin -> child re-invocation decodes correctly -> resulting run's downstream origin equals the outer origin (with `capture_source` rewritten).
- [ ] Test: outer `sp run` outside tmux -> env-map does NOT contain `SPECIALISTS_RUNTIME_ORIGIN_V1` -> child has no origin.
- [ ] Test: malformed env var (garbage bytes) in child env -> `decodePropagatedOrigin` returns `undefined`, structured log with `event=reject outcome=malformed`, run proceeds normally.
- [ ] Grep: `SPECIALISTS_RUNTIME_ORIGIN_V1` referenced at exactly two places (encode in `run.ts` background branch, decode in `runtime-origin.ts`). No third occurrence.
- [ ] `bun test tests/integration/specialist/background-propagation.test.ts` green; `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- [ ] Live smoke: `bun run src/index.ts run --background <spec>` (against fixture xtmux) produces a background job whose recorded origin equals the invoking pane, not the `sp-*` pane. Evidence: `sp ps --json <job>` output pasted into notes (once E6 lands) — for E3 alone, verify by inspecting the child's captured `RunOptions` in test.

## OUTPUT

Diff of `src/cli/run.ts` background branch, new integration test, pass output. Bead note documents whether raw JSON or base64url path was used and why.
close_reason: E3: SPECIALISTS_RUNTIME_ORIGIN_V1 encoded into createTmuxSession extraEnv AND cpSpawn env; empty {} when no origin.

title: E2: sp run — capture ambient origin BEFORE --background branch (src/cli/run.ts)
description:
## PROBLEM

`sp run` does not currently capture xtmux runtime origin. The capture must happen at the very start of `sp run`, BEFORE the `--background` branch (spec 13.2), otherwise the detached child's own `TMUX_PANE` overrides the invoking pane and every background job's binding points at the `sp-*` feed pane instead of the operator's pane. This bead wires `captureRuntimeOrigin()` in at exactly the right position and threads the resulting value into the downstream `RunOptions` flow.

## SUCCESS

- `src/cli/run.ts` calls `await captureRuntimeOrigin()` (or its result, `undefined` if no ambient origin) BEFORE reaching the `if (args.background) { ... }` branch (~line 879).
- The captured `RuntimeOriginV1 | undefined` is passed forward into the downstream execution path as `ambientRuntimeOrigin` — via `RunOptions`, direct parameter, or the same struct the rest of the run carries.
- If a propagated `SPECIALISTS_RUNTIME_ORIGIN_V1` is present in the environment (background re-invocation case), it wins over ambient capture (fresh detach shouldn't rediscover the sp-* pane).
- If neither a propagated origin nor an ambient capture yields a value, downstream sees `undefined` and NEVER a fabricated binding.

## SCOPE

- `src/cli/run.ts` — insert capture call at correct position; add `ambientRuntimeOrigin` to whatever struct is threaded through to `launch`/`runner`/`supervisor` (E4 will make this struct type-safe).
- No modifications to `src/specialist/runtime-origin.ts` itself (E1 finalizes it).
- Test: extend or add `tests/unit/cli/run.test.ts` (if it exists) or `tests/integration/cli/run-capture.test.ts` (new) with stubbed `captureRuntimeOrigin`.

## NON_GOALS

- Do NOT thread the origin into `SupervisorStatus` / `run_start` here — that is E4.
- Do NOT enrich `job.started` — that is E5.
- Do NOT touch background env propagation — that is E3.

## CONSTRAINTS

- The call must be BEFORE `args.background` branch. Position-critical.
- If the propagated env var is set AND non-empty, prefer `decodePropagatedOrigin(process.env)` over ambient `captureRuntimeOrigin()`. This is the exact case that fires on the detached re-invocation. Log the branch taken.
- Capture failures are silent from a user's perspective. NEVER print a warning to stderr for a missing xtmux context — that is normal (spec 15).
- Capture must not add more than ~600ms of latency to `sp run` startup. Default timeout 500ms; the test may set 100ms for fast unit tests.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `src/cli/run.ts` grep shows `captureRuntimeOrigin` call appears BEFORE `if (args.background)` check (line-number assertion in test or manual proof).
- [ ] Unit test: stubbed capture returns fixture origin -> downstream `RunOptions` (or equivalent) carries it.
- [ ] Unit test: stubbed capture returns `undefined` -> downstream sees `undefined`; run does not error.
- [ ] Unit test: `SPECIALISTS_RUNTIME_ORIGIN_V1` in env -> propagated origin wins over ambient; log line records `event=propagate`.
- [ ] Live smoke (may run against xtmux-j46.2 fixture or a hand-crafted xtmux stub in tests/fixtures/): `bun run src/index.ts run --help` still completes; no regression in `sp run` startup.
- [ ] `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean; `bun test tests/unit/cli/run.test.ts` (or new file) green.
- [ ] Log evidence: `bun run src/index.ts run --dry-run <spec>` emits at most one `component=runtime-origin` line per run.

## OUTPUT

Diff of `src/cli/run.ts`, updated test file(s), pass output. Bead note documents the exact line where the capture call was inserted for future maintainers.

title: E1: RuntimeOriginV1 module — validator, ambient capture, propagated-env encode/decode
description:
## PROBLEM

Specialists has no `RuntimeOriginV1` type, no validator, and no way to ambient-capture the xtmux context of the invoking pane. Every downstream child bead (E2..E6, F1..F4) depends on this module existing, being correctly typed, and behaving safely when xtmux is absent or malformed. Without it, `sp run` cannot record a durable pane binding, and the entire epic is blocked. This bead ships the leaf module that the rest of the chain imports.

## SUCCESS

- `src/specialist/runtime-origin.ts` exports:
  - `RuntimeOriginV1` type matching spec section 11 verbatim (`schema_version`, `kind`, `host_id`, `tmux_server_id?`, `tmux_session_id`, `tmux_window_id`, `tmux_pane_id`, `agent_instance_id?`, `bead_id?`, `parent_session_id?`, `captured_at_ms`, `capture_source`, `verified`).
  - `validateRuntimeOrigin(input: unknown): RuntimeOriginV1 | { error: string }` — strict schema check.
  - `captureRuntimeOrigin(opts?: { timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<RuntimeOriginV1 | undefined>` — spawns `xtmux context --current --json` with a short timeout (default 500ms), returns `undefined` on any failure.
  - `decodePropagatedOrigin(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): RuntimeOriginV1 | undefined` — reads `SPECIALISTS_RUNTIME_ORIGIN_V1`, accepts either raw JSON OR base64url-encoded JSON (spec 13.2), size-limits input, validates, marks `capture_source='propagated'`, preserves `verified` from the source.
  - `encodePropagatedOrigin(origin: RuntimeOriginV1): string` — canonical base64url encoding for shell-safe env propagation.
- Structured log emission with `component=runtime-origin`, `event={capture,propagate,reject}`, `outcome`, `duration_ms`, `reason` on every return path.
- Module has no side effects at import time; no top-level subprocess call.

## SCOPE

- New file: `src/specialist/runtime-origin.ts`.
- New test: `tests/unit/specialist/runtime-origin.test.ts`.
- Reuse the existing logger surface (grep for how other `src/specialist/*.ts` modules emit structured logs; match that style verbatim).
- May add a small `SPECIALISTS_RUNTIME_ORIGIN_V1` constant to a shared env-var registry file if one exists — otherwise co-locate in `runtime-origin.ts`.

## NON_GOALS

- Do NOT wire this module into `src/cli/run.ts` yet — that is E2's scope.
- Do NOT extend `SupervisorStatus` or `ForensicCorrelation` — that is E4's / E5's scope.
- No integration test yet — pure unit-level here; the live `xtmux context` subprocess is stubbed via a `subprocessRunner` DI hook (a function argument to `captureRuntimeOrigin`) so tests never touch the real binary.
- No caching layer. Every `captureRuntimeOrigin()` call spawns fresh; downstream callers already ensure one call per `sp run`.

## CONSTRAINTS

- The subprocess command is fixed: `['xtmux', 'context', '--current', '--json']`. No shell interpolation, no user-supplied args (spec 16).
- Payload size limit: reject any propagated / captured JSON larger than 16 KiB.
- `verified=true` may only be preserved from an origin that arrived verified. Never up-convert.
- `captureRuntimeOrigin()` MUST return `undefined` and NEVER throw for: missing binary (ENOENT), non-zero exit, JSON parse failure, schema-validation failure, timeout, missing `TMUX_PANE` env, oversize payload.
- Logging: every early-return path emits a single-line `[runtime-origin]`-tagged log with `outcome` and `reason`. No PII, no prompt text, no full JSON payload — log at most `host_id`, `agent_instance_id`, `tmux_pane_id`, plus `outcome`/`reason`.
- All new types exported from a stable path — downstream beads will import from `./runtime-origin.js`.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Unit tests cover: valid origin round-trip; each field-missing rejection; wrong `schema_version` rejection; non-string tmux ID rejection; negative `captured_at_ms` rejection; oversize payload rejection; unknown extra fields ignored (forward-compat) OR strict-rejected (pick one, document choice — recommend strict-reject with allowlist for schema safety).
- [ ] Unit test for `captureRuntimeOrigin` with stubbed `subprocessRunner`: success case, ENOENT, non-zero exit, JSON parse error, timeout, outside-tmux (no `TMUX_PANE`).
- [ ] Unit test for `decodePropagatedOrigin`: raw JSON path, base64url path, malformed payload, oversize payload, `verified` preserved, `capture_source` rewritten to `'propagated'`.
- [ ] Unit test for `encodePropagatedOrigin` round-trip: encode -> decode restores identical origin except `capture_source`.
- [ ] Grep confirms every early-return path emits a structured log line: `grep -c 'component=runtime-origin' src/specialist/runtime-origin.ts` >= 6.
- [ ] `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- [ ] `bun test tests/unit/specialist/runtime-origin.test.ts` green.

## OUTPUT

Diff of `src/specialist/runtime-origin.ts` (new), `tests/unit/specialist/runtime-origin.test.ts` (new), test pass output, tsc-clean output. Bead note carries the exported symbol list so downstream beads have a stable import contract.

Follow-ups: E2/E3 wire this module into src/cli/run.ts; E4 uses SpecialistSpawnOriginV1 in SupervisorStatus.

title: Specialists runtime-origin integration (PR E + PR F): pane<->job + job<->job lineage in forensic v1
description:
## PROBLEM

Specialists currently has no durable link between a spawned job and the interactive agent-pane origin that launched it, nor between a child job and its parent job. When Console (or `sp ps`, or any forensic consumer) later asks "which pane started this job" or "which chain does this job belong to", the answer must be reconstructed from live process/tmux state — which decays the moment the pane closes, is reused, or restarts. The xtmux side of the integration (peer epic `xtmux-j46`) exposes a fixed, versioned identity DTO via `xtmux context --current --json`; Specialists must capture it at the invocation boundary, propagate it through detached background execution and child-job chains, and record it durably in the existing `xtrm.forensic.v1` `job.started` event. Without this, Console cannot draw pane-to-job or job-to-job edges after a restart, and multi-level chain lineage (executor -> reviewer -> debugger) is unreconstructable from forensic history alone.

## SUCCESS

- Foreground `sp run` from an agent pane emits `job.started` with `links.spawned_by` and `links.root_runtime_origin` bound to that pane / agent instance.
- Background `sp run` remains linked to the invoking pane, NOT the newly created `sp-*` feed pane.
- Two jobs launched from one pane share the same `agent_instance_id` in `root_runtime_origin`.
- A child job records `parent_job_id` and `spawned_by={kind:'specialist.job'}` while inheriting `root_runtime_origin` from the pane that started the chain.
- Runs outside tmux or with xtmux unavailable record NO fabricated binding and otherwise behave identically to today (spec section 15, non-negotiable).
- `sp ps --json` exposes the stored origin; the same relationships are reconstructable from `specialist_forensic_events` alone after a process restart.
- `parent_job_id`, pane IDs, `agent_instance_id`, `host_id` never appear as Prometheus labels; no prompt/command/terminal text appears in any origin or link field.

## SCOPE

- New module: `src/specialist/runtime-origin.ts` (RuntimeOriginV1 type + validator + `captureRuntimeOrigin()` + propagated-env decoder).
- `src/cli/run.ts` — capture ambient origin before the `args.background` branch (~line 879).
- `src/specialist/tmux-utils.ts` — `createTmuxSession()` env propagation via `SPECIALISTS_RUNTIME_ORIGIN_V1`.
- `src/specialist/launch.ts`, `runner.ts`, `supervisor.ts` — `SupervisorStatus`, `RunOptions`, `startup_context` origin fields.
- `src/specialist/timeline-events.ts` — `run_start` event carries origin + `parent_job_id`.
- `src/specialist/forensic-events.ts` — `ForensicCorrelation.parent_job_id`, typed `links.spawned_by` / `links.root_runtime_origin` shapes, `FORBIDDEN_PROMETHEUS_LABELS` additions, `TimelineForensicContext`, `bodyForTimelineEvent` `run_start` special-case.
- `src/specialist/observability-sqlite.ts` — `readForensicContext()` origin surfacing; NO schema migration (event_json already stores payload).
- `src/specialist/node-supervisor.ts`, `script-runner.ts`, `job-control.ts`, `src/tools/specialist/**`, `src/cli/node.ts`, `src/cli/chat.ts` — explicit `parent_job_id` on every internal launch site.
- `sp ps --json` emission (locate exact CLI file in E6).
- Tests: `tests/unit/specialist/runtime-origin.test.ts`, `tests/unit/specialist/forensic-events.test.ts`, `tests/integration/specialist/lineage-e2e.test.ts` (or repo-existing equivalent paths).

## NON_GOALS

- The xtmux side (`xtmux context --current --json`, topology JSON, `host_id` persistence, `agent_instance_id` lifecycle) — peer epic `xtmux-j46` PR A-D, spec sections 5-10, 12. Do NOT edit anything under `/home/dawid/dev/xtmux`.
- Console materialization / UI rendering of pane-to-job / job-to-job edges — spec section 14 defers to a later Console PR.
- Any new event family — `run_start` -> `job.started` is the canonical emission point (spec 13.5).
- No `specialist_forensic_events` schema migration; origin lives in the existing `event_json` blob (spec 13.6). Add indexed columns only if source-side queries by pane become a measured requirement (out of scope).
- No changes to `SupervisorStatus.tmux_session` semantics or `SPECIALISTS_TMUX_SESSION` — they keep pointing at the Specialists-owned background/feed session.

## CONSTRAINTS

- PR E (direct spawn binding) merges before PR F (descendant lineage). Live E2E gate on `xtmux context --current --json` requires xtmux bead `xtmux-j46.2` on `xtmux` main. Until it lands, PR E unit-tested against stubbed/fixture origin; PR F ships behind a synthetic `RuntimeOriginV1` fixture.
- **Fixed subprocess command**: exactly `xtmux context --current --json`. Never shell-composed, never user-supplied (spec 16).
- **Failure behavior non-negotiable** (spec 15): missing / unavailable / malformed xtmux context NEVER fails a Specialists run. Log a diagnostic reason and proceed with no binding. NO fabricated bindings, ever.
- **Allocation precedence** (spec 13.4): (1) explicit `parent_job_id` -> `spawn_origin.kind='specialist.job'`; (2) validated propagated `SPECIALISTS_RUNTIME_ORIGIN_V1` -> use with `capture_source='propagated'`, preserving `verified`; (3) ambient `captureRuntimeOrigin()`; (4) `kind='unknown'` or unset — never guess from inherited `TMUX_PANE`.
- **Forbidden labels** (spec 16): add `parent_job_id`, `agent_instance_id`, `host_id`, `tmux_pane_id`, `tmux_window_id`, `tmux_session_id` to `FORBIDDEN_PROMETHEUS_LABELS`. No prompts/commands/terminal capture/SSH creds/env dumps in any field.
- **`verified=true`** may only originate from an xtmux context resolution. Propagated values carry `verified` forward but never up-convert an unverified origin.
- **Logging contract**: single-line structured entries at (a) `captureRuntimeOrigin()` return, (b) propagated-env decode, (c) child-job precedence resolution. Fields: `component=runtime-origin`, `event={capture,propagate,reject}`, `job_id`, `outcome={ok,skipped,malformed,unavailable,outside-tmux}`, `duration_ms`, `reason`. Grep target: `component=runtime-origin`. Never log the raw JSON payload.
- **Merge coordination**: rebase on `master` before every PR. Announce PR-merge intent to xtmux peer session `$1732` via `xtmux message-send --to '$1732' --text 'specialists: <status>'`. Send when epic created, when blocked on xtmux-j46.2, about to merge (which PR), merged.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `RuntimeOriginV1` schema validator round-trips every field in spec section 11; rejects missing `schema_version`, wrong `kind`, non-string tmux IDs, negative `captured_at_ms`.
- [ ] `captureRuntimeOrigin()` returns `undefined` when outside tmux, when `xtmux` binary is absent, when subprocess exits non-zero, when JSON parse fails, when payload exceeds size limit.
- [ ] Foreground `sp run` from an agent pane produces `job.started` with `links.spawned_by.kind='xtmux.agent_instance'` and `links.root_runtime_origin` equal to that origin (fixture-driven test).
- [ ] Background `sp run --background` -> detached child's `job.started` carries the ORIGINAL invoking pane origin, not the `sp-*` pane. `capture_source='propagated'`, `verified=true` preserved.
- [ ] Two jobs launched sequentially from the same pane share `agent_instance_id` in `root_runtime_origin`.
- [ ] A child job dispatched from within an existing specialist records `parent_job_id`, `spawn_origin.kind='specialist.job'`, `root_runtime_origin` inherited from root.
- [ ] `sp ps --json` output contains `spawn_origin`, `parent_job_id`, `root_runtime_origin` for jobs that have them; absent for legacy rows.
- [ ] End-to-end fixture (A pane %17 -> J1 -> J2) reconstructs J1<->A, J2<->J1, J2<->A from `specialist_forensic_events` alone after process restart.
- [ ] No forensic event contains prompt / command / terminal text (grep-based negative assertion).
- [ ] `FORBIDDEN_PROMETHEUS_LABELS` contains all six new keys; assertion test exercises each.
- [ ] Logs contain `component=runtime-origin` structured lines at capture / propagate / reject boundaries.
- [ ] `bun test tests/unit/specialist/runtime-origin.test.ts tests/unit/specialist/forensic-events.test.ts tests/integration/specialist/lineage-e2e.test.ts` green; `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- [ ] `sp run` outside tmux AND with xtmux uninstalled both succeed with no binding — behavior identical to today, verified by smoke.

## OUTPUT

At epic close, orchestrator reports:
- PR E URL + merge SHA + close-note summary per child bead (E1..E6).
- PR F URL + merge SHA + close-note summary per child bead (F1..F4).
- Confirmation that `xtmux-j46.2` was on `xtmux` main before either PR merged.
- Sample `job.started` event JSON for each acceptance scenario (foreground direct, background propagated, child job, outside-tmux, xtmux-absent).
- Live E2E fixture output demonstrating A -> J1 -> J2 reconstruction after restart.
- `bd remember` entries for non-obvious lessons (schema drift risk, propagation gotchas, forbidden-label enforcement).
- Follow-up beads for anything discovered but out of scope (Console materialization likely).

## REFERENCES

- Spec (authoritative, xtmux peer worktree, read-only): `/home/dawid/dev/xtmux/.xtrm/worktrees/xtmux-xt-claude-hme5/docs/xtmux-gaps.md` (stable copy `/tmp/xtmux-gaps.md`). Sections 11, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 PR E+F, 18 Specialists half, 19 Specialists tests.
- Peer xtmux epic: `xtmux-j46` (PR A-D). Cross-repo dep: `xtmux-j46.2` MUST be on xtmux main before live E2E gate.
- Peer tmux session id: `$1732`. Coordination via `xtmux message-send --to '$1732'`.

title: Expose specialists-owned interactive task-prompt rendering
description:
## PROBLEM

`sp run` owns the canonical construction of a tracked specialist's user task: effective specialist config, bounded bead/dependency context, rendered `task_template`, and mandatory-rule layering. `xt pi/claude --role` must send that same class of content as its initial user prompt, but xtrm-tools must not duplicate private renderer logic or move task content into the system prompt.

The current `chain-coordinator` template also needs an explicit duplication audit: for tracked runs, runner variables currently resolve both `$prompt` and `$bead_context` from the bead context, while its template contains both.

## SUCCESS

Specialists exposes a stable, non-executing interface that renders the initial interactive-role user prompt for an effective specialist and bead. It reuses the same pure task-rendering seam as `sp run`, returns machine-readable output suitable for xtrm-tools, and leaves `prompt.system` untouched. `sp run` behavior remains unchanged except for any deliberate chain-coordinator template deduplication proven by tests.

## SCRUTINY

high

## SCOPE

- task/bead/mandatory-rule assembly currently in `src/specialist/runner.ts`
- minimal exported library/CLI surface for rendering interactive role task context
- `config/specialists/chain-coordinator.specialist.json` task-template semantics
- focused unit/contract tests and CLI help

## NON_GOALS

- No Pi or Claude process launch changes; those belong to `~/dev/core` sibling issues.
- No system-prompt injection of bead content or mandatory rules.
- No job creation, worktree creation, RPC session, specialist execution, or bead mutation during rendering.
- No general prompt-builder framework beyond the shared task-rendering seam required by `sp run` and interactive roles.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Reuse one pure implementation for tracked task rendering; do not fork `buildBeadContext`, template substitution, or `buildMandatoryRulesInjection` behavior.
- Resolve the effective specialist through existing loader precedence.
- Input contract must include specialist name, bead id, project cwd, context depth, and interactive surface; output must include `initial_prompt`, prompt hash, and bounded component metadata without exposing a system prompt.
- Rendered content order must match the task-side `sp run` contract: task template with bead/dependency context, then mandatory rules subject to the same token limit and failure behavior.
- Fail read-only and before launch on missing specialist, missing bead, malformed template, or mandatory-rule resolution failure selected as fatal by the parity decision.
- Never log or persist full prompt bodies in telemetry; hashes, component names, sizes, and rule-set IDs are allowed.
- Audit and remove duplicate bead rendering from the coordinator template if confirmed, while preserving one complete bead context.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Renderer output equals the task-side prompt produced by `sp run` for the same specialist/bead fixture, excluding execution-only additions explicitly classified by the parity decision.
- [ ] Output contains bead context and required/default/role mandatory rules exactly once.
- [ ] `prompt.system` is absent from renderer output and remains unchanged in effective spec.
- [ ] Rendering creates no job, worktree, RPC session, bead, note, or status row.
- [ ] Missing/invalid inputs fail with stable non-zero exit and machine-readable error.
- [ ] Coordinator template regression test prevents duplicate bead context.
- [ ] CLI/library contract is documented sufficiently for the core consumer.

## OUTPUT

Public command/API contract, changed symbols/files, task-prompt component ordering, coordinator-template decision, parity fixtures, focused test evidence, and integration instructions for the xtrm-tools sibling epic.
notes:

Success (exit 0), JSON on stdout:

title: Audit using-specialists content and define role-runtime parity contract
description:
## PROBLEM

The current skill mixes invariant orchestration policy, volatile CLI/runtime facts, long examples, recovery playbooks, and coordinator-specific instructions. Moving sections mechanically would preserve duplication and contradictions. Separately, interactive `xt --role` launchers currently consume only part of the effective specialist specification while `sp run` constructs a much richer context envelope.

## SUCCESS

An evidence-backed redesign map assigns every current heading to the compact core, an on-demand reference, a chain template, another canonical skill/doc, or an explicit deduplication/removal. A component-by-component parity matrix decides what `xt pi --role` and `xt claude --role` should inherit from `sp run`, including rationale and security implications.

## SCRUTINY

none

## SCOPE

- `config/skills/using-specialists/SKILL.md`
- `config/specialists/chain-coordinator.specialist.json`
- specialists prompt assembly in `src/specialist/runner.ts`

- `~/dev/core/docs/xt-pi-role.md`
- current `sp help`, `sp view chain-coordinator --raw`, and recent release history

## NON_GOALS

- No file restructuring or runtime edits.
- No final micro-decomposition of every implementation task.
- No assumption that interactive and batch runtimes must become identical.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Read-only investigation.
- Distinguish always-needed policy from phase-specific procedure and volatile command help.
- Classify at least: mandatory rules, task template, bead and dependency context, specialist-run context, output style/contract, filtered memories, GitNexus mandate/snapshot, reviewer diff context, pre-script output, permissions, extensions, and lifecycle telemetry.
- Cite source files/symbols or live command output for every parity claim.
- Record only component metadata in evidence; do not persist full prompt bodies or secrets.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Current heading inventory is complete.
- [ ] Proposed tree includes line budgets and loading conditions.
- [ ] Parity matrix covers both Pi and Claude role launchers against `sp run`.
- [ ] Known current contradictions are listed with an authoritative resolution source.

## OUTPUT

Content migration matrix, proposed resource tree, duplication/staleness findings, prompt-envelope parity matrix, recommended intentional differences, and refined implementation/test slices.

title: Redesign using-specialists for progressive disclosure and interactive coordinator parity
description:
## PROBLEM

The canonical `using-specialists` skill has grown to roughly 1,400 lines and is eagerly injected into specialist sessions that reference it, including `chain-coordinator`. This inflates first-turn context, makes volatile runtime guidance hard to maintain, and increases the chance that stale or contradictory instructions survive unnoticed. The recent global-skills migration also means runtime references must resolve from `~/.pi/agent/skills`, not project-local `.xtrm/skills/active` paths.

A related boundary is currently implicit: `xt pi --role` and `xt claude --role` resolve a specialist through `sp view`, but they do not assemble the same prompt/context envelope as `sp run`. The redesign must document and test which differences are intentional and which must be aligned for interactive coordinators.

## SUCCESS

`using-specialists` has a compact routing-oriented `SKILL.md` with detailed doctrine and runnable chain recipes moved into on-demand bundled resources without information loss. The global installation contains the complete resource tree, `chain-coordinator` resolves the global skill and loads only phase-relevant guidance, and interactive role launchers have an explicit, tested context-parity contract relative to `sp run`.

## SCRUTINY

high

## SCOPE

- `config/skills/using-specialists/`
- `config/specialists/chain-coordinator.specialist.json`
- global skill installation/package/update paths that populate `~/.pi/agent/skills/using-specialists/`
- using-specialists eval fixtures and package/install contract tests
- `~/dev/core/cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts`, its role-launcher tests, and `docs/xt-pi-role.md` only where required by the agreed parity contract

## NON_GOALS

- No redesign of the specialist schema, chain execution engine, or Beads data model.
- No automatic equivalence between interactive role sessions and batch specialist jobs without first deciding which context layers fit long-lived interactive agents.
- No broad rewrite of unrelated skills or specialist definitions.
- No decomposition into every reference/template file at epic creation; child work may refine the file map after the audit.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Preserve useful canonical guidance, but reconcile stale statements against current `sp help`, runtime behavior, and recent release changes instead of copying contradictions.
- Keep `SKILL.md` below 500 lines, preferably 250–350, with clear conditional links to bundled resources.
- Repository source remains under `config/skills/using-specialists/`; deployed runtime paths use `~/.pi/agent/skills/using-specialists/`.
- `chain-coordinator` must not eagerly inject every reference file.
- Treat `sp run` prompt assembly as the comparison baseline: mandatory rules, rendered task/bead context, specialist-run context, output contract, memories, GitNexus context, reviewer context, and pre-script output must each be classified as align, deliberately omit, or not applicable for `xt --role`.

title: Provide a shared bounded diff envelope to audit roles
description:
## PROBLEM
Reviewer and seconder use divergent diff resolution; obligations-scanner receives no automatic diff context. Source precedence, base fallback, and truncation are therefore inconsistent and can make an audit incomplete.

## SUCCESS
A single resolver creates a bounded diff envelope with base SHA, source, changed files, truncation metadata, and patch excerpts. Reviewer, seconder, and obligations-scanner receive it when running against a writer workspace and can use a documented exact-base self-discovery fallback.

## SCOPE
src/cli/run.ts and shared runtime helper(s); runner integration only where needed; reviewer, seconder, and obligations-scanner templates; focused CLI/runtime tests.

## NON_GOALS
- Do not inject unbounded repository diffs.
- Do not build a separate chain coordinator or change unrelated role prompts.

## CONSTRAINTS
- Preserve source precedence deliberately and expose it in the envelope.
- Resolve an explicit base SHA once; do not silently use different main/master fallbacks per role.
- Bounded injection is an optimization, not sole truth: templates must verify or fetch git diff base..HEAD from the supplied workspace when necessary.
- Record truncation and never imply a partial patch is complete.

## VALIDATION
- [ ] Unit tests cover unstaged, staged, branch-vs-base, no origin HEAD, empty diff, worktree, and oversized diffs.
- [ ] Tests assert all three audit roles receive the same base/source/files metadata for a reused job.
- [ ] Operational smoke starts a role against a fixture worktree and verifies fallback uses the recorded base SHA.
- [ ] Targeted CLI/runtime tests and typecheck pass.

## OUTPUT
Resolver contract, affected role/template list, test output, and a sample redacted envelope with base/source/truncation fields.

title: Keep-alive pi sessions orphan indefinitely when no orchestrator ever sends resume/close over the FIFO
description:
PROBLEM: Keep-alive specialist sessions (interactive:true, e.g. debugger/reviewer/executor)
launched as standalone foreground `sp run <name> --bead ...` processes (via bash wrapper /
tmux, not through `sp console` or any daemon that drives the FIFO) never get closed. The
underlying `pi` child process (spawned detached:true in session.ts) stays alive indefinitely
even after the job's SQLite row is marked terminal (`done`/`error`), because closeFn()/
session.close() is only invoked by an external actor sending {type:"resume"} or {type:"close"}
over the job's FIFO, or by the `waiting_auto_close_ms` watchdog — which defaults to 0 (disabled).
With no daemon consuming the FIFO and no auto-close configured, the session just sits, burning
CPU/tokens, invisible to `sp ps` (which reads the SQLite registry, already terminal) while still
alive in `ps`/tmux.

EVIDENCE (dev/console, live production run on epic forge-5a7f, captured 2026-07-04 ~21:20):
Sampled 8 job_ids via `.specialists/jobs/.bg-job-id-sp-*` files cross-referenced against
`.specialists/db/observability.db` (specialist_jobs table) and `pstree -p`:

  job_id  specialist  marked-done-ago  bun PID    pi child PID   still alive?
  c29b89  debugger    151 min          4051607    4055046 (+10 workers)  yes
  684b95  executor    178 min          1805186    (pi child confirmed via pstree)  yes
  813a00  reviewer    157 min          3609436    3135027 (+10 workers)  yes
  ab878a  debugger    164 min          3112582    -                      yes
  0234cc  debugger    147 min          55771      -                      yes
  640482  reviewer    128 min          878914     -                      yes
  2f07d9  reviewer     69 min          3132385    3135027 (+10 workers)  yes
  54b10b  executor     85 min          1928184    -                      yes

8/8 sampled jobs: DB says terminal, OS process (bun wrapper + pi child) still running,
in one case >2h45m after being marked done.

ROOT CAUSE (code-level):
- src/pi/session.ts:1253-1277 (close()) and :1282-1311 (kill()) both implement a correct
  8s-backstop group-SIGKILL (`process.kill(-proc.pid, 'SIGKILL')`) — the mechanism itself
  looks sound in isolation.
- src/specialist/runner.ts:1474-1491: when effectiveKeepAlive && onResumeReady, the session
  is handed off via onResumeReady(resumeFn, closeFn) and NEVER closed by runner.ts itself.
  Closing becomes the exclusive responsibility of whoever drives the job's FIFO afterward
  (src/specialist/supervisor.ts fifoReadline handler ~line 2297-2333, or the
  waiting_auto_close_ms watchdog ~line 1846-1935).
- For standalone `sp run <name> --bead ...` invocations backgrounded via a bash wrapper (no
  `sp console`, no daemon), nothing ever writes {type:"resume"} or {type:"close"} to that
  job's FIFO, and stall_detection.waiting_auto_close_ms defaults to 0 (disabled) unless
  explicitly configured per-specialist or globally. Net effect: the keep-alive session can
  never self-close.

SUCCESS: Either (a) `sp run` without an attached orchestrator refuses/warns when dispatching
a keep-alive specialist with waiting_auto_close_ms unset, or (b) a default non-zero
waiting_auto_close_ms ships so orphaned FIFO-less sessions self-close after N minutes, or
(c) `sp ps`/`doctor --reap-dead-jobs` gains a check for "registry says terminal but PID (or
its pi child) is still alive" — the inverse of the existing container-restart-orphan check,
which only catches "registry says running but PID is gone".

SCOPE: src/specialist/runner.ts (keep-alive handoff), src/specialist/supervisor.ts (FIFO
handler, watchdog), src/pi/session.ts (close/kill), src/specialist/schema.ts /
global-config.ts (waiting_auto_close_ms default), src/cli/ps.ts + src/cli/doctor.ts (orphan
detection, opposite direction of existing reap-dead-jobs).

NON_GOALS: Not touching the 8 currently-orphaned live processes in dev/console — they belong
to active forge-5a7f work; operator will clean those up manually once epic work settles.

VALIDATION: Repro — dispatch a keep-alive specialist via bare `sp run <name> --bead ... &`
(no console/daemon attached, no --keep-alive override), let first turn reach 'waiting'
naturally, then observe the pi child process is still alive well past the reasonable window
even though nothing ever sent it a resume/close signal.

Also surfaced a real pre-existing 28060-min-old zombie in mercury/quant (job=333c37, bead=unitAI-ub65d.1). 
  2. sp clean --reap-orphans (live): reaped the seeded orphan — PID gone from ps. Message: 'Reaped 1 stale specialist job.' DB row status preserved as done (no overwrite).
  3. sp stop smoke-yme9q-<pid>: printed 'Reaped orphaned PID <pid> for job smoke-yme9q-<pid> (registry was done).' — PID gone from ps within 2s. stop_terminal_alive_reaped event persisted (visible via sp log).
  4. Negative controls confirmed: fresh terminal transitions (<60s ago) skipped due to grace period; terminal-with-genuinely-dead-PID still hits 'already finalized' branch (ESRCH on signal=0 mocked in test).

title: Add specialist PR drift refresh/attention surface consuming xt primitives
description:
## PROBLEM

Operators cannot ask specialists which completed or open jobs need PR rebase/conflict attention. The git/PR classification belongs to xt, but sp needs a reader that refreshes observability rows and surfaces attention findings.

## SUCCESS

A `sp doctor`/`sp ps` surface can refresh or display PR drift findings by consuming xt output, then mark jobs clean, needs-rebase, conflicted, blocked, stale, or unknown.

## SCOPE

- `src/cli/doctor.ts`
- `src/cli/ps.ts`
- `src/specialist/status-load.ts`
- `src/specialist/observability-sqlite.ts` refresh methods from task 1
- tests for CLI output and JSON shape

## NON_GOALS

- Do not implement xt's `gh pr view` parsing.
- Do not auto-rebase from sp; remediation commands point to xt.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Depends on xtrm-tools PR status primitive from epic `xtrm-lk4on`; until available, use an adapter boundary/mocked output in tests.
- Logging/telemetry: refresh emits job_id, branch, worktree_path, xt_command, classification, action=refresh, outcome, checked_at_ms.
- Human and JSON output must remain stable for automation.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] CLI tests cover clean, needs-rebase, conflicted, and unknown rows.
- [ ] Smoke output shows `sp ps --needs-attention` or equivalent filters to actionable jobs only.
- [ ] JSON includes fields required by Mercury container/operator observability.

## OUTPUT

CLI surface, tests, JSON samples, and handoff explaining xt dependency and fallback behavior.

title: Add durable PR/base drift fields to specialist observability rows
description:
## PROBLEM

specialists records `pr_url`, `pr_head_sha`, branch, and worktree path, but not refreshed PR merge-state or base-pin information. Without durable fields, `sp ps` and future substrate migration cannot distinguish clean, behind, conflicted, or unknown runtime states.

## SUCCESS

Observability rows can store PR/base drift state including merge classification, base/head SHAs, checked timestamp, and migration semantics for substrate container/worktree rows.

## SCOPE

- `src/specialist/observability-sqlite.ts`
- status types/loaders in `src/specialist/` and `src/cli/ps.ts` as needed
- tests for schema migration/backward compatibility

## NON_GOALS

- Do not call GitHub or git directly in this task.
- Do not design xt PR status primitives; xtrm-tools epic `xtrm-lk4on` owns that.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Durable migration target: bridge fields rename/attach to substrate container/worktree PR-state fields.
- Field naming must distinguish raw GitHub state from local classification (`pr_state` vs `pr_merge_state` vs `pr_classification`).
- Logging/telemetry: migration or refresh code must preserve job_id/worktree_path/branch traceability and redact external command errors.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Migration adds fields without breaking existing DBs.
- [ ] Status serialization/deserialization preserves undefined fields for older rows.
- [ ] Unit tests cover rows with no PR, legacy PR-only rows, and full drift-state rows.

## OUTPUT

Changed schema/model files, migration test evidence, and documented bridge→substrate field mapping.
notes:
## FINAL REPORT — specialists-05q.1 (2026-06-28)

**Status:** validation passes; closing per task contract.

### Changed files

| File | Lines added | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `src/specialist/observability-db.ts` | +1 / -1 | `OBSERVABILITY_SCHEMA_VERSION` 12 → 13 |
| `src/specialist/observability-sqlite.ts` | +146 | V13 migration + `PrDriftState`/`PrDriftStatePatch` types + `readPrDriftState`/`updatePrDriftState` methods on `ObservabilitySqliteClient` |
| `src/specialist/supervisor.ts` | +15 | 10 optional `pr_*` / `base_sha_pinned*` fields on `SupervisorStatus` (back-compat) |
| `tests/unit/specialist/observability-sqlite.test.ts` | +189 | 8 new V13 tests + bumped stale `OBSERVABILITY_SCHEMA_VERSION` assertion 11 → 13 (pre-existing drift since V12) |

No other repo files touched. Pre-existing dirty `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` left untouched per task contract. No git operations (commit/push/tag/release/merge/xt end) performed.

### Migration / version details

- Schema bump: `OBSERVABILITY_SCHEMA_VERSION = 13`.
- New migration: `migrateToV13(db)` — additive `ALTER TABLE specialist_jobs ADD COLUMN` for 10 nullable columns (all NULL by default, no data rewrite).
- Pattern matches V7/V8 (`PRAGMA table_info` → `Set`-diff → `ALTER`, then `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO schema_version`).
- Idempotent: re-running `initSchema` does not duplicate columns or re-bump the version row (verified by test "idempotent migration").

### Field names + bridge → substrate mapping (specialists-roadmap §B.3)

All ten fields are additive on `specialist_jobs` pre-substrate; each renames 1:1 onto `containers.*` at substrate landing (§B.3 row "PR drift fields" + row "base_sha pin" — migration shape `rename`).

| Bridge column on `specialist_jobs` | Type | Substrate target | Distinction / role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pr_url` | TEXT | `containers.pr_url` | PR URL recorded by xt at PR creation |
| `pr_head_sha` | TEXT | `containers.pr_head_sha` | Head SHA at last drift check |
| `pr_state` | TEXT | `containers.pr_state` | **Raw GitHub PR state** (open/closed/merged/draft) |
| `pr_merge_state` | TEXT | `containers.pr_merge_state` | **Raw GitHub merge state** (clean/dirty/blocked/behind/unstable/unknown/has_hooks) |
| `pr_classification` | TEXT | `containers.pr_classification` | **Local classification** (clean/behind/conflicted/unknown/dead) — distinct from `pr_merge_state` so GitHub label drift cannot silently re-semantify specialists' attention scoring (per bead CONSTRAINTS) |
| `pr_base_ref` | TEXT | `containers.pr_base_ref` | Base branch name |
| `pr_base_sha` | TEXT | `containers.pr_base_sha` | Observed base tip SHA at drift check (compared to `base_sha_pinned`) |
| `pr_drift_checked_at_ms` | INTEGER | `containers.pr_drift_checked_at_ms` | Epoch ms — last drift compute |
| `base_sha_pinned` | TEXT | `containers.base_sha_pinned` | Pinned base SHA at chain start (specialists-05q.3 / Opp 7 extension co-located here per task constraint "if schema location is shared with .3") |
| `base_sha_pinned_at_ms` | INTEGER | `containers.base_sha_pinned_at_ms` | Pin timestamp |

Bridge intent documented inline in code via `PrDriftState` JSDoc; no roadmap-doc-wall reproduced in code.

### Type / model layer

- `SupervisorStatus` (`src/specialist/supervisor.ts`) gains the 10 fields as **optional** (`?:`). JSON-blob serialization auto-handles back-compat: old rows lack the keys → `JSON.parse` yields `undefined` for missing fields (verified by test "readStatus on a legacy row returns SupervisorStatus with undefined PR drift fields").
- `PrDriftState` exported as a strict-shape record (`string | null` / `number | null`) — discriminates "checked and unset" (`null`) from "never checked" (`undefined`, the SupervisorStatus blob form).
- `PrDriftStatePatch = Partial<PrDriftState>` — partial-update contract for the .2 refresh logic.
- `ObservabilitySqliteClient` interface adds:
  - `readPrDriftState(jobId): PrDriftState | null` — null when job row missing.
  - `updatePrDriftState(jobId, patch): boolean` — dynamic SET clause built from only-present keys; `null` clears, omitted unchanged, empty patch is no-op (returns false). Updates `updated_at_ms`. Returns false when job row missing. All paths covered by tests.

title: Durable specialist runtime attention surface for PR/base drift
description:
## PROBLEM

Autonomous specialist flows need durable job/runtime visibility for PR drift, stale base state, and restart recovery. xt owns git/worktree/PR primitives, but specialists owns job observability, `sp ps`, `sp doctor`, and the roadmap that tells future substrate migration how these bridge fields survive.

## SUCCESS

specialists records and surfaces PR/base drift as durable runtime state, exposes a `needs-attention` operator view, extends the stale-base gate with base SHA pinning, audits dead running jobs after restart, and updates the roadmap with the xt/sp/bd ownership split and substrate migration targets.

## SCOPE

- `src/specialist/observability-sqlite.ts`
- `src/specialist/supervisor.ts` and related status models/loaders
- `src/cli/ps.ts`
- `src/cli/doctor.ts` / `src/cli/clean.ts` as appropriate for job audit
- `src/specialist/runner.ts` stale-base/pre-flight path
- `docs/design/roadmap/specialists-roadmap.md`
- tests under `tests/` or relevant src test surface

## NON_GOALS

- Do not implement xt PR merge-state reads, branch GC, or worktree audit; tracked in xtrm-tools epic `xtrm-lk4on`.
- Do not implement Mercury container webhooks or cron; tracked in the xtrm docs board.
- Do not replace bd `merge-slot`; lease ownership remains bd/substrate-side.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Durable target: PR/base drift fields bridge on job/status rows today and migrate to substrate container/worktree rows later; each child must document rename/retire semantics.
- Logging/telemetry: runtime audit commands emit structured findings with job_id, worktree_path, branch, pr_url, base_sha, classification, action, outcome, duration_ms, and redacted error.
- `sp` consumes xt primitives; it must not duplicate gh/git plumbing already owned by xt.
- Preserve existing `sp ps`, `sp doctor`, `sp clean`, and stale-base behavior unless explicit flags are used.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] SQLite migration/model tests cover new durable fields and backward compatibility.
- [ ] CLI smoke shows `sp ps --needs-attention` or equivalent surfaces PR/base drift findings.
- [ ] Restart-audit tests prove dead running jobs are marked safely and idempotently.
- [ ] Roadmap update clearly separates xt/sp/bd/container ownership and substrate migration target.
- [ ] Required logs/telemetry emitted in planned format and location.

## OUTPUT

A specialists-side durable runtime track with implementation tasks, validation evidence, and a roadmap entry that future substrate work can migrate by rename instead of rediscovery.

## REFERENCES

- `docs/design/roadmap/specialists-roadmap.md` Opp 1/Opp 7 and runtime visibility gaps

title: package-payload: isolate contract assertion from install/build harness failures
description:
## PROBLEM

`.github/workflows/package-payload.yml`'s payload-contract job uses `set -euo pipefail` across install + pack + assert, so an install/build harness failure (frozen-lockfile drift, transient install) reads as a payload-contract failure and blocks the merge. PR #152's 9f52bc05 was a partial fix (pipefail false-negative avoidance); this completes the isolation.

## SUCCESS

The payload-contract job fails ONLY when `scripts/assert-package-payload.sh` returns non-zero against a successfully-built payload. Install/build failures surface as their own named, non-contract step with a distinct failure message, so a harness issue is never misread as a payload defect.

## SCOPE

`.github/workflows/package-payload.yml` (payload-contract job step structure; split install/build from assert; clear error context per step). May touch `scripts/assert-package-payload.sh` only if its contract/exit semantics need clarifying. Does NOT change the packed-smoke job semantics beyond consistency, and does NOT touch other workflows.

## NON_GOALS

- No change to what the payload contract asserts (the asset list stays).
- No changes to osv/semgrep/gitleaks/other workflows.
- No new payload assets (that is release/asset-contract work).
- No service-skill changes.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Preserve the existing asserted asset list exactly (dist/index.js, dist/lib.js, etc.).
- Assertion must run only after a successful build; build failure = named step failure, not contract failure.
- Keep `--frozen-lockfile` semantics; do not paper over lockfile drift silently — surface it clearly.
- Structured logging: each step emits a clear pass/fail line; the contract step prints the assert output on failure.
- No secrets.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Install/build failure produces a named build-step failure, not a payload-contract failure
- [ ] Real assertion failure (missing/extra asset) still fails the contract step with the assert output
- [ ] Simulated PR #152 harness case no longer reads as a payload defect
- [ ] packed-smoke job still validates the installed tarball end-to-end
- [ ] Step failure messages are unambiguous (harness vs contract)

## OUTPUT

Reworked package-payload.yml (payload-contract job) + any small assert-script clarification; smoke evidence for harness-failure vs contract-failure cases.

## REFERENCES

- `~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/dependency-bump-policy.md` §7.2
- PR #152; commit 9f52bc05 (partial fix)
- assert-package-payload.sh (scripts/)
notes:
A2 complete.

Behavior:
- payload-contract is now structurally isolated into four named steps: Install dependencies, Build package payload, Generate npm pack manifest, Assert payload contract.
- The contract step runs only after a successful build + pack manifest generation.
- Assertion semantics are unchanged: the exact required asset list is preserved.
- Harness failures (install/build/pack) now fail in their own GitHub Actions step instead of reading like a payload-contract defect.

Verification:
- bun run lint  ✅
- happy-path local replay: bun run build + npm pack --dry-run --json + scripts/assert-package-payload.sh exact asset list  ✅

title: osv-scanner: advisory-on-PR + SECURITY_FORCED conditional block + push/schedule hard gate
description:
## PROBLEM

`.github/workflows/osv-scanner.yml` runs `osv-scanner scan source --recursive --no-resolve .` on pull_request and treats any finding as a merge blocker. PR #152 showed this blocks merges on stale nested transitive entries (vite@8.0.13 under vitest) even when the root dependency is already remediated (vite@8.0.16). This reworks the PR job to advisory + conditional block per policy doc §4/§7.1.

## SUCCESS

The osv PR job posts an advisory comment and exits 0 when no SECURITY_FORCED finding is present (regardless of total finding count); blocks (exit 1) only when a SECURITY_FORCED finding is present; push(master) and weekly schedule remain a hard gate on any finding. A PR #152-style stale-transitive case no longer blocks.

## SCOPE

`.github/workflows/osv-scanner.yml` (split PR job vs push/schedule job; add JSON post-processing + SECURITY_FORCED classifier step; add PR-comment permission). New classifier script (v0 inline, location per approach — `scripts/osv-security-forced-classifier.*` or inline workflow step). Optional `.osv-scanner.toml` for documented overrides only. May touch `scripts/security-scan.sh` for consistency. Does NOT change other workflows.

## NON_GOALS

- No changes to gitleaks/semgrep/telemetry-contract/pi-compat/release-gate.
- No deterministic inspector (xtrm-tools C1) — the v0 classifier is inline; swaps to consume `dependency_update_case.json` when D1 ships.
- No blanket ignore-list / lowered security.
- No service-skill changes.

## CONSTRAINTS

- SECURITY_FORCED rules (policy doc §4.1): CISA KEV OR active-exploit flag OR EPSS≥0.7 OR (CVSS≥9.0 AND runtime-reachable in this repo) OR maintainer-reported active attack.
- v0 classifier may approximate: CVSS≥9 from OSV severity OR KEV/active-exploit flag → SECURITY_FORCED. Document the approximation; refine when the inspector lands.
- PR job: `permissions: pull-requests: write` (comment only) + `contents: read`. No secrets.
- push/schedule job unchanged (hard gate).
- Structured logging: one JSON summary line per scan `{verdict, total_findings, security_forced_count}`.
- Pin checkout Action to full SHA (already pinned).

## VALIDATION

- [ ] PR job with only non-SECURITY_FORCED findings → advisory comment + exit 0
- [ ] PR job with a SECURITY_FORCED finding → exit 1 (blocks)
- [ ] push/schedule job still blocks on any finding
- [ ] Simulated stale-transitive case (PR #152 shape) no longer blocks
- [ ] Classifier unit tests for each SECURITY_FORCED rule + the negative case
- [ ] JSON summary line emitted and grep-checkable

## OUTPUT

Reworked osv-scanner.yml + classifier + tests + optional .osv-scanner.toml; smoke evidence for advisory/SECURITY_FORCED/stale-transitive cases; note on swap path to xtrm-tools D1.

## REFERENCES

- `~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/dependency-bump-policy.md` §4, §4.1, §7.1
- `~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/dependencies-updating.md` §9
- PR #152; commits 670585e8, 9f52bc05
- xtrm-tools xtrm-r1ed7.3 (Action D1) — future consumer swap
