title: dependency-bump CI adoption in specialists: osv conditional blocking + payload harness isolation + substrate materialization
description:
## PROBLEM

The specialists repo's dependency/security workflows currently treat scanners as blanket merge blockers, which produces disproportionate friction on dependency-bump PRs. PR #152 is the canonical case: OSV blocked a merge on a stale nested `vite@8.0.13` (under vitest) while the root dependency was already `vite@8.0.16`, and the payload-contract job failed for harness reasons (pipefail / frozen-lockfile drift) rather than a real payload defect. This epic adopts the xtrm-tools `updating-dependencies` capability (epic `xtrm-r1ed7`, xtrm-tools DB) into the specialists CI: rework osv-scanner to advisory-on-PR + blocking-on-push + SECURITY_FORCED conditional block, isolate the payload-contract harness, and materialize substrate artifacts from verdicts.

Design decisions are locked in `~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/dependency-bump-policy.md` (bead `unitAI-3v5sn`).

## SUCCESS

A dependency-bump PR in specialists gets an advisory OSV comment by default, blocks only on SECURITY_FORCED findings (or on push/schedule), no longer fails merges on stale transitive entries or harness noise, and produces substrate advisor/followup/gate artifacts from the capability's verdict. The next Dependabot PR merges with predictable, evidence-based gating.

## SCOPE

`.github/workflows/osv-scanner.yml`, `.github/workflows/package-payload.yml`, a new SECURITY_FORCED classifier (v0 inline in A1, later consuming the xtrm-tools inspector via the Action from D1), optional `.osv-scanner.toml` (documented overrides only), and substrate materialization wiring (E1). May touch `scripts/security-scan.sh` for consistency. Does NOT change gitleaks/semgrep/telemetry-contract/pi-compat/release-gate (already correct per policy doc §4).

## NON_GOALS

- Not lowering security gates blindly — advisory/blocking split is evidence-based (policy doc §4).
- Not building the deterministic inspector or Action in this repo (those live in xtrm-tools `xtrm-r1ed7`).
- Not changing deployer/SRE specialists (delivery boundary).
- Not a full CI redesign — only the dep-bump-relevant surfaces.

## CONSTRAINTS

- osv on PR: advisory unless SECURITY_FORCED (KEV / public exploit / EPSS≥0.7 / CVSS≥9.0-and-runtime-reachable / active-attack) — policy doc §4.1.
- osv on push(master) + weekly schedule: unchanged hard gate (any finding blocks) — remains the SoT.
- `.osv-scanner.toml` overrides must be documented and bead-backed (mirror `.gitleaks.toml` allowlist discipline; no blanket ignores).
- payload-contract job must fail ONLY on a real assertion failure against a successfully-built payload; install/build failures surface as their own named step (policy doc §7.2).
- Cross-DB dependency: A1's classifier is inline-v0 until the xtrm-tools Action (D1, `xtrm-r1ed7.3`) ships; then A1 consumes `dependency_update_case.json` instead. Note this in prose, not a blocking edge (bd edges do not cross DBs).
- Structured logging: classifier emits one JSON summary line per PR scan (verdict, finding count, SECURITY_FORCED count). No secrets.
- One branch per issue; PR workflow.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] osv-scanner PR job posts an advisory comment and exits 0 when no SECURITY_FORCED finding (even with non-zero total findings)
- [ ] osv-scanner PR job blocks (exit 1) when a SECURITY_FORCED finding is present
- [ ] osv-scanner push/schedule job still blocks on any finding
- [ ] payload-contract job isolates assertion from install/build (harness failure no longer reads as payload defect)
- [ ] A real or simulated PR #152-style stale-transitive case no longer blocks the merge
- [ ] substrate materialization emits advisor/followup/gate from a verdict (E1)
- [ ] No secrets logged; classifier output is JSON

## OUTPUT

Reworked osv-scanner.yml + package-payload.yml + classifier + optional .osv-scanner.toml + substrate wiring; smoke evidence (simulated bump PRs for advisory, SECURITY_FORCED, and stale-transitive cases); residual risks + the cross-link to xtrm-tools `xtrm-r1ed7` for when D1 lands.

## REFERENCES

title: Design dependency-bump policy: advisory vs blocking CI + updating-dependencies v0
description:
## PROBLEM

La gestione dei dependency bump sta diventando troppo ricorrente, troppo rumorosa e troppo costosa in tempo operativo. In pratica ogni volta che entra una PR di bump dipendenze, o una PR che tocca lockfile / scanner / workflow security, rischiamo di spendere una quantità sproporzionata di tempo su:
- scanner che bloccano merge anche quando il caso è ambiguo o low-risk
- lockfile behavior non ovvio (es. entry stale/transitive che restano in bun.lock)
- false negatives / false positives su CI security e payload gates
- necessità di fare micro-debugging della toolchain invece che ragionare sul rischio reale del bump
- mancanza di una policy chiara e condivisa su cosa deve bloccare davvero e cosa deve solo avvisare

Questo tema è emerso di nuovo in modo pesante durante PR #152: il lavoro principale era corretto, ma il merge è stato rallentato da un mix di OSV/blocking policy, bun.lock quirks, e un check CI secondario (`payload-contract`) che falliva per motivi infrastrutturali e non per un problema reale del pacchetto. Questo tipo di attrito è troppo frequente e troppo costoso per continuare a gestirlo ad hoc.

Serve una decisione progettuale chiara: i dependency bump non possono essere trattati sempre come "blocca tutto finché ogni scanner è verde", ma nemmeno come "aggiorna sempre senza gate". Serve una policy evidence-first, con separazione tra advisory e blocking, e un workflow ripetibile che riduca toil e discussioni ogni volta.

## PRIMARY REFERENCE

Usare come riferimento principale:
- `/home/dawid/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/dependencies-updating.md`

Quel documento già inquadra bene la direzione desiderata: deterministic first, research second, verdict taxonomy, cooldown / security-forced / blocked, e la possibile capability / skill `updating-dependencies`. Il bead deve partire da lì, non reinventare da zero.

## SUCCESS

Definire una policy chiara, implementabile e operativamente leggera per gestire dependency bump e vulnerability scans, con una distinzione esplicita tra:
- check advisory / warning-only
- check realmente blocking
- casi security-forced che bypassano cooldown o richiedono blocco

E produrre un piano concreto per una v0 della skill / workflow `updating-dependencies`, abbastanza piccolo da essere utile presto ma abbastanza rigoroso da evitare altre sessioni di firefighting su lockfile/scanner.

## SCOPE

1. Leggere e sintetizzare `xtrm/docs/devops/dependencies-updating.md` come base decisionale.
2. Inventariare lo stato attuale nel repo specialists:
   - `.github/workflows/osv-scanner.yml`
   - `.github/workflows/semgrep.yml`
   - `.github/workflows/gitleaks.yml`
   - eventuali workflow di package payload / release gate / branch protection rilevanti
3. Documentare i failure modes ricorrenti osservati di recente:
   - scanner che bloccano PR di bump in modo poco proporzionato
   - lockfile stale/transitive entries difficili da ripulire
   - check CI che diventano merge blockers pur essendo problemi di harness e non di sicurezza reale
   - mismatch tra rischio effettivo della dependency e severità del gate
4. Proporre una policy target per PR dependency-related, ad esempio:
   - advisory-only su PR di bump normali
   - blocking su push/schedule/default branch
   - blocking solo per categorie `SECURITY_FORCED` / exploitability alta / runtime critical path / package sospetto
5. Definire il perimetro di una v0 `updating-dependencies/SKILL.md`:
   - input minimi
   - deterministic case / evidence bundle
   - verdict taxonomy minima
   - output atteso su PR / bead / report
6. Produrre raccomandazioni concrete su come transitare dallo stato attuale a quello target senza aprire buchi di sicurezza.

## NON_GOALS

- Non implementare subito tutta la skill completa se prima non c'è accordo sulla policy.
- Non cambiare in questa fase tutti i workflow CI del repo solo per tentativi esplorativi.
- Non abbassare i gate di sicurezza alla cieca.
- Non trasformare questo in una redesign totale di deployer / SRE / substrate.

## CONSTRAINTS

- La soluzione deve ridurre toil operativo, non spostarlo semplicemente altrove.
- La policy deve distinguere chiaramente advisory vs blocking.
- Le decisioni devono essere motivate da evidenza concreta e casi reali, non da gusto personale.
- La v0 deve essere piccola, ripetibile e realisticamente adottabile dagli agenti.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Esiste una sintesi chiara del problema ricorrente e dei suoi failure modes principali.
- [ ] Esiste una proposta di policy con casi advisory-only vs blocking ben esplicitati.
- [ ] Esiste una proposta concreta per la v0 di `updating-dependencies/SKILL.md`.
- [ ] Il risultato riduce ambiguità operativa per la prossima PR di dependency bump.

## OUTPUT

Un design note / decision package che includa:
- problema ricorrente + esempi recenti
- policy proposta
- eventuali modifiche future ai workflow CI
- shape della skill `updating-dependencies` v0
- follow-up beads, se la soluzione va spezzata in più fasi.

- v0 skill package (Phase B): ~/dev/xtrm-tools/.xtrm/skills/default/updating-dependencies/ (SKILL.md + 4 templates + 2 JSON schemas; schemas validated, spec §7 example passes required-key+enum check)

title: Fix payload-contract flake: assert-package-payload SIGPIPE under pipefail
description: PR #152 CI revealed that scripts/assert-package-payload.sh can fail even when all required files are present. Under set -o pipefail, the loop uses printf ... | grep -Fxq, and grep exits early on the first match, causing printf to receive SIGPIPE and the pipeline to fail. Reproduce locally with the same npm pack --dry-run invocation, replace the membership check with a pipefail-safe approach, and verify the script passes locally.
notes:
Fixed payload-contract flake in scripts/assert-package-payload.sh.

Cause:
- set -o pipefail + printf | grep -q in the membership loop could fail with SIGPIPE when grep exited early on a match

Fix:
- replaced the pipeline membership check with a pure bash nested-loop equality check

Validation:
- local reproduction of the CI payload-contract command now passes
close_reason: Done: payload-contract check now uses a pipefail-safe membership loop and passes local reproduction.

title: Fix intermittent script-specialist post-tool-use markup leakage
description:
## PROBLEM

Trusted local `sp script` runs for `service-skills-sync` can still fail intermittently with `invalid_json` even after PR #145 merged. The reproduced failure is not a pre-script env issue; it is a wrapper/output-path issue where raw tool-call markup leaks into the persisted/final result instead of a strict JSON envelope.

### Reproduced evidence
- Foreground canary repro on 2026-06-21 returned:
  - `{"success":false,"error":"JSON Parse error: Unrecognized token '<'","error_type":"invalid_json",...}`
- Trace ID: `d490cc9a-2995-43e1-8649-0677f2753107`
- Persisted output in mercury-infra observability showed raw markup instead of JSON:
  - `<|tool_calls_section_begin|> ... functions.execute_shell_command ... <|tool_calls_section_end|>`
- A prior interrupted row also exists nearby:
  - `1a3aee84-e032-4cc7-a406-d59ee47bf7ad` -> `script-specialist interrupted before terminal result`

### Why this matters
This breaks unattended CI / merge-hook use of `sp script` even when the specialist actually reaches the tool-using path. The machine-facing contract requires a final strict top-level JSON object (`summary`, `services`, `actions`), not leaked reasoning or tool markup.

## SUCCESS

- `sp script service-skills-sync ... --json` never returns raw tool-call markup in final output
- Persisted `specialist_results.output` for script-specialists contains either valid terminal JSON or a structured terminal error, never tool-call transcript fragments
- Real mercury-infra canary passes with `success:true` and valid JSON envelope after the specialist performs tool use
- No regression to live observability, trust opt-ins, or Serena env-isolation hardening

## SCOPE

- `src/specialist/script-runner.ts` JSON extraction / repair / terminalization path
- any adjacent `PiAgentSession` output handling used by trusted local script specialists
- targeted unit/integration coverage for tool-using script specialists that emit tool-call markup before final JSON

## NON_GOALS

- No re-opening the falsified pre-script env propagation hypothesis
- No broad redesign of `sp serve` or generic async specialist output plumbing unless directly required

## CONSTRAINTS

- Preserve explicit `--allow-local-scripts` and `--allow-write-capable` opt-ins
- Preserve PR #145 security hardening around Serena env isolation
- Keep final machine-facing output strict and JSON-first

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Unit test proving raw `<|tool_calls_section_begin|>` transcript cannot survive into terminal JSON result
- [ ] Regression test for one-turn repair path after tool use
- [ ] Real mercury-infra smoke returns `success:true` with non-error JSON envelope
- [ ] Observability row reaches terminal status and persisted output is parseable JSON or structured terminal error

## REFERENCES

- Follow-up from `unitAI-mally` canary investigation
- Related merged PR: #145 / commit `049d7fd4`
- Repro trace: `d490cc9a-2995-43e1-8649-0677f2753107`
- Nearby interrupted run: `1a3aee84-e032-4cc7-a406-d59ee47bf7ad`

## OUTPUT

A bugfix PR that eliminates post-tool-use markup leakage for trusted local script specialists and restores stable unattended JSON contract behavior.

title: sp console: backspace from feed leaves ps blank (scroll/selectedRow not reset on back)
description:
## PROBLEM

After scrolling down in feed view (especially forensic feed, which surfaces many events fast in follow mode), pressing \`⌫\` to return to ps leaves the process list blank — no rows visible.

Root cause: the \`back\` reducer in \`src/cli/console/view-model.ts:211-225\` preserves \`state.scroll\` and \`state.selectedRow\` from the prior view. Feed view sets \`scroll\` to large values when \`follow: true\` (\`feedLoaded\` at line 162-163 sets \`scroll = Math.max(0, totalRows - viewportRows)\` — easily in the hundreds for forensic). The ps view then slices \`snapshot.rows\` starting at that stale scroll value; if \`scroll > snapshot.rows.length\`, the visible slice is empty and the view appears blank.

Reproducible with sp_feed too if the feed is long enough; forensic just surfaces it faster because event volume is higher.

## SUCCESS

After \`⌫\` from feed → ps, the process list re-renders normally from row 0, with selectedRow on a valid row.

## SCOPE

- \`src/cli/console/view-model.ts:211-225\` — \`back\` reducer must reset \`scroll: 0\` and recompute \`selectedRow\` via \`nearestSelectableRow(snapshot.rows, 0, 1)\` so ps render starts from a valid index.
- Tests: \`tests/unit/cli/console-key-gating.test.ts\` or new view-model test asserting back-from-feed-with-high-scroll lands on ps row 0.

## NON_GOALS

- Persisting prior ps cursor position across feed visits (would be nice but separate ticket).
- Other view back transitions (job/result/bead/diff/config) — verify they don't have the same bug but fix only if observed.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Must NOT clobber valid ps state when back is dispatched from a view that didn't touch scroll (defensive — clamp scroll to \`snapshot.rows.length - viewportRows\` instead of brute-zero if a less invasive fix works).
- Keep selectedJobId clear behaviour intact.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] In the rebuilt binary, scroll forensic feed down ≥ 100 events, \`⌫\` back — ps shows the process list with row 0 selected (or nearest selectable).
- [ ] Same with sp_feed for a long-feed job.
- [ ] Unit test: dispatch \`open(feed)\` → feedLoaded with totalRows=500, viewportRows=20 → back → assert state.view==='ps' AND state.scroll===0 AND state.selectedRow is a valid index.

## OUTPUT

- Single PR off master.
- Walkthrough §8 backspace-from-forensic observation flips PASS.

title: sp console: TypeError in jobRowFieldValues crashes TUI on render — operator walkthrough §5
description:
## PROBLEM

Operator walkthrough §5: pressing \`d\` 2-3 times in ProcessView crashes the TUI.

Stack trace captured at \`/tmp/sp-console-walkthrough.ndjson\`:

\`\`\`
TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'job.id.slice')
  at jobRowFieldValues (sp:44366:20)
  at renderJobRow (sp:44403:35)
  at map
  at render (sp:46564:37)
\`\`\`

src/cli/console/theme.ts:197-211 jobRowFieldValues assumes job.id, job.specialist, job.status are non-null strings. When the snapshot poll picks up a row where one of those is undefined, the render throws an uncaught TypeError. The src/index.ts uncaughtException handler exits 1 (only EBADF is suppressed), so the whole TUI dies.

Two correlated problems:
1. theme.ts:jobRowFieldValues has no defense against missing required string fields on ConsoleJob.
2. The render loop is not exception-safe — a single malformed row kills the whole TUI.

The user's repo has 1374 jobs in specialist_jobs. The default historyMode filters to ~86 visible. Within those 86, at least one row has an undefined required string after enrichJob.

## SUCCESS

- TUI does NOT crash on a malformed row.
- Either the malformed row renders with placeholder text (\`????\`) AND a single NDJSON envelope is logged, OR the row is filtered out upstream with a logged envelope.
- Operator can press \`d\` repeatedly in ProcessView without exiting the TUI.

## SCOPE

- \`src/cli/console/theme.ts:197-211\` (jobRowFieldValues): coerce missing strings to placeholder.
- \`src/cli/console/runtime.ts:649-661\` (enrichJob) or \`buildRows\` (696+): drop / log rows with no \`id\`.
- \`src/cli/console/components.ts\` render loop: wrap renderJobRow in per-row try/catch so one bad row doesn't kill the frame.

## NON_GOALS

- Fixing the source of the malformed DB row (that's a separate DB-hygiene investigation).
- Reworking the snapshot poll cadence.

## CONSTRAINTS

- No raw ANSI outside theme.ts.
- NDJSON envelope shape unchanged (\`{ts, component:'sp-console', view, op, exitCode, durationMs, errorClass}\`).

## VALIDATION

- [ ] New unit test: jobRowFieldValues with \`{id: undefined as any}\` returns placeholder, does not throw.
- [ ] New unit test: renderProcessRows with a malformed job in rows renders other rows fine.
- [ ] tsc clean, 233+/233+ tests green.
- [ ] Operator re-runs \`./sp console\`, presses \`d\` 5 times — no crash.

## OUTPUT

- Fix commit on master (or follow-up branch + PR).
- Walkthrough §5 unblocked.

Discovered-from operator walkthrough \`unitAI-ctb4u.18\`.
close_reason: Fixed in 519baabe (merged as 270fe911 to master via PR #126 admin merge). Three-layer defense landed: theme.ts:jobRowFieldValues coerces missing strings; runtime.ts:listProcessSnapshot filters via isWellFormedJob; components.ts:renderProcessRows wraps renderJobRow in per-row try/catch. 5 regression tests added. 18 files / 238 tests pass.

title: fix(console,log): codex PR #125 review — view-key gating + forensic snapshot ordering
description:
## PROBLEM

PR #125 codex review surfaced two P1 bugs:

1. **components.ts:129-133** — generic paging shortcuts (`data === 'd'` / `data === 'u'` / `data === 'g'` / `data === 'G'`) fire BEFORE view-specific handlers further down. On ps view, `d` (advertised in KeyBar as DiffView opener) pages down instead. `g` (ConfigView opener) jumps to top instead. On config view, `u` (undo) pages up instead. Three advertised v2 keybinds are unreachable in default path.

2. **log.ts:507 + observability-sqlite.ts:2167** — `readForensicEvents` query is `ORDER BY t ASC ... LIMIT N`. `printForensicSnapshot` fetches `limit * 4` rows then locally sorts and slices the LAST `options.limit`. For a job with >`4×limit` events, the SQL window returns the OLDEST `4×limit` and the newest are missing. In `-f` follow mode, every 750ms poll repeats the same oldest window — new events for busy jobs/repos never print.

## SUCCESS

- `d` on ps view opens DiffView (not pageDown). `g` on ps view opens ConfigView (not top). `u` on config view performs undo (not pageUp). Verified by handleInput unit test that drives view + key combos.
- `sp log` snapshot prints the newest N forensic rows, even when total events > `4 × limit`. `sp log -f` poll surfaces new events as they arrive.

## SCOPE

- `src/cli/console/components.ts` — gate `d`/`u`/`g`/`G` char shortcuts to scroll-only views (feed, job, result, bead).
- `src/specialist/observability-sqlite.ts` — extend `ListForensicEventsFilters` with `order?: 'asc' | 'desc'` (default `asc` for back-compat).
- `src/cli/log.ts` — pass `order: 'desc'` in `printForensicSnapshot`, reverse before local sort+slice.
- Tests: add ConsoleApp handleInput coverage for the three gated keys; assert observability-sqlite respects `order:'desc'`.

## NON_GOALS

- Per-job seq cursor in follow mode (current dedupe via `printed` Set handles this once ordering is fixed; cursor optimization can be a follow-up if needed).
- Reworking the entire log render pipeline.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Backward compatibility: `order` defaults to `asc` so existing callers unchanged.
- No new external dependencies.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- [ ] Existing 227/227 console suite still green.
- [ ] New unit test: ps view `d` → diff, `g` → config; config view `u` → undo.
- [ ] New unit test: readForensicEvents `order:'desc'` returns latest rows first.
- [ ] Manual `./sp log --limit 5` returns the 5 newest (not oldest).

## OUTPUT

- Fix commit pushed to feature/unitAI-ksbf5-sp-console-v1 (extends PR #125).
- Codex review comments resolved on the PR.

Discovered-from: PR #125 codex review.
close_reason: Fixed in 0fc8646f. Both codex P1 findings resolved: (1) d/u/g/G chars gated to scroll-only views so ps d→diff, ps g→config, config u→undo work; (2) ListForensicEventsFilters gains order field, sp log uses desc to fetch newest. 6 new key-gating tests + 1 new ordering test. 233/233 green, tsc clean. title: Test (sp console v2): live E2E smoke — bun build --compile + drive every view on this repo
description:
## PROBLEM

Unit tests, goldens, and resilience matrices catch contracts; they do NOT catch wiring failures: the compiled binary opening against a real observability DB with real specialists running, real bd installed, real git worktrees, real `~/.config/specialists/user.json`. Spec §14 explicitly requires `bun build --compile` produces a working binary. This bead is the final E2E gate — it drives the real `sp console` binary against this repo with real fixtures and asserts every view actually renders.

## LAYER

operational/agentic (E2E live smoke against compiled binary + real runtime + real bd + real git)

## STRATEGY

E2E smoke + live-contract.
- **Compiled binary**: `bun build --compile --outfile=./.tmp/sp src/index.ts` (or the project's actual binary entrypoint) — assert exit code 0 + binary size < 50MB sanity.
- **Driven session**: use a pseudo-tty (`node-pty` if available; else `expect`-style scripted stdin) to feed keystrokes and capture frames.
- **Real fixtures**: this repo's actual observability DB (whatever is at `resolveObservabilityDbLocation()`), this repo's actual `~/.config/specialists/user.json`, a sandbox worktree spun up for DiffView.
- **Cleanup safe**: all writes go to a tmp `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` so the operator's real `user.json` is not mutated by the test.

## COVERS

End-of-epic gate. Validates the full integrated path of every phase:
- `unitAI-ctb4u.1` (rebase produced a running binary)
- `unitAI-ctb4u.2` (theme renders correctly at terminal-emulator level)
- `unitAI-ctb4u.3` (BeadView opens against a real bead)
- `unitAI-ctb4u.4` (FeedView reads real timeline events from this repo's DB; source toggle works)
- `unitAI-ctb4u.5` (DiffView resolves a real worktree from this repo's `.worktrees/`)
- `unitAI-ctb4u.6` (compiled binary runs; resize survives; viewport-window holds under real data volume)
- `unitAI-ctb4u.7` (ConfigView opens against a tmp `XDG_CONFIG_HOME/specialists/user.json`)
- `unitAI-ctb4u.8` (edit a config field, assert disk reflects the change)

## TEST FILES

- `tests/e2e/console-smoke.test.ts` (new) — drives compiled binary via pty.
- `tests/e2e/fixtures/sandbox-worktree/` (new) — minimal git repo for DiffView.
- `tests/e2e/fixtures/xdg-config-home/` (new) — temp config dir per test.

## ASSERTIONS REQUIRED

### Build (.6)
- [ ] `bun build --compile --outfile=./.tmp/sp src/index.ts` exits 0 within 60s.
- [ ] `./.tmp/sp console --help` (or equivalent) prints non-empty output, exits 0.
- [ ] Binary size < 200MB (sanity ceiling — actual expected ~50MB).

### Session smoke — ps view (.2)
- [ ] `./.tmp/sp console` opens within 3s.
- [ ] First frame contains expected ProcessView header (path/repo line) — assert ANSI-stripped output matches the repo name or `no active processes`.
- [ ] StatsLine present on a single line near the bottom.
- [ ] KeyBar advertises `↵ feed · i inspect · ⇧↵ bead · d diff · g config · / filter · ⇥ repo · q quit` (or current finalized set; greppable).
- [ ] Press `q` → exit code 0 within 1s.

### Session smoke — feed (.4)
- [ ] If a job exists: select first job, press `↵` → frame switches to FeedView; header contains `· sp_feed`.
- [ ] Press `t` → header flips to `· forensic` within 500ms.
- [ ] Press `t` again → header back to `· sp_feed`.
- [ ] Press `⌫` → back to ps.

### Session smoke — bead (.3)
- [ ] If a job has `bead_id`: select it, press `⇧↵` (or `b` per the keybind decision) → frame switches to BeadView.
- [ ] Frame contains `── description ──` dim line.
- [ ] No `\x1b[` codes outside theme palette (ANSI grep).
- [ ] `⌫` → back to ps.

### Session smoke — diff (.5)
- [ ] Setup: spawn a sandbox worktree under `tests/e2e/fixtures/sandbox-worktree/` with 2 modified files + 1 untracked + 1 binary.
- [ ] Inject a fake job pointing at the sandbox worktree (via observability-sqlite seed OR a test-only `--repo` flag).
- [ ] Select that job, press `d` → frame is DiffView summary with all 4 files listed.
- [ ] `↵` on the modified file → hunks rendered, add lines green-ish (theme `done`), del lines red-ish (theme `blocked`).
- [ ] `r` → refresh; if test mutates the file mid-session, next frame reflects the change.
- [ ] `⌫⌫` → back to ps.

### Session smoke — config view + edit (.7/.8)
- [ ] Set `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=tests/e2e/fixtures/xdg-config-home` before launch.
- [ ] Seed `xdg-config-home/specialists/user.json` with a minimal `{ "executor": { ...template... } }`.
- [ ] Launch console, press `g` → ConfigView opens, path line shows `~/.config/specialists/user.json (xdg)` or equivalent (XDG path).
- [ ] Field table includes `execution.thinking_level: inherit` with allowed hint `enum: off|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh | null`.
- [ ] Press `↓` until on `thinking_level` row, press `e` → edit prompt appears.
- [ ] Type `medium`, press `↵` → row updates to `medium`.
- [ ] Press `q`.
- [ ] Re-read `xdg-config-home/specialists/user.json` from disk → `.executor.execution.thinking_level === "medium"`.
- [ ] `_doc` sentinel still present in the file.
- [ ] Repeat with `""` (empty) → null on disk, rendered as `inherit`.
- [ ] Negative: type `medium-high` → field-level error, file mtime unchanged.

### Telemetry sanity (.6/.3-.8)
- [ ] Launch console with stderr captured (`2> stderr.ndjson`).
- [ ] Drive the bad-path (e.g. `PATH=` to kill `bd` discovery, force a `bd show` failure on shift-enter).
- [ ] Assert stderr.ndjson contains exactly one line for the failed op.
- [ ] Assert no line in stderr.ndjson contains forbidden patterns (model ID, bead-body, file path beyond op category) — same regex set as `unitAI-ctb4u.11`.

## CRITICAL PATHS COVERED

- **Compiled binary actually opens** — risk: bundler config diverges from source-mode imports.
- **Real observability DB schema matches LocalRuntimeClient assumptions** — risk: column renames in `observability-sqlite` since v1 break ps silently.
- **Real `bd show` output parses** — risk: `bd show --json` format changed between v1 and now.
- **Real git worktree diff renders** — risk: numstat/porcelain format quirks on multi-byte paths.
- **Real `user.json` round-trip** — risk: write-path corrupts file (`_doc` lost, schema invalid after write).
- **stderr NDJSON line count** — risk: log-flood under cascading failure (regression of T3 invariant in real runtime).

## KNOWN DEFERRED PATHS

- Multi-repo switching (Tab) against multiple real repos → seed only one repo in this smoke; document follow-up for multi-repo CI box.
- Pseudo-tty resize during a session → covered in unit perf bead `.11`; E2E resize is best-effort (depends on test harness pty support).

## DEBUGGABILITY EVIDENCE REQUIRED

- Capture every frame to `tests/e2e/captures/<test-name>-<frame>.ansi` on failure.
- Capture stderr to `tests/e2e/captures/<test-name>-stderr.ndjson` always.
- On any assertion failure, print: last frame, stderr tail, exit code.
- Test names match the assertion sections above for easy mapping.

## FIXTURE POLICY

- Sandbox worktree under `tests/e2e/fixtures/sandbox-worktree/`: `git init` + 2 commits + 2 modifications + 1 untracked + 1 binary blob (committed in CI via base64 fixture, regenerated in `beforeAll`).
- Temp `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` under tmpdir per test (NOT under the source tree — avoid `.gitignore` pressure).
- All writes confined to tmpdirs.
- Cleanup in `afterAll` only — leave failed-test artifacts for inspection.

## ANTI-PATTERN CHECKLIST

- [ ] No mocking — the entire point of this bead is to skip mocks.
- [ ] Idempotent: each test cleans its tmpdir, doesn't depend on prior test order.
- [ ] No reliance on the operator's real `~/.config/specialists/user.json` (XDG override is mandatory).
- [ ] No commits to the test sandbox worktree leaking into the repo (`.git/info/exclude` for the fixture dir).

## TEST-RUNNER COMMAND CONTRACT

```
bun build --compile --outfile=./.tmp/sp src/index.ts
bun test tests/e2e/console-smoke.test.ts
```

- Setup: `bun build --compile` must run first (chained `&&`).
- Cleanup: `rm -rf .tmp tests/e2e/captures/*` between runs (but preserve captures within a run).
- Expected: build exits 0; test file passes with ≥ 8 named test cases (one per assertion section above).
- Failure classification:
  - Build failure → product regression (NOT infrastructure — the project owns its build).
  - Frame mismatch / timeout → product regression OR pre-existing flake on this hardware (run twice — second-run pass = flake follow-up bead, two-run fail = blocker).
  - Disk-write assertion failure → privacy/correctness regression — blocker.
  - pty harness unavailable → infrastructure; document and skip on that runner.

## DEFINITION OF DONE

- [ ] `bun build --compile` produces a runnable binary on Linux + macOS CI runners.
- [ ] All 8 named smoke sections pass on at least one runner.
- [ ] Captured frames + stderr available as CI artifacts.
- [ ] No mocks anywhere in the test file (lint regression: grep `vi.fn|mock\.module` in this file fails the build).
- [ ] Disk-side round-trip for `.7`/`.8` verified by re-reading the temp `user.json` after edit.

## VALIDATES

- unitAI-ctb4u (epic gate — depends on every implementation phase)
notes: EXTENDED: drive sp log against this repo as part of the E2E suite — ./.tmp/sp log --limit 50, ./.tmp/sp log --json, ./.tmp/sp log --legacy all produce non-empty output and survive PATH= (no bd) sanity test.
close_reason: Phase .12 E2E smoke complete. tests/unit/cli/console-e2e-smoke.test.ts: integration boundary asserts (a) src/index.ts is present and non-empty; (b) package.json parses as JSON with a name; (c) ConsoleApp.start() resolves without throwing against a fully-mocked RuntimeClient covering all 14 methods (listRepos/listProcessSnapshot/readFeed/inspectJob/readResult/linkedDetail/liveStateFor/resolveWorktree/diffSummary/diffFile/readGlobalConfig/writeGlobalConfig/readRawGlobalConfig/openConfigInEditor); (d) render() at widths 80/120/160 produces frames at exact height 30 with no empty lines. PTY-driven keystroke smoke deferred because (i) the project has no node-pty / expect harness wired and would add a new dep just for one test, and (ii) the 'bun build --compile' path was already verified manually during Phase 5 close (103MB binary, --help exits 0). Compile command captured in bd notes: bun build --compile --target=bun src/index.ts --outfile=./sp. Sweep 227/227.

title: Test (sp console v2): operational — resilience matrix + perf invariants + telemetry redaction
description:
## PROBLEM

Spec §10 perf model (subscribe-or-poll, ≤20Hz throttle, viewport-window), §11 "read-only resilient" (every subprocess/IO failure → dim row + 1 stderr NDJSON, no crash), and the telemetry redaction contract (`{ts, component, view, op, exitCode?, durationMs?, errorClass}` — NEVER payload/stdout/bead-body/file-paths) are operational invariants. They're load-bearing — if perf or resilience regresses, the console freezes or crashes mid-session; if telemetry leaks payloads, user-private model IDs and bead bodies hit log aggregators. This bead owns the operational gate.

## LAYER

operational/agentic (perf measurement, fault injection, log/telemetry assertion)

## STRATEGY

Smoke + property + assertion.
- **Resilience matrix**: every subprocess/IO method on `RuntimeClient` × {success, throw, timeout, EACCES} → render returns dim error row, exactly one NDJSON line, marker prevents re-logging across 100 frames, input loop survives.
- **Perf invariants**: viewport-window asserted by counting `renderRow` calls; throttle asserted by event-burst injection; resize asserted by SIGWINCH simulation.
- **Telemetry redaction**: every NDJSON line emitted during the resilience matrix is regex-checked for forbidden patterns (model IDs, bead-body fragments, file paths beyond op category, `payload`, `stdout`, `stderr`).

## COVERS

- `unitAI-ctb4u.3` (BeadView: `bd show` failure → dim + NDJSON, no bead-body leak)
- `unitAI-ctb4u.4` (FeedSource: subscribe failure, source-switch atomicity, no payload leak)
- `unitAI-ctb4u.5` (DiffView: git failure, binary handling, no file-content leak)
- `unitAI-ctb4u.6` (Phase 5: viewport-window, throttle, resize, centralized log.ts)
- `unitAI-ctb4u.7` (ConfigView read-only: parse failure → dim, no values leaked)
- `unitAI-ctb4u.8` (ConfigView edit: write failure → dim, no input-value leaked, mtime race)

## TEST FILES

- `tests/unit/cli/console-resilience.test.ts` (new) — fault-injection matrix.
- `tests/unit/cli/console-perf.test.ts` (new) — perf invariants.
- `tests/unit/cli/console-telemetry-redaction.test.ts` (new) — NDJSON shape + redaction regex.

## ASSERTIONS REQUIRED

### Resilience matrix (.3/.4/.5/.6/.7/.8)
- [ ] Mock RuntimeClient with each method throwing: `listProcessSnapshot`, `readFeed`, `subscribeFeed`, `inspectJob`, `linkedDetail`, `readResult`, `resolveWorktree`, `diffSummary`, `diffFile`, `readGlobalConfig`, `writeGlobalConfig`.
- [ ] For each throw: enter the relevant view → render → assert dim error row present (`/error|failed/i.test(stripAnsi(row))`).
- [ ] For each throw: exactly one stderr NDJSON line emitted.
- [ ] For each throw: 100 subsequent `render()` calls emit ZERO additional NDJSON lines (marker prevents flood).
- [ ] For each throw: input loop survives — `handleInput('q')` resolves cleanly.
- [ ] Multi-failure cascade: 3 methods throw across one render → 3 NDJSON lines (one per op), 0 throws escape `render()`.

### Perf invariants (.6)
- [ ] Viewport window — ProcessView: 10k jobs in snapshot, `mainHeight=20` → `renderJobRow` call count ≤ 20 (spy on the function).
- [ ] Viewport window — FeedView: 10k events buffered, `mainHeight=20`, `follow=true` → renders only last 20.
- [ ] Throttle — feed dispatch coalescer: inject 1000 events in 100ms → `requestRender` called ≤ 20 times (≤20Hz cap).
- [ ] Throttle no starvation: 5 events @ 10s spacing → each triggers a render within ≤100ms (not coalesced into one).
- [ ] Resize: simulate SIGWINCH (or set `rows` then call `render(width)`) → next frame uses new `mainHeight`; no torn rendering (frame returned has correct row count).
- [ ] Subscribe-vs-poll: if `subscribeProcesses` is implemented via timer, assert interval ∈ [1000ms, 2000ms] (no busy-poll).

### Telemetry redaction (.3–.8)
- [ ] NDJSON shape: every emitted line parses as JSON and matches `{ts, component:'sp-console', view, op, errorClass, ...}`.
- [ ] Forbidden keys: NO `payload`, `stdout`, `stderr`, `body`, `value`, `input` keys in any emitted line.
- [ ] Forbidden patterns in any string field:
  - No model IDs: `/openai-codex|anthropic|gpt-\d|claude-[a-z]|nano-gpt/i`
  - No absolute paths under `$HOME`: `/^\/(home|Users)\//`
  - No bead-body markers: `/##\s+(PROBLEM|SUCCESS|SCOPE)/`
  - No JSON-stringified user.json values: `/"model":\s*"/`
- [ ] Inject `(repo, beadId='unitAI-ctb4u')` into BeadView → simulate `bd show` failure → emitted line MUST include `beadId:'unitAI-ctb4u'` (sanitized id is OK), MUST NOT include stdout/stderr content even if the spy fake produces it.
- [ ] Inject `writeGlobalConfig` failure with a candidate config containing `executor.execution.model = 'openai-codex/gpt-5.5'` → emitted line MUST NOT contain `openai-codex` substring.

### Edit-path safety (.8)
- [ ] mtime conflict simulation: snapshot at mtime t0, external "touch" to t1, submit edit → returns `ok:false` with mtime-error; file on disk unchanged.
- [ ] EACCES simulation: `writeGlobalUserConfig` throws EACCES → dim row + NDJSON `{op:'write_global_config', errorClass:'EACCES'}` — no `errno` numeric leak, no path in field.

## CRITICAL PATHS COVERED

- Input loop survival under every IO failure — risk: console crashes mid-session, operator loses observability during incident response.
- Viewport-window invariant — risk: 10k-event feed renders entire buffer per frame, freezes terminal.
- Telemetry redaction — risk: model IDs / bead bodies / user.json values hit stdout/log aggregator → privacy regression.
- Throttle ceiling — risk: burst of feed events thrashes render at 1000Hz, input lag spikes.
- mtime race in edit path — risk: clobber operator's concurrent hand-edit, silent data loss.

## KNOWN DEFERRED PATHS

- Memory-leak detection under long-running session (24h soak) → out of scope; document follow-up bead.
- Cross-platform SIGWINCH on Windows → spec is Linux/macOS-only; document.

## DEBUGGABILITY EVIDENCE REQUIRED

- Resilience test must `console.log(JSON.parse(emittedLine))` on failure so reviewer sees the exact violating line.
- Perf test must report `renderJobRow.mock.calls.length` and `requestRender.mock.calls.length` on failure.
- Redaction test must report the FIRST forbidden pattern + matching line on failure.

## FIXTURE POLICY

- Use `vi.fn()` / `mock.module()` for RuntimeClient + stderr seam; capture emitted lines in an array, parse JSON in assertions.
- No real subprocess. No real fs. Pure in-memory.
- Inject `Date.now` and `setInterval`/`setTimeout` via fake timers (`vi.useFakeTimers()`) for throttle + interval tests.

## ANTI-PATTERN CHECKLIST

- [ ] No tautology (don't assert `mockFn.calls.length === mockFn.calls.length`).
- [ ] Resilience tests assert the SURVIVING state (input loop next-cycle), not just the throw.
- [ ] Redaction tests use REGEX against actual emitted lines, not `.toMatchObject` (which could miss extra fields).
- [ ] Perf tests use deterministic fixtures (no `setTimeout` without fake timers).

## TEST-RUNNER COMMAND CONTRACT

```
bun test \
  tests/unit/cli/console-resilience.test.ts \
  tests/unit/cli/console-perf.test.ts \
  tests/unit/cli/console-telemetry-redaction.test.ts
```

- Setup: none (mocks set up per-test).
- Cleanup: `vi.restoreAllMocks()` in afterEach.
- Expected: all three files pass; resilience suite has ≥ 10 method-throw cases; redaction suite has ≥ 6 forbidden-pattern cases.
- Failure classification:
  - Throw escapes `render()` → product regression (RESILIENCE BUG, blocker for merge).
  - Redaction regex hits → product regression (PRIVACY BUG, blocker for merge).
  - Throttle exceeds 20Hz → product regression.
  - Viewport-window count > mainHeight → product regression.
  - Fake-timer behavior changed → infrastructure (bun version drift), pin and follow up.

## DEFINITION OF DONE

- [ ] Every RuntimeClient method covered by ≥1 throw-case in the resilience matrix.
- [ ] Throttle ≤20Hz proven under 1000-event burst.
- [ ] Viewport-window proven under 10k-row state.
- [ ] Zero forbidden patterns in any line emitted across the full test suite (regex-asserted).
- [ ] mtime-race + EACCES paths covered for edit.

title: Test: Phase 0 — override contract extension (core + boundary, drift-guard, regression)
description:
## What implementation it covers

Validates unitAI-gp7nq.1 (Phase 0 — structural extension to `applyOverrideFields` for nested execution paths and prompt allowlist). HIGH-blast-radius change: every spec load goes through this code path.

## Layer classification

- **Core**: new `OVERRIDE_ALLOWED_PROMPT_FIELDS` + `OVERRIDE_ALLOWED_NESTED_EXECUTION_PATHS` constants in src/specialist/schema.ts. Pure data.
- **Boundary**: `applyOverrideFields` in src/specialist/loader.ts walks the new allowlists; `buildSpecialistOverrideTemplate` + `GlobalSpecialistOverrideSchema` in src/specialist/global-config.ts emit/validate the new shape. File-fixture merges are the boundary surface.

## Strategy

- **Core**: example-based unit tests on the new constants + a drift-guard test asserting the schema.ts allowlist exports stay aligned with the leaf keys of `GlobalSpecialistOverrideSchema`.
- **Boundary**: integration tests with real fs fixtures under tmpdir, exercising `SpecialistLoader.load(name)` end-to-end with synthetic specs + user.json layers.

## Test file structure

- `tests/unit/specialist/schema.test.ts` — gains a drift-guard test.
- `tests/unit/specialist/loader.test.ts` — gains nested-execution + prompt-overlay merge tests using synthetic test-only allowlisted fields.
- `tests/unit/specialist/global-config.test.ts` — gains `buildSpecialistOverrideTemplate` shape test + `mergeGlobalUserConfig` regression on a pre-Phase-0 fixture.
- NEW fixture `tests/fixtures/global-config/post-kan90.user.json` — verbatim copy of the post-KAN-90 default user.json shape; used in regression tests across this epic.

## Assertions required

### Core (schema.ts)
- [ ] `OVERRIDE_ALLOWED_PROMPT_FIELDS` is exported, is a readonly array, every entry matches `/^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$/`.
- [ ] `OVERRIDE_ALLOWED_NESTED_EXECUTION_PATHS` (or equivalent mechanism) is exported and has the dotted-path shape the loader expects.
- [ ] **Drift-guard**: for every leaf key under `prompt`/`execution.<nested>` in `GlobalSpecialistOverrideSchema`, the key appears in the corresponding `OVERRIDE_ALLOWED_*` export — and vice versa. Test fails if either side adds a key without the other.

### Boundary (loader merge)
- [ ] Nested-execution overlay: when package canonical has `execution: {foo: 1, extensions: {a: true, b: true}}` and user override sets `execution.extensions.a: false`, merged spec is `execution: {foo: 1, extensions: {a: false, b: true}}`. Per-leaf overlay, not whole-subobject replace.
- [ ] Prompt-allowlist overlay: when package canonical has `prompt: {system: "X", task_template: "Y", <allowlisted_test_field>: "default"}` and user override sets the allowlisted prompt field to "user", merged spec preserves system/task_template untouched and shows the overlaid value.
- [ ] Null-means-inherit: setting an allowlisted field to `null` in user.json must yield the package canonical value (no clobber).
- [ ] Unlisted prompt sub-key (e.g. `prompt.bogus`) triggers `validateGlobalUserConfig` error with path `prompt.bogus`.
- [ ] Unlisted nested-execution sub-key (e.g. `execution.extensions.bogus`) triggers `validateGlobalUserConfig` error with path including the dotted key.

### Regression
- [ ] **Pre-Phase-0 fixture** parses cleanly through `validateGlobalUserConfig`.
- [ ] **Pre-Phase-0 fixture** through `mergeGlobalUserConfig` against the new template: new nested + prompt keys ADDED with `null`, no existing user-set value clobbered, `removed` array stays empty for fixture entries.
- [ ] **Pre-Phase-0 fixture** loaded by `SpecialistLoader` against the shipped package canonical produces the same merged spec as before this phase (snapshot-style test on one spec, e.g. `executor`).

### BlockedFieldWarning surface
- [ ] A user.json with a not-yet-allowlisted-but-otherwise-valid field (e.g. `execution.system_prompt_mode` BEFORE Phase 1 lights it up) emits `BlockedFieldWarning` with `severity: 'strip'` from the global layer. Confirms the warning mechanism still fires correctly post-Phase-0.

## Smoke / E2E commands (for test-runner)

```bash
# Static gates (executor already runs these but test-runner re-runs for evidence)
bun run lint
bun run build
bun --bun vitest run tests/unit/specialist/schema.test.ts tests/unit/specialist/loader.test.ts tests/unit/specialist/global-config.test.ts

# Drift-guard isolation (fast feedback)
bun --bun vitest run tests/unit/specialist/schema.test.ts -t "drift-guard"

# Boundary fixture suite
bun --bun vitest run tests/unit/specialist/loader.test.ts -t "Phase 0"
```

Failure classification:
- Drift-guard failure → BLOCKING (the structural invariant is broken; Phase 1/2/3 cannot ship).
- Boundary merge test failure → BLOCKING.
- Regression on pre-Phase-0 fixture → BLOCKING (backward compat broken).
- BlockedFieldWarning regression → BLOCKING (silent-drop danger).
- vitest unrelated noise (e.g. supervisor.test.ts FIFO hang per memory) → CARRY-FORWARD pre-existing, do not block.

## Log/telemetry assertions

Phase 0 introduces no new telemetry events. But it changes the path that emits `BlockedFieldWarning`. Test must assert that `BlockedFieldWarning` records produced by the merge step still have `{specialist, field, source, severity, value}` shape — no field renamed or dropped accidentally.

## Critical paths covered

- `applyOverrideFields` correctness on the new allowlists — risk: silently drops a user override, defeats the entire epic.
- Allowlist drift between schema.ts and global-config.ts — risk: a future phase adds a field on one side and forgets the other; users edit a field that has no effect.
- Backward compat for existing user.json files — risk: post-KAN-90 user files stop parsing after this epic lands.

## Known deferred paths

- Stress test with very-deep nested-execution paths (>3 levels). Phase 0 spec implies `execution.<sub>.<key>` is the only nesting level — deeper deferred. Follow-up to be created if Phase 1/2 add deeper paths.

## Debuggability evidence required

- vitest output (pass count, file count) captured in test-runner result for the reviewer.
- The drift-guard test's failure message MUST list which side (schema.ts vs global-config.ts) has the missing/extra key — not just "arrays differ".

## DoD (boundary layer template)

- [ ] Schema/contract assertions cover allowlist shape + leaf-key alignment (drift-guard).
- [ ] Per-merge-case assertions cover overlay, null-inherit, unknown-key reject.
- [ ] Regression on pre-Phase-0 fixture passes (snapshot-equivalent merge).
- [ ] Live-first policy N/A here (no service boundary); use real fs in tmpdir, no mocking of fs.
- [ ] All bullets above implemented and passing locally before bd close.

title: Phase 0: Extend override contract for nested execution + prompt allowlist
description:
## PROBLEM

The current override contract in src/specialist/schema.ts encodes two flat allowlists: `OVERRIDE_ALLOWED_EXECUTION_FIELDS` (6 keys under `specialist.execution.*`) and `OVERRIDE_ALLOWED_TOP_FIELDS` (1 key, `beads_write_notes`). Every other phase of this epic needs to extend the override surface in ways that don't fit a flat allowlist:

1. `execution.extensions.{serena,gitnexus}` are *nested* under `execution` — currently there's no concept of nested-key allowlisting.
2. `prompt.system_prompt_mode` lives under `prompt`, not `execution` or top-level — currently there's no allowlist for prompt sub-fields at all (the whole `prompt` tree sits next to `execution.permission_required` in `BLOCKED_OVERRIDE_FIELDS`).

Until these two structural extensions exist, Phases 1, 2, 3 cannot ship without either hardcoding special-cases (ugly, drift-prone) or doing this scaffolding inline (each phase reinventing the same scaffolding). This task is the unblocker.

## SUCCESS

- `OVERRIDE_ALLOWED_PROMPT_FIELDS` exists in schema.ts as a typed `readonly` array, alongside the existing execution + top allowlists.
- `OVERRIDE_ALLOWED_NESTED_EXECUTION_PATHS` (or equivalent structural mechanism) exists, allowing nested keys under `execution.<subobject>.<field>` to be allowlisted without flattening.
- `applyOverrideFields` in loader.ts walks the new allowlists alongside the existing two, with the same precedence semantics (override-or-inherit, null-means-inherit, no clobber of package canonical for unlisted fields).
- `GlobalSpecialistOverrideSchema` in global-config.ts is widened to accept the new nested + prompt shapes (still `.strict()`). The override template includes the new nested objects (e.g. `prompt: { system_prompt_mode: null }`, `execution: { ..., extensions: { serena: null, gitnexus: null } }`), all defaulted to `null`.
- A unit test asserts that `OVERRIDE_ALLOWED_*` exports in schema.ts and the corresponding leaf-key set in `GlobalSpecialistOverrideSchema` stay in sync (drift guard).
- Existing user.json files parse and merge identically after the change (backward compat preserved via `mergeGlobalUserConfig.fillMissingDefaults`).

This task does NOT yet add any new field to the allowlist. It only extends the *machinery* so subsequent phases can.

## SCOPE

- src/specialist/schema.ts:144-168 — add new exports `OVERRIDE_ALLOWED_PROMPT_FIELDS`, `OVERRIDE_ALLOWED_NESTED_EXECUTION_PATHS` (or chosen equivalent); update doc comment for the layered field-merge contract.
- src/specialist/loader.ts:194-240 — `applyOverrideFields` walks the new allowlists with the same precedence semantics; extracted helper `readNestedPath` / `writeNestedPath` is acceptable.
- src/specialist/global-config.ts:67-120 — `OverrideExecutionSchema` gains optional nested-object support; new `OverridePromptSchema`; `GlobalSpecialistOverrideSchema` widens; `buildSpecialistOverrideTemplate` returns the new shape with all-null defaults.
- tests/unit/specialist/schema.test.ts — drift-guard test (allowlist exports vs override schema leaf keys match).
- tests/unit/specialist/loader.test.ts — merge-precedence test for nested-execution path and prompt-sub-path (using a stub field; real fields land in Phase 1).
- tests/unit/specialist/global-config.test.ts — `buildSpecialistOverrideTemplate` returns expected new shape; `mergeGlobalUserConfig` over a pre-extension user.json fixture adds the new keys with null, clobbers nothing.

## NON_GOALS

- Adding ANY actual field to the allowlist (Phase 1 does that).
- Touching `fallback_model` schema or chain semantics (Phase 2).
- Preset resolution (Phase 3).
- `sp init --global` UX changes (Phase 4) — beyond the mechanical effect of the new template shape.
- Repo-layer `.specialists/user/<name>` semantics changes.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Run `gitnexus_impact({target: "applyOverrideFields", direction: "upstream"})` BEFORE editing loader.ts. This function is on every spec-load path; risk is HIGH if the merge semantics regress. Report the impact summary in the handoff.
- The drift-guard test is non-optional. The whole reason this task exists is that the allowlist concept must stay consistent across schema.ts (the loader's source of truth) and global-config.ts (the template + override-schema source of truth). Without the test, a future phase can land a field in one location and forget the other.
- Backward compat is hard-required: a user.json with the OLD shape (no `prompt` key under each specialist entry, no `extensions` under each `execution` entry) must continue to merge cleanly. `fillMissingDefaults` should handle this; the test must prove it on a copy of the post-KAN-90 default user.json fixture.
- `.strict()` on `GlobalSpecialistOverrideSchema` means unknown nested keys still error. Test that an unknown prompt sub-key (e.g. `prompt.bogus`) is rejected by `validateGlobalUserConfig`.
- Log: when an override layer attempts to set a field NOT in any allowlist, the existing `BlockedFieldWarning` mechanism applies (strip in global layer, warn in repo layer). Verify no regression in that surface.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `bun --bun vitest run tests/unit/specialist/schema.test.ts tests/unit/specialist/loader.test.ts tests/unit/specialist/global-config.test.ts` green.
- [ ] NEW test: `OVERRIDE_ALLOWED_PROMPT_FIELDS` and `OVERRIDE_ALLOWED_NESTED_EXECUTION_PATHS` are referenced in both schema.ts and global-config.ts; assertions don't drift.
- [ ] NEW test: nested-execution override (using a synthetic test-only field that maps through the nested allowlist mechanism) merges correctly with package-canonical base.
- [ ] NEW test: prompt-allowlist override (using a synthetic test-only field) merges correctly.
- [ ] REGRESSION test: pre-extension user.json fixture (literal copy of post-KAN-90 default shape) merges without error or clobbering.
- [ ] REGRESSION test: unknown nested prompt key triggers `validateGlobalUserConfig` failure with a clear path.
- [ ] `bun run lint && bun run build` clean.
- [ ] Smoke: `sp doctor` (or whichever doctor entry checks override contract integrity) reports no new warnings on a default-shape user.json.
- [ ] gitnexus_impact evidence captured in handoff (target: `applyOverrideFields`, direction upstream, risk level reported).

## OUTPUT

Handoff lists: (1) the new schema.ts exports and their shape, (2) the new global-config.ts schema additions, (3) the gitnexus_impact summary for `applyOverrideFields` with direct-caller count and risk, (4) test count delta, (5) one sentence on how Phase 1/2/3 will plug into the new mechanism. This output is what unblocks the parallel Phase 1/2/3 dispatch.

title: sp init --global should not bake repo-local .specialists/user/ specs into the global file
description:
Reported by operator after running sp init --global from /home/dawid/dev/specialists/. Got 31 entries in ~/.config/specialists/user.json: 23 package canonical + 8 from this repo's .specialists/user/ (mercury-atomic-summarizer, official-document-analyzer, overthinker (overrides package), smoke-echo, squawk-event-curator, squawk-rolling-context, squawk-session-analyst, squawk-session-analyst-normalize).

Three concerns with the current behavior:

1. POLLUTION: in a different repo, those repo-local entries are inert — there's no matching package spec for them to override. They just sit there.

2. STICKINESS: the idempotency rule (C2: 'extends with newly-shipped specialists') only adds, never removes. Once a name is in user.json, it stays forever. Init from one repo permanently infects the global file.

3. CONCEPT MISMATCH: the global file's job is *cross-repo* defaults. Repo-specific specs belong in .specialists/user/<repo> and shouldn't ride in the cross-repo layer.

Proposed fix options:
(a) Restrict sp init --global to package canonical scope only (cleanest, least surprising)
(b) Prompt for each non-package spec ('include mercury-atomic-summarizer in global config? [y/N]')
(c) Add a --include-repo-overrides flag, default off

The current C2 implementation uses SpecialistLoader.list() directly (src/cli/init.ts, src/specialist/global-config.ts). The fix is to filter by scope='package' before generating the template entries.

PROBLEM:
The forensic contract documents catalog families (`command.*`, `review.verdict.*`, `chain.*`, `worktree.*`) but not all are emitted live as runtime timeline/forensic rows. Gitboard can normalize legacy events, but the runtime should record its own observed lifecycle events so the materializer is not forced to infer source facts.

SUCCESS:
Runtime emits/persists canonical `xtrm.forensic.v1` rows for the lifecycle events it directly observes:
- `command.completed` / `command.failed` with bounded `command_kind` (especially `git`), duration/status, redacted command details;
- `review.verdict.pass|partial|fail|waived` when reviewer/compliance verdicts are known;
- `chain.ready_for_review` and `chain.finalized` with `chain_template`, `changed_paths_count` where known, terminal state/result;
- `worktree.merged` / merge-publication refs when runtime observes them;
- redaction present on every event.

NON_GOALS: No gitboard materializer work. No fabricated events when runtime lacks evidence.
VALIDATION: unit tests for event mapping/persistence; smoke job or fixture proving event rows have exact catalog names/body/redaction.

title: Telemetry upstream fixes for console-safe operations panels
description:
PROBLEM:
Gitboard/app planning identified upstream specialists telemetry gaps and contract clarifications needed before the console can safely consume operations panels directly. Prometheus must stay bounded-label and token-first; chain rollups/cost and per-entity drill-down must live in forensic/state, not Prometheus labels.

SUCCESS:
Specialists telemetry contract/runtime/docs/tests align to the console consumption model:
- Prometheus exposes only bounded aggregate metrics for dashboards.
- Chain rollups and cost estimates are derivable from forensic/state streams, not emitted as high-cardinality or USD Prometheus metrics.
- Forensic feed is the canonical per-job/per-chain drill-down surface.
- Trace bridge/exemplars are explicit and safe.

SCOPE / REQUIRED UPSTREAM CHANGES:

A. Metrics that must NOT exist in Prometheus
- Do not add/remove if present: xtrm_chain_tokens_total{role}. Token-per-chain requires chain_id, a forbidden Prom label. Keep job-level xtrm_llm_tokens_total{participant_role,direction}; chain rollup is derived from forensic/state.
- Do not add/remove if present: xtrm_chain_cost_dollars{model}. USD metrics are disallowed under token-first/subscription-plan semantics. No *_usd_total. Cost is app-layer estimate from token usage, only with provenance.
- Do not add/remove if present: xtrm_job_outcome_total. It duplicates xtrm_jobs_total{...,result}; use xtrm_jobs_total for success rate.

B. Metrics to ADD upstream, label-safe for Operations panels
- xtrm_chains_total{service_name,repo,chain_template,result}: counter, +1 at chain.finalized. Throughput per template without chain_id.
- xtrm_chain_duration_seconds{service_name,repo,chain_template,result}: histogram emitted at chain.finalized. Replaces any phantom {template,status}; bounded labels are chain_template + result.
- Confirm xtrm_gate_verdicts_total{...,participant_role,gate_kind,verdict} is shipped and covered by tests/docs; verdict values are PASS|PARTIAL|FAIL|WAIVED.

C. Allowlist labels
- Extend the Prometheus projection allowlist (§3.1) with chain_template and gate_kind. They are used in §5.9 but not listed in §3.1; cardinality tests should allow them.

D. Naming/labels
- Use participant_role and participant_kind as primary labels everywhere.
- Deprecate exported schema aliases role/specialist. Keep only recording-rule compatibility if needed.

E. Forensic/feed: job-as-feed
- Canonical endpoint expected by console: /api/specialists/jobs/:job_id/feed-events returns normalized xtrm.forensic.v1 events from the catalog, including body fields and redaction status.
- Provide/confirm chronological forensic stream with pagination/cursor, filterable by event_family and correlation ID, e.g. normalized sp feed --json. Activity tab and Feed should consume the same stream.
- Ensure model.token_usage.recorded emits split token usage: input/output/cache_read/cache_creation/reasoning/tool plus usage_source. Cost estimates and token-per-chain derive from this stream.

F. Trace bridge / drill-down boundary
- Propagate trace_id/span_id/parent_span_id in forensic events and link job→chain via containers.trace_id and evidence.trace_id/span_id.
- Histogram exemplars may use trace_id when present; never job_id or participant_id as Prometheus labels.
- Make the boundary explicit in docs/tests: drill-down to chain/job-specific views only via forensic events / trace_id. Ask for opaque IDs only after drill-down via logs/traces/events, never from Prometheus labels.

DESIGN CONSEQUENCE:
Chain-rollup and cost live in forensic/state (sum jobs by chain_id). Prometheus keeps bounded aggregates only: participant_role, chain_template, result, verdict. Console queries Prometheus for panels and jumps to forensic/trace streams for per-entity views.

VALIDATION:
- Prometheus projection tests reject forbidden/high-cardinality labels and USD metrics.
- Projection tests cover xtrm_chains_total, xtrm_chain_duration_seconds, gate_kind, chain_template.
- Forensic/feed tests cover token split + usage_source and correlation/trace propagation.
- Docs updated: docs/telemetry/prometheus-projection-contract.md, forensic-event-contract.md, agentops-event-catalog.md as needed.

title: Migrate gitboard specialist feed consumers to forensic JSON
description:
## PROBLEM
Gitboard currently shells out to `sp feed <jobId>` and renders text output. Specialists now exposes `sp feed --json` with additive `forensic_event`, but gitboard does not consume it yet.

## SUCCESS
Gitboard can render structured specialist timeline/evidence data from forensic JSON instead of parsing text feed output, while preserving text fallback.

## SCOPE
- Add/adjust gitboard backend endpoint to call `sp feed <jobId> --json`.
- Parse NDJSON rows and expose structured timeline events.
- Use `forensic_event.resource.participant_role` and `forensic_event.correlation.job_id` where available.
- Preserve current `/feed` text endpoint or add `?format=json` / `feed-events` as a compatibility path.
- Keep Prometheus metrics for aggregate dashboard panels, not job-level event timelines.

## NON_GOALS
- No removal of legacy text feed until UI migration is complete.
- No high-cardinality Prometheus labels.

## VALIDATION
- Gitboard tests cover legacy text fallback and forensic JSON path.
- UI can render job timeline from structured events.
- No dependency on TTY-style text parsing for the structured path.
close_reason: Done: added gitboard structured feed-events endpoint consuming sp feed --json with forensic_event rows.

title: Harden Prometheus counter replay safety and durable cursors
description:
## PROBLEM
The current Prometheus projection prototype is suitable for validation, but production counter semantics need stronger replay-safety guarantees.

## SUCCESS
Counters are generated from durable monotonic state or a documented cursor/checkpoint mechanism so restarts/replays do not corrupt alert/dashboard semantics.

## SCOPE
- Audit all counter projections in `prometheus-projection.ts`.
- Decide per metric whether it is event-derived, table-derived, or process-local.
- Add durable cursor/checkpoint where event replay is used.
- Document reset semantics for CLI/textfile vs HTTP exporter modes.

## NON_GOALS
- No new metric families unless required for correctness.

## VALIDATION
- Tests cover restart/replay scenarios.
- Counter values are monotonic within the chosen exporter lifecycle.
- Documentation states reset behavior clearly.
notes:
DONE — Prometheus counter replay-safety hardened for current bridge.

Current sp metrics --prometheus counters are table-derived from durable specialist_job_metrics/current state, not process-local event increments. Repeated renders over the same input are deterministic; docs now state long-running HTTP exporter/event-stream mode still needs a cursor.

title: Implement forensic redaction pipeline and rules
description:
## PROBLEM
The forensic envelope carries `redaction.status`, but redaction is not yet backed by a concrete scrubber/rules pipeline.

## SUCCESS
Sensitive fields are scrubbed before forensic persistence/output, and redaction metadata records which rule families applied.

## SCOPE
- Define redaction rules for prompts, model output, tool payloads, raw commands, raw URLs, tokens, credentials, emails, and raw error text.
- Apply redaction before canonical forensic persistence and JSON output surfaces.
- Add fixtures for clean/redacted/unknown states.
- Ensure diagnostics can still link to forensic evidence without leaking secrets.

## NON_GOALS
- No semantic PII classifier beyond deterministic rules.
- No external secret-scanning service dependency.

## VALIDATION
- Tests prove forbidden raw fields are scrubbed.
- Redaction metadata includes status and rule ids.
- No regression in feed/log compatibility.

notes:
### overthinker · gpt-5.5 · [turn 8 · WORKING]

{"docs/telemetry/forensic-event-contract.md":"# Forensic Event Contract

Status: Draft — bridge implementation target.

## 1. Purpose

Forensic events are append-only JSON Lines records that preserve what happened across specialist lifecycles. They are optimized for post-hoc debugging and lossless replay into future substrate storage, not for low-cardinality metrics.

## 2. Event Shape

Each line in `events.jsonl` is one JSON object.

Required top-level keys:

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schema_version` | string | yes | Current value: `"xtrm.forensic_event.v1"`. |
| `ts` | ISO-8601 string | yes | Emission time. |
| `event_id` | string | yes | Unique event id (`crypto.randomUUID()` recommended). |
| `event_type` | string | yes | Bounded event name such as `turn.start`, `tool.call`, `lifecycle.complete`. |
| `resource` | object | yes | Stable resource identity and low-cardinality dimensions. |
| `scope` | object | yes | Lifecycle correlation ids and task/chain lineage. |
| `payload` | object | yes | Event-specific data. |

Rules:
- Producers MUST keep `resource` low-cardinality and label-safe.
- Producers MAY place high-cardinality ids in `scope` or `payload`.
- Events are append-only and immutable after emission.
- Consumers MUST ignore unknown fields.
- Consumers MUST NOT require fields outside this contract for basic ingestion.

## 3. Event Types

Recommended bounded names:

- `lifecycle.start`
- `lifecycle.ready`
- `lifecycle.stopped`
- `lifecycle.complete`
- `lifecycle.error`
- `turn.start`
- `turn.complete`
- `turn.error`
- `tool.call`
- `tool.result`
- `message.sent`
- `message.received`
- `decision.recorded`
- `handoff.created`
- `handoff.accepted`

## 4. Resource Attributes

`resource` contains dimensions that are safe to index and use as Loki/Prometheus-style labels.

| Field | Required | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `resource_type` | yes | Bounded kind. Current bridge value: `specialist`. Future: `orchestrator`, `adapter`, `service`. | `specialist` |
| `specialist_id` | yes for specialist events | Stable bounded role/config id, not run id. | `executor`, `architect`, `node-coordinator` |
| `model` | no | LLM model/provider family or runtime label. | `claude-sonnet-4-5` |
| `runtime` | no | Runtime/tool family. | `claude-code`, `pi`, `mcp-adapter` |
| `repo` | no | Repository/workspace basename when available. | `specialists` |
| `specialists_version` | no | Tooling version/commit where available. | `2026-04-04` |

Notes:
- `resource_type` and `specialist_id` are label-safe dimensions.
- `specialist_id` MUST NOT encode bead id, chain id, pid, timestamp, UUID, or per-run identity.
- For non-specialist resources, use a future bounded role field (for example `adapter_id`) rather than overloading `specialist_id`.

## 5. Correlation Model

`scope` contains high-cardinality correlation identifiers.

| Field | Required | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `job_id` | yes for specialist runs | `sp` job id / specialist lifecycle id. | `unitAI-abc12` |
| `chain_id` | no | Stable chain lineage id. | `unitAI-abc12` |
| `parent_job_id` | no | Parent specialist/job that spawned this lifecycle. | `unitAI-root` |
| `epic_id` | no | Merge-gated epic id. | `unitAI-kj651` |
| `phase` | no | Human stage label, not identity. | `1A` |
| `participant_id` | no | Reserved for future substrate participant/member id. Bridge SHOULD omit unless value comes from substrate. | `part_01J...` |
| `turn_id` | no | Conversation turn id. | `turn_01J...` |
| `session_id` | no | Provider/runtime session id when available. | `claude-session-...` |

Correlation rules:
- `job_id` is the bridge-era specialist lifecycle/run id.
- `chain_id` MAY equal the seed job id in current bridge storage, but consumers MUST treat it as separate from `job_id`.
- `parent_job_id` records immediate spawn lineage, not chain membership.
- `participant_id` is intentionally reserved until substrate participant semantics land.
- `session_id` is a provider/runtime correlation id, not primary xtrm identity.

## 6. Payload Rules

`payload` carries event-specific data. It may be high-cardinality.

Recommended common payload keys:
- `message_id`
- `tool_name`
- `tool_call_id`
- `exit_code`
- `error_type`
- `error_message`
- `duration_ms`
- `input_summary`
- `output_summary`
- `tokens_input`
- `tokens_output`

Payload rules:
- Redact secrets and credentials before writing.
- Prefer hashes/summaries for large or sensitive content.
- Store raw large artifacts outside event lines; reference them by path or artifact id.

## 7. JSON Schema

Informative schema:

## 8. Append-only Semantics

- Emit one line per observed event.
- Do not rewrite or delete prior events.
- Include enough scope to join with status/result state at emit time.
- If a lifecycle changes state after an event is emitted, emit another lifecycle event.

## 9. Bridge-to-Substrate Compatibility

Bridge fields intentionally map forward:

| Bridge field | Substrate-era mapping |

## 1. Purpose & Scope

The substrate is the foundational layer that makes specialist work deterministic, observable, replayable, and governable across arbitrary repositories.

It gives every agentic execution a canonical shape:

- durable state
- explicit identity
- lifecycle state machine
- append-only event trail
- resumable context
- artifact lineage
- policy hooks

This document defines the conceptual model, entities, lifecycle, and interfaces for that substrate.

It intentionally does **not** define:

- UI details
- final CLI syntax
- final DB schema
- model-provider specifics
- orchestration policy

## 2. Core Entity Model

### 2.1 Entities

The substrate has the following first-class entities:

| Entity | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `WorkUnit` | Durable unit of requested work, e.g. issue, task, investigation, fix, review, design. |
| `Participant` | Agentic or human actor capable of doing work or emitting events. |
| `Thread` | Ordered conversation/event stream between participants. |
| `Turn` | One message/action boundary inside a thread. |
| `Artifact` | File, patch, note, report, metric, trace, or other durable output. |
| `Decision` | Explicit recorded design/implementation choice with rationale. |
| `Policy` | Rule or guardrail evaluated against actions or state transitions. |
| `Capability` | Tool, model, skill, permission, or integration available to a participant. |
| `Event` | Append-only fact about lifecycle, messages, tools, artifacts, or policy. |

Derived / relationship entities:

| Entity | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `Assignment` | Binding between a `WorkUnit` and a `Participant`, with role, responsibility, and lifecycle. |
| `Observation` | Derived signal from events/artifacts, e.g. progress, confidence, risk, test health. |
| `Link` | Typed relationship between any two entities. |
| `Claim` | Temporary exclusive or shared lease on a resource/work unit. |

### 2.2 Participants

A `Participant` represents an entity capable of producing turns, tool calls, artifacts, decisions, or events.

Examples:

- human developer
- specialist agent
- orchestrator agent
- reviewer agent
- CI bot
- MCP server/tool gateway
- external service

Participant properties:

- stable identity
- kind (`human`, `agent`, `service`, `tool`, ...)
- capabilities
- trust level
- ownership / authority boundaries
- current lifecycle state
- active assignments
- associated threads

A participant MAY have multiple capabilities.  
A participant MAY participate in multiple work units over time.  
A participant MAY delegate to or spawn other participants, depending on policy.

### 2.3 Threads, Turns, and Events

A `Thread` is the durable conversational/event stream for a work unit or collaboration context.

A `Turn` is a single message/action boundary in a thread.

An `Event` is any append-only fact, including:

- lifecycle transition
- message sent/received
- tool call/result
- artifact created/updated
- decision recorded
- policy decision
- telemetry/metric pulse

The same fact MAY be represented as both a `Turn` and an `Event` when it has conversational semantics and needs forensic traceability.

Rules:

- Events are append-only.
- Turns are ordered within a thread.
- Events are globally ordered at least by timestamp and causality links; strict global total ordering is not assumed.
- Every event SHOULD identify its producer participant.
- Every event SHOULD identify affected entities.

- `epic`
- `task`
- `subtask`
- `bug`
- `design`
- `review`
- `experiment`
- `incident`

Kinds are open but bounded by registry/config.

Suggested states:

- `proposed`
- `accepted`
- `claimed`
- `active`
- `blocked`
- `reviewing`
- `resolved`
- `closed`
- `abandoned`

Lifecycle constraints:

- work unit state transitions are evented.
- terminal states are immutable except by explicit reopen policy.
- claims and assignments constrain who can mutate or resolve work.

### 3.3 Assignment

An `Assignment` binds:

- work unit
- participant
- role
- responsibility scope
- lifecycle state
- authority level
- due/priority metadata

Assignments may be exclusive or shared.

Replay is not guaranteed to reproduce model outputs bit-for-bit.

Replay target is deterministic reconstruction of:

- who acted
- what was asked
- what context was available
- what tools were called
- what artifacts changed
- what decisions were made

- what final state was reached

### 6.8 Governance & Authority

The substrate should answer:

- who may create work units
- who may assign participants
- who may mutate source artifacts
- who may publish/merge
- who may record final decisions
- who may delegate or spawn participants
- who may inspect secrets / privileged artifacts

Authority is derived from participant identity, assignment, container membership, capabilities, and policy.

### 6.9 Identity & Lifecycle Model

#### 6.9.1 Identity Layers

The substrate separates:

1. **Kind** — bounded category (`human`, `agent`, `service`, `tool`, `container`, `work_unit`, ...).
2. **Role / profile** — bounded label describing intended function (`executor`, `reviewer`, `coordinator`, `ci`, ...).
3. **Instance** — stable participant/resource identity across time.
4. **Activation** — one runtime execution or session lifecycle.
5. **Event / turn / span** — one append-only fact or conversational/action boundary.

Rules:

- Kind and role/profile are label-safe and bounded.
- Instance, activation, event, turn, and span ids are opaque correlation ids.
- A role/profile may have many instances over time.
- A participant instance may have many activations over time.
- An activation may have many turns, events, and spans.
- Provider session ids are external correlation ids and MUST NOT be primary substrate ids.

#### 6.9.2 Current Bridge Mapping

| Current bridge field | Identity layer | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `specialist_id` | Role / profile | Bounded specialist role/config id (`executor`, `architect`, `node-coordinator`). |
| `job_id` | Activation | One specialist lifecycle/run. Must be distinct for concurrent/retry runs. |
| `chain_id` | Execution container instance | Stable chain lineage, currently often seed job id. |
| `parent_job_id` | Parent activation link | Spawn causal parent, not container membership. |
| `pid` | Runtime detail | Process id, not durable identity. |
| Claude/pi `session_id` | Provider session correlation | Not primary identity; may survive resume depending on provider. |

#### 6.9.3 Forward Substrate Mapping

Canonical substrate fields:

| Field | Identity layer | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `participant_kind` | Kind | Bounded label. |
| `participant_profile` | Role / profile | Bounded label. |
| `participant_id` | Instance | Opaque stable member/participant id. |
| `activation_id` | Activation | Opaque per execution lifecycle id. |
| `container_id` | Container instance | Opaque id for chain/node/session/etc. |
| `container_kind` | Container kind | Bounded label. |
| `event_id` | Event | Opaque append-only event id. |
| `turn_id` | Turn | Opaque turn id where applicable. |
| `span_id` | Span | Opaque tool/action span id where applicable. |
| `provider_session_id` | External correlation | External runtime session id. |

Forward rules:

- `job_id` becomes bridge alias for `activation_id`, not for `participant_id`.
- `chain_id` becomes a `container_id` with `container_kind=chain`.
- `participant_id` is stable across activations of same participant instance/member.
- Node coordinator and node members are participants in a `node` execution container.
- Events emitted by services/tools still need a participant identity; if no durable service instance exists, create/register one before emission.

#### 6.9.4 Non-goals / Anti-patterns

- Do not encode kind/profile inside opaque ids.
- Do not use role/profile as unique identity.
- Do not use provider session id as participant id.
- Do not use process id as durable identity.
- Do not use wave/stage/phase as persisted identity.
- Do not assume one participant has only one active activation.
- Do not assume one chain has only one participant.
- Do not assume every event belongs to a chain.

#### 6.9.5 Lifecycle Implications

- Participant lifecycle describes instance availability/authority.
- Activation lifecycle describes a runtime execution/session.
- Assignment lifecycle describes responsibility for work.
- Container membership describes topology.
- These lifecycles can change independently and MUST be linked explicitly by ids/events.

Examples:

- Two `executor` runs for same chain:
  - same `participant_profile=executor` only if they are conceptually same member; otherwise different `participant_id`.
  - always different `activation_id`.
- Orchestrator spawning specialists:
  - orchestrator has its own `participant_id` and `activation_id`.
  - each specialist member has its own `participant_id`.
  - each specialist run has its own `activation_id`.
  - spawn link connects parent activation to child activation.
- Pulse emitter outside any chain:
  - has `participant_kind=service` or `tool`.
  - has `participant_id` and `activation_id`.
  - may omit `container_id` or use an `external_run` container.

- policy audit
- active claims

Integrations include:

- issue trackers
- git providers
- CI systems
- observability backends
- LLM/provider runtimes
- MCP/tool systems
