title: Fix gitnexus-mcp leak: detached pi spawn + group-SIGKILL escalation in session.ts
description:
## Parent
unitAI-ctl0o (investigation)

## Root cause (from audit)
1. `src/pi/session.ts:653` spawns pi WITHOUT `detached: true`, so pi shares the caller's process group. MCP children (gitnexus mcp) run in pi's group.
2. `src/pi/session.ts:1165-1170` has a 2s fallback that re-sends SIGTERM via `proc.kill()`.
3. Pi's RPC mode SIGTERM handler (rpc-mode.js:266) starts graceful shutdown, which emits session_shutdown and triggers pi-mcp-adapter manager.closeAll(). Each MCP transport.close() takes up to 4s (stdin.end -> SIGTERM -> SIGKILL).
4. Our 2s redundant SIGTERM hits pi mid-dispose. Pi's shutdown() at rpc-mode.js:533 sees shuttingDown=true and calls process.exit(143) immediately, ABORTING in-flight MCP cleanup. gitnexus orphaned to pid 1.

## Fix
- session.ts:653 — add `detached: true` to spawn options (puts pi in its own process group).
- session.ts:1162-1172 — drop the redundant SIGTERM at 2s. Replace with a longer (8s) timer that escalates to `process.kill(-this.proc.pid, 'SIGKILL')` — group kill. This gives pi time for MCP graceful close (~4s worst case); if pi hangs, group-SIGKILL reaps gitnexus directly.
- session.ts:1193 — keep first SIGTERM as is (single-PID graceful).

## Validation
- npx tsc --noEmit clean
- Live smoke: launch a brief specialist with --keep-alive, sp stop it, verify no leftover gitnexus mcp under pi PID 1 (`ps -ef | awk '/gitnexus mcp/ && $3==1'`).
- Existing tests in tests/unit/pi/session.test.ts must still pass.

## Out of scope
- Pi upstream fixes (PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, MCP transport detached)
- sp clean reaper for already-orphaned gitnexus (separate follow-up)
close_reason: Implemented per audit spec: detached:true on pi spawn, 8s group-SIGKILL backstop replacing redundant 2s SIGTERM. Type-check + build clean. tests/unit/pi/session.test.ts 59/59 + runner.test.ts/script-runner.test.ts 89/89 pass.

title: Specialists --keep-alive leaks gitnexus-mcp child processes after job ends
description:
## Symptom
Each invocation of `bun specialists run <role> --bead <id> --keep-alive`
spawns a `pi` process which auto-loads `gitnexus mcp` as an MCP server.
When the specialist job ends (or the parent shell is killed/abandoned),
the `gitnexus mcp` child often outlives the cleanup chain and runs
indefinitely.

Process tree (verified 2026-05-09):
  bun specialists run <role> --bead <id> --keep-alive   (PID A)
   └── pi                                                (PID B)
        └── node /home/dawid/.nvm/.../gitnexus mcp       (PID C, leaks)

## Impact
- ~150-300 MB RSS per leaked gitnexus instance
- Observed yesterday: 6 leaked gitnexus mcp processes simultaneously,
  ~1 GB RAM tied up
- Recurs every few hours during active specialist usage
- Cleanup workaround: pkill -f 'gitnexus mcp' (one-shot, returns soon)

## Root cause hypothesis
- `--keep-alive` keeps the `pi` process alive after the bead's task
  completes, presumably for observability/replay
- When the specialist run is finally cleaned up (job complete, user
  cancellation, parent shell death), `pi` does not signal its child MCP
  servers
- Or: pi spawns gitnexus with a fresh process group / detached mode that
  prevents SIGTERM propagation

## Suggested investigation
- src/pi/session.ts handles MCP extension lifecycle — confirm it
  registers a SIGTERM handler that tears down loaded MCP servers
- Check if --keep-alive is supposed to also keep MCP servers alive (in
  which case there should be an explicit kill on job-complete)
- Reproduce: run a short specialist job with --keep-alive, kill the
  parent bun process, verify gitnexus is also gone

## Cross-ref
- Same gitnexus-leak observation noted in infra session memory:
  'xt-worktree-removal-leaks-executor-processes' (different vector — that
  one is git worktree removal not signaling executors at all)
notes: Fix shipped in unitAI-1phu7 / commit pending. Audit findings: pi rpc-mode.js:533 has `if(shuttingDown) process.exit()` guard that synchronously aborts in-flight MCP dispose. Our session.ts re-fired SIGTERM at 2s, hitting that guard mid-cleanup; gitnexus orphaned. Fix: detached:true on spawn + 8s group-SIGKILL backstop in close()/kill() (instead of redundant SIGTERM). pi-mcp-adapter/index.ts:137 confirms session_shutdown handler exists and calls manager.closeAll → graceful path is structurally correct, only the race needed fixing.
close_reason: Already fixed by unitAI-1phu7 / commit b12dd0fc. Verified: src/pi/session.ts:671 detached:true + 1186 group SIGKILL present.

### Keep as-is?

Bad move. Current state machine already caused operator pain: loops A/B/C plus manual git fallback. State machine protects batch publish, but also blocks publish path when keep-alive reviewer PASS leaves executor waiting.

### Parent tag only?

Good direction, incomplete alone. Parent tag can identify sibling chains. But status, drift repair, merge history, abandonment, and PR label need storage or derived command behavior.

### Benefits surviving “epic = bd parent tag only”

| Benefit | Survives? | Replacement |
|---|---:|---|
| Worktree sibling awareness | Yes | Read bead parent; use bd children |
| Batch merge target discovery | Yes | `bd children <epic>` |

| Abandon | Partial | bd close/abandon parent + optional live-job force check |
| Sticky FAILED recovery | Better | no sticky FAILED exists |
| Sibling-aware merge | Yes | parent tag gives sibling set |
| Merge gates | Yes | gate per chain readiness, not epic state |

```text
chain membership cache optional
merged_at / abandoned_at optional
audit summary optional
```

Derive:

```text
failed terminal state
manual transition ceremony
merge_ready persisted prerequisite
```

Keep:
```text

sp epic merge
sp epic sync --apply as repair/cache cleanup
sp epic abandon
```

## Phase 4 - Final Refined Output

### Recommendation

**Simplify epics. Do not remove.**

Reason:
- Epics earn keep as **grouping + batch publish + sibling ordering + stale-base context**.
- Epics fail as **operator-facing state machine**.
- Just-delivered chain lifecycle redesign makes hard epic state **less necessary**, because PASS auto-finalize + per-chain merge inside unresolved epics moves correctness to chain readiness.
- Same redesign makes epic **still useful**, because sibling chain ordering and batch publish remain real.

### Migration plan

1. Treat existing `failed` epics as non-terminal unless `abandoned` or `merged`.
2. Run derived readiness from chain statuses.
3. If all chains PASS + no active jobs: allow `sp epic merge`.
4. If some chains PASS: allow per-chain `sp merge <chain>` inside epic.
5. Keep old `epic_runs` rows for audit, but stop requiring `resolve`.
6. Convert `sp epic status` to show derived state:
   ```text

   persisted: merged|abandoned|legacy
   ```
7. Keep worktree grouping through bd parent + optional membership cache.

## Risks

- Parent tag lookup must be reliable.
- Removing persisted transitions loses some audit detail.
- `sp epic merge` still needs strong idempotency around already-published branches.
- Abandon semantics need live-member force gate preserved.

## Phase 2 - Devil's Advocate

### Unscoped `xtrm` risk

`xtrm` risky unless already controlled. Short unscoped name means:

- higher typosquat/confusion risk
- ownership uncertainty
- harder support story if package ever transferred
- user expectation: `npm install -g xtrm` should install whole CLI, not alias weirdness
- bad if existing unrelated `xtrm` exists

Use only after `npm view xtrm` proves controlled/available.

### Keeping `xtrm-tools` risk

Keeping `xtrm-tools` preserves current install command and search history, but bad 2.x history cannot be erased. npm semver means:

- repo `0.7.x` cannot satisfy consumers pinned to `^2.0.2`
- publishing `0.8.x` under `xtrm-tools` will not fix `^2.0.2`
- package must publish corrected `2.1.x` or deprecate `2.x` and force manual migration

### Scoped alias risk

Scoped package improves trust, but global CLI bins can collide:

- `@jaggerxtrm/xtrm-tools` can expose `xt` and `xtrm`
- `xtrm-tools` can also expose `xt` and `xtrm`
- npm global install last-wins symlink behavior can surprise users

Need docs: install one package, not both.

### Specialists dependency risk

Putting `xtrm-tools` in `dependencies` of `@jaggerxtrm/specialists` does not guarantee global `xt` command exists. Transitive package bins do not become user global workflow tools in reliable way.

Better model: runtime prerequisite check plus optional peer dependency metadata/docs.

### Naming strategy

Best path: **canonical scoped package + unscoped compatibility package**.

- Canonical implementation package:
  - `@jaggerxtrm/xtrm-tools`
  - owns code, docs, release notes, stable semver
  - exposes bins `xt` and `xtrm`
- Compatibility package:
  - `xtrm-tools`
  - keep unscoped for CLI continuity
  - publish fixed `2.1.x` because users on `^2.0.2` need compatible semver path
  - wrapper/shim or identical tarball
  - deprecate bad `2.0.x` versions with message pointing to fixed path
- Avoid unscoped `xtrm` until ownership verified.
  - If controlled later, reserve as thin alias only.
  - Do not make it primary while ecosystem still says `xtrm-tools`.

### Versioning model

Two options:

1. **Scoped canonical resets to repo reality**

CLI contract drift. `sp script --db-path` is documented as a path to `observability.db`, but code passes it to `createObservabilitySqliteClient()` like a cwd/project dir. This can silently write/read the wrong DB.

## What to build

- Implement true DB file-path support or rename/deprecate the flag to reflect cwd semantics.
- Prefer true file path support if bounded and low-risk.
- Update docs/tests for `sp script` and `sp serve` observability behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- Test proves `--db-path /tmp/x/observability.db` writes/opens that exact file or returns clear unsupported/deprecated error.
- Docs match implementation.
- Existing default `.specialists/db/observability.db` behavior remains unchanged.
close_reason: Done: --db-path now opens exact observability SQLite file for script/serve; tests/lint/build pass

title: sp serve: add optional Pi compatibility/readiness canary checks
description:
## Context

Service readiness is currently basic: auth file readable, DB writable, user dir valid. Production darth-feedor needs early detection that the installed Pi version and service image still support required flags and can perform minimal generation.

## What to build

- Add optional readiness/canary checks for Pi binary availability, required flag presence, and smoke specialist generation.
- Keep `/healthz` liveness unchanged.
- Ensure canary failure reason is explicit and does not block deployments unless configured to do so.

## Acceptance criteria

- Tests cover missing Pi binary, missing required flag, failed smoke call, and disabled canary mode.
- `/readyz` response includes actionable reason without secrets.
- Docs explain operational use in Docker/Podman deployments.
close_reason: Done: optional Pi compatibility/readiness canary checks added; tests/lint/build pass

title: Script runner: wire trusted skills through explicit Pi --skill args and audit
description:
## Context

Trust hardening. `--allow-skills` currently allows specs through compat/audit, but script-runner still passes `--no-skills` and never adds explicit `--skill <path>` for allowed paths. `prompt.skill_inherit` also needs to be treated as a skill source.

## What to build

- When trust allows skills, pass explicit `--skill <path>` args for resolved `skills.paths` and `prompt.skill_inherit`.
- Include both sources in `computeSkillSources()` audit hashing.
- Keep default behavior deny-all and zero skills.

## Acceptance criteria

- Tests assert default runner has `--no-skills` and no `--skill` args.
- Tests assert trusted runner adds explicit `--skill` args after allowlist validation.
- Audit row records sha256 for `skills.paths` and `prompt.skill_inherit` sources.
close_reason: Done: trusted skills now pass as explicit --skill args and audit includes inherited skill source; tests/lint/build pass

title: Script runner: harden --allow-skills-roots path boundary validation
description:
## Context

Trust hardening. Current `allowSkillsRoots` validation uses string `startsWith`, so sibling prefixes can bypass intended root boundaries (for example `/opt/skills-evil` vs `/opt/skills`).

## What to build

- Resolve configured roots and candidate skill paths to absolute normalized paths.
- Validate containment with path-relative boundary semantics, not string prefix.
- Apply to both `skills.paths` and `prompt.skill_inherit`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Tests cover allowed child path, rejected sibling prefix, rejected relative traversal, and multiple root entries.
- Error message names offending path and root policy without leaking file contents.
close_reason: Done: allowSkillsRoots now uses path-boundary validation; tests/lint/build pass

title: Script/service runner: make --allow-local-scripts semantics fail-closed
description:
## Context

Trust semantics drift. `--allow-local-scripts` currently lets specs with `skills.scripts` pass compat guard, but script-runner does not execute those local scripts. That creates a misleading and unsafe contract.

## What to build

- Decide and implement one clear behavior:
  - Preferred production-fast option: keep rejecting `skills.scripts` for script-class specialists and remove/deprecate `--allow-local-scripts` for `sp serve`/`sp script`.
  - Only implement execution if a separate design explicitly specifies pre/post script lifecycle, sandboxing, auditing, and timeout.
- Update CLI help/docs accordingly.

## Acceptance criteria

- Tests assert scripts are rejected with clear error in script-class runner.
- `sp serve` docs and using-script-specialists skill no longer imply unimplemented script execution.
- No local script can run from service path by accident.
close_reason: Done: local scripts now fail closed in script/service mode; tests/lint/build pass

title: Script runner: inject minimal JSON output contract from output_schema
description:
## Context

Fast quality fix. Script-class JSON specialists validate `output_schema.required` after model output, but the runner does not centrally inject a minimal output contract. Each service spec/template must remember to include schema instructions, which caused schema drift in darth-feedor-style summarizers.

## What to build

- Add minimal output-contract instruction for script-class specialists when `execution.response_format === "json"`.
- Include required fields and, when available, schema/example shape without overloading prompt size.
- Avoid changing package-class `sp run` output contract behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- Test verifies rendered prompt sent to Pi includes required JSON keys for a JSON script specialist.
- Test verifies markdown/text response formats are not forced into JSON.
- Existing invalid-json validation remains intact.
close_reason: Done: JSON script prompts now include required output contract; tests/lint/build pass

title: Epic: production-harden script/service specialists and evaluate SDK runner
description:
## Overview

Harden script-class specialists (`sp script` and `sp serve`) for production non-coding pipelines such as darth-feedor article/news summarization, then evaluate and roll out a Pi SDK-backed runner if benchmarks prove it better than per-request Pi subprocesses.

This epic is ordered for production recovery first: small subprocess hardening fixes land before trust cleanup, readiness improvements, and SDK migration work.

## Goals

- Resume darth-feedor production pipeline ASAP with deterministic prompt handling and bounded failure modes.
- Keep script/service specialists usable as non-coding LLM transforms with no coding tools by default.
- Preserve Pi auth/model compatibility while reducing prompt leakage, process-list leakage, and runtime drift.
- Establish an SDK migration path behind a flag, with subprocess fallback until proven safe.

## Non-goals

- Do not change package-class `sp run` specialist orchestration semantics.
- Do not enable coding tools for service/script specialists.
- Do not require darth-feedor to clone specialists source or change its HTTP contract unless explicitly versioned.

## Success criteria

- Production-fast hardening tasks are complete before SDK work begins.
- `sp script`/`sp serve` prompts are not passed via argv and run with correct cwd/project context.
- Prompt size, output schema, trust flags, db path, and readiness behavior are test-covered.
- SDK runner is benchmarked against subprocess runner on darth-feedor-style article workloads before becoming default.

## Context / background

- Discovered from specialists-6vy: Pi CLI auto-context injection required isolation flags for script-class calls.
- Relevant code: `src/specialist/script-runner.ts`, `src/cli/script.ts`, `src/cli/serve.ts`, docs under `docs/specialists-service*.md`, skill docs under `config/skills/using-script-specialists/`.
- Pi docs reviewed: CLI JSON mode, stdin in print/json mode, SDK `createAgentSession`, zero-tool/custom ResourceLoader possibilities, RPC mode tradeoffs.

description:

### Specialist Output — overthinker (job 5568c9) [WAITING — more output may follow]

## Summary

Reviewer PASS should finalize chain. Finalize closes keep-alive executor, marks reviewer terminal, writes audit note, then chain becomes publishable through `sp merge` or `sp epic merge`.

Recommended design: **auto-finalize on PASS + explicit `sp finalize` retry command**.

## Phase 1 - Initial Analysis

### Current deadlock replaced

Current loop:

```text
executor --keep-alive -> waiting
reviewer -> done + Verdict: PASS
chain/epic readiness sees PASS path
sp epic merge blocks because waiting counts active
sp merge blocks because epic unresolved
sp resume "End" only writes fifo
manual sp stop / git merge becomes escape hatch
```

Target loop:

```text
executor --keep-alive -> waiting
reviewer -> done + Verdict: PASS
PASS hook -> finalize chain
finalize -> close waiting executor -> done
chain -> pass + no active jobs
sp merge <chain> allowed inside unresolved epic
or sp epic merge allowed when all chains pass
```

### Target job state machine

No schema rewrite. Use existing persisted statuses.

```text
starting
  emitter: Supervisor initial status / status.json writer
  -> running
     emitter: runner starts active specialist session

running
  -> waiting
     emitter: JobRegistry.setResumeFn / keep-alive executor finished turn
     replaces: "success state stays active forever"
  -> done
     emitter: JobRegistry.complete / non-keep-alive completion
  -> error
     emitter: JobRegistry.fail / runner error
  -> cancelled
     emitter: JobRegistry.cancel / sp stop
  -> done
     emitter: reviewer completes with PASS/PARTIAL/FAIL output

waiting
  -> running
     emitter: JobRegistry.followUp / sp resume
     preserves: PARTIAL fix loop
  -> done
     emitter: NEW finalizeChain()
     owners:
       - reviewer PASS auto-hook
       - sp finalize <chain>
       - sp finalize --epic <epic>
     replaces: manual sp stop --force after PASS
  -> cancelled
     emitter: sp stop --force
     remains escape hatch only
  -> error
     emitter: failed resume/close path

done
  terminal

error
  terminal for readiness unless new fix-loop job follows

cancelled
  terminal for process liveness, not proof of PASS
```

### PASS hook location

Hook should run after reviewer result persists.

Proposed emitter path:

```text
reviewer job writes done + output
  -> parse reviewer verdict
  -> if PASS:
       finalizeChain(chain_root_bead_id)
       append bead note: reviewer PASS finalized executor(s)
       recompute readiness
```

Files touched:

| Need | File |
|---|---|
| Parse verdict from reviewer completion | `src/specialist/runner.ts` or `src/specialist/supervisor.ts` |
| Persist status transitions | `src/specialist/supervisor.ts` |
| Reuse close waiting session logic | `src/specialist/jobRegistry.ts`, `src/cli/stop.ts` |
| Recompute chain/epic readiness | `src/specialist/epic-readiness.ts`, `src/specialist/epic-reconciler.ts` |

## Phase 2 - Devil's Advocate

### Risk: auto-finalize kills PARTIAL loop

Mitigation: finalize only on parsed `Verdict: PASS`. PARTIAL and FAIL never close executor. Executor stays `waiting`, so `sp resume` remains valid.

### Risk: reviewer PASS parsing brittle

Current readiness parses raw text via regex. Runner has structured verdict schema too. Target should prefer structured verdict when present, fallback regex for compatibility.

### Risk: reviewer crashes after writing PASS but before finalize

Mitigation: `sp finalize <chain> --passed` scans latest reviewer result and finalizes idempotently. `sp epic status` should show:

```text
PASS verdict found, finalization pending
Run: sp finalize <chain>
```

### Risk: executor crashes mid-review

If waiting executor PID dead, readiness marks failed today. Target should distinguish:
- PASS exists + close/finalize possible: finalize dead waiting executor to `done` with audit reason `pass-finalized-dead-session`
- no PASS: chain failed or blocked; PARTIAL loop cannot resume dead executor

### Risk: dirty worktree at merge

Finalization must not merge. Merge commands keep current dirty gates:
- `assertMainRepoCleanForMerge`
- dirty overlap checks
- stash/shelve logic if already supported

Dirty worktree blocks publication, not finalization.

### Risk: per-chain merge inside epic breaks epic bookkeeping

Mitigation: `sp merge <chain>` inside unresolved epic must call `syncEpicStateAfterMerge`. Epic remains unresolved until all chains published/pass. No terminal epic transition from one chain merge.

## Phase 3 - Synthesis

### Target chain state machine

Readiness states stay:

```text
pending | blocked | pass | failed
```

Target interpretation:

```text
pending
  current: active jobs, no terminal reviewer verdict
  proposed: active work in progress
  transition:
    executor waiting + reviewer not done -> pending/blocked

blocked
  current: no reviewer verdict, or fix-loop work after PARTIAL/FAIL
  proposed: needs reviewer or reviewer rerun
  transition:
    PARTIAL + post-review fix done -> blocked until reviewer rerun

failed
  current: latest reviewer FAIL/PARTIAL with no fix-loop, dead active jobs
  proposed: hard failure requiring fix-loop/reviewer rerun
  transition:
    reviewer FAIL -> failed
    dead executor no PASS -> failed

pass
  current: reviewer PASS, but active waiting job may block merge
  proposed: reviewer PASS + finalize complete + no active jobs
  transition:
    reviewer PASS -> auto-finalize -> pass
```

### Exact `merge_ready` rule

Epic readiness `merge_ready` when:

```text
all chains have state=pass
AND no chain has active job status in starting|running|waiting
AND prep jobs are terminal
AND persisted epic not merged/abandoned
```

Replace current sticky failed rule:

```text
failed -> merge_ready only when allChainsPass
```

With recoverable rule:

```text
failed -> resolving when no current failed chains but not all pass
failed -> merge_ready when all chains pass and no active jobs
```

### Publishability rule

Chain publishable when:

```text
latest reviewer verdict == PASS
AND chain has no active jobs after finalize
AND merge worthiness passes
AND branch not already published
```

This permits:

```text
sp merge <chain>
```

inside epic states:

```text
open | resolving | merge_ready
```

if target chain publishable.

### Command surface table

| Command | Now | Proposed | Files |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sp merge <chain>` | Blocks if epic unresolved | Allow when target chain publishable | `src/cli/merge.ts` |
| `sp epic merge <epic>` | Requires resolving/merge_ready, blocks on any waiting job | Runs finalize preflight for PASS chains, then merges all publishable/all-pass chains | `src/cli/epic.ts`, `src/specialist/epic-lifecycle.ts` |
| `sp resume <job>` | Writes fifo only | Same. No termination semantics | `src/cli/resume.ts` |
| `sp stop --force` | Only practical terminator | Escape hatch, not normal PASS path | `src/cli/stop.ts` |
| `sp result <job>` | Reads result | May show PASS-finalization hint | `src/cli/result.ts` |
| NEW `sp finalize <chain>` | Missing | Idempotently closes waiting executor(s) after PASS | `src/cli/finalize.ts`, command router |
| NEW `sp finalize --epic <epic>` | Missing | Finalizes all PASS chains in epic | `src/cli/finalize.ts` |
| `sp epic sync --apply` | Sticky failed heal only all-pass | Recompute failed->resolving/merge_ready | `src/specialist/epic-readiness.ts`, `src/specialist/epic-reconciler.ts` |

## Phase 4 - Final Refined Output

### Recommended design

Use hybrid:

1. **Reviewer PASS auto-finalizes executor**
2. **`sp finalize <chain>` exists as retry/recovery command**
3. **`sp merge <chain>` allowed for publishable PASS chain inside unresolved epic**
4. **`sp epic merge` finalizes PASS chains before readiness gate**
5. **FAILED persisted state heals on recompute**

### Direct answer: waiting executor termination

Waiting `--keep-alive` executor terminates through `finalizeChain()`.

```text
reviewer PASS
  -> supervisor detects PASS
  -> finalizeChain(chain)
  -> close waiting executor session
  -> set executor status=done
  -> append bead note
  -> recompute readiness
  -> chain publishable
```

No manual `sp stop`. No manual `git merge`.

### Failure modes covered

| Failure | Behavior |
|---|---|
| PARTIAL | Executor stays waiting. Orchestrator runs `sp resume`. Reviewer rerun required |
| FAIL | Chain failed. No finalize unless later fix-loop PASS |
| Reviewer crash before verdict | Chain blocked. Rerun reviewer |
| Reviewer crash after PASS before finalize | `sp finalize <chain>` recovers |
| Executor crash mid-review | PASS can finalize as done with audit; no PASS means failed |
| Dirty worktree at merge | Merge blocks. Finalized chain remains publishable |
| Sticky FAILED epic | `sp epic sync --apply` heals to resolving or merge_ready |
| Already finalized | `sp finalize` no-op, exits 0 with audit summary |

### Migration plan

1. Add compatibility reader: no new required `status.json` fields.
2. Add optional audit metadata only:
   - `finalized_by`
   - `finalized_at_ms`
   - `finalize_reason`
3. Run recovery:
   ```text
   sp epic sync --apply <epic>
   sp finalize --epic <epic> --passed
   sp epic status <epic>
   ```
4. For epics stuck `FAILED`:
   - recompute readiness
   - if no current failed chains: move `failed -> resolving`
   - if all chains pass: move `failed -> merge_ready`
5. Delete gotchas from docs/skills:
   - “use manual git merge --no-ff after PASS”
   - “sp stop --force waiting executor before merge”
   - “FAILED means terminal broken”
   - “sp resume End terminates job”

### Alternatives

#### Alternative A: Auto-finalize on PASS

Pros:
- Best UX.
- Deterministic.
- Removes manual stop/merge habit.
- Preserves PARTIAL loop.

Cons:
- More supervisor coupling.
- Needs idempotency.
- PASS parser must be reliable.

Verdict: recommended.

#### Alternative B: Explicit `sp finalize <chain>` only

Pros:
- Simple.
- Safer operator control.
- Easier audit.

Cons:
- Still manual step after PASS.
- Orchestrators can forget.
- Deadlock reduced, not eliminated.

Verdict: required fallback, not primary path.

#### Alternative C: Reviewer-owned merge

Pros:
- PASS directly publishes.
- Few orchestrator steps.

Cons:
- Reviewer gains git side effects.
- Dirty worktree conflicts happen inside reviewer job.
- Harder retry boundary.
- Worse audit separation.

Verdict: reject.

## Final Answer

Implement **auto-finalize on reviewer PASS plus explicit `sp finalize` retry**.

Core rule:

```text
PASS is not publishable until finalization closes waiting keep-alive executor(s).
Finalization happens automatically on PASS.
sp finalize repairs missed finalization.
sp merge can publish one PASS chain inside unresolved epic.
sp epic merge publishes all chains only when all pass and no active jobs remain.
```

Best files to change:
- `src/specialist/supervisor.ts`
- `src/specialist/jobRegistry.ts`
- `src/specialist/epic-readiness.ts`
- `src/specialist/epic-reconciler.ts`
- `src/cli/merge.ts`
- `src/cli/epic.ts`
- add `src/cli/finalize.ts`

Files touched:

| Need | File |
|---|---|
| Parse verdict from reviewer completion | `src/specialist/runner.ts` or `src/specialist/supervisor.ts` |
| Persist status transitions | `src/specialist/supervisor.ts` |
| Reuse close waiting session logic | `src/specialist/jobRegistry.ts`, `src/cli/stop.ts` |
| Recompute chain/epic readiness | `src/specialist/epic-readiness.ts`, `src/specialist/epic-reconciler.ts` |

## Phase 2 - Devil's Advocate

### Risk: auto-finalize kills PARTIAL loop

Mitigation: finalize only on parsed `Verdict: PASS`. PARTIAL and FAIL never close executor. Executor stays `waiting`, so `sp resume` remains valid.

### Risk: reviewer PASS parsing brittle

Current readiness parses raw text via regex. Runner has structured verdict schema too. Target should prefer structured verdict when present, fallback regex for compatibility.

### Risk: reviewer crashes after writing PASS but before finalize

Mitigation: `sp finalize <chain> --passed` scans latest reviewer result and finalizes idempotently. `sp epic status` should show:

```text
PASS verdict found, finalization pending
Run: sp finalize <chain>
```

### Risk: executor crashes mid-review

If waiting executor PID dead, readiness marks failed today. Target should distinguish:
- PASS exists + close/finalize possible: finalize dead waiting executor to `done` with audit reason `pass-finalized-dead-session`
- no PASS: chain failed or blocked; PARTIAL loop cannot resume dead executor

### Risk: dirty worktree at merge

Finalization must not merge. Merge commands keep current dirty gates:
- `assertMainRepoCleanForMerge`
- dirty overlap checks
- stash/shelve logic if already supported

Dirty worktree blocks publication, not finalization.

### Risk: per-chain merge inside epic breaks epic bookkeeping

Mitigation: `sp merge <chain>` inside unresolved epic must call `syncEpicStateAfterMerge`. Epic remains unresolved until all chains published/pass. No terminal epic transition from one chain merge.

## Phase 3 - Synthesis

### Target chain state machine

Readiness states stay:

```text
pending | blocked | pass | failed
```

Target interpretation:

```text
pending
  current: active jobs, no terminal reviewer verdict
  proposed: active work in progress
  transition:
    executor waiting + reviewer not done -> pending/blocked

blocked
  current: no reviewer verdict, or fix-loop work after PARTIAL/FAIL
  proposed: needs reviewer or reviewer rerun
  transition:
    PARTIAL + post-review fix done -> blocked until reviewer rerun

failed
  current: latest reviewer FAIL/PARTIAL with no fix-loop, dead active jobs
  proposed: hard failure requiring fix-loop/reviewer rerun
  transition:
    reviewer FAIL -> failed
    dead executor no PASS -> failed

pass
  current: reviewer PASS, but active waiting job may block merge
  proposed: reviewer PASS + finalize complete + no active jobs
  transition:
    reviewer PASS -> auto-finalize -> pass
```

### Exact `merge_ready` rule

Epic readiness `merge_ready` when:

```text
all chains have state=pass
AND no chain has active job status in starting|running|waiting
AND prep jobs are terminal
AND persisted epic not merged/abandoned
```

Replace current sticky failed rule:

```text
failed -> merge_ready only when allChainsPass
```

With recoverable rule:

```text
failed -> resolving when no current failed chains but not all pass
failed -> merge_ready when all chains pass and no active jobs
```

### Publishability rule

Chain publishable when:

```text
latest reviewer verdict == PASS
AND chain has no active jobs after finalize
AND merge worthiness passes
AND branch not already published
```

This permits:

```text
sp merge <chain>
```

inside epic states:

```text
open | resolving | merge_ready
```

if target chain publishable.

### Command surface table

| Command | Now | Proposed | Files |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sp merge <chain>` | Blocks if epic unresolved | Allow when target chain publishable | `src/cli/merge.ts` |
| `sp epic merge <epic>` | Requires resolving/merge_ready, blocks on any waiting job | Runs finalize preflight for PASS chains, then merges all publishable/all-pass chains | `src/cli/epic.ts`, `src/specialist/epic-lifecycle.ts` |
| `sp resume <job>` | Writes fifo only | Same. No termination semantics | `src/cli/resume.ts` |
| `sp stop --force` | Only practical terminator | Escape hatch, not normal PASS path | `src/cli/stop.ts` |
| `sp result <job>` | Reads result | May show PASS-finalization hint | `src/cli/result.ts` |
| NEW `sp finalize <chain>` | Missing | Idempotently closes waiting executor(s) after PASS | `src/cli/finalize.ts`, command router |
| NEW `sp finalize --epic <epic>` | Missing | Finalizes all PASS chains in epic | `src/cli/finalize.ts` |
| `sp epic sync --apply` | Sticky failed heal only all-pass | Recompute failed->resolving/merge_ready | `src/specialist/epic-readiness.ts`, `src/specialist/epic-reconciler.ts` |

## Phase 4 - Final Refined Output

### Recommended design

Use hybrid:

1. **Reviewer PASS auto-finalizes executor**
2. **`sp finalize <chain>` exists as retry/recovery command**
3. **`sp merge <chain>` allowed for publishable PASS chain inside unresolved epic**
4. **`sp epic merge` finalizes PASS chains before readiness gate**
5. **FAILED persisted state heals on recompute**

### Direct answer: waiting executor termination

Waiting `--keep-alive` executor terminates through `finalizeChain()`.

```text
reviewer PASS
  -> supervisor detects PASS
  -> finalizeChain(chain)
  -> close waiting executor session
  -> set executor status=done
  -> append bead note
  -> recompute readiness
  -> chain publishable
```

No manual `sp stop`. No manual `git merge`.

### Failure modes covered

| Failure | Behavior |
|---|---|
| PARTIAL | Executor stays waiting. Orchestrator runs `sp resume`. Reviewer rerun required |
| FAIL | Chain failed. No finalize unless later fix-loop PASS |
| Reviewer crash before verdict | Chain blocked. Rerun reviewer |
| Reviewer crash after PASS before finalize | `sp finalize <chain>` recovers |
| Executor crash mid-review | PASS can finalize as done with audit; no PASS means failed |
| Dirty worktree at merge | Merge blocks. Finalized chain remains publishable |
| Sticky FAILED epic | `sp epic sync --apply` heals to resolving or merge_ready |
| Already finalized | `sp finalize` no-op, exits 0 with audit summary |

### Migration plan

1. Add compatibility reader: no new required `status.json` fields.
2. Add optional audit metadata only:
   - `finalized_by`
   - `finalized_at_ms`
   - `finalize_reason`
3. Run recovery:
   ```text
   sp epic sync --apply <epic>
   sp finalize --epic <epic> --passed
   sp epic status <epic>
   ```
4. For epics stuck `FAILED`:
   - recompute readiness
   - if no current failed chains: move `failed -> resolving`
   - if all chains pass: move `failed -> merge_ready`
5. Delete gotchas from docs/skills:
   - “use manual git merge --no-ff after PASS”
   - “sp stop --force waiting executor before merge”
   - “FAILED means terminal broken”
   - “sp resume End terminates job”

### Alternatives

#### Alternative A: Auto-finalize on PASS

Pros:
- Best UX.
- Deterministic.
- Removes manual stop/merge habit.
- Preserves PARTIAL loop.

Cons:
- More supervisor coupling.
- Needs idempotency.
- PASS parser must be reliable.

Verdict: recommended.

#### Alternative B: Explicit `sp finalize <chain>` only

Pros:
- Simple.
- Safer operator control.
- Easier audit.

Cons:
- Still manual step after PASS.
- Orchestrators can forget.
- Deadlock reduced, not eliminated.

Verdict: required fallback, not primary path.

#### Alternative C: Reviewer-owned merge

Pros:
- PASS directly publishes.
- Few orchestrator steps.

Cons:
- Reviewer gains git side effects.
- Dirty worktree conflicts happen inside reviewer job.
- Harder retry boundary.
- Worse audit separation.

Verdict: reject.

## Final Answer

Implement **auto-finalize on reviewer PASS plus explicit `sp finalize` retry**.

Core rule:

```text
PASS is not publishable until finalization closes waiting keep-alive executor(s).
Finalization happens automatically on PASS.
sp finalize repairs missed finalization.
sp merge can publish one PASS chain inside unresolved epic.
sp epic merge publishes all chains only when all pass and no active jobs remain.
```

Best files to change:
- `src/specialist/supervisor.ts`
- `src/specialist/jobRegistry.ts`
- `src/specialist/epic-readiness.ts`
- `src/specialist/epic-reconciler.ts`
- `src/cli/merge.ts`
- `src/cli/epic.ts`
- add `src/cli/finalize.ts`

### Specialist Output — overthinker (job 8cf271) [WAITING — more output may follow]

## Summary

Design recommendation: **default auto-shelve unrelated dirty main state**, block dirty overlap with epic incoming paths. Reason: preserves lifecycle path, avoids manual merge bypass, protects local work.

## Phase 1 — Initial Analysis

### Design Recommendation

`sp epic merge` should:

1. Compute incoming epic path set before merge.
2. Compute dirty main path set, tracked + untracked.
3. If dirty path intersects incoming path set: fail safely.
4. If dirty path unrelated: stash/shelve named state.
5. Run existing readiness/reviewer PASS/lifecycle checks unchanged.
6. Run existing direct merge or PR mode unchanged.
7. Restore shelved state after success/failure.
8. If restore conflicts: stop with exact recovery commands.

Recommended CLI:

- Default: `--auto-shelve` behavior enabled.
- `--no-shelve`: preserve old strict clean-tree refusal.
- `--manual-fallback`: optional later; not first choice. Too easy to drift from lifecycle semantics.

### Core Algorithm

Preflight:

```text
incomingPaths = union git diff --name-only <main>...<chainBranch> for all chains
dirtyPaths = git status --porcelain=v1 -z parsed tracked + untracked
overlap = dirtyPaths ∩ incomingPaths
```

Decision:

```text
overlap non-empty -> fail, list paths, no stash
dirty unrelated -> git stash push --include-untracked --message "sp epic merge <epic-id> auto-shelve <timestamp>" -- <dirtyPaths>
clean -> normal merge
```

Restore:


title: xt update: bulk refresh xtrm-managed assets across one or many repos
description:
PROBLEM: After tsnwh.3 detects drift, the operator needs a single command to apply the fix across N repos.

SUCCESS:
- `xt update [--apply] [--root <dir>] [--repo <path>]`:
  - Without `--apply`: dry-run, prints what would change.
  - With `--apply`: refreshes `.xtrm/skills/default/` and `.xtrm/hooks/default/` from canonical for each detected repo.
  - `--root <dir>`: discovers all xtrm-managed repos under <dir> and processes each.
  - `--repo <path>`: targets a single repo.
- Per-repo atomic refresh: write to `.xtrm/skills/default.tmp/`, swap on success, leave existing on failure.
- Output: per-repo table (refreshed / already-current / failed reason).
- Failures in one repo do not abort the loop.

- Reviewer PASS gate.

- Idempotent: running twice produces same result on second.

title: sp pin: explicit snapshot command + version sentinel + drift warning
description:
PROBLEM: With live-from-package as the default (z9cku.1), explicit pinning becomes a meaningful opt-in for projects that want stability against npm package upgrades. Today `sp init --sync-defaults` does the snapshot but treats the result as authoritative; there is no detection if the package version drifts. unitAI-edl3 (deferred) covers the sentinel idea. This bead subsumes it.

SUCCESS:
- New command `sp pin` (alias `sp init --sync-defaults`): snapshots package canonical specialists into `.specialists/default/` AND writes `.specialists/default/.installed-version` containing the package version string + git SHA if known.
- New flag `sp pin --refresh`: re-syncs the snapshot to the current package version (idempotent if same version).
- New flag `sp pin --check`: prints pin status (pinned at version X, current package is Y, drift: yes/no), exits 0/1 accordingly.
- When sp commands run in a project with `.specialists/default/.installed-version` present AND mismatched against the live package version: print one-line stderr warning "specialists: pinned at v3.X.Y, package is v3.Z.W. Run `sp pin --refresh` to update.". Print at most once per session via env or a small cache.
- When no sentinel + no `.specialists/default/`: silent (user is on live mode, no pin to drift).
- When no sentinel + `.specialists/default/` present (legacy): treat as legacy unpinned; suggest pinning explicitly.
- Close `unitAI-edl3` as subsumed.

CONSTRAINTS:

title: Bug: auto-commit path parsing strips first character of modified-file paths
description:
PROBLEM: src/specialist/supervisor.ts:listSubstantiveWorktreeFiles() corrupts paths reported by `git status --porcelain` for modified files (XY status with leading space like ` M `), causing `git add` to fail with `fatal: pathspec did not match any files`.

Root cause: lines 304-307 do `.map((line) => line.trim())` before `.map((line) => line.slice(3).trim())`. The `git status --porcelain` format is exactly 2 chars XY + 1 space + path, so path starts at index 3. But for single-letter statuses like ` M path` (modified, not staged), the leading space is part of the XY field; trimming it shifts everything left, making `slice(3)` cut into the path itself.

Examples observed in .specialists/db/observability.db (events: auto_commit_failed):
- ` M src/pi/session.ts`         → trim → `M src/pi/session.ts`         → slice(3) → `rc/pi/session.ts` (DROPS "s")
- ` M src/specialist/manifest-resolver.ts` → trim → `M src/specialist/manifest-resolver.ts` → slice(3) → `rc/specialist/manifest-resolver.ts`
- ` M .specialists/default/explorer.specialist.json` → trim → `M .specialists/default/explorer.specialist.json` → slice(3) → `specialists/default/explorer.specialist.json` (DROPS leading dot)

`?? path` (untracked) and `UU path` (conflict) work correctly because XY already occupies both bytes without a leading space. So the bug is silent for untracked files and breaks for modified-but-not-staged files.

This means executor/debugger checkpoint_on_waiting auto-commit silently fails on every modified file; only newly-created files are committed.

SUCCESS:
- listSubstantiveWorktreeFiles parses porcelain v1 output correctly: XY at byte 0-1, space at byte 2, path from byte 3 onward (with rename split on " -> " for renamed entries, quoting handled).
- Test added in tests/unit/specialist/supervisor.test.ts (or new file) covering: untracked (`??`), modified-unstaged (` M`), modified-staged (`M `), added-staged (`A `), deleted (` D`), renamed (`R `), and a path with embedded spaces (quoted).
- Existing event: parsed paths must NOT alter the first character; e.g. ` M src/pi/session.ts` parses to exactly `src/pi/session.ts`.
- After fix, regenerate the qujxo.2 scenario locally (or write a small repro test) and confirm no `auto_commit_failed` with `did not match` for legitimate paths.
- No regression to noise-path filter behavior.

SCOPE:
- src/specialist/supervisor.ts:294-316 (listSubstantiveWorktreeFiles parsing)
- tests/unit/specialist/supervisor.test.ts (new tests)
- No CLI surface change. No event schema change.

NON_GOALS:
- No move to `git status --porcelain=v2` (v1 is fine once parsed correctly).
- No change to noise-path prefix list.
- No change to auto_commit policy enums or schema.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Reviewer PASS gate.
- Must support porcelain v1 quoting rules: paths with special characters are wrapped in double quotes; the existing dequote `replace(/^"|"$/g, "")` should be preserved or improved.
- Renames format: `XY old -> new` — keep using the destination side.

VALIDATION:
- npx tsc --noEmit passes.
- New unit tests pass; existing tests stay green.
- Manual repro: in a worktree, modify an existing file (do not stage), run a short-lived debugger/executor with checkpoint_on_waiting, observe that the auto-commit succeeds and the modified file is included.

OUTPUT: Diff summary, new test names + counts, before/after porcelain parse table for each XY case, residual risks. Closes a silent data-loss class for executor/debugger workflow checkpoints.

Three concrete gaps prevent the gzrx design from being realized at runtime: (a) PiSessionOptions does not carry specialist name/permissions so the resolver cannot apply per-specialist overrides, (b) the resolver path is opt-in via SPECIALISTS_USE_RESOLVER env var so no production runs touch it, (c) the legacy hardcoded GITNEXUS_*_TOOLS / SERENA_*_TOOLS arrays in src/pi/session.ts:156-219 remain the production source of truth.

SUCCESS: After this bead:
- PiSessionOptions has new fields specialistName?: string and specialistPermissions?: ManifestPolicy['permissions'] threaded from runner.ts/use_specialist.tool.ts callers.
- src/pi/session.ts:resolvePermissionTools accepts and applies these as specialistOverride to resolveManifestTools (matching the diagnostic path in resolution-diagnostics.ts).
- The runtime decision is no longer env-gated. Either remove SPECIALISTS_USE_RESOLVER entirely and always use the resolver, or make resolver default-on with SPECIALISTS_USE_LEGACY=1 as the escape hatch.
- One specialist per tier (READ_ONLY/LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH) has been spawned end-to-end and the actual --tools observed (sp ps + feed) match what sp config show --resolved predicts.
- The hardcoded GITNEXUS_READ_TOOLS, SERENA_READ_TOOLS, SERENA_LOW_TOOLS, SERENA_WRITE_TOOLS, GITNEXUS_WRITE_TOOLS constants and the mapPermissionToTools function in src/pi/session.ts:156-280 are deleted.
- Audit of config/specialists/*.specialist.json: confirm only specialists whose policy diverges from tier default need a permissions[tier] block; today that's just explorer.
- Original §0 problem verified: a live explorer run shows --tools that excludes grep,find,ls and includes gitnexus_query / search_for_pattern / find_file. Capture a feed snippet as evidence.

SCOPE:
- src/pi/session.ts (PiSessionOptions interface, resolvePermissionTools, mapPermissionToTools removal, hardcoded array constant removal)

- tests/unit/pi/session.test.ts (update to reflect resolver-only path)
- config/specialists/*.specialist.json (audit only; mutate only where policy genuinely diverges)
- Read context: docs/design/gzrx-tool-catalog.md §7 steps 7,9,11; resolution-diagnostics.ts loadResolvedConfigReport for the wiring pattern.

NON_GOALS:
- No new design.
- No new specialist roles.
- No catalog file changes.
- Do not migrate specialists whose tier-default policy is fine; only add permissions[tier] where genuinely needed.

- Reviewer PASS gate.

Snapshot tests in tests/unit/specialist/manifest-resolver.test.ts already cover this for the tier-default path; extend if needed.

## Core Principles

**SRP** — Single Responsibility. Every function does ONE thing. Every file has ONE reason to change.
**DRY** — Don't Repeat Yourself. Similar code twice → extract.
**KISS** — Simplest solution that works. No premature abstraction.
**YAGNI** — Don't build what isn't asked. No speculative features.
**Boy Scout Rule** — Leave code cleaner than found. Fix adjacent smells.

---

## Naming

- Variables reveal intent: `userCount` not `n`, `isAuthenticated` not `flag`
- Functions verb+noun: `getUserById()`, `validateToken()`, `parseConfig()`
- Booleans are questions: `isActive`, `hasPermission`, `canEdit`, `shouldRetry`
- Constants SCREAMING_SNAKE: `MAX_RETRY_COUNT`, `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`
- Types/Interfaces PascalCase: `UserProfile`, `RunOptions`, `EventHandler`
- Files kebab-case: `user-service.ts`, `parse-config.ts`

Need comment to explain name → name wrong. Rename.

---

## Functions

- **Small**: 5-15 lines ideal, 25 max. Longer → split.
- **One thing**: Does one thing, does it well, does it only.
- **One abstraction level**: Don't mix high-level orchestration with low-level parsing.
- **Few arguments**: 0-2 preferred, 3 max. Options object for more.
- **No side effects**: Don't mutate inputs. Return new values.
- **Guard clauses first**: Handle edge cases early, return/throw, then happy path.

```typescript
// GOOD — guard clauses, single level, clear intent
function getUserRole(user: User): Role {
  if (!user.isActive) return Role.NONE;
  if (user.isAdmin) return Role.ADMIN;
  return user.roles[0] ?? Role.DEFAULT;
}

// BAD — nested, mixed levels, unclear
function getUserRole(user: User): Role {
  if (user) {
    if (user.isActive) {
      if (user.isAdmin) {
        return Role.ADMIN;
      } else {
        if (user.roles.length > 0) {
          return user.roles[0];
        } else {
          return Role.DEFAULT;
        }
      }
    } else {
      return Role.NONE;
    }
  }
  return Role.NONE;
}
```

---

## Type Safety

- **Strict TypeScript always**: `strict: true`, no `any` unless interfacing with untyped externals.
- **Zod for runtime validation**: All external input (API params, CLI args, config files) validated with Zod schemas.
- **Discriminated unions over type assertions**: Use `type Result = Success | Failure` not `as Success`.
- **Exhaustive switches**: `never` default case for union exhaustiveness.
- **No non-null assertions** (`!`): Proper narrowing or optional chaining.
- **Readonly where possible**: `readonly` arrays and properties for data that shouldn't mutate.

```typescript
// GOOD — discriminated union with exhaustive handling
type Result = { ok: true; data: string } | { ok: false; error: Error };

function handle(result: Result): string {
  switch (result.ok) {
    case true: return result.data;
    case false: throw result.error;
    default: return result satisfies never;
  }
}
```

---

## Error Handling

- **Fail fast, fail loud**: Throw on invalid state. Don't silently return defaults.
- **Specific error types**: `class NotFoundError extends Error` not generic `Error`.
- **Error messages include context**: `Failed to load config from ${path}: ${e.message}`.
- **Try-catch at boundaries only**: Don't wrap every function call. Catch at API/CLI/handler level.
- **Never swallow errors**: No empty catch blocks. At minimum, log.
- **Errors not control flow**: Don't use try-catch for expected conditions.

---

## Code Structure

- **Guard clauses over nesting**: Early returns flatten logic.
- **Max 2 nesting levels**: Deeper → extract function.
- **Composition over inheritance**: Small functions composed together.
- **Colocation**: Keep related code close. Tests next to source.
- **Barrel exports sparingly**: Only for public API surfaces, not internal modules.
- **No circular dependencies**: A imports B and B imports A → restructure.

---

## Async & Concurrency

- **async/await over raw Promises**: Clearer control flow.
- **`Promise.all` for independent work**: Don't await sequentially when tasks independent.
- **`AbortController` for cancellation**: Wire timeouts and cancellation through `AbortSignal`.
- **No fire-and-forget Promises**: Every Promise must be awaited or explicitly voided with comment.
- **Backpressure awareness**: Streams and queues need bounded buffers.

---

## Performance Defaults

- **Measure before optimizing**: No premature optimization. Profile first.
- **O(n) fine**: Don't prematurely reach for hash maps on small collections.
- **Lazy initialization**: Don't compute until needed.
- **Stream large data**: Don't buffer entire files into memory.
- **Cache at boundaries**: Cache external calls, not internal pure functions.

---

## Security Baseline

- **Never interpolate user input into shell commands**: Use `execFile` with args array, never `exec` with string.
- **Validate all external input**: Zod schemas at API/CLI boundary.
- **No secrets in source**: Use environment variables or config files.
- **Path traversal**: Resolve and validate file paths before I/O.
- **Sanitize output**: Escape user content before rendering in HTML/terminal.

---

## Comments

- **Delete obvious comments**: `// increment counter` above `counter++` = noise.
- **Comment WHY, never WHAT**: Code says what. Comments explain non-obvious decisions.
- **TODO format**: `// TODO(issue-id): description` — always link to tracking issue.
- **No commented-out code**: Delete it. Git remembers.
- **JSDoc for public APIs only**: Internal functions self-documenting.

---

## Testing Awareness

- **Write testable code**: Pure functions, dependency injection, no hidden globals.
- **Don't mock what you own**: Test real collaborators. Mock only at system boundaries.
- **If asked to write tests**: Use project's test framework. Prefer integration over unit for I/O code.

| ❌ Do NOT | ✅ Instead |
|-----------|-----------|
| Create `utils.ts` with one function | Put code where it's used |
| Write factory for 2 object types | Direct construction |
| Add helper for one-liner | Inline expression |
| Create abstraction used once | Wait until third use |
| Add error handling for impossible states | Trust type system |

title: [bug] Replace pi stdout raw-byte cap with retained-state caps
description:
PROBLEM: unitAI-a47ub raised DEFAULT_STDOUT_LIMIT_BYTES to 128MB to unblock changelog-keeper. This is a band-aid: the cap counts RAW bytes received from pi's stdout pipe regardless of how much script-runner actually retains. pi-mode-json emits dense per-token-delta events that the parser correctly discards on the fly (only retaining the final message_end / agent_end / assistant text). So the cap is rejecting runs based on pipe throughput, not memory usage. Worse: any caller that forwards raw stdout downstream could overflow a specialist context. Pipe-volume cap is the wrong knob.

ROOT CAUSE: src/specialist/script-runner.ts:335-373 accumulates stdoutBytes (raw pipe bytes) and kills the pi process when stdoutBytes > stdoutLimitBytes. But the retained state (assistantText replaces; pending is one partial line) is already bounded by single-message size. Only stderr accumulates unbounded.

SUCCESS:
1. Remove the raw-byte cap on stdout entirely. The streaming parser already bounds retained memory.
2. Add bounded caps on (a) single-line size during line accumulation in 'pending' (default ~16MB; protects against malformed unending lines), (b) assistantText replaceable size (default ~4MB; sanity cap for one final message), (c) stderr accumulation (default ~1MB; truncate when exceeded).
3. Revert DEFAULT_STDOUT_LIMIT_BYTES change (kept only for the cap-on-raw-bytes — no longer relevant). Either delete the constant or repurpose it as the assistantText cap.
4. SPECIALISTS_SCRIPT_STDOUT_LIMIT_BYTES env var: deprecate or repurpose to the assistantText cap. Backward-compatible if value still parsed; emit a one-time stderr warning if used.
5. classifyAttempt's outputTooLarge flag: keep but trigger only when retained-state caps are hit (not raw pipe).
6. Update tests: remove or rewrite the 'defaults stdout limit to 128MB' assertion to match new architecture. Add tests covering: huge token-delta stream succeeds (mock pi output >200MB total but with small final message); single oversized line truncated; stderr truncated.

SCOPE: src/specialist/script-runner.ts (runSingleAttempt loop, classifyAttempt, exported constants), tests/unit/specialist/script-runner.test.ts.

NON_GOALS:
- Do not change extractAssistantText or the post-attempt parser (extractAssistantText runs in script-runner.ts:162 and is fed lines from a buffer — verify it still works given streaming, but no semantic change).
- Do not modify changelog-keeper spec.
- Do not change pi invocation flags.
- Do not run real pi.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Final assistant text extraction must remain identical for healthy pi runs.
- outputTooLarge error semantics: the user-visible error should distinguish 'assistant message too large' vs 'stderr too large' vs 'malformed line too large'.
- Preserve incremental parser correctness for message_end / agent_end / assistant / legacy data.content[0].text events.

crashes with `Missing template variable: <name>` when the substituted
template contains a `$word` introduced by a *value* (e.g. `$pre_script_output`
that includes git-log/bead-query text discussing template variables literally).

The bug is in `src/specialist/script-runner.ts:117-122`
(`renderTaskTemplate`):
- `renderTemplate(template, variables)` substitutes correctly.
- `hasUnsubstitutedVariables(output)` then scans the *output* for any `$word`.
- If a commit message or bead description in the substituted data
  contains literal `$cwd` / `$next_tag` etc., it is misreported as a
  missing template variable and the run crashes.

Reproduction (live, 2026-05-01):
```
sp release prepare --from v3.10.0 --to HEAD
# -> [specialists] [ERROR] Fatal error: Error: Missing template variable: cwd
```
because commit `35a9f5df` body says `$cwd / $pre_script_output before
dispatch.`

SUCCESS:
1. `hasUnsubstitutedVariables` validates the **template** (pre-substitution)
   against the variable dictionary keys, not the rendered output. Throws
   only if the template references a `$word` not in `variables`.
2. `sp release prepare --from v3.10.0 --to HEAD` runs to completion (or
   fails on the model side, not on substitution).
3. Tests cover a `pre_script_output` value containing a literal `$cwd`
   / `$prev_tag` / `$next_tag` token; assert no crash.
4. No regression on legitimately-missing variables (template uses `$foo`
   not in dict -> still throws).

SCOPE: src/specialist/script-runner.ts (renderTaskTemplate +
hasUnsubstitutedVariables), tests/unit/specialist/script-runner.test.ts.

NON_GOALS:
- No change to renderTemplate semantics (still leaves unknown $word
  literal — that is correct because data may contain $word).
- No change to release CLI variable shape.

CONSTRAINTS: Backward compat: legitimate "template references unknown
variable" still errors as today. Only false-positives from data values
are eliminated.

VALIDATION: Unit tests + manual dogfood `sp release prepare --from v3.10.0
--to HEAD` succeeds (or fails with non-template error).

OUTPUT: Diff summary, dogfood smoke evidence (final `sp release prepare`
output reaches model call without template-substitution crash).

DISCOVERED-FROM: unitAI-8elrc dogfood pass 2026-05-01. Commit-body in
master history contains `$cwd / $pre_script_output before dispatch`
which triggered the false-positive.

title: Implement specialists-service v1 — sp serve HTTP wrapper
description:
PROBLEM: docs/specialists-service.md is finalized as the canonical spec but the implementation does not exist yet. Ship a thin HTTP wrapper that exposes script-class specialists over POST /v1/generate, reusing the existing loader, schema parser, template engine, and observability writer. Mirrors qwen-service in shape — small, single-tenant sidecar, no orchestration, no session lifecycle.

SUCCESS:
1. New CLI command 'sp serve' starts an HTTP server on --port (default 8000).
2. POST /v1/generate accepts {specialist, variables, template?, model_override?, timeout_ms?, trace?}, returns {success, output, parsed_json?, meta:{specialist, model, duration_ms, trace_id}} or {success:false, error, error_type, ...}.
3. Request flow: load spec via existing SpecialistLoader (configured --user-dir); reject at runtime if execution.interactive=true OR execution.requires_worktree=true OR execution.permission_required != READ_ONLY OR skills.scripts non-empty (error_type=specialist_load_error); render prompt.task_template via existing templateEngine, raising template_variable_missing on un-substituted $varname; resolve model (override -> execution.model -> fallback_model); spawn pi --mode json --no-session --no-extensions --no-tools --model <m> [--thinking <l>] -- <prompt>; parse final assistant text from NDJSON; if response_format=json, parse output and check output_schema.required.
4. Writes ONE row per call to .specialists/observability.db via the existing observability-sqlite client — same writer 'sp run' uses; surface marker in status_json so trace queries can filter (e.g. status_json.surface='script_specialist').
5. Concurrency semaphore at --concurrency (default 4); excess requests wait briefly then return HTTP 429.
6. SIGTERM handling: stop accepting new connections, drain in-flight up to --shutdown-grace-ms (default 30000), forward SIGTERM to pi children, then exit.
7. Errors map to closed taxonomy: specialist_not_found | specialist_load_error | template_variable_missing | auth | quota | timeout | network | invalid_json | internal. HTTP 200 for post-call errors with success:false; HTTP 400 only for malformed requests.

## 2. PiAgentSession Lifecycle vs Proposed One-Shot pi Flags

**Current lifecycle (src/pi/session.ts:490-800+):**

| Step | Method | Line | Behavior |
|------|--------|------|----------|
| Create | `PiAgentSession.create(options)` | ~522 | Returns instance, NO process spawned |
| Start | `session.start()` | ~534 | Spawns `pi --mode rpc`, sets up stdout/stderr handlers |
| Prompt | `session.prompt(renderedTask)` | runner.ts:~1191 | Sends task to stdin |
| Wait | `session.waitForDone(timeout)` | runner.ts:~1192 | Waits for `agent_end` JSON |
| Output | `session.getLastOutput()` | runner.ts:~1193 | Returns accumulated output |
| Close | `session.close()` | ~1268 | Sends EOF, awaits graceful exit |
| Kill | `session.kill()` | ~1288 | SIGTERM, emergency cleanup |

**State maintained across lifecycle:**
- `_lastOutput`, `_lineBuffer`, `_pendingRequests`, `_testWindowToolCallIds`, `_metrics`
- `_stallTimer` for stall detection
- `proc` ChildProcess reference

**Proposed one-shot pi flags (from docs/specialists-service.md):**
- Bypass session management entirely
- Skip keepAlive handling, retry loops, event callbacks
- Direct `pi --mode once` or equivalent

**What is gained:**
- Simpler process model (no RPC mode state machine)
- Reduced memory footprint (no persistent session object)
- Faster spawn-to-completion for simple tasks

**What is lost:**
- `--keep-alive` sessions for multi-turn (runner.ts:~1275-1286)
- Steer/resume callbacks (runner.ts:1184-1186)
- Event streaming for progress (runner.ts:1177-1181)
- Stall detection window (session.ts:_stallTimer)
- Retry logic with backoff (runner.ts:~1195-1213)
- Kill function registration (runner.ts:~1182)
- Circuit breaker integration (runner.ts:~871, ~1274, ~1280)

## Summary

Explored specialists codebase observability system. Identified current SQLite schema coverage, runtime metadata gaps, and file dependencies that block SQLite-only operation.

## Status

Analysis complete. Ready to report findings.

## Architecture Overview

**Current Observability Stack:**
- SQLite DB at `.specialists/db/observability.db` (schema v11)
- Job files at `.specialists/jobs/<id>/` with `status.json`, `events.jsonl`, `result.txt`
- `latest` marker file in jobs dir (file-only)
- Supervisor writes to both SQLite and files; CLI readers still read files

**Key Tables in SQLite:**
- `specialist_jobs` — job metadata (status, worktree, chain info, bead_id, node_id, epic_id)
- `specialist_events` — timeline events with seq
- `specialist_results` — final output
- `epic_runs`, `epic_chain_membership` — epic lifecycle
- `node_runs`, `node_members`, `node_events`, `node_memory` — node coordination

## Execution Flows

**Write Path (Supervisor):**
- `writeStatusFile()` → SQLite `upsertStatus` + file `status.json`
- `appendTimelineEvent()` → SQLite `appendEvent` + file `events.jsonl`
- `upsertResult()` → SQLite `upsertResult` + file `result.txt`
- `writeReadyMarker()` → file `.specialists/ready/<jobId>` (SQLite: no equivalent)

**Read Path (CLI/tools):**
- `specialists status` → tries SQLite first, falls back to `status.json`

```
runner.ts appends to task prompt
```

- `config/mandatory-rules/index.json`: defines `required_template_sets` + `default_template_sets`
- Template resolution: checks `.specialists/mandatory-rules/${id}.md` first, then `config/mandatory-rules/${id}.md`

```typescript
export function buildMandatoryRulesBlock(specialistConfig: { cwd?: string }): string {

  const setIds = [
    ...(index.required_template_sets ?? []),
    ...(index.default_template_sets ?? []),
  ];
  // ...loads only index.json sets, ignores specialist config
}
```
Function signature accepts `specialistConfig` but only extracts `cwd`. Never reads `template_sets`, `disable_default_globals`, or `inline_rules`.


These declarations have **zero effect**.

Not analyzed — task scope focused on mandatory-rules. No evidence found that `.specialists/default` interacts with mandatory-rules system.

title: [bench:2026-04-19-21-08-09] implementation :: zai/glm-5
description:
## Problem

The CLI-native coordinator (unitAI-t4ss) works mechanically — it polls sp node status and calls sp node complete. It adds zero value over the orchestrator dispatching specialists directly with --background.

## What's missing

### 1. Read member output and steer
The coordinator never reads member results. When explorer finds something interesting, the coordinator should tell the researcher 'go deeper on X' or tell the overthinker 'analyze the tradeoff between A and B'. Currently members run their initial prompt blindly and stop.

Requires: coordinator must call `sp result <job_id>` to read member output, then `sp steer <job_id> 'new direction'` or `sp resume <job_id> 'next task'` to redirect.

### 2. Synthesize before completing
The coordinator's final output is 'Node completed. ok:true.' — useless. It should read ALL member outputs, synthesize findings into a unified report, and produce that as its own output before calling sp node complete.

### 3. Phase management
The coordinator should create explicit phases: 'explore phase' → read results → 'deep-dive phase' based on findings → 'synthesis phase'. Currently it has no phase progression — everything runs as one flat blob.

### 4. Dynamic member steering
For research tasks: explorer finds the code, researcher finds external patterns, coordinator reads both and says 'overthinker, analyze this specific tradeoff with these inputs'. Currently the overthinker just runs its generic prompt with no coordinator input.

## What needs to change

### System prompt / using-nodes skill
- Add explicit instruction: 'Before completing, read all member outputs with sp result <job_id>'
- Add synthesis requirement: 'Produce a unified research report as your final output'
- Add steering guidance: 'After each member completes, read their output and decide whether to steer remaining members or spawn follow-up work'
- Add phase examples showing multi-phase coordination

### CLI surface gaps
- Coordinator needs `sp result <job_id>` and `sp steer <job_id>` in its allowed commands (currently only sp node commands)
- Or: add `sp node result --node <id> --member <key>` to read member output through the node interface
- Add `sp node steer --node <id> --member <key> 'message'` for member steering through node interface

### Node config
- research.node.json should NOT have static members with on_start triggers — coordinator should decide what to spawn
- Remove or make on_start optional so coordinator MUST call sp node spawn-member

## Success criteria
A research node run where the coordinator:
1. Spawns members itself (no static pre-seeding)
2. Reads explorer output and steers researcher based on findings
3. Reads all member output and produces a synthesis report
4. Uses at least 2 distinct phases (explore → synthesis)

title: [bench:2026-04-19-21-08-09] bug-fix :: zai/glm-5
description:
sp stop sends SIGTERM but never updates status.json to terminal state. The dying process (keep-alive/interactive) doesn't update its own status because SIGTERM kills it mid-wait. Result: sp merge refuses with 'non-terminal chain jobs', requiring manual status.json patching.

Fix: sp stop should read current status.json, check if run_complete evidence exists (hasRunCompleteEvent from observability-sqlite.ts), write status to 'done' (if evidence) or 'cancelled' (if no evidence), THEN send SIGTERM. This ensures status is terminal before the process dies.

Key files: src/cli/stop.ts, src/specialist/supervisor.ts (hasRunCompleteEvent, writeStatusFile pattern)

title: [bench:2026-04-19-20-43-00] implementation :: openai-codex/gpt-5.3-codex
description:
## Problem

The CLI-native coordinator (unitAI-t4ss) works mechanically — it polls sp node status and calls sp node complete. It adds zero value over the orchestrator dispatching specialists directly with --background.

## What's missing

### 1. Read member output and steer
The coordinator never reads member results. When explorer finds something interesting, the coordinator should tell the researcher 'go deeper on X' or tell the overthinker 'analyze the tradeoff between A and B'. Currently members run their initial prompt blindly and stop.

Requires: coordinator must call `sp result <job_id>` to read member output, then `sp steer <job_id> 'new direction'` or `sp resume <job_id> 'next task'` to redirect.

### 2. Synthesize before completing
The coordinator's final output is 'Node completed. ok:true.' — useless. It should read ALL member outputs, synthesize findings into a unified report, and produce that as its own output before calling sp node complete.

### 3. Phase management
The coordinator should create explicit phases: 'explore phase' → read results → 'deep-dive phase' based on findings → 'synthesis phase'. Currently it has no phase progression — everything runs as one flat blob.

### 4. Dynamic member steering
For research tasks: explorer finds the code, researcher finds external patterns, coordinator reads both and says 'overthinker, analyze this specific tradeoff with these inputs'. Currently the overthinker just runs its generic prompt with no coordinator input.

## What needs to change

### System prompt / using-nodes skill
- Add explicit instruction: 'Before completing, read all member outputs with sp result <job_id>'
- Add synthesis requirement: 'Produce a unified research report as your final output'
- Add steering guidance: 'After each member completes, read their output and decide whether to steer remaining members or spawn follow-up work'
- Add phase examples showing multi-phase coordination

### CLI surface gaps
- Coordinator needs `sp result <job_id>` and `sp steer <job_id>` in its allowed commands (currently only sp node commands)
- Or: add `sp node result --node <id> --member <key>` to read member output through the node interface
- Add `sp node steer --node <id> --member <key> 'message'` for member steering through node interface

### Node config
- research.node.json should NOT have static members with on_start triggers — coordinator should decide what to spawn
- Remove or make on_start optional so coordinator MUST call sp node spawn-member

## Success criteria
A research node run where the coordinator:
1. Spawns members itself (no static pre-seeding)
2. Reads explorer output and steers researcher based on findings
3. Reads all member output and produces a synthesis report
4. Uses at least 2 distinct phases (explore → synthesis)

title: Memory gate hook infinite loop for specialist-closed beads
description:
When a specialist (not the orchestrator) closes a bead via bd close, the memory gate hook fires repeatedly in the orchestrator's session — 15+ times in a row, ignoring all KV acks.

Reproduction:
1. Dispatch sync-docs with --bead unitAI-wbvl
2. Specialist closes the bead itself during its run
3. Orchestrator session receives Stop hook feedback for unitAI-wbvl on every subsequent tool call
4. Setting bd kv set memory-gate-done:<session-id> and memory-acked:<bead-id> both fail to silence it

Root cause hypothesis: the hook checks for closed beads that were claimed in the current session, but the KV key format it writes vs reads may differ. Or the hook re-scans all recently closed beads on every trigger instead of checking the ack KV first.

File: .xtrm/hooks/beads-memory-gate.mjs

Impact: floods orchestrator context with repeated hook messages, wastes tokens, degrades UX. Observed 15+ repetitions in a single session before giving up.
close_reason: Fixed: fast path cleanup was clearing memory-gate-done sentinel, allowing claimed:<sessionId> or inferIssueIdFromBranch() to re-discover the issue and re-trigger the gate in a loop. Fix: preserve memory-gate-done as permanent session sentinel.

title: Vision model pipeline: Read tool blocked by pi-serena-tools — need lighter LSP or serena opt-out
description:
When specialists need to read images (screenshots, diagrams, visual artifacts) in a pipeline, the Read tool is required. But pi-serena-tools overrides/replaces the native Read tool with its own LSP-based file reading, which doesn't support image files.

This blocks vision-capable models from being used in pipelines where image reading is necessary (e.g. design QC, screenshot validation, visual diff review).

Options to evaluate:
1. Disable pi-serena-tools entirely for specialists that need vision/Read (opt-out per specialist config)
2. Replace pi-serena-tools with a lighter LSP that doesn't override Read (e.g. just symbol navigation without file reading takeover)
3. Make pi-serena-tools coexist with native Read — serena handles code files, native Read handles images/binary
4. Add a specialist config flag like `extensions.serena: false` that controls whether -e pi-serena-tools is passed in session.ts

Current wiring: session.ts lines 521-529 unconditionally adds pi-serena-tools via -e for all specialists. No per-specialist opt-out exists.

Related: session.ts also unconditionally adds pi-gitnexus. Both extensions should probably be configurable per specialist.

description:

1. MERGE-TIME REBASE (merge.ts:runMergePlan): Before each mergeBranch() call, rebase the worktree branch onto current master. This prevents silent reversions when Wave B merges after Wave A. If rebase has conflicts, fail with actionable error (list conflicting files, suggest manual resolution).

title: Design: worktree base staleness guard — enforce merge-before-dispatch for sequential chains
description:
When multiple executors run sequentially under the same epic, each new worktree branches from master at dispatch time. If the previous chain hasn't been merged yet, the new worktree is working on stale code. This causes silent reverts when both merge — B's diff against master shows reversions of A's changes.

Current state: nothing enforces merge-before-dispatch. The orchestrator can forget and dispatch B while A is still in review. provisionWorktree() in worktree.ts blindly branches from HEAD.

Desired: provisionWorktree or sp run --worktree should detect unmerged sibling chains under the same epic and either warn/block or auto-rebase. Options to explore:
1. Guard at worktree provisioning: check for unmerged epic siblings with commits, refuse unless --force-stale-base
2. Guard at sp run: validate no pending merges before allowing new worktree dispatch
3. Auto-rebase: branch from latest sibling branch tip instead of master
4. Orchestrator-level nudge: sp run warns but doesn't block

Related memories: sp-merge-worktree-branch-divergence, when-running-parallel-executor-worktrees
