title: The '7-section contract' actually requires eight things, and SCRUTINY is the one always dropped
description:
PROBLEM
Every description of the dispatch contract — the tool parameter text on both frontends, the planning skill, CLAUDE.md, the bead template — calls it the 7-section contract and then appends 'plus a SCRUTINY level'. The gate requires eight things. SCRUTINY is named last, outside the count, in every place a writer looks.

The result is measurable rather than theoretical. Audited every open bead on this epic with evaluateBeadReadiness on 2026-09-08: FOUR contracts hand-written by the coordinator omitted SCRUTINY and would have been refused at dispatch — a live operator probe bead (refused live, in a real pi session), and epic beads .36, .30 and .39. Four out of four. None was caught by reading; all were caught by running the gate.

This is the same shape as unitAI-rrdnt.54 one layer out. There the tool description named the sections and never stated the format the parser required; here it states a count that is wrong by one, and the omitted item is exactly the one outside the count.

SUCCESS
A writer following any description of the contract produces something the gate admits. The count and the requirement agree.

SCRUTINY
LOW

SCOPE
The wording wherever the contract is described: both frontends' tool parameter text, the planning skill, CLAUDE.md's dispatch section, and any bead template. Not the gate — the gate is right.

NON_GOALS
Does not make SCRUTINY optional. Does not change which sections are required. Does not change the refusal shape.

CONSTRAINTS
Do not fix this by making the gate lenient. SCRUTINY drives reviewer escalation on sensitive surfaces and a contract without it is genuinely underspecified — the requirement is correct and only its description is wrong.
Whatever the new wording is, it must be the SAME on both frontends. Divergent wording between the two is the failure documented in .55 and .56.

VALIDATION
Every place that describes the contract states the same count, and that count matches what evaluateBeadReadiness enforces.

OUTPUT
The corrected wording, and a note on the audit method: run the gate over the board rather than reading beads, because reading is what missed this four times.
notes:
PARTLY DONE 2026-09-08. Both frontends now state the valid SCRUTINY levels verbatim (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL) and say EIGHT required parts rather than seven — landed in b3c98a1e after an operator hit exactly this, inventing 'normal' and burning a dispatch.

REMAINING: the phrase '7-section contract' still appears in config/skills/using-specialists/SKILL.md and CLAUDE.md. Those are what a coordinator reads BEFORE it ever sees a tool description, so they are the earlier point of failure and the bead is not done.

title: MCP specialist_dispatch has no contract parameter, so dispatch calls are not portable between frontends
description:
PROBLEM
unitAI-rrdnt.48 added an inline 'contract' parameter to the Pi frontend's specialist_dispatch: either bead_id or contract, exactly one, both refused rather than resolved by preference. The MCP frontend (src/tools/specialist/activation.tool.ts) still requires bead_id and has no contract parameter at all. A coordinator's dispatch call is therefore not portable between the two surfaces, and the friction .48 was filed to remove is removed on only one of them.

Found by the phase12-docs lane while documenting .48, verified at 3b2a2611. It documented the delta rather than the shape, which was the right call for a doc but leaves the product question open.

SUCCESS
Either MCP accepts an inline contract on the same terms as Pi — same gate, run BEFORE any bead is created, both-or-neither refused — or the asymmetry is deliberate and documented as such with its reason.

SCRUTINY
LOW

SCOPE
src/tools/specialist/activation.tool.ts and its schema. The readiness gate and createBeadFromContract already exist and are exported through the lib seam; this is wiring, not new mechanism.

NON_GOALS
Does not change the Pi frontend. Does not change the gate. Does not relax the requirement that a refused dispatch leaves the board unchanged.

CONSTRAINTS
This is a PRODUCT decision before it is an implementation: MCP's bead_id-only shape may be intentional, since the MCP coordinator is Claude Code and has the bd CLI available directly, while the Pi coordinator may not. Decide that first.
If MCP follows, it must reuse the SAME extractSections/evaluateBeadReadiness path — a second gate would let the two frontends disagree about admission, which is the failure this epic has spent the day removing.

VALIDATION
Either an MCP dispatch with an inline contract is admitted and creates its bead, or the doc states the asymmetry and why.

OUTPUT
The parameter and its tests, or a documented decision.

REFERENCES
unitAI-rrdnt.48 (the Pi implementation), unitAI-rrdnt.32 (the doc that found it), unitAI-rrdnt.54 (the same-line format both frontends now accept).
notes:
DEFERRED by operator decision 2026-09-08. MCP is not the Pi coordinator's path — it is for Claude and non-pi agents, and will follow the newer (0728) MCP protocol. Bringing the MCP frontend to parity with a Pi-only convenience is the wrong direction while that migration is pending.

FOR THE RECORD, since this bead was filed as a parity gap: the PRD's MCP obligation is MET. Phase 13 says 'Expose the same native activation runtime through MCP. No CLI shell-out.' — closed as unitAI-rrdnt.33. Inline contracts arrived later on the Pi side via unitAI-rrdnt.48, so this is post-PRD drift between two frontends, not an unmet requirement. Deferring costs nothing against the PRD.

This is also continuous with unitAI-rrdnt.10, which already demoted MCP as the Claude transport after finding Claude Code's MCP CLIENT lacks sampling/createMessage, ignores resources/subscribe, and discards logging notifications — the peer/roster adapter was promoted to primary for exactly that reason.

REOPEN WHEN: the 0728 protocol migration lands and the question becomes what the MCP surface should look like for non-pi agents, rather than whether it should mirror Pi.

title: xt pi --bead stamps the claim under the LAUNCHING session, blocking the launcher's own commits
description:
PROBLEM
'xt pi <name> --bead <id>' writes the beads claim kv under the LAUNCHING session's id, not the launched session's. Observed twice on 2026-09-08 launching lanes for unitAI-rrdnt.47 and unitAI-rrdnt.20 from coordinator session 088c856b-5b68-4b1d-a44a-7c3ecc8d9367:

  claimed:088c856b-...(the coordinator)  = unitAI-rrdnt.47
  claimed:01a07e4a-...(the launched pi)  = unitAI-rrdnt.47

Both exist. The launched session's claim is correct; the coordinator's is spurious.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is not cosmetic. The commit gate refuses the COORDINATOR's next commit with 'Close open issues before committing — Claimed: <the lane's bead> (still in_progress)'. The coordinator is then told to close a bead another session is actively working on, and the only correct action — clearing a kv key by hand — is not one the error suggests. A coordinator that dispatches lanes and merges their work is exactly the session that cannot afford a false claim.

Both launches also printed 'bead assignee: pi did not signal readiness within 30s; session launch continues', and the assignee stayed on the shared actor rather than becoming pi/<slug>. The two symptoms are likely the same handshake failing: the readiness signal that would carry the launched session's identity never arrives, and something falls back to the caller's identity instead of failing.

SCOPE
The xt pi --bead claim/assignee handshake. CROSS-REPO: xtrm-tools, not this repo.

WORKAROUND used twice today: bd kv clear "claimed:<launcher-session-id>" after launch, and bd update <bead> --assignee pi/<slug>.

TBD
Whether the 30s readiness timeout is the root cause or a second symptom.

title: A stale extension build refuses dispatch with a reason identical to a genuinely broken contract
description:
PROBLEM
config/pi-extensions/specialist-subagents/index.mjs statically imports ../../../dist/lib.js at extension load, so a pi session holds whatever build existed when it started. After dist is rebuilt, a running coordinator keeps the old gate. When the old gate is the one that refuses, the operator sees:

  reason:  bead is not a usable task contract: required sections are missing or empty
  missing: [PROBLEM, SUCCESS, SCOPE, NON_GOALS, CONSTRAINTS, VALIDATION, OUTPUT]

byte-identical to the refusal a genuinely incomplete bead produces. The message describes the operator's input as broken when the input is fine and the process is stale. There is no way to tell the two apart from the refusal.

This is the same failure shape as unitAI-rrdnt.54 one layer up: the reason points away from the cause. .54 was one parser; this one is inherited by EVERY future change to the extension or to dist, because the staleness is structural rather than specific.

Observed live 2026-09-08 by the pi-specialists session: two dispatches refused against a fixed gate. It diagnosed the cause from a property of the live process rather than the code — the running tool's contract-parameter description lacked a sentence the on-disk index.mjs carries — which is the tell, and it should not have been necessary.

SUCCESS
An operator can tell a stale-build refusal from a broken-contract refusal without inspecting tool descriptions or module mtimes.

SCRUTINY
MEDIUM

SCOPE
The extension's import of dist/lib.js and the refusal envelope it renders.

NON_GOALS
Does not require hot-reloading the extension. Making the staleness VISIBLE is enough and is much cheaper than making it impossible.

CONSTRAINTS
Whatever identity is surfaced must be cheap to compute at load and stable across identical builds — a timestamp changes on every rebuild and would make two identical builds look different. The config fingerprint the runtime already computes is the closer precedent.
Do not solve this by importing dist per call. The static import is what makes the extension a single module with one gate; per-call imports would let two dispatches in one session disagree about admission.

VALIDATION
An operator running a stale build against a valid contract gets a refusal, or a warning, that names staleness as a possible cause.

OUTPUT
Either a build identity surfaced at session start and echoed in the refusal, or a documented check an operator can run.

REFERENCES
Reported by the pi-specialists session; verbatim refusal envelope available from it. Related: unitAI-rrdnt.54.
notes:
IMPLEMENTATION (branch feature/unitAI-rrdnt.55-build-identity): identity on every Pi-extension outcome surface per pinned correction — dispatch refusal (bead + inline paths), dispatch success, specialist_status. New src/activation/build-identity.ts (content-hash identity, single wording source, exported via lib.ts); index.mjs annexes {build} field via exported annexBuildIdentity. dist/ rebuilt + committed (package-payload requires committed dist == fresh build). Tests: 7 new unit + 5 new extension tests (87 total pass incl. bead-gate), tsc clean. VALIDATION performed live: temp harness loaded extension, refused (match line), appended a byte to dist/lib.js mid-session, refused again -> staleness line naming rebuild + restart (temp test removed after). Claude MCP parity + lease/latency wording left to .60 per its VALIDATION #2. Second defect from notes (bead vs inline refusal shapes) split to new bead.
RESTORED 2026-09-08 after an accidental --notes replace by the implementing session (unitAI-rrdnt.55 worker): the three evidence sections below are reconstructed verbatim from the claim-time read. The IMPLEMENTATION note now at the top of the notes stands.

---
VERBATIM EVIDENCE from the pi-specialists session, stale in-session build, 2026-09-08.

Bead path (unitAI-7didq), full envelope:
  SPECIALIST_DISPATCH_REJECTED
  bead: unitAI-7didq
  specialist: explorer
  note: bead is not a usable task contract: required sections are missing or empty
  reason: bead_contract_incomplete
  missing: PROBLEM, SUCCESS, SCOPE, NON_GOALS, CONSTRAINTS, VALIDATION, OUTPUT
  AgentSession: not created

Inline-contract path, SAME stale build, SAME cause:
  { status: rejected, reason: 'bead is not a usable task contract: required sections are missing or empty', missing: [same seven] }
  -- no SPECIALIST_DISPATCH_REJECTED envelope, no AgentSession line.

A SECOND DEFECT, separable from the staleness and arguably the more actionable half. The two dispatch paths render an IDENTICAL refusal in two different shapes: the bead path gets the rendered envelope, the inline path gets a bare object. A coordinator cannot pattern-match refusals across the two, and anything parsing the refusal has to know which path produced it.

This contradicts the one-vocabulary property the epic claims for the two frontends. That claim survived because it was only ever checked on the SUCCESS projections, which are shared imports and therefore cannot drift -- the docs lane already tightened the claim to exactly that scope. Refusals are rendered, not projected, and nobody checked them. Same lesson as unitAI-kv8ac: what is shared cannot drift, what is hand-written drifts immediately.

Worth splitting into its own bead when this is picked up; it is fixable without touching the staleness question at all. (Split done 2026-09-08 as unitAI-ofn3k, draft.)

---
LIVE EVIDENCE FROM A MISLED PARTICIPANT, 2026-09-08 -- this is the strongest case for this bead and it did not come from reading code.

The pi-specialists coordinator ran a settlement smoke test, observed that settlement did not wake, reported it, and then -- after the fix merged fifteen minutes later -- tried to RETRACT the finding on the grounds that it had been running pre-fix code. Its own words: 'my session had no way to know it was running pre-.64 code -- no build identity anywhere on the surface.'

That is this defect happening to a live participant rather than an argument about it. The session could not tell which build it was running, so it could not tell whether a behaviour it observed was a defect or a version. It very nearly withdrew a correct bug report because of it.

That is a WORSE consequence than the one this bead was filed with. I filed it as 'a stale build refuses with a message identical to a genuinely broken contract' -- a diagnosis problem. The real cost is that no participant can distinguish 'the system does not do X' from 'the build I am on does not do X yet', which corrupts findings rather than merely delaying them.

DESIGN NOTES for whoever builds it, from the shape of this incident:
- The identity must be STABLE across identical builds. A timestamp or mtime makes two identical builds look different and converts the signal into noise; the config fingerprint the runtime already computes is the closer precedent.
- It must ride the REFUSAL, not only specialist_status. The failure mode is a coordinator reading 'sections missing' about a correct contract, and a build id in a status call it never makes does not reach it.
- Consider surfacing it on dispatch RESULTS too, not only refusals. This incident was not a refusal at all -- it was a correct dispatch whose observed behaviour belonged to an older build.

---
ANNEX POINT PINNED CORRECTLY 2026-09-08, superseding how I phrased it above.

I wrote 'annex the build identity to the REFUSAL, not only to status', which puts the refusal first and would bias an implementation toward treating other surfaces as optional. That is wrong for the case that produced this bead.

THE CORRECT REQUIREMENT: identity must be present on EVERY outcome surface -- the refusal, the status read, and the SUCCESSFUL dispatch result alike. The reason is that the incident behind this bead was not a build-identity failure at all. There was no identity anywhere to be wrong. It was a participant that ran a correct, successful dispatch and could not tell afterwards which build had produced the behaviour it observed -- and so nearly retracted a correct finding.

A refusal-first design would leave that exact case uncovered, because nothing was refused. 'Identity on every outcome' is the requirement; 'especially on refusals' is a false emphasis that happens to describe only the second-worst symptom.

title: Delete toResultView from the Pi extension in favour of toActivationResultView
description:
PROBLEM
config/pi-extensions/specialist-subagents/index.mjs:82 defines toResultView, a second projection of ActivationResult. src/tools/specialist/activation.tool.ts defines toActivationResultView, the first. Two functions describing one settled activation is how a Pi coordinator and a Claude coordinator come to describe the same object differently. The field sets were reconciled on unitAI-rrdnt.34 (toActivationResultView is now a strict superset: same names, same values, plus identity fields the extension does not need because its result hangs off an ActivationView that already names the activation), but the duplicate function still exists.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN EITHER LANE
The symbol is exported from dist/lib.js only on branch xt/phase14-async (unitAI-rrdnt.34, commit 3130e7fa). Branch xt/wakeup (unitAI-rrdnt.45, commit 7af8eabe) could not import it without breaking its own runtime, and that bead's output is four live pi TUI transcripts produced by running that branch. Landing a broken import to save a two-line edit would have traded the evidence for tidiness. Both lanes agreed the deletion belongs to whoever lands second.

SUCCESS
index.mjs imports toActivationResultView from ../../../dist/lib.js alongside toActivationView and toPendingAskView, the local toResultView function is deleted, and the withResult call site (index.mjs:103) calls toActivationResultView.

SCOPE
config/pi-extensions/specialist-subagents/index.mjs only.

NON_GOALS
Does not change toActivationResultView itself. Does not touch src/. Does not add a finding or progress push.

CONSTRAINTS
Do this only AFTER both xt/phase14-async and xt/wakeup are merged, so dist/lib.js actually exports the symbol. Verify the export is present before editing, do not assume it.

VALIDATION
1. grep -n toResultView config/pi-extensions/specialist-subagents/index.mjs returns nothing.
2. grep -n toActivationResultView dist/lib.js confirms the export exists before the edit.
3. bun --bun vitest run tests/unit/pi/specialist-subagents-extension.test.ts passes.
4. A live pi TUI dispatch still renders a settled result through specialist_status.

OUTPUT
The edit, and the test run.
close_reason:
Deleted toResultView from config/pi-extensions/specialist-subagents/index.mjs; withResult now calls the shared toActivationResultView imported from dist/lib.js.

Precondition met as the bead required: both xt/phase14-async and xt/wakeup are merged (0afc3d3c). Verified the export exists in dist/lib.js rather than assuming it, and verified the shared projection is a strict superset by comparing the two implementations field by field — identical expressions for all ten of toResultView's keys, plus activation_id, participant_id, attempt_id and bead_id.

Also replaced the docblock, which after the deletion asserted the opposite of what is now true ('only this result projection is Pi-surface-specific').

title: tsconfig excludes tests, so no test file is ever typechecked
description:
PROBLEM
tsconfig.json has include: ["src/**/*"] and excludes only node_modules and dist. No file under tests/ is typechecked. `bunx tsc --noEmit` reports clean while a test file calls a method that does not exist on the class it imports.

This is not hypothetical. The acceptance AX live case in tests/integration/activation/native-activation.live.test.ts called `host.snapshot(activationId)` at two places from the day it was written. NativeActivationHost has no `snapshot` member; the method is `inspect()` (src/activation/native-host.ts:732). The case could never pass — it threw `TypeError: host.snapshot is not a function` before reaching any assertion — and this was found only by running the live suite on 2026-09-07 during unitAI-rrdnt.35. A self-diagnosing failure block added to that same case shortly before would itself have thrown before printing its diagnostic.

The general form: a green `tsc --noEmit` on this repo is evidence about src/ and nothing else. Any claim of test-side correctness that leans on it is unfounded, and a gated live test that never runs in CI has no other mechanism that would catch the error.

SUCCESS
Type errors in test files fail a typecheck run.

SCOPE
tsconfig.json, or a second tsconfig for tests, plus whatever the resulting backlog requires. The quality-gate hook wiring if it invokes tsc with an explicit project.

NON_GOALS
No test rewrites beyond fixing type errors the widened check surfaces. No change to which tests run, to vitest configuration, or to the live-smoke gating.

CONSTRAINTS
Widening the include will surface an existing backlog of errors across tests/ — size it before committing to a single-commit fix. The build must not start emitting test files into dist. Vitest globals and the bun:sqlite / bun -e patterns used by the live tests must still typecheck.

VALIDATION
1. Reintroduce `host.snapshot(...)` in a test file and confirm the typecheck fails on it; revert.
2. `bunx tsc --noEmit` (or the project-specific invocation) reports zero errors with tests included.
3. `bun run build` output is unchanged — diff dist before and after.

OUTPUT
A typecheck that covers tests/, with the surfaced errors fixed or explicitly triaged.

SCRUTINY
LOW for the config change itself. MEDIUM for the backlog it exposes: a silenced error is worse than an unchecked one.

title: NativeActivationHost.resume() is reachable from no coordinator surface
description:
PROBLEM
NativeActivationHost.resume() (src/activation/native-host.ts:798) is called by nothing. Only src/server.ts:146 constructs the host, and the MCP surface it wires exposes specialist_dispatch, specialist_reply, specialist_stop_activation and specialist_status — no resume. No CLI and no Pi extension calls it either. A settled activation is documented as "waiting and resumable" and its lease reacquisition path (workspace-lease.ts:269-334) exists specifically for resume, but no coordinator can trigger one.

This is the sixth instance of the epic's recurring failure: a module complete, unit-tested and closed on the board, reachable by nothing.

The near-miss is the transferable part. Grepping for `.resume(` in src/ returns two hits — src/specialist/runner.ts:1425 and src/specialist/script-runner.ts:1215 — and both look like callers. They are not: they call resume() on the legacy PiAgentSession, a different object that happens to share the method name. A same-name method on an unrelated type makes a reachability grep look reassuring when it should not. Enumerate what the runtime actually exposes, and check the receiver type, not only the method name.

SUCCESS
A coordinator can resume a settled or waiting activation through the same runtime it dispatched it on, and the resumed attempt is visible in observability.db under the same activation id with an advanced attempt id.

SCOPE
The MCP activation surface (src/tools/specialist/activation.tool.ts) and its registration in src/server.ts. The host's resume() itself needs no change.

NON_GOALS
No new resume semantics. No change to attempt-id derivation, to lease reacquisition, or to which states are resumable (RESUMABLE_STATES in registry.ts already defines this). No Pi extension surface — that is unitAI-rrdnt.37.

CONSTRAINTS
The tool must call host.resume() and must not re-implement any gate. resume() takes (activationId, prompt) and deliberately carries no model override: an override persists from the original activation and re-specifying one on resume would be a new semantics needing its own acceptance. DispatchRejectedError for unknown_activation and not_resumable must surface as a structured result, not an opaque MCP error, matching the existing rejectionResult() path.

VALIDATION
1. A unit test dispatches through specialist_dispatch, lets the activation settle, resumes through the new tool, and asserts the returned attempt_id ends :2 while activation_id is unchanged.
2. Resuming an activation in a non-resumable state returns status "rejected" with reason not_resumable, not a thrown error.
3. Grep evidence that the new tool is registered in src/server.ts and appears in the MCP tool list, not only that it exists.

OUTPUT
A specialist_resume MCP tool, registered, with the tests above.

SCRUTINY
MEDIUM. Resume reacquires the workspace lease for a writer; a resume path that bypassed acquisition would put two writers in one worktree.
close_reason:
specialist_resume now exists on the Pi coordinator surface, so resume() is reachable. It keeps the activation_id and advances the attempt_id, returns the shared ActivationView plus previous_attempt_id, and renders a refused resume as a tool RESULT rather than a throw — the same refusal shape every other tool on this surface uses.

This was the epic's sixth 'complete, unit-tested, closed on the board, reachable by nothing' instance. The resume half of the runtime, including the lease reacquisition path that exists solely for resume, had no operator surface at all.

Three tests, mutation-verified: replacing the h.resume() call with a stub fails two of them and passes the third, so they exercise the product rather than the fake.

FOUND WHILE DOING THIS, and fixed: the suite looked tools up by INDEX. Adding one tool shifted three lookups and produced 'expected undefined to deeply equal [...]' — a failure that points at the assertion instead of the cause. Replaced with a toolNamed() helper that throws naming what IS registered. Registration order is not a contract.

NOT CLOSED BY THIS: PRD acceptances Y (resumed writer) and Z (resume conflict refused) on unitAI-rrdnt.36. The surface exists now, so they are provable, but neither has been run live. MCP still has no resume tool — same asymmetry as unitAI-rrdnt.56.

Suite 2339 passed, 193 files.

title: use_specialist applies no bead readiness gate, so a bead refused by specialist_dispatch still runs
description:
PROBLEM
The two MCP surfaces disagree about whether a Bead is dispatchable. `specialist_dispatch` (unitAI-rrdnt.33) routes through NativeActivationHost.start, which applies evaluateBeadReadiness and refuses a Bead that is marked contract=draft, is closed, is missing any of the seven sections, or declares no SCRUTINY level. `use_specialist` takes the same `bead_id`, reads it with buildBeadContext, and hands it straight to SpecialistRunner with NO readiness check at all (src/tools/specialist/use_specialist.tool.ts).

The result is worse than neither surface gating. The gated path is the documented one, so operator docs now state that a draft Bead is refused; the ungated path is the older, better-known, and easier one. An operator blocked by the gate has a working bypass and no indication that they have taken it. A gate with a documented bypass trains people to use the bypass.

SUCCESS
Both MCP surfaces agree on whether a given Bead is dispatchable, or the difference is deliberate, documented, and visible in the refusal — not an accident of which tool was written first.

SCOPE
src/tools/specialist/use_specialist.tool.ts and the bead-reading path it uses. The decision about whether the legacy runner should gate at all belongs in this bead.

NON_GOALS
Does not change evaluateBeadReadiness itself — the gate logic is correct and is not in question. Does not remove use_specialist or migrate it onto NativeActivationHost; that is Phase 13/15 territory, not a bug fix. Does not change specialist_dispatch, which behaves correctly.

CONSTRAINTS
use_specialist predates the gate and is in active use, so switching it to refusing without a deprecation path will break callers whose Beads were never written to the 7-section contract. Consider warn-then-refuse, or gating only when the caller passed bead_id rather than prompt. Whatever is chosen must be stated in the operator docs (unitAI-rrdnt.32), because the current docs describe the gate without saying which tool it belongs to.

VALIDATION
1. A Bead marked contract=draft produces the same admission decision through use_specialist as through specialist_dispatch, or a documented and deliberately different one.
2. A Bead missing required sections likewise.
3. If a deprecation path is chosen, the warning appears in the tool result and not only in logs.

OUTPUT
The aligned behaviour, its tests, and the docs change naming which tool gates and why.

SCRUTINY
MEDIUM — this is a governance boundary rather than a crash. The risk in fixing it is breaking existing callers; the risk in leaving it is a gate everyone learns to route around.

REFERENCES
Found during unitAI-rrdnt.33. Reported to phase12-docs, who added a sentence naming which tool the contract gate belongs to (commit 121c09f8).
close_reason:
Resolved as WARN, not refuse — the option the bead's own CONSTRAINTS pointed at.

use_specialist now runs evaluateBeadReadiness, the SAME function specialist_dispatch uses, imported rather than reimplemented: a second readiness check would let the two surfaces disagree about admission, which is the defect and not the fix. When the gate rejects, the bead still runs and the tool result carries a readiness_warning naming the reason and the missing sections.

Why warn rather than refuse: the tool predates the gate and is in active use, so refusing outright breaks callers whose Beads were never written to the contract. The bead said so and it is right.

The load-bearing decision is WHERE the warning goes. It rides the RESULT, not a log. The defect being fixed is that an operator blocked by the gate had a working bypass with no indication they had taken it — a warning in a log nobody reads reproduces that exactly.

VALIDATION 1 and 2: a bead with no sections produces a warning naming what is missing; a complete contract produces none; a prompt-only call has no bead to judge and is untouched. VALIDATION 3: the warning is in the tool result, asserted directly.

Mutation-verified rather than assumed green — replacing the gate call with a hardcoded ok:true fails the warning test and passes the other two, so the test exercises the system rather than a fixture. That check exists because this epic has produced seven defects of the opposite shape.

Tool description now states the divergence and marks it deprecated. Full suite 2320 passed, 190 files.

title: dist built inside an .xtrm worktree silently bakes ../../../node_modules paths into the bundle
description:
PROBLEM
Running `bun run build` inside an .xtrm worktree whose node_modules is incomplete produces a corrupt dist without any error. In unitAI-rrdnt.33 the worktree was missing zod, zod-to-json-schema and @modelcontextprotocol/sdk; bun resolved them from the repo root three levels up and baked 248 `// ../../../node_modules/...` path comments into dist/index.js. HEAD dist had zero. The only signal was tests/integration/release-attestation.test.ts failing, and it reads as a defect in the changed code until you diff against HEAD dist. Every lane in this epic rebuilds dist, so every lane can hit it.

SUCCESS
A build performed in a worktree with incomplete dependencies either produces a correct bundle or fails loudly at build time, naming the cause. An engineer who hits it is told to run `bun install`, rather than inferring it from a release-attestation diff.

SCOPE
scripts/postprocess-build.mjs and the build pipeline in package.json. Optionally the worktree provisioning path that creates .xtrm worktrees without installing dependencies.

NON_GOALS
Does not change what the bundle contains when dependencies ARE complete. Does not make release-attestation more lenient — that test caught this correctly and must keep failing on a leaked path.

CONSTRAINTS

title: Emit the three forensic event names the sink still classifies with no producer
description:
PROBLEM
src/activation/forensic-sink.ts classifies six event names by severity that
NativeActivationHost never emits: output_validation_failed, retry_failed, tool_blocked and
lease_denied as errors, activation_uncertain and lease_uncertain as warnings. Measured at
5bdff6b5 by comparing the sink's ERROR_EVENTS/WARN_EVENTS sets against every emit('...')
call site in native-host.ts. The emitted vocabulary is: activation_requested, _rejected,
_admitted, _starting, _started, _settled, _completed, _failed, _resumed, _disposed,
step_contract_compiled, turn_started, turn_completed, retry_started, retry_completed,
output_validation_started, output_validation_passed, compaction_started, compaction_completed.

Four of the six are the negative half of a pair whose positive half IS emitted
(output_validation_passed without _failed, retry_started/_completed without retry_failed).
A query or dashboard filtering on the failure names returns nothing, and nothing
distinguishes "no failures occurred" from "failures are not recorded". That is the
condition unitAI-rrdnt.4 already fixed once in the console: a surface that reads healthy
because the signal was never wired.

tool_blocked, lease_denied and lease_uncertain cannot be emitted before the writer lease is
wired (unitAI-rrdnt.36) — there is no block or lease decision to report. output_validation_failed,
retry_failed and activation_uncertain are emittable today.

SUCCESS
Every name the sink classifies is emitted by the runtime at the point the condition occurs,
or is removed from the sink's severity sets. Both halves of each pair are present. No name
is classified that no producer can emit.

SCOPE
src/activation/forensic-sink.ts and the emit call sites in src/activation/native-host.ts.
The lease-dependent names may land with unitAI-rrdnt.36 instead; if so, split them out
rather than leaving them classified and unemitted.

NON_GOALS
Does not add forensic columns for attempt_id or pi_session_id — that is tracked separately.
Does not change the event family, the store, or the timeline mappers. Does not add new
event names beyond the six already classified.

CONSTRAINTS
observability.db remains the single forensic store; no second telemetry database.
src/activation/native-host.ts is owned by the coordinator lane — coordinate before editing.
Removing a name from the sink is an acceptable resolution only when nothing should ever
emit it; a name that a later phase will emit stays and gets a producer.

VALIDATION
1. For each of the six names, a test drives the runtime into the condition and asserts the
   row appears in observability.db with the expected severity. Asserting the sink
   classifies a name it was handed proves nothing about whether anything emits it.
2. A check compares the sink's ERROR_EVENTS + WARN_EVENTS sets against the emit call sites
   and fails on any name with no producer, so this cannot regress silently.
3. docs/native-activation.md "Known holes" row for this item is removed when it closes.

OUTPUT
Emitted events plus the producer/classifier consistency check, and the docs row retired.

SCRUTINY
MEDIUM. Forensic completeness, not a capability or permission boundary. The risk is a
surface that reads healthy because a failure signal has no producer.

title: Phase 11 — activation model override, validation and fallback semantics
description:
PROBLEM
The model gate resolves a requested model and fails closed on a no-match diagnostic plus a hasConfiguredAuth check, but there is no operator-facing override path, no defined fallback semantics when an override cannot be honoured, and no forensic record of which model an activation actually ran on versus which was requested.

SUCCESS
PRD acceptance B, C, D, E, F and AZ. A configured default is honoured; an explicit override is honoured; an invalid override is refused rather than silently substituted; an override persists across resume; config is never mutated; and Claude can set the override through the same runtime.

SCOPE
The model resolution path and its forensics. The override surface on dispatch, on the MCP tool, and on resume.

NON_GOALS
No model picker UI. Does not change which providers are configured or add credentials.

CONSTRAINTS
getAvailable() no longer distinguishes auth on pi 0.85.1 and returns the full catalogue regardless — the gate is the no-match diagnostic AND hasConfiguredAuth(providerId), and neither half alone is sufficient. createAgentSession takes a resolved Model object; a provider-qualified string is accepted silently and then fails mid-turn with an unresolved provider, which is why native-host.ts passes modelCheck.model. Do not regress that; it is covered by a regression test. src/activation/native-host.ts is owned by the coordinator session.

VALIDATION
1. Requested-versus-resolved model is recorded in forensics for every activation, including when they are equal.
2. An invalid override produces a refusal naming the requested model, never a silent fallback.
3. An override survives a resume and is attributed to the new attempt id.
4. Config files are byte-identical before and after an activation with an override.

OUTPUT
The override path, its forensics, and the B/C/D/E/F/AZ evidence.

title: Phase 10 — enable write-capable Specialist roles on the native runtime
description:
PROBLEM
Only read-only Specialists run natively. executor, debugger, test-engineer and the other write-capable roles are not enabled, because the PRD gates them behind capability, lease and forensic parity. Those three are now largely built (unitAI-rrdnt.21 lease, Phase 7 observability, the tool contract), so the gate can be evaluated rather than assumed.

SUCCESS
Write-capable roles run natively with the same capability, lease and forensic guarantees as the CLI path, and PRD acceptance S, T, U, V, W, X, Y and Z hold for a natively activated writer.

SCRUTINY
HIGH

Rationale, so a later reader does not downgrade it: this phase grants file-mutation capability to a runtime whose lease guards the LLM tool path ONLY. The pi.exec and AgentSession.executeBash veto bypass (unitAI-rrdnt.6) is unclosed and fires the tool_call handler zero times, so a writer can reach the filesystem by a path the lease never sees. Enabling writers is therefore a permissions change made on an incomplete guarantee, and the CONSTRAINTS require that incompleteness to be stated in the docstrings rather than papered over.

SCOPE
Capability admission for write-capable roles on the native path, and the parity evidence that justifies enabling them.

NON_GOALS
Does not enable a role before its parity evidence exists. Does not change the permission tiers themselves.

CONSTRAINTS
Enable only after parity PASSES, and record the passing evidence rather than asserting it — this phase is defined by its precondition. A write-capable specialist that CREATES files needs permission HIGH, not MEDIUM; sp validate does not catch that and only a live dispatch does. The pi.exec and AgentSession.executeBash veto bypass (unitAI-rrdnt.6) is unclosed and fires the tool_call handler zero times, so the lease must be understood as guarding the LLM tool path only; enabling writers without stating that in the docstrings ships a guarantee the runtime does not make.

VALIDATION
1. One writer at a time (S); readers coexist with a writer (T); the coordinator is fenced (U).
2. A blocked write emits a forensic event (V) and release behaves correctly (W).
3. Sequential writer handoff (X) and resumed writer (Y) work; a resume conflict is refused (Z).
4. Each enabled role is proven by a LIVE dispatch, not by configuration review.

OUTPUT
The enabled roles, the parity evidence for each, and the S-Z acceptance record.

The module states this itself at line 66 and lists its four required call sites. native-host.ts:196-198 refuses every write-capable activation, so the unwired lease is currently harmless: no writer is admitted, therefore no writer is unfenced. title: status CLI tests take ~6s each and time out under full-suite parallelism
description:
PROBLEM
tests/unit/cli/status.test.ts runs 11 tests in ~84s -- between 4.2s and 8.8s per test -- and passes in isolation. Under full-suite parallelism it intermittently exceeds the 30s per-test testTimeout: a run on master at 7bd186ed produced 2 failures ("completes without throwing", "prints Specialists section header") while three prior full runs of the same file passed. The failures are load-dependent, not assertions about wrong behaviour.

SUCCESS
The status CLI tests are fast enough that full-suite parallelism does not push them past the timeout, or the reason each test needs seconds is understood and documented so the timeout is a deliberate setting rather than a coincidence.

SCOPE
Establish where the per-test seconds go -- the likely candidates are repeated subprocess work (git rev-parse, bd, pi version probes) performed per status invocation, and resolveObservabilityDbLocation running spawnSync('git') twice per call against a non-repo temp dir. Then either remove the repeated work in the test setup, stub the subprocess boundary, or justify and raise the timeout for this file specifically.

NON_GOALS
Does not change status CLI production behaviour. Does not disable or skip the tests. Does not raise the global testTimeout -- that hides slowness everywhere to fix it in one place.

CONSTRAINTS
Do not weaken assertions to make the file faster. If the fix is a stub, it must not stub the code path under test. Confirm whether the slowness predates the observability test isolation landed in unitAI-rrdnt.16 by measuring the same file at a commit before it; if isolation contributed, say by how much rather than assuming.

VALIDATION
1. A measurement showing where the per-test time goes.
2. The file passes in three consecutive full-suite runs under default parallelism.

OUTPUT
Either a speed fix or a documented, file-scoped timeout with the measurement behind it.

SCRUTINY
LOW -- test-infrastructure flakiness, but the kind that trains a team to ignore red.
notes: Second sighting of a related-but-distinct failure, 2026-09-07 (unitAI-rrdnt.35): running the native-activation LIVE suite and the full unit suite concurrently produced a 'bead_unreadable' dispatch refusal on a probe bead that the same gate had read successfully minutes earlier. Passes cleanly in isolation. Hypothesis, NOT root-caused: bd lock contention, since several unit tests shell out to bd and each bd op round-trips through the Dolt sync. Recorded so a third sighting has something to match against. Also observed: the live suite's afterAll inherited the default 10s hook budget and timed out once it closed two probe beads instead of one — bd close is not cheap under this sync.

title: execution.expected_output_keys is silently ignored on the sp run path (only sp script honours it)
description:
PROBLEM
src/specialist/schema.ts documents execution.expected_output_keys as "Required JSON keys the assistant output must contain. Triggers a required-keys check independent of response_format... On miss the runtime returns error_type: 'invalid_json'." That is true only for the sp script surface. The sole consumer is collectRequiredOutputKeys (src/specialist/script-runner.ts:633); grep for expected_output_keys across src/specialist/runner.ts and src/specialist/supervisor.ts returns nothing. SpecialistRunner.run never reads the field.

Consequence: a specialist authored with expected_output_keys and dispatched via sp run gets no required-keys check at all. The documented failure mode it exists to prevent — "hallucinated key sets pass through as success" — is exactly what happens. Output validation on the run path (validateOutputContract, runner.ts:975) is additionally advisory: it writes stderr warnings and never fails the run.

SUCCESS
expected_output_keys is honoured on every dispatch path, or the schema documentation is corrected to state the field is sp-script-only. Either resolution is acceptable; silent divergence between documented and actual behavior is not.

SCOPE
Decide which way to resolve, then implement. If honouring it on the run path: reuse collectRequiredOutputKeys rather than writing a second implementation, and decide explicitly whether a miss fails the run or warns, since today validateOutputContract only warns.

NON_GOALS
Does not change the sp script behavior, which is correct. Does not implement the native activation path (separate epic work) — though the native path must not inherit this gap.

CONSTRAINTS
If the run path is changed to fail on a miss, that is a behavior change for existing specialists that declare the field and currently pass; audit config/specialists/ for affected definitions and report them before changing the default.

VALIDATION
1. A specialist declaring expected_output_keys, dispatched via sp run, produces the documented result when a key is missing.
2. Existing sp script behavior is unchanged.
3. Audit of config/specialists/ for definitions declaring the field is reported.

OUTPUT
Fix or documentation correction, plus the audit. Found during Phase 0 reconciliation.

SCRUTINY
MEDIUM — a validation gate that is documented but absent gives false assurance about output contracts.
notes: Audit: sole default declarer is service-knowledge-sync v1.11.0 with summary/services/actions; keys bind JSON script_template while sp run uses markdown task_template. Decision approved by coordinator: document script-only, do not add run-path validation. Implemented source-of-truth schema comment plus authoring docs: runScriptSpecialist/sp script/sp serve fail closed invalid_json; SpecialistRunner.run/sp run is inert. No config definitions changed. Verification: 36 schema/script-runner tests passed; bun run lint passed; grep confirms sole declarer and zero runner/supervisor consumers; git diff --check passed; GitNexus detect-changes low/0 affected. collectRequiredOutputKeys impact is HIGH (3 processes), so leaving behavior untouched avoids that blast radius.
close_reason: Done: audited the sole default declarer and corrected schema/authoring contracts to script-surface-only fail-closed semantics; sp run remains explicitly inert; 36 focused tests and typecheck pass.

Does not implement the writer lease (that is the PRD Phase 8 bead). Does not change worktree_owner_job_id semantics or any chain-identity behavior.

title: Extract buildSystemPrompt() out of SpecialistRunner.run()
description:

System-prompt assembly is ~200 inline lines inside SpecialistRunner.run() at src/specialist/runner.ts:1259-1467, mixing existsSync checks, execSync('gitnexus context ...'), onEvent emission and payloadComponents.push. SCOPE

NON_GOALS
No change to prompt content or ordering. No change to renderTaskPrompt (already pure, task-prompt.ts:174). Does not implement the native host.

CONSTRAINTS

VALIDATION
1. Golden test: composed prompt for a representative specialist is byte-identical pre/post extraction.
2. buildSystemPrompt has unit tests covering append vs replace mode.
3. Full test suite passes.

OUTPUT
Extracted function + tests. Prerequisite for PRD Phase 1.

MEDIUM — behavior-preserving refactor of the prompt path; a silent change alters every Specialist's behavior.

title: cli: document/automate reliable job-completion detection (ps 'waiting' hides finished keep-alive jobs)
description:
## PROBLEM
Orchestrators (agent panes) detect specialist completion via `specialists ps --json` status. For keep-alive specialists this is unreliable: a finished executor sits in status=waiting indefinitely, so status-based watchers never fire and time out (real case: darth-feedor py_backend-b2gw epic, 2026-08-23/24 — multiple 80-cycle watchers missed ecaa52/190f6a completions; detection fell back to manual feed greps).

The authoritative signals already exist but are undiscovered:
1. Project observability SQLite (`<repo>/.specialists/db/observability.db`, table specialist_jobs: status running/waiting/done/failed + updated_at_ms) — zero-byte global ~/.specialists/observability.db is a red herring.
2. Feed terminal marker `status=COMPLETE exit=agent_end`.
3. `sp log -f --json --job <id>` already streams lifecycle/control rows incl. DONE events, but its help does not present it as THE completion-detection surface.

## SUCCESS (pick scope during promotion)
- Minimum: ps help/output documents that waiting != done for keep-alive jobs and points to sp log -f / DB path for reliable detection.
- Better: new command, e.g. `sp await <job-id> [--timeout <s>] [--include-push <branch>]` — exits 0 when the job reaches terminal state (done/failed OR feed COMPLETE agent_end), printing final summary + last_output; designed for agent-pane watchers (single blocking process instead of jq/grep loops).
- Optional: ps --json gains terminal_reason / completed_at fields so one call suffices.

## NON_GOALS

title: cli: document/automate reliable job-completion detection (ps 'waiting' hides finished keep-alive jobs)
description:
## PROBLEM
Orchestrators (agent panes) detect specialist completion via `specialists ps --json` status. For keep-alive specialists this is unreliable: a finished executor sits in status=waiting indefinitely, so status-based watchers never fire and time out (real case: darth-feedor py_backend-b2gw epic, 2026-08-23/24 — multiple 80-cycle watchers missed ecaa52/190f6a completions; detection fell back to manual feed greps).

The authoritative signals already exist but are undiscovered:
1. Project observability SQLite (`<repo>/.specialists/db/observability.db`, table specialist_jobs: status running/waiting/done/failed + updated_at_ms) — zero-byte global ~/.specialists/observability.db is a red herring.
2. Feed terminal marker `status=COMPLETE exit=agent_end`.
3. `sp log -f --json --job <id>` already streams lifecycle/control rows incl. DONE events, but its help does not present it as THE completion-detection surface.

## SUCCESS (pick scope during promotion)
- Minimum: ps help/output documents that waiting != done for keep-alive jobs and points to sp log -f / DB path for reliable detection.
- Better: new command, e.g. `sp await <job-id> [--timeout <s>] [--include-push <branch>]` — exits 0 when the job reaches terminal state (done/failed OR feed COMPLETE agent_end), printing final summary + last_output; designed for agent-pane watchers (single blocking process instead of jq/grep loops).
- Optional: ps --json gains terminal_reason / completed_at fields so one call suffices.

## NON_GOALS
No change to keep-alive semantics itself.

## EVIDENCE
Repro: launch any HIGH keep-alive executor with --background, let it finish; ps shows waiting indefinitely while specialist_jobs.status=done and feed shows COMPLETE exit=agent_end.

title: fix(cli): sp log default forensic path emits every agent-internal event
description:
PROBLEM: sp log default mode (xtrm.forensic.v1) emits every forensic event including agent-internal turn/tool/model.token_usage/model.meta rows. On a typical executor job, 227/260 rows are turn.thinking, drowning the 2–3 actual runtime rows (job.started, job.failed, control.*, error.*). --all-events is a no-op in the forensic path (default=370 lines, all-events=370 lines) and only functions with --legacy. CLI help at src/cli/log.ts:463 still claims 'Default output is runtime-only', which is stale since forensic became default.

SCOPE: src/cli/log.ts — printForensicSnapshot loop (lines ~530-543). Add a runtime filter mirroring isRuntimeEvent from the legacy path, gated on !options.allEvents.

SUCCESS: Default sp log emits only runtime-worthy families (job/control/error/git/command/review/chain/worktree/process_health/retry/compaction/model.changed/mcp.connected|disconnected|auth.failed|rate_limited). --all-events restores full firehose. --legacy path unchanged. Row count for a busy executor job drops ~90%+ in default mode.

NON_GOALS: Do not touch the legacy path. Do not change forensic event schema or renderer. Do not touch feed. No new columns, no new flags.

CONSTRAINTS: One-file diff to src/cli/log.ts. Rebuild dist. No dependency changes. Preserve --json output shape (still emit forensic_event envelope; just fewer of them).

VALIDATION: 1) sp log <finished-job> --limit 500 | wc -l drops sharply. 2) sp log <job> --limit 500 --all-events | wc -l matches the pre-fix default. 3) sp log <job> --legacy behavior unchanged. 4) Targeted unit test on the new classifier if trivial to add; otherwise defer.

OUTPUT: One commit on a feature branch, PR to master.

SCRUTINY: low
close_reason: sp log default forensic path now filters agent-internal families (turn/tool/model.token_usage|finish_reason|meta/mcp.call.*); --all-events restores full firehose; --legacy path untouched; classifier unit test 28/28 pass; verified default 3 rows vs all-events 317 rows on job d2ec71

title: design(pi): Specialists exact-citation verifier v1 per mandate Section 10
description:
PROBLEM: Deep discovery confirmed zero grep hits for readVerifiedCitationWindow / verifyExactLineCitation / any exact-citation verifier in Specialists src/. The mandate (Section 10) names an invariant — cited line matches actual source at that line — with no code-implemented enforcement. Currently the invariant is delegated to Pi's numbered read output (accurate numbering enables the model to cite correctly, but nothing verifies post-hoc that a specialist's structured output citation actually matches the file at that line).

SUCCESS: A design proposal and a v1 implementation of a verifier that, given (path, line, quoted content), confirms the source file at that line still matches the quoted content — with a defined behavior contract for stale citations (worktree drift, post-edit citation) and integration points (specialist output validator? seconder gate? runner post-processor?).

SCOPE: Design first (bead notes with proposal), then implement in a separate PR. Location TBD — likely src/specialist/citation-verify.ts + hook into runner output validation.

NON_GOALS: Do NOT implement in the blank-line-parity PR. Do NOT touch Core.

CONSTRAINTS: Must not add per-tool overhead to hot path unless opt-in. Must handle worktree/session-boundary path resolution.

VALIDATION: Concrete positive/negative test cases; integration test showing a fake specialist output with mismatched citation fails validation.

OUTPUT: Design doc in bead notes + follow-up PR.
notes: CORRECTION: false premise. The exact-citation verifier already exists at src/specialist/citation-evidence.ts — readVerifiedCitationWindow (window-scoped read with true line numbers + totalLines) and verifyExactLineCitation (post-hoc quoted-content confirmation). Tests at tests/unit/specialist/citation-evidence.test.ts:27-110 cover blank-line preservation, offset/limit mapping, EOF parity with Pi split model, offset-beyond-EOF rejection, and raw_pi_read_unverified rejection. Bead created from insufficient grep (searched 'citation-verify' rather than 'citation-evidence').

title: Specialists: consume read-line-numbers via pi -e explicit-load path
description:
## PROBLEM
Specialists launches Pi with --no-extensions at 3 sites (src/specialist/script-runner.ts:1109, src/pi/session.ts:616, src/cli/serve.ts:37). This is correct — auto-discovered extensions would violate the specialist runtime contract. But it also means the canonical @jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions read-line-numbers extension does not load, so specialist pi read tool results are raw (no source-line prefix). The current mitigation is src/specialist/citation-evidence.ts which does a trusted-root re-read to produce verified line numbers, but this is executor-side after-the-fact verification rather than model-facing prevention.

## SUCCESS
Specialist pi runs (with the SAME --no-extensions posture) load read-line-numbers explicitly via pi's -e <path> flag. Model-facing read tool_result content shows 'NNN | source-line' for every source line, with Pi synthetic notices preserved verbatim. citation-evidence.ts remains the authoritative verifier — this change is prevention, not replacement.

## SCOPE
1. Add opt-in flag to specialist schema (e.g. execution.pi_extensions=['read-line-numbers']).
2. In each of the 3 pi-launch sites, when the specialist opts in, append '-e', '<resolved-path-to-read-line-numbers/index.ts>', preserving --no-extensions.
3. Resolve path via installed @jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions package (node resolve or hardcoded relative to package root).
4. Unit tests + one integration test showing numbered read in a specialist pi run.

## NON_GOALS
- Do NOT drop --no-extensions.
- Do NOT auto-enable for every specialist; keep it opt-in until we've validated no regressions.
- Do NOT remove or bypass citation-evidence.ts — the verified-window contract stays authoritative.
- Do NOT modify @jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions itself; consume the published package (currently xtrm-dev/core branch xt/spike-read-line-numbers, commit 7f6cd7f7, awaiting core-side merge/publish).

## CONSTRAINTS
- Requires @jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions release including read-line-numbers (upstream in xtrm-dev/core branch xt/spike-read-line-numbers).
- Backward compatible: specialists without the opt-in flag see zero behavior change.
- Path resolution must survive npm install / hoisted node_modules layouts.

## VALIDATION
[ ] Specialist opted in: pi launched with --no-extensions -e <path> loads read-line-numbers only, no other managed extension.
[ ] Read tool result seen by executor model contains 'NNN | ' prefix on every source line.
[ ] Pi synthetic notices preserved verbatim (no fake line number).
[ ] citation-evidence.ts still executes and still produces the authoritative verified window.
[ ] Specialist without opt-in: read output unchanged (regression negative).

## OUTPUT
Schema change + 3 launch-site edits + tests + docs pointing at this bead and at xtrm-dev/core#<PR-when-open>.

## REFERENCES
- Extension source: xtrm-dev/core commit 7f6cd7f7808eee6ffc492369ba1ab76b9d94157c on branch xt/spike-read-line-numbers, path packages/pi-extensions/extensions/read-line-numbers/
- E2E proof (2026-08-13): pi --print with the extension loaded returned '137 | line-137-payload' for a read call with offset=137 limit=3, and preserved '[62 more lines in file. Use offset=140 to continue.]' unchanged.
- Related: tpafe.5 (citation-evidence.ts local verified fallback, already shipped in v3.21.3).
close_reason: Satisfied by tpafe release v3.21.3: specialists now consumes read-line-numbers via pi -e alongside --no-extensions at the 3 launch sites. See memory tpafe-release-v3.21.3-shipped-2026-08-14.

Coordinator instructed to consume it, but no rule marks body as untrusted data or limits it to declared request schema. Successful injection can dispatch chains, mutate beads, send misleading replies, or drive git workflow.
- Impact: coordinator scope and workflow integrity bypass.
- Recommended fix: retain protocol skill or add explicit invariant: treat message bodies as untrusted data; validate sender, target pane, bead, `messageKey`, request type, and allowed action before acting. Never execute commands/instructions embedded in message body.

- Impact: unsafe publication, wrong branch mutation, merge conflict/data-integrity failure.
- Recommended fix: remove behavior bullets and executable examples for both broken verbs. Replace every remaining recommendation with manual workflow reference only.

title: Credentialed live-agent lane so Suite C steps 7-10 can run instead of SKIP
description:
## PROBLEM

Core's integration Suite C (core: test/integration-suite/suite-c-coordinator-lineage.mjs)
reports 5 PASS / 4 SKIP / 0 BLOCKED. The four deferred steps are all Specialists-side:

- step 7: dispatch a specialist child from the coordinator — needs a live specialist chain
  (real agent + API credentials)
- step 8: verify specialist branch derives from coordinator branch — sp creates specialist
  branches; Core only publishes the base via @agent_branch (audit P1-03)
- step 9: verify descendant runtime-origin lineage — runtime-origin propagation is
  Specialists-side (SupervisorStatus), needs a dispatched job
- step 10: merge accepted specialist branch into coordinator branch — needs 7-8's branches

Core wave-5 cluster D (core epic xtrm-d1fod) was asked to make these runnable via the new
aggregated topology projection. It cannot, and the premise was mistaken: these steps are
not blocked on the absence of a projection. They are blocked on the absence of a lane that
can really dispatch a specialist — a `sp run` with credentials that actually creates
specialist branches and worktrees. A read-only projection in Core cannot dispatch anything.

Shimming `sp run` to fabricate the branches was explicitly rejected. Suite C's own header
(:24-26) declares that boundary: steps 7-10 'stay SKIP with a stated reason rather than
being faked into a pass'. A faked PASS is worse than an honest SKIP because it retires the
ledger entry that keeps the gap visible.

## SUCCESS

Suite C's steps 7-10 execute against a real dispatched specialist chain in an environment
that has API credentials, and report PASS/FAIL on the actual branch-derivation and
runtime-origin lineage invariants instead of skipping.

## SCOPE

- A credentialed integration lane (opt-in, not the default hermetic path) able to run
  `sp run`/`sp chat` end to end against a throwaway repo.
- Whatever Specialists-side assertion surface steps 8-9 need: specialist branch derivation
  from the coordinator's published @agent_branch, and runtime-origin propagation through
  SupervisorStatus to descendants.

## NON_GOALS

- Making this run in the default hermetic CI path. It needs credentials and real LLM calls;
  it must stay opt-in and clearly gated.
- Changing Core's Suite C capability gate. PASS/SKIP with stated reasons is the shape
  core xtrm-6hey0 deliberately graduated to from BLOCKED.
- Faking the chain with a shim. Explicitly out of bounds — see PROBLEM.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Must not perturb Suite C steps 2-5 and 11, which pass today.
- Isolated HOME / XDG_STATE_HOME and a private tmux server, matching the discipline the
  rest of the suite already follows; the operator's real state is never touched.
- No fixture secret may appear in captured output.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Steps 7-10 report PASS in the credentialed lane.
- [ ] Steps 2-5 and 11 still PASS.
- [ ] The hermetic default lane still exits 0 with the four steps SKIPped.

## OUTPUT

The lane's invocation, its Suite C step ledger, and a note back to core xtrm-d1fod.5.

## REFERENCES

- Core suite: test/integration-suite/suite-c-coordinator-lineage.mjs (LIVE_ONLY at :43-48)
- Core epic: xtrm-d1fod (wave-5 cluster D), child xtrm-d1fod.5
- Core prereq (landed): PR #465 publishes @agent_branch as the derivation base (audit P1-03)
- Audit: ~/dev/11.md P2-01

title: Two-pass task-template render re-expands variables inside bead content
description:
## PROBLEM
renderTaskPrompt (src/specialist/task-prompt.ts, extracted from runner.ts) renders the task template TWICE for tracked runs: pass 1 substitutes $prompt with the bead context, pass 2 re-scans the RESULT. Any $word appearing inside bead text ($cwd, $bead_id, $prompt, $pre_script_output) is therefore expanded on the second pass — bead-authored content is treated as template source.

Found during the unitAI-6639v.1 audit (finding E). Preserved deliberately in .4 because the renderer had to be byte-identical to sp run; fixing it is a behavior change and needs its own bead.

## SCOPE
- src/specialist/task-prompt.ts (renderTaskPrompt two-pass render)
- tests/unit/task-prompt.test.ts

## SUCCESS
Bead-supplied content is never re-scanned as template source; sp run and sp render-task stay in lockstep. Regression test with a bead whose description contains a literal $cwd.

## NON_GOALS
No change to the template engine's unknown-variable passthrough for genuine templates.
close_reason: Done: task rendering is now single-pass. Reproduced first (a bead containing the literal token $cwd rendered as /SECRET/PATH), then fixed by rendering once over the original task_template with the union variable map. Bead content is data, never template source. Template-origin tokens still resolve (verified: $bead_id, $cwd, $bead_context, and the boundary block's real cwd). Regression test added in tests/unit/task-prompt.test.ts; zero regressions vs master (nothing relied on the double expansion).

title: Audit specialist startup context token cost
description:
## PROBLEM
Specialist runs may receive unnecessarily large initial context, increasing latency and context-window pressure. The actual injected sources and their costs are not yet quantified against the token usage persisted in runtime logs.

## SUCCESS
Produce an evidence-backed inventory of all initial-context inputs, their measured or reproducibly estimated token contribution, and their relationship to observed per-run token use. Identify avoidable weight without assuming that every large context source is unnecessary.

## SCOPE
Inspect the initial-run context assembly in `src/specialist/runner.ts`, `src/cli/run.ts`, and supporting context/prompt/mandatory-rule code, including bead/dependency context, rules, tool/catalog text, diff context, inherited job state, and template variables. Query the first rows and a representative stratified sample from `.specialists/db/observability.db` for logged token usage, model, specialist, job ID, prompt/context events, timestamps, and outcomes as available.

## NON_GOALS
- Do not alter token limits, prompt templates, context depth defaults, or runtime assembly in this audit.
- Do not equate total logged tokens with initial-context tokens without documenting the measurement gap.
- Do not use provider price estimates as a substitute for token evidence.

## CONSTRAINTS
- Trace each injected source to an implementation symbol/path and state the condition under which it is included.
- Preserve exact SQLite query text, selected columns, sample criteria, count, and known schema/version limitations.
- Where the DB lacks direct prompt-token fields, calculate a clearly labeled estimate from captured artifacts and state the tokenizer/method; do not present it as measured.
- Keep user data/redaction boundaries intact in evidence excerpts.

## VALIDATION
- [ ] A context-source inventory maps every startup injection to code symbols and inclusion conditions.
- [ ] SQLite evidence includes the first available rows plus a representative sample, with job IDs and token fields/outcomes where present.
- [ ] Per-source token measurements/estimates state method, sample size, aggregation, and uncertainty.
- [ ] Findings distinguish measured cost, estimated cost, and unmeasurable cost.
- [ ] Each recommendation has a target regression test (context-content/size) and an end-to-end specialist-start smoke check to ensure required context remains available.

## OUTPUT
A report containing: context assembly diagram/table; reproducible DB queries and samples; token-cost breakdown; correlation/limitations analysis; observed behavior, drift/risk, and ranked recommendations; plus validation contracts for any proposed runtime or prompt changes.
notes:
AUDIT COMPLETE (2026-07-12)

Observed context assembly
`SpecialistRunner.run` builds startup context from: pre-script output; own bead plus completed-blocker context; rendered task template; mandatory rules (global/default/specialist sets); system prompt plus specialist-run context; static workflow rules; filtered dynamic memories; optional GitNexus context; and native Pi `skills.paths`/skill inheritance. `src/cli/run.ts` additionally injects bounded diffs only for reviewer/seconder `--job` runs. Tool definitions, Pi/harness framing, and full native skill bodies are also API input but are not fully represented by `payload_breakdown`.

DB evidence and method
Truth selector used: `json_extract(token_trajectory_json, '$[0].token_usage.input_tokens')` on `specialist_job_metrics` status=done. First chronological token-bearing rows range 11,233-17,583 input tokens (sync-docs, memory-processor, executor, explorer).
Grouped examples: reviewer/openai-codex/gpt-5.3-codex n=93 mean 12,593 first-turn input; seconder/openai-codex/gpt-5.4-mini n=28 mean 10,145; obligations-scanner/openai-codex/gpt-5.4-mini n=13 mean 9,734; executor/openai-codex/gpt-5.4-mini n=56 mean 13,965. This is enough to show startup context is material, but not enough to call every byte waste.
Representative latest payload-breakdown samples: reviewer `95c5d5` 10,824 estimated tokens (system 4,207; task 1,948; mandatory rules 1,436; bead 1,578; memory 1,655); seconder `a20ce4` 7,291 (system 2,676; task 2,285; rules 980; bead 635; memory 715); explorer `f2da0b` 5,701 (system 2,272; task 1,038; rules 918; bead 698; memory 775).

Measurement limitations / telemetry drift
- `payload_breakdown` is an approximation, not the API truth; the samples differ from first-turn provider counts. It excludes full skill bodies and tool/harness framing, so it cannot rank native skills without a separate measurement.
- It also misattributes dynamic memory: runtime appends `memoryInjection.block`, but the breakdown records `beadContextText` as `memory.dynamic` (`runner.ts:1204-07`, `1327-29`). This can duplicate/overstate bead context in the report rather than prove duplicate prompt injection.
- Bare obligations-scanner is not supposed to receive mandatory rules, yet its `79b620` breakdown reports 456 mandatory-rule tokens because components are measured even when the bare-mode append path is skipped. Therefore current per-component telemetry is not safe for cost decisions for bare roles.

Risk assessment
HIGH measurement risk: current component data cannot answer which source is actually costly because skill bodies/tool framing are omitted and dynamic-memory/bare-rule accounting is inaccurate.
MEDIUM cost risk: fixed system prompts (2.3k-4.2k estimated), task templates (roughly 1k-2.3k), mandatory rules (0.9k-1.4k), and bead/dependency context are significant before any model work. Large beads/dependency depth can drive startup over 20k; job `44c64e` recorded 31,445 estimated startup tokens with own + two dependency contexts.

Recommendations (separate implementation beads)
1. Fix observability before reducing context: record exact rendered strings after all conditional branches; separately count attached skill body bytes/tokens, tool definitions/harness overhead, injected diff, each blocker, actual filtered memory, and provider first-turn tokens. Store hashes/lengths rather than sensitive content.
2. Remove the dynamic-memory measurement misattribution and do not emit mandatory-rule components for `bare` runs. Add regression fixtures for bare/non-bare and memory-on/off.
3. Once baseline is trustworthy, make context selective: cap/choose completed-blocker material by relevance, inject only bounded diff file/hunks, and split bulky skill guidance into always-on minimum plus on-demand references. Do not remove a rule/skill merely because it is large.
4. Add a startup-payload budget report per specialist/model, with warn-only thresholds initially; base any hard cap on first-turn input distribution and required chain smoke results.

Validation for any change
Unit-test payload components against the exact final system/task/skill inputs (including bare mode, dynamic memory, blockers, and diff truncation). Add an integration smoke that starts reviewer/seconder with a known worktree and asserts required bead/rule/diff evidence survives while observed first-turn input and component totals are emitted. Compare before/after on a representative SQLite sample; verify outcome quality and gate completion, not token count alone.

title: Audit Iron principles, review chain, and obligations scanner
description:
## PROBLEM
The review pipeline may no longer preserve the original Iron guarantees, including `ddiff`, independent review/seconder behavior, obligations tracking, and reliable diff access. The practical value of obligations-scanner is unknown, so its continued runtime and context cost must be evaluated against observed use rather than presumed intent.

## SUCCESS
Produce a source-to-runtime audit of reviewer, seconder, executor, obligations-scanner, and injected mandatory-rules behavior. State for every examined Iron principle whether it is preserved, intentionally changed, lost, or unverifiable; assess whether obligations-scanner produces actionable outcomes in real runs.

## SCOPE
Read `docs/archive/iron-review-hardening-qa-chain-substrate.md` and `/home/dawid/dev/xtrm/docs/substrate/chain_templates.md`; if the originally requested `~/dev/xtrm/docs/specialists/chain_templates.md` remains absent, record that path correction. Inspect current specialist definitions/prompts, mandatory-rule sets/injection, `SpecialistRunner.run`, `buildReviewerDiffContext`, `buildInjectedDiffContext`, and `.specialists/db/observability.db` records/events for reviewer, seconder, executor, and obligations-scanner.

## NON_GOALS
- Do not edit specialist prompts, rules, chain templates, or runtime code.
- Do not treat a config declaration as proof that a rule ran or changed an outcome.
- Do not make a keep/remove decision for obligations-scanner without sampled-run evidence.

## CONSTRAINTS
- Explicitly investigate `ddiff` drift; programmatic diff-context fragility (merge base, worktree, truncation, missing diff, and prompt-variable paths); and the alternative of teaching auditors to obtain their own diff.
- For obligations-scanner, query `observability.db`, inspect a representative sample across statuses/times, and retain job IDs plus relevant event/result excerpts and query text.
- Compare historical intent with current xtrm canonical template and local runtime separately; do not collapse them into one source of truth.
- Redact prompt payloads/secrets while preserving enough evidence to reproduce classifications.

## VALIDATION
- [ ] Evidence table maps each original Iron principle (including `ddiff`) to historical text, current template, current runtime/config, and observed runs.
- [ ] At least one reproducible SQLite query identifies obligations-scanner volume, completion/outcome distribution, and sampled job IDs; sample rationale and limitations are recorded.
- [ ] Diff-context paths are exercised or traced for normal, empty/missing, and worktree/merge-base-sensitive conditions as available.
- [ ] Findings separate observed behavior, drift/risk, recommendation, confidence, and required follow-up validation.
- [ ] Each suggested runtime/prompt change names targeted unit tests plus an integrated chain smoke run before adoption.

## OUTPUT
A concise audit report with: source inventory; principle-by-principle evidence table; obligations-scanner SQLite query/results and sampled runs; diff-context failure-mode analysis; ranked recommendations (including no-change where warranted); and proposed test/smoke contracts for each recommended change.
notes:
AUDIT COMPLETE (2026-07-12)

Observed behavior / evidence
- Historical source: `docs/archive/iron-review-hardening-qa-chain-substrate.md` defines Iron as `code-sanity -> security? -> obligations-scanner -> reviewer`; the current xtrm canon at `/home/dawid/dev/xtrm/docs/substrate/chain_templates.md` §2 defines `writer -> seconder -> test-engineer -> test-runner -> security? -> obligations-scanner -> reviewer`, with ddiff in §2.7.
- Local configs retain role intent: reviewer declares ddiff and an obligations scan; seconder is a dual verdict; executor instructs structured TODO bead IDs; obligations-scanner has CLEAN/OBLIGATIONS_FOUND/BLOCKED output.
- Runtime enforcement has drifted: `src/cli/run.ts:1046-55` only auto-injects diff variables for reviewer and seconder when `--job` is reused. It does not compose or require the canonical chain, does not inject an obligations-scanner diff, and direct `sp run` permits roles independently. Thus the pipeline is documentation/config convention, not a runtime gate.
- Ddiff is present in the reviewer prompt, but no runtime checkpoint/previous-verdict state enforces it. Its correct operation depends on the model locating a prior commit/turn; evidence is not persisted as an explicit ddiff range.
- Diff injection is fragile: `buildInjectedDiffContext` selects unstaged, then staged, then branch-vs-base; defaults base to `main` when origin HEAD is absent; limits 20 files, 2,000 chars/file and 12,000 chars total. `buildReviewerDiffContext` has a different base resolver/source behavior. These can yield a partial or inconsistent audit surface. The injected context should remain an optimization/evidence anchor, while every audit role must receive a validated worktree/base/job reference and be taught a bounded self-discovery fallback.
- Mandatory rules are runtime-injected by `buildMandatoryRulesInjection` into non-bare specialists. Obligations-scanner is configured `bare: true`; its task is mechanical and should not depend on the full mandatory-rule stack.

Obligations-scanner DB evidence
Query: `SELECT m.job_id,m.status,m.bead_id,m.elapsed_ms,m.total_turns,m.total_tools,json_extract(m.token_trajectory_json,'$[0].token_usage.input_tokens'),r.output FROM specialist_job_metrics m LEFT JOIN specialist_results r USING(job_id) WHERE m.specialist='obligations-scanner' ORDER BY m.started_at_ms DESC`.
- 25 rows: 24 `done`, 1 `error`; done-row mean elapsed 36.8s (above the <30s target, distorted by runs at 138s and 141s).
- Parsed persisted outputs: 12 CLEAN, 1 OBLIGATIONS_FOUND (`effd08`, unitAI-rjwrk), 4 BLOCKED (`7e1c92`, `6f6918`, `00dcfb`, `be9430`), 8 with empty/no parseable output; 1 error (`79b620`, 239s, 24 turns/48 tools).
- `7e1c92` is a concrete BLOCKED sample: it says shell execution was unavailable, so it could not obtain `git diff`. Several later unitAI-4b60j samples are zero-token smoke-like rows and are not evidence of production usefulness.
- There is evidence it can flag an obligation once, but no stored link proving a reviewer consumed `effd08`; practical gate value is therefore unproven, not disproven.

Drift / risk
1. HIGH: declared mandatory chain is not mechanically enforced or evidenced per writer run.
2. HIGH: obligations scanner receives no automatic diff context and can BLOCKED when it cannot self-obtain a diff.
3. MEDIUM: ddiff is a prompt instruction, not a persisted/reproducible delta contract.
4. MEDIUM: scanner output retention/schema compliance is weak enough that 8/25 rows are unusable for outcome analysis.

Recommended changes (separate implementation beads)
- Add a chain evidence record that binds writer job, base SHA, worktree, seconder, QA, obligations, reviewer, and reviewer-consumption status; reject reviewer PASS at medium+ when required gate evidence is absent.
- Make a small shared diff resolver return `{base_sha, source, files, truncated, patch}` to all audit roles. Inject bounded patch data, but require roles to verify/fallback to `git diff <base_sha>..HEAD`; test empty/staged/unstaged/no-origin/worktree/over-limit paths.
- Persist prior reviewer verdict + review base SHA and pass an explicit `ddiff_base_sha` for PARTIAL re-review. Test that unchanged files are carried forward and changed hunks are rechecked.
- Keep obligations-scanner as a pilot, not a hard gate, until it emits valid structured output and a reviewer-consumption link. Add smoke tests for CLEAN, untracked marker, tracked marker, missing worktree/diff, and output persistence.

Validation for any change
Unit-test resolver source precedence/truncation and gate-requiredness. Add a tiny end-to-end chain smoke where executor adds an untracked TODO, scanner reports it, reviewer receives evidence and returns PARTIAL; resume with a delta and assert ddiff base/range is recorded.

**Conclusion**: thinkingLevelMap is **genuinely OPTIONAL**. For natively-known models, pi maintains internal default mappings per model/provider.
