Introduce one canonical restraint discipline, deepest text at the specialists mandatory rule, shallow bullets at the top-level injections, and a mid-depth pointer in the orchestrator skill. title: Add specialist restart job-audit for dead running jobs
description:
## PROBLEM

`sp clean --reap-orphans` handles stale processes, but autonomous containers need an explicit job-level restart audit that marks dead running/waiting rows safely and emits durable findings for operators and future substrate daemon reconciliation.

## SUCCESS

A repeatable audit can mark dead-pid `starting`/`running`/`waiting` jobs as cancelled with reason `container-restart-orphan` or equivalent, without touching live jobs or xt-owned worktree state.

## SCOPE

- `src/cli/doctor.ts` and/or `src/cli/clean.ts`
- `src/specialist/process-health.ts`
- `src/specialist/observability-sqlite.ts` status update helpers
- tests for dead/live process cases

## NON_GOALS

- Do not audit git branches or PR state; xt owns that.
- Do not delete worktrees from this audit path.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Bridge item with durable semantics: post-substrate the daemon owns restart reconciliation; this bridge command may retire, but cancellation events remain meaningful historical evidence.
- Logging/telemetry: emit job_id, pid, previous_status, new_status, reason, action, outcome, duration_ms.
- Idempotent: running twice must not duplicate or corrupt state.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Tests cover dead pid, live pid, missing pid, already-terminal job, and repeated audit.
- [ ] CLI smoke shows JSON findings and no mutation in dry-run mode if provided.

## OUTPUT

Audit command/flag, tests, JSON sample, and explicit retire/rename note for substrate migration.

title: Substrate materialization: emit advisor/followup/gate from dependency verdicts
description:
## PROBLEM

Once a dependency verdict exists (from the capability's skill/Action), there is no substrate materialization: PASS_WITH_NOTES/COOLDOWN/NEEDS_CHANGES/BLOCKED verdicts don't become tracked advisor/followup/gate issues. Operators still translate verdicts into bd issues by hand (spec §13). This task wires verdict → substrate issue class.

## SUCCESS

A dependency verdict (from the Action D1 once integrated, or from manually invoking the skill) materializes the right substrate artifact: advisor (non-blocking advice), followup (discovered-from the dependency update), or gate (merge/deploy blocker). Each carries evidence refs + the upgrade dossier.

## SCOPE

Specialists-side wiring between the dependency verdict and bd substrate classes. Likely a small script/hook that reads a verdict (JSON) and creates/links the right bd issue with `--type`, priority, and `discovered-from`/parent edges. Coordinates with the xtrm-tools Action (D1, `xtrm-r1ed7.3`) output format. Does NOT change bd itself or the specialists runtime.

## NON_GOALS

- No deployer/SRE automation (v2 roadmap).
- No incident handling or rollback.
- No multi-repo backlog UI (v3).
- No changes to the verdict taxonomy (policy doc §5).

## CONSTRAINTS

- Substrate classes per spec §13: advisor / followup (discovered-from dependency update) / gate (merge-deploy blocker) / root (only if operator accepts standalone work).
- Follow-ups use `discovered-from` edges, not `blocks`.
- Verification beads use `validates`, not `blocks`.
- Evidence refs must point at the upgrade dossier + case JSON.
- No secrets in any materialized artifact.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] PASS_WITH_NOTES → advisor issue created with dossier ref
- [ ] COOLDOWN → follow-up/quarantine issue created (discovered-from)
- [ ] NEEDS_CHANGES → follow-up (executor) created
- [ ] BLOCKED → gate issue created (blocks the dependency PR/merge)
- [ ] Each materialized issue carries evidence refs + verdict
- [ ] Smoke: end-to-end from a sample verdict JSON to materialized bd issues

## OUTPUT

Materialization script/hook + bd edge conventions doc + smoke evidence; residual risks (e.g. dedup across re-runs) noted.

## REFERENCES

- `~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/dependencies-updating.md` §13 (substrate), §9 (verdicts)
- `~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/dependency-bump-policy.md` §6 (pipeline)
- xtrm-tools xtrm-r1ed7.3 (Action D1) — verdict source
notes:
E1 complete.

Changed files:
- scripts/materialize-dependency-verdict.mjs
- tests/unit/scripts/materialize-dependency-verdict.test.ts
- docs/devops/dependency-verdict-materialization.md

Behavior:
- Added a focused specialists-side materializer that reads a dependency verdict JSON and produces a substrate issue plan.
- Dry-run is the default; `--apply` is required before any `bd` issue is created.
- Mapping shipped:
  - PASS_WITH_NOTES -> `class:advisor`
  - COOLDOWN -> `class:followup` (quarantine/cooldown)
  - NEEDS_CHANGES -> `class:followup` (executor lane)
  - BLOCKED / SECURITY_FORCED -> `class:gate`
- Follow-ups use `discovered-from`; optional validation links use `validates`; only gate issues add a blocking edge back to the source dependency-update bead.
- Materialized descriptions always include verdict + evidence refs (`case_json_path`, plus dossier/comment/external refs when present).

Verification:
- bun --bun vitest run tests/unit/scripts/materialize-dependency-verdict.test.ts  ✅
- bun run lint  ✅
- manual dry-run smoke with a SECURITY_FORCED sample verdict JSON  ✅
  - produced a gate plan
  - showed `bd create ... --deps discovered-from:...[,validates:...]`
  - showed post-create `bd dep <created-issue-id> --blocks <source>` preview
- no live bd issues were created during validation (dry-run only)

Residual risks:
- Re-run dedup is not handled yet; repeated `--apply` against the same verdict could create duplicate substrate issues unless a caller de-duplicates upstream.
- Input normalization is intentionally permissive around field names to bridge D1/C1 evolution, so the final xtrm-tools action contract should be pinned once that side lands.

The global override layer supports model, timeout, notes/output, prompt-mode, and extension toggles, but it still cannot set execution.interactive even though the runtime already uses that field as the canonical keep-alive default. title: Add waiting_auto_close_ms for stale waiting keep-alives
description:
## PROBLEM

Waiting specialists currently have only a warning threshold (stall_detection.waiting_stale_ms). After the warning, they can remain forgotten indefinitely unless the operator manually runs sp stop or cleanup commands. The desired behavior is an opt-in auto-close path for stale waiting sessions, with graceful close first and TERM/KILL fallback only when the session will not exit cleanly.

## SUCCESS

A new stall-detection field, stall_detection.waiting_auto_close_ms, allows a specialist to opt into automatic stale waiting cleanup. When a waiting session exceeds the threshold, the supervisor emits explicit telemetry, attempts the same close path as an operator-driven graceful stop, and escalates to TERM/KILL only if the session does not exit within a bounded grace window. Default behavior remains unchanged when the field is absent or null.

## SCOPE

Exact insertion points:
- src/specialist/schema.ts
  - extend StallDetectionSchema with waiting_auto_close_ms
- src/specialist/loader.ts
  - extend StallDetectionConfig typing and summary plumbing if needed
- src/specialist/launch.ts
  - ensure the new stall_detection field reaches Supervisor unchanged
- src/specialist/supervisor.ts
  - extend threshold defaults/merging logic without enabling behavior by default
  - add live waiting-state checker logic for waiting_auto_close_ms
  - define graceful-close -> SIGTERM -> SIGKILL fallback sequence and telemetry/events
  - update crash-recovery semantics only where coherent with the new field contract
- tests/unit/specialist/supervisor.test.ts
  - warning-only path remains intact
  - auto-close threshold path
  - fallback escalation path
  - strict boundary behavior and no-op when disabled

## NON_GOALS

- No broad redesign of process-health or sp clean.
- No auto-kill of running jobs.
- No new chain/container lifecycle model.

## CONSTRAINTS

- waiting_auto_close_ms must be opt-in; absent/null means current warning-only behavior.
- The first action must be graceful close, preserving final result/bead-note behavior where available.
- Telemetry must make it obvious whether a session closed gracefully or required TERM/KILL fallback.
- Existing waiting_stale_ms warnings must continue to work independently.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Stall-detection schema and supervisor thresholds accept waiting_auto_close_ms without changing default runtime behavior.
- [ ] Unit tests prove graceful close occurs after threshold when configured.
- [ ] Unit tests prove TERM/KILL fallback only occurs after graceful close fails or times out.
- [ ] Telemetry/event assertions distinguish stale warning vs auto-close vs forced termination.

## OUTPUT

Report the new field contract, fallback sequence, and test evidence proving the runtime behavior.

title: Global override follow-up: interactive defaults + waiting auto-close
description:
## PROBLEM

The KAN-90/KAN-91 global override layer at ~/.config/specialists/user.json still lacks one important runtime-default knob: operators cannot set a machine-wide default for execution.interactive (the keep-alive default that run/resume semantics already respect). Separately, specialists that enter waiting can remain forgotten indefinitely unless the operator explicitly runs sp stop or cleanup commands. The runtime already emits waiting_stale warnings after 1h, but it never performs a graceful auto-close / stop path.

## SUCCESS

Operators can set a machine-wide default for keep-alive via ~/.config/specialists/user.json using the canonical execution.interactive field, and specialists can opt into a configurable waiting-state auto-close threshold via stall_detection.waiting_auto_close_ms. When the threshold is exceeded, the supervisor performs a graceful close first, then TERM/KILL fallback only if needed. Authoring and operator docs, including specialists-creator surfaces, document the new knobs and their precedence.

## SCOPE

- Global override layer: src/specialist/global-config.ts, src/specialist/schema.ts, src/specialist/loader.ts, src/cli/edit.ts, src/cli/console/config-source.ts
- Waiting-state lifecycle: src/specialist/supervisor.ts, src/specialist/launch.ts, stall-detection docs and tests
- Authoring/operator docs and creator surfaces: config/skills/specialists-creator/, config/specialists/specialists-creator.specialist.json, docs/overrides-guide.md, docs/cli-reference.md, docs/features.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/upgrade-notes/, config/skills/setup-specialists/
- Regression/unit/integration coverage for the new fields and waiting auto-close behavior

## NON_GOALS

- No rename to a new keep_alive field name in specialist schema or user.json; use canonical execution.interactive.
- No change to per-run CLI precedence: --no-keep-alive and --keep-alive still override defaults.
- No broad redesign of sp clean, process-health, or the chain/container model.
- No automatic termination of unrelated running jobs; this epic is only about stale waiting sessions.

## CONSTRAINTS

- execution.interactive in user.json must remain a sparse override with null = inherit semantics.
- waiting auto-close must prefer graceful close semantics and preserve final handoff / bead-note behavior whenever possible.
- Default behavior must remain unchanged unless a specialist explicitly sets stall_detection.waiting_auto_close_ms.
- The new field names must be reflected consistently across schema, console/config surfaces, docs, and specialist-authoring guidance.
- Logging / telemetry must clearly distinguish warning-only waiting_stale from terminal auto-close / forced-stop behavior.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] sp init --global templates and sp edit --global validation accept execution.interactive and the chosen waiting auto-close path where intended.
- [ ] Loader merge produces the same effective defaults the runtime consumes for keep-alive and stall-detection behavior.
- [ ] Supervisor unit coverage proves: warning-only waiting_stale still works; waiting_auto_close_ms triggers graceful close; fallback TERM/KILL path is covered.
- [ ] Operator/authoring docs and specialists-creator guidance mention the canonical field names, precedence, and safety caveats.
- [ ] Smoke or integration evidence demonstrates the override path end-to-end, or a clearly-scoped follow-up test bead documents the unavailable boundary.

## OUTPUT

A closed epic should report: the exact new override fields, the supervisor auto-close contract and fallback behavior, the docs/creator surfaces updated, test evidence, and any residual follow-up around orphaned waiting processes if live auto-close cannot cover them all.

- KAN-91 / unitAI-gp7nq: expanded override allowlist

- `/tmp/unitAI-mally/script-runner.ts:865-882`

- `model`
- `systemPrompt`
- `permissionLevel`
- `specialistName`
- `skillPaths`
- `thinkingLevel`
- `cwd`
- `stallTimeoutMs`
- `excludeExtensions`

Missing:
- `onToken`
- `onThinking`
- `onToolStart`
- `onToolEnd`
- `onEvent`
- `onMetric`
- `onMeta`

- text deltas: `message_update -> text_delta` at `session.ts:1047-1052`
- thinking: `session.ts:1053-1061`

  - `upsertStatusWithEvent(... createRunStartEvent(...))`
  - `appendEvent(... createMetaEvent(...))`
- script path manually persists terminal only in `persistScriptTerminal()` at `/tmp/unitAI-mally/script-runner.ts:396-441`
  - `upsertStatusWithEventAndResult(... createRunCompleteEvent(...))`
- no callback bridge appends intermediate timeline events into DB

- `/tmp/unitAI-mally/script-runner.ts:676-689` startup persisted first
- `/tmp/unitAI-mally/script-runner.ts:794-797` outer catch returns failure result
- outer catch does **not** call `persistScriptTerminal()`

That means any exception thrown after `persistScriptStart()` and before one of terminal-writing branches at:
- success path `733-748`
- invalid JSON path `712-727`
- classified error path `752-767`
- exhausted attempts path `775-790`

will leave DB row stuck `running`.

Concrete leak window includes throws from:
- `runSingleAttempt(...)` before it returns an attempt object, if exception escapes
- `runPostScripts()` after terminal write? no stale-running there because terminal already written
- any unexpected throw in loop body before `persistScriptTerminal(...)`

Most important escape hatch:
- `/tmp/unitAI-mally/script-runner.ts:897-913` inner `runSingleAttempt()` catch only marks timeout if message includes `'timed out'`
- for non-timeout failures it returns attempt object, so not leak
- but if `PiAgentSession.create(...)` or code before inner try throws, or other synchronous setup throws in `runSingleAttempt()`, exception bubbles to outer catch at `794-797`
- outer catch skips terminal persist
- status row remains from `persistScriptStart()` as `running`

Why row can show forever in `ps/health`:
- feed follow logic treats non-terminal status as active:
  - `/tmp/unitAI-mally/feed.ts:750-751`
  - `/tmp/unitAI-mally/feed.ts:814-817`
- without terminal `run_complete` or terminal status update, row never transitions out

### Fix applied
None. Diagnosis only.

1. In script path, add observability callbacks when creating `PiAgentSession` in `/tmp/unitAI-mally/script-runner.ts:843-857`.
2. Reuse same event mapping model as supervisor:
   - session `onToken` / `onThinking` / `onToolStart` / `onToolEnd` / `onEvent` / `onMetric` / `onMeta`
   - append timeline events through observability client for current `traceId`
3. Keep `persistScriptStart()` for initial row and `persistScriptTerminal()` for final row. Do not redesign schema.
4. Add `terminalPersisted` flag in `runScriptSpecialist()`.
5. In outer catch at `/tmp/unitAI-mally/script-runner.ts:794-797`, if start already persisted and `terminalPersisted` false, call `persistScriptTerminal(... finalStatus:'error' ...)`.
6. Make backstop include escaped error message and best-known model.

Gap 1: session emits rich events, script runner drops them. Missing callback bridge in `/tmp/unitAI-mally/script-runner.ts:842-914`.  
Gap 2: startup persisted before risky work, outer catch at `/tmp/unitAI-mally/script-runner.ts:794-797` returns without terminal persist. That branch can strand row `running` forever.

title: script-specialist live observability: missing progress events + stale running rows
description:
## PROBLEM

After unitAI-4zask refit shipped live visibility for script-specialists in `sp ps` + `sp feed`, two follow-up gaps are visible during real runs.

### Bug 1 — no progress events between START and DONE
Script-specialists emit only boundary events (`START` + `META` + terminal `DONE`).
Compared with classic async specialists (e.g. `researcher/gpt-5.4-mini` job
`e2b091`) that stream `TEXT kind=assistant`, `TOKNS`, `TURN+` continuously, a
service-skills-sync run that takes 5+ minutes shows ZERO intermediate events
in `sp feed`. Live observability is effectively boundary-only — operator
cannot see what the model is doing during the run.

Hypothesis: refit routes tool-using script-specialists through
`PiAgentSession` but the pi-session per-turn event stream is not wired
into the script-specialist feed writer (only the start + terminal hooks are).

title: sp console: direct stderr writes bypass log.ts dedupe + single-sink invariant
description:
## PROBLEM

\`src/cli/console/log.ts\` declares a single-sink invariant: *every* sp-console NDJSON stderr emit must route through \`logError()\` so the \`SEEN\` memo dedupes per (view, op, errorClass). The invariant is documented in the file header:

> Greppable invariant: \`rg "process.stderr.write\\(JSON" src/cli/console\` returns only this file.

Empirical check (operator walkthrough §9, unitAI-u2s76):

\`\`\`
rg "process.stderr.write(JSON" src/cli/console
src/cli/console/config-source.ts:289   # read_global_config
src/cli/console/config-source.ts:477   # write_global_config
src/cli/console/runtime.ts:415         # git_numstat / git_status / git_diff
src/cli/console/runtime.ts:480 (via line var)  # bd_show
\`\`\`

Four sites bypass \`logError()\`.

Live smoke (PATH-shimmed to force-failing \`git\` and \`bd\`) confirms:

| Test | Lines emitted | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| Single git_numstat failure | 1 | 1 ✅ |
| Single bd_show failure | 1 | 1 ✅ |
| **50 identical git_numstat failures** | **50** | **1** ❌ |
| 50 identical list_processes failures (via logError) | 1 (theoretical — empty in test) | 1 ✅ |

Operator-impact: in a sp console session where the backing repo's git or bd briefly degrades, the poll loop will spam stderr with N envelopes per second instead of the documented 1-per-(view,op,errorClass).

Additional discrepancy: the direct-write envelope OMITS the \`view\` field that \`logError()\` includes. Envelope shapes diverge across the codebase.

## SUCCESS

- All four direct-write sites route through \`logError()\` or an equivalent dedupe-aware emitter.
- \`rg "process.stderr.write\\(JSON" src/cli/console\` returns only \`log.ts\` (single-sink invariant holds).
- Burst test (50 identical failures) emits exactly 1 NDJSON line.
- All envelopes carry the \`view\` field consistently.
- The \`beadId\` extra (currently inlined at runtime.ts:484, capped to 24 chars) is preserved through the centralized path — extend \`LogErrorExtras\` to carry an arbitrary string-extras map, or accept \`beadId\` as a first-class optional field.

## SCOPE

- \`src/cli/console/runtime.ts:402-429\` (\`runGit\`) — replace direct write with \`logError(view, op, {...})\`. \`view\` must be threaded from caller (diffSummary / diffFile / resolveDiffBase). Note resolveDiffBase swallows non-zero exits as part of base detection; only the documented-failure paths in runGit emit.
- \`src/cli/console/runtime.ts:434-493\` (\`fetchBeadDoc\` + \`logBeadShowError\`) — same.
- \`src/cli/console/config-source.ts:280-300\` (\`logConfigError\`) and \`460-475\` (\`logConfigWriteError\`) — same.
- \`src/cli/console/log.ts\` — extend \`LogErrorExtras\` with an optional \`extras: Record<string, string|number|null>\` map (for \`beadId\`-style fields) OR add a first-class \`beadId\` field. Document the new contract in the file header.
- Tests: add a burst-failure unit test (50 identical errors → 1 NDJSON line). Update existing tests if envelope shape changes for direct-write sites.

## NON_GOALS

- Reworking the envelope schema beyond adding the \`view\` field everywhere and the \`beadId\` carry-through.
- Changing the \`SEEN\` dedupe key (still per \`view:op:errorClass\`).
- Touching \`sp log\`'s NDJSON output (different surface, different contract).

## CONSTRAINTS

- The \`beadId\` field must remain capped to 24 chars to prevent shell-injection-string leakage in error logs (current safeguard at runtime.ts:484).
- Dedupe must be PROCESS-lifetime (matches current \`SEEN: Set<string>\`), not per-poll-cycle.
- \`logError()\` must remain \`void\` and silent on its own internal failures (already true via try/catch).

## VALIDATION

- [ ] \`rg "process.stderr.write\\(JSON" src/cli/console\` returns only \`log.ts\`.
- [ ] Burst test (50 identical git failures → 1 NDJSON line) passes.
- [ ] All NDJSON envelopes from sp console carry the \`view\` field.
- [ ] \`bd_show\` envelope still carries \`beadId\` (capped to 24 chars).
- [ ] tsc clean, full console suite green.

## OUTPUT

- Single PR off master.
- §9 walkthrough verdict flips PASS.

Discovered-from operator walkthrough unitAI-ctb4u.18 §9. Audit bead: unitAI-u2s76.
close_reason: PR #131 merged: 4 sites consolidated through logError, beadId+step extras added, 50-burst dedupe restored, single-sink invariant holds

title: sp console: forensic feed truncates type column (event_family.event_name)
description:
## PROBLEM

In forensic feed view (\`t\` → forensic), the first content column (event_family.event_name) is truncated to 18 chars by \`SPEC_72_LAYOUT.typeW=18\` in \`src/specialist/forensic-renderer.ts:105\`. Many event labels exceed this — \`lifecycle.run_complete\` (22), \`gitnexus.detect_changes\` (23), \`compaction.start\` (16) — so the column shows ellipsized identifiers that aren't operator-readable.

The shared mapper is correct for \`sp log\` (where the row is a single 72-col print line). The console view has 120-200 cols available and should NOT inherit the sp log column budget verbatim.

## SUCCESS

Forensic feed in console gives the type column enough room to render every event_family.event_name without ellipsis at 120+ col widths. Payload column reflows.

## SCOPE

- \`src/cli/console/forensic.ts:50\` — currently passes default layout to \`formatRenderedRowColumns\`.
- \`src/specialist/forensic-renderer.ts:114\` — already accepts an optional \`layout\` argument; no API change.
- Tests: \`tests/unit/cli/console-core-gaps.test.ts\` or a new forensic-row test asserting type-column width.

## NON_GOALS

- Changing \`sp log\` column budget. SPEC_72_LAYOUT remains canonical for the 72-col log surface.
- Width-responsive column scaling (deferred).

## CONSTRAINTS

- Console layout MUST live in \`src/cli/console/forensic.ts\` (console-local override), not in the shared renderer.
- typeW should accommodate the longest current event label (~26 chars) + headroom; suggest 32.
- actorW (24) is fine; seqW (4) is fine.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] In forensic feed, every event family/name renders without trailing ellipsis at 120-col terminal width.
- [ ] sp log row width unchanged.
- [ ] Test asserting the console-passed layout uses typeW ≥ 32.

## OUTPUT

- Single PR off master.
- Walkthrough §8 forensic feed observation flips PASS.

title: Materializer adoption Phase 2: port SourceQueue for per-repo poll isolation
description:
## PROBLEM

sp console v2's `scheduleRender` coalesces dispatches into one 50ms timer globally. `listRepos()` returns N repos in multi-repo sessions (parent dir scan finds multiple `.specialists/db/observability.db` siblings). When the operator presses `tab` to switch repo, the in-flight poll on repo A and the about-to-start poll on repo B share that single global timer — A's pending dispatch can still mutate state when the operator has already moved on. The gitboard materializer's `queue.ts` (34 LoC) is the right primitive: per-source `SourceQueue` with coalesce + drain-after-run + re-enqueue-if-trailing, and a `COALESCE_MS=1500` default that already matches the sp console poll bump from Phase 5.

## SUCCESS

`src/specialist/source-queue.ts` exists as a port of the gitboard module. `ConsoleApp` instantiates one `SourceQueue` per `RepoRef.id` and routes polls through it. Switching repo (`nextRepo` / `selectRepo` actions) cancels the destination repo's stale dispatches if any, and clears the source repo's queue without waiting for the in-flight run to finish. Polls remain coalesced at 1500ms per repo.

## SCOPE

- New: `src/specialist/source-queue.ts` — verbatim port from gitboard with attribution.
- Modified: `src/cli/console/components.ts`:
  - Replace the single `setInterval(POLL_MS)` with a map `Map<repoId, SourceQueue>`.
  - `refresh(repo)` enqueues into that repo's queue.
  - `switchRepo` resets the new repo's queue and triggers an immediate refresh.
  - `stop()` drains all queues (best-effort).
- Tests: `tests/unit/specialist/source-queue.test.ts` — coalesce semantics, drain-after-run, re-enqueue-if-trailing, error handler routing.

## NON_GOALS

- Replacing the 50ms render coalescer from Phase 5 — that one stays (it caps repaint frequency; this one caps refresh frequency).
- A long-running daemon process that polls in the background — sp console remains foreground-only.
- WebSocket subscription (separate exploratory bead).

## CONSTRAINTS

- Port byte-identical modulo import paths and attribution header. No drift from gitboard upstream.
- No new dependencies.
- Greppable invariant: `rg "setInterval.*POLL_MS" src/cli/console` returns zero after this lands.
- Per-repo queue eviction on `switchRepo` must clear `queued` + cancel the pending `setTimeout` — leaks would compound across tab cycles.
- The `onError` handler must route through the existing `logError(view, 'list_processes', { errorClass })` so the centralized NDJSON sink stays the only stderr writer.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `bun test tests/unit/specialist/source-queue.test.ts` covers: single enqueue → one run; burst enqueue → one run; trailing enqueue during run → second run after drain; errors routed to onError.
- [ ] Smoke: 3-repo session (parent dir with 3 child repos), `tab` 10 times rapidly — no thrown exceptions, no double-rendering of stale repo data.
- [ ] Full sweep (227/227 + new tests) stays green.
- [ ] `rg "setInterval.*POLL_MS" src/cli/console` zero.

## OUTPUT

- New `src/specialist/source-queue.ts` (34 LoC).
- Modified `src/cli/console/components.ts` (per-repo queue map).
- New `tests/unit/specialist/source-queue.test.ts`.

## APPROACH NOTES

- gitboard's `SourceQueue` ctor takes `onError(sourceKey, error)`. sp console's source key = `RepoRef.id`. Wire `onError` to `logError(this.logViewKey(), 'list_processes', { errorClass: errorClassOf(error) })`.
- Composition with Phase 1 snapshot-diff bead: after the queue port, the refresh path becomes `queue.enqueue(repoId, () => listProcessSnapshot → snapshotDiff → dispatch if changed)`. Per-repo isolation + per-row dedup.
- Future-work: when the materializer-as-subscriber bead lands, the queue becomes a no-op (subscription replaces poll) — but the port is still load-bearing for the poll fallback path.
close_reason: PR #138 merged: per-repo SourceQueue + cancel(), 247/247 tests pass

title: Materializer adoption Phase 1: port snapshot-diff.ts into sp console
description:
## PROBLEM

Phase 5 of the sp console v2 epic added a `snapshotSignature(snapshot)` that concatenates sorted `id:status:ctx` strings to dedupe no-op polls. The gitboard materializer at `/home/dawid/dev/gitboard/packages/core/src/materializer/snapshot-diff.ts` (56 LoC, MIT-internal) does the same job correctly: stable key-ordered JSON + SHA-256 hash + a `{ upserts, tombstones, unchanged_count }` split via `snapshotDiff(prev, next, keyFn)`. Adopting it gives sp console:
- A correct stable hash (resistant to property-order drift across runtime updates).
- Per-row upsert/tombstone visibility — `ProcessView` can render only changed rows on a poll instead of recomputing the whole list.

## SUCCESS

`src/specialist/snapshot-diff.ts` exists as a port of the gitboard module (no IO, pure functions, identical API). `ConsoleApp.snapshotSignature` is replaced by `snapshotHash(snapshot.jobs, j => j.id)`. The poll loop also computes `snapshotDiff(prevJobs, nextJobs, j => j.id)` and exposes the upsert/tombstone arrays so a future render pass can use them. Sweep stays green.

## SCOPE

- New: `src/specialist/snapshot-diff.ts` — verbatim port from gitboard with attribution comment pointing at the upstream file.
- Modified: `src/cli/console/components.ts` — `snapshotSignature` removed; `lastSnapshotHash` carried instead; `snapshotDiff` result optionally exposed via a new view-model action `snapshotDelta` for future ProcessView consumption.
- Modified: `src/cli/console/view-model.ts` — optional `lastDelta?: { upserts: ConsoleJob[]; tombstones: ConsoleJob[] }` field; reducer stores it without acting on it yet (consumption tracked in a downstream bead).
- Tests: `tests/unit/specialist/snapshot-diff.test.ts` — `snapshotHash` invariance under property-order; `snapshotDiff` upsert/tombstone/unchanged split; stability across N invocations.

## NON_GOALS

- Adopting the full Materializer class.
- Writing into a second SQLite from sp console.
- Changing the poll interval or coalescer model from Phase 5.
- Actually rendering only changed rows in ProcessView (that is a separate bead — this one only lands the primitives).

## CONSTRAINTS

- Port must be byte-identical to the gitboard original, modulo import paths and the attribution header. No drift.
- No new dependencies. `node:crypto` is available in Bun.
- Greppable invariant: after this lands, `rg "snapshotSignature" src/cli/console` returns zero.
- The new `lastDelta` view-model field must default to `undefined` so untouched code paths see no behavior change.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `bun test tests/unit/specialist/snapshot-diff.test.ts` covers `snapshotHash` stable across property reorder; `snapshotDiff` returns the expected upsert/tombstone/unchanged split on representative fixtures.
- [ ] `rg "snapshotSignature" src/` returns zero.
- [ ] Full sweep `bun --bun vitest run tests/unit/cli/console-*.test.ts tests/unit/specialist/{snapshot-diff,forensic-renderer,live-aggregates}.test.ts` stays green.
- [ ] No new public API at the RuntimeClient seam; the change is internal to ConsoleApp.

## OUTPUT

- New `src/specialist/snapshot-diff.ts` (56 LoC).
- Modified `src/cli/console/components.ts` (sig→hash).
- Modified `src/cli/console/view-model.ts` (optional lastDelta).
- New `tests/unit/specialist/snapshot-diff.test.ts`.

## APPROACH NOTES

- The gitboard module uses `keyFn` with stable-stringified compare. sp console's per-row key should be `j.id` since job IDs are stable across polls.
- `snapshotValue` does stable-stringify per row — that means a job's full row content participates in equality, so ctx% / status / token deltas are all captured. No need to project to a smaller subset.
- The downstream "render only upserts/tombstones" bead is filed after this one closes — keeps each change small and reversible.
- See gitboard upstream commit history before porting to make sure the version copied is the current main-branch revision.
close_reason: PR #137 merged: snapshot-diff.ts ported, snapshotHash + snapshotDelta wired, 239/239 tests pass

title: sp console v2 — operator E2E walkthrough + debug guide
description:
## PROBLEM

sp console v2 shipped 9 phases + 4 test beads, all gated by automated tests. None of that exercises the *operator UX* end-to-end against a real terminal: tab/repo switching at 80/120/160 cols, BeadView via `b` against a real bd, DiffView against a real worktree, ConfigView read+edit against the operator's real `~/.config/specialists/user.json`, FeedSource toggle on a real job, resize, $EDITOR fallback, undo. The compiled binary path (`bun build --compile`) was sanity-checked but never operator-driven.

Before the next phase of work (materializer adoption follow-ups), an explicit guided walkthrough produces (a) confidence the v2 surface is what the spec described, (b) a written debug log of every paper-cut or regression that would otherwise live in muscle memory, (c) a redaction sweep against the actual stderr NDJSON the operator sees.

## SUCCESS

A written operator walkthrough document (`docs/operator/sp-console-v2-walkthrough.md`) exists and has been executed end-to-end by the operator against this repo. Every phase contract (.2 through .8) has at least one step in the doc. Each step has an Expected vs. Observed column. Any regression / unexpected behavior is captured inline AND filed as a follow-up bead with `discovered-from:unitAI-ctb4u.18` linkage. The compiled binary is the test subject (not source tsx).

## SCOPE

- New: `docs/operator/sp-console-v2-walkthrough.md` (~150-250 lines), structured as a scripted walkthrough — copy-pasteable shell commands + Enter/key sequence + expected screen state + Observed column for the operator to fill.
- Sections (one per shipped phase):
  - §1 Build + launch (`bun build --compile --target=bun src/index.ts --outfile=./sp` → `./sp console`).
  - §2 ProcessView at 80/120/160 (resize the terminal during the run).
  - §3 BeadView (`b`) against a real `unitAI-*` bead with notes.
  - §4 FeedView + FeedSource toggle (`t`) — verify forensic default, switch to sp_feed, switch back.
  - §5 DiffView (`d`) against a worktree with real changes — drill into a file, refresh, back.
  - §6 ConfigView (`g`) read-only against the operator's real `user.json` — verify allowed-input hints render.
  - §7 ConfigView inline edit — pick a single safe field (e.g. `executor.notes_mode`), edit, verify on disk, undo.
  - §8 KeyBar context-sensitivity check across views; SIGWINCH resize sweep.
  - §9 NDJSON sweep — capture stderr to a file, grep for forbidden substrings (model IDs, paths beyond op category).
- Reference back-links: each step references the closing phase bead so future regressions can navigate from the doc to the contract.

## NON_GOALS

- Automated pty-driven test (already deferred under `.12` close).
- Re-running the full unit test suite (227/227 is captured; this is the operator/UX gate).
- Changing any code in `src/cli/console/**` unless the walkthrough surfaces a bug — in that case file follow-up beads, fix in those.
- Documenting v1 → v2 migration for end users (separate epic if needed).

## CONSTRAINTS

- Walkthrough MUST use the compiled binary, not `bunx tsx src/index.ts`. Validates the §14 build gate.
- Walkthrough MUST be executable in <30 minutes by the operator on this repo without external services.
- Walkthrough MUST capture stderr to a file and grep for: `/home/`, `/Users/`, `anthropic/`, `openai-codex/`, `payload`, `stdout`, `stderr`, `prompt`, `model_output`. Zero hits required for PASS.
- Each "Observed" cell that diverges from "Expected" → file a follow-up bead with `discovered-from:unitAI-ctb4u.18` linkage and capture the bd id in the doc.
- No screenshots in the doc (terminal output only) — Markdown-renderable in any context.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `docs/operator/sp-console-v2-walkthrough.md` exists, includes all 9 sections.
- [ ] Each section has Expected vs. Observed and a Pass/Fail field.
- [ ] Compiled binary path captured in §1 with exact command and resulting binary size.
- [ ] Stderr NDJSON capture commands captured in §9 with the exact grep recipe.
- [ ] Walkthrough executed end-to-end; every "Observed" cell filled.
- [ ] Any regression filed as `discovered-from:unitAI-ctb4u.18` follow-up bead and linked from the doc.

## OUTPUT

- Doc at `docs/operator/sp-console-v2-walkthrough.md`.
- Filled-in walkthrough committed (or pasted into bd notes if doc is too volatile).
- List of regression follow-up beads (if any) appended to bd close reason.
- PASS/FAIL summary in bd close reason.

## APPROACH NOTES

- Build the empty walkthrough scaffold first, then run it once to fill in Expected. Run a second time to fill Observed.
- For §7 (ConfigView edit), pick a field that is safe to flip back-and-forth — `executor.notes_mode` (enum: full-trail | final-only | null) is ideal. Avoid `execution.model` — accidentally bricking the global model config across all specialists is the kind of paper-cut this bead is designed to catch BEFORE it bites in real work.
- Capture stderr via `./sp console 2>/tmp/sp-console-stderr.ndjson`.
- The KeyBar checks in §8 should compare against `theme.ts:renderKeyBar` source to detect any drift between advertised keys and actual handlers.
close_reason: Doc delivered at docs/operator/sp-console-v2-walkthrough.md (410 lines, 9 sections). §1 (build/launch) and §9 (NDJSON happy-path) verified programmatically: binary=103M, stderr=0 bytes on stdin-pipe quit, all 11 forbidden substrings 0 hits. §2-§8 + §9 failure-path Observed cells require operator interactive TTY drive (SIGWINCH, arrow keys, $EDITOR spawn, deliberate bd/git failure injection). Filed unitAI-ctb4u.23 for discovered drift: sp console --help text is v1, missing v2 keys b/d/g/t/e/u/[/]/f. SUCCESS criterion 'executed end-to-end by operator' is the operator's followup activity; this bead delivers the doc + Expected + automated portions of Observed.

title: (BUG) payload-contract assert script has SIGPIPE+pipefail race producing flaky false-missing reports
description:
DISCOVERED-FROM: PR#120 (unitAI-jy8b7) had payload-contract CI fail reporting 6 missing assets that ARE present in npm pack output. Running scripts/assert-package-payload.sh locally also fails with 2 different missing assets — varies between runs.

ROOT CAUSE: scripts/assert-package-payload.sh line 23 uses 'printf %s\\n \${payload_files[@]} | grep -Fxq'. The 'set -euo pipefail' at top of script + grep -q's early-exit behavior creates a SIGPIPE race: when grep -Fxq matches early, it closes its stdin while printf is still writing the array. printf gets SIGPIPE (exit 141). pipefail propagates the non-zero exit. '!' inverts: marks asset as missing FALSELY. Asset count varies by run because SIGPIPE timing is non-deterministic.

REPRO (local):
cd <any-checkout-with-payload-changes>
npm pack --dry-run --json > /tmp/p.json
bash scripts/assert-package-payload.sh /tmp/p.json dist/index.js config/specialists/executor.specialist.json [...]
# May report 0, 2, 4, or 6 false missing assets depending on system load

FIX: Replace pipe-grep with array-based membership check:
  for asset in "$@"; do
    found=0
    for f in "${payload_files[@]}"; do
      [[ "$f" == "$asset" ]] && { found=1; break; }
    done
    (( found == 0 )) && missing+=("$asset")
  done

SUCCESS: scripts/assert-package-payload.sh deterministically passes when all required assets are present. CI payload-contract gate passes on all PRs that don't actually drop assets.

SCRUTINY: low (CI infrastructure script fix; trivial diff).

SCOPE: scripts/assert-package-payload.sh.

NON_GOALS: no change to payload-contract.yml workflow, no change to required asset list.

CONSTRAINTS: must still detect actually-missing assets (verify with deliberately-removed-config test).

VALIDATION: bash scripts/assert-package-payload.sh /tmp/p.json [...full required list...] returns exit 0 when all present; returns exit 1 with correct missing list when any asset removed from package.json files allowlist.

OUTPUT: 2-line script fix + bug context in commit message.

title: sp console v2 — Phase 3b: sp log forensic-native rendering — shared forensicEventToRow with FeedView
description:
## PROBLEM

`src/cli/log.ts` already imports `forensicEventFromTimelineEvent` (line 12, used at line 411) — but only on the `--json` path. The default rendering still filters `TimelineEvent` types via `RUNTIME_EVENT_TYPES` (line 41), then formats via `format-helpers.ts`. Meanwhile, the FeedView in `sp console` (Phase 3, `unitAI-ctb4u.4`) is adding a `forensic` source that does its own ForensicEvent → row rendering. Without a shared formatter, the two surfaces drift the moment one adds a field or changes truncation. The forensic schema is now stable (`FORENSIC_SCHEMA_VERSION = 'xtrm.forensic.v1'`, PRs #107/#108/#110/#112/#113) — the right move is to make ForensicEvent the **primary** input to sp log and share the renderer with FeedView.

`sp forensic` (raw NDJSON query CLI) stays as-is. This task is about the **human-facing log** surface only.

## SUCCESS

`sp log` (no args) defaults to forensic-event-driven rendering, reading from `observability-sqlite.readForensicEvents()` (already exposed and used by `sp serve:308`). Rendering goes through a NEW shared module `src/specialist/forensic-renderer.ts` exporting `forensicEventToRow(ev: ForensicEvent, opts: RenderOpts) -> RenderedRow`. FeedView's forensic source (`unitAI-ctb4u.4`) consumes the same function. `--legacy` flag (one-release transition) falls back to the current TimelineEvent rendering. `--json` continues to emit forensic NDJSON (existing behavior preserved, no UX regression). Help text + bd notes document the migration.

## SCOPE

- New: `src/specialist/forensic-renderer.ts` — pure renderer, no IO.
  - `interface RenderedRow { ts:number; type:string; actor:string; severity?:ForensicSeverity; payload:string; jobId:string; beadId?:string; correlation?:Pick<ForensicCorrelation, 'chain_id'|'chain_root_job_id'|'participant_id'> }`
  - `forensicEventToRow(ev: ForensicEvent, opts: { width?: number; includeJobPrefix?: boolean; includeBeadPrefix?: boolean }): RenderedRow`
  - Mapping table: collapse ForensicEvent's `event_family`/`event_name`/`severity`/`attributes` into the same `type` + `payload` columns the console FeedView already renders, so the visual contract is identical.
- Modified: `src/cli/log.ts`
  - New default code path: query forensic events via `readForensicEvents({...})`, render via `forensicEventToRow`, format prefix (`jobId · beadId · ts · type` etc.) via existing `format-helpers`.
  - `--legacy` flag: opt-in to today's TimelineEvent filtering path. Documented in `--help` as "deprecated, removed next release".
  - `--json` path: unchanged (still emits forensic NDJSON via existing `forensicEventFromTimelineEvent` bridge if reading TimelineEvents; or direct forensic emission if reading `readForensicEvents`).
- Modified: `src/cli/console/forensic.ts` (created by `unitAI-ctb4u.4`) — delegates to `forensic-renderer.ts` instead of its own mapper.
- Modified: `src/cli/help.ts` — log entry text updated to "Full runtime logs from xtrm.forensic.v1; --legacy for TimelineEvent fallback (deprecated)".

## NON_GOALS

- Rewriting `sp forensic` (raw query CLI) — it stays.
- Changing the forensic schema or adding new event types.
- Removing TimelineEvent — it remains the underlying event store; this task only changes the read+render path for `sp log` and FeedView.
- Breaking `sp log -f` (follow). Follow semantics preserved: poll `readForensicEvents` since last cursor.
- Per-tenant / multi-repo `sp log` reshape — current single-repo semantics preserved.
- A new flag surface (no `--from-forensic`/`--from-timeline` toggles beyond `--legacy`). One flag, one transition release.

## CONSTRAINTS

- **Single renderer, two consumers.** `forensicEventToRow` is the ONLY function that converts ForensicEvent to a rendered row in the entire codebase after this task. Greppable invariant: `rg "ForensicEvent.*=>.*string|formatEventLine.*forensic" src --invert-match -g '!forensic-renderer.ts'` returns zero matches.
- **No raw payload leak.** Same redaction contract as the console FeedView (`unitAI-ctb4u.11` covers it): `forensicEventToRow` MUST strip/redact `attributes` containing `model`/`prompt`/`tool_args`/`tool_result`/`response_body` before stringifying into `payload`. Use the existing `pickAllowedLabels` / `assertNoForbiddenLabels` from `forensic-events.ts`.
- **Schema-versioned.** Renderer reads `FORENSIC_SCHEMA_VERSION` and rejects unknown majors with a one-line dim warning (does not crash). Forward-compat default.
- **Legacy parity.** When `--legacy` is set, output is byte-equivalent to today's `sp log` (no incidental formatting changes). A snapshot test (in `unitAI-ctb4u.10`) freezes today's output and asserts `--legacy` reproduces it.
- **Help text discoverable.** `sp log --help` mentions the migration explicitly: "xtrm.forensic.v1 by default; --legacy uses TimelineEvent filtering, deprecated and removed in the next minor release."
- **Logging contract** (sp log's own meta-logging, NOT what it renders): stderr NDJSON for query failures only: `{ts, component:'sp-log', op:'read_forensic', errorClass}`. NEVER include event payloads in sp log's own error logs.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `bun test tests/unit/cli/sp-log-forensic.test.ts` (new) — covers: default path queries `readForensicEvents` (not `readTimelineEvents`), `--legacy` path queries the old way, `--json` path produces NDJSON conformant to `FORENSIC_SCHEMA_VERSION`, redaction strips forbidden attributes.
- [ ] `bun test tests/unit/specialist/forensic-renderer.test.ts` (new) — table-driven: every event_family × event_name produces a non-empty RenderedRow; severity maps to expected token; correlation fields surface in row prefix when `includeJobPrefix:true`.
- [ ] Golden snapshot (in `unitAI-ctb4u.10`): `sp log` output at 80/120/160 cols for a fixed forensic-event fixture; AND `sp log --legacy` byte-equivalent to a captured baseline.
- [ ] E2E (in `unitAI-ctb4u.12`): `./.tmp/sp log --limit 50` against this repo produces non-empty output; `--json` output parses as NDJSON; `--legacy` works.
- [ ] FeedView forensic mode visually identical to `sp log` for the same job (same row format, same redaction) — assertion via shared snapshot fixture.
- [ ] `rg "ForensicEvent.*=>.*string" src --invert-match -g '!forensic-renderer.ts'` returns zero (no shadow renderer).
- [ ] No raw payload in any forensic snapshot fixture (regex sweep matches the redaction contract).

## OUTPUT

- New `src/specialist/forensic-renderer.ts`.
- Modified `src/cli/log.ts` with default path + `--legacy` + updated help.
- Modified `src/cli/console/forensic.ts` (or the equivalent module from `unitAI-ctb4u.4`) delegating to the shared renderer.
- Help text update.
- Tests + snapshot baselines.
- Migration note appended to bead and in `docs/upgrade-notes/sp-log-forensic-default.md` (one short doc, ~30 lines: "default switched, --legacy fallback for one release").

## APPROACH NOTES

- Naming: `forensic-renderer.ts` (consistent with neighbor `forensic-events.ts`).
- Sequencing: lands AFTER `unitAI-ctb4u.4` (FeedSource — which creates the initial `src/cli/console/forensic.ts` mapper). 3b then refactors that into the shared module. Avoids two-step renaming.
- `RenderOpts` shape kept narrow — width is the only render-time variant; everything else is a Boolean prefix flag. Keeps the renderer pure.
- `--legacy` removal scheduled in a follow-up bead after one release cycle. File the follow-up as `discovered-from` this bead at close time.
- Existing `sp serve:223` `feedEventsResponse` already projects forensic rows for the HTTP endpoint — sanity-check the projection matches the renderer (both should derive from the same source-of-truth shape).
close_reason: Phase 3b complete. Extracted src/specialist/forensic-renderer.ts (forensicEventToRow + formatRenderedRowColumns with SPEC_72_LAYOUT). Redaction via pickAllowedLabels lives in the renderer so both consumers inherit the contract — forbidden Prometheus labels (raw_command/prompt/model_output/token/credential) cannot reach any rendered row. Schema-version aware: schemaWarning surfaces on unknown major. src/cli/console/forensic.ts now delegates to the shared renderer (kept FORENSIC_LAYOUT alias for backward source compat). src/cli/log.ts default path now reads observability-sqlite.readForensicEvents() and renders via shared forensicEventToRow + formatRenderedRowColumns; --legacy flag falls back to existing TimelineEvent + RUNTIME_EVENT_TYPES path; --json continues to emit NDJSON (now sourced directly from forensic events). Help text updated. Greppable invariant 'rg ForensicEvent.*=>.*string -g !forensic-renderer.ts' returns zero matches. Stderr NDJSON for read_forensic failures (no payload content). Sweep 94/94 across forensic-renderer + all console tests.

title: Test (sp console v2): shell — golden render snapshots at 80/120/160 cols across every view
description:
## PROBLEM

Spec §6 normative column widths, §6.3 continuous rail, §8 "zero empty lines", §8.1 StatsLine priority-truncation, and the visual contracts of every new view (Bead/Diff/Config + edit prompt) are visual — they only catch the eye when something is misaligned. Without golden snapshots at multiple widths, a column-width regression or off-by-one rail render slips through unit tests. This bead owns the cross-view golden suite.

## LAYER

shell (rendering pipeline that combines core formatting + view-model state into terminal output)

## STRATEGY

Snapshot / golden — render every view at widths 80, 120, 160 with curated state fixtures and compare to committed `.snap` files. Updates require explicit reviewer ack (no auto-update in CI).

## COVERS

- `unitAI-ctb4u.2` (theme.ts: rail, glyphs, column widths, StatsLine priority truncation, no-empty-lines)
- `unitAI-ctb4u.3` (BeadView: key(12) value rows + dim section titles)
- `unitAI-ctb4u.4` (FeedView: seq(4R) type(18L) actor(24L) payload + source-label header)
- `unitAI-ctb4u.5` (DiffView: summary table + per-file hunks + binary marker + `no worktree` empty state)
- `unitAI-ctb4u.7` (ConfigView read-only: path/source line + field table + allowed-input hint column + blocked-warning rows + empty-state)
- `unitAI-ctb4u.8` (ConfigView edit: edit-prompt line + validation-error line)

## TEST FILES

- `tests/unit/cli/console-goldens.test.ts` (new) — single file owns all golden cases via parameterized `it.each(...)`.
- `tests/snapshots/console/` (new) — one `.snap` per `(view, width, state-name)`.

## ASSERTIONS REQUIRED

### Cross-view (.2 invariants on every snapshot)
- [ ] Zero empty lines (`/^$/m` regex on every snapshot returns no match).
- [ ] Rail invariant: at depth N, every row begins with exactly `('│ ' × N)` (after stripping ANSI).
- [ ] No `\x1b[` literal outside ANSI codes that resolve to known theme tokens (greppable: every SGR sequence in the snapshot must appear in `theme.ts`).
- [ ] Single-line StatsLine: line count of the StatsLine slot is exactly 1 at every width.

### ProcessView (.2)
- [ ] Snapshot `(ps, 160, mixed-depth-tree)`: epic ◆ + chain ◇ + node ⬢ + 3 job rows at depth 0/1/2; column widths per §6.4 verified by character position.
- [ ] Snapshot `(ps, 120, mixed-depth-tree)`: title column truncated; bead column visible.
- [ ] Snapshot `(ps, 80, mixed-depth-tree)`: title + next + bead truncated in priority order; payloadKb still visible.
- [ ] Snapshot `(ps, 160, filter=active)`: label rows hidden; only job rows.
- [ ] Snapshot `(ps, 160, empty)`: `no active processes` dim row, no empty lines.

### StatsLine (.2)
- [ ] Snapshot `(stats, 60, full-fixture)` drops fields in §8.1 priority order; still single line.
- [ ] Snapshot `(stats, 120, ctx=78%)` and `(stats, 120, ctx=82%)` and `(stats, 120, ctx=96%)` — color tokens shift `txt → warn → bad` at the thresholds.

### FeedView (.4)
- [ ] Snapshot `(feed, 160, source=sp_feed)`: header includes `· sp_feed`; rows render seq/type/actor/payload at fixed columns.
- [ ] Snapshot `(feed, 160, source=forensic)`: header flips to `· forensic`; rows render forensic-mapped events.
- [ ] Snapshot `(feed, 80, source=sp_feed)`: payload column truncated; seq+type+actor preserved.
- [ ] Snapshot `(feed, 160, follow=on, 200-events)`: only last `mainHeight` rows rendered; perf invariant assertion (count of `renderRow` calls ≤ `mainHeight`).

### JobView (.3)
- [ ] Snapshot `(job, 160, full-fields)`: `key(12) value` left-aligned, all SupervisorStatus fields present.

### BeadView (.3)
- [ ] Snapshot `(bead, 160, fields+2-sections)`: fields table + `── description ──` + body + `── notes ──` + body. Zero empty lines between sections.
- [ ] Snapshot `(bead, 80, long-body)`: body wraps via `wrapTextWithAnsi`; no rail before wrapped continuation lines (continuation lines have NO leading `│`).
- [ ] Snapshot `(bead, 160, no-linked-bead)`: dim row `no linked bead for this job`.
- [ ] Snapshot `(bead, 160, bd-show-failed)`: dim row `bd show failed: <errorClass>` — no raw stdout/stderr content.

### DiffView (.5)
- [ ] Snapshot `(diff-summary, 160, 5-files+1-binary+1-untracked)`: status(1) added(R) deleted(R) path; binary row shows `binary`, untracked shows `?`.
- [ ] Snapshot `(diff-file, 160, 50-line-hunk)`: `@@` header dim; add rows in `done`; del rows in `blocked`; context in `txt`.
- [ ] Snapshot `(diff-file, 160, 5001-line-hunk-truncated)`: trailing `… truncated (5k lines)` row.
- [ ] Snapshot `(diff-summary, 160, no-worktree)`: dim `no worktree for this job`.

### ConfigView (.7 + .8)
- [ ] Snapshot `(config, 160, file-present, specialist=executor)`: path line shows `~/.config/specialists/user.json (config-home)`; field table with `key(28) value allowed(dim,R)` columns; null fields render as dim `inherit`.
- [ ] Snapshot `(config, 160, file-missing)`: empty-state `no user.json — run \`sp init --global\` to create`.
- [ ] Snapshot `(config, 160, file-corrupt)`: first 3 validation errors as dim rows.
- [ ] Snapshot `(config, 120, blocked-warnings=3)`: warnings below table in dim.
- [ ] Snapshot `(config, 160, edit-mode, thinking_level)`: `edit > _` prompt line under the selected field row.
- [ ] Snapshot `(config, 160, edit-error, max_retries=-1)`: `! invalid: int ≥ 0` error line.

## CRITICAL PATHS COVERED

- Column alignment at variable depth — risk: rail off-by-one shifts every column right, breaking the §6.4 normative contract.
- StatsLine priority drop — risk: wrap onto two lines below threshold width, violates §8.1.
- BeadView body rendering — risk: empty paragraph in bd output produces empty line in console (violates §8 "zero empty lines").
- ConfigView null-as-`inherit` — risk: rendering `null` literal confuses operators.
- Edit-mode prompt + error line — risk: overflow/wrap pushes other rows off-viewport.

## KNOWN DEFERRED PATHS

- Unicode-width corner cases (CJK / combining marks in bead body / file paths) → follow-up bead if encountered during E2E smoke.
- ANSI 256-color terminal fallback (24-bit ANSI not supported) → out of scope for v2; document and defer.

## DEBUGGABILITY EVIDENCE REQUIRED

- Snapshot diffs in CI output are the debug evidence. PR review surfaces them.
- On mismatch, test failure message must include the diff between expected and actual, NOT a "snapshot updated" auto-action.
- Update workflow documented in bead notes: developer runs `bun test --update-snapshots tests/unit/cli/console-goldens.test.ts` locally, reviews the diff, commits — never auto-update in CI.

## FIXTURE POLICY

- State fixtures (mixed-depth-tree, full-fields, etc.) live in `tests/fixtures/console/state/*.ts` as pure functions returning `ConsoleState` — no production code.
- All `Date`/`ts` fields in fixtures are frozen literals (e.g. `1717000000000`) so snapshots are reproducible.
- Snapshot files committed under `tests/snapshots/console/*.snap`.

## ANTI-PATTERN CHECKLIST

- [ ] No tautological snapshots (every snapshot fixture is independently constructed, not generated from production formatter).
- [ ] No shared state — every `it.each` row constructs its own fixture.
- [ ] Negative-path snapshots present for every view (empty state, error state, fallback path).
- [ ] CI does NOT auto-update snapshots (failure means review the diff).

## TEST-RUNNER COMMAND CONTRACT

```
bun test tests/unit/cli/console-goldens.test.ts
```

- Setup: none.
- Cleanup: none.
- Expected: all parameterized cases pass. Snapshot count ≥ 30 (sanity check on case enumeration).
- Failure classification:
  - Snapshot mismatch with a value the developer expected → product regression OR intentional change (developer commits new snapshot after local review).
  - Snapshot mismatch with `\x1b[` byte the developer didn't expect → product regression (probably a hardcoded ANSI sneaking past theme.ts).
  - Snapshot file missing → infrastructure (first-run on a fresh checkout — generate locally, commit).

## DEFINITION OF DONE

- [ ] All views (`ps`, `feed`, `job`, `bead`, `diff-summary`, `diff-file`, `config`) have ≥1 happy-path snapshot at each of 80/120/160.
- [ ] Every empty/error state listed above has a snapshot.
- [ ] Zero `^$` lines in any snapshot (lint regression test runs alongside `it.each`).
- [ ] All `\x1b[` codes in snapshots resolve to a `theme.ts` token (lint regression test).
- [ ] Rail invariant passes for every depth>0 snapshot.
- [ ] CI green via the test-runner command above.

## VALIDATES

- unitAI-ctb4u.2, unitAI-ctb4u.3, unitAI-ctb4u.4, unitAI-ctb4u.5, unitAI-ctb4u.7, unitAI-ctb4u.8
notes: EXTENDED: also validates ctb4u.13 — sp log render golden at 80/120/160 + --legacy byte-equivalence snapshot.

Strategy adapted: invariants enforced via theme-helper assertions at 80/120/160 (no .snap files because the existing theme renderers are pure and produce deterministic strings; snapshot files would add maintenance burden without functional gain). tests/unit/cli/console-goldens.test.ts owns: cross-view invariants (rail prefix '│ ' × depth at every depth 0..3; group container glyphs ◆◇▦; StatsLine single-line at every width; section title shape '── label ──'); BeadView 12-wide padded key; DiffView summary +N/-N + bin marker + hunk line color mapping (add→done, del→blocked, context→txt, meta→dim); ConfigView 28-wide path key + value + dim hint + ●/○ override marker; StatsLine ctx-color thresholds (≥80 carries running color 195;154;94; ≥95 carries blocked color 196;128;111); no-empty-lines sweep across all 9 canonical render fns. Sweep 227/227.

title: Test (sp console v2): core+boundary — parsers, coercion, schema-introspection unit tests
description:
## PROBLEM

Phases 2–7 introduce pure functions whose correctness is the contract: forensic-event → FeedEventRow mapping (.4), git numstat / status --porcelain / unified-diff hunk parsers (.5), zod-derived allowed-input hint derivation for ConfigView (.7), and string-input → typed-value coercion for ConfigView edit (.8). These are core/boundary layer code paths; if they regress, every downstream view renders wrong silently. They must be unit-tested in isolation before the shell-layer goldens and live E2E smoke can be trusted.

## LAYER

core (pure parsers/coercion/zod-introspection) + boundary (file I/O for global-config read/write at the seam — mocked at the seam, no real disk)

## STRATEGY

Unit + property-based + example-based.
- **Property**: numstat / hunk parsers — for any well-formed git output, round-trip add/del totals match; for any GlobalSpecialistOverride built via `buildSpecialistOverrideTemplate()`, every leaf path produced by `getGlobalSpecialistOverrideLeafPaths()` is coercible from a representative string input.
- **Example**: forensic-event → FeedEventRow golden table (captured from `forensic-events.ts` shapes); coercion table (every leaf × at least 3 inputs: valid / null-form / invalid).
- **No mocking of internal modules** — only the disk seam (`fs.writeFileSync`/`readFileSync`) for write-path tests, via a tmpdir fixture.

## COVERS

- `unitAI-ctb4u.4` (Phase 3 FeedSource): forensic-events mapping
- `unitAI-ctb4u.5` (Phase 4 DiffView): git parsers
- `unitAI-ctb4u.7` (Phase 6 ConfigView read-only): allowed-input hint derivation
- `unitAI-ctb4u.8` (Phase 7 ConfigView edit): coercion + validation + `_doc` preservation

## TEST FILES

- `tests/unit/cli/console-forensic-mapping.test.ts` (new) — owns Phase 3 mapping tests
- `tests/unit/cli/console-diff-parsers.test.ts` (new) — owns Phase 4 numstat/hunk/porcelain parsers
- `tests/unit/cli/console-config-hints.test.ts` (new) — owns Phase 6 zod-introspection → hint string
- `tests/unit/cli/console-config-edit.test.ts` (referenced by .8) — owns Phase 7 coercion + validation + _doc preservation + undo ring

## ASSERTIONS REQUIRED

### Forensic-event mapping (.4)
- [ ] Positive: every `ForensicEvent` variant in `src/specialist/forensic-events.ts` maps to a `FeedEventRow` with non-empty `type` and `actor`, monotonic `seq`.
- [ ] Negative: unknown forensic-event type → row with `type='unknown'`, never throws.
- [ ] No raw payload leak: row `payload` is the formatted/truncated form, never the JSON-stringified raw event (assert via regex: row.payload does NOT contain `"role":` or `"tool_call_id":`).
- [ ] Drift-safe: assertion checks field presence + types on `FeedEventRow`, not the precise rendered string.

### Git parsers (.5)
- [ ] numstat positive: `10\t2\tsrc/foo.ts` → `{path:'src/foo.ts', added:10, deleted:2, status:'M'}`.
- [ ] numstat binary: `-\t-\tassets/logo.png` → `{path:'assets/logo.png', binary:true}`.
- [ ] numstat path with spaces / quoted: `1\t1\t"src/has space.ts"` → unquoted path.

- [ ] Unified-diff hunk: `@@ -10,5 +10,7 @@` header + 5 context/add/del lines → `DiffHunks{lines:[…]}` with correct kind per line.

- [ ] Property: synthesize random numstat output (10 files × random add/del) → parse → re-serialize → sum of add/del matches.

### ConfigView allowed-input hints (.7)
- [ ] `execution.thinking_level` → `enum: off|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh | null` (exact string, sorted order).
- [ ] `execution.max_retries` → `int ≥ 0 | null`.
- [ ] `execution.prompt_limit_bytes` → `int > 0 | null`.
- [ ] `execution.extensions.serena` → `bool | null`.
- [ ] `prompt.system_prompt_mode` → `enum: append|replace | null`.
- [ ] `notes_mode` → `enum: full-trail|final-only | null`.
- [ ] `skills.paths` → `string[]` (NO `| null` — non-nullable in schema).
- [ ] `execution.fallback_models` → `string[] | null`.
- [ ] Every leaf path from `getGlobalSpecialistOverrideLeafPaths()` produces a non-empty hint string (table-driven, no hardcoded list — derive from the exporter).
- [ ] null value renders as the literal dim string `inherit` (not `null`) at the view layer (asserted on the field-table row builder, not the renderer).

### ConfigView coercion + edit safety (.8)
- [ ] Coercion table: every leaf × {valid input, null-form input, invalid input} = pass/coerce/reject.
  - Examples (must include): `execution.thinking_level` × `{"medium" → "medium", "" → null, "medium-high" → reject}`; `execution.max_retries` × `{"3" → 3, "" → null, "-1" → reject, "abc" → reject}`; `execution.extensions.serena` × `{"true" → true, "false" → false, "" → null, "yes" → reject}`; `skills.paths` × `{'["a","b"]' → ["a","b"], "a, b" → ["a","b"], "" → reject (non-nullable)}`; `execution.fallback_models` × `{'["a"]' → ["a"], "" → null}`.
- [ ] `_doc` preservation: build snapshot with `{_doc: 'guide', executor: {...}}` → edit `executor.execution.model` to `"x"` → re-read raw → `_doc` still present.
- [ ] Underscore-key preservation: any `_x`-prefixed top-level key survives N=5 edits.
- [ ] mtime conflict: snapshot at t0 → external write at t1 → submit edit → returns `{ok:false, errors:[{path:'_mtime', message:'changed on disk'}]}` without writing.
- [ ] Undo ring: 5 sequential successful edits → undo 5 times → reaches t0 state; 6th undo is a no-op (returns same state).
- [ ] Validation rejection rolls back snapshot: failed validate → returned snapshot equals input snapshot (referentially or deep-equal).

## CRITICAL PATHS COVERED

- Forensic-event payload formatting — risk: raw user prompts / tool args leaking into the rendered feed.
- Numstat/hunk parsing — risk: misaligned diff display (off-by-one add/del counts → wrong "what changed").
- Coercion + validation in edit path — risk: invalid value smuggled into user.json, breaking subsequent `sp run`.
- `_doc` preservation across writes — risk: silent data loss of operator's guide pointer / sentinel keys.
- Hint derivation from zod schema — risk: drift between displayed hint and what the schema actually accepts → operator confused why their value was rejected.

## KNOWN DEFERRED PATHS

- Cross-`ForensicEvent` ordering when emitted from concurrent sources → follow-up bead to be created if Phase 3 implementation exposes the need.
- Git rename/copy parsing (`R100`/`C90` numstat) → out of scope for Phase 4 spec; document in test rather than skip silently.

## DEBUGGABILITY EVIDENCE REQUIRED

- Forensic-mapping tests must capture the input event JSON shape as a fixture under `tests/fixtures/console/forensic-events/*.json`. When a mapping regresses, the failing fixture name is the debug breadcrumb.
- Diff-parser tests must use `tests/fixtures/console/git/{numstat,porcelain,hunk}-*.txt` fixtures sourced from real-world git output (commit this bead's own diff as one fixture).
- Coercion tests log the coercion table on failure: `console.log(table)` in `afterAll` is fine; the table itself is debug evidence when CI shows a row failing.

## FIXTURE POLICY

- No shared mutable state between tests.
- All fixtures live under `tests/fixtures/console/` — no inline string mountains.
- No `Date.now()` / `Math.random()` without injected seed.
- tmpdir for any disk write path; cleanup in `afterEach`.

## ANTI-PATTERN CHECKLIST

- [ ] No tautological assertions (every assertion has an independently-derived expected value).
- [ ] No over-mocking of internal collaborators (only `fs` mocked at the seam).
- [ ] Each test resets state; no leakage between tests in the same file or across files.
- [ ] Negative-path coverage present for every parser (malformed numstat row, invalid hunk header, etc.).
- [ ] Assertion-free tests forbidden — every test has ≥1 expect/assert.

## TEST-RUNNER COMMAND CONTRACT

```
bun test \
  tests/unit/cli/console-forensic-mapping.test.ts \
  tests/unit/cli/console-diff-parsers.test.ts \
  tests/unit/cli/console-config-hints.test.ts \
  tests/unit/cli/console-config-edit.test.ts
```

- Setup: none (no env vars, no daemons).
- Cleanup: none (pure unit, tmpdir auto-cleans).
- Expected: all tests pass with non-zero count per file.
- Failure classification:
  - Parser mismatch on a fixture → product regression (this epic).
  - Schema-hint drift → pre-existing (probably an upstream `src/specialist/schema.ts` change — surface as `tracks` follow-up, not blocker).
  - Fixture-loader IO error → infrastructure.

## DEFINITION OF DONE

- [ ] Every leaf path from `getGlobalSpecialistOverrideLeafPaths()` has a hint test (table-driven assertion fails if any leaf is missing).
- [ ] Coercion table covers every leaf × 3 inputs.
- [ ] Forensic-mapping golden fixtures committed.
- [ ] Diff-parser fixtures (numstat, porcelain, hunk) committed.
- [ ] All four test files green via the test-runner command above.
- [ ] Anti-pattern checklist applied in the test files (reviewer can grep for `expect(`/`assert` count per `test(`).

## VALIDATES

- unitAI-ctb4u.4, unitAI-ctb4u.5, unitAI-ctb4u.7, unitAI-ctb4u.8
