After Phases 0-3 land, the global user.json gets many new knobs (system_prompt_mode, extensions, notes_mode, output_file, prompt/stdout limits, fallback_models, @preset/<name> refs). The current `sp init --global` (src/cli/init.ts:881+) emits the template via `buildGlobalUserConfigTemplate` and a console block telling the user how to edit it — but the file itself has no inline guidance. With more fields, the user.json becomes opaque without context: it's just keys with `null` values.

The user-facing CLI output and the upgrade docs need to surface what each new knob does. Without this, the work in Phases 0-3 is invisible to users until they read the source.

## SUCCESS

- `sp init --global` console output references each new knob category (extensions opt-out, system_prompt_mode, fallback chains, preset refs) with a one-line "for X, set Y to Z" hint.
- `sp init --global` does NOT inject comments into user.json (it's strict JSON, no comments). Instead, the user.json gets a top-level `_doc` key with a one-line pointer to the upgrade-notes path; loader tolerates this (it's ignored by the schema since it's a `_`-prefixed sentinel, not a specialist name — verify the loader skips `_`-prefixed keys).

  - Overview: what this expansion adds (six allowlisted fields + chains + preset refs).

  - Preset reference syntax: how to write `@preset/<name>`, where presets live, depth cap, cycle behavior.
  - Fallback chain semantics: singular vs plural, precedence, when each chain step fires.
  - Migration: how existing user.json files auto-extend on next `sp init --global`.

## SCOPE

- src/specialist/global-config.ts: add tolerance for `_`-prefixed top-level keys in `GlobalUserConfigSchema` (so `_doc` doesn't fail validation). Probably swap `z.record(z.string(), GlobalSpecialistOverrideSchema)` for a refined record that filters `_`-prefixed keys at parse OR uses a discriminated shape. Choose the smaller change. title: Phase 2: Fallback model chains (string | string[]) with multi-step runtime walk
description:
## PROBLEM

`fallback_model` is currently singular: `z.string().nullable().optional()` in `SpecialistSchema` (src/specialist/schema.ts:19) and in `OverrideExecutionSchema` (src/specialist/global-config.ts:69). The runtime (src/specialist/runner.ts:946 and src/specialist/script-runner.ts:514) treats it as a single fallback. A user with multi-provider quota (anthropic + openai-codex + nano-gpt) cannot express "try anthropic, fall back to openai-codex, fall back to nano-gpt" without forking the specialist.

The asymmetry is small but ergonomically real: every spec-load on a flaky-provider day requires the user to either (a) manually fork the spec to a chain shape that doesn't exist, or (b) accept the single-fallback ceiling and hope that one secondary is up.

## SUCCESS

A user can set `execution.fallback_models: ["openai-codex/gpt-5.4", "nano-gpt/moonshotai/kimi-k2.5"]` in their `~/.config/specialists/user.json` and the runtime walks the chain top-to-bottom on transient failure (rate limit, 5xx, network), only giving up after every step fails. Existing `fallback_model: "openai-codex/gpt-5.4"` (singular) continues to work unchanged — it's treated as the head of a single-element chain.

Schema accepts both shapes:
- `fallback_model: "openai-codex/gpt-5.4"` (singular, legacy — keeps working)
- `fallback_models: ["openai-codex/gpt-5.4", "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6"]` (new, plural)
- If BOTH are set in the same layer, plural wins; document this precedence.

Observability: each fallback step emits a structured event `event=fallback_step, attempt_n, model_tried, error_class` so the user can see why a chain step was taken.

## SCOPE

- src/specialist/schema.ts: extend `ExecutionSchema` with `fallback_models: z.array(z.string()).nullable().optional()`; add `fallback_models` to `OVERRIDE_ALLOWED_EXECUTION_FIELDS`.
- src/specialist/global-config.ts: mirror in `OverrideExecutionSchema` (`fallback_models: z.array(z.string()).nullable()`) and in `buildSpecialistOverrideTemplate` (defaulted `null`).
- src/specialist/runner.ts:946 (`executionFallbackModel` read site): replace single-string assumption with an ordered chain resolver helper.
- src/specialist/script-runner.ts:514 (the `candidates` array): same helper feeds the same chain.
- NEW helper (probably src/specialist/model-chain.ts): `resolveModelChain(execution) → string[]` that returns `[primary, ...plural_or_singular_fallbacks]`. Plural wins when both set. Logs precedence at debug.
- Runtime fallback loop: wherever today's code retries on transient failure (find it via gitnexus_impact on the existing `fallback_model` reads), iterate the chain.
- tests/unit/specialist/{loader,schema,model-chain}.test.ts: schema acceptance of both shapes; resolver precedence; chain walk under simulated transient failures.

## NON_GOALS

- Smart routing (cost-aware, latency-aware, quota-aware) — that's a separate feature.
- Per-task chain (different chain for review vs codegen) — separate feature.
- Auto-discovery of available providers — user lists what they want explicitly.
- Promoting `fallback_model` to also accept an array shape (we add `fallback_models` as the array form; singular `fallback_model` stays singular for backward compat). This avoids the union-type complexity in the existing field.
- Modifying preset format to express chains in `config/presets.json` (defer to Phase 3 if needed — for now presets stay singular-model).

## CONSTRAINTS

- Phase 0 (unitAI-gp7nq.1) MUST be merged first.
- `fallback_model` (singular) MUST remain accepted for at least one minor version after this lands, so existing user files migrate naturally.
- Precedence when both `fallback_model` and `fallback_models` are set in the same layer: plural wins. Document loudly in the upgrade note. (Cross-layer mixing — singular in package canonical + plural in user override — must also have a defined semantics. Recommended: plural in any layer replaces the singular chain entirely, because mixing them is incoherent.)
- The runtime fallback loop must be transient-failure-only. NEVER walk the chain on a logical error (4xx model-rejected-prompt). Use the existing error-class taxonomy in src/pi/ (or wherever the transient classifier lives). Run gitnexus_query for "transient retry classify" before touching the loop.
- Telemetry: emit a structured event per chain step. Log fields: `event=fallback_step, specialist, attempt_n (1-indexed), model_tried, error_class, terminal (true if last)`. Verify the event lands in observability.db via the standard pipeline; smoke command must grep this in `sp log`.
- gitnexus_impact required before editing runner.ts:946 — this is on every specialist's dispatch path. Report risk in handoff.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Schema test: `fallback_model: "x"` parses; `fallback_models: ["x", "y"]` parses; both-set is accepted and resolver returns plural.
- [ ] Resolver unit test: `resolveModelChain({model: "p", fallback_models: ["a","b"]})` returns `["p","a","b"]`; with only singular returns `["p","f"]`; with neither returns `["p"]`.
- [ ] Runtime test (probably in runner.test.ts): chain walk on simulated transient — first model rejected with 503 → second model dispatched → assertion on observability event sequence.
- [ ] Regression: existing tests using `fallback_model` singular pass without change.
- [ ] `bun run lint && bun run build && bun --bun vitest run tests/unit/specialist/` clean.
- [ ] Smoke: user.json with `fallback_models: ["bad-provider/bad-model", "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6"]` for a READ_ONLY spec (e.g. explorer or echo); dispatch live; observe `fallback_step` events in `sp log <job-id>`; final dispatch model is `claude-sonnet-4-6`.
- [ ] gitnexus_impact evidence on `runner.ts` and `script-runner.ts` fallback sites recorded in handoff.

## OUTPUT

Handoff lists: schema additions, resolver helper signature, the two runtime edit sites with gitnexus_impact summary, the live smoke output (annotated to show the chain step events), and the precedence rule for singular+plural mixing.

title: Phase 1: Allowlist user-environment fields (system_prompt_mode, extensions, notes_mode, output_file, prompt/stdout limits)
description:
## PROBLEM

Six fields already exist in `SpecialistSchema` (src/specialist/schema.ts) as user-environment knobs but are silently dropped if a user sets them in `~/.config/specialists/user.json`, because none are in the override allowlist:

- `execution.system_prompt_mode` (append|replace) — controls how the spec's `prompt.system` composes with pi's system prompt. Mode of composition, NOT prompt content.
- `execution.extensions.serena` (boolean) — opt-out for Serena LSP injection; per-user RAM/extensions choice.
- `execution.extensions.gitnexus` (boolean) — opt-out for GitNexus extension injection.
- `notes_mode` (full-trail | final-only) — bead-notes verbosity preference.
- `output_file` (string) — where the result is mirrored (per-user FS preference).
- `execution.prompt_limit_bytes` (number) — host resource ceiling for input.
- `execution.stdout_limit_bytes` (number) — host resource ceiling for output.

None of these are part of the specialist's identity or security contract. They are exactly the "user-environment preferences" that KAN-90 (unitAI-o328h) was designed to surface, and Rico's allowlist missed them. This phase lights them up via the Phase 0 machinery.

## SUCCESS

A user can set any of the six fields above (or all of them) in their `~/.config/specialists/user.json` and they take effect on next spec load:

- `system_prompt_mode: "replace"` swaps the spec's system-prompt-composition mode without forking the specialist.
- `extensions.serena: false` skips Serena injection for that one spec (e.g. on a RAM-constrained machine, or for a vision workflow).
- `notes_mode: "final-only"` quiets per-turn handoff appends.
- `output_file: "/tmp/my-runs/<spec>.md"` redirects the mirror.
- `prompt_limit_bytes: 8388608` widens (or narrows) the prompt size guard.
- `stdout_limit_bytes: 67108864` widens (or narrows) the stdout cap.

The merge precedence is unchanged: package canonical ⊕ global user.json ⊕ repo `.specialists/user/<name>`, with null/absent meaning "inherit from layer below". Existing user.json files continue to validate; new fields auto-fill as `null` on next `sp init --global`.

## SCOPE

- src/specialist/schema.ts: add to `OVERRIDE_ALLOWED_EXECUTION_FIELDS` (prompt_limit_bytes, stdout_limit_bytes), `OVERRIDE_ALLOWED_TOP_FIELDS` (notes_mode, output_file), `OVERRIDE_ALLOWED_PROMPT_FIELDS` (system_prompt_mode — landed in Phase 0), and `OVERRIDE_ALLOWED_NESTED_EXECUTION_PATHS` (execution.extensions.serena, execution.extensions.gitnexus — landed in Phase 0).
- src/specialist/global-config.ts:67-120: extend `OverrideExecutionSchema`, `OverridePromptSchema` (added Phase 0), `GlobalSpecialistOverrideSchema` to include each new field nullable; extend `buildSpecialistOverrideTemplate` to emit null defaults for all of them.
- tests/unit/specialist/{loader,global-config,schema}.test.ts: per-field merge precedence tests (package ⊕ user) for each of the six fields.

## NON_GOALS

- `execution.auto_commit` — handled in a separate decision bead (sibling under this epic). The tradeoff (lost executor work risk vs. user-discipline override) deserves its own thread.
- `execution.requires_worktree` — isolation/safety boundary, stays blocked.
- `execution.interactive` — runtime contract (keep-alive), stays blocked.
- `prompt.task_template`, `prompt.skill_inherit` — content/sandbox boundaries, stay blocked.
- `output_type`, `response_format`, `expected_output_keys` — output contract, stay blocked.
- `beads_integration` — coupling to bd; defer unless explicitly asked.
- Doc updates (Phase 4 owns docs).

## CONSTRAINTS

- Phase 0 (unitAI-gp7nq.1) MUST be merged first. This task uses the new nested-execution and prompt allowlists; if Phase 0's mechanism isn't there, this task will reinvent it inconsistently.
- Backward compat: existing user.json (post-KAN-90 shape) must continue to parse, validate, and merge identically. `mergeGlobalUserConfig.fillMissingDefaults` should add the new keys as null without clobbering anything — verify on a fixture.
- Field-merge semantics for nested execution.extensions: when the user sets `extensions.serena: false` and the package canonical has `extensions: { serena: true, gitnexus: true }`, the merged result must be `extensions: { serena: false, gitnexus: true }`. Per-key overlay, not whole-subobject replace. The test must prove this on every nested pair.
- `output_file` is a path; do NOT validate it (caller-side responsibility). But do NOT auto-expand `~` or env vars in the loader — that's a separate concern; if the user writes `~/foo`, the runtime gets `~/foo` and may fail. Document in the upgrade note (Phase 4).
- Telemetry: existing `BlockedFieldWarning` mechanism continues to fire for fields NOT in any allowlist. After this phase, set a guard in the test that proves the six new fields no longer trip blocked-warning.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Six new per-field merge tests in tests/unit/specialist/loader.test.ts, one per allowlisted field, asserting package ⊕ user overlay produces expected resolved spec.
- [ ] Regression test on a pre-Phase-1 user.json fixture: still parses, still merges, no clobber.
- [ ] Guard test: each new field, when set in user.json, does NOT appear in any `BlockedFieldWarning`.
- [ ] `bun run lint && bun run build && bun --bun vitest run tests/unit/specialist/` clean.
- [ ] Smoke: write user.json with `extensions: {serena: false}` for the `executor` spec; run `sp config show executor --resolved` and confirm `extensions.serena: false` in the rendered output.
- [ ] Smoke: write user.json with `notes_mode: "final-only"` for a READ_ONLY spec; dispatch `sp run <spec> --bead <test-bead>`; bd show on bead confirms only ONE handoff block (final), not per-turn.

## OUTPUT

Handoff: list of the six fields lit up, the per-field test names, the smoke command + observed output. Note any blocked-warning false positives or precedence surprises (none expected, but document if seen).

title: Expand global user config: broaden allowlist + model chains + preset references
description:
## PROBLEM

The KAN-90 (unitAI-o328h) override allowlist ships with six execution fields (model, fallback_model, timeout_ms, stall_timeout_ms, thinking_level, max_retries) plus beads_write_notes and skills.paths append. That's narrower than the "user-environment preferences" framing actually warrants: several user-environment fields landed in the spec schema before or alongside KAN-90 and were silently excluded from the allowlist — system_prompt_mode (append|replace), execution.extensions.{serena,gitnexus}, notes_mode, output_file, prompt_limit_bytes, stdout_limit_bytes. Users wanting any of these knobs must fork the full specialist via .specialists/user/<name>, defeating KAN-90's whole purpose.

In addition, two ergonomic capabilities were never built: (a) multi-provider fallback chains (today `fallback_model` is singular — one backup), and (b) preset references at load time (today `config/presets.json` is one-shot CLI sugar via `sp edit --preset`, not a runtime resolver). With chains, a user with multi-provider quota can express "try anthropic, then openai-codex, then nano-gpt" once. With preset references, the user defines "fast"/"quality"/"cheap" in their global file and every spec inherits via `model: "@preset/fast"` instead of one-by-one override of 25 specialists.

## SUCCESS

A user can edit `~/.config/specialists/user.json` and:
- Set `execution.extensions.serena: false` on a single spec without forking it.
- Set `execution.system_prompt_mode: "replace"` to control how their global system prompt composes with the package spec's.
- Set `notes_mode: "final-only"` to quiet per-turn handoff appends from chatty specs.
- Set `execution.fallback_models: ["anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6", "openai-codex/gpt-5.4"]` and the runtime walks the chain on transient failure.
- Set `execution.model: "@preset/cheap"` and the loader resolves it to `nano-gpt/moonshotai/kimi-k2.5` (from `config/presets.json`) at merge time — with cycle detection if a preset references another preset.

Newly-shipped fields are auto-backfilled into existing user.json on next `sp init --global` (idempotent merge, no clobber). Blocked fields stay blocked: prompt.system, prompt.output_schema, mandatory_rules, capabilities, permission_required, skills.scripts. The override system remains contract-preserving, not specialist-forking.

## SCOPE

- src/specialist/schema.ts: `OVERRIDE_ALLOWED_EXECUTION_FIELDS`, `OVERRIDE_ALLOWED_TOP_FIELDS`, NEW `OVERRIDE_ALLOWED_PROMPT_FIELDS`, NEW nested-execution allowlist concept, `fallback_model` schema (string | string[]).
- src/specialist/loader.ts: `applyOverrideFields` extension for nested paths and prompt overlay; preset reference resolver hook (post-merge or in-merge); cycle detection.
- src/specialist/global-config.ts: `GlobalSpecialistOverrideSchema` widening (.strict() schema needs explicit fields added); `buildSpecialistOverrideTemplate` defaulted-null shape for new fields; `mergeGlobalUserConfig.fillMissingDefaults` already handles backward compat.
- src/specialist/runner.ts:946 and src/specialist/script-runner.ts:514: fallback chain walking (today both treat `fallback_model` as a single string).
- src/cli/init.ts: stub generation for new knobs (commented JSON or top-of-file explainer).
- config/presets.json: format extension may be needed for chains (e.g. preset that itself defines a fallback chain).
- tests/unit/specialist/{loader,global-config,schema}.test.ts: merge precedence tests for every new field.
- docs/upgrade-notes/kan-91-expanded-overrides.md: NEW upgrade note.

## NON_GOALS

- Promoting any currently-blocked field (prompt.system, output_schema, mandatory_rules, capabilities, permission_required, skills.scripts) to user-overridable. Those define the specialist's contract or security envelope; overriding them is forking.
- Building a per-task model router (`models.tasks: {review: x, fix: y}`) — that's a separate epic if ever wanted.
- Adding `model: "@user/myalias"` for user-defined personal aliases. Preset refs use the package-shipped presets file as authoritative; user-defined presets is a follow-up (Phase 3.5 if scope creeps).
- Touching the repo-layer `.specialists/user/<name>` semantics. The override-allowed list is shared between global and repo layers today; this epic keeps it shared.
- Restructuring `sp init --global` repo-spec pollution (that's `unitAI-ucpcy`, runs in parallel).
- Backfilling KAN-90 in canonical docs (that's `unitAI-aav4w`); but Phase 4 of this epic adds NEW docs and must not contradict the canonical-doc update done by aav4w.
- Fixing the stale 4-layer mentions in CHANGELOG + kan-90 upgrade-notes (that's `unitAI-v4i0j`).

## CONSTRAINTS

- Backward compat: any existing user.json must continue to parse and merge identically after the schema widens. New fields default to `null` (= inherit). `mergeGlobalUserConfig.fillMissingDefaults` already covers this — verify in tests.
- `GlobalSpecialistOverrideSchema` is `.strict()` — every new field must be added explicitly to the schema, or `sp init --global` will start producing files that fail validation.
- Preset resolution must be deterministic and cycle-safe. A preset referencing another preset (`{"cheap": {"fields": {"specialist.execution.model": "@preset/super-cheap"}}}`) must either resolve fully or fail with a clear error — never infinite-loop. Cap depth at 4.
- `fallback_model` (singular) must stay accepted as a string for at least one minor version after `fallback_models` (plural array) ships, to allow existing user files to migrate naturally. Runtime treats `fallback_model` as the head of a single-element chain when `fallback_models` absent.
- Telemetry: log preset resolution at debug level (`[loader] resolved @preset/cheap → nano-gpt/...`) and emit a structured event with `event=preset_resolved, specialist, preset_name, resolved_model, depth` when telemetry is on. Log fallback chain walk on each transient failure with `event=fallback_step, attempt_n, model_tried, error_class`.
- Never silently drop a user override. If a field is recognized but invalid (e.g. preset doesn't exist), surface a loud error from `validateGlobalUserConfig` and refuse to load that spec; do not fall back to package default without warning. (Matches current strict-fail policy.)
- Phase 0 is a structural change to `applyOverrideFields` — it affects every spec load in every repo. HIGH blast radius; the implementation task must include impact analysis evidence via gitnexus_impact before any edit.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `bun --bun vitest run tests/unit/specialist/{loader,global-config,schema}.test.ts` green; new tests cover: nested-execution override merge, prompt-allowlist override merge, fallback-chain schema acceptance of string and string[], preset reference resolution to known preset, preset reference resolution to unknown preset (error), preset cycle detection.
- [ ] `bun run lint` and `bun run build` clean.
- [ ] Smoke: write a user.json with one of each new field, run `sp config show <name> --resolved` from a fresh tmpdir, confirm resolved spec matches expected overlay.
- [ ] Smoke: end-to-end live run of one spec (e.g. `sp run echo` or any safe READ_ONLY) with `model: "@preset/cheap"` set in user.json; confirm the actual model dispatched matches the preset.
- [ ] Smoke: end-to-end live run of one spec with `fallback_models: ["bad-provider/bad", "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6"]`; first dispatch fails, second succeeds, observability log shows `fallback_step` events.
- [ ] After `sp init --global` from a clean tmp HOME, the generated user.json contains every new field defaulted to `null` (and the schema validates).
- [ ] After `sp init --global` over an existing user.json (using the test fixture from KAN-90), no existing user value is clobbered and every new field is added with `null`.

## OUTPUT

For each phase: the closing chain handoff lists changed files, the new test count, the smoke command output, and any blast-radius surprises caught by gitnexus_impact. Epic close (at end) summarizes: total new allowlisted fields, total new schema concepts (nested allowlist, prompt allowlist, preset refs, fallback chains), test count delta, and a one-paragraph migration note for `docs/upgrade-notes/kan-91-expanded-overrides.md` linking back to KAN-90.

## REFERENCES

- Origin design: unitAI-o328h (KAN-90 — 3-layer field-merge decision, CLOSED).
- Parallel follow-ups: unitAI-ucpcy (sp init --global pollution), unitAI-v4i0j (stale 4-layer docs), unitAI-aav4w (canonical doc backfill).
- Touchpoints already grounded this session: src/specialist/schema.ts:144-168 (allowlists), src/specialist/global-config.ts:67-120 (override schema + template), src/specialist/loader.ts:194-313 (applyOverrideFields + buildMergedSpec), src/cli/init.ts:881-935 (sp init --global), config/presets.json (cheap/medium/power existing format), src/cli/edit.ts:48-833 (current preset consumer — read at apply, not at load).

title: seconder: auto-inject $writer_diff from --job worktree (mirror reviewer_diff_*)
description:
## PROBLEM

The `seconder` specialist (READ_ONLY, dual-verdict scope/quality gate per docs/design/chain-templates.md §2.3) cannot evaluate scope/quality when the writer's diff is empty in its context. Its system prompt explicitly says: *"If bead sections or diff evidence are missing, return UNCLEAR for the affected dimension instead of guessing"* and *"Stop after at most 8 tool calls"* — i.e. the specialist is bounded and is told to wait for an injected diff rather than fish for it itself.

In practice, when an orchestrator dispatches:

```
sp run seconder --bead <bead-id> --job <writer-job-id>
```

the seconder's startup-context variables_keys are:
```
[bead_context, bead_id, reused_worktree_awareness, reviewed_job_id]
```

The `$writer_diff` template variable referenced by `config/specialists/seconder.specialist.json` task_template is **not populated**. Compare to `reviewer`, which when given `--job <id>` receives auto-injected `reviewer_diff_source`, `reviewer_diff_stat`, `reviewer_diff_files`, `reviewer_diff_hunks`. The asymmetry means seconder defaults to UNCLEAR on any chain where the orchestrator hasn't manually pasted the diff into the bead description — which is exactly the *cheap pre-review* the seconder gate is supposed to be.

Observed in 4 dispatches during mercury-infra epic infra-cxn execution (2026-06-07): seconder #2 on cxn.4 (job 9fcb72), seconder #2 on cxn.6 (job 7d4b09), and others returned `scope_verdict: UNCLEAR` with finding "No writer diff or job evidence provided" — even though `--job` was set and the worktree was reused. Each forced an orchestrator workaround (grep evidence pasted into reviewer rebuttal) rather than the seconder doing its actual job.

## SUCCESS

When `sp run seconder --bead <id> --job <writer-job-id>` is dispatched, the seconder's runtime context receives `$writer_diff` populated from the writer job's worktree diff (`merge-base main HEAD..HEAD` or equivalent), analogous to how reviewer's `reviewer_diff_*` variables are populated today. Seconder can then produce concrete PASS/FAIL scope+quality verdicts on the writer diff without orchestrator workaround.

## SCOPE

- `src/specialist/runner.ts` (or equivalent — the runner code path that prepares the seconder's task template variables when `--job` is set).
- `config/specialists/seconder.specialist.json` task_template (only if the variable name needs adjustment — preferably keep `$writer_diff` and just populate it).
- Whatever reviewer's diff-injection code path is — copy/factor that for seconder.

## NON_GOALS

- Do NOT change seconder's system prompt or evidence-priority discipline. The fix is runner-side context injection, not telling seconder to fish for the diff itself (which would conflict with the 8-tool-call bound and the GitNexus-preferred design).
- Do NOT add a pre-script that shells out to git from the seconder worktree as the primary fix. A pre-script is an acceptable fallback, but the canonical fix is the runner injecting the same diff payload it already prepares for reviewer.
- Do NOT extend this to other READ_ONLY specialists (overthinker, security-auditor, obligations-scanner) — each has its own evidence model; out of scope here.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Reviewer's diff variables are `reviewer_diff_source / _stat / _files / _hunks`. Seconder's task_template uses `$writer_diff` (a single placeholder, per current JSON). Either (a) populate `$writer_diff` as a concatenated payload, or (b) extend seconder.task_template to consume `seconder_diff_*` variables mirroring reviewer — pick one, document the choice.
- Respect seconder's `prompt_limit_bytes: 80000` cap. For very large diffs, truncate sensibly (e.g., diff --stat always, hunks up to a byte budget). Same approach reviewer uses today is fine.
- Preserve READ_ONLY permission and `requires_worktree: true` semantics.
- No change to the chain-coordinator reducer logic — the verdict interpretation stays as-is (PASS advances, FAIL routes back to writer, UNCLEAR → PARTIAL).

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Unit / integration test: dispatching `sp run seconder --bead <test-bead> --job <writer-job-id>` results in `$writer_diff` non-empty in the seconder's startup-context.
- [ ] End-to-end: on a known-good writer chain, seconder returns `scope_verdict: PASS` (or actionable FAIL) instead of UNCLEAR, with the diff visible to it.
- [ ] No regression on reviewer's diff injection.
- [ ] Truncation behavior verified for large diffs (>80kb prompt limit).

## OUTPUT

- PR with the runner change + (if applicable) seconder.specialist.json task_template tweak.
- Test evidence (startup-context dump showing populated `$writer_diff`).
- One-line note in CHANGELOG / changelog-drafter input describing the fix.
- If the canonical-vs-fallback decision (pre-script vs runner injection) was non-obvious, a short ADR or `bd remember` capturing it.

## APPROACH NOTES

- Look at the code path that prepares `reviewer_diff_source` etc. for `--job` dispatches — that's the template to mirror.
- The task_template in `seconder.specialist.json` already references `$writer_diff`, so the smallest possible diff is "populate that variable in the runner the same way reviewer's diff variables are populated."
- Document the variable name choice (writer_diff vs seconder_diff_*) so future specialists with similar shape can adopt one or the other consistently.

title: Expand §6.7 issue relationships: edge schema + cycle + mutation + bidirectionality + query patterns + evolution
description:
Discovered-from bgyp0 (substrate rev11 round-3 audit). The §6.7 design-note 2026-06-02 flags 7 under-drilled questions about issue relationships, all of which would otherwise become implementer guesswork:

1. **Edge metadata schema.** Can a `blocks` edge carry `reason` / `expiry` / `creator` / `severity` / `created_at`? Pin the `issue_dependencies` row shape canonically.
2. **Cycle prevention.** A blocks B and B blocks A — validator rejection at insert, runtime detection on dispatcher walk, or silently dropped? Same for `parent-child` cycles.
3. **Edge mutation authority.** Who can remove an edge? Creator only / container owner / seed validator at re-open? `supersedes` has clear semantics; others silent.
4. **Bidirectionality per kind.** Pin canonical direction per edge kind (esp. `validates` — verifier→impl or impl-is-validated-by-verifier).
5. **Context-edge semantics handoff.** Which edge kinds enter the memory pack at which depth? §6.7 says they feed §6.8/§10.2 but rule lives elsewhere — either expand §6.7 or cross-link.
6. **Query patterns.** Canonical examples per edge class (gate / context / lifecycle / tracing): 'all issues validating X transitively', 'caused-by chain back to root', 'all issues this seed advisor's plan transitively blocks'.
7. **Schema evolution discipline.** Mechanism for shipping a 10th edge type without migration script — `issue_dependencies.kind` enum vs free-string vs catalog row?

Proposed shape: §6.7 grows from 2 to 5-6 sub-sections (6.7.3 edge schema + metadata, 6.7.4 cycle + mutation rules, 6.7.5 canonical query patterns by class, 6.7.6 evolution discipline). Cross-link §6.8 + §10.2 consumers explicitly.

Source observation: bridge work in unitAI-kj651 repeatedly leans on §6.7 (parent-child, validates, discovered-from edges materialize chain shape and gate logic). Under-drill becomes recurring blocker.

Acceptance: substrate_design_it.md + substrate_design_en.md §6.7 grows the 4 new sub-sections; rev marker bumped (rev12 likely); §6.8 + §10.2 cross-links updated.

Previous forensic smoke used a synthetic telemetry job. Validate the forensic and Prometheus paths against a real specialist runtime job.

- No source edits.

Report exact commands, job id, and pass/fail evidence.

The forensic bridge defines the envelope, but xtrm still needs a concrete event catalog for better AgentOps observability across jobs, chains, reviewers, tools, MCP, service skills, pulse emitters, processes, and worktrees.

## SUCCESS
A documented AgentOps event catalog exists and can guide specialists, substrate, Gitboard, MCP implementations, and future dashboards.

## SCOPE
Create or update documentation with event families and event names, including at minimum:

### Job lifecycle
- `job.created`
- `job.started`
- `job.waiting`
- `job.resumed`
- `job.completed`
- `job.failed`
- `job.cancelled`

### Chain and epic orchestration
- `chain.created`
- `chain.member.started`
- `chain.member.completed`
- `chain.ready_for_review`
- `chain.finalized`
- `epic.merge_attempted`
- `epic.merged`
- `epic.merge_failed`

### Reviewer flow
- `review.started`
- `review.verdict.pass`
- `review.verdict.partial`
- `review.verdict.fail`
- `review.rebuttal_requested`
- `review.recheck_started`

### Tool and command runtime
- `tool.call.started`
- `tool.call.completed`
- `tool.call.failed`
- `command.started`
- `command.completed`
- `command.failed`

### Process health
- `process.spawned`
- `process.exited`
- `process.orphan_detected`
- `process.reaped`
- `process.health.degraded`

### Worktree health
- `worktree.created`
- `worktree.dirty_detected`
- `worktree.merged`
- `worktree.cleanup_started`
- `worktree.cleanup_failed`
- `worktree.cleanup_completed`

### MCP observability
- `mcp.connected`
- `mcp.disconnected`
- `mcp.call.started`
- `mcp.call.completed`
- `mcp.call.failed`
- `mcp.auth.failed`
- `mcp.rate_limited`
- `mcp.latency.observed`

### Service skills
- `service_skill.activated`
- `service_skill.completed`
- `service_skill.failed`
- `service_skill.drift_detected`
- `service_skill.updated`

### Pulse emitters
- `pulse.emitted`
- `pulse.dropped`
- `pulse.delayed`
- `pulse.backpressure_detected`

Also clarify two MCP meanings:
1. an internal xtrm AgentOps/DevOps MCP for observing and controlling xtrm;
2. a telemetry standard for any MCP we build for Mercury/client systems so they integrate cleanly with xtrm observability.

## NON_GOALS
- Do not implement every emitter yet.
- Do not introduce high-cardinality Prometheus labels.

## VALIDATION
- Catalog maps every event family to allowed forensic envelope fields.
- Catalog identifies which events should also project to aggregate Prometheus metrics.
- Documentation is beginner-readable and implementation-ready.

title: service-skills-sync v1.4.0: add diff/PR-body scan phase to catch non-symbol drift (renamed env vars, new error strings, removed endpoints)
description:
## PROBLEM

The v1.3.0 librarian's drift signal surface only catches *symbol-level* drift:

- `drift_detector.py scan`: mtime > last_sync timestamp → list of files
- `gitnexus_detect_changes()` / `gitnexus_impact()`: symbol-graph diff against last_sync_ref
- Serena `search_for_pattern`: secondary cross-check on known strings

What's MISSING — non-symbol drift the librarian provably cannot see:

- New `raise SomeNewError(...)` strings the SKILL.md Failure Modes table should list
- New `logger.error / logger.critical` patterns (per the v1.3.0 prompt's own Phase 2(d): "New error pattern in territory → edit required" — but the prompt names no mechanism to discover them)
- Renamed env vars (QWEN_SERVICE_URL → SPECIALISTS_SERVICE_URL pattern; symbol graph doesn't see string-literal renames)
- Renamed container/service names in docker-compose YAML (territory globs often skip infra/)
- New or removed HTTP endpoints (FastAPI route decorators may be tier=medium in gitnexus but the path string change isn't surfaced)
- New config keys (env var keys, settings.py constants)
- Stated breaking changes in merged-PR descriptions

`drift_detector.py` internally calls `_git_diff_files(project_root, base_ref)` for tier enrichment scope (line 96-138), but only as a file-list filter — the actual diff body is never read.

Concrete failure mode observed 2026-06-01 in darth-feedor (bead py_backend-0ndo): librarian flagged 'audited-and-unchanged' for services whose docker-compose files had renamed containers and whose error message strings had changed. Only caught after a separate `gh pr list` / manual diff review.

## SUCCESS

v1.4.0 librarian system prompt mandates a **Phase 2.5 — Diff content scan** between `last_sync_ref` and HEAD on every drifted territory file, and produces concrete enforceable evidence in the per-service verdict.

## SCOPE

`config/specialists/service-skills-sync.specialist.json` — system prompt + mandatory_rules.

Optionally: `.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/drift_detector.py` — surface a new `diff <service-id>` subcommand that returns the actual diff body filtered to interesting patterns, so the librarian doesn't have to compose the git command itself.

## NON_GOALS

- Not rewriting drift detection from scratch.
- Not auto-fetching from GitHub PRs (`gh pr list` is an optional enrichment, not core flow).
- Not changing the gitnexus-triage rule — adds a complementary signal, doesn't replace it.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Compatible with v1.3.0 contract: still no string-only `audited-and-unchanged`. The Phase 2.5 diff scan is an ADDITION, not a replacement.
- Diff scan must not silently fail. If `git diff <last_sync_ref>..HEAD` returns empty (e.g., no last_sync_ref set), emit explicit `diff-scan-unavailable: reason` in the per-service report.
- Keep token cost reasonable — for each drifted file, sample at most ~200 lines of diff (head/tail). Larger diffs invoke gitnexus_impact on the file's symbols and grep for the keyword set instead.

## DESIGN SKETCH

Add to system prompt between Phase 2(c) (gitnexus cross-check) and Phase 2(d) (classify):

> **(c.5) Diff content scan — catches non-symbol drift**
>
> For every drifted file in this service's territory, read the actual diff body:
>
> ```bash
> git diff <last_sync_ref>..HEAD -- <file>
> ```
>
> Grep the diff for these patterns and feed every hit into the classify step (Phase 2d):
>
> - `^[+-]\s*(raise|except)\b` — new/removed exception sites
> - `^[+-]\s*logger\.(error|critical|warning)` — new/removed error logs
> - `^[+-]\s*[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+\s*=` — env var keys / config constants
> - `^[+-].*container_name:` — docker container renames
> - `^[+-].*@(app|router)\.(get|post|put|delete)` — endpoint additions/removals (FastAPI; also check Flask/Express equivalents)
> - `^[+-].*image:` — docker image refs (rename detection)
>
> If `last_sync_ref` is unset (`gitnexus_status: no_ref`), record `diff-scan-unavailable: no last_sync_ref` and DO NOT emit `audited-and-unchanged`. Treat as a triage failure.

Add mandatory_rule: `service-skills-diff-scan-mandatory` enforcing the above.

## VALIDATION

- New rule `service-skills-diff-scan-mandatory` exists in templates/rules with the Phase 2.5 spec.
- Spec test: dispatch librarian on a service whose territory had a string-literal-only change (renamed env var). Confirm the rename is surfaced in the per-service report and the SKILL.md is edited.
- Negative test: dispatch on a service with no `last_sync_ref`. Confirm verdict is NOT `audited-and-unchanged` and the report names the diff-scan failure.

## REFERENCES

- Bead py_backend-0ndo (darth-feedor): bug that motivated this — string-only audit mislabeled as semantic.
- Bead py_backend-t58t (darth-feedor): umbrella regression from same librarian run — separate fix, mentioned only as evidence the v1.3.0 librarian wasn't catching non-symbol drift even when working at full strength.
- v1.3.0 commit 0711a6ad on this repo ("forbid string-only drift verdicts; gitnexus triage mandatory") — the predecessor change; v1.4.0 builds on it.

## OUTPUT

Updated `config/specialists/service-skills-sync.specialist.json` v1.4.0 + new `service-skills-diff-scan-mandatory` template rule + entry in CHANGELOG / RELEASES.
close_reason: v1.4.0: added Phase 2.5 diff content scan to service-skills-sync system prompt + new service-skills-diff-scan-mandatory template rule. audited-and-unchanged now gates on clean diff scan in addition to gitnexus cosmetic signal. Triage-incomplete verdict for missing last_sync_ref.

title: FLAG to substrate-author: substrate.md §2.1 missing Activation entity — propose adding canonical 5-layer Identity Model section
description:
Substrate.md §2.1 declares Participant as an entity but does NOT declare a separate Run/Activation entity, leaving per-execution identity under-specified. Runtime requires distinguishing stable member identity (across restitch/handoff) from per-pi-session activation identity. Confirmed gap by searching all substrate variants (substrate.md, substrate-it.md, substrate-it-rev11.md) — no 'Identity Layers' / 'Activation' / 'Run entity' section.

Bridge-side resolution: roadmap kj651 Opp 18 + forensic-event-contract.md §4/§5 + substrate_design_it.md §2.7 (added 2026-06-02) all adopt the canonical 5-layer model:

L1 participant_kind (bounded) — specialist / orchestrator / pulse_emitter / adapter / node_member / future
L2 participant_role (bounded) — executor / reviewer / claude-code-session / drift-detector / etc
L3 participant_id (opaque, stable per scope+role) — derivation table per kind
L4 job_id (opaque, per-activation) — survives by name; one pi-session = one job
L5 turn_id / tool_call_id / event_id (opaque, per-fact)

Invariant: two activations of same role in same scope → identical L3, distinct L4.

ASK to substrate-author: add a §X.Y 'Identity Model' subsection to substrate.md (canonical) formalizing these 5 layers, OR explicitly accept/reject this model and document the chosen alternative. Either way the gap should close in substrate canonical — bridge owns it today but the canonical doc should not be silent.

Related: this is informational/notification, not a blocker on Opp 18 implementation. Bridge ships regardless.
notes: Published specialists-side contract alignment commit: 85522dfe docs: align telemetry contract identity examples. Vault edits are on disk in second-mind (substrate_design_it.md, channels.md, chains.md); second-mind repo has broad pre-existing untracked/deleted state, so not committed there in this pass.

title: Design Prometheus projection/exporter for xtrm forensic telemetry
description:
## PROBLEM
The forensic contract draws a hard line between high-cardinality logs/events and Prometheus-friendly metrics. The projection/exporter design is not yet specified.

## SUCCESS
A design and implementation plan exists for curated metrics such as job totals, duration histograms, tool call counters, MCP operation metrics, token counters, and service-skills drift counters using only allowlisted labels.

## SCOPE
- Map forensic events/current SQLite state to metric names and types.
- Define allowlisted labels and exemplar/log-link strategy.
- Identify infra ownership split with mercury/infra for scraping/storage/alerts.

## NON_GOALS
- No dashboard UX implementation.
- No high-cardinality labels.

## VALIDATION
- Proposed labels exclude all forbidden identifiers from the forensic contract.
- Metric names follow base-unit Prometheus conventions.
notes:
DOC COMPLETE 2026-06-02 — created `docs/telemetry/prometheus-projection-contract.md`.

Key decisions:
- Prometheus is a projection, not source of truth; forensic events/runtime state remain canonical.
- Primary bounded identity labels are `participant_kind` + `participant_role`; `specialist` is bridge alias only.
- `participant_id`, `job_id`, `bead_id`, `issue_id`, `container_id`, `chain_id`, `pulse_id`, trace/span/tool ids, commit/pr ids are forbidden labels.
- Metric catalog covers job lifecycle, turns/context/LLM usage, tool calls, MCP operations, result/evidence/git, worktree/process health, service-skills drift, pulses/channels/substrate, and gate/eval outcomes.
- Exporter should be a projection engine with durable cursor/replayable events for counters and current-state reads for gauges.
- Exemplars may use `trace_id` when available; otherwise dashboards link from metrics to forensic logs by bounded labels + time range.
- Ownership split: xtrm owns semantics/exporter; mercury/infra owns scrape/storage/alert routing; gitboard/console owns UX.

Cross-links added:
- `docs/telemetry/forensic-event-contract.md` §8 points to this projection contract.
- `docs/observability-metrics.md` now has a bridge-era note pointing to forensic + projection contracts.

Follow-ups created:
- unitAI-60w93.6 — implement specialists Prometheus projection/exporter prototype.
- unitAI-60w93.7 — handoff projection contract to infra/console observability work.

title: Add forensic telemetry schema, cardinality, and redaction tests
description:
## PROBLEM
The forensic telemetry contract needs enforceable tests before implementation work expands. Without tests, job IDs, bead IDs, trace IDs, raw commands, or error text could become labels or leak secrets.

## SUCCESS
A reusable test fixture suite validates `xtrm.forensic.v1` events, forbidden labels, and redaction behavior.

title: HEAD epic: Professional AgentOps telemetry contract for specialists
description:
## PROBLEM

Specialists currently has strong local traceability through `.specialists/db/observability.db`, `sp log --json`, `sp feed --json`, job status rows, timeline events, and result persistence, but it is not yet a professional telemetry product surface. The system lacks a formal telemetry contract that separates forensic logs/events from Prometheus-friendly metrics and trace/span correlation.

This epic is the living head epic for AgentOps/SRE telemetry in `~/dev/specialists`. It should be iterated as more research lands. It intentionally links existing DevOps/platform specialist work rather than replacing it.

## SUCCESS

- A versioned specialists telemetry contract exists and is used as the source of truth for future implementation beads.
- Logs/events remain forensic and high-cardinality; metrics become curated, low-cardinality, Prometheus-friendly projections.
- The contract names resource attributes, metric names, allowed labels, forbidden labels, event/log fields, trace/span hierarchy, and SLO/alert candidates.
- Cross-repo ownership is clear:
  - `~/dev/specialists` owns runtime emission, DB schema, JSON log/event shape, metric projection/exporter, and specialist role contracts.
  - `~/projects/mercury/infra` owns Prometheus/Grafana/Loki/Alertmanager/exporters and platform scrape/storage/alert routing.
  - `~/dev/gitboard` owns xtrm/operator console UX and datasource-backed panels, unless future research explicitly changes that.
- Existing related beads (`unitAI-eoqxp`, children, `unitAI-rgu4q`, `unitAI-itn9h`) are either absorbed, superseded, or cross-linked with explicit rationale.

## SCOPE

Specialists-owned telemetry surfaces:

- `.specialists/db/observability.db` and `src/specialist/observability-sqlite.ts`
- timeline event schema in `src/specialist/timeline-events.ts`
- structured runtime surfaces: `sp log --json`, `sp feed --json`, `sp ps --json`, `sp result --json`
- future metrics exporter / `/metrics` or equivalent projection layer
- trace/span/session propagation for `job → turn → tool_call → external call`
- specialist/devops role contracts that consume telemetry evidence
- documentation: `docs/observability-metrics.md`, `docs/design/substrate/devops-platform-engineering-prd.md`, future telemetry contract docs

Current known telemetry facts:

- `observability.db` is the canonical runtime/audit store.
- `sp log --json` is structured log export, not a Prometheus metric surface.
- `sp feed --json` is event-stream export, not alerting/SLO telemetry.
- Current useful event/status data includes job id, specialist, bead id, node id, status, pid, model/backend, chain fields, tool calls, token/cost, elapsed, control signals, errors, retries, compactions, and result durability.
- Prometheus must not ingest high-cardinality IDs as labels; those belong in logs/traces/exemplars.

## NON_GOALS

- Do not build Mercury infra stack in this repo.
- Do not build gitboard dashboards here unless a later cross-repo decision explicitly moves that responsibility.
- Do not page on raw root-cause signals alone; alerts must be symptom/SLO driven.
- Do not expose `job_id`, `bead_id`, `chain_id`, raw paths, raw URLs, user IDs, request IDs, or error text as Prometheus labels.
- Do not treat JSON logs as a substitute for curated metrics.
- Do not grant autonomous production remediation or Terraform apply rights.

## CONSTRAINTS

Mandatory reading before child work:

- `/home/dawid/second-mind/1-projects/xtrm/research/sre-telemetry-patterns-for-mercury.md`
- `/home/dawid/second-mind/1-projects/xtrm/research/agentops-telemetry-for-specialists.md`
- `/home/dawid/second-mind/1-projects/xtrm/research/devops-query-surfaces-mcp-architecture.md`
- `/home/dawid/second-mind/1-projects/xtrm/research/devops-specialists.md`
- `/home/dawid/second-mind/1-projects/xtrm/research/devops-specialists-research.md`
- `/home/dawid/second-mind/1-projects/xtrm/research/aws-devops-agent-official-docs.md`
- `/home/dawid/second-mind/1-projects/xtrm/research/aws-agentcore-observability-official-docs.md`
- `docs/design/substrate/devops-platform-engineering-prd.md`
- `docs/design/substrate/substrate.md`
- `docs/observability-metrics.md`
- `docs/specialists-service.md`

Telemetry contract rules imported from `sre-telemetry-patterns-for-mercury.md`:

- Use Four Golden Signals / RED for service behavior: rate, errors, duration, saturation.
- Use USE for host/container/process health: utilization, saturation, errors.
- Define SLIs/SLOs from user/operator outcomes, not implementation causes.
- Metric names use base units and suffixes: `_total`, `_seconds`, `_bytes`, `_ratio`, etc.
- Labels must be bounded/low-cardinality.
- Logs and traces carry high-cardinality identifiers and forensic detail.
- Alerts should be symptom-first and dashboard/runbook linked.

Proposed specialists resource identity:

- `service.namespace=xtrm`
- `service.name=specialists`
- `service.instance.id=<stable local instance id>`
- `service.version=<package version>`
- `deployment.environment.name=<local|staging|production>`
- `service.criticality=<critical|high|medium|low>`

Initial Prometheus-friendly metric candidates to validate:

- `specialists_jobs_started_total{specialist,model,backend,repo}`
- `specialists_jobs_completed_total{specialist,status,model,backend,repo}`
- `specialists_jobs_active{specialist,status,repo}`
- `specialists_job_duration_seconds_bucket{specialist,status,model,backend}`
- `specialists_tool_calls_total{specialist,tool,result}`
- `specialists_tool_duration_seconds_bucket{specialist,tool,result}`
- `specialists_llm_input_tokens_total{specialist,model,backend}`
- `specialists_llm_output_tokens_total{specialist,model,backend}`
- `specialists_llm_cost_usd_total{specialist,model,backend}`
- `specialists_context_pct{specialist,repo}`
- `specialists_queue_depth{repo}`
- `specialists_orphan_processes{repo}`
- `specialists_sqlite_write_failures_total{repo}`

Allowed metric labels, pending validation:

- `service`, `specialist`, `repo`, `model`, `backend`, `status`, `result`, `tool`, `operation`, `queue`, `worker`

Forbidden metric labels:

- `job_id`, `bead_id`, `chain_id`, `trace_id`, `span_id`, request ids, user ids, raw URLs, raw file paths, exception text, unbounded model output text

Trace/log direction:

- Introduce trace/span correlation for `job → turn → tool_call → external call`.
- Keep `job_id`, `bead_id`, `chain_id`, `node_id`, `worktree_path`, detailed errors, command args, and result summaries in structured logs/traces, not metrics.
- Every new event kind must have an `sp log` formatter and JSON export coverage; no event ships dark.

## VALIDATION

Head-epic validation is documentary and contract-driven until implementation children are created:

- A child bead must produce a telemetry contract document with exact metric/event/log/trace shape.
- A child bead must inventory current emissions from `observability.db`, `sp log --json`, `sp feed --json`, `sp ps --json`, and identify gaps.
- A child bead must define an exporter/projection plan and a test strategy with fixture DB rows and expected Prometheus text exposition or JSON output.
- Future implementation beads must include:
  - unit tests for metric derivation from DB rows/events,
  - snapshot tests for metric names/labels,
  - cardinality guard tests rejecting forbidden labels,
  - smoke test proving exporter reads a seeded DB and emits expected metrics,
  - structured log/trace tests proving ids are present in logs/traces but absent as metric labels.

## OUTPUT

This head epic should accumulate:

- research notes and deltas from second-mind docs,
- decisions about Grafana vs gitboard visualization ownership,
- a telemetry taxonomy and metric/log/trace contract,
- cross-links to existing and future implementation beads,
- explicit supersession/absorption notes for old observability beads.

## EXISTING RELATED BEADS FOUND DURING DRAFT

- `unitAI-eoqxp` — existing in-progress epic: DevOps/platform specialist substrate and AgentOps telemetry. This should become a child/track under this head epic or remain the role/substrate workstream.
- `unitAI-eoqxp.1` — research refresh, currently the likely first unblocker.
- `unitAI-eoqxp.3` — AgentOps telemetry contract gaps for specialists runtime; directly overlaps and should be refined under this head epic.
- `unitAI-eoqxp.4` — DevOps specialist telemetry-query answer contract; relevant consumer/answer-contract workstream.
- `unitAI-eoqxp.5` — cross-repo integration contract; relevant integration workstream.
- `unitAI-rgu4q` — open feature: agentic observability/Grafana/monitor specialist, already reframed away from Grafana-first toward gitboard-native console; should be related and revisited.
- `unitAI-itn9h` — deferred design: Grafana adapter + monitor specialist; likely superseded or parked pending this head epic’s decisions.
notes:
unitAI-60w93.5 produced `docs/telemetry/prometheus-projection-contract.md`: low-cardinality Prometheus metric names/types/labels/buckets/exporter architecture/alert candidates. Forensic contract remains source for rich events; projection contract is now the metrics-side SSOT. Follow-ups: 60w93.6 exporter prototype, 60w93.7 infra/console handoff.

## 2026-06-07 docs relocation redirect
Canonical shared xtrm docs moved from `~/second-mind/1-projects/xtrm/...` to `/home/dawid/dev/xtrm/docs/`. Treat older second-mind references in mandatory reading as historical redirects. Current DevOps canon: `/home/dawid/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/devops-system.md`; AgentOps telemetry contracts: `/home/dawid/dev/xtrm/docs/telemetry/{forensic-event-contract,agentops-event-catalog,prometheus-projection-contract,prometheus-infra-console-handoff}.md`; research inputs: `/home/dawid/dev/xtrm/docs/research/`.

title: Define substrate class taxonomy for DevOps-created recommendations and escalations
description:
## Problem
The DevOps/platform specialist will discover operational findings and recommendations. Under substrate, those must not become arbitrary flat beads; they need the correct structural `class` so the runtime knows whether they block, advise, validate, or merely preserve follow-up work.

## Mandatory reading
Read the canonical xtrm docs under `/home/dawid/dev/xtrm/docs/` first, especially:
- `/home/dawid/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/devops-system.md`
- `/home/dawid/dev/xtrm/docs/substrate/substrate_design_it.md`
- `/home/dawid/dev/xtrm/docs/research/aws-devops-agent-official-docs.md`
- `/home/dawid/dev/xtrm/docs/research/aws-agentcore-observability-official-docs.md`
- `/home/dawid/dev/xtrm/docs/telemetry/agentops-event-catalog.md`

Historical `second-mind/1-projects/xtrm/...` references are redirects only.

## Initial policy to validate
- DevOps participant emits `proposal`/`escalation`; substrate/orchestrator materializes issues.
- Non-blocking out-of-scope recommendations become `class:followup` with `discovered-from` provenance.
- Current-chain safety failures remain unsatisfied `class:gate` evidence or cause an inserted step/escalation.
- Accepted standalone recommendations promote to `class:root` with type `bug|task|chore|research|spike|design` by content.
- DevOps can be `class:advisor` pre-work and `class:gate` post-work; same role, different structural class.

## Output
A short design note and updates to the devops/platform PRD describing DevOps-created issue materialization, relationship kinds, and recommendation/journal evidence shape.

title: sp stop --all + sp chain stop --<chain-id>: chain-scoped job termination
description:
PROBLEM
At chain completion the operator has N waiting/done specialist jobs (keep-alive executors + reviewers + advisors) that must be torn down one-by-one via 'sp stop <job-id>'. When multiple chains run concurrently in the same repo, no command targets jobs of a specific chain — operator manually filters 'sp ps' + runs N stops.

SUCCESS
- 'sp chain stop <chain-id>' terminates every job (running/waiting/starting) whose chain_id matches. Cross-chain-safe by construction. DEFAULT verb when concurrent chains exist.
- 'sp stop --all' terminates only WAITING + STARTING jobs in the repo. NEVER touches running. REFUSES if any running job exists OR if jobs from other chains exist (sole-orchestrator gate). Refusal envelope teaches the right alternative ('sp chain stop <chain-id>').
- --dry-run on both; --yes on --all skips confirmation but NOT refusal.

SCOPE
- src/cli/stop.ts: --all flag + sole-orchestrator predicate + refusal envelope
- src/cli/chain.ts (or extend run.ts chain surface): sp chain stop subcommand
- Reuse: stopJob(), listLiveJobsForBead(), chain-identity resolution
- config/skills/using-specialists-v4/SKILL.md (Phase 6): "Chain teardown discipline" section
- .xtrm/hooks (or .claude/hooks): PreToolUse hook on 'sp stop --all' to fire blocking hint before CLI refusal (defense-in-depth)

NON_GOALS
- Cross-repo stop
- Substrate sb container close equivalent (lands with substrate §6.10)
- Bypassing the sole-orchestrator predicate via any flag

CONSTRAINTS
- --all NEVER terminates running jobs
- Sole-orchestrator predicate: (no running jobs in repo) AND (no jobs from chains other than current orchestrator context)
- Refusal envelope must surface the running/cross-chain counts AND the suggested 'sp chain stop' command
- Both verbs must respect the keep-alive flush path (handoff block written to bead notes before terminal transition)
- Hook layer must use the SAME predicate as the CLI — single source of truth (shared helper)

VALIDATION
- Live smoke: dispatch a 3-step chain, let it reach waiting, 'sp chain stop <id>' transitions all 3 to terminal.
- Live smoke: dispatch two parallel chains, 'sp stop --all' REFUSES with envelope naming both chains.
- Live smoke: chain reaches waiting, no other chain present, 'sp stop --all' succeeds.
- Live smoke: 'sp stop --all' with 1 running + 2 waiting REFUSES (does NOT kill the waiting).
- Unit: --yes does not bypass refusal.

OUTPUT
- src/cli/stop.ts + src/cli/chain.ts
- docs/cli-reference.md updates
- config/skills/using-specialists-v4/SKILL.md "Chain teardown discipline" section
- PreToolUse hook script
- Tests for refusal cases, --chain filter, --dry-run, cross-chain isolation

SCRUTINY: medium (control-plane action, can affect running work — refusal envelope is the safety net)

title: docs: document output_file + notes_mode + handoff envelope in authoring.md + specialists-creator skill
description:
PROBLEM: This session shipped the handoff-persistence work (unitAI-sx5qk/10y07/mis38/yiazs) and the output_file env-gate decouple (unitAI-f58ma), but the authoring docs are stale: docs/authoring.md and config/skills/specialists-creator/SKILL.md still describe output_file as "writes final output after completion" with no mention of (a) the rendered handoff-block format, (b) the f58ma decouple (no env flag needed), (c) single-writer behavior, or (d) notes_mode interaction. notes_mode is a top-level schema field (schema.ts:129) but is COMPLETELY undocumented. Specialist authors cannot correctly configure output_file / notes_mode for pipelines.

GOAL: Document output_file + notes_mode + the handoff-note envelope accurately in the two package-shipped authoring surfaces, using the canonical text below. Match each file's existing heading level (## in docs/authoring.md, ### in the SKILL.md). Do NOT invent behavior — use the text as given; it was verified against live code + a live smoke this session.

SCOPE (docs-only — NO code changes):
- docs/authoring.md: REPLACE the "## `specialist.output_file`" section (currently ~line 339) with CANONICAL-OUTPUT-FILE below; INSERT a new "## `specialist.notes_mode`" section (CANONICAL-NOTES-MODE) immediately after it; EXPAND the beads_write_notes line (~line 422) with CANONICAL-BEADS-NOTES.
- config/skills/specialists-creator/SKILL.md: REPLACE the "### `specialist.output_file`" section (~line 570) with the same content adapted to ### heading level; INSERT a "### `specialist.notes_mode`" section after it; ADD a short "### Handoff / pipeline output recipe" (CANONICAL-RECIPE) — place it near the output_file/notes_mode sections.

NON_GOALS:
- No code edits. No schema edits. No changes to docs/cli-reference.md (its SPECIALISTS_JOB_FILE_OUTPUT line is about the debug file-mirror fallback, which is still correctly env-gated — leave it).
- Do not touch docs/specialists/handoff-schema.md (that documents the model's JSON OUTPUT contract, a separate concern).
- Do not reword the canonical text's technical claims; you may adjust markdown formatting to fit each file.

CONSTRAINTS:
- These are package-shipped files (config/skills ships in the npm package; docs/ ships). Keep prose tight and consistent with surrounding sections.
- config/skills/specialists-creator/SKILL.md is the canonical skill source (NOT .xtrm/skills/* — those are generated mirrors). Edit only config/skills.

VALIDATION:
- bunx tsc --noEmit (no code touched, must stay clean).
- Confirm both files contain a notes_mode section and the updated output_file section (grep).
- No broken markdown (headings/tables/code-fences balanced).

SCRUTINY: low (docs-only, no code, no runtime behavior change).

OUTPUT: changed files (2), confirmation grep that notes_mode + updated output_file present in both, residual notes.

================ CANONICAL TEXT (verbatim source — transcribe accurately) ================

[CANONICAL-OUTPUT-FILE]
When set, the specialist writes its **handoff block** to this file on every substantive turn — foreground and `--background`. The content is identical to what is appended to the input bead notes and shown by `sp result`: a markdown heading, the verbatim specialist output, and an italic metadata footer.

- **No env flag required.** `output_file` is honored whenever it is set (since unitAI-f58ma). It does NOT require `SPECIALISTS_JOB_FILE_OUTPUT` — that flag now only gates the debug file-mirrors (events.jsonl / status.json / result.txt).
- **Single writer.** In a supervised run (`sp run`) the supervisor owns the file and the runner's own write is suppressed, so the file is never double-written. (In script/serve runs there is no supervisor; the runner writes the raw output instead of the enveloped block.)
- **Format is the rendered handoff block, not bare output.** A downstream specialist that consumes this file as input will see the header/footer envelope around the body.
- **Append vs overwrite is controlled by `notes_mode`** (see below): `full-trail` appends each turn; `final-only` overwrites with just the final `[FINAL · DONE]` block.
- **Gitignore the path** if you don't want it committed — specs with `output_file` always write, so add the path (e.g. `.specialists/*-result.md`) to `.gitignore`.

Relative paths resolve from the working directory.

[CANONICAL-NOTES-MODE]
Controls how per-turn handoff output is persisted to BOTH the input bead notes and `output_file`.

| Value | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `"full-trail"` (default) | Append every substantive turn. Bead notes / `output_file` accumulate `### … [turn N · WAITING]` blocks, ending with a final `## … [FINAL · DONE]` block. Best for keep-alive specialists where the operator wants the full trail. |
| `"final-only"` | Persist only the single canonical `## … [FINAL · DONE]` block; intermediate turns are skipped and `output_file` is OVERWRITTEN (not appended). Best for non-coding / chained pipelines where the next specialist reads the previous specialist's bead note or `output_file` as its input and only wants the final result. |

Empty turns are never persisted. The handoff block is markdown-native (heading + verbatim body + one italic metadata footer); the model string is normalized (provider prefix stripped, e.g. `nano-gpt/moonshotai/kimi-k2.5` renders as `kimi-k2.5`).

Example JSON:
{ "notes_mode": "final-only" }

[CANONICAL-BEADS-NOTES]
`beads_write_notes` (boolean, default `true`) — when `true`, the specialist appends its handoff block to the associated bead's notes on every substantive turn. The appended block is the rendered handoff format described under `notes_mode`: a markdown heading (`### <specialist> · <model> · [turn N · WAITING]` for trail turns, `## … [FINAL · DONE]` for the final turn), the verbatim specialist output, and an italic footer with timing / token / git metadata. Set to `false` to suppress bead-note writes entirely. The same content also feeds `output_file` and `sp result` (one shared content source).

[CANONICAL-RECIPE]
For a non-coding pipeline where each specialist reads the previous one's result, set `output_file` to a known path AND `notes_mode: "final-only"` so the file (and the bead note) holds exactly the final result, overwritten each run — clean for the next specialist to consume. For a human-monitored keep-alive specialist, leave `notes_mode: "full-trail"` (default) so the operator sees every turn accumulate. `output_file` needs no env flag; just gitignore its path.

title: Synthesize spec-to-beads architecture proposal
description:
## PROBLEM

We have external research and local integration findings. We need a design synthesis for an OpenSpec-inspired framework adapted to beads/specialists without duplicating or weakening existing planning/test-planning workflows.

## SUCCESS

Produce a clear recommended architecture: artifacts, command flow, data model, transform rules, validation gates, implementation phases, risks, and open decisions.

SCRUTINY: high

## SCOPE

Use researcher job 842fec and explorer job c86559 results as primary inputs. Consider local constraints from using-specialists-v3, planning, and test-planning skills. No file edits.

## NON_GOALS

- No implementation.
- No bd issue board for implementation yet.
- No long treatise; prioritize actionable architecture and decision points.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Respect 7-section bead contracts and SCRUTINY behavior.
- Keep planning/test-planning as the compiler target or delegated planning engine, not duplicated freehand logic.
- Prefer thin spec artifacts plus strong transform/validation over heavy bureaucracy.
- Explicitly call out whether to extend create-spec, add a new sp/spec command, or route through planner.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Reconciles external OpenSpec/Spec Kit patterns with local bead rules.
- [ ] Includes recommended command UX.
- [ ] Includes artifact schema and transform mapping to bd create/bd dep/test issues.
- [ ] Includes risks and MVP implementation phases.

## OUTPUT

Architecture brief suitable for operator review and later conversion into implementation beads.
notes:
### overthinker · gpt-5.5 · [turn 29 · WORKING]

## Summary

Spec system should be thin front-end. Planner/test-planning stay compiler backend.

Best shape: new `sp spec` CLI. Keep `/create-spec` as draft-only alias. Do not make slash command create beads directly.

Core rule: **spec owns intent; planner owns bd graph; test-planning owns test issue strategy; reviewer owns implementation gate.**

## Status

Read inputs from bead notes:
- researcher job `842fec` via `unitAI-2dazr.1`
- explorer job `c86559` via `unitAI-2dazr.2`

No file edits.

## Phase 1 — Initial Analysis

### Goal

Create OpenSpec-inspired flow that turns feature specs into:
- 7-section bead contracts
- typed `bd dep` graph
- batched test issues
- specialist-ready handoff

Without duplicating planning/test-planning logic.

### External patterns worth borrowing

From OpenSpec:
- proposal/change lifecycle
- validation before archive
- delta/spec sync idea
- lightweight brownfield workflow

From Spec Kit:
- `specify → plan → tasks → implement`
- human gate steps
- traceability from requirement to task
- story-scoped task breakdown

From SDD paper:
- behavior-focused specs
- testable requirements
- small validated increments
- spec anchored, not spec-as-source dogma

### Local constraints

Non-negotiable local rules:
- bead contracts need `PROBLEM / SUCCESS / SCOPE / NON_GOALS / CONSTRAINTS / VALIDATION / OUTPUT`
- `SCRUTINY: low|medium|high|critical` must propagate
- planner specialist already injects planning + test-planning
- test-planning batches by layer: core / boundary / shell
- current `/create-spec` writes standalone markdown only
- `bd dep` vocabulary has specific meanings: `blocks`, `validates`, `discovered-from`, `relates-to`, `supersedes`, etc.

## Phase 2 — Devil's Advocate

### Main failure modes

1. **Direct spec-to-bd compiler duplicates planner**
   - Bad. Recreates decomposition, phasing, test grouping.
   - Fix: `sp spec` validates + prepares planner input; planner creates real board.

2. **Spec bureaucracy kills speed**
   - OpenSpec/Spec Kit can become waterfall.
   - Fix: one thin artifact, optional design section only for high/critical risk.

3. **Spec and beads become competing sources of truth**
   - Fix: spec owns intent pre-plan; beads own execution post-plan. Link both ways.

4. **SCRUTINY under-inferred**
   - Fix: explicit field plus local auto-escalation table. Inferred floor can only raise.

5. **Test issues become checklist theater**
   - Fix: invoke test-planning rules: layer classification, DoD templates, critical path map, `validates` edges.

6. **Archive semantics hide unfinished work**
   - Fix: archive only after linked epic done + validation evidence exists. No warning-only archive for high/critical work.

## Phase 3 — Synthesis

## Architecture

### Recommended command UX

Add new CLI namespace:

```bash
sp spec draft "feature description" --template full --out docs/specs/<slug>/spec.yaml
sp spec validate docs/specs/<slug>/spec.yaml
sp spec apply docs/specs/<slug>/spec.yaml --parent <epic-id optional>
sp spec status docs/specs/<slug>/spec.yaml
sp spec archive docs/specs/<slug>/spec.yaml
```

Keep `/create-spec`:
- legacy draft command
- maybe alias to `sp spec draft`
- should not create beads directly

### Why new `sp spec`

`sp` already owns specialists + bd workflow. Slash command is Claude-only, tool-permission-dependent, weak for validation/status/archive. New CLI gives durable workflow and testable behavior.

### Artifact model

Use one thin tracked artifact:

```yaml
schema_version: 1
id: spec-auth-refresh
title: Auth refresh hardening
status: draft # draft|validated|planned|archived
scrutiny: high

problem: >
  User-facing/project-facing problem.

success:
  - Observable end-state.

scope:
  include:
    - src/auth/refresh.ts
    - src/cli/login.ts
  exclude:
    - storage migration
    - auth provider redesign

non_goals:
  - No auth protocol redesign.

constraints:
  - Preserve token format.
  - Keep CLI flags stable.

requirements:
  - id: R1
    story: User survives one transient refresh failure.
    behavior: Retry once after bounded backoff.
    acceptance:
      - Refresh succeeds after one transient failure.
      - Final failure surfaces clear message.
    layer_hint: shell
    priority: 1
    risks:
      - auth/session state

validation:
  - kind: unit
    target: refresh retry state
  - kind: integration
    target: login CLI output and exit code

dependencies:
  - from: R2
    requires: R1

open_questions: []

links:
  parent_epic: null
  planner_bead: null
  epic: null
  children: []
  test_issues: []
```

Optional later:
- `design.md` for high/critical architecture notes
- `archive/<slug>.yaml` snapshot after close

### Transform mapping

`sp spec apply` does not create child beads itself. It creates/updates planner bead and dispatches planner.

Mapping into planner input:

| Spec field | Planner/bead target |
|---|---|
| `problem` | epic `PROBLEM` |
| `success` | epic/task `SUCCESS` |
| `scrutiny` | `SCRUTINY` on every substantive bead |
| `scope.include` | `SCOPE` |
| `scope.exclude`, `non_goals` | `NON_GOALS` |
| `constraints` | `CONSTRAINTS` |
| `requirements[].acceptance` | `VALIDATION` + task `SUCCESS` |
| `validation[]` | test-planning hints |
| `requirements[].layer_hint` | test-planning layer classification hint |
| `dependencies.requires` | `bd dep add <dependent> <required> --type blocks` |
| generated test issues | `bd dep add <test> <impl> --type validates` |
| source spec | `REFERENCES` / bd notes link |

### Validation gates

Before planner dispatch:

- schema valid
- maps to all 7 bead sections
- `SCOPE` not vague
- all requirements testable
- no unresolved high-risk open question
- SCRUTINY explicit or inferred
- layer hint present or inferable
- dependencies acyclic
- high/critical specs require design note or overthinker pass

After planner result:

- planner output has `epic_id`, `children`, `test_issues`, `first_task`
- every child has 7-section contract
- every substantive child has SCRUTINY
- test issues cover core/boundary/shell groups where applicable
- `bd dep cycles` clean
- no raw `blocks` misuse for `validates`/`discovered-from`

Archive gate:

- linked epic closed
- validation evidence present
- spec links updated
- high/critical review gates complete

## Implementation Phases

### MVP 0 — Contract spec

- Define `spec.yaml` schema.
- Define validator.
- Define SCRUTINY inference table from local auto-escalation surfaces.
- No bd writes.

### MVP 1 — Draft + validate

- `sp spec draft`
- `sp spec validate`

## Architecture

### Contract Surface

**7-section mandatory contract** (planning + using-specialists-v3 aligned):
1. PROBLEM — why exists, what problem solves
2. SUCCESS — observable acceptance criteria in prose
3. SCOPE — files/symbols/surfaces (no generic "src/")
4. NON_GOALS — related improvements explicitly excluded
5. CONSTRAINTS — hard rules (API compat, style, do-not-touch)
6. VALIDATION — checkbox list of proof-of-done
7. OUTPUT — what executing specialist hands back

**SCRUTINY field** (universal, optional, defaults `medium`):
```
SCRUTINY: low | medium | high | critical
```

| Level | Reviewer behavior | Gates required |
|-------|-------------------|----------------|
| low | Seconder-only spot-check | code-sanity OK sufficient |
| medium | Standard review | code-sanity + security-auditor (if surface) |
| high | File-by-file sign-off | code-sanity + security-auditor + gitnexus_impact |
| critical | High + second opinion | high + obligations-scanner CLEAN + independent review |

**Auto-escalation surfaces** (reviewer raises floor regardless of stated SCRUTINY):
- `auth/*`, `**/credentials*`, `**/token*` → high
- `config/specialists/*.json`, `.specialists/user/*` → high
- `**/*.lock` → medium + security-auditor required
- `migrations/**` → high
- `src/permissions/*`, `hooks/**` → critical

### Planning Workflow

**6-phase flow** (planning/SKILL.md):
1. Clarify Intent — problem, constraints, priority
2. Explore Codebase — GitNexus-first (query → context → impact)
3. Structure Plan — phases, deps, CoT reasoning
4. Create bd Issues — epic + tasks with 7-section contracts
5. test-planning — layer classification + companion test issues
6. Handoff — claim first issue

- Model: `openai-codex/gpt-5.4`

- Output: structured "Planner result" block with epic_id, children, test_issues, first_task

### Test-Planning Workflow

**Layer detection**:
- Core: pure logic, no I/O → unit + property tests

- Shell: CLI/orchestration → integration tests

- Batched test issues (not per-impl)

| discovered-from | Follow-up source | `bd dep add <follow-up> <reviewer> --type discovered-from` |
| caused-by | Failure attribution | `bd dep add <fail> <root-cause> --type caused-by` |
| relates-to | Soft linkage | `bd dep relate <a> <b>` |
| parent-child | Epic ownership | `bd create --parent <epic>` |

## PROBLEM

We need current external patterns from OpenSpec-like and spec-driven development frameworks before designing a local variant. The goal is to understand concepts worth borrowing, not to copy another workflow blindly.

## SUCCESS

Research identifies useful patterns: spec/proposal/change lifecycle, validation commands, templates, traceability, approval gates, and how specs decompose into tasks/tests.

SCRUTINY: medium

## SCOPE

OpenSpec/OpenSpec-like framework docs if available, spec-driven development tooling, PRD-to-task workflows, and examples of spec validation/change proposal systems.

## NON_GOALS

- No local repo code mapping.
- No implementation plan beyond transferable patterns.
- No vendor lock-in recommendation.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Cite source names and URLs when available.
- Separate confirmed source facts from design recommendations.
- Prefer patterns compatible with beads and specialists; flag incompatibilities.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Sources consulted are named.
- [ ] Pattern inventory covers lifecycle, templates, validation, traceability, and task decomposition.
- [ ] Recommendations state what to borrow, adapt, or reject.
