### researcher · gpt-5.4-mini · [turn 20 · WORKING]

## Summary
Current external evidence says:

- **OpenSpec**: lightweight, brownfield-first spec/change system. Core flow = **propose → apply → sync → archive**. Expanded flow = **new/continue/ff → apply → verify → archive**. Specs live in `openspec/specs/`; proposed work lives in `openspec/changes/` with `proposal.md`, `design.md`, `tasks.md`, and delta specs. Archive merges delta specs back into source-of-truth, then moves change into archive folder. Validation exists both as `openspec validate` and `/opsx:verify`.  
  Sources: OpenSpec docs + commands/workflows/getting-started/cli/concepts.  
  URLs:  
  - https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md  
  - https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec/blob/main/docs/commands.md  
  - https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec/blob/main/docs/workflows.md  
  - https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec/blob/main/docs/cli.md  
  - https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec/blob/main/docs/concepts.md  
  Accessed: 2026-05-30

- **GitHub Spec Kit**: more rigid SDD pipeline. Core commands = **constitution → specify → plan → tasks → implement**. Optional = **clarify, analyze, checklist**. Workflow engine supports **run/resume/status**, human **gate** steps, and persisted state. Templates push test-first and story-scoped task breakdown.  
  Sources: Spec Kit README, spec-driven guide, workflows, plan/tasks templates.  
  URLs:  
  - https://github.com/github/spec-kit/blob/main/README.md  
  - https://github.com/github/spec-kit/blob/main/spec-driven.md  
  - https://github.com/github/spec-kit/blob/main/docs/reference/workflows.md  
  - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/spec-kit/main/templates/plan-template.md  
  - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/spec-kit/main/templates/tasks-template.md  
  Accessed: 2026-05-30

- **SDD paper**: framework spectrum = **spec-first / spec-anchored / spec-as-source**. Strong pattern: specs should be behavior-focused, testable, unambiguous; plan should hold architecture/data/interfaces/NFRs; implement in small validated increments; validate via unit/integration/acceptance + BDD.  
  Source: arXiv HTML paper.  
  URL: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.00180v1  
  Accessed: 2026-05-30

## Status
Research only. No local code edits.

## Changes
None.

## Pattern inventory

| Pattern | Confirmed source fact | Beads/specialists fit |
|---|---|---|
| Lifecycle artifact chain | OpenSpec: proposal/specs/design/tasks → apply → sync → archive. Spec Kit: constitution/specify/plan/tasks → implement. Paper: specify → plan → implement → validate. | Good |
| Validation gate | OpenSpec `verify` + `validate`; Spec Kit `analyze`, `checklist`, workflow gates; paper validate phase. | Good |
| Human approval checkpoints | Spec Kit workflow `gate`, resume after pause. OpenSpec review/verify before archive. | Good |
| Traceability | Spec Kit ties plan/tasks to constitution/spec. Paper says every tech choice traces to requirements. OpenSpec delta specs preserve change history. | Good |
| Task decomposition | Spec Kit `tasks` breaks plan into story-scoped tasks, marks parallel work `[P]`, tests first if requested. OpenSpec tasks.md checklist. | Good |
| Change/archive semantics | OpenSpec archive syncs delta specs into main specs, then archives change folder. | Good |
| Source-of-truth spec | OpenSpec specs are authoritative. Spec Kit constitution/spec/spec/plan chain. Paper spec-as-source extreme. | Good, but not too rigid |
| Workflow state/resume | Spec Kit workflow runs persist state; resume exact step. | Good if bead jobs need pause/resume |

## Borrow / adapt / reject

### Borrow
- **Artifact chain**: proposal/spec/plan/tasks, with explicit handoff between artifacts.
- **Validation step**: separate “artifact sanity” from “implementation matches spec” checks.
- **Trace links**: every task/decision should point back to spec requirement.
- **Story-scoped tasks**: tasks grouped by user story, with parallel flags where safe.
- **Archive semantics**: close only after sync/validation; keep archive history.

### Adapt
- **Gates**: use human approval only at high-risk boundaries, not every micro-step.
- **Resume**: keep pause/resume for long specialist runs, but map to bead state, not CLI workflow state.
- **Templates**: use strict templates, but keep them short so agents do not drown in ceremony.
- **Delta specs**: good for brownfield changes; adapt to bead dependency graph + issue notes.

### Reject
- **Spec-as-source strictness**: too rigid for beads/specialists. Local workflow needs iterative human/AI edits, not “only regenerate, never hand-edit.”
- **Heavy waterfall**: bad fit when discovery still open. OpenSpec’s own docs prefer fluid/iterative; keep that.
- **Over-specification**: paper warns specs can become pseudo-code and bureaucracy. Same risk here.
- **Archive-without-verification**: OpenSpec archive can warn but still proceed; beads should not treat that as done for important work.

## Risks
- **OpenSpec beta workspace/state**: workspace behavior still evolving; do not treat as stable foundation.
- **Spec Kit command drift**: slash commands and template paths may change by release.
- **Strict lifecycle mismatch**: beads already has issue/dependency semantics; do not mirror all framework phases 1:1.

## Follow-ups
- Next useful step: design local bead template for **proposal / spec / plan / tasks / validate / archive** with thin, explicit handoffs.
- Next useful guardrail: add “done only after validation + spec sync” rule for close.

## Sources consulted
- OpenSpec README/getting-started/commands/workflows/cli/concepts. URLs above.
- GitHub Spec Kit README/spec-driven/workflows/templates. URLs above.
- arXiv SDD paper. URL above.

description:
PROBLEM: found via live multi-turn smoke (job 55edb8, bead unitAI-8t1t6: keep-alive smoke-echo → sp resume → sp stop). TWO issues in the 10y07 handoff persistence:

(1) NO canonical [FINAL · DONE] block on sp stop. Requirement #3 (final dones) fires on NATURAL termination (verified: single-turn non-keepalive job 277196 got a [FINAL · DONE] block via terminal path supervisor.ts ~2168/2181) but NOT when a keep-alive job is ended via 'sp stop' (which auto-closes the bead). The finalizeWaitingJob (supervisor.ts ~791) path does not emit the {final:true} formatHandoffBlock. IMPACT: keep-alive + sp stop is the DOMINANT workflow (all epic 544sf research children); the canonical block a downstream 'read previous note' consumer greps for never materializes — only [turn N · WAITING] blocks exist. Demo bead unitAI-8t1t6 shows 4 blocks, 0 FINAL.

(2) Per-turn DOUBLE-WRITE: each turn appends BOTH a '[turn N · WORKING]' block (footer status=done) AND a '[turn N · WAITING]' block — identical content twice. appendResultToInputBead is invoked on turn-complete (status done → WORKING token) then again on waiting-status set (→ WAITING token). Noisy for full-trail; the WORKING-header/status=done-footer is also self-contradictory.

SCOPE: src/specialist/supervisor.ts (finalizeWaitingJob ~791, the sp-stop/auto-close path, appendResultToInputBead call sites, statusToken WORKING vs done). VALIDATION: keep-alive run → resume → sp stop yields exactly one [FINAL · DONE] block + one block per substantive turn (no WORKING+WAITING duplication). Add a test covering the finalize-on-stop path. Discovered-from unitAI-10y07. Minor also: model string inconsistency (with/without provider prefix) between WORKING and WAITING blocks.

title: feat(supervisor): 3-state handoff persistence + notes_mode + output_file unification
description:
PROBLEM: per-turn handoff notes (post-sx5qk --append-notes) work, but (a) a downstream specialist instructed to read the previous bead note can't deterministically locate the canonical answer among appended turn blocks, and (b) output_file (runner.ts:1455) writes RAW final output only, never the turn summaries, in a different layer than the per-turn writer. Make handoff persistence clean and unify the sinks.

SUCCESS — persist THREE distinct, clearly-marked states (operator requirement):
  1. SUBSTANTIAL TURN SUMMARIES captured AS THEY HAPPEN (not only on agent stop) — each non-empty turn lands mid-run (the trail).
  2. KEEP-ALIVE WAITING persists — a parked keep-alive job's latest turn stays visible with a [WAITING] status marker.
  3. FINAL DONE — the terminal turn is an unmistakable, greppable [FINAL]/[DONE] block.
Downstream 'read previous note' instructions target the terminal block deterministically (by status token, never by guessing). notes_mode=final-only collapses the trail to just the canonical block.

SCRUTINY: high (runtime core: src/specialist/supervisor.ts + schema.ts; reviewer auto-escalates schema.ts → gitnexus_impact required).

SCOPE:
  - src/specialist/supervisor.ts — formatBeadNotes (166) rename→formatHandoffBlock(result,{final}); appendResultToInputBead (1411) per-turn writer; terminal writers (2168/2181); finalizeWaitingJob (791) hook.
  - src/specialist/runner.ts — output_file write (1455): remove raw write; route through the unified writer.
  - src/specialist/schema.ts — add notes_mode: z.enum(['full-trail','final-only']).default('full-trail').
  - src/specialist/job-file-output.ts — reuse isJobFileOutputEnabled gate.
  - tests: extend tests/unit/specialist/supervisor-bead-notes.test.ts (DEFAULT-suite; do NOT touch supervisor.test.ts — excluded, FIFO hang) + bead-notes/output-file tests.

FORMAT (header status taxonomy, greppable):
  - intermediate substantive turn:  divider '____'(70) + '### 🔬 <specialist> · <model> · [turn N · WORKING]'
  - parked keep-alive turn:          '[turn N · WAITING]'
  - terminal:                         heavy rule '════'(70) + '### ✅ <specialist> · <model> · [FINAL · DONE]' (or [FINAL · FAIL]/[FINAL · ERROR]/[FINAL · CANCELLED])
  - footer metadata unchanged set: timestamp,status,specialist,job_id,turn_index,model,backend,prompt_hash,git_sha,elapsed_ms,token usage.

IMPLEMENTATION:
  1. Rename formatBeadNotes→formatHandoffBlock(result,{final:boolean}); final=true → heavy rule + ✅ + [FINAL · <STATUS>]; else light rule + [turn N · <STATUS>]. Keep tokenUsage wiring.
  2. Skip append when result.output.trim() is empty (kills empty [WAITING] envelopes — root of the sx5qk noise).
  3. Per-turn (req 1): appendResultToInputBead keeps appending each SUBSTANTIVE turn as it completes (turn_summary), independent of stop.

  7. output_file unification: thread output_file into the supervisor handoff writer; ONE formatter, TWO sinks (bead note + output_file). full-trail→append per turn to output_file; final-only→overwrite output_file with the [FINAL] block. AWS summit raised 'datadog/snowflake = agentic monitoring done well; reproduce/copy features = appetible'. Operator question: how far can grafana go before scaling needed? Can we build an agentic monitoring pipeline where specialists watch metrics + auto-suggest fixes?

SCOPE:
- Datadog core features that AREN'T already in our stack (alerting, anomaly detection, distributed tracing, log aggregation, dashboards)
- Snowflake what's relevant (data warehouse for cross-repo observability? cost prohibitive?)
- Grafana integration: does our observability.db expose Prometheus-compatible metrics? what does a grafana dashboard look like over our existing data?
- Agentic monitoring pattern: specialist subscribes to metric thresholds, wakes on anomaly, suggests/applies fix, has memory of prior suggestions to avoid re-suggesting (per backlog 09/05/26 note)
- Cross-reference: existing memory specialist-runtime-runtime-has-6-architectural-asymmetries; observability.db structure; sp log canonical event stream

OUTPUTS expected:
- Capability gap matrix: nostre superfici vs Datadog vs Grafana
- Agentic-monitoring pattern: spec sketch for a 'monitor' specialist (sleeps subscribed to metric thresholds, wakes, with memory of suggestions made)
- Recommendation: grafana integration as immediate next-step? building monitor specialist as roadmap addition? skip Datadog (lock-in / cost)?
- Boundary: what should live in observability.db vs ship to grafana vs ship to external (Datadog/Snowflake)

NON_GOALS: no installation; no metric exporters built; no monitor specialist drafted.

VALIDATION: memo with capability matrix + monitor-specialist spec sketch + recommendation per integration target.

### 🔬 researcher · openai-codex/gpt-5.4-mini · [WAITING — more output may follow]

## Summary
Grafana first. Datadog already has bigger managed surface; Snowflake fits cold cross-repo warehouse, not hot alert loop.  
Our stack already has enough bones: SQLite canonical stream, `sp log`/`sp feed`, channels/wakes, and memory tables. No Prometheus exporter found, so Grafana needs adapter/ETL/plugin.

## Status

## Changes

## Capability gap matrix

| Capability | Our stack | Datadog | Grafana | Snowflake | Take |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Alerting | `sp ps` dashboard-ish view, pulses/channels exist, but no alert rules UI; `sp log` is runtime stream over SQLite (`README.md`, `docs/cli-reference.md`, `src/specialist/observability-sqlite.ts`) | Monitors + notifications + downtimes; proactive detection and real-time response. https://docs.datadoghq.com/monitors/ (accessed 2026-05-29) | Grafana Alerting watches metrics/logs from multiple data sources, with notifications and triage. https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/alerting/ (accessed 2026-05-29) | Not alert plane | Grafana now |
| Anomaly detection | No native engine found; would need baseline logic / new service | Built-in anomaly monitors with seasonality, windows, preview graphs, API. https://docs.datadoghq.com/monitors/types/anomaly/ (accessed 2026-05-29) | Grafana Cloud has forecasts/anomaly detection. https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/machine-learning/dynamic-alerting/forecasting/ (accessed 2026-05-29); core Grafana docs center on alerting, not native OSS anomaly engine | Snowflake has cost anomaly ideas, but for warehouse usage | Monitor specialist needed |
| Logs | `sp log` is canonical runtime/debug stream; `sp feed` replay; child-repo aggregation; SQLite-backed | Log Management: ingest, process, archive, Live Tail, analytics, patterns; log/metric/trace correlation. https://docs.datadoghq.com/logs/ (accessed 2026-05-29) | Loki / Elasticsearch core sources; generic data-source model. https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/datasources.md (accessed 2026-05-29) | Not log plane | Keep raw in `observability.db`; export curated view |
| Traces | None today | APM distributed tracing, Trace Explorer, trace↔logs/metrics correlation. https://docs.datadoghq.com/tracing/ (accessed 2026-05-29) | Tempo / Jaeger / Zipkin core sources. https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/datasources.md (accessed 2026-05-29) | Not trace plane | Later only |
| Dashboards | CLI dashboard-ish surfaces only; no web panels | Dashboards/timeboards/screenboards. https://docs.datadoghq.com/dashboards/ (accessed 2026-05-29) | Panels + Explore over many sources; built-in data sources + plugins. https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/datasources.md (accessed 2026-05-29) | Not dashboard plane | Grafana immediate |
| Cross-repo warehouse | SQLite per repo; no `/metrics` or `Prometheus` hit in `src` grep; `sp log` can aggregate child repo DBs | Managed SaaS, strong correlation, but lock-in | Can correlate many sources; core SQL sources are MSSQL/MySQL/PostgreSQL, not SQLite. https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/datasources.md (accessed 2026-05-29) | Good for long-horizon warehouse analytics; credits by warehouse size/runtime, billed per-second with 60s minimum. https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/cost-understanding-compute (accessed 2026-05-29) | Snowflake only cold/history |

## Monitor-specialist spec sketch

```json
  "wake_sources": [
```

- **Grafana now**: best immediate read layer + alert UI. But need adapter, because `observability.db` is SQLite and Grafana core SQL sources don’t include SQLite.

## Summary

`sp epic` CLI surface provides 5 subcommands (list/status/sync/abandon/merge) that manage specialist-side wave/chain observability state. Core functionality: (1) `epic_runs` table stores persisted lifecycle state (open/merge_ready/merged/failed/abandoned), (2) `epic_chain_membership` table tracks chain→epic linkage, (3) derived readiness is computed live from chain job statuses. Substantial redundancy with `bd` exists: `bd children` is called to resolve epic children; `bd show` resolves bead parent for epic inference. However, `sp epic` owns merge orchestration (`sp epic merge` publishes topologically-sorted chains with tsc gates), readiness evaluation (reviewer verdict parsing, chain pass/fail derivation), and terminal-state `epic_runs` bookkeeping that `bd` does not model.

## Architecture

**Data Model:**

| Table | Schema Location | Purpose |
|-------|-----------------|---------|
| `epic_runs` | `observability-sqlite.ts:642-647` | Persisted lifecycle state (epic_id PK, status, status_json, updated_at_ms) |
| `epic_chain_membership` | `observability-sqlite.ts:652-660` | Chain→epic linkage (chain_id PK, epic_id, chain_root_bead_id, chain_root_job_id) |
| `specialist_jobs.epic_id` | `observability-sqlite.ts:422,1096-1123` | Job→epic association; indexed for efficient epic-scoped queries |

**Lifecycle States** (`epic-lifecycle.ts:18`):
- Terminal: `merged`, `failed`, `abandoned`
- Non-terminal: `open`, `resolving`, `merge_ready`
- Derived readiness states (`epic-readiness.ts:20`): `pending`, `blocked`, `pass`, `failed` → mapped to `EpicReadinessState` (`unresolved`, `resolving`, `blocked`, `failed`, `merge_ready`, `merged`, `abandoned`)

**Key Flows:**

1. **`sp run --epic <id>`** (`run.ts:114,125-130`): passes `epicId` to `SupervisorOptions`; supervisor upserts `epic_runs`, `epic_chain_membership`, and syncs derived readiness (`supervisor.ts:947-973`).

2. **`sp ps`** (`ps.ts:320-322,687-735`): groups jobs by `epic_id`, loads readiness summaries, renders epic banners with `readiness_state` + `persisted_state`.

3. **`sp epic list`** (`epic.ts:285-318,478-511`): reads `sqlite.listEpicRuns()`, evaluates per-epic readiness, filters `--unresolved`.

4. **`sp epic merge`** (`epic.ts:344-437`): gathers context via `bd children` + `sqlite.listEpicChains`, validates readiness, publishes chains topologically via `executePublicationPlan`, transitions persisted state.

5. **`sp epic sync`** (`epic.ts:573-635`): drift detection (dead jobs, stale chain refs, integrity flags) + optional apply (`markDeadJobsAsError`, prune stale memberships, resync readiness).

6. **`sp epic abandon`** (`epic.ts:657-680`): force-terminates epic with `--reason`; blocks on `merged`/`abandoned`, requires `--force` for live members.

7. **`sp end --epic <id>`** (`end.ts:125-146`): short-circuits to `handleEpicMergeCommand(['merge', epicId, ...])`.

8. **Epic guard for standalone merge** (`merge.ts:514`): `checkEpicUnresolvedGuard` blocks `sp merge <chain>` if chain belongs to unresolved epic; `sp epic merge` is canonical path.

## (3) Redundancy vs bd

| Function | sp epic | bd equivalent | Verdict |
|----------|---------|---------------|---------|
| Enumerate epic children | `bd children <epicId>` (`epic.ts:251`, `merge.ts:215,231`) | `bd children` is authoritative | Duplication (read-only call) |
| Resolve epic ID from bead | `readBeadSummary(beadId).parent` + `issue_type==='epic'` check (`run.ts:206-212`) | `bd show --json` returns `parent` | Duplication |
| Track epic state machine | `epic_runs.status` + transition guards | `bd` has no native epic lifecycle state | No overlap |
| Chain readiness evaluation | Reviewer verdict parsing, dead-job detection | `bd` has no job-state tracking | No overlap |
| Multi-chain topological merge | `executePublicationPlan` with tsc gate | `bd` has no merge orchestration | No overlap |

**Conclusion:** `sp epic` duplicates `bd` for *epic child enumeration* and *epic ID inference* (reads only). All write operations (lifecycle transitions, readiness derivation, merge orchestration) are sp-owned with no `bd` equivalent.

---

## (4) Load-bearing in sp (not in bd)

1. **Derived readiness evaluation** (`epic-readiness.ts`): Live computation of per-chain `pass`/`blocked`/`pending`/`failed` from reviewer verdicts + active job detection. `bd` has no job-state observability.

2. **Terminal-state bookkeeping** (`epic_runs`): `merged`, `failed`, `abandoned` are persisted for audit and dashboard filtering. `bd` issue tracker has separate status namespace.

3. **Merge orchestration** (`epic.ts:mergeEpicChains`, `merge.ts:executePublicationPlan`): Topological sort of chains, per-merge tsc gate, dirty-tree auto-shelve, dependency-order publishing. `bd` does not orchestrate git merges.

4. **Drift repair** (`epic-reconciler.ts:syncEpicState`): Dead-job detection → mark `error`, stale chain ref pruning, readiness resync. Specialist-side consistency enforcement.

5. **Epic guard for standalone merges** (`merge.ts:checkEpicUnresolvedGuard`): Blocks `sp merge <chain>` when chain belongs to unresolved epic; enforces `sp epic merge` as canonical publication path for epic-bound work.

| Pattern | Source | Evidence |
|---------|--------|----------|
| `sp epic merge` fails on dirty tree → epic transitions to terminal `failed` with no CLI recovery | `2026-05-04-2b52300a.md:240` | "Manual git merge --no-ff per chain is the documented fallback, but skips tsc/conflict gates" |
| Epic state machine got tangled when keep-alive jobs stopped → `failed` instead of `merge_ready` | `2026-04-26-523fc559.md:116,131` | "Used direct git merge --no-ff instead of sp epic merge" |
| `sp epic merge` "dependency cycle detected" with multiple chain roots per bead | `2026-05-04-2b52300a.md:241,457` | "Failed retry chains coexist in epic_runs alongside successful chains" |
| `sp epic merge` refused on already-merged chains → wedged epic into `failed` | `2026-04-29-e9919694.md:85` | Fixed by `unitAI-tejk7` (idempotency pass/skip) |
| `failed` persisted state blocked recovery even after chains went PASS | `2026-05-08-1e257afe.md:157` | Fixed: relaxed validation to only block `merged`/`abandoned`, not persisted `failed` |
| Auto-commit filters `.xtrm/` paths → unstaged changes block rebase | `2026-05-04-2b52300a.md:599,648` | Memory: `auto_commit-filters-xtrm-paths-blocks-sp-epic-merge-rebase` |

**Common theme:** `sp epic merge` is fragile when repo state diverges from expected (dirty tree, retry chains, unstaged noise). Operators frequently fallback to manual `git merge --no-ff`.

## (6) Recommended deprecation candidates

| Candidate | Reasoning |
|-----------|-----------|
| `sp epic resolve` | Already deleted (`unitAI-aurbi.10`). No longer needed — derived readiness replaced explicit transition. |
| `sp epic status` (subcommand) | Could be thin wrapper: `echo "SELECT * FROM epic_runs WHERE epic_id=?"; sp ps --json \| jq`. Low utility vs `sp ps` epic groups. |
| `sp epic list` | Thin wrapper over `sqlite.listEpicRuns()` + readiness eval; could be `sp ps --include-terminal --json \| jq '.epics[]'`. |
| `sp epic sync` | Valuable for drift repair, but rarely used; operator-facing `sp ps` already derives live state. Consider deprecating CLI, keeping `syncEpicState` as internal repair. |

**Keep:**
- `sp epic merge`: Core value (topological publish + tsc gate); no `bd` equivalent.
- `sp epic abandon`: Terminal-state bookkeeping required for audit trail.

---

## (7) Recommended decoration pattern

| Verb | Current Implementation | Decoration / Thin Wrapper |
|------|------------------------|---------------------------|
| `sp epic list` | Full evaluation loop (`epic.ts:285-318`) | `sqlite.listEpicRuns()` → `loadEpicReadinessSummary` per row; could be `sp ps --include-terminal --json \| jq` + post-process. Read-only; candidate for thin wrapper. |
| `sp epic status` | Reads `epic_runs`, `epic_chain_membership`, runs `evaluateReadiness` | Subset of `sp ps` epic-group rendering. Decoration: `sp ps --json \| jq '.epics[] | select(.epic_id=="$ID")'`. |
| `sp epic sync` | Internal `syncEpicState()` call + drift report | Keep as internal repair; CLI surface adds little vs `sp doctor --epic <id>` pattern. |
| `sp epic abandon` | Write `epic_runs.status='abandoned'`, audit trail in `status_json` | Requires write; cannot be decoration. Keep as-is. |
| `sp epic merge` | Topological publish, git ops, state transition | Cannot be decoration. Core orchestration. |

**Pattern:** Commands that *only read* `epic_runs` + evaluate derived state (`list`, `status`) are strong decoration candidates — they duplicate `sp ps` epic-group rendering. Commands that *write* (`merge`, `abandon`) remain full implementations.

title: feat: add execution.bare mode + shipped bare.specialist.json template (zero runtime injection)
description:
PROBLEM
Package-class specialists (sp run) always have ~9 runtime injection blocks layered onto the prompt by runner.ts — Specialist Run Context, caveman output style, GitNexus mandate, STATIC_WORKFLOW_RULES_BLOCK, memory injection, GitNexus pre-query, reviewer-only injections, output contract, plus mandatory_rules layered onto the task message. For non-coding specialists (researchers, document analyzers, news summarizers, anything that is not a coding agent) these injections are noise: irrelevant instructions, tokens, and behavioral framing the author did not ask for. There is no way today to opt out as a whole — `system_prompt_mode: "replace"` only kills pi's coding-agent base prompt, leaving the 9 specialist-runtime injections untouched. Authors who want a truly fresh canvas have no clean path.

SUCCESS
- A new optional `execution.bare: boolean` field exists with default `false` (backward compatible).
- When `execution.bare: true`, the package-class runner injects NOTHING beyond the rendered `prompt.system` (into agentsMd) and the rendered `prompt.task_template` (into renderedTask). Specifically gated off:
  Channel A — agentsMd (system prompt) appendages:
    1. Specialist Run Context block (runner.ts:1080-1088)
    2. Output Style / caveman block (runner.ts:1092-1103)
    3. GitNexus mandate (runner.ts:1104-1124)
    4. STATIC_WORKFLOW_RULES_BLOCK (runner.ts:1134-1135)
    5. Memory injection block (runner.ts:1144-1150)
    6. GitNexus pre-query snapshot (runner.ts:1155-1196)
    7. Reviewer patch retrieval (runner.ts:1239-1241)
    8. Output contract instruction (runner.ts:1247)
  Channel B — renderedTask (task message) appendages:
    9. mandatoryRulesBlock concat (runner.ts:1037-1052)
    10. Reviewer diff context (runner.ts:1054-1061)
- `execution.bare` is independent of `prompt.system_prompt_mode` — they compose orthogonally. An author who sets `bare: true` without `system_prompt_mode: "replace"` still gets pi's coding-agent base prompt (their choice; no validator hard-fail).
- A reference template specialist ships at `config/specialists/bare.specialist.json` with: `category: "template"`, `tags: ["template", "bare-mode", "copy-me"]`, a description that starts with "TEMPLATE — do not dispatch.", and a `prompt.system` body that demonstrates how to teach an agent autonomously (commands, output schema, termination condition, tool list — all in plain prose).
- The specialists-creator skill documents the bare mode: when to use, how to copy from the installed npm package (not from a repo clone), what gets disabled, and the orthogonality of `bare` and `system_prompt_mode`.
- A smoke test verifies that for `execution.bare: true`, none of the 9+ injected strings appear in the assembled agentsMd or renderedTask.

SCOPE
- `src/specialist/schema.ts`: add `bare: z.boolean().default(false)` to `ExecutionSchema` (alongside `extensions`, `requires_worktree`, etc.).
- `src/specialist/runner.ts`: wrap each of the 10 injection sites listed above in `if (!execution.bare) { ... }`. The reviewer-specific sites (1054, 1239) already have `metadata.name === 'reviewer'` gates — keep those AND add the bare gate.
- `config/specialists/bare.specialist.json`: new file. Full schema-valid spec with bare:true, system_prompt_mode: "replace", extensions.serena/gitnexus: false, permission_required: READ_ONLY, category: "template", tags include "template", description starts "TEMPLATE — do not dispatch. Copy from the installed @jaggerxtrm/specialists package to .specialists/user/<your-name>.specialist.json...". prompt.system body is a multi-paragraph teaching example showing how an author would brief a totally fresh agent (no commands assumed, explicit output schema, explicit termination condition).
- `config/skills/specialists-creator/SKILL.md`: new h3 subsection "Bare specialists" placed inside the Schema Reference section near "specialist.execution". Subsection includes: when bare mode is appropriate (non-coding LLM transforms), what gets disabled (link to or repeat the 10-site list at high level), orthogonality with `system_prompt_mode`, the exact `cp` command to copy from the installed npm package (NOT from a repo clone) using `node -p "require.resolve('@jaggerxtrm/specialists/package.json').replace(/package\\.json$/, '')..."`, and an explicit warning that `mandatory_rules` (all fields) are also bypassed in bare mode.
- `tests/unit/specialist/runner.test.ts` (or the closest existing file): add a unit test asserting that when `execution.bare: true`, the assembled `agentsMd` and `renderedTask` strings do NOT contain identifiable injection markers: "Specialist Run Context", "Output Style (mandatory)", "MANDATORY: GitNexus Code Intelligence", the STATIC_WORKFLOW_RULES_BLOCK header text, "GitNexus Pre-query Snapshot", "Reviewer patch retrieval", "Output Contract", any mandatoryRulesBlock content. Test the inverse (default `bare: false`) still gets those injections to lock the gate to bare-mode only.

NON_GOALS
- Do not change `system_prompt_mode` behavior or its defaults.
- Do not change `script-runner.ts` — script-class already injects nothing.
- Do not change mandatory_rules.ts internals or the index.json behavior.
- Do not auto-set `system_prompt_mode: "replace"` when `bare: true` — keep orthogonal.
- Do not add a CLI flag `--bare` to `sp run` (the spec controls behavior).
- Do not migrate any existing specialist to bare mode.
- Do not add a `--no-templates` filter to `specialists list` (future enhancement, separate bead).
- Do not change the loader to special-case template specialists — `bare.specialist.json` loads like any other, the category/tags/description carry the warning.

CONSTRAINTS
- `bare` default must be `false` — every existing specialist must behave identically.
- The 10 injection sites must each be gated independently with a single `if (!execution.bare)` block; do not refactor the surrounding code or change injection content.
- Reviewer-only injections (1054, 1239) keep their `metadata.name === 'reviewer'` gate AND get the bare gate added as the outer condition (a bare reviewer would still skip them, even though running a bare reviewer makes no sense).
- The bare template`s `prompt.system` content must be a realistic, working teaching example — not a stub. It should demonstrate the contract an author writes: role, tools available, output format, termination condition.
- Copy command in skill must use `node -p "require.resolve(...)"` form (the robust npm-prefix-agnostic version), not `npm root -g` (which varies across nvm setups).
- Schema additions are minimal: one `bare: z.boolean().default(false)` line. No new sections, no new files in `src/specialist/`.

VALIDATION
- `bun run lint` passes.
- `bunx vitest run tests/unit/specialist/` passes, including the new bare-mode injection test (both directions: bare:true skips, bare:false injects).
- `specialists list` shows the bare specialist with the "TEMPLATE — do not dispatch" first clause.
- `bun config/skills/specialists-creator/scripts/validate-specialist.ts config/specialists/bare.specialist.json` returns OK.
- Manual grep: `grep -nE "if \(!execution\.bare\)" src/specialist/runner.ts` returns at least 8 hits (one per injection site).

OUTPUT
Changed/added files, test proof (new test name + pass count), grep evidence for the gate hits, residual risks (especially: any injection sites I may have missed in the scope above).

title: docs(specialists-creator): document system_prompt_mode, mandatory_rules, and script-class vs package-class runtime divergence
description:
PROBLEM
The /specialists-creator skill (config/skills/specialists-creator/SKILL.md) drifted from runtime reality on three fronts:

(1) `prompt.system_prompt_mode: "append" | "replace"` (added in unitAI-qngis, commit 78a7883e) is not mentioned anywhere. Spec authors have no guidance on when to use replace vs append, and no warning that replace mode strips pi's coding-agent base prompt — meaning the author must teach the agent every command/tool/convention explicitly in `prompt.system`.

(2) `mandatory_rules` (schema.ts:99-103) — `template_sets`, `disable_default_globals`, `inline_rules` — is documented only as a one-line example in the "Canonical References" intro. Nowhere does the skill explain how rules layer, what `disable_default_globals` actually disables (only `STATIC_WORKFLOW_RULES_BLOCK`), what `required_template_sets` / `default_template_sets` from `config/mandatory-rules/index.json` are, or how to truly opt into a user-rules-only setup.

(3) Script-class vs package-class runtime divergence is not documented. Script-runner (script-runner.ts) IGNORES `mandatory_rules` entirely — script specialists are bare LLM transforms that only receive `prompt.system` + rendered `task_template`. Package-runner (runner.ts) builds a much larger `agentsMd` with STATIC_WORKFLOW_RULES, mandatory rules, memory injection, GitNexus mandate, Specialist Run Context block, caveman output style, output contract, etc. A spec author needs to know which surface their specialist runs on, because `mandatory_rules` settings silently do nothing on script-class.

SUCCESS
Update config/skills/specialists-creator/SKILL.md with three new top-level sections plus targeted edits to the existing Schema Reference:

A. New section "System Prompt Mode" (after "specialist.prompt" subsection of Schema Reference):
   - Field syntax: `prompt.system_prompt_mode: "append" | "replace"` (optional)
   - Default behavior PER RUNNER when field absent:
     * Package-class (sp run via runner.ts → session.ts): append (legacy)
     * Script-class (sp script/serve via script-runner.ts): replace (legacy)
   - Truth table of 4 combinations (package×append, package×replace, script×append, script×replace) explaining what the agent sees:
     * append → agent sees pi's coding-agent base prompt + specialist agentsMd (or prompt.system for script)
     * replace → agent sees ONLY specialist agentsMd (or prompt.system for script)
   - **Replace-mode warning (mandatory call-out)**: When using `replace`, pi's coding-agent default prompt is GONE. The author must explicitly teach the agent every command, tool, convention, output format, and behavioural rule it needs. No implicit "you are a coding assistant" framing remains. Recommended for non-coding LLM transforms (researchers, summarizers, analyzers) where the coding-agent base adds noise.

B. New section "Mandatory Rules" (new top-level Schema Reference subsection between "specialist.skills" and "specialist.capabilities"):
   - Field shapes: `mandatory_rules.template_sets: string[]`, `disable_default_globals: boolean (default false)`, `inline_rules: MandatoryRule[]`
   - Index-driven layering: `config/mandatory-rules/index.json` has `required_template_sets` (always loaded, NOT suppressed by disable_default_globals) and `default_template_sets` (also always loaded — note this is currently a quirk; the only thing disable_default_globals actually disables is the inline STATIC_WORKFLOW_RULES_BLOCK).
   - What disable_default_globals ACTUALLY does: suppresses only the "Beads Workflow Quick Rules" block. Does NOT suppress index-driven sets. To get a true user-rules-only setup the operator must also override the index file via `.specialists/user/mandatory-rules/index.json`.
   - Reference set listing: name the existing sets in `config/mandatory-rules/*.md` (bead-id-verbatim, changelog-conventions, code-quality-defaults, diagnose-loop, executor-delivery, explorer-readonly, git-workflow-safe, gitnexus-required, core-session-boundary, etc — list them all from `ls config/mandatory-rules/`).
   - Sample minimal "user rules only" spec snippet using both `disable_default_globals: true` AND `inline_rules`.
   - Inline rule shape: `{ id, level: "error"|"warn"|"info", text, when? }`.

C. New section "Script-Class vs Package-Class Runtime" (new top-level section after "File Placement"):
   - Explain the two specialist runtime classes (sp run vs sp script / sp serve).
   - Table listing what each runner injects into the system prompt:
     * Package: prompt.system + Specialist Run Context + caveman output style + GitNexus mandate (if .gitnexus exists) + STATIC_WORKFLOW_RULES_BLOCK + memory injection + mandatory rules + skills inheritance + output contract + reviewer patch retrieval (if reviewer reusing executor workspace)
     * Script: prompt.system ONLY
   - Pi flags: package always uses --no-extensions then re-enables quality-gates/service-skills/caveman/gitnexus/serena. Script uses --no-extensions --no-tools --offline --no-context-files --no-prompt-templates --no-themes (and --no-skills when skills.paths is empty).
   - "Settings that silently do nothing on script-class": mandatory_rules (all sub-fields), beads injection, GitNexus mandate, memory injection, output contract auto-generation (script handles json/markdown contract differently).
   - Per-runner default for `system_prompt_mode` repeated here so spec authors don't miss it.

D. Targeted edit to existing "specialist.prompt" subsection of Schema Reference:
   - Add `system_prompt_mode` row to the field table with brief notes + link to new "System Prompt Mode" section.
   - Add an inline warning under the table referencing the replace-mode caveat.

E. Bump skill version frontmatter from `1.2` to `1.3` and update `synced_at` (recompute or set to a short commit-style placeholder; the executor should use `git rev-parse --short HEAD` of master post-merge for the value).

SCOPE
- config/skills/specialists-creator/SKILL.md — full file scope; add new sections, edit existing prompt table, bump version frontmatter.

NON_GOALS
- Do not modify any source files (src/, tests/, config/specialists/*.json, config/mandatory-rules/*.md).
- Do not modify other skill files (.xtrm/skills/, .claude/skills/, other config/skills/ folders).
- Do not change the existing "Canonical References" or "ACTION REQUIRED" sections — only add new sections after them.
- Do not invent additional schema fields. Only document what schema.ts actually defines.
- Do not change scaffold-specialist.ts behavior or templates.

CONSTRAINTS
- Stay factually accurate vs runtime — verify each claim against src/specialist/schema.ts, src/specialist/runner.ts, src/specialist/script-runner.ts, src/specialist/mandatory-rules.ts, config/mandatory-rules/index.json before writing.
- Keep the existing tone (operational, terse, table-heavy, code-block heavy).
- Use the same markdown style as existing sections (no emojis, no headers deeper than h4).
- Replace-mode warning must be prominent — use a blockquote or bold call-out, not buried in a paragraph.
- Preserve all existing examples and tables verbatim; new content goes in new sections or as additive rows.

VALIDATION

- `grep -n "script-class\|package-class\|script.runner\|package.runner" config/skills/specialists-creator/SKILL.md` returns at least 4 hits.
- The new sections appear in TOC-style reading order (after Schema Reference for A and B; after File Placement for C).

OUTPUT

title: feat: add system_prompt_mode append|replace field to specialist prompt schema (both runner paths)
description:
PROBLEM
Package-class specialists (sp run) always call pi with --append-system-prompt, giving the specialist no way to run with a clean system prompt — the pi coding-agent base prompt is always prepended. Script-class specialists (sp script/serve) always call pi with --system-prompt (full replace), giving spec authors no way to opt into append mode. Neither path exposes a spec-level field to control this behavior. Non-coding specialists on the package-class path carry irrelevant coding instructions and token overhead; there is no escape hatch.

SUCCESS
- A new optional field `system_prompt_mode: "append" | "replace"` exists on the `prompt` section of the specialist JSON schema with no default (field is optional).
- Package-class runner (session.ts): when field is absent, behavior is unchanged (`--append-system-prompt`). When `"replace"`, uses `--system-prompt`.
- Script-class runner (script-runner.ts): when field is absent, behavior is unchanged (`--system-prompt` when prompt.system is set). When `"append"`, uses `--append-system-prompt` instead.
- All existing specialists continue to behave identically — no field set means no behavior change on either path.
- Tests cover all four combinations: script-class replace (existing), script-class append (new), package-class append (existing), package-class replace (new).

SCOPE
- `src/specialist/schema.ts` lines 46-57: Add `system_prompt_mode: z.enum(["append", "replace"]).optional()` (no default) to `PromptSchema`. Update the corresponding TypeScript exported type if one is derived from the schema.
- `src/pi/session.ts` lines 99-147: Add `systemPromptMode?: "append" | "replace"` to `PiSessionOptions` interface.
- `src/pi/session.ts` line 652: Change unconditional `--append-system-prompt` to conditional: use `--system-prompt` when `systemPromptMode === "replace"`, else `--append-system-prompt`.
- `src/specialist/runner.ts` lines 1325-1335: In the `sessionFactory` call, plumb `systemPromptMode: prompt.system_prompt_mode` alongside existing `systemPrompt: agentsMd`.
- `src/specialist/script-runner.ts` lines 520-530: Change the `--system-prompt` push to conditional: when `spec.specialist.prompt.system_prompt_mode === "append"` use `--append-system-prompt`, otherwise use `--system-prompt` (preserving current default-replace behavior).
- `tests/unit/pi/session.test.ts` lines 362-366: Add a companion test asserting that when `systemPromptMode: "replace"` is passed, `--system-prompt` is used and `--append-system-prompt` is absent.
- `tests/unit/specialist/script-runner.test.ts` lines 629-643: Add a companion test asserting that when `system_prompt_mode: "append"` is set on the spec, `--append-system-prompt` is used and `--system-prompt` is absent.

NON_GOALS
- Do not add system_prompt_mode to the ExecutionSchema section — it belongs on prompt.
- Do not update any existing specialist JSON files — absent field means legacy behavior on both paths.
- Do not change the agentsMd construction logic in runner.ts — the field only controls which pi flag receives the already-built prompt string.
- No documentation or skill file updates in this bead.
- Do not change what happens when prompt.system is absent/empty in script-runner — existing early-return behavior is unchanged.

CONSTRAINTS
- No schema-level default. Each runner uses its own legacy fallback when the field is absent: script-runner falls back to replace, session.ts falls back to append. This is the only way to preserve backward compat for both paths simultaneously.
- Use `z.enum(["append", "replace"]).optional()` (Zod 3 syntax — project is on Zod 3, migration to Zod 4 is a separate open bead unitAI-a5ys3).
- Both `--system-prompt` and `--append-system-prompt` are confirmed present in `pi --help`. No compat guard needed.
- Preserve the existing tests at session.test.ts:362-366 and script-runner.test.ts:600-643 unchanged. Add new companion tests alongside them.
- Schema uses `.passthrough()` so the new optional field is non-breaking.

VALIDATION
- `bun run lint` passes (ESLint + tsc) after all changes.
- `bun --bun vitest run tests/unit/pi/session.test.ts` passes including the new replace-mode test.
- `bun --bun vitest run tests/unit/specialist/script-runner.test.ts` passes including the new append-mode test.
- `bun --bun vitest run tests/unit/specialist/` passes full specialist unit suite with no regressions.

## Summary

Two divergent paths exist for system prompt handling. Script-runner uses `--system-prompt` (full replace). Package-class runner via PiAgentSession uses `--append-system-prompt` (always appends). No schema field exists for authors to control mode. Implementation requires 4 targeted changes.

## Evidence Map

### 1. Script-runner path: `--system-prompt` (full replace)

**File: `src/specialist/script-runner.ts`**
- Line 471: `const systemPrompt = spec.specialist.prompt.system || undefined;`
- Line 527: `if (systemPrompt) args.push('--system-prompt', systemPrompt);`

Call chain:
1. `runScriptSpecialist()` extracts `spec.specialist.prompt.system` at line 471
2. Passes to `runSingleAttempt()` as `systemPrompt` param at line 473
3. `runSingleAttempt()` builds args array, conditionally adds `--system-prompt` at line 527

**Tests: `tests/unit/specialist/script-runner.test.ts`**

### 2. Package-class session path: `--append-system-prompt` (always append)

**File: `src/pi/session.ts`**
- Lines 99-147: `PiSessionOptions` interface — has `systemPrompt?: string` field
- Line 652: `args.push('--append-system-prompt', this.options.systemPrompt);`

Key: No mode field in `PiSessionOptions`. Always appends.

**File: `src/specialist/runner.ts`**
- Lines 1070-1075: Builds `agentsMd` from `prompt.system` + template variables + mandatory injections
- Lines 1334-1348: Passes `agentsMd` as `systemPrompt` to `sessionFactory()`:
```typescript

  model,
  systemPrompt: agentsMd || undefined,
  ...
});
```

**Tests: `tests/unit/pi/session.test.ts`**
- Lines 362-366: Test "keeps package runner system prompt appended instead of replacing Pi system prompt" — explicitly asserts `--append-system-prompt` used and `--system-prompt` absent

### 3. Specialist JSON schema

**File: `src/specialist/schema.ts`**

```typescript

  system: z.string().optional(),
  task_template: z.string(),
  output_schema: z.record(z.unknown()).optional(),
  skill_inherit: z.string().optional(),
```

### 4. SpecialistLoader

**File: `src/specialist/loader.ts`**
- Lines 132-146: `get()` method loads spec, resolves `skills.paths`, caches and returns raw `Specialist` type
- No transformation of `prompt.system` — passes through as-is from JSON/YAML

### 5. Reference specialist schema

**File: `config/specialists/executor.specialist.json`**
- Lines 94-278: `prompt.system` — long text content
- Lines 279-287: `prompt.task_template`
- No `system_prompt_mode` field

---

## Implementation Sketch

Add `system_prompt_mode: 'append' | 'replace'` to control behavior:

1. **Schema (`src/specialist/schema.ts:46-57`)** — Add to `PromptSchema`:
   ```typescript
   system_prompt_mode: z.enum(['append', 'replace']).default('append'),
   ```
   Default `'append'` preserves backward compatibility.

2. **PiSessionOptions (`src/pi/session.ts:99-147`)** — Add field:
   ```typescript
   systemPromptMode?: 'append' | 'replace';
   ```

3. **Session spawn (`src/pi/session.ts:652`)** — Conditional flag:
   ```typescript
   if (this.options.systemPrompt) {
     const flag = this.options.systemPromptMode === 'replace' ? '--system-prompt' : '--append-system-prompt';
     args.push(flag, this.options.systemPrompt);
   }
   ```

4. **Runner (`src/specialist/runner.ts:1334`)** — Plumb mode from spec:
   ```typescript

     ...
     systemPrompt: agentsMd || undefined,
     systemPromptMode: prompt.system_prompt_mode,
     ...
   });
   ```

Script-runner already uses `--system-prompt` (replace) — no change needed there. It hardcodes the "replace" behavior which is correct for script-class specialists.

---

## Risks

1. **Breaking change for existing specialists** — If default is `'replace'` instead of `'append'`, existing package-class specialists lose pi's coding-agent base prompt. Must default to `'append'`.

2. **Test coverage gap** — `session.test.ts` line 365 explicitly asserts `--append-system-prompt` is used. Need new test for `'replace'` mode.

3. **Schema passthrough** — Both `PromptSchema` and `ExecutionSchema` use `.passthrough()`. Adding the field is non-breaking for validation, but TypeScript types must be updated.

4. **Script-runner vs package-runner semantic split** — Script-class already uses replace. Package-class defaults to append. If a spec author sets `system_prompt_mode: 'replace'` on a script-class specialist, it's a no-op (already replace). Documentation should clarify this.

```
    ├── TUI stack (@earendil-works/pi-tui)
    │   ├── TUI + ProcessTerminal — terminal raw mode, rendering
    │   ├── ChatFeed (src/cli/chat/feed.ts) — event rendering
    │   ├── ChatStatus (src/cli/chat/status.ts) — status bar polling
    │   └── Input — user text input
    ├── Control (src/cli/chat/control.ts) — slash command dispatch
    └── Data sources
        ├── loadStatuses() (src/specialist/status-load.ts) — job status from SQLite/files
        ├── startChatEventTailer() (in chat.ts) — events from SQLite/files
        └── FIFO (.specialists/jobs/<id>/steer.pipe) — steer/resume messages
```

### Legacy `sp attach`

```
sp attach (src/cli/attach.ts)
    └── tmux attach-session -t <tmux_session>
```

No TUI, no feed, just raw terminal handoff to tmux session.

---

## Execution Flows

### Flow 1: sp chat launch (new job)

**Path**: `src/index.ts` → `src/cli/chat.ts:run()`

1. `parseArgs()` extracts specialist name, prompt, beadId, contextDepth, model
2. Creates ephemeral bead via `bd create` if no `--bead`
3. Loads specialist via `SpecialistLoader.get()`
4. Imports pi-tui, constructs `TUI(ProcessTerminal)`
5. Creates `ChatFeed`, `ChatStatus`, `ChatControl`, `Input`
6. Mounts: `tui.addChild(root)`, `tui.setFocus(input)`
7. Starts status polling: `status.start()`
8. Starts TUI: `tui.start()`
9. Launches specialist via `launchSpecialist()` (non-awaited)
10. `onJobStarted` callback sets `currentJobId`, starts event tailer
11. Event tailer polls `readEventsAfterSeq()` and renders to feed

**Key symbols**:
- `src/cli/chat.ts:run()` — entry point
- `startChatEventTailer()` — event polling
- `launchSpecialist()` in `src/specialist/launch.ts` — job start

### Flow 2: sp chat detach (unitAI-17kx3)

- `/quit` or Ctrl+C → `requestDetach()` → sets `shouldExit=true`, resolves `exitRequested` promise
- Does NOT call `stopJob()` — job continues running/waiting
- Cleanup: `stopChatEventTailer()`, `tui.stop()`, `terminal.stop()`
- Exit code 0

### Flow 3: sp attach (legacy tmux)

**Path**: `src/index.ts` → `src/cli/attach.ts:run()`

1. Parses `<job-id>` from argv
2. Reads `status.json` from `.specialists/jobs/<job-id>/`
3. Validates job not terminal (`done`/`error`)
4. Validates `tmux_session` present
5. `execFileSync('tmux', ['attach-session', '-t', sessionName])`

No TUI, no event feed, no control commands.

---

| Symbol | File | Purpose |
|--------|------|---------|
| `run()` | `src/cli/chat.ts` | Chat entry, TUI setup, job launch |
| `startChatEventTailer()` | `src/cli/chat.ts` | Poll events, render to feed |

| `attach.ts:run()` | `src/cli/attach.ts` | Legacy tmux attach |

---

## Implementation Plan

### Extraction seams

1. **Shared TUI rendering** — extract from `src/cli/chat.ts`:
   - `ChatFeed`, `ChatStatus`, `Input` wiring
   - `startChatEventTailer()` — already parameterized on `jobId`, `jobsDir`, `feed`
   - Signal guards, cleanup orchestration

2. **Shared control logic** — `src/cli/chat/control.ts`:
   - `dispatchInput()`, `executeInput()` already stateless
   - `ControlOps` interface for `getJobState`, `stopJob`, `finalizeJob`, `appendBeadNote`

3. **Existing-job attach flow**:
   - New command `sp attach <job-id> --tui` or make `sp attach` use TUI by default
   - Load existing job status via `loadStatuses()` or `Supervisor.readStatus()`
   - Check job state: `running`/`waiting` → attach, terminal → error
   - Start event tailer for existing job (reuse `startChatEventTailer()`)
   - Create FIFO if missing (may need to handle jobs started without keep-alive)

title: sp attach: interactive TUI attach to existing specialist job
description:
## PROBLEM
Operators can start an interactive `sp chat`, but cannot attach that same TUI/control surface to an already-running or waiting specialist job. Today they must use separate `sp feed`, `sp result`, `sp steer`, and `sp resume` commands, which fragments interactive follow-up.

## SUCCESS
`sp attach <job-id>` opens the chat TUI for an existing job without launching a new specialist. Bare `sp attach` offers a simple interactive picker in TTY mode for attachable jobs.

## SCOPE
- Add CLI command `sp attach [job-id]`.
- Reuse/extract the existing `sp chat` TUI runtime so it supports two modes:
  - launch mode: existing `sp chat <specialist> ...`
  - attach mode: bind to an existing `jobId` and skip `launchSpecialist`.
- Attached TUI should:
  - tail existing timeline via SQLite first with `events.jsonl` fallback, same as current chat feed.
  - pin `ChatStatus` to the attached job id.
  - infer specialist/bead/model/status from persisted status/timeline where possible.
  - send plain text as `steer` when job is running and `resume` when job is waiting, using `status.fifo_path`.
  - keep slash commands working: `/quit`, `/stop`, `/finalize`, `/notes`, `/show`.
- Bare `sp attach` in an interactive TTY should show a minimal job picker prioritized by `running` and `waiting` jobs, displaying job id, specialist, bead, status, model/tokens when available.
- Bare `sp attach` in non-TTY should fail with concise usage unless a future `--json`/`--list` flag is added.
- Terminal jobs (`done`, `error`, `stopped`) may be attached read-only: show feed/result/status, but input should explain that the job is terminal.

## NON_GOALS
- Do not redesign specialist lifecycle or job storage.
- Do not create a new event/feed renderer; reuse the chat/feed parity path.
- Do not change `sp chat` launch semantics except through shared extraction needed by attach.
- Do not implement a full-screen job dashboard.

## CONSTRAINTS
- Preserve existing `sp chat` behavior and tests.
- Avoid raw stdout/stderr writes while the TUI owns the terminal.
- Use existing Supervisor/status/fifo conventions; no new IPC mechanism.
- Keep picker simple and dependency-light.

## VALIDATION
- Unit/integration tests for attach target resolution and terminal/non-terminal input behavior.
- Smoke test that `sp attach <job-id>` renders a visible TUI against a prepared job fixture or short-lived background job.
- Existing chat tests still pass:
  - `bunx vitest run tests/unit/cli/chat-status.test.ts tests/integration/chat/status.test.ts tests/smoke/sp-chat.smoke.test.ts`
- Typecheck/build:
  - `bunx tsc --noEmit`
  - `bun run build`

## OUTPUT
- New `sp attach` command wired into CLI help/dispatch.
- Shared chat TUI attach/launch runtime.
- Tests documenting attach behavior and picker fallback.

title: sp chat: auto-create ephemeral bead when --bead omitted
description:
## PROBLEM

V1 of sp chat requires --bead <id>. For ad-hoc interactive use, creating a tracking bead first is friction. The chat should accept a positional prompt (or --prompt) without --bead, auto-create an ephemeral tracking bead, and use it.

## SUCCESS

\`sp chat reviewer "look at this PR"\` works without --bead. Internally creates a bead titled from the first line of the prompt (truncated), stores it, dispatches the chain against it. Bead persists for audit trail.

## SCOPE

- src/cli/chat.ts — make beadId optional in parseArgs; auto-create when absent
- New helper or inline: bd create with title="<first 60 chars of prompt>" -t task -p3
- Update help text

## NON_GOALS

- No /quit auto-close (V2)
- No --no-bead mode (separate feature, defer)
- No bead deletion on chat exit

## CONSTRAINTS

- If both --bead and a prompt are given, --bead wins
- Auto-create uses bd CLI (consistent with the rest of the project)
- Failure to auto-create → clear error, no fallback

## VALIDATION

- [ ] \`sp chat reviewer "test prompt"\` succeeds without --bead
- [ ] Created bead has expected title format
- [ ] \`sp chat reviewer --bead unitAI-xyz\` still works unchanged
- [ ] Smoke test extended for the no-bead path

## OUTPUT

Updated chat.ts, parser change, smoke test extension, help text update.
notes:

title: Test: sp chat boundary — runner-launch, control helpers, status, mailbox routing
description:
## PROBLEM

The boundary layer of sp chat V1 spans four touchpoints with I/O: the extracted `launchSpecialist` (u4fdd.1), the control helpers `stopJob`/`finalizeJob`/`appendBeadNote` (u4fdd.2), the SupervisorStatus poll for the status row (u4fdd.4), and the mailbox steer/resume writes inside dispatch (u4fdd.5). All four interact with the file system, FIFO, or observability DB and need contract-level proof that schemas, exit codes, and write paths are correct.

## SUCCESS

Contract tests assert:
- `launchSpecialist` returns the same job handle shape as `sp run` did before extraction, and `sp run` itself is byte-identical (regression test against captured pre-refactor output)
- `stopJob` / `finalizeJob` / `appendBeadNote` are idempotent and surface error envelopes (not exceptions) on no-op cases
- Status-row poll reads the exact field set used by the formatter (token total, model, state)
- Mailbox routing dispatcher returns typed Actions (kind=steer for running, kind=resume for waiting). Note: actual DB row writes are part of the integration layer (u4fdd.6 wiring + u4fdd.7 smoke), out of scope here.

Live-first: tests run against a real ephemeral specialist job and a real test bead. No mocks of internal collaborators.

## SCOPE

- New file: `test/integration/chat/launch.test.ts`
- New file: `test/integration/chat/control.test.ts`
- New file: `test/integration/chat/status.test.ts`
- New file: `test/integration/chat/mailbox-routing.test.ts`
- Uses existing observability DB read paths and a temp-bead fixture helper

## NON_GOALS

- No full TUI assembly tests (u4fdd.7 owns that)
- No core-layer unit tests (sibling test bead u4fdd.8 owns that)
- No load testing
- No mocked-HTTP tests — these are boundary contracts against the real local components

## CONSTRAINTS

- Live-first: hit the real observability DB, real FIFO, real `bd` CLI for the test bead
- Ephemeral fixtures: every test creates + closes its own test bead and job, even on failure (afterEach cleanup)
- FIFO writes use the async + timeout helper from u4fdd.2 — assert the timeout fires when the reader is dead
- Tests must run in <30s total

## VALIDATION

Layer: boundary
Strategy: live-contract (no mocks of internal collaborators)
Covers: unitAI-u4fdd.1, unitAI-u4fdd.2, unitAI-u4fdd.4, unitAI-u4fdd.5 (routing portion)

Assertions required:
- [ ] `launchSpecialist`: returns `{ jobId, supervisor, ... }` with same field shape as pre-refactor `sp run` exposes internally; reject mocking the runner
- [ ] `sp run` regression: capture `sp run reviewer --bead <fixture>` stdout pre- and post-refactor; assert equality
- [ ] `stopJob` idempotency: call twice on the same job; second returns no-op result, not error
- [ ] `finalizeJob` on non-chain job: returns structured error (matches the error envelope shape established in conversations.md §10.2), does not throw
- [ ] `appendBeadNote` empty text: refuses to write, returns structured error
- [ ] `appendBeadNote` happy path: text appears in `bd show <id>` output
- [ ] FIFO write timeout: kill the reader, attempt write, assert the timeout fires within configured ms (default ≤500ms)
- [ ] Status poll: query SupervisorStatus, assert `metrics.token_usage.total_tokens`, `model`, `status`, `id`, `bead_id` fields are all present and correctly typed
- [ ] Status poll thrash guard: 10 consecutive polls with unchanged state cause exactly one render call (mock the render callback)
- [ ] Mailbox routing (dispatcher action): with state=running, dispatchInput returns Action with kind="steer" and target text passed through
- [ ] Mailbox routing (dispatcher action): with state=waiting, dispatchInput returns Action with kind="resume"
- [ ] Mailbox routing race: snapshot state, post, job finishes between snapshot and post — assert the post is rejected with a clear error and no retry loop

Drift-safe:
- [ ] Schema assertions check field presence + types, not exact internal struct identity
- [ ] Status row tests assert the formatted string contains job-id and bead-id, not exact positional layout

Anti-pattern checks:
- [ ] No mocks of internal collaborators — only the runner output stream is mocked (we don't want to spin up a real LLM call in tests)
- [ ] No shared mutable state — each test creates fresh fixture beads/jobs
- [ ] Negative-path assertions present for each helper

## OUTPUT

Test files, fixture-bead helper module, command to run (`npm test test/integration/chat`), pass/fail summary, residual risks (esp. around race-window in mailbox routing).

Critical paths covered:
- `sp run` byte-identical before/after refactor — risk: silent breaking change to canonical CLI
- FIFO write timeout — risk: dead-reader hang freezes the TUI
- Mailbox kind selection by state — risk: steer sent to waiting job (or vice versa) breaks runner state machine
- Error-envelope shape — risk: TUI exception-catches a non-error and crashes

Known deferred paths:
- Status poll under DB contention (parallel writers) — follow-up: to be created if V2 reveals flakiness
- launchSpecialist with custom backend overrides — follow-up: to be created when V2 adds --model attach

## Scope clarification (authoritative — supersedes any earlier VALIDATION strictness on DB rows)

This bead tests the BOUNDARY layer surfaces of sp chat. End-to-end mailbox DB-row verification belongs to u4fdd.7 (smoke), which exercises the full integration. At this layer:
- control.test.ts: real bd CLI hits for stopJob/finalizeJob/appendBeadNote ✓
- launch.test.ts: real CLI invocation for handle-shape contract ✓
- mailbox-routing.test.ts: dispatcher action-return contract + race-window via DI sequence-flip ✓
- status.test.ts: thrash guard + format substring + field-type assertions ✓

Reviewers must use this scope; do NOT mark the DB-row item unmet — it's deferred to u4fdd.7 by design.

title: Test: sp chat core — ChatFeed + slash parser (unit + property)
description:
## PROBLEM

Two pieces of pure-logic in the sp chat V1 surface need unit-level proof before integration: the row-buffer rendering in ChatFeed (u4fdd.3) and the slash command parser inside the dispatch module (u4fdd.5). Both are deterministic, I/O-free, and ideal for property tests on the wrap/parse invariants.

## SUCCESS

Unit tests for ChatFeed assert width-aware rendering with ANSI passthrough; property tests assert wrap invariants (no line exceeds width, visible content preserved). Unit tests for the slash parser cover all 5 commands plus unknown-slash and plain-text dispatch decisions.

## SCOPE

- New file: `test/unit/chat/feed.test.ts` — ChatFeed unit + property tests
- New file: `test/unit/chat/dispatch.test.ts` — slash parser unit tests
- Imports only the modules under test; no DB, no FIFO, no spawn

## NON_GOALS

- No integration-level tests (those land in u4fdd.7)
- No status-row polling tests (boundary layer — see sibling boundary test bead)
- No TUI-assembly tests (shell layer — covered by u4fdd.7)
- No visual regression / snapshot of rendered output

## CONSTRAINTS

- All tests deterministic — no random seeds without fixed values, no `Date.now()` without injection
- Function-scoped fixtures only — zero shared mutable state between tests
- Tests must run in <2s total

## VALIDATION

Layer: core
Strategy: unit + property-based
Covers: unitAI-u4fdd.3 (ChatFeed), unitAI-u4fdd.5 (parser portion only)

Assertions required:
- [ ] ChatFeed positive path: append a mixed sequence of token/tool/event/result rows, render at width=80, assert visible rows count and content
- [ ] ChatFeed ANSI preservation: append a styled token (e.g. `\\x1b[31mred\\x1b[0m`), wrap across boundary, assert ANSI codes still bracket the visible text correctly
- [ ] ChatFeed width invariant (property): for any seq of rows and any width 20-200, `visibleWidth(line) ≤ width` for every rendered line
- [ ] ChatFeed content-preservation invariant (property): concatenated visible chars across wrapped lines equal the source row's visible chars
- [ ] Parser positive path: `/stop`, `/finalize`, `/notes hello`, `/show`, `/quit` each return their typed Action
- [ ] Parser negative path: `/unknown` returns ErrorAction with usage hint
- [ ] Parser empty-notes: `/notes` (no body) returns ErrorAction, not a notes write
- [ ] Parser plain-text branch: with injected state=running → Steer action; state=waiting → Resume action; state=done → freeform-rejected hint

Fixture policy:
- [ ] No shared mutable state — each test constructs its own ChatFeed / dispatch input independently
- [ ] Deterministic — property tests use fixed seeds

Anti-pattern checks:
- [ ] No tautological assertions (e.g. asserting parser-output against itself)
- [ ] No mocking of internal collaborators — ChatFeed and parser are pure
- [ ] At least one negative-path assertion per module

## OUTPUT

Test files, command to run them locally (`npm test test/unit/chat`), pass/fail summary, residual gaps (with follow-up issue IDs).

Critical paths covered:
- ANSI passthrough through wrap — risk: garbled output mid-stream
- Empty-notes guard — risk: writing empty notes to bead silently
- State-aware routing — risk: steer sent to done job, silent drop

Known deferred paths:
- Property tests with multi-byte / wide-char glyphs — follow-up: to be created if V2 sees CJK users

title: sp chat: entrypoint — TUI assembly, dep install, signal/crash guards
description:
## PROBLEM

All the building blocks (launch helper T1, control helpers T2, ChatFeed T3, status row T4, dispatch T5) need a single entrypoint that:
1. Adds `@earendil-works/pi-tui` as a direct dependency (pinned to align with the installed pi-coding-agent 0.75.4)
2. Parses CLI args, launches the specialist via T1, wires the TUI tree (TUI + Container + ChatFeed + ChatStatus + Input)
3. Installs an `addInputListener` to intercept Ctrl+C BEFORE the Input gets it — stop TUI, restore terminal, call `stopJob` from T2
4. Wires signal/crash guards (SIGTERM, SIGHUP, uncaughtException, unhandledRejection) that drain input, stop TUI, restore terminal, optionally finalize/note

## SUCCESS

`sp chat <specialist> [prompt...] --bead <id> [--context-depth N] [--model M]` launches the interactive shell, streams the runner's output into ChatFeed, refreshes the status row, accepts input, and cleans up the terminal on any exit path.

## SCOPE

- New file: `src/cli/chat.ts` (entrypoint, ~150–250 LOC)
- Modify: `src/index.ts` or wherever CLI subcommands are registered, to add `chat`
- Modify: `package.json` — add `@earendil-works/pi-tui` to `dependencies` pinned to `^0.75.4`
- Modify: `package-lock.json` after `npm install`

## NON_GOALS

- No `--job <id>` attach to running jobs (V2)
- No multi-job (V3)
- No theme support, no mouse, no scrollback search
- No input history, no multiline — use `Input` (V2 will swap to `Editor`)

## CONSTRAINTS

- Ctrl+C semantics: intercepted, NOT treated as input cancellation; calls `stopJob` then exits cleanly (terminal fully restored)
- All exit paths (normal /quit, Ctrl+C, signal, uncaught throw, job process crash) MUST restore the terminal — wrap in try/finally + handlers
- Always `--keep-alive` (chat lifecycle is by definition long-running)
- Submit binding: Enter (single-line for V1)
- Use Input not Editor for V1
- pi-tui import path: `@earendil-works/pi-tui` NOT `@mariozechner/pi-tui` (see saved memory)

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `npm run lint` + `npx tsc --noEmit` + `npm run build` clean
- [ ] `sp chat --help` displays the new command
- [ ] Manual smoke: `sp chat reviewer --bead <test-bead>` opens the TUI, streams output, accepts Enter-submit, slash commands work, Ctrl+C kills the job and restores the terminal (no garbled prompt after exit)
- [ ] Crash path: induce an `uncaughtException` in a dev branch and verify terminal restores

## OUTPUT

New entry file, registry change, dependency bump, manual smoke evidence (terminal recording or screenshot), residual risks.

## APPROACH NOTES

Copy pi-coding-agent's signal-guard pattern: it covers SIGTERM, SIGHUP, dead-terminal stdout/stderr errors, and uncaughtException. Also add `unhandledRejection`. Single shared `cleanup()` function called from every guard + finally.

Reference primitive list (from spike unitAI-55l4p):
- `TUI(new ProcessTerminal())` — root
- `Container` — layout
- `Component` subclass (ChatFeed from T3)
- `TruncatedText`-like for status (T4)
- `Input` — single-line
- `addInputListener` for Ctrl+C
- `matchesKey(data, Key.ctrl("c"))` for the intercept check
- `tui.requestRender()` on status or feed change
- `drainInput()` + `tui.stop()` + `ProcessTerminal.stop()` for teardown

title: sp chat: slash command dispatch + steer/resume input routing
description:
## PROBLEM

When the user submits input in the chat shell, we need to route it correctly:
- Leading `/` → parsed slash command (`/stop`, `/finalize`, `/notes <text>`, `/show`, `/quit`)
- Otherwise → mailbox post as `steer` (job running) or `resume` (job waiting) based on the live state
- Job state must be re-read on submit (state can change between keystrokes)

Terminal states (done/error/cancelled) accept only slash commands; freeform input is silently rejected with a UI hint.

## SUCCESS

A pure `dispatchInput(text, ctx) → Action` function plus an executor that performs the action. Both unit-testable. Five slash commands recognized; unknown slashes show "unknown command" in the feed without crashing.

## SCOPE

- New file: `src/cli/chat/control.ts`
- Reuses helpers from T2 (`stopJob`, `finalizeJob`, `appendBeadNote`)
- Reuses runner-launch / supervisor status query from T1 / T4

## NON_GOALS

- No quote parsing, no shell-like escaping (V2)
- No completion (V2)
- No history (V2 — Editor instead of Input)
- No multi-job switcher (V3)

## CONSTRAINTS

- FIFO writes for steer/resume MUST be async with a timeout (existing `sp steer` uses `writeFileSync` which can block — see spike unitAI-55l4p findings)
- All slash command implementations are idempotent: `/stop` on an already-stopped job is a no-op with an info line, not an error
- `/notes <text>` requires text — empty body shows usage hint, no bead write
- `/quit` detaches but does NOT kill the job — Ctrl+C is the kill path (owned by T6)

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `npm run lint` + `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [ ] Unit tests: parser recognizes 5 slashes, unknowns return error action, plain text returns Steer/Resume action depending on injected job state
- [ ] Unit test: empty `/notes` does not call appendBeadNote
- [ ] Integration test: simulate "running" state, submit plain text → mailbox.post called with kind=steer

## OUTPUT

Module file, parser unit tests, integration test snapshot, residual risks (race when state flips between read and write).

## APPROACH NOTES

For state read: use the same SupervisorStatus path as T4. Snapshot state once per submit; if the post races and is rejected (e.g. job finished between read and write), surface a feed message and continue. Do NOT loop-retry.

description:
## PROBLEM

The chat shell needs a one-line status row showing the current job's identity, state, token usage, and model — refreshed live as the runner ticks. Format requested by operator:

  `executor/<job-id>/<bead-id> · running · 14.4k tok · claude-4.6`

Source of truth is the SupervisorStatus record (already populated by the runner; readable from observability state).

## SUCCESS

A `ChatStatus` component that:
- Polls SupervisorStatus every ~500ms (configurable)
- Formats the status row exactly as specified, truncating to terminal width
- Calls `tui.requestRender()` only when meaningful fields change (no thrash)
- Returns a single ANSI-styled line via `render(width)`

## SCOPE

- New file: `src/cli/chat/status.ts`
- Reads from: existing SupervisorStatus / observability DB (use the same query path `sp ps` uses; do not re-implement)
- No writes

## NON_GOALS

- No history/sparkline (V3)
- No per-chain rollup (V2 multi-job)
- No interactivity in the status row

## CONSTRAINTS

- Poll interval configurable, default 500ms
- Must use existing DB read path (no duplicate queries; if sp-ps exposes a helper, reuse; otherwise extract)
- Token count uses `metrics.token_usage.total_tokens`
- Model field reads `backend` + `model` from status
- Truncate via `truncateToWidth` from pi-tui (ANSI-safe)

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `npm run lint` + `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [ ] Manual: render produces correct format string for a running, waiting, and done state
- [ ] Manual: thrash check — 100 polls with unchanged state cause zero render calls (only field-change should trigger render)

## OUTPUT

Component file, integration with TUI render loop, sample formatted outputs for each lifecycle state.

## APPROACH NOTES

Don't poll harder than the runner ticks — 500ms is the floor. Field equality check should be on a hash of (state, total_tokens, model) so token deltas trigger redraw but unchanged ticks don't.

title: sp chat: ChatFeed row-buffer component with ANSI passthrough
description:
## PROBLEM

The TUI feed area must render streaming specialist output — tokens, tool calls, events, results — as a vertically-scrolling row buffer that supports ANSI styling for colored token streams. Pi's runner emits via `onToken` / `onToolStart` / `onToolEnd` / `onEvent` callbacks; the feed must accept those deltas and produce wrapped, width-aware lines.

## SUCCESS

A `ChatFeed` class extending `@earendil-works/pi-tui` `Component` that:
- Accepts append-style API: `appendToken(text)`, `appendToolStart(name, args)`, `appendToolEnd(name, result)`, `appendEvent(type, details)`, `appendResult(text)`
- Renders via `render(width: number): string[]`, returning ANSI-preserved wrapped lines using `wrapTextWithAnsi`
- Maintains an internal row buffer; on width change, re-wraps from source rows
- Compact tool rendering for V1: one-line collapse of tool calls (file path + status), full text only for `appendResult`

## SCOPE

- New file: `src/cli/chat/feed.ts`
- New types: `FeedRow` (`{ kind: 'token' | 'tool' | 'event' | 'result' | 'meta'; text: string; ts: number }`)
- Dependency: `@earendil-works/pi-tui` (added in T6 — this task can `import type` ahead of install if needed, but real wiring waits for T6)

## NON_GOALS

- No scrollback search (V3)
- No expand/collapse interaction for tools (V2)
- No mouse support
- No persistence — buffer is in-memory only, lost on `/quit`
- No multi-job — one feed per chat session

## CONSTRAINTS

- ANSI strings must round-trip through `wrapTextWithAnsi` (verify with a styled token sample)
- `render(width)` is called frequently (every redraw); must be O(visible-rows × wrap-cost), not O(full-buffer)
- No I/O inside the component — it accepts data, it renders. Polling/source lives in T5/T6.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `npm run lint` + `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [ ] Unit test: feed accepts 1000 mixed appends and renders the last N rows at width=80 in <10ms
- [ ] Unit test: ANSI styling preserved across wrap boundary

## OUTPUT

Component file, unit tests, render benchmarks, residual risks.

## APPROACH NOTES

Spike (unitAI-55l4p) confirmed the primitive surface — see saved memory `earendil-works-pi-tui-not-mariozechner-pi-tui`. Use `wrapTextWithAnsi` from `@earendil-works/pi-tui` for ANSI-aware wrapping; do NOT use the bash component path (it strips ANSI).

title: sp chat: extract stop / finalize / notes helpers for TUI reuse
description:
## PROBLEM

`sp chat` slash commands (`/stop`, `/finalize`, `/notes <text>`) must invoke the same logic `sp stop`, `sp finalize`, and bead-note attachment use today. Without extraction, slash handlers become a re-implementation that can drift in subtle ways (signal choice, race handling, KV updates, beads claim semantics).

## SUCCESS

Three reusable helpers — `stopJob(jobId, opts)`, `finalizeJob(chainMemberId, opts)`, `appendBeadNote(beadId, text)` — callable from both their existing CLI sites and from a TUI loop. Existing `sp stop`, `sp finalize`, `bd notes` CLI behavior unchanged.

## SCOPE

- `src/cli/stop.ts` — extract stop logic
- `src/cli/finalize.ts` (if it exists) or wherever `sp finalize` is wired — extract finalize logic
- Any CLI code that calls `bd update --notes` to attach result — extract or thinly wrap
- New file(s): `src/specialist/control.ts` (or co-locate per concern)

## NON_GOALS

- No new behavior, no signal-policy changes, no new flags
- No changes to bead schema or `bd` CLI

## CONSTRAINTS

- Existing CLI surfaces (`sp stop`, `sp finalize`) byte-identical before/after
- Helpers must be safe to call concurrently from a TUI tick (no global mutable state leakage)
- No new dependencies

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `npm run lint` + `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [ ] Manual: `sp stop <id>` and `sp finalize <id>` work as before
- [ ] Helpers are pure functions of (jobId, options) — no hidden CLI parsing inside

## OUTPUT

Helper signatures, file moves, before/after verification of `sp stop` and `sp finalize`, residual risks.

## APPROACH NOTES

Pay attention to FIFO write semantics — the existing `writeFileSync` on `steer.pipe` is synchronous; if the reader is dead, it blocks. The TUI consumer in T5 will want async with a timeout. Make the helper async and document the wait/timeout policy.
