title: sp console: console.json config + first-run repo auto-discovery
description:
## PROBLEM

`listRepos()` returns exactly one repo when cwd resolves to a git root (worktree or main repo), so Tab is a silent no-op for the common case. Multi-repo setups across `~/dev/` + `~/projects/` are invisible without manually setting `SPECIALISTS_CONSOLE_REPOS` in every shell.

## SUCCESS

`./sp console` auto-discovers all specialists-enabled repos on first run, writes the result to `~/.config/specialists/console.json`, and loads from that config on subsequent runs. Operator never needs to set the env var for the common case.

## SCOPE

- New: `src/cli/console/repo-config.ts` — schema + read/write helpers. Atomic write via tmp+rename (mirrors `writeGlobalUserConfig` from unitAI-ctb4u.17).
- New: `src/cli/console/repo-discovery.ts` — scan base dirs for child dirs with `.specialists/db/observability.db`. One level deep only.
- Modified: `src/cli/console/runtime.ts:listRepos` — precedence chain: `SPECIALISTS_CONSOLE_REPOS` env > `console.json` config > cwd-as-repo + parent-scan > scan default base dirs (first-run).
- Modified: `src/cli/console/view-model.ts` — accept a startup `message` so the discovery result lands in the existing message area without a modal.
- Tests: `tests/unit/cli/console-repo-config.test.ts` (schema + atomic write + first-run flow).

## NON_GOALS

- Interactive RepoConfigView (filed separately as Wave B follow-up).
- Persisting per-repo metadata beyond `{name, path}` — db status / activity counts live in the runtime snapshot, not the config.
- Watching for new repos appearing during a session.
- Cross-host discovery.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Atomic write via tmp+rename (no partial console.json after a crash).
- `SPECIALISTS_CONSOLE_REPOS` env var ALWAYS wins (back-compat).
- First-run scan must be cheap: only scan dirs that actually exist (`~/dev`, `~/projects`, `~/work`, `~/repos`, `~/code`), one level deep, with a 1500ms wall-clock budget.
- Stderr NDJSON envelopes for read/write failures route through `logError` (single-sink invariant from unitAI-21sn4).
- Schema versioned (`schema_version: 1`) so a future migration is mechanical.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] First run on a fresh `$HOME` writes `console.json` with discovered repos.
- [ ] Subsequent runs load from the config without re-scanning.
- [ ] `SPECIALISTS_CONSOLE_REPOS=foo=/path ./sp console` bypasses the config.
- [ ] Crash mid-write leaves the prior `console.json` intact (atomic write test, mirrors unitAI-ctb4u.17).
- [ ] `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- [ ] Console suite stays green (231+ tests).
- [ ] Smoke: `./sp console` from `~/dev/specialists` discovers gitboard, xtrm-tools siblings.

## OUTPUT

PR + 5-10 unit tests + smoke run output captured in bead notes.

## APPROACH NOTES

- Reuse `resolveRepoRef` for filtering candidate dirs.
- Default base dirs: `~/dev`, `~/projects`, `~/work`, `~/repos`, `~/code`. The set is hardcoded — operator can override via `console.json.base_dirs` array if they ever edit the file.
- First-run success message: `discovered N repos in <base dirs> · g R to manage` in the existing stats/message area, no modal.
- Config schema: `{ _doc, schema_version: 1, base_dirs: string[], repos: Array<{name, path}>, auto_discovered_at: ISO string }`.
- Discovered-from unitAI-ctb4u.18 (operator E2E walkthrough §7).
close_reason: PR #141 merged: console.json + first-run auto-discovery wired into runtime.listReposWithContext, markCurrent prefers cwd-prefix, 16 unit tests + live smoke. Wave B tracked at unitAI-hneld.

title: sp console ConfigView: enrich hint text for each overridable field with operational guidance
description:
## PROBLEM

- What format \`execution.model\` accepts (\`provider/id\` is convention but never stated).
- What units \`timeout_ms\` / \`stall_timeout_ms\` use (ms — but the field also accepts \`0\` to disable, never documented).

- What \`extensions.serena\`/\`extensions.gitnexus\` = false does to memory / capability.

- What \`prompt_limit_bytes\` / \`stdout_limit_bytes\` typical values are or what they cap.

The hint slot in the field row is the only place this guidance can land for someone editing in the TUI.

- Format / units / valid syntax (e.g. \`<provider>/<id>\` for model).
- Concrete example (e.g. \`openai-codex/gpt-5.4-mini\`).
- Operational consequence in plain words (e.g. \`false = disable Serena MCP, saves ~80-150 MB per spawn\`).

title: sp console DiffView: fall back to git history for jobs without live worktree
description:
## PROBLEM

Operator walkthrough §5: for the ~85 historical jobs in the user's DB whose worktrees have been cleaned, DiffView shows \`no worktree for this job\` — accurate, but the operator has no path to inspect what that job actually changed. \`bd show\` notes capture the handoff text; the diff itself only lives in git history.

We already record \`last_auto_commit_sha\` on \`specialist_jobs.status_json\` (executor + debugger via auto-commit checkpoint pipeline; see memory \`auto-commit-checkpoint-supervisor-auto-commits-worktree-chan\`). Most repo commit messages embed \`unitAI-<id>\` references. \`runtime.ts:diffSummary\` doesn't currently exploit either.

## SUCCESS

Pressing \`d\` on a job whose worktree is gone shows the actual diff the job produced (via git history), with no new ref/tag/notes infrastructure beyond what git already gives.

## SCOPE

- \`src/cli/console/runtime.ts:resolveWorktree\` and \`diffSummary\` / \`diffFile\`: layered fallback chain.
- New helper(s) in \`src/cli/console/git.ts\` for \`git show <sha>\` and \`git log --grep=<bead>\` parsing.
- View-model update if a new "commit history" stage is added to \`DiffViewState\`.
- Tests in \`tests/unit/cli/console-diff-view.test.ts\` for each fallback branch.

## NON_GOALS

- Auto-tagging worktrees on cleanup (\`refs/tags/specialists/<job_id>\`) — pollutes the tag namespace.
- \`refs/notes/specialists\` integration — not pushed by default, fragile across clones.
- Cross-repo diff browsing.
- Recovering work from jobs that NEVER committed (READ_ONLY specialists: reviewer / code-sanity / obligations-scanner / security-auditor — those genuinely have nothing to show, and that's correct).

## CONSTRAINTS

- Layered fallback order (live worktree → recorded SHA → bead-id grep) — DiffView header should indicate which source it's reading from so the operator knows whether they're looking at a live patch or a historical snapshot.
- No raw ANSI outside \`theme.ts\`.
- NDJSON envelope shape unchanged for git failures (\`op: 'git_show' | 'git_log_grep'\` to be added).

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Live worktree job → DiffView renders existing happy path (regression).

title: Materializer adoption Phase 4 (exploratory): sp console as materializer sync_hint subscriber
description:
## PROBLEM

The Phase 5 close documented that observability-sqlite has no notify / WAL-listener surface, so sp console polls. The gitboard materializer emits `specialists:sync_hint` on channel `specialists:repo:<slug>` after every successful run. That IS the subscribe primitive sp console lacks today. When (a) a long-running specialists daemon process exists and (b) it runs the materializer, sp console becomes a WebSocket subscriber to those exact events and the 1500ms poll loop dies for active sessions.

This bead is EXPLORATORY. It does not commit to a daemon architecture. It produces a written design proposal + a feasibility prototype that the operator can read and decide on.

## SUCCESS

A design doc `docs/design/sp-console-subscribe-via-materializer.md` exists. It enumerates:
1. The daemon process model required for the materializer to live longer than a sp console invocation.
2. Authentication / authorization for the WS channel (local-only via UNIX socket vs HTTP+token).
3. The fallback model: subscribe when available, poll otherwise — sp console must not require the daemon.
4. The materializer pieces that need to live in the specialists repo vs stay in gitboard.
5. An assessment of whether sp console should consume `MaterializedSpecialistJob` shape or stay on `ConsoleJob` (extends `SupervisorStatus`).

A feasibility prototype lives at `src/cli/console/subscribe-prototype.ts` (gated behind `SPECIALISTS_CONSOLE_SUBSCRIBE_PROTOTYPE=1` env var) demonstrating one of the two transport models against a fake materializer. It is NOT production code.

## SCOPE

- New: `docs/design/sp-console-subscribe-via-materializer.md` (~200-400 lines).
- New: `src/cli/console/subscribe-prototype.ts` (~50-100 LoC, gated, illustrative only).
- Tests: optional smoke around the prototype if the operator wants to validate transport choice.

## NON_GOALS

- Building the daemon itself.
- Modifying any production code path in sp console.
- Committing to MaterializedSpecialistJob as the canonical shape.
- Implementing a full WebSocket server in this repo.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Prototype gated by env var — no production import path can reach it.
- Design doc must reference substrate-review.md §11 channels work for the cross-repo direction.
- Design doc must capture the "subscribe when daemon available, poll otherwise" fallback explicitly — sp console can never hard-require a daemon to run.
- No dependency additions until the operator decides to proceed.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Design doc exists and covers all 5 enumeration points.
- [ ] Prototype runs when env var set, no-ops when not set.
- [ ] Operator review documented in bd notes — explicit ACK to proceed or stop, with rationale.

## OUTPUT

- Design doc.
- Optional gated prototype.
- Operator decision in bd close reason — proceed (file Phase 5 bead) or stop (close as decided-not-to-build).

## APPROACH NOTES

- The lighter prototype model is UNIX socket + line-delimited JSON, since sp console is local-only and a full WS handshake adds complexity for no payoff.
- Look at how gitboard's existing materializer + ws fan-out is wired before designing — most of the answers are already in `/home/dawid/dev/gitboard/packages/core/src/materializer/materializer.ts:publishHint`.
- The MaterializedSpecialistJob question is the real fork in the road: if sp console consumes it, the materializer in gitboard becomes the shared source of truth and sp console's runtime client becomes a thin reader. If not, two projections of the same data continue to live.
close_reason: PR #140 merged. Phase 4 exploratory deliverables: design doc with five recommendations + gated prototype (smoke-validated). Phase 5 build-out bead intentionally NOT filed — operator review of §4 decisions required first. Recommendations: (1) sp materialize-daemon subcommand, (2) UNIX socket transport, (3) subscribe-when-available fallback as mandatory invariant, (4) keep Materializer class in gitboard, (5) stay on ConsoleJob.

title: Materializer adoption Phase 3: render only upserts/tombstones in ProcessView
description:
## PROBLEM

After Phase 1 (`unitAI-ctb4u.19`) lands `snapshotDiff` and surfaces `lastDelta`, ProcessView still recomputes the entire row list on every poll. For repos with 50-200 jobs in history mode, that's 50-200 paint-row calls per second when most rows didn't change. Render-only-changed-rows reuses the diff result to keep the visible window stable.

## SUCCESS

ProcessView reuses the previous render output for rows whose IDs appear in `lastDelta.unchanged`, only re-painting rows in `lastDelta.upserts`. Tombstone rows are spliced out cleanly. Scroll position is preserved across upsert-only deltas (operator doesn't lose their place when one job updates).

## SCOPE

- Modified: `src/cli/console/components.ts:renderProcessRows` — cache per-row rendered string keyed by `(job.id, job.status, ctxBucket)`. Cache invalidates when the row's signature changes. Hit-rate target ≥80% under a steady-state poll on a 100-job snapshot.
- Modified: `src/cli/console/view-model.ts` — selection navigation respects tombstones (selectedRow may need clamping when a tombstoned row removes itself).
- Tests: extend `tests/unit/cli/console-perf.test.ts` with a "delta-only repaint" gate (mock theme.renderJobRow, count calls on a synthetic burst of 100 polls where only 1 job changes per poll).

## NON_GOALS

- Caching across repo switches (cache cleared on `switchRepo`).
- Persisting the cache to disk.
- Caching FeedView / BeadView / DiffView (their refresh pattern is different).

## CONSTRAINTS

- Cache must clear on `switchRepo` action to avoid cross-repo bleed.
- Cache key must include the rendered width — a row painted at 120 cols can't be reused at 80.
- Cache size capped at `totalJobs * 2` to prevent unbounded growth in long sessions.
- No new public types — internal to ConsoleApp.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Perf test asserts `renderJobRow` call count ≤ delta.upserts.length + delta.tombstones.length per render after the first frame.
- [ ] Smoke: long-running poll on a busy repo — visible repaint frequency matches Phase 5's 20Hz cap, but the per-row work is bounded by deltas, not total jobs.
- [ ] No regression in any existing console test.

## OUTPUT

- Modified `components.ts:renderProcessRows` with row-level cache.
- Extended `console-perf.test.ts` with the delta-only repaint assertion.

## APPROACH NOTES

- The simplest cache is `Map<string, string>` keyed by `"${jobId}|${status}|${ctxBucket}|${width}"`.
- Tombstones don't need a cache entry — they're just spliced out by ID.
- Selection clamping: if `selectedRow` was on a tombstoned job, fall back to the next selectable row in the existing `nearestSelectableRow` helper.
- Composition: this bead is ONLY worth doing after Phase 1 (snapshot-diff) lands. Hard `blocks` on `unitAI-ctb4u.19`.
close_reason: PR #139 merged: per-row paint cache + ctxBucket coalesce + repo-switch / tombstone invalidation + perf assertions

title: sp console v2 — Phase 5b: live-aggregates.ts — shared StatsLine + Prometheus projection math
description:
## PROBLEM

The StatsLine in `sp console` (today: `src/cli/console/runtime.ts:75-94`, after rebase under `unitAI-ctb4u.2`) and the Prometheus projection (`src/specialist/prometheus-projection.ts`) BOTH compute the same live aggregates from `SupervisorStatus[]`: running/waiting/done/error counts, distinct epics/nodes/worktrees, ctx max %, total tokens. Two independent implementations; the moment one adds a status (`reviewing`, `dead`) or changes a denominator, they drift silently. The console says one thing in StatsLine; Grafana shows another. Operators lose trust in both surfaces.

Routing the console through Prometheus is the wrong fix (different cardinality, console wants per-job dimensions Prometheus deliberately drops). The right fix is a **shared aggregator core**: both surfaces call the same pure functions; only the projection format differs.

## SUCCESS

`src/specialist/live-aggregates.ts` exists with pure aggregator functions consumed by BOTH `src/cli/console/runtime.ts` (via the StatsLine path) AND `src/specialist/prometheus-projection.ts`. Zero behavior change for external observers (Prometheus scrape format byte-identical to pre-refactor; console StatsLine renders identical numbers). Adding a new aggregate (e.g. `blocked` count) requires editing ONE file.

## SCOPE

- New: `src/specialist/live-aggregates.ts` — pure functions, no IO, no state.
  - `aggregateStatusCounts(statuses: SupervisorStatus[]): { running: number; waiting: number; starting: number; done: number; error: number; cancelled: number; dead: number }`
  - `aggregateDistinctContainers(statuses: SupervisorStatus[]): { epics: number; nodes: number; worktrees: number; chains: number }`
  - `aggregateContextHealth(statuses: SupervisorStatus[]): { ctxMaxPct: number | undefined; ctxAvgPct: number | undefined; nearThresholdCount: number }` — `nearThresholdCount` = jobs with ctxPct ≥ 80.
  - `aggregateTokens(statuses: SupervisorStatus[]): { totalTokens: number; promptTokens: number; completionTokens: number }`
  - `aggregateLiveSnapshot(statuses: SupervisorStatus[]): LiveSnapshot` — single object combining all of the above + `generatedAtMs`.
- Modified: `src/cli/console/runtime.ts` — `listProcessSnapshot` calls `aggregateLiveSnapshot` and spreads its fields into `ProcessSnapshot` (existing field names preserved for the StatsLine renderer).
- Modified: `src/specialist/prometheus-projection.ts` — replaces the inline aggregation with calls to `live-aggregates.ts`. Histogram bucketing stays in `prometheus-projection.ts` (Prometheus-specific concern, not shared).
- Tests: `tests/unit/specialist/live-aggregates.test.ts` (new) — property-based + example-based.

## NON_GOALS

- Changing the Prometheus scrape output format. Byte-identical before/after.
- Changing the StatsLine fields rendered.
- Adding new metrics. This is a refactor + extraction.
- Moving histogram bucketing out of `prometheus-projection.ts`. Buckets are a Prometheus contract, not a shared concern.
- Re-implementing `collectPrometheusProjection` from scratch.

## CONSTRAINTS

- **Pure functions only.** No `Date.now()` inside aggregators — pass `nowMs` via opts when needed (matches existing `PrometheusProjectionInput.nowMs` pattern).
- **No new dependencies.** Just TypeScript + `SupervisorStatus` type.
- **Status enum source of truth.** The status counts function MUST cover every `SupervisorStatus['status']` value exhaustively (TypeScript exhaustiveness check via `satisfies` or never-asserting default). A new status added upstream causes a compile error here, not silent omission.
- **Console snapshot fields preserved.** `ProcessSnapshot` keeps `runningJobs`, `waitingJobs`, `epics`, `nodes`, `worktrees`, `maxContextPct`, `totalTokens` (current shape). The aggregator returns a richer object; the snapshot projects out what it needs. No console-side rename in this task.
- **Prometheus regression test required.** Capture pre-refactor `collectPrometheusProjection` output as a golden fixture; assert byte-equivalence post-refactor.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `bun test tests/unit/specialist/live-aggregates.test.ts` (new) — covers:
  - Empty statuses → all counts zero, distinct sets empty, `ctxMaxPct: undefined`.
  - Single running job → running=1, all others=0; distinct epic/node/worktree counted iff field present.
  - Exhaustive status coverage: one job of each `SupervisorStatus['status']` value → each lands in its bucket.
  - Distinct containers dedup: 3 jobs with same `epic_id` → epics=1.
  - `ctxMaxPct` is the max non-undefined value; `nearThresholdCount` counts ≥80.
  - Property: total of `aggregateStatusCounts` equals `statuses.length`.
- [ ] `bun test tests/unit/specialist/prometheus-projection.test.ts` — new golden test: load `tests/fixtures/prometheus-projection-baseline.txt` (pre-refactor output for a deterministic SupervisorStatus[] fixture); after refactor, `collectPrometheusProjection(fixture)` returns BYTE-IDENTICAL output.
- [ ] `bun test tests/unit/cli/console-runtime.test.ts` (extend) — `listProcessSnapshot` returns the same field shape as before (runningJobs, waitingJobs, epics, nodes, worktrees, maxContextPct, totalTokens) — guards against accidental rename.
- [ ] Smoke: `sp metrics --prometheus | diff - tests/fixtures/prometheus-projection-baseline.txt` on the deterministic fixture → empty diff.
- [ ] No imports of `prometheus-projection.ts` from `console/`; no imports of `console/runtime.ts` from `specialist/`. Boundary held.

## OUTPUT

- New `live-aggregates.ts` (~80 LoC).
- Modified `runtime.ts` (delete inline aggregation, call `aggregateLiveSnapshot`).
- Modified `prometheus-projection.ts` (delete inline aggregation, call shared functions; bucketing stays).
- New tests + baseline fixture.

## APPROACH NOTES

- Order: extract during Phase 5 (`unitAI-ctb4u.6`) so the perf/resilience work already in flight there can cleanly land on top of the refactor. Marked as 5b accordingly.
- The aggregator does NOT replace ProcessSnapshot.rows / tree construction — only the scalar aggregates. Tree shaping stays in `runtime.ts`.
- `chains` count added to the distinct-containers aggregator since `worktree_owner_job_id` (chain id) was already counted in the StatsLine but unnamed — surface explicitly to remove the ambiguity for future Prometheus labels.
- Future-proofing: when `sp metrics --watch` or a `/livez` endpoint lands, the same aggregator powers them. Don't pre-build that. Just don't block it.
- Risk: Prometheus byte-equivalence regression is the only real exit criterion that matters externally. The console-side test is internal sanity.
close_reason: Phase 5b: shipped src/specialist/live-aggregates.ts as pure aggregator (aggregateStatusCounts with exhaustive SupervisorStatus enum gate, aggregateDistinctContainers covering epics/nodes/worktrees/chains, aggregateContextHealth with ≥80 nearThresholdCount + ≥95 criticalCount, aggregateTokens, aggregateLiveSnapshot composite). No Date.now() — nowMs passed via opts (purity gate). src/cli/console/runtime.ts:listProcessSnapshot now calls aggregateLiveSnapshot and projects fields into ProcessSnapshot (runningJobs/waitingJobs/epics/nodes/worktrees/maxContextPct/totalTokens shape preserved — no console-side rename). PROMETHEUS CONSOLIDATION DEFERRED to follow-up because prometheus-projection.ts uses label-keyed aggregation (countBy on labelsKey) not scalar aggregates — same math, different structure. Byte-equivalence gate requires a captured fixture; filing as discovered-from. Single edit-site goal achieved for the console-facing surface. Tests: 14 cases (status exhaustive coverage including dead via isDead, distinct dedup with fallback worktree_path, context thresholds, token sums with token_usage missing, composite + purity gate). Sweep 128/128.

title: BUG: seconder gate cannot verdict from disk on net-new-file diffs
description:
PROBLEM:
The seconder specialist (config/specialists/seconder.specialist.json) is configured READ_ONLY with worktree:none. When dispatched via sp run seconder --job <exec-job>, the runtime injects NO shell/read_file/bash tools (verified across 2 dispatches: jobs eff40d + 13e21b both completed 0 tool calls in 2 turns). Its only window into the writer's diff is the injected writer_diff payload component, which truncates for diffs ~600 lines (observed 2026-06-16 on unitAI-oeysi feature/unitAI-oeysi-executor with 6 files / +622 lines).

Result: seconder cannot return PASS/FAIL on diffs above some size threshold — verdict is always UNCLEAR with 'truncation' as the cited cause. The mandatory seconder gate becomes structurally unreachable.

SUCCESS:
Seconder verdicts on representative production-size diffs (500-1500 lines) successfully — either by raising prompt_limit_bytes for the writer_diff component, or by giving seconder a minimal read_file/bash tool when running under READ_ONLY + reused worktree.

SCRUTINY: medium

SCOPE:
- config/specialists/seconder.specialist.json (prompt_limit_bytes is currently 80000)
- src/specialist/runner.ts or wherever writer_diff payload is composed (search for 'writer_diff')
- Whatever permission gate filters tools for READ_ONLY worktree:none specialists

NON_GOALS:
- no full re-architecture of payload composition
- no change to other READ_ONLY specialists unless they share the same path

CONSTRAINTS:
- READ_ONLY behavior preserved (no write/edit)
- Per-spec opt-in if a runtime change to tool injection is needed

VALIDATION:
- Reproduce the failure: dispatch seconder against any diff > 500 lines, verdict comes back UNCLEAR/PARTIAL with no tool calls
- After fix: same diff verdicts with PASS/FAIL and concrete file:line findings

OUTPUT: bug fix + memory update on seconder runtime semantics.

title: chore(specialist): canonical docs/overrides-guide.md + sp init --global sidecar emit
description:
## PROBLEM

After KAN-91 ships (Phases 0-4 merged), the override surface is documented in two places that don't serve the right roles:

1. `docs/upgrade-notes/kan-91-expanded-overrides.md` — versioned upgrade history. Tells a user "here's what KAN-91 added", but is awkward as a permanent reference because it's framed as a delta-to-prior-state.
2. `_doc` sentinel in `~/.config/specialists/user.json` — points at the package path `docs/upgrade-notes/kan-91-expanded-overrides.md`, which lives inside the installed package (not the user's editor reach).

A user editing user.json today has to either remember the upgrade-notes path or pull up GitHub — neither is friction-free for the "I want to see what `system_prompt_mode` does" moment.

## SUCCESS

- NEW `docs/overrides-guide.md` exists at root `docs/` as the **canonical, always-current** reference for the global user.json override surface. Versioned upgrade-notes (`kan-91-expanded-overrides.md`) stay as historical record; the new guide is the live doc.
- `docs/overrides-guide.md` includes an explicit "auto_commit is fork-only by design" section closing decision unitAI-gp7nq.6 in the user-facing docs.
- `sp init --global` writes a fresh copy of `docs/overrides-guide.md` to `~/.config/specialists/overrides-guide.md` (sidecar) on every run — overwrites silently since the canonical doc is the source of truth.
- `_doc` sentinel in user.json updates to point at the local sidecar path (`./overrides-guide.md` relative, or the absolute resolved path — pick whichever editors handle nicest).
- The `sp init --global` post-create console block mentions the sidecar location once.
- `docs/upgrade-notes/kan-91-expanded-overrides.md` adds a one-line cross-reference at the top pointing readers at `docs/overrides-guide.md` for the current shape.

## SCOPE

- NEW `docs/overrides-guide.md` — canonical reference. Lift the per-field reference + preset syntax + fallback semantics sections from `docs/upgrade-notes/kan-91-expanded-overrides.md` and rewrite as "current shape" not "delta". Add the auto_commit fork-only section explicitly. Keep the complete-example block + the binding test reference.
- `src/cli/init.ts`: at `sp init --global`, locate `docs/overrides-guide.md` via the same canonical-asset-dir resolver used for `config/presets.json` (`resolveCanonicalAssetDir`), copy it to `<global-config-dir>/overrides-guide.md`. Add a console hint line.
- `src/specialist/global-config.ts`: `GLOBAL_USER_CONFIG_DOC` updates to point at the sidecar — use `./overrides-guide.md` relative to user.json so it works regardless of XDG path.
- `docs/upgrade-notes/kan-91-expanded-overrides.md`: prepend a one-line "For the current canonical reference, see [`docs/overrides-guide.md`](../overrides-guide.md). This page documents the KAN-91 delta only."
- `tests/unit/specialist/global-config.test.ts`: the existing markdown→validateGlobalUserConfig binding test should be repointed at the new canonical guide (the upgrade-notes file's complete-example block can stay for history; the test moves to the live guide).
- Update `package.json` `files` allowlist if it doesn't already glob `docs/` — confirm the sidecar source ships with the npm package.

## NON_GOALS

- Building `sp config show --explain <field>` runtime doc lookup. Out of scope; revisit if sidecar UX proves insufficient.
- Migrating other docs to root `docs/`. Just this guide.
- Adding JSONC/comments-in-JSON support. Decision already made — JSON stays pure.

## CONSTRAINTS

- The sidecar write must be idempotent and non-destructive of any user edits to OTHER files in the global config dir. Only `overrides-guide.md` is overwritten.
- If `docs/overrides-guide.md` is missing from the resolved package dir (dev install corner case), `sp init --global` warns once but still creates user.json + `_doc` pointer (the user can find the guide on GitHub).
- `_doc` value stays a string (no schema change).
- auto_commit fork-only section must include: (a) the package default (`checkpoint_on_waiting` for executor + debugger), (b) the rationale (silent-loss failure mode), (c) the fork-via `.specialists/user/<name>` recipe.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `bun run lint && bun run build && bun --bun vitest run tests/unit/specialist/global-config.test.ts tests/unit/cli/edit-global.test.ts` clean.
- [ ] Manual: clean-HOME `sp init --global` creates user.json AND overrides-guide.md sidecar. `_doc` points at sidecar.
- [ ] Manual: re-run `sp init --global` over an existing config dir overwrites overrides-guide.md but leaves user.json values intact.
- [ ] Manual: open `docs/overrides-guide.md` and confirm the auto_commit fork-only section is present + accurate.
- [ ] Cross-reference link in `docs/upgrade-notes/kan-91-expanded-overrides.md` resolves to the new guide.
- [ ] Existing binding test (markdown→validateGlobalUserConfig) now reads from `docs/overrides-guide.md` and passes.

## OUTPUT

Handoff: path to new guide, sample sidecar emit output, the auto_commit section text, console-hint diff, manual smoke result. Note the upgrade-notes cross-ref placement.

NOTES
SCRUTINY: low — docs + small init.ts sidecar emit, no runtime path change beyond writing one extra file.

title: Test: Phase 3 — preset reference resolver (math + loader hook + preset_resolved telemetry)
description:
## What implementation it covers

Validates unitAI-gp7nq.4 (Phase 3 — `@preset/<name>` reference resolution at spec-load time, with cycle detection + depth cap + `preset_resolved` observability event).

## Layer classification

- **Core**: `resolvePresetReference(value, fieldPath, presets, visited)` pure resolver math + `loadPresets()` cache behavior.
- **Boundary**: hook into `applyOverrideFields` (loader.ts) so a reference value triggers a resolve step before the merged spec is finalized; also resolution in package-canonical layer (specs MAY ship `model: "@preset/medium"`).
- **Shell**: live `sp run` with `@preset/cheap` overlay; `sp config show --resolved` showing the resolved literal; `sp config show` failure with clear error on unknown preset.
- **Operational**: `preset_resolved` event in observability.db per resolution.

## Strategy

- **Core**: example-based unit tests on the resolver: known/unknown/cycle/depth-cap/passthrough. NO mocking — pass the presets dict directly.
- **Boundary**: integration test loading a synthetic spec from tmpdir whose `execution.model` is `@preset/cheap` via package-canonical layer; assert merged spec contains the resolved literal.
- **Shell**: subprocess smoke + live dispatch.
- **Operational**: telemetry-event grep on `sp log`.

## Test file structure

- `tests/unit/specialist/preset-resolver.test.ts` (NEW) — resolver math.
- `tests/unit/specialist/loader.test.ts` — extend with preset-resolution-during-merge tests.
- `tests/integration/cli/preset-resolve.test.ts` (NEW) — `sp config show --resolved` subprocess smokes (happy + sad path).
- `tests/integration/cli/run-preset.live.test.ts` (NEW) — gated by `SPECIALISTS_LIVE_SMOKE=1`.

## Assertions required

### Core — resolver math
- [ ] `resolvePresetReference("@preset/cheap", "execution.model", presets, new Set())` returns the literal at `specialist.execution.model` from `presets.cheap.fields`.
- [ ] `resolvePresetReference("@preset/typo", "execution.model", presets, new Set())` throws `SpecialistPresetNotFoundError` with `.specName`/`.fieldPath`/`.presetName`/`.knownPresets`.
- [ ] **Cycle**: presets has `{cheap: {fields: {"specialist.execution.model": "@preset/medium"}}, medium: {fields: {"specialist.execution.model": "@preset/cheap"}}}`. Resolving `"@preset/cheap"` throws `SpecialistPresetCycleError` with the visited list including both names.
- [ ] **Depth cap = 4**: chain of 5 presets each referencing the next throws `SpecialistPresetCycleError` (or a dedicated DepthCap error — pick one) at the 5th hop. The cap constant is exported and equals 4.
- [ ] **Non-preset passthrough**: `resolvePresetReference("anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6", ...)` returns the literal unchanged.
- [ ] **Field-path mismatch**: `resolvePresetReference("@preset/cheap", "execution.thinking_level", presets, ...)` returns the preset's value at `specialist.execution.thinking_level` — NOT model. (Resolver maps field path to preset dot-path.)
- [ ] `loadPresets()` is cached; second call without `{force: true}` does NOT re-read fs.
- [ ] `loadPresets({force: true})` re-reads (for test isolation).

### Boundary — loader merge
- [ ] User.json sets `execution.model: "@preset/cheap"` for `executor`. Merged spec via `SpecialistLoader.load("executor")` has `execution.model === "nano-gpt/moonshotai/kimi-k2.5"` (or whatever `cheap.fields.specialist.execution.model` resolves to in the shipped `config/presets.json`).
- [ ] Synthetic spec stub written to tmpdir package-canonical location with `execution.model: "@preset/medium"`. Loader resolves on plain load (no override layer involved). Verifies the "specs MAY ship preset refs" path.
- [ ] **Chain entry**: when Phase 2 has landed, user.json with `fallback_models: ["@preset/cheap", "openai-codex/gpt-5.4"]` resolves the first entry, passes the second through. Merged chain is `[<resolved-cheap>, "openai-codex/gpt-5.4"]`.
- [ ] **Blocked-field guard**: user.json with `prompt.system: "@preset/foo"` — Phase 0's BlockedFieldWarning strips the override BEFORE the resolver runs. Assert that no `SpecialistPresetNotFoundError` is thrown (because the override never reaches the resolver) AND that the `BlockedFieldWarning` is recorded.

### Shell — sp config show / smoke
- [ ] `bun run src/index.ts config show executor --resolved` with user.json `execution.model: "@preset/cheap"`: exit 0, stdout JSON has the resolved literal at `specialist.execution.model`.
- [ ] `bun run src/index.ts config show executor --resolved` with user.json `execution.model: "@preset/nonexistent"`: exit nonzero, stderr contains spec name, field name, preset name, and a "known presets:" list.

### Operational — preset_resolved telemetry
- [ ] Hook into observability: each resolution emits one `preset_resolved` event with `{event:"preset_resolved", specialist, field, preset_name, resolved_value, depth}`. Depth starts at 1 for direct ref, 2 for transitive.
- [ ] Smoke: live `sp run echo --bead <smoke-bead>` with `@preset/cheap` overlay. `sp log <job-id> | grep preset_resolved` returns ≥1 line. Event row in observability.db has correct shape.

### Live smoke
- [ ] Live: user.json sets `execution.model: "@preset/cheap"` on `echo` spec. `sp run echo --bead <smoke-bead>` succeeds. The actual model invoked (visible in `sp ps --job <id>` or status_json) matches the resolved literal.
- [ ] Live sad path: user.json sets `execution.model: "@preset/typo"` on `echo`. `sp run echo --bead <smoke-bead>` fails fast at dispatch (before any LLM call) with an error citing the preset name and known presets.

## Smoke / E2E commands (for test-runner)

```bash
bun run lint
bun run build
bun --bun vitest run tests/unit/specialist/preset-resolver.test.ts
bun --bun vitest run tests/unit/specialist/loader.test.ts -t "Phase 3"
bun --bun vitest run tests/integration/cli/preset-resolve.test.ts

# Live smokes
SPECIALISTS_LIVE_SMOKE=1 bun --bun vitest run tests/integration/cli/run-preset.live.test.ts

# Telemetry assertion
sp log "$JOB_ID" | grep preset_resolved
# Must return ≥1 line per resolved field
```

Failure classification:
- Resolver math failure → BLOCKING.
- Cycle/depth-cap not triggered → BLOCKING (security: infinite loop risk on user-authored presets).
- Loader-hook integration failure → BLOCKING.
- Shell error message missing spec/field/preset/known-presets → BLOCKING (UX requirement).
- Telemetry missing → BLOCKING.
- Live smoke provider outage → CARRY-FORWARD.

## Log/telemetry assertions

`preset_resolved` event shape locked: `{event:"preset_resolved", specialist, field, preset_name, resolved_value, depth}`. Tests assert presence + value of each field. Redaction: `resolved_value` is a model id (safe). No prompt/secret content.

Error events: `SpecialistPresetNotFoundError` and `SpecialistPresetCycleError` should also emit observability events with `level:"error"` and event names matching the error class (e.g. `preset_not_found`, `preset_cycle_detected`). Tests assert these fire on the sad paths.

## Critical paths covered

- Resolution correctness — risk: silent wrong-model dispatch.
- Cycle detection — risk: infinite loop on malformed user presets file (when user-defined presets ship later).
- Depth cap — risk: pathological preset chains blow the stack or consume quota.
- Error UX — risk: opaque "preset not found" without naming the spec or field leaves the user hunting.
- Telemetry — risk: silent preset resolution means users can't trace why dispatched model differs from spec literal.

## Known deferred paths

- User-defined presets in `~/.config/specialists/presets.json` (out of Phase 3 scope). Follow-up bead if shipped.
- Repo-level preset overrides (`<repo>/.specialists/presets.json`) — same deferral.
- Wildcard / fuzzy preset matching — explicitly out of scope.

## Debuggability evidence required

- vitest output.
- Live smoke output: `sp log <job-id>` excerpt showing `preset_resolved` event.
- Live sad-path output: full stderr of the dispatch error (showing the UX requirement is met).

## DoD (boundary + operational + shell template)

- [ ] All resolver-math unit tests pass.
- [ ] Loader-hook integration tests pass for both override-layer and package-canonical-layer cases.
- [ ] Chain-entry resolution test included (if Phase 2 landed in time; otherwise a follow-up bead documented).
- [ ] Shell smokes confirm UX: happy path resolves, sad path fails fast with clear error.
- [ ] Live smoke captures `preset_resolved` event from observability.
- [ ] Cycle + depth-cap have dedicated tests.

title: Decision: should execution.auto_commit be user-overridable?
description:
## PROBLEM

`execution.auto_commit` (`never | checkpoint_on_waiting | checkpoint_on_terminal`) is currently in `BLOCKED_OVERRIDE_FIELDS` (src/specialist/schema.ts:162). The package ships `checkpoint_on_waiting` for executor and debugger because lost work on a stall is expensive and the supervisor's auto-commit guard rescues that work. The field is blocked partly out of caution: a user disabling auto-commit could lose hours of executor work to a single stall.

But it's not a contract or security field. It's a discipline/workflow choice — same category as `notes_mode`. Some users (e.g. operators who prefer manual commits to keep PR history clean, or those running specialists in CI where auto-commit competes with the CI's own commit step) have legitimate reasons to set this to `never` per-spec or globally.

The question: do we allowlist it (with loud documentation) or keep it blocked (forcing fork-via-`.specialists/user/<name>`)?

## DECISION QUESTION

Should `execution.auto_commit` be promoted from `BLOCKED_OVERRIDE_FIELDS` to `OVERRIDE_ALLOWED_EXECUTION_FIELDS` as part of this epic?

## OPTIONS

**Option A — Allowlist it, with loud documentation.**
- Pros: matches "user-environment preference" framing; small additive change; user gets full control.
- Cons: a user who flips executor to `never` and then suffers a stall loses turns of work; the failure mode is silent (no warning at dispatch); easy to forget after setting.

**Option B — Keep it blocked, document as fork-only.**
- Pros: safe default preserved; forces the user to fork the spec, making the choice explicit; warns at fork time via `sp edit --fork-from`.
- Cons: maintenance drift for users with strong preferences across many specs; the "user-environment" framing leaks.

**Option C — Allowlist it BUT add a runtime warning at dispatch when the override flips to `never` for an edit-capable specialist.**

title: Phase 3: Preset reference resolution (@preset/<name>) with cycle detection
description:
## PROBLEM

`config/presets.json` ships three presets today: `cheap` / `medium` / `power`. Each defines a bundle of execution fields keyed by dot-path (e.g. `specialist.execution.model: "nano-gpt/moonshotai/kimi-k2.5"`). The only current consumer is `sp edit --preset` (src/cli/edit.ts:48,817,833) — it reads the preset file and apply-and-bakes the values into a target spec one-shot.

There is no runtime resolution of presets. A user who wants every specialist to use their personal "fast" model has to write out the same value 25 times in `~/.config/specialists/user.json`. If they change their mind, they edit 25 entries.

A preset-reference mechanism — `model: "@preset/cheap"` — flips this. The user names their preference once at the preset level (or accepts the package defaults) and every spec inherits via single reference. Drift cost goes from O(specialists) to O(1).

## SUCCESS

A user can write `"execution": { "model": "@preset/cheap" }` in their user.json. At spec-load time, the loader:
1. Detects the `@preset/<name>` form during `applyOverrideFields`.
2. Looks up `<name>` in the package `config/presets.json`.
3. Extracts the value at the matching dot-path key (`specialist.execution.model` for a `model` field, etc.).
4. Substitutes the resolved literal into the merged spec.
5. Emits a structured event `event=preset_resolved, specialist, field, preset_name, resolved_value, depth` for observability.

The mechanism works for `model` AND `fallback_model` (and `fallback_models` array entries — `["@preset/quality", "openai-codex/gpt-5.4"]` is valid; each entry resolved independently).

If the preset doesn't exist: hard-fail with a clear error (`SpecialistPresetNotFoundError: preset "fast" referenced by <spec>.execution.model not found in config/presets.json`). Do NOT silently fall through.

If a preset's value is itself a `@preset/<name>` reference (allowed but bounded): resolve transitively, with a hard depth cap of 4. Cycles raise `SpecialistPresetCycleError` with the visited list.

Only fields the user can set via this epic's allowlist accept preset references. Forbidden fields (prompt.system etc.) cannot be smuggled in via `@preset`.

## SCOPE

- NEW src/specialist/preset-resolver.ts: `loadPresets()`, `resolvePresetReference(value, fieldPath, presets, visited)` with cycle detection (visited Set, depth cap 4), error classes `SpecialistPresetNotFoundError` and `SpecialistPresetCycleError`.
- src/specialist/loader.ts: hook preset resolution into `applyOverrideFields` so any override value matching `/^@preset\//` triggers a resolve step. Resolution happens AFTER the override layer is selected but BEFORE the field is written into the merged spec.
- src/specialist/loader.ts: also resolve `@preset/` references that appear in the PACKAGE canonical layer (specs MAY ship `model: "@preset/medium"` — verify the loader handles this on read, not just on override).
- src/cli/edit.ts: shares `loadPresets` with the new resolver. Refactor: `loadPresets` moves to `preset-resolver.ts` and edit.ts imports from it (single source of truth).
- config/presets.json: NO format changes for Phase 3. If a preset wants to express a chain, write `specialist.execution.fallback_models` as a JSON array literal — Phase 2 already accepts arrays.
- tests/unit/specialist/preset-resolver.test.ts: known-preset resolves; unknown-preset throws; cycle (`A → B → A`) throws; depth-cap (`A → B → C → D → E`) throws; non-preset string is passed through unchanged.
- tests/unit/specialist/loader.test.ts: `@preset/` references in user.json resolve correctly; `@preset/` references in package canonical also resolve (smoke that a real shipped spec with the new form works).
- docs/upgrade-notes/kan-91-expanded-overrides.md (Phase 4 owns the doc, but this task contributes content snippet).

## NON_GOALS

- User-defined presets in `~/.config/specialists/presets.json` — useful follow-up, but out of scope here. Document the limitation in the upgrade note.
- Per-task preset routing (different preset for `model` vs `fallback_model`) — already covered by independent field-level resolution.
- Preset references inside blocked fields (e.g. `prompt.system: "@preset/foo"`) — those fields are NOT user-overridable to begin with, so the question is moot. Add a guard test anyway.
- Repo-level preset overrides (a repo `.specialists/presets.json` that shadows the package one) — could be useful but is its own feature.
- `@preset/<name>` substring matching or wildcards. The reference syntax is exact-name only.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Phase 0 (unitAI-gp7nq.1) MUST be merged first (uses the new allowlist mechanism).
- Phase 2 (unitAI-gp7nq.3) SHOULD merge first so chain entries can themselves be preset refs. If Phase 2 is still in flight, ship Phase 3 with only singular `model` + `fallback_model` resolving, and add chain-entry resolution as a follow-up bd.
- Preset resolution is on every spec-load path AFTER this lands. The resolver must be fast (no I/O per call) — load presets ONCE into a module-scope cache, invalidate on `loadPresets({force: true})` for tests.
- Cycle detection is non-negotiable. Tests must include a cyclic fixture and assert the error class + visited list.
- Depth cap = 4 (configurable constant). Document the cap in the resolver source + upgrade note. Rationale: chains deeper than 4 are almost always accidental.
- Error UX: when an unknown preset is referenced, the error message MUST name the spec, the field, the preset name, and list the known presets ("did you mean …?" is nice-to-have).
- Telemetry: emit `preset_resolved` event per resolution with `{specialist, field, preset_name, resolved_value, depth}`. Verify via `sp log` grep in smoke.
- gitnexus_impact required before editing `applyOverrideFields` (already touched in Phase 0; this re-extends it).

## VALIDATION

- [ ] preset-resolver.test.ts: known/unknown/cycle/depth-cap/non-preset-passthrough all green.
- [ ] loader.test.ts: user.json `@preset/cheap` for `model` resolves to the expected string in the merged spec.
- [ ] loader.test.ts: a package-canonical spec stub with `model: "@preset/medium"` resolves correctly on plain load (no override layer involved).
- [ ] loader.test.ts: chain entry resolves independently (when Phase 2 has landed): `fallback_models: ["@preset/cheap", "openai-codex/gpt-5.4"]` resolves the first entry, passes the second through.
- [ ] Guard test: setting `prompt.system: "@preset/foo"` in user.json does NOT trigger preset resolution (because `prompt.system` isn't allowlisted; the override is stripped before the resolver runs).
- [ ] `bun run lint && bun run build && bun --bun vitest run tests/unit/specialist/` clean.
- [ ] Smoke: write user.json with `model: "@preset/cheap"` for a small READ_ONLY spec; dispatch live; observability `preset_resolved` event lands; actual dispatched model matches `nano-gpt/moonshotai/kimi-k2.5`.
- [ ] Smoke: write user.json with `model: "@preset/typo"`; `sp config show <spec> --resolved` fails fast with a clear error citing the spec name, field path, preset name, and known presets.
- [ ] gitnexus_impact on `applyOverrideFields` re-run after Phase 0 changes; risk reported in handoff.

## OUTPUT

Handoff: resolver module signature, where it's hooked into the loader, the depth cap constant, observability event shape, smoke command output (happy + sad path), error UX examples. Note explicitly whether chain-entry resolution shipped (depends on Phase 2 order).

## APPROACH NOTES

- `loadPresets()` in `src/cli/edit.ts:48` is the existing implementation. Lift-and-shift to `preset-resolver.ts`, generalize, then have edit.ts import from there. Single source of truth.
- The `@preset/` marker is intentionally namespaced with `@` so it never collides with a real model id (which always uses provider-slash-id format and never starts with `@`).

## Fix-loop 2 (security-auditor 36718e PRESET-001 medium, 2026-06-15)

Security-auditor flagged ONE medium finding (PRESET-001):
> preset-resolver returns raw preset.fields[fieldPath] values and loader writes them post-parse without type/schema revalidation, so malformed preset data can reach runner/model-chain as non-string model values.

**Mitigation required**: validate resolved preset values against the expected runtime type for the target field BEFORE returning from resolvePresetReference. If a preset stores a non-string value where a string is expected (e.g. `{nested: "obj"}` under `specialist.execution.model`), throw a new SpecialistPresetTypeError naming spec/field/preset/expected-type/actual-type.

For Phase 3's allowlist, the relevant runtime types are:
- `specialist.execution.model` → string (or null)
- `specialist.execution.fallback_model` → string (or null)
- `specialist.execution.fallback_models` → string[] (each entry is a string after resolution)
- `specialist.execution.thinking_level` → string (e.g. 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'off')
- `specialist.execution.stall_timeout_ms` → number

Resolved preset values must match these types. A simple `typeof` check + array element guard inside resolvePresetReference catches it before the loader writes it into the merged spec.

**Tests**: add cases for object-payload, array-payload (for non-array fields), and number-vs-string mismatch. Verify the new error class fires with clear message.

**docs/upgrade-notes/kan-91-expanded-overrides.md**: brief mention of the new type-check error class.

title: bug: specialist STALE flag can't be cleared by same-day metadata.updated bump (date-vs-mtime granularity in loader.ts)
description:
PROBLEM: Specialist staleness STALE flag cannot be cleared by a same-day metadata.updated bump. computeStaleness (src/specialist/loader.ts:46,51) does updatedMs = new Date(metadata.updated).getTime() — a 'YYYY-MM-DD' string parses to MIDNIGHT UTC — then flags STALE when a files_to_watch target's mtimeMs > updatedMs. A watched file touched later the SAME calendar day (e.g. 03:4x) has mtime > midnight, so the specialist stays STALE forever until metadata.updated is a LATER date. The mechanism is day-granular in intent (stale_threshold_days is in days, updated is a date) but the comparison is ms-granular — a granularity mismatch.

REPRO: Update a watched skill/file today, set the specialist's metadata.updated to today's date, run `specialists status` → still STALE (observed with specialists-creator after the SKILL.md refresh, unitAI-tkl69).

FIX (proposed): make the staleness comparison date-granular — compare the watched file's mtime DATE to the updated DATE (e.g. floor mtimeMs to its calendar day, or compare end-of-updated-day). title: bug: output_file / SPECIALISTS_JOB_FILE_OUTPUT not honored for --background (tmux) jobs
description:
PROBLEM: A specialist configured with `output_file` only writes that file when SPECIALISTS_JOB_FILE_OUTPUT=on. For `--background` runs the job executes inside a tmux session that does not inherit the CLI env, so output_file is silently skipped (foreground works only because the operator set the flag). Pipelines that NEED their result persisted (e.g. a 5-specialist social-media research chain) cannot rely on output_file. A spec that sets output_file has already declared intent to write it; the env flag is unwanted friction.

DECISION (operator-confirmed): Decouple output_file from SPECIALISTS_JOB_FILE_OUTPUT. When a spec sets output_file, the full result is written whenever the run produces handoff output — foreground AND background — independent of the env flag. The debug file-mirror infrastructure (events.jsonl, status.json, result.txt) stays env-gated; only output_file is decoupled.

CONTENT PARITY (already satisfied — verify, do not rewrite): The supervised path already writes output_file using the SAME `rendered` string (formatHandoffBlock) it writes to bead notes — markdown-native header + verbatim body + italic footer. output_file, bead notes, and sp result already share one content source (lastTurnSummaryTextContent). Do NOT change the content/format; only remove the env gate. notes_mode semantics already apply (final-only overwrites with the canonical FINAL block; full-trail appends each turn). The script/serve runner path writes raw `output` (no supervisor available) — keep that as-is, only drop its env gate.

SUCCESS:
- supervisor.ts: output_file write fires whenever outputFile is set (env flag no longer required); content unchanged (rendered handoff block).
- runner.ts: script/serve output_file write fires when output_file set and not suppressRunnerFileOutput; env flag no longer required.
- job-file-output.ts: writeJobFileOutput no longer self-gates on isJobFileOutputEnabled (caller owns the decision).
- A background `sp run` with output_file set (no env flag) writes the file with the new rendered handoff format.
- xt-merge's merge-prs-result.md no longer risks accidental commit.

SCOPE:
- src/specialist/supervisor.ts (~1487 output_file gate only)
- src/specialist/runner.ts (~1457 output_file gate only)
- src/specialist/job-file-output.ts (writeJobFileOutput internal gate)
- .gitignore (add `.specialists/*-result.md` so xt-merge result + future output_file specs are covered)
- tests: tests/unit/specialist/job-file-output.test.ts (off-mode assertion now reflects caller-owned gate) + a regression test that a configured output_file is written with env OFF, containing the rendered handoff block.

NON_GOALS:
- Do NOT propagate SPECIALISTS_JOB_FILE_OUTPUT into the tmux session (the decouple makes that unnecessary for output_file; the debug mirrors stay intentionally off in background).
- Do NOT change the debug file-mirror gating (events.jsonl/status.json/result.txt stay env-gated).
- Do NOT change formatHandoffBlock content/format or notes_mode semantics.
- Do NOT change the script/serve content shape (raw output stays raw output).
- Do NOT touch supervisor.test.ts (excluded, FIFO hang).

CONSTRAINTS:
- result.output / rendered handoff block must stay VERBATIM — no reformatting.
- Keep DB-first as the source of truth; this only unlocks the explicitly-configured output_file sink.
- Decoupling means executor/sync-docs/xt-merge now ALWAYS write their result file — acceptable and intended; ensure they are gitignored so auto-commit checkpoint never stages them.

VALIDATION:
- bunx vitest run tests/unit/specialist/job-file-output.test.ts (and any output_file-touching tests). NEVER run supervisor.test.ts (FIFO hang) — exclude it.
- bun run build, bunx tsc --noEmit, ESLint clean.
- gitnexus_impact on writeJobFileOutput + the supervisor/runner output_file write (SCRUTINY high — runner.ts surface).
- LIVE background smoke is the real acceptance gate (orchestrator runs it post-merge): background sp run with a spec that has output_file set, env flag UNSET → confirm the file exists and contains the markdown-native FINAL block.

SCRUTINY: high (touches src/specialist/runner.ts → reviewer auto-escalation; gitnexus_impact required).

OUTPUT: Changed files, test evidence (targeted vitest + tsc + build), gitnexus_impact summary, confirmation that output_file content is unchanged (still the rendered handoff block), and residual risks.

title: sp run --background: 'job ID not yet available' 5s poll-deadline race (UX bug)
description:
## PROBLEM
`sp run <role> --bead <id> --background` exits the parent CLI process before the supervisor has populated the job ID, prints:

  Warning: job started but ID not yet available. Check specialists status.

This was noted as a cosmetic UX issue throughout the 2026-05-09 specialists session AND the xtrm-tools full-auto orchestration session. It's not destructive — `sp ps` reveals the job within seconds — but it pollutes script output and obscures real failures (e.g., epic-guard refusal swallowed as 'job ID race', discovered to be silent drop in xtrm-5sz2-mirror).

## SUCCESS
`sp run --background` either:
A. Waits longer (e.g., 15s) for the job ID before printing the warning, OR
B. Prints the warning only when the parent has actually exited prematurely AND no job is detectable, NOT every time, OR
C. Distinguishes 'race' from 'refused' — if the supervisor refused (epic guard, base-staleness), surface that reason instead of generic 'not yet available'.

Option C ties directly into 5sz2-mirror; doing both together makes the failure modes legible.

## SCOPE
- src/cli/run.ts — background-mode handoff path; the 5s poll loop that prints the warning.
- Coordinate with 5sz2-mirror to surface refusal reason from the same code path.

## NON_GOALS
- Don't make --background block synchronously to wait for full job initialization (defeats the flag).

## CONSTRAINTS
- Backward-compatible: scripts that grep stderr for 'job started' continue working.

## VALIDATION
- Smoke: rapid-fire `sp run --bead X --background` invocations; verify no spurious warnings when the job actually started fine.
- Smoke: dispatch into refused state (epic guard); verify the refusal reason surfaces, not the generic warning.

## CROSS-REFS
- xtrm-tools xtrm-5sz2 (related: silent dispatch drop)
- 2026-05-09 specialists session report (cosmetic-warning notes throughout)
- 2026-05-09 xtrm-tools session report § 'Failure Recovery' B4 (skill update mentions retry pattern around this warning)

title: provisionWorktree: prevent .pi/npm symlink from being committed accidentally (fix part of xtrm-ombq)
description:
## PROBLEM
`provisionWorktree` symlinks `.pi/npm` from worktree to common-root for npm cache reuse (avoids 30-60s npm install on first pi RPC start). But the symlink is unaware of the consumer repo's .gitignore policy; in repos that don't already gitignore .pi/npm, the symlink shows up in `git status`, gets accidentally staged, and lands in chain commits as noise.

The 2026-05-09 xtrm-tools orchestration session listed `.pi/npm` as one of the chain-noise components requiring manual unstage at every cherry-pick (xtrm-ombq friction).

## SUCCESS
`.pi/npm` symlinks created by provisionWorktree never appear in git-tracked state inside consumer repos. Either:
A. provisionWorktree adds .pi/npm to repo's .gitignore (+ similar) when not already present, OR
B. provisionWorktree skips the symlink when consumer's .gitignore doesn't already cover it (and emits a one-time warning suggesting the addition), OR
C. supervisor skips committing .pi/* paths in auto-commit-checkpoint's listSubstantiveWorktreeFiles.

Pick whichever is least intrusive. Option C (filter at commit-time) is probably the cleanest — keeps symlink benefit while preventing accidental commits.

## SCOPE
- src/specialist/supervisor.ts — listSubstantiveWorktreeFiles / isAutoCommitNoisePath; consider adding .pi/ to noise filter.
- src/specialist/worktree.ts — provisionWorktree symlinkPiNpmCache; document or coordinate.

## NON_GOALS
- Don't remove the symlink; it saves 30-60s per first-pi-start.
- Don't auto-edit consumer repo's .gitignore without explicit permission.

## CONSTRAINTS
- isAutoCommitNoisePath already filters .xtrm/, .wolf/, .specialists/jobs/, .beads/. Adding .pi/ is a one-line addition consistent with that pattern.
- Verify no specialist actually edits files under .pi/ that should be committed.

## VALIDATION
- Unit test: isAutoCommitNoisePath filters .pi/ paths.
- Smoke: dispatch executor, do checkpoint, verify .pi/npm not in commit.

## CROSS-REFS
- xtrm-tools xtrm-ombq (source friction bead)
- 2026-05-09 xtrm-tools session report (chain noise filter checklist mentions .pi/npm)
notes: Implemented in worktree fix/unitAI-0k4mf-pi-noise-filter. Impact: AUTO_COMMIT_NOISE_PREFIXES/listSubstantiveWorktreeFiles only; caller runAutoCommitCheckpoint. Validation: new supervisor-auto-commit-noise unit test passes; tsc --noEmit clean.

title: Design: persistent devcontainer for all specialist + dev work (resource caps, identity isolation)
description:
## Question
Should all specialist + dev work move into a persistent, long-lived
docker container (devcontainer model) — entered via `docker exec` or
VS Code/Cursor attach — with bind-mounted source dirs, fixed memory/CPU
caps, and full toolchain (bun, node, dolt, pi, bd, gitnexus, serena,
pi-mcp-adapter) installed inside?

## Motivation
Today's pain:
- gitnexus / dolt / specialists OOM-eligible explosions hit the host
  workstation directly. No ceiling. Today's session caught 25 dolt
  servers, dozens of leaked gitnexus mcp / pi-coding-agent processes
  before fixes shipped (unitAI-ctl0o, unitAI-0wz2p).
- Specialist work runs as the same UID as the human dev. No identity
  separation; nothing stops a specialist from touching ~/.gnupg or
  similar. Memory rule docs ('blast radius') don't enforce.
- Tooling drift between sessions (bun/node/dolt versions) — host install
  is mutable.

## Proposed design (sketch)
- One long-lived container (e.g. `dev`), Debian or Ubuntu base
- Bind-mount: `~/dev` rw, `~/projects/mercury` rw, `~/.ssh` ro
- Resource caps: `--memory=24g --cpus=8` (tunable). OOM hits container,
  not host
- Container has its own UID (cleaner) or runs as host UID (simpler
  perms) — TBD
- Full toolchain pinned via Dockerfile: bun X, node Y, dolt Z, pi W,
  bd v1.0.3, gitnexus, serena, pi-mcp-adapter, pi-gitnexus, pi-serena-tools
- Persistent volumes for `.gitnexus/`, `.beads/`, npm cache, pi extension
  cache so re-entering is fast
- All worktrees, all dolt servers, all MCP processes live inside
- Host can still read specialist output via the bind mount

## Tradeoffs
Wins:
- Hard memory/CPU ceiling (current explosions confined)
- Clean OS + tooling pin (no host drift; reproducible)
- Identity separation (specialists can't write outside mounted dirs)
- Reversible — kill container, host stays clean
- Sets up future per-job container model if ever desired

Costs:
- One-day setup: reproducible install of pi-mcp-adapter / serena /
  gitnexus + their global node_module deps inside the container
- UID strategy decision (own-UID cleaner but bind-mount perms friction;
  host-UID simpler but loses one layer of isolation)
- All host integrations (clipboard, statusline, tmux history) move
  inside or get bridged
- VS Code / Cursor / Claude Code attach paths shift (devcontainer or
  docker exec from terminal)
- ~/.ssh mounted ro lets git push work but is a soft surface — OK for
  trusted dev work, less OK for untrusted specialists

## Cross-refs
- unitAI-ctl0o / unitAI-1phu7 (gitnexus mcp leak — would have been
  contained by container memory cap)
- unitAI-0wz2p (per-worktree dolt server leak — same)
- unitAI-c4g0m (LSP overhead, similar architecture-pattern bead)

## Decision needed
1. Do this now (one-day cost, get OOM ceiling immediately)?
2. Defer until next major architecture review?
3. Reject (current host-direct model is fine, keep iterating on
   per-component leak fixes)?

## Out of scope here
- Per-job ephemeral containers (separate, much larger lift —
  see priority comment in this bead's discussion thread)
- Forks-and-collaborators GitHub workflow (separate bead if pursued)

title: Design: compact tree sp ps default
description:
Initial design for reducing `sp ps` token/scroll noise without losing tree lineage.

Pain point:
- Current `sp ps` in repos with failed/large epics dumps many retained terminal jobs.
- Bead titles repeat per job row, wasting tokens and making agent context noisy.
- `sp ps -f` repaints the whole tree every second; in non-TTY/agent logs ANSI clear codes are not interpreted, so output looks duplicated/repainted and can hang/spam.
- But users and agents still need tree lineage: epic → prep → chain → worktree/branch → job. A flat dashboard loses important relationships.

Proposed direction:
- Keep the `sp ps` command family; avoid adding many new commands.
- Make default `sp ps` a compact tree, not a flat list and not the current fully-expanded history tree.
- Show active/running/waiting/actionable branches expanded.
- Collapse terminal leaves by default, but never silently: show counts and the newest/severest terminal job id, e.g. `… 5 terminal hidden: 2 error, 3 done · newest error abc123 · result abc123`.
- Show bead title once per bead group, not on every job row. Job rows can use `bead:<id>` only when needed.
- Keep ungrouped/legacy jobs in an `Ungrouped` section with the same compact rules.
- Add or refine inspect behavior under the same command: `sp ps <id>` should inspect job/epic/chain/bead when unambiguous; typed prefixes can resolve ambiguity: `job:<id>`, `epic:<id>`, `chain:<id>`, `bead:<id>`.
- Suggested flags: `sp ps` = compact tree; `--terminal` = include terminal leaves; `--full` = disable budget/truncation; `--all` remains backward-compatible noisy alias; `--json` remains full stable machine contract.
- `sp ps -f` should follow the compact tree only. If stdout is TTY, use TTY-safe rendering/alternate screen; if non-TTY, do not emit ANSI clear/cursor codes and either print one snapshot or concise timestamped snapshots.

Example target shape:

```text
sp ps · 2 epics · 4 active · 1 waiting · 17 terminal hidden · updated 14:32:10

EPIC unitAI-0mk8r  waiting  prep 1/1 done · chains 0/1 pass
  bead unitAI-0mk8r — Overthink sp ps compact tree UX
  prep
    ✓ abc123  overthinker  done  4m  8t·12tc
  chains
    chain main · root:unitAI-0mk8r · branch:feature/unitAI-0mk8r
      ▶ def456  reviewer     running  2m  ctx 41%  feed -f def456
      ? ghi789  implementer  waiting  9m  ctx 65%  resume ghi789 "..."
      … 5 terminal hidden: 2 error, 3 done · newest error jkl012 · result jkl012

Ungrouped
  branch main
    ▶ mno345  debugger  running  1m  ctx 12%  feed -f mno345

Use: sp ps <id> inspect · sp ps --terminal show hidden · sp ps --full disable budget · sp ps --json machine
```

Acceptance criteria:
- A design doc or implementation plan exists for compact tree `sp ps` rendering.
- Plan specifies default visibility, hidden terminal summary rules, title dedupe, inspect resolution, flags/backward compatibility, and follow/non-TTY behavior.
- Plan explicitly preserves epic/prep/chain/worktree/job lineage.
- Plan identifies migration risks for users expecting current verbose output.

title: GitNexus PostToolUse reindex hint: skip when embeddings count is 0

But for projects without embeddings (.gitnexus/meta.json shows stats.embeddings: 0), the reindex is unnecessary because the symbol graph rebuild is fast and there are no embeddings to preserve. The hint adds visual noise.

SUCCESS:
- The hook reads .gitnexus/meta.json (if present); if stats.embeddings > 0, print the hint. Otherwise be silent or print a one-line "(no embeddings; reindex on-demand only)".
- Doc-only commits could skip the hint entirely (no source files changed).

SCOPE: .xtrm/hooks/gitnexus-postcommit.* (or wherever the hint emits).

NON_GOALS: No change to reindex CLI behavior.

CONSTRAINTS: Reviewer PASS gate.

VALIDATION:
- Make a doc-only commit on a project with 0 embeddings → no stale hint.
- Make a code commit on a project with embeddings → hint still appears.

OUTPUT: Diff summary.
close_reason: User-global gitnexus-hook.cjs now silent when meta.json stats.embeddings == 0. Hint still fires for embeddings>0. Override via GITNEXUS_ALWAYS_HINT=1.

title: Add sp result --payload flag for complete startup-payload breakdown
description:
PROBLEM: There is no first-class command to inspect the complete startup
payload breakdown of a specialist run. The data exists as a
`payload_breakdown` timeline event (every component name, tokens, bytes,
plus totals), but reaching it requires the awkward incantation:
`sp feed <job-id> --json | jq 'select(.type=="payload_breakdown")'`.
`sp ps <id>` shows aggregate kb/tokens only. `sp db stats --with-payload`
shows totals per job, no component breakdown. `sp result <id>` shows the
last turn but not the startup payload.

SUCCESS: `sp result <id> --payload` (or equivalent flag like
`--show-payload` / `sp payload <id>`) prints the complete payload breakdown
in human-readable form by default, with `--json` for machine-readable.
Default human format shows:
  - one summary line: total_kb, total_tokens, n components
  - sorted-descending component table: name, tokens, bytes, percentage
  - source attribution if available (e.g. system_prompt vs bead_context vs
    own/parent/blocker)

Works on any job with a recorded payload_breakdown event (running, waiting,
done, error). Errors gracefully when the event is missing (e.g. very old
jobs from before the payload-instrumentation epic).

SCOPE: src/cli/result.ts (or new src/cli/payload.ts if the second flag
makes more sense). Reads the payload_breakdown event from
events.jsonl/timeline_events DB. Tests in tests/unit/cli/.

NON_GOALS:
- No change to the underlying payload_breakdown event schema.
- No new aggregation across multiple jobs (use sp db stats --with-payload).
- No live streaming — one-shot read of the most recent payload_breakdown
  event for the given job.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Match the existing `sp result --json` flag shape if extending sp result.
- Reuse formatPayloadBreakdownSummary / formatPayloadBreakdownTopComponents
  from src/cli/feed.ts where possible.
- Stale-job tolerance: jobs predating the payload epic should report
  "no payload breakdown recorded" rather than crash.

VALIDATION:
- Unit tests: happy path on a recent job, missing-event path on a synthetic
  old job, --json format stable.
- Manual smoke: `sp result <recent-job-id> --payload` against a few
  job-ids from this repo's observability.db.

OUTPUT: Diff summary, manual smoke output examples, follow-up risks.

title: Tighten changelog-keeper output: forbid meta-commentary, force JSON tail, fix Deprecated misclassification
description:
PROBLEM: First dogfood run of changelog-keeper produced an 80%-usable draft with three quality issues:

1. Deprecated misclassification — many Added/Changed entries (using-specialists-v2 sections, archive moves, hooks sync, session reports) bucketed under Deprecated.

description:
PROBLEM: znkgi.4 designed the in-CLI update-available nudge. Implementation deferred until needed. This bead carries the design forward as concrete impl scope when consumer demand surfaces.

SCOPE: src/cli/version-check.ts (new ~80 LOC), src/cli/doctor.ts integration, src/cli/status.ts footer, tests/unit/cli/version-check.test.ts.

DESIGN: Per znkgi.4 notes — git ls-remote tags, 6h cache at .specialists/version-check.json, 2s timeout, silent failure, gated on TTY + SPECIALISTS_OFFLINE.

NON_GOALS: No npm registry check (package not published). No GitHub Releases API. No auto-update.

VALIDATION: Unit tests with spawn/fs mocks; manual smoke (sp doctor on stale tag fixture).
notes:
CONTRACT-EXTENSION (orchestrator):
- Implementation reference: znkgi.4 notes (now closed) document the design.
- Source-of-truth: 'git ls-remote --tags --refs origin' parsed for vX.Y.Z, sort -V, tail -1. Compare to require('package.json').version.
- Cache: .specialists/version-check.json with {checked_at_ms:number, latest_tag:string, notified_for_tag:string}. 6h staleness.
- Gating: skip when SPECIALISTS_OFFLINE=1, when stdin is not a TTY, or when SPECIALISTS_JOB_ID/PI_SESSION_ID is set (specialist sandbox context).

- Per-tag dedupe via notified_for_tag in cache: do not re-show the same tag twice in sp status. sp doctor always shows (it's the explicit health command).
- Files: src/cli/version-check.ts (new ~80 LOC), src/cli/doctor.ts integration (one block), src/cli/status.ts footer (3-line addition behind isTTY guard), tests/unit/cli/version-check.test.ts.
- Test approach: mock spawnSync (git ls-remote stub returning fixture refs), mock fs (read/write cache file), assert all gating conditions. No live network calls in tests.
- New-file scope: src/cli/version-check.ts and tests are new files. doctor.ts and status.ts get small additive blocks (existing-symbol mutations) — gitnexus_impact required on those two only per the new escape-hatch rule.
- Format reference: a sample line is 'specialists v3.8.0 is local; v3.9.0 published — consider /update-specialists before substantial work.' Keep terse, single line.

title: Mandatory rule: new-file escape hatch for gitnexus-required
description:
PROBLEM: The gitnexus-required mandatory rule fires 'verify blast radius checked before edits' on reviewer audits even when executor PRs add only new files (no existing symbols touched). This produces PARTIAL verdicts (88-92 score) on otherwise-clean work and creates unnecessary fix-loops.

SUCCESS: Rule allows executors to satisfy 'blast radius checked' when symbols_touched=[] (new-file-only PRs), without lying about gitnexus calls.

SCOPE: config/mandatory-rules/gitnexus-required.md (and mirror), reviewer prompt template if needed.

OBSERVED: Hit on znkgi.2 (changelog-keeper specialist creation, 6 new files, 0 symbol edits) — reviewer flagged 'no direct feed/tool-event record of gitnexus_impact'. Real but moot finding.

OPTIONS:
1. Rule-side: add 'When PR scope is exclusively new files (no existing symbols modified), explicitly note new-file-only scope and skip impact analysis.'
2. Reviewer-side: change 'verify blast radius' from 'unmet' to 'n/a' when authoritative_diff shows zero modified existing symbols.
3. Executor-side: emit a 'no_symbols_touched' meta event when applicable.

CONSTRAINTS: Don't weaken the rule for symbol-edit PRs. Don't introduce a self-attestation loophole that executors can game.

VALIDATION: Re-run reviewer against a synthetic new-file PR; verdict should be PASS without orchestrator hand-waving.

title: Wire skill-side update awareness: using-specialists-v2 + update-specialists
description:
PROBLEM: .4 covers the CLI nudge surface for humans. This bead covers the skill (LLM-side) surface for agents. Two complementary changes:

1. config/skills/using-specialists-v2/SKILL.md — currently teaches orchestration but says nothing about update awareness. Agents loading this skill should be primed to check whether their local specialists is current before starting substantial work, so they don't apply outdated patterns or miss flag changes (e.g. --user-dir → --project-dir, pi 0.70 compat, schema strict-cut).

2. config/skills/update-specialists/SKILL.md — currently a reconciliation guide for installed projects. It should additionally teach the agent how to discover the latest published sp release: query origin tags, compare to local package.json version, decide whether 'xt update specialists' is warranted, run the update.

SUCCESS:
A) using-specialists-v2/SKILL.md gets a small new section near the top — 'Update awareness on skill load' — instructing the agent to:
   - On first activation in a session, check 'git ls-remote --tags origin | tail -3' (or sp doctor's update output once .4 lands) for latest tag.
   - Compare to package.json version.
   - If behind, surface a single line in chat: 'specialists vX.Y.Z is local; vA.B.C published — consider /update-specialists before substantial work.'
   - Do NOT block, do NOT spam, do NOT auto-update.
   - Skip the check if SPECIALISTS_OFFLINE=1 or no TTY (specialist-spawned subagent context).
B) update-specialists/SKILL.md gets a 'Discover latest release' section that walks the agent through: fetching origin tags, reading CHANGELOG.md for the latest entry (once .1 lands), summarizing what changed, asking the user before running the actual reconcile flow.
C) The new sections cross-reference each other and both link to CHANGELOG.md and 'sp release publish' docs (post-.3).

SCOPE: 2 SKILL.md edits. No code. Nothing in .specialists/ runtime.

NON_GOALS:
- No new CLI command (that's .4 territory).
- No automatic updates.
- No skill-load-time hooks (skills are markdown — they instruct, they don't execute).

CONSTRAINTS:
- Must not increase the skill token cost meaningfully (target +30 lines max each).
- Must respect offline / headless contexts.
- Must work even if .1 / .3 / .4 haven't landed yet — degrade gracefully (e.g. fall back to 'git fetch && git tag --sort=-creatordate | head -1').

VALIDATION: visual review; smoke by activating using-specialists-v2 in a fresh session and asserting the agent surfaces the version check before tackling the first substantial task.
