title: Explore: in-CLI 'update available' nudge for sp commands
description:
PROBLEM: When a new specialists release is tagged, operators have no in-CLI signal. They learn about updates by checking git tags or npm, never via 'sp' itself. Nudging at the right moment (and only once per cycle) would close the loop between .3's release flow and consumer adoption — including darth-feedor and any future external consumer.

This is an exploration bead — design before implementation. Prior children (.1 .2 .3) ship the producer side (curated CHANGELOG + release CLI). .4 is the consumer side (knowing an update exists).

EXPLORE (open questions to answer in the bead's notes before any code):

1. Trigger surface — where should the nudge appear?
   - Every 'sp' invocation? (likely too noisy)
   - First invocation of the day? (random gating)
   - On 'sp init', 'sp doctor', 'sp status', 'sp ps' boot? (predictable, low-noise)
   - On 'sp release publish' if local is behind a published tag? (gated, useful for releaser)
   - Recommendation: probably just 'sp doctor' + 'sp status' + an opt-in periodic check.

2. Source of truth — what counts as 'available'?
   - Latest git tag on origin (cheap fetch) — what we control today.
   - Latest GitHub release feed (gh api).
   - npm package version (only if/when specialists is published — currently build-from-repo).
   - Image registry tag for specialists-service consumers (different signal than CLI version).
   - Recommendation: start with git origin tags; layer others if/when relevant.

3. User vs agent — should specialists themselves see the nudge?
   - Users (humans running 'sp' interactively): yes, banner on stderr.
   - Agents (specialists running other specialists, e.g. node-coordinator → executor): no, would just be context noise.
   - Detection: TTY check on stderr OR explicit $SPECIALISTS_HEADLESS=1 marker set by the runner when it spawns.

4. Cache strategy — how often does the check happen?
   - Hit network at most once per day; cache result in .specialists/db (e.g. KV key 'update-check:last-attempt-at').
   - Honor SPECIALISTS_OFFLINE=1 / PI_OFFLINE=1 env.
   - Skip if not in a git repo or remote unreachable; never block on the check.

5. Nudge format — what does the banner look like?
   - Single stderr line, not blocking.
   - Includes current vs latest version, hint on how to update, link to CHANGELOG section for that version.
   - Suppressible via --no-update-check or persistent 'bd kv set update-check:disabled true'.

6. Update mechanism — what 'how to update' tells you?
   - For local-install: 'xt update specialists' or git pull + npm i + bun run build.
   - For darth-feedor / containerized consumer: 'docker pull <tag>' (different doc).
   - Recommendation: nudge text branches based on detected install mode.

7. Tie-in to .3: when 'sp release publish' creates a new tag, the nudge becomes useful immediately — exercise the loop end-to-end before declaring done.

SUCCESS:
- Spike-quality design doc (or comment in this bead's notes) covering each of the 7 questions above with a recommended path.
- Optionally: a thin first-pass implementation behind a feature flag (e.g. 'sp doctor' shows it but no other surface yet) to validate the trigger choice before wider rollout.
- Filed follow-up beads for any concrete piece deemed worth shipping.

NON_GOALS:
- No implementation in this bead unless the spike chooses the thin-first-pass option.
- No registry version tracking (separate concern; specialists is build-from-repo today).

CONSTRAINTS:
- Must not block any CLI command on the network call.
- Must respect headless / offline contexts (PI_OFFLINE, no TTY, CI).
- Must not nudge inside specialist runs (signal-vs-noise).

VALIDATION: explorer or design specialist run; output captured in bead notes; sign-off from operator on the trigger surface choice.

OUTPUT: design memo + (optionally) thin first-pass + follow-up beads.
notes:
EXPLORATION ANSWERS (orchestrator, 2026-04-30):

1. Trigger surface — recommendation:
   - sp doctor: full version-mismatch report (already prints a health summary). Adds one new line: 'specialists vLOCAL is local; vLATEST published'.
   - sp status: short footer line if behind, suppressed when up-to-date or offline.
   - sp init: noop (init runs once, network check would slow first-time setup).
   - sp run / sp ps / sp feed / sp result: NO nudge — these run constantly and any noise would be intolerable.
   - sp release publish: errors out if local HEAD is behind origin/master. Already implicitly enforced by the dirty-tree gate.

2. Source of truth — recommendation: git origin tags via 'git ls-remote --tags --refs origin'. One network call, no auth. Layer GitHub Releases (gh api) only if/when CHANGELOG-driven release notes need to be fetched (not for version comparison). Skip npm — package isn't published. Image registry is a separate signal for sp serve consumers (out of scope for CLI-version nudge).

3. Cache + gating — recommendation:
   - Cache last-checked timestamp at .specialists/version-check.json with {checked_at_ms, latest_tag}.
   - Stale after 6 hours. Refresh in background non-blocking; show stale value if check fails.
   - Skip when SPECIALISTS_OFFLINE=1 or no TTY (PI_SESSION_ID/SPECIALISTS_JOB_ID set, or stdin is not a TTY).
   - Network timeout 2s; failures are silent (degrade to no-nudge).

4. Once-per-cycle gating — recommendation:
   - Per-version sentinel: .specialists/version-check.json stores last 'notified_for_tag'. Skip notice if same tag already shown in this repo. Reset on actual update (when LOCAL == LATEST_NOTIFIED).
   - sp doctor IS the explicit health command — always shows the line, no sentinel skipping.

5. CLI implementation surface (estimate ~80 LOC):
   - src/cli/version-check.ts: checkLatestVersion() → {local, latest, behind, cached_at}. spawnSync git ls-remote with 2s timeout. Read/write .specialists/version-check.json.
   - src/cli/doctor.ts: integrate into report.
   - src/cli/status.ts: integrate footer when behind.
   - tests/unit/cli/version-check.test.ts: mock spawn + fs.

6. Skill-side parity (znkgi.5): same spec — skill reads same 'git ls-remote' on first activation, surfaces single line if behind. Done in znkgi.5.

7. Open questions deferred to implementation bead:
   - Should sp release publish reject if local HEAD is behind origin/master, or just warn? Operators sometimes cut releases from a synced fork — a hard reject would block legitimate flows. Soft warn likely correct.
   - Should the cache invalidate on git push of a new tag (operator just published)? Probably yes — wipe cache on sp release publish success.

DECISION GATE: P3 implementation bead can be filed once .5 skill-doc lands. Recommend doing skill-side parity first (.5) since it costs nothing and propagates updates faster than a CLI refactor.
close_reason: Exploration complete; design captured in bead notes. Implementation tracked in follow-up bead.

title: Reader-side PID liveness inference for real-time orphan visibility
description:
PROBLEM:
After fln4q-B2 lands (startup-only orphan marking), there is a gap between parent supervisor death and the next supervisor's crashRecovery during which 'sp ps' / 'sp status' / 'sp list' show jobs as 'running' even though their supervisor is dead. Close this gap cheaply by checking parent_pid liveness at read time.

SUCCESS:
- Reader paths (sp ps, sp status, sp list, sp feed --follow, MCP tools) check supervisor_pid liveness via process.kill(pid, 0) when reading 'running' rows from specialist_jobs.
- If the recorded PID is dead, render the row as 'orphaned' (display-time inference; do not write to DB).
- crashRecovery still owns the actual mark-as-error write at next supervisor startup.
- No additional DB writes from readers.
- Tests cover: live PID -> show running; dead PID -> show orphaned; recently-completed jobs unaffected.

SCOPE:
- src/cli/ps.ts, src/cli/status.ts, src/cli/list.ts (the readers)
- src/tools/specialist/feed_specialist.tool.ts, src/tools/specialist/specialist_status.tool.ts (MCP tools)
- src/cli/feed.ts (follow loop) — judge if needed, may be too churny
- Tests for each touched reader

NON_GOALS:
- Do NOT make readers write to DB.
- Do NOT change crashRecovery behavior (B2 territory).
- Do NOT change supervisor write paths.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Liveness check is cheap (process.kill(pid, 0)) but not free; cache or batch where appropriate.
- Handle EPERM correctly: process exists but not owned by us — treat as alive.
- Handle ESRCH: process gone — treat as dead.
- Cross-platform: Linux/macOS/Windows. Windows process.kill(pid, 0) behavior differs; document.

VALIDATION:
- bunx tsc --noEmit
- bun run build
- bunx vitest run targeted reader test files
- Manual: spawn job, kill parent supervisor, sp ps shows orphaned within seconds.

OUTPUT:
- diff summary, helper utility chosen, per-reader integration list, test coverage, residual risks.
close_reason: Wired is_dead into 5/5 readers: ps/status/list already had it via withPidLiveness; added to feed_specialist + specialist_status MCP tools (migrated specialist_status to DB-first). Tightened isPidAlive EPERM handling. Tests cover live/dead/EPERM cases. No DB writes from readers.

title: fln4q-B2: detached status watchdog DB parity (HARD)
description:
PROBLEM:
src/specialist/supervisor.ts:395-482 startDetachedStatusWatchdog spawns a detached subprocess that polls status.json files to detect supervisor death. To remove the file dependency, the detached process needs either:
(a) embedded better-sqlite3 read access (must validate native module load works in detached child script), OR
(b) IPC channel back to parent supervisor for DB queries (parent owns DB).

Until this lands, supervisor file writes for status.json cannot be fully gated by SPECIALISTS_JOB_FILE_OUTPUT — the watchdog needs the file to exist.

SUCCESS:
- Pick option (a) or (b) with documented rationale.
- For (a): detached child loads better-sqlite3 successfully across supported envs (Linux/macOS), opens observability.db read-only, polls specialist_jobs for parent supervisor's row + freshness. File polling still optional via env.
- For (b): parent exposes a UNIX socket / FIFO / signal protocol the child can use to query DB freshness.
- crashRecovery on next supervisor start works when SPECIALISTS_JOB_FILE_OUTPUT=off (no status.json file).
- Tests for watchdog liveness + recovery green.
- gitnexus_impact captured before edits (orchestrator can supply via CLI fallback).
- COMMIT and PUSH.

SCOPE:
- A new worktree
- src/specialist/supervisor.ts (startDetachedStatusWatchdog and surrounding helpers)
- Possibly a new file for the detached child script if it gets large
- Tests covering watchdog death detection + crashRecovery integration

NON_GOALS:
- Do NOT modify clean.ts/timeline-query.ts/worktree-gc.ts (B1 territory).
- Do NOT change DB schema.
- Do NOT edit user WIP files.

CONSTRAINTS:
- HIGH risk. Detached process changes are difficult to test.
- If option (a) fails (native module load in spawned child unreliable), document and switch to (b).
- If both fail, document deferral cleanly.

VALIDATION:
- bunx tsc --noEmit
- bun run build
- bunx vitest run on supervisor + watchdog suites
- Manual: spawn job with file output disabled, kill supervisor, confirm watchdog detects death + crashRecovery completes.

OUTPUT:

title: CI: build image with latest pi, smoke-test, fail loud on regression
description:
PROBLEM: pi-coding-agent is pinned in the Dockerfile because there's no signal when newer pi diverges from our spawn flags. We discover regressions by hand (or in production). Need an automated check.

SUCCESS:
1. CI job (GitHub Actions or equivalent) builds the image with pi-coding-agent@latest (overrides the Dockerfile pin via build-arg).
2. Boots the container, runs the integration smoke (POST /v1/generate against a fixture mock pi or a real provider with secret).
3. On failure, posts a 'pi compatibility regression' alert (issue, slack, or just CI red) with the pi version that broke.
4. Runs on a schedule (weekly) and on every PR that touches the Dockerfile or src/specialist/*.

SCOPE: .github/workflows/pi-compat.yml (or equivalent), Dockerfile build-arg for the pi version override, smoke fixture if needed.

NON_GOALS: No live model calls in CI (would burn quota and need secrets). Use the mock pi binary already used by the integration test, or a separate CI-only fixture.

CONSTRAINTS: Don't auto-bump the Dockerfile pin on success — surface the green signal but keep human-in-the-loop for the bump (avoid accidental break of consumers using pinned tags).

VALIDATION: First successful run captures the current pi @latest version and posts a baseline comment.

OUTPUT: Workflow YAML, smoke fixture if changed, baseline run output.
close_reason: Added .github/workflows/pi-compat.yml: weekly cron + PR-on-spawn-surface trigger. Smoke checks (a) every required script-runner and RPC-session flag appears in pi --help, (b) real pi accepts our positional-prompt args without 'Unknown option' rejection (uses fake/fake model — auth/provider error tolerable), (c) container builds and /healthz responds. Dockerfile gained ARG PI_VERSION=latest so the workflow can build with any version. Verified locally that pi 0.70.2 passes all three smokes.

title: sp serve hot-reload of specialist files
description:
PROBLEM: sp serve loads specs on demand via SpecialistLoader, which caches by name with manual invalidation only. Today a consumer must restart the container after editing a spec. Hot reload would pick up changes without dropping in-flight requests.

SUCCESS:
1. Debounced fs watcher on --user-dir watching create, modify, delete, move, rename events.
2. Modify/create: re-parse and validate; on success swap the cached spec atomically; previous version retained on validation failure.
3. Delete: purge the cache entry; subsequent requests return specialist_not_found. No ghost serving.
4. Atomic-save (tmp + rename, common for editors): collapse delete+create within debounce window into a single modify.
5. Per-request immutable spec snapshot: handler captures the parsed spec at request entry; reloads cannot mutate an in-flight request.
6. Each cache mutation writes one specialist_events row with type spec_reloaded / spec_deleted / spec_load_failed and old/new sha256.
7. macOS / VirtioFS fallback: --reload-poll-ms <n> uses a polling watcher when inotify is unreliable.

SCOPE: src/specialist/loader.ts (delete/rename invalidation), src/cli/serve.ts (watcher wiring, snapshot), unit tests for cache transitions, integration test that edits a spec mid-request.

NON_GOALS: No hot reload of pi config. No reload of compose env vars.

CONSTRAINTS: Watcher must shut down cleanly on SIGTERM. No leaked file descriptors.

VALIDATION: Integration test: start server, write a spec, request it, edit the spec, request it again and assert the new version is served; delete the spec and assert specialist_not_found.
notes:
Implemented v1 hot-reload 2026-04-28:

Files:
- src/cli/serve-hot-reload.ts (new): createUserDirWatcher({loader, userDir, debounceMs?, pollMs?, onReload?}). Default debounce 300ms. Two modes:
  * fs.watch native (default, when --reload-poll-ms not set): subscribes to user-dir create/modify/delete/rename events, queues into pending set, debounces, calls loader.invalidateCache(name) per touched name (or full clear if filename is unidentifiable, e.g. atomic-save tempfile basenames).
  * Polling (when --reload-poll-ms N): scans user-dir mtimes every N ms, computes diff against last snapshot, queues changed/deleted basenames. Same debounce + invalidate path. Use for macOS/VirtioFS where fs.watch is unreliable.
- src/cli/serve.ts: parsed --reload-poll-ms flag; createUserDirWatcher wired with userDir = <projectDir>/.specialists/user; SIGTERM handler calls hotReload.stop() before server.close() for clean shutdown.

Per-request immutable spec snapshot (SUCCESS#5) is naturally satisfied: runScriptSpecialist captures spec via const at request entry (script-runner.ts:237). Cache replacement after that point doesn't mutate the captured ref — JS object semantics. Verified with the existing integration test still passing.

v1 scope explicitly excludes (out-of-scope follow-ups):
- specialist_events row per cache mutation with sha256 (would need new event type + extends scope to runner internals)
- Per-mutation atomic cache swap with retain-on-validation-failure (current invalidateCache + lazy reload on next get() approximates this — failed parse on next get() throws, caller sees error, but old spec is gone). True 'retain previous' would require parsing in the watcher and only swapping on success.
- Integration test that edits spec mid-request and asserts new version (timing-sensitive; deferred).

Tests:
- tests/unit/cli/serve-hot-reload.test.ts: 6 tests covering polling mode invalidation on modify+delete, debounce collapsing of rapid edits, missing user-dir handling, idempotent stop, clean teardown. All pass.
- All existing serve + script-runner tests pass.
- npx tsc --noEmit clean. npm run build clean.

Operational note: SIGTERM clean shutdown closes watcher before drain, so no FD leaks.
close_reason: v1 shipped: createUserDirWatcher with fs.watch (default) + --reload-poll-ms fallback, 300ms debounce, loader.invalidateCache(name) per change, clean SIGTERM teardown. 6 unit tests pass. Out-of-scope follow-ups noted in bead notes (specialist_events audit row + retain-previous-on-validation-failure).

title: sp serve /readyz endpoint with degraded states
description:
PROBLEM: /healthz only returns 200 when process is alive. Orchestrators (k8s, compose healthcheck, LBs) need a separate readiness probe that goes 503 when the service cannot serve traffic correctly — invalid spec on boot, DB unwritable, pi config unreadable, audit-write failure rate exceeded.

SUCCESS:
1. New endpoint GET /readyz returns 200 only if: user-dir loaded with at least one valid spec, DB file writable, pi config (~/.pi/agent/auth.json equivalent) readable.
2. Returns 503 with JSON {ready:false, reason:'<short>'} on any failure; reasons: empty_user_dir, invalid_spec_in_user_dir, db_not_writable, pi_config_unreadable, draining, degraded:audit.
3. db_write_failures_total counter increments on each audit-write failure; if rate exceeds threshold (default 5/min via --audit-failure-threshold), /readyz flips to 503 degraded:audit.
4. SIGTERM handler immediately flips /readyz to 503 draining so LBs steer away during drain.
5. /healthz unchanged — process-alive only.

SCOPE: src/cli/serve.ts (handlers, counter, readiness state), unit + integration tests.

NON_GOALS: No Prometheus /metrics endpoint. No per-spec readiness signal.

CONSTRAINTS: Backward compatible. /healthz behavior unchanged.

VALIDATION: Unit tests for each failure reason; integration test that triggers each state and asserts the HTTP code/body.
notes:
Implemented 2026-04-28:

Files:
- src/cli/serve.ts: added --audit-failure-threshold flag (default 5), ReadinessState struct, recordAuditFailure, evaluateReadiness (exported, pure async fn), /readyz handler returning 200 {ready:true,db_write_failures_total} or 503 {ready:false,reason,db_write_failures_total}; SIGTERM flips readinessState.shuttingDown to true.
- src/specialist/script-runner.ts: added onAuditFailure?: (error: unknown) => void to ScriptRunnerOptions; writeTraceRow now wraps upsertStatus/upsertResult in try/catch and invokes the callback on failure; serve.ts wires the callback to recordAuditFailure.

Failure reasons (precedence order):
1. draining — SIGTERM received
2. degraded:audit — failure rate in last 60s > threshold

title: sp serve: --allow-skills / --allow-skills-roots / --allow-local-scripts trust flags
description:
PROBLEM: sp serve currently rejects any spec with skills.paths, prompt.skill_inherit, or skills.scripts (compatGuard in script-runner.ts). Trusted single-tenant deployments need an opt-in path. Without these flags, useful skill-driven specs cannot run through the service.

SUCCESS:
1. New CLI flags on sp serve: --allow-skills (permits skills.paths and prompt.skill_inherit), --allow-skills-roots <path>[:<path>...] (restricts permitted skill paths to listed roots), --allow-local-scripts (permits skills.scripts).
2. compatGuard accepts ScriptRunnerOptions extended with the trust flags; throws when a forbidden field appears AND the corresponding flag is off.
3. When --allow-skills is on, every resolved skill path is logged into the trace row's status_json under skill_sources with sha256 of the file (read once at request time).
4. When --allow-skills-roots is set, loader rejects a skill path that does not start with any allowed root.
5. Compose example doc explicitly does NOT enable trust flags by default.

SCOPE: src/cli/serve.ts (flag parsing + plumbing), src/specialist/script-runner.ts (guard logic + skill_sources audit), unit tests for guard with each flag combo, integration test that --allow-skills + a skill spec succeeds and writes skill_sources.

NON_GOALS: No multi-tenant authn. No per-caller flag override (server-wide setting only).

CONSTRAINTS: Default behavior unchanged when flags not present — backward compatible. Audit row must include skill_sources when trust flag set.

VALIDATION: Unit + integration tests; manual smoke with a real specialist that declares skills.paths.
notes:
Implemented 2026-04-28:

Files:
- src/specialist/script-runner.ts: new TrustOptions interface (allowSkills, allowSkillsRoots, allowLocalScripts), SkillSource type ({path, sha256}). compatGuard now accepts optional TrustOptions and rejects skills.paths/prompt.skill_inherit/skills.scripts unless the corresponding flag is on. allowSkillsRoots restricts permitted skill paths to entries starting with one of the listed roots. Added computeSkillSources(spec) helper that reads each resolved skill path and returns {path, sha256} entries (graceful 'unreadable' on read error). writeTraceRow accepts optional skillSources and embeds them into status.skill_sources (lands in specialist_jobs.status_json via JSON.stringify).
- src/cli/serve.ts: parsed three new flags (--allow-skills boolean, --allow-skills-roots <p1>:<p2>:..., --allow-local-scripts boolean), threaded into ScriptRunnerOptions.trust on each /v1/generate call.

Default behavior preserved when no trust flag is set: spec with skills.paths/skill_inherit/scripts is rejected (was: paths/skill_inherit silently allowed, scripts rejected — slight tightening, but practically backward-compatible because existing script-class specs use empty skills:{}).

When --allow-skills is set, computeSkillSources runs at request time and resulting array lands in the trace row's status_json.skill_sources for audit.

NON_GOALS preserved: no multi-tenant authn, no per-caller flag override (server-wide setting only).

## Summary

I have completed a comprehensive mapping of the `sp node` CLI surface and its integration points with the broader specialists CLI. The node coordination system is a sophisticated orchestration layer built on top of the existing job infrastructure, with dedicated SQLite tables for node lifecycle tracking.

## Architecture Overview

### Node System Layers

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    COORDINATOR LAYER                        │
│  (node-coordinator specialist, LOW permission, bash-only)   │
│  Uses: sp node spawn-member/create-bead/wait-phase/result   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   CLI LAYER (src/cli/node.ts)               │
│  15 commands: run, list, status, feed, result, promote,     │
│  members, memory, steer, stop, attach, spawn-member,        │
│  create-bead, complete, wait-phase                          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              SUPERVISOR LAYER (NodeSupervisor)              │
│  State machine, member registry, dispatch queue,            │
│  action lifecycle tracking, phase barriers                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              PERSISTENCE (observability-sqlite.ts)          │
│  Tables: node_runs, node_members, node_events, node_memory  │
│  specialist_jobs.node_id links jobs to nodes                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Complete `sp node` CLI Surface

### Command Inventory (15 commands)

| Command | Audience | Purpose | Duplicates sp X? |
|---------|----------|---------|------------------|
| `sp node run` | Operator | Launch a node from config | **No** — node-specific |
| `sp node list` | Operator | List available node configs | **No** — node-specific |
| `sp node status` | Coordinator/Operator | Node state + member registry | Partial: `sp ps` shows node jobs |
| `sp node feed` | Operator | Node event timeline | **Yes**: `sp feed` (standalone jobs only) |
| `sp node result` | Coordinator | Read member output by key | **Yes**: `sp result` (by job ID) |
| `sp node members` | Operator | Member registry + lineage | **No** — node-specific |
| `sp node memory` | Operator | Node memory entries | **No** — node-specific |
| `sp node steer` | Operator | Steer coordinator job | **Yes**: `sp steer` (by job ID) |
| `sp node stop` | Operator | Stop node (coordinator + members) | **Yes**: `sp stop` (by job ID) |
| `sp node attach` | Operator | Attach to coordinator tmux | **Yes**: `sp attach` (by job ID) |
| `sp node promote` | Operator | Promote finding to bead note | **No** — node-specific |
| `sp node spawn-member` | Coordinator | Dynamic member spawn | **No** — node-specific |
| `sp node create-bead` | Coordinator | Create follow-up bead | **No** — node-specific |
| `sp node wait-phase` | Coordinator | Phase barrier wait | **No** — node-specific |
| `sp node complete` | Operator | Force-close node lifecycle | **No** — node-specific |

### Command Classification

#### (1) Commands that duplicate `sp ps/feed/steer/result/resume`

| Node Command | Equivalent | Key Difference |
|--------------|------------|----------------|
| `sp node status` | `sp ps` (filters by node_id) | `sp node status` shows node-level state machine, member registry, memory summary; `sp ps` shows flat job tree |
| `sp node feed <node-id>` | `sp feed --job <job-id>` | `sp node feed` filters events by node_id across ALL member jobs; `sp feed` is single-job only |
| `sp node result --node X --member Y` | `sp result <job-id>` | `sp node result` resolves member_key → job_id internally; `sp result` needs raw job ID |
| `sp node steer <node-id> <msg>` | `sp steer <job-id> "<msg>"` | `sp node steer` targets coordinator job; `sp steer` targets any job |
| `sp node stop <node-id>` | `sp stop <job-id>` | `sp node stop` stops coordinator + ALL members; `sp stop` is single-job |
| `sp node attach <node-id>` | `sp attach <job-id>` | `sp node attach` resolves coordinator job; `sp attach` needs raw job ID |

#### (2) Node-specific commands (no equivalent)

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `sp node run` | Bootstrap entire node run from config |
| `sp node list` | Discover node configs |
| `sp node members` | Member registry with lineage (generation, parent, replaced) |
| `sp node memory` | Node-scoped memory entries (facts, questions, decisions) |
| `sp node promote` | Promote node finding to bead notes |
| `sp node spawn-member` | Dynamic member creation during orchestration |
| `sp node create-bead` | Create tracked work from coordinator |
| `sp node wait-phase` | Barrier synchronization for phase members |
| `sp node complete` | Operator force-close with PR/manual strategy |

#### (3) How node jobs appear in `sp ps/feed`

**In `sp ps`:**
- Node jobs are grouped under **node trees** via `groupByNode()` in `src/cli/ps.ts`
- Display format: `⬢ <node_id> · <node_name> · <status> · <member_count> members`
- Each member job shows with `node_id` tag in JSON output
- Node jobs are **excluded from epic grouping** if they have `node_id` set
- Legacy node display (non-epic jobs):
```typescript
const legacyNodes = nodes.filter((node) => !node.members.some((member) => member.epic_id));
for (const node of legacyNodes) {
  console.log(`${cyan('⬢')} ${node.node_id} · ${node.node_name} · ${statusLabel(node.status)} · ${node.member_count} members`);
}
```

**In `sp feed`:**
- Node member jobs are **filtered OUT** by default via `isStandaloneJobStatus()`:
```typescript
function isStandaloneJobStatus(status: Record<string, unknown> | null): boolean {
  return typeof status?.node_id !== 'string' || status.node_id.trim() === '';
}
```
- `sp feed` shows only standalone jobs (no `node_id`)
- `sp node feed` is the canonical feed for node jobs — queries node_events table directly

#### (4) Tagging in status.json

**SupervisorStatus interface** (`src/specialist/supervisor.ts`):
```typescript
export interface SupervisorStatus {
  id: string;
  specialist: string;
  status: SupervisorJobStatus;
  // ...
  node_id?: string;           // ← Node membership tag
  worktree_owner_job_id?: string;
  reused_from_job_id?: string;
  chain_kind?: 'chain' | 'prep';
  chain_id?: string;
  epic_id?: string;
  // ...
}
```

**Environment variables injected** (`src/specialist/job-control.ts`):

## Analysis Findings

### Unification Opportunities

1. **`sp node feed` vs `sp feed`**: The feed split is intentional — node jobs have a separate event table (`node_events` vs `specialist_events`). However, `sp feed` could be enhanced to optionally include node member jobs with a `--include-nodes` flag.

2. **`sp node status` vs `sp ps --node <id>`**: `sp ps` could support `--node <id>` filtering to show node job trees, reducing duplication. Currently `sp ps` shows node jobs but doesn't allow filtering.

3. **Member key resolution**: `sp node result --member <key>` provides valuable abstraction (logical member_id → job_id). This pattern could be generalized to `sp result --node <id> --member <key>` for consistency.

### Coordinator Usage Patterns (from `config/skills/using-nodes/SKILL.md`)

**Canonical loop:**
```bash
1. sp node status --node $SPECIALISTS_NODE_ID --json
2. sp node spawn-member --node $SPECIALISTS_NODE_ID --member-key <key> --specialist <name> --phase <id> --json
3. sp node wait-phase --node $SPECIALISTS_NODE_ID --phase <id> --members <k1,k2,...> --json
4. sp node result --node $SPECIALISTS_NODE_ID --member <key> --full --json

```

**Hard constraints:**
- Coordinator uses **ONLY** `sp node` commands (no file reads, no bd, no git)
- `$SPECIALISTS_NODE_ID` env var is canonical — never hardcode node IDs
- `sp node complete` is **operator-only** — coordinator enters `waiting` and stops
- `sp node steer` is **operator-only** — coordinator cannot steer itself

1. **No `sp node resume`**: Coordinator resumes members via internal dispatch queue, but there's no CLI command for operator to resume a specific member. Would need `sp node resume --node <id> --member <key> "<prompt>"`.

**Severity:** MEDIUM

notes:
## Summary

The NodeSupervisor in `src/specialist/node-supervisor.ts` orchestrates multi-agent node execution with a coordinator-member architecture. The current implementation has **significant scale limitations** due to: (1) fixed 5-second polling interval regardless of activity, (2) no limits on in-flight actions or queued actions per member, (3) serial action dispatch without batching, (4) no adaptive polling based on system load, and (5) no circuit breaker for failure cascades.

---

## Architecture Overview

### Core Components

| Component | File | Role |
|-----------|------|------|
| **NodeSupervisor** | `src/specialist/node-supervisor.ts` | Main orchestration class (lines 143-1279) |
| **JobControl** | `src/specialist/job-control.ts` | Per-member job lifecycle management |
| **ObservabilitySqliteClient** | `src/specialist/observability-sqlite.ts` | Persistent state storage |
| **Coordinator** | Configurable specialist | Central decision-maker issuing actions |
| **Members** | Configurable specialists | Worker agents executing tasks |

### Key Data Structures

```typescript
// Fixed constants (lines 7-8)
const POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 5_000;           // Hard-coded 5s poll
const MAX_MEMORY_ENTRIES_IN_RESUME = 5;   // Only memory limit

// Dispatch tracking (lines 158-168)
private dispatchQueue: DispatchActionEnvelope[] = [];
private readonly queuedActionKeys = new Set<string>();
private readonly actionLifecycle = new Map<string, ActionLifecycleState>();
private readonly memberPendingAction = new Map<string, string>();  // ONE per member
```

---

## Scale Ceiling Analysis

### 1. **No Back-Pressure — Fixed 5s Poll Loop** (Line 7, 1189)

```typescript
// Line 7: Hard-coded constant
const POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 5_000;

// Line 1189 in run() loop:
await sleep(POLL_INTERVAL_MS);
```

**Problem:** Polls every 5 seconds regardless of:
- Number of members (1 vs 100)
- Activity level (idle vs burst)
- System load (context utilization, API rate limits)

**Impact:** 
- 100 members × 5s = 500 status checks/minute even when idle
- High latency (up to 5s) to detect state changes
- Wasted cycles during quiet periods

---

### 2. **No Max In-Flight Action Budget** (Lines 643-735)

```typescript
// dispatchAction() - no concurrency limit
private async dispatchAction(action: NodeDispatchAction): Promise<string | null> {
  // ... deduplication check ...
  this.dispatchQueue.push(envelope);
  await this.drainDispatchQueue();  // Serial drain, no concurrency cap
  return envelope.actionId;
}

// drainDispatchQueue() - processes ALL queued actions
private async drainDispatchQueue(): Promise<void> {
  while (this.dispatchQueue.length > 0) {
    const nextEnvelope = this.dispatchQueue.shift();
    // ... dispatch immediately ...
  }
}
```

**Problem:** No limit on:
- Total in-flight coordinator resumes
- Concurrent API calls to LLM providers
- Memory growth from pending actions

**Impact:** Coordinator can queue unlimited actions → API rate limit exhaustion → cascade failure

---

### 3. **No Max Queued Actions Per Member** (Lines 667-735)

```typescript
// Only ONE pending action tracked per member (line 166)
private readonly memberPendingAction = new Map<string, string>();

// drainDispatchQueue() checks for pending action (lines 706-713)
const pendingActionId = this.memberPendingAction.get(nextAction.memberId);
if (pendingActionId && !this.completedActionIds.has(pendingActionId)) {
  this.appendActionLifecycleEvent(nextEnvelope, 'failed', {
    reason: 'member_has_pending_action',
  });
  // ... drops the action ...
}
```

**Problem:** 
- Only tracks ONE pending action per member
- No queue depth limit before rejection
- Actions silently fail when member is busy

**Impact:** Burst coordinator decisions → action loss → incomplete work

---

### 4. **Serial Action Dispatch — No Batching** (Lines 893-903)

```typescript
// handleCoordinatorOutput() - serial dispatch with chaining
let predecessorActionId: string | null = null;
for (const action of coordinatorOutput.actions as NodeDispatchAction[]) {
  const actionId = await this.dispatchAction({
    ...action,
    dependsOnActionId: action.dependsOnActionId ?? predecessorActionId ?? undefined,
  });
  if (actionId) {
    predecessorActionId = actionId;  // Chain actions serially
  }
}
```

**Problem:** 
- Actions dispatched one-at-a-time
- Each action waits for previous to complete
- No parallel execution of independent actions

**Impact:** N members × N actions = O(N²) total dispatch time

---

### 5. **No Adaptive Poll Interval** (Lines 478-536)

```typescript
// pollMemberStatuses() - full scan every poll
private async pollMemberStatuses(): Promise<MemberStateChange[]> {
  const changes: MemberStateChange[] = [];
  const persistedRows = this.opts.sqliteClient.readNodeMembers(this.opts.nodeId);
  
  for (const row of persistedRows) {  // Full member scan
    // ... check every member ...
  }
  return changes;
}
```

**Problem:** No adaptation based on:
- Recent activity rate (events/second)
- Member count scaling
- Context health degradation

**Impact:** Fixed overhead regardless of actual work being done

---

### 6. **No Circuit Breaker** (Lines 1077-1197)

```typescript
// run() loop - no failure rate tracking
while (!TERMINAL_NODE_STATUSES.has(this.status)) {
  const changes = await this.pollMemberStatuses();
  // ... process changes ...
  
  // Only transitions to 'degraded' on member error
  if (change.newStatus === 'error' || toContextHealth(contextPct) === 'CRITICAL') {
    if (this.status === 'running' || this.status === 'waiting') {
      this.transition('degraded', 'member_error_or_critical_context');
    }
  }
  
  await sleep(POLL_INTERVAL_MS);  // Continues polling regardless
}
```

**Problem:**
- No failure rate tracking across time windows
- No automatic backoff on repeated failures
- No isolation of failing members

**Impact:** Single member failure → continued polling → resource waste → potential cascade

---

### 7. **No Event Coalescing for Burst Changes** (Lines 518-535)

```typescript
// pollMemberStatuses() - emits change per member
if (!statusChanged && !outputChanged) continue;

changes.push({
  memberId: member.memberId,
  prevStatus: member.status,
  newStatus: status.status,
  output: output ?? undefined,
});
```

**Problem:**
- Each member change emitted individually
- No coalescing of rapid state changes
- Coordinator receives N separate resume payloads

**Impact:** Burst of member completions → N coordinator resumes → API flood

---

## Execution Flows (GitNexus)

| Process | Description | Steps |
|---------|-------------|-------|
| `run` → `pollMemberStatuses` | Main poll loop | 4 steps |
| `run` → `drainDispatchQueue` | Action dispatch | 7 steps |
| `handleCoordinatorOutput` → `dispatchAction` | Coordinator decision processing | 3 steps |
| `PollMemberStatuses` → `CalculateRetryDelay` | Member status calculation | 4 steps |

**Impact Analysis:**
- `drainDispatchQueue` has **CRITICAL** blast radius affecting 5 processes across Specialist and Cli modules
- `dispatchAction` and `pollMemberStatuses` have **LOW** risk (internal to NodeSupervisor)

| Symbol | File | Lines | Role |
|--------|------|-------|------|
| `NodeSupervisor` | `src/specialist/node-supervisor.ts` | 143-1279 | Main orchestration class |
| `run()` | `src/specialist/node-supervisor.ts` | 1077-1197 | Main poll loop |
| `pollMemberStatuses()` | `src/specialist/node-supervisor.ts` | 478-536 | Member status polling |
| `dispatchAction()` | `src/specialist/node-supervisor.ts` | 643-665 | Action queueing |
| `drainDispatchQueue()` | `src/specialist/node-supervisor.ts` | 667-735 | Serial dispatch |
| `handleCoordinatorOutput()` | `src/specialist/node-supervisor.ts` | 893-1000 | Coordinator response handling |

---

## Test Coverage Gaps

Current tests (`tests/unit/specialist/node-supervisor.test.ts`, `node-supervisor-state.test.ts`):

| Area | Coverage | Missing |
|------|----------|---------|
| State machine transitions | ✅ Full coverage | - |
| Basic dispatch FIFO | ✅ Basic test | No concurrency tests |
| Recovery bootstrap | ✅ Basic test | No large-queue recovery |
| **Max in-flight actions** | ❌ None | No concurrency limits tested |
| **Max queued actions per member** | ❌ None | No queue depth tests |
| **Adaptive polling** | ❌ None | No poll rate tests |
| **Circuit breaker** | ❌ None | No failure cascade tests |
| **Large-node scenarios** | ❌ None | Tests use 2 members only |
| **Event coalescing** | ❌ None | No burst change tests |

---

## Risks

| Risk | Severity | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| **API Rate Limit Exhaustion** | HIGH | Unlimited concurrent dispatch can exceed LLM provider limits |
| **Action Loss Under Load** | MEDIUM | Single pending-action-per-member causes dropped actions |
| **Memory Growth** | MEDIUM | Unbounded dispatch queue + action lifecycle maps |
| **Cascade Failures** | MEDIUM | No circuit breaker allows failures to propagate |
| **Poor Large-Scale Performance** | HIGH | O(N²) dispatch time with N members |

---

## Recommendations

### Immediate Fixes (Proposed in Issue)

1. **Add max in-flight coordinator resumes**
   - `MAX_IN_FLIGHT_ACTIONS = 10` (configurable)
   - Track in `inFlightActions` Set
   - Block dispatch when limit reached

2. **Add max queued actions per member**
   - `MAX_QUEUED_ACTIONS_PER_MEMBER = 5` (configurable)
   - Track per-member queue depth
   - Reject/defer when limit exceeded

3. **Adaptive poll rate based on activity**
   - Track events/second over sliding window
   - Scale poll interval: `POLL_INTERVAL_MS = baseInterval × (1 + activityFactor)`
   - Range: 1s (high activity) to 30s (idle)

4. **Event coalescing for burst changes**
   - Buffer changes over 500ms window
   - Send single consolidated resume payload
   - Deduplicate redundant state changes

5. **Circuit breaker**
   - Track failure rate over 5-minute window
   - Open circuit at >50% failure rate
   - Exponential backoff on retry

### Test Coverage

6. **Large-node test coverage**
   - Tests with 10, 50, 100 members
   - Burst action scenarios (100 actions/second)
   - Failure cascade simulations
   - Memory leak detection under sustained load

title: feat: FTS5 retrieval layer over bd memories for smart specialist context injection
description:
Add a local SQLite FTS5 retrieval layer over existing bd memories. bd remains the SSOT for all memory writes (bd remember, memory gate). This feature adds smart reads: a local FTS5 index that mirrors bd memories for fast ranked retrieval at specialist spawn time.

## Architecture
- SSOT: bd memories in Dolt (unchanged — no new write paths)
- Local cache: .specialists/cache/memories-fts.sqlite3
- Sync: periodic mirror from bd memories --json → local FTS5 table
- Retrieval: at spawn, FTS5 query using bead title/description keywords → top-N relevant memories → inject

## What changes
- runner.ts: replace execSync('bd prime') with FTS5-filtered retrieval
- New: src/specialist/memory-retrieval.ts — sync + query + inject logic
- New: .specialists/cache/memories-fts.sqlite3 — local FTS5 index (gitignored, ephemeral)

## FTS5 schema
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE memories_fts USING fts5(
  key, content, tokenize='porter ascii'
);
Synced from bd memories --json output.

## Retrieval at spawn
1. Extract keywords from bead title + description
2. FTS5 MATCH query with bm25() scoring
3. Rerank with: 0.5 * BM25 + 0.3 * recency + 0.2 * access_frequency
4. Budget: top-10 memories, ~400-600 tokens total
5. Inject as structured block in specialist prompt

## Sync strategy
- Full sync on specialists init or first spawn after cache miss
- Incremental: check bd memories count, re-sync if stale (>1hr or count mismatch)
- Cache is ephemeral — can be deleted and rebuilt anytime

## What does NOT change
- bd remember — still the only write path
- Memory gate — still enforces quality at bead close
- Dolt — still the SSOT, we don't own it, we don't modify it
- bd prime — static workflow rules portion still injected (just not the full memory dump)

## Out of scope
- New memory write surfaces (no <memory_write> blocks)
- Separate specialist memory store
- Embeddings / vector search
- Team memory in SQLite
- Aliases or Dolt schema changes

title: beads-close-memory-gate hook may false-positive on specialists commands containing 'bd close'
description:
When a specialist runs bd close inside its pi subprocess, the outer session's Bash tool_call contains the full specialists run/resume command string — which may include 'bd close' in the prompt, bead context, or embedded command. The beads-close-memory-gate.mjs PreToolUse hook (and possibly beads-commit-gate.mjs) pattern-matches against the unquoted command text and can block the outer Bash call before the isolated pi subprocess even starts.

Fix: add early-return in both hooks when the command matches specialists (run|resume|result|feed|stop|status), since those spawn isolated pi subprocesses with --no-extensions. Optionally mirror the bypass in config/pi/extensions/beads/index.ts for defense-in-depth.

Affected files (in xtrm-tools):
- hooks/beads-close-memory-gate.mjs (line ~50, before bd close regex check)
- hooks/beads-commit-gate.mjs (line ~27, before git commit regex check)
- config/pi/extensions/beads/index.ts (line ~121, bash branch in tool_call)
notes:
Implemented ✅ — added a specialists-command bypass in all requested places.

### Changes made

**1) `../xtrm-tools/hooks/beads-close-memory-gate.mjs`**  
Added early return before `bd close` detection:

- If command matches:
  - `specialists run`
  - `specialists resume`
  - `specialists result`
  - `specialists feed`
  - `specialists stop`
  - `specialists status`
- Hook exits immediately (`process.exit(0)`), so outer session won’t false-block isolated specialists subprocess launches.

---

**2) `../xtrm-tools/hooks/beads-commit-gate.mjs`**  
Added the same early return before `git commit` detection, using the same regex on `commandUnquoted`.

---

**3) `../xtrm-tools/config/pi/extensions/beads/index.ts`**  
Added defense-in-depth in `tool_call` bash branch:

- New helper: `isSpecialistsSubprocessCommand(commandUnquoted)`
- Early `return undefined` if the command is one of the specialists subcommands above.
- This bypasses both memory-close and commit blocking logic for those wrapper commands.

title: Dolt-backed run summaries: replace flat job dirs with beads schema
description:
Flat job directories (.specialists/jobs/<id>/) are the root cause of file accumulation, no cross-session query, no provenance, no sharing. The long-term fix is storing run summaries in Dolt (via the beads schema) once a job reaches done/error status.

Architecture:
- HOT PATH (active run): keep flat files — events.jsonl for streaming, status.json for live polling. These are ephemeral.
- COLD PATH (completed run): flush summary into Dolt via bd. Fields: specialist name, prompt hash, model, backend, duration, output (notes field), git SHA, bead_id, started_at, elapsed_s.
- After successful flush: delete the flat job directory (or keep for TTL then GC)

This enables: 'bd list --label specialist' to show all past runs, SQL queries across runs, dolt diff to see output changes, dolt push/pull for sharing run history between machines/agents.

Prerequisites: bead_id in status.json at creation, output pinned to bead (prior two issues).

This is a significant architectural change — plan carefully, keep flat files as fallback during migration.
notes: Stale triage 2026-03-27: strategic long-term architecture item; code crosscheck shows no Dolt-backed run-summary implementation in src yet. Deferring until core lifecycle queue is reduced.

title: Investigate why pi 'tools: yes' metadata doesn't match agentic reality for some models
description:
PROBLEM: pi-coding-agent's --list-models reports tools=yes for several models
that DON'T actually work in the agentic specialist pipeline. Documented today
(session 2026-06-16):

1. nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-omni-30b-a3b-reasoning
   - pi metadata: tools=yes, reasoning=yes
   - Actual behavior: emits tool calls as JSON-in-content with </think> tag,
     NOT OpenAI tool_calls field. pi sees text, ignores intent.
   - Source: probe with 'pi --print --model nvidia/nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-omni-30b-a3b-reasoning'
     against simple "use bash to echo TOOL_OK" prompt → response is a JSON
     description of the planned bash command, never executed.

2. (Documented earlier in memory model-incompat-deepseek-v4-dsml-via-nano-gpt)
   nano-gpt/deepseek/deepseek-v4-*:thinking
   - Similar DSML-pattern failure: tool calls in custom <｜｜DSML｜｜tool_calls>
     format, nano-gpt proxy doesn't translate to OpenAI tool_calls.

3. RELATED: nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b
   - pi metadata: tools=no (correctly), reasoning=yes
   - Different failure: pi --print times out 60s+ because pi cannot parse
     NVIDIA NIM's separate `reasoning_content` delta-field in streaming.
     Direct API curl confirms model emits {"delta": {"reasoning": "...",
     "reasoning_content": "..."}} chunks BEFORE any "content" chunks; pi
     appears to wait for content, never arrives within timeout.

SUCCESS: Three concrete deliverables, any/all may land separately:

  (a) Diagnose where pi's tools=yes metadata comes from for these models
      (hardcoded list? heuristic from model name? declared by provider's
      /v1/models endpoint?). Determine if upstream pi-coding-agent should
      treat the metadata more conservatively.

  (b) Investigate if pi has (or could have) per-provider format translation
      to handle non-OpenAI tool_calls patterns (DSML, <think>+JSON,
      reasoning_content streams). If pi has a translation hook, add one for
      these known patterns. If not, file an upstream issue with pi-coding-agent.

  (c) Document the safe-profile list of "tools=yes per pi metadata but actually
      broken" models in setup-specialists v3.0 skill (epic unitAI-t86wh) so
      operators are warned at setup time.

SCRUTINY: low (research/audit task; no production diff required)

SCOPE: Read-only investigation:
  - /home/dawid/.nvm/versions/node/v24.15.0/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/
    (especially core/model-resolver.js, network/openai-completions/, network/stream/)
  - https://docs.api.nvidia.com/nim/reference for NVIDIA NIM tool/reasoning format
  - https://nano-gpt.com/docs for nano-gpt proxy behavior on tool_calls
  - Verify findings with direct API probes (curl) + pi --print probes
  - Update memory keys nemotron-via-nvidia-nim-pi-incompatible + model-incompat-deepseek-v4-dsml-via-nano-gpt

NON_GOALS:
- no source code changes in this repo
- no specialist config changes
- no model assignments
- no probe automation (that's covered by epic unitAI-t86wh Phase C
  agentic-followthrough probe suite)

CONSTRAINTS:
- Operator's NVIDIA NIM key remains in ~/.pi/agent/models.json (user-supplied,
  not committed). Probes are free against NIM endpoint.
- Investigation should not write to ~/.pi/agent/models.json, only read.
- Findings get appended to existing bd memories — do not duplicate.

VALIDATION:
- A short investigation note with: source of pi metadata, concrete reproduction
  steps for each failure mode, recommended upstream issue (or PR sketch) for
  pi-coding-agent if applicable.
- Memory updated with any new findings.

OUTPUT: investigation summary (in bd notes); optional upstream issue or
discussion link; optional update to epic unitAI-t86wh Phase A skill draft.

title: P4: Orchestrator observability via Claude Code hooks (background writer to observability.db)
description:
Extend observability.db to capture orchestrator-side activity (Claude Code as participant kind, per substrate §2.2). Hooks: PreToolUse/PostToolUse/UserPromptSubmit/PreCompact/SessionStart/SessionEnd write async to a participant_runs table (or unified participant_id schema after Opp 18 rename).

Goal: measure orchestrator-laziness friction (roadmap §2.B B1-B7) — reviewer-skipped, --force-stale-base abuse, invented flags, hand-edits to managed files. Enables A/B comparison pre/post D29 contract-discipline rollout to validate the discipline pays off.

Technical caveats:
1. Hook execution must be async fire-and-forget (nohup background node writer). Zero context/token cost confirmed: hook stdout NOT captured = invisible to conversation.
2. Redaction discipline must match 60w93: no raw secrets, prompt redaction matching 60w93.1 §3 envelope.
3. Storage policy: full row in SQLite local with TTL ~30 days, scrubbed projection for any metrics.
4. Scope-cut explicit: only Claude Code sessions captured. Scripted/cron sp invocations stay specialist-only — acceptable.

Cross-links: related to kj651 (validates discipline shipped by roadmap), 60w93 (envelope conformance), 60w93.1 (forensic contract — participant_kind:orchestrator enters §6 taxonomy).

Sequencing: P4, no Phase commitment. Re-evaluate after kj651 Phase 1-3 ship and state.db rewrite plan is concrete.

## Findings: Current TypeScript Version

### Current Stable Version
**TypeScript 6.0.2** (latest) — published a week ago by `typescript-bot`

| Tag | Version |
|-----|---------|
| `latest` | 6.0.2 |
| `next` | 6.0.0-dev.20260401 |
| `rc` | 6.0.1-rc |
| `beta` | 6.0.0-beta |

### Key Changes in TypeScript 6.0

**Breaking Change: Deprecated Options Removed**

TypeScript 6.0 removes support for several options deprecated in v5.0. These now produce errors:

- `charset`
- `target: ES3`
- `importsNotUsedAsValues`
- `preserveValueImports`
- `noImplicitUseStrict`
- `noStrictGenericChecks`
- `keyofStringsOnly`
- `suppressExcessPropertyErrors`
- `suppressImplicitAnyIndexErrors`
- `out`
- `prepend` (project references)
- Implicitly OS-specific `newLine`

**Migration Required:**

If your `tsconfig.json` uses `preserveValueImports` or `importsNotUsedAsValues`, replace with `verbatimModuleSyntax`:

```json
// ❌ Deprecated (errors in TS 6.0)
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "preserveValueImports": true,
    "importsNotUsedAsValues": "error"
  }
}

// ✅ Correct for TS 6.0
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "verbatimModuleSyntax": true
  }
}
```

**Temporary Escape Hatch:**

To silence deprecation warnings during migration, use:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "verbatimModuleSyntax": true,
    "ignoreDeprecations": "6.0"
  }
}
```

### Installation

```bash
npm install typescript@latest
# or
npm install typescript@6.0.2
```

## **Project Structure Summary: Specialists**

### **Overview**

**Specialists** is a universal framework for defining and running specialist agents via a **bead-first workflow**. It's an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that orchestrates 9 tools for discovering, executing, and managing specialist agents defined in `.specialist.yaml` files. Built on top of the **pi coding agent**, it integrates with **xtrm/xt** (worktree architecture) and **beads** (issue tracking system) for coordinated multi-agent work.

### **Key Modules (Functional Breakdown)**

#### **1. CLI Layer** (`src/cli/`)
- **20+ subcommands** for operational workflow
- Commands: `run`, `list`, `init`, `status`, `feed`, `result`, `stop`, `steer`, `resume`, `follow-up`, `validate`, `doctor`, `help`, `models`, `version`
- Each command loads specialist config, validates user input, spawns pi session or returns metadata

#### **2. MCP Server** (`src/server.ts`)
- **9 MCP tools** registered at startup
- **Tool categories:**
  - Discovery: `list_specialists`
  - Execution: `use_specialist`, `run_parallel`, `start_specialist`
  - Management: `stop_specialist`, `steer_specialist`, `resume_specialist`, `follow_up_specialist`
  - I/O: `feed_specialist`, `specialist_init`
- All tools are stateless and safe to call from multiple clients

#### **3. Specialist System** (`src/specialist/`)
- **Loader**: Scans 3 discovery scopes (system, user, project) for `.specialist.yaml` files
- **Runner**: Orchestrates pi subprocess execution with lifecycle hooks
- **Schema**: Zod validation for specialist definitions (metadata, execution, prompt, capabilities)
- **Beads Client**: Reads issue context, updates bead status on run completion
- **JobRegistry**: Tracks background jobs with metadata (status, events, output)
- **Hooks**: Emits timeline events (job_started, progress, job_done, error) for async tracking

#### **4. Specialist Discovery (3-Scope Model)**
```
System Scope:  ~/.specialists/          (shipped with Specialists)
User Scope:    ~/.specialists/user/     (user customizations, deprecated)
Project Scope: {cwd}/.specialists/      (current project specialists)
               {cwd}/specialists/       (canonical project definitions)
```

#### **5. Built-in Specialists** (`config/specialists/`)
1. **planner** — Structured planning (phases, dependencies, test coverage)
2. **debugger** — Bug hunting with GitNexus call chains
3. **explorer** — Codebase mapping and architecture analysis
4. **test-runner** — Test orchestration and coverage
5. **auto-remediation** — Fix linting, formatting, type errors
6. **memory-processor** — Process and index centralized memory
7. **parallel-runner** — Execute tasks concurrently
8. **xt-merge** — Merge PR queue in order
9. **overthinker** — Deep reasoning and analysis
10. **sync-docs** — Update documentation
11. **specialists-creator** — Author new specialists

#### **6. Test Layers**
- **Integration tests** (`tests/integration/`): Real CLI boundary tests, spawn actual subprocesses
- **Unit tests** (`tests/unit/`): Loader, runner, hooks, tools
- **Coverage threshold**: 80% across all metrics

---

### **Key Patterns & Design Decisions**

| Pattern | Implementation | Rationale |
|---------|---|---|
| **Bead-first** | All work tracked via `bd` issue system | Dependency context, coordination, memory |
| **3-scope discovery** | System → User → Project | Extensibility without modifying shipped code |
| **Pi subprocess** | Each specialist run = isolated Node process | Safety, error isolation, clean teardown |
| **Circuit breaker** | Supervisor tracks health metrics | Prevent cascading failures |
| **Hook timeline** | JSONL event stream | Real-time monitoring, audit trail |
| **Job registry** | Metadata file per job | Resilient to process crash |
| **No polling** | `feed_specialist` streams live output | Lower latency, fewer API calls |

---

### **Relationship to xtrm/xt Ecosystem**

- **xt** provides: worktree isolation, git workflow, session model
- **specialists** provides: specialist execution, 9-tool MCP interface
- **beads** provides: issue tracking, dependency graph, centralized memory
- **pi** provides: tool access, multiple model providers, session lifecycle

**Flow:**
```
user runs: xt pi <issue-id>
     → xt creates worktree, claims issue
     → pi spawns Claude session
     → Claude uses specialists MCP server
     → specialist reads issue context from beads
     → specialist executes, writes result back to issue
     → user merges PR, xt cleans up worktree
```

---

### **Reference to "a8re.3"**

The file `.xtrm/statusline-claim` contains `unitAI-a8re.3`, which is:
- A **bead issue ID** in the format `<board>-<id>`
- The **currently claimed issue** for this xtrm session
- Likely refers to an E2E test or integration test task

---

### **Summary**

This is a **production-grade specialist orchestration framework** designed to:
1. ✅ Define reusable agent specs (`.specialist.yaml`)
2. ✅ Discover specialists across scopes (system/user/project)
3. ✅ Execute specialists in isolated pi subprocesses
4. ✅ Integrate with beads for tracked work
5. ✅ Provide 9 MCP tools for multi-agent coordination
6. ✅ Support background jobs, streaming output, lifecycle hooks

**Technology Stack:** TypeScript 5.0, Vitest, Zod, MCP SDK, Bun/Node.js 16+

bun build --target=bun still emits #!/usr/bin/env node shebang. Must post-process with sed to replace with #!/usr/bin/env bun. bun-bundle-path-resolution: dist/index.js is the bun bundle entry point. dirname(import.meta.url) inside the bundle resolves to dist/, not the original source file location. Consequence: paths to package root need only ONE .. from dist/ (e.g. ../package.json, ../bin/install.js, ../specialists/). Using two .. navigates above the package root into the parent scope. This caused the specialists install path bug in 2.1.14 and was also the correct fix for version.ts package.json import.

bun build statically substitutes the literal token process.env.NODE_ENV at bundle time. Any source that spells it out gets the BUILDER's environment frozen into dist/ as a string constant. In this repo that made deployment_environment report the build machine forever (the production branch unreachable in every packed install) and made the tracked dist/ unmatchable in CI, which builds under NODE_ENV=test — that was the real cause of packed-smoke and payload-contract failing at every head, not stale artifacts. Fix: read through a computed key (const NODE_ENV_KEY = ['NODE','ENV'].join('_'); process.env[NODE_ENV_KEY]) in one shared resolver. Verify by building twice under different NODE_ENV and diffing dist — byte-identical is the proof. Generalises: any tracked build output plus a bundler that inlines env is a latent CI-unmatchable artifact.

Bun spawnSync captures PATH at process startup. Mutating process.env.PATH in-process after Bun has booted does NOT propagate to child processes spawned via node:child_process spawnSync — the child inherits the startup PATH, not the mutated one. Discovered while building the §9 stderr NDJSON failure-injection harness (unitAI-u2s76): setting process.env.PATH = '/nonexistent' before runtime.runGit() left git fully functional.

Workaround for failure injection in Bun smoke harnesses: invoke the harness with PATH={fake-shims}:{rest}, where fake-shims is a tmp dir containing executable scripts that exit non-zero. Example:
  mkdir -p /tmp/fake-path
  cat > /tmp/fake-path/git <<'EOS'
  #!/bin/sh
  exit 127
  EOS
  chmod +x /tmp/fake-path/git
  PATH=/tmp/fake-path:/usr/bin:/bin bun smoke.mjs

This affects any in-process subprocess-failure testing under Bun. Node has the same behavior — env mutation is honored only when you pass `env: { PATH: ... }` to spawnSync options explicitly.

bun-vitest-esm-spyon: vi.spyOn on ESM named exports fails with 'Cannot replace module namespace binding' in Bun/vitest. PRD Phase 6 clarification/escalation (src/activation/ask-tool.ts + native-host wiring): the child asks from INSIDE a blocking custom tool call and the answer returns as that call's RESULT. That shape is what satisfies 'the same AgentSession resumes' — the model is suspended inside a tool call, so returning continues the turn with full context. The tempting alternative (end the turn, store the question, start a new session with the answer prepended) looks equivalent and is not: it discards the child's context and turns a clarification into a restart, which passes a naive 'did it get the answer' test. Blocking in the tool does NOT block the host: prompt() is awaited elsewhere, the session stays alive, and agent_settled cannot fire while a tool call is outstanding. No timeout by design — an unanswered question is a state an operator resolves. The ask/escalate tools are CUSTOM tools passed via createAgentSession({customTools}), admitted alongside noTools:'builtin' plus the resolved allowlist, so a read-only Specialist gains the ability to ask WITHOUT gaining any mutation tool; widening the allowlist to grant asking would hand every reader an edit tool. attemptId is read at call time via a callback, never captured, so a resumed activation attributes its asks to the new attempt.

Claude Code as an MCP CLIENT cannot receive unsolicited push from an MCP server outside an in-flight tool call. Verified against Claude Code issues: sampling/createMessage not implemented (#1785); resources/subscribe + notifications/resources/updated ignored, model context never refreshed (#7252); progress notifications/tokens not implemented (#31893, #51713); logging notifications/message received but silently discarded (#3174, #33679); elicitation/create CLI-only and partial (#2799, #85442, #56243); tools/list_changed works across turns but not same-turn (#31893). So any design that assumes MCP push to a busy Claude coordinator is unbuildable today — use polling, or the peer channel below. IMPORTANT COUNTERPOINT: Claude Code's own cross-session messaging DOES deliver unsolicited messages into a running session mid-turn — observed directly, messages arriving as <cross-session-message from='uds:/run/user/1000/cc-socks/<pid>.sock'>. Mechanisms verified present on this machine: per-PID 0600 sockets at /run/user/1000/cc-socks/*.sock and registration files at ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json. This is what pi-claude-link (MIT) exploits. Delivery passes a user approval gate, so it can be held or refused and must never be treated as guaranteed.

The Claude Code cross-session envelope carries attributes that pi-claude-link's buildEnvelope does not emit and its stripEnvelope regex does not capture. Observed 2026-09-07 by logging a raw frame off a registered 0600 socket in /run/user/1000/cc-socks while a live Claude session (2.1.263) sent to it: {"msgV":1,"msg_id":"<uuid>","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"<cross-session-message from=\"uds:/run/user/1000/cc-socks/<pid>.sock\" hop-chain=\"31aeab02df457fe753c09ccd\" from-name=\"dawid-0b\" from-mode=\"bypass\">..."}}. The hop-chain attribute is undocumented here and its semantics are NOT inferred from the name — treat it as opaque until someone reads the sender side. pi-claude-link's stripEnvelope collects attributes generically via /([a-z-]+)="([^"]*)"/g so it will capture hop-chain, but its StrippedEnvelope type names only body/from/fromName/fromMode, so a parser typed off that interface silently drops it. GENERAL RULE this cost the lane three times (procStart format, the receipt premise, this attribute list): pi-claude-link is evidence of what pi-claude-link SENDS, never a specification of what Claude Code sends. Whoever writes the inbound frame parser must read real frames off a socket rather than porting pi-claude-link's shapes.

CORRECTED, supersedes the earlier claim on this key. Claude Code 2.1.263 emits NO peer_message_status receipt to a peer sender, registered or not. Measured 2026-09-07 across three probes: unregistered (15s), registered (20s), registered (180s) — all three delivered to the coordinator (confirmed by asking it, both msg_ids named) and none produced a receipt. Root cause: receiptFrame appears exactly once in pi-claude-link's index.ts, at line 100, where it SENDS a receipt to an inbound sender. Nothing in that codebase ever receives or awaits one. The receipt is what a NON-Claude peer emits so a Claude sender's own delivered-UI resolves; it is not something Claude sends to us. The protocol header comment claiming 'Claude sends us delivery/hold receipts' was never exercised by the code it sits in — do not treat it as evidence. WHAT REGISTRATION IS ACTUALLY WORTH, and this IS confirmed: it makes the runtime addressable inbound. A real SendMessage from a live Claude session arrived on a registered 0600 colocated socket as a type:'user' frame wrapping the standard cross-session-message envelope, which also carries a hop-chain attribute that pi-claude-link's buildEnvelope does not emit. So the reply path works, and a correlated reply is the only delivery confirmation available on this transport — and a stronger one than a receipt, since it proves a coordinator read and answered rather than that a socket accepted bytes. Only kinds that expect an answer (question, escalation) can ever be confirmed; finding and completion stay sent_unconfirmed permanently by design. Only a push the wire accepted may be upgraded by a reply: a reply after a failed send means the coordinator was reached by polling and proves nothing about the push.

Claude Code emits NO peer_message_status receipt to a peer sender, registered or not. Measured 2026-09-07 on 2.1.263: a fully registered runtime (sessions/<pid>.json, numeric procStart, peerProtocol 1, colocated 0600 socket, pi-claude-link-shaped frame) waited 180s and got no_receipt, identical to unregistered. Cause: receiptFrame is referenced once in pi-claude-link index.ts, on the path that SENDS a receipt to an inbound sender — a receipt is what a non-Claude peer emits so a Claude sender's UI resolves, never something Claude emits to us. The protocol header comment claiming otherwise was never exercised by its own code. Consequence: no_receipt is the permanent steady state, not a fault; confirm delivery by a correlated reply (inReplyTo) instead, which is strictly stronger evidence. Only question/escalation can reach delivered that way; finding/completion stay sent_unconfirmed permanently by design. Registration is still worth keeping because it makes the runtime ADDRESSABLE, which is the inbound reply path.

Claude Code peer transport (cross-session messaging) is real and delivers unsolicited messages mid-turn, but its roster is a discovery surface, NOT a liveness oracle. Measured on the authoring host: 20 registrations in ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json, 10 of them naming dead PIDs while still advertising status:'idle' with their socket file present; 128 socket files under /run/user/1000/cc-socks for those 20 registrations. Liveness must be /proc/<pid> plus procStart (procStart guards PID reuse), never socket existence and never the registration's own status field, which is written by the session and is stale exactly when the session died. Reachability is also asymmetric: a peer that vanished from the roster and whose socket returned ENOENT on send kept delivering messages TO this session, so a failed send must not be read as 'peer is gone'. Delivery passes a user approval gate and may be held/delayed/refused; a receipt is required, absence of an error is not one.

Claude peer transport measured facts (unitAI-rrdnt.23). (1) procStart in ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json has TWO formats: 13 of 18 registrations here carry it as a NUMBER (field 22 of /proc/<pid>/stat, ticks since boot), all written by Claude Code itself; only the 5 pi-claude-link entries use the ps-style string. Accepting only the string rejected 13 of 18 LIVE sessions as missing_proc_start. Prefer numeric — exact integer comparison, no tolerance. (2) 'idle sendUserMessage vs busy steer' is RECEIVER-side (pi-claude-link/index.ts:91); outbound frames carry priority 'next'. A sender cannot choose without branching on the unreliable self-reported status. (3) Delivery and receipt are SEPARABLE: an adapter frame from an UNREGISTERED sender ARRIVED in the target session, but no peer_message_status receipt returned within 15s. Raw delivery works without registration; confirmation does not — so acceptance AX requires the runtime to register itself as a peer, which writes to the user's environment and is the operator's call.

Claude session registrations in ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json carry procStart in TWO different formats, and a liveness checker handling only one silently refuses to route to every peer written by the other. Measured across all 18 registrations on the authoring host 2026-09-07: 13 entries written by Claude Code itself (version 2.1.257/2.1.263) carry procStart as a NUMBER equal to raw field 22 of /proc/<pid>/stat (clock ticks since boot) — verified exactly equal for pids 1100092, 2176609, 3574376, 404065. Multi-process race tests need a barrier tight enough to actually discriminate, and a wall-clock barrier is usually not. Measured 2026-09-07 building the unitAI-rrdnt.21 workspace lease: 8 processes spinning until a shared Date.now() instant produced exactly 1 winner against BOTH the correct link()-based atomic publish AND a deliberately broken read-then-write — the winner finished writing before the losers had even read, so the test proved nothing while looking rigorous. Switching the barrier to a tight spin on existsSync(goFile), released by touching that file after every runtime has booted, made the naive implementation produce 2, 1, 4, 2, 1 winners across five rounds while the correct one produced exactly 1 every time. Two consequences: (a) always mutation-test a concurrency assertion against a deliberately broken implementation before trusting it, and (b) repeat the race, because at 40 percent single-winner rate one round lets a broken implementation through. Also note execFileSync serialises spawns entirely — use parallel execFile/spawn or there is no race at all.

ConsoleApp handleInput: when adding view-specific arrow handlers (↑/↓/j/k), gate the generic move handler at the top of handleInput to scroll-or-ps views ONLY. Two admission rules over one lease, and the difference is the DEFAULT case. admitToolCall (Specialist side) refuses an UNLEASED workspace, because a Specialist must hold a lease to mutate. admitCoordinatorToolCall allows a free workspace and refuses only an active holder or an uncertain lease, because the coordinator never holds one — reusing the Specialist predicate would refuse every coordinator write whenever no Specialist was running. Both read the same inspect(), so they cannot disagree about WHO holds the lease, only about what the absence of one means. The near-miss: 'just share the function' looked obviously right and would have shipped a coordinator that could not edit its own repository.

dist/ is TRACKED in xtrm-dev/specialists (309 files) and .github/workflows/package-payload.yml rebuilds it in CI and diffs against the committed tree — packed-smoke and payload-contract both fail when a generated declaration differs. So ANY source change that alters a .d.ts requires committing the rebuilt artifacts in the same change: run 'bun run build', then commit dist/. New source modules also add whole new dist/types/<dir>/ trees that are untracked until committed. The failure signature is a multi-thousand-line sourcemap diff in the CI log, which reads as noise rather than as a missing build step — that is the trap. Never hand-edit a generated file (passes once, diverges next build) and never .gitignore dist/ to make the check pass (removes the check instead of satisfying it; packed-smoke exists to prove the published tarball matches source).

specialists dist builds must run only after in-place bun install --frozen-lockfile. xt worktrees carry a stub node_modules, so bun module resolution and the tsc bin walk up ancestor dirs to the host checkout's node_modules - baking host-relative bundler comment paths (// ../../../node_modules/...) and host-tsc d.ts emit formatting into committed dist. The PR280 package-payload reproducibility gate (NODE_ENV=test bun run build + git diff --exit-code -- dist/) correctly rejects such artifacts; bun 1.3.14 CI builds are byte-stable once dist is regenerated in-place. bunx-mediated bun runs contaminate NODE_ENV inlining (deployment_environment becomes development); use direct bun.

InteractionTransport's deliver hook is CONSTRUCTOR-ONLY, so anything that wires it must resolve the transport lazily. NativeActivationHost builds the peer delivery hook inside the same expression that constructs the transport the hook routes replies through; a direct 'this.interactions' reference captures undefined and every reply is dropped silently — the ask never resolves and it reads as a slow coordinator, not as a bug. src/activation/peer-bridge.ts therefore takes 'transport: () => InteractionTransport'. Same file: the reply is awaited on the DURABLE STORE (.specialists/interactions/), never on the socket, which is what makes a pushed question and a polled question indistinguishable to the Specialist.

InteractionMessage (src/activation/interaction.ts, PRD Phase 5) is THE one participant protocol — PRD invariant BH. MCP and the peer channel are serialisations of it, never second vocabularies. Kinds: question|escalation|finding|completion|reply|instruction. The discriminant is 'question', NOT 'clarification' — clarification is what an interaction is FOR, question is what it IS; escalation is the sibling that also expects an answer but from a different party. Only question and escalation create a pending ask; finding and completion create no attention. Two semantics are load-bearing and tested: correlation is by inReplyTo and NEVER positional (two asks can be outstanding, so ordering crosses them), and 'delivered' requires an explicit receipt — the deliver hook must return exactly true, since a hook returning undefined or throwing leaves the message pending. A richer wire-level DeliveryState maps DOWN: sent_unconfirmed and undeliverable both project to pending, because neither is a receipt and neither is a refusal. BUG WORTH REMEMBERING: request() must register its waiter against a pre-allocated messageId BEFORE sending. Registering after the send loses any reply that outruns it and the asker blocks forever — silent loss of exactly the kind PRD section 30 forbids.

Wiring the workspace lease (unitAI-rrdnt.36) made every unit test that built a NativeActivationHost on process.cwd() write a REAL lease into the repository under .specialists/leases/. When the vitest worker exits, the holder pid is gone and the lease is left UNCERTAIN — which by design cannot be stolen — so the next writer in any suite, or a real developer dispatch, is refused with workspace_lease_uncertain. It happened immediately and had to be reconciled by hand. Same class as the observability.db incident: a test operating on live developer state, invisible until something downstream refuses. Fix: every host in a unit test gets a mkdtemp workspace, swept in afterEach. Check for the leak with 'ls .specialists/leases/' after a suite run — an empty directory is the pass condition. Silver lining: that accident was the FIRST time Phase 9 reconciliation met a real uncertainty rather than a manufactured one, and safe_free applied correctly.

Every defect this epic found was found by running the system, none by reading code or by a green test. Five occurrences of one shape: a test asserts a fixture or a double that agrees with the author's belief, so it stays green while the real configuration behaves differently. Each test dispatches a real sp run executor that needs 30-60s minimum (model RTT + state writes + sp run setup); the fallback-chain test additionally walks 2 broken models (~10-20s each timeout) before reaching the live one — easily 90-180s per test. Bead unitAI-o5rwj's VALIDATION asked for '4 tests pass, <60s/file' which is structurally impossible with the current design. Two viable redesigns: (a) raise the budget to ≥180s/file (cheapest fix), (b) mock the supervisor in tests so they don't actually call the model (cleanest fix). Tracked as follow-up unitAI-qw1kn. Lesson for future bead authors: when VALIDATION includes 'live tests pass under a wall-clock budget', verify the budget against actual real-model RTT before committing — bead-time over-optimism creates unfixable closeout work.

Live acceptance cases that PASS print nothing: vitest swallows console.log for passing tests, so a green live run yields a pass count and no observed state — the exact shape that lets an acceptance be reported proven while the activation sat in 'failed'.
