In multiplexed tmux-agent work, Serena create_text_file/replace tools target Serena's active project root, not necessarily the target pane's git worktree cwd. A delegated agent in a worktree may think it wrote files there while Serena summarized a write elsewhere or no visible file appears. For worktree-specific file creation during multiplexing, prefer shell heredocs executed with explicit 'cd <worktree>' and verify with shell find/git status before validation.

Native activation Phase 3 bead gate (src/activation/bead-gate.ts) refuses any bead that is not a complete 7-section task contract with a SCRUTINY level, BEFORE createAgentSession. Two design choices worth keeping: (1) an ABSENT 'bd state <id> contract' marker is NOT treated as draft — only an explicit contract=draft is refused — because most beads predate the marker and refusing them all makes the gate unusable; (2) the gate proves a section exists and is non-empty, never that it is good, because judging scope quality is not something a parser can do. Consequence for test authors: any fixture bead used with NativeActivationHost must now carry all seven sections plus SCRUTINY, and unit tests should inject beadGate: { readContractState: () => undefined } to keep the gate off the real bd binary.

Native activation host (src/activation/) design decisions, Phase 1 unitAI-rrdnt.5: (1) Specialists does NOT hard-depend on @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent — src/activation/pi-sdk.ts resolves it at runtime, preferring normal module resolution then falling back to the global install via the existing resolveGlobalNodeModulesDir(). Hard-depending would version-couple Specialists to every pi release; the legacy sp run path needs none of it. The SDK is typed structurally rather than by importing pi's declarations, so tsc still passes where pi is absent. (2) createAgentSession must be called with noTools:'builtin' plus an explicit tools allowlist — tools:[] also empties customTools, which is the wrong knob. (3) The host must NOT dispose on agent_settled; settling means waiting-and-resumable. Disposal is only via explicit stop(). (4) Phase 1 refuses MEDIUM/HIGH specialists outright because the writer lease does not exist yet — remove that refusal only in Phase 10. Pi SDK createAgentSession takes model?: Model<any> — an OBJECT, not a provider-qualified string. Passing the string is accepted silently and fails mid-turn with 'No API key found for undefined'. Resolve the Model via resolveModelScopeWithDiagnostics (scopedModels[0].model) and pass that object. Also: waitForIdle() returning does NOT mean the turn succeeded — pi records a failed turn as an assistant message with stopReason 'error'|'aborted' plus errorMessage (provider 429/401/400/410 all land here), so a host that only checks for exceptions reports 'completed' with empty output. Native Specialist activation (unitAI-rrdnt) Phase 0 findings, verified against installed @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent 0.84.3: (1) Pi's tool_call veto {block,reason,terminate} is the LOAD-BEARING lease enforcement, NOT setActiveToolsByName — the latter takes effect only on the next agent turn because the agent loop executes off a currentContext snapshot taken at turn start (agent-loop.js:393-394,130-145). PRD §52's defense-in-depth ordering is inverted; building it as written leaks the lease for the rest of every turn. (2) tool_call covers built-ins, bash-as-tool, registerTool, SDK customTools and baseToolsOverride, but NOT AgentSession.executeBash(), NOT the user_bash/RPC-bash operator path, NOT pi.exec() in an extension handler, NOT direct fs/child_process in extension code — so PRD §54 is unsatisfiable for the last two on 0.84.3. (3) createAgentSession does NOT require running inside pi's process — the xtrm vertical-slice experiment hosts sessions from its own bun process with zero spawn, so the Claude MCP server can host in-process and needs no RpcClient. (4) resolveCliModel is unsafe for model-override validation: with a known provider an unknown model id becomes a custom model with only a warning. Gate on resolveModelScopeWithDiagnostics no-match diagnostics PLUS modelRuntime.hasConfiguredAuth. (5) agent_settled is a distinct event from agent_end; agent_end is per-turn and carries willRetry.

NativeActivationHost.resume() must RE-SUBSCRIBE the host's lifecycle listener, not reuse the one from start(). The emit closure created in start() captures attemptId by value, so a resumed activation would keep emitting forensic events tagged with attempt 1 forever — invisible until someone queries lineage across attempts, which is exactly what the v15 identity migration exists to make answerable. resume() must also rebind BOTH record.unsubscribe and record.result, or stop() later calls a stale unsubscribe and leaks the old listener. Related: resumable states are settled/waiting/needs_reply/escalated only. 'failed' is deliberately NOT resumable — resuming a failed attempt is a RETRY, a different operation; admitting it silently blurs the two. 'uncertain' is excluded because crash recovery is PRD Phase 9 with its own semantics (crash yields uncertain, never a blind free).

StepContract (src/activation/step-contract.ts, PRD section 15) is DERIVED and in-memory: compiled per activation from the Bead's 7 sections plus the SpecialistDefinition, never persisted, never given an id, never linked to another StepContract. The PRD forbids a second work graph twice (Phase 4 'do not create step issues', invariant 4). Design notes worth keeping: mandate = SUCCESS bounded by SCOPE, deliberately excluding PROBLEM because PROBLEM says what is wrong rather than what this activation is asked to do; the scope boundary lives ONLY in nonGoals, not duplicated into ScopeContract, so the two cannot drift; the PRD's EvidenceRef/OutputRequirement/ScopeContract/ValidationRequirement have no field definitions upstream, so they are narrowed to what a Bead can supply today rather than modelling an evidence subsystem that does not exist. bead-gate.ts owns the single section parser (extractSections) and step-contract.ts reuses it — a second parser would let the gate and the compiler disagree about what a Bead says.

Phase 9 workspace reconciliation (unitAI-rrdnt.31): the way out of an uncertain lease is a PROPOSAL the module validates, never an inference. Caller supplies {outcome, decidedBy, basis[]}; reconcile() re-inspects the live lease at decision time and refuses anything the current uncertainReason does not permit. Two properties make it unforgeable: recovered_holder is computed rather than proposed (a caller that could assert 'the holder came back' could assert it falsely), and an empty basis[] is insufficient evidence for every outcome including manual_attention_required. The four uncertainReason values are NOT one rule: holder_process_gone and holder_start_mismatch permit safe_free/superseded/manual; unreadable_record permits superseded/manual only (no holder identity means nothing can be attributed as safely finished); liveness_unverifiable permits manual ONLY, because on a host that cannot observe processes an abandoned lease and a live writer produce identical evidence, so every timeout/staleness argument for relaxing it is an inference from absence. safe_free and superseded do the same thing to the lease file and differ only in what is asserted; neither publishes a successor lease, because that would fabricate liveness for an unprobed process.

node:sqlite bind forms vs bun: on node, db.run(sql, [a,b]) (bun array form) is read as a single named-parameter OBJECT — array keys '0','1' → SQLITE error 'Unknown named parameter 0', ALL writes silently lost while the client still OPENS (sink try/catch swallows). The vitest suite used to operate on the repository's OWN observability.db, because resolveObservabilityDbLocation falls back to <gitRoot>/.specialists/db when XDG_DATA_HOME is unset. IMPORTANT dead end: forcing XDG_DATA_HOME globally was tried first and is WRONG — tests that build their own temp git repo expect git-root resolution inside it, so a global override puts the writer and the reader of a single test on different databases (40 failures across 14 files). Relocation must be targeted. Also: the setup must CREATE the relocated store, because createObservabilitySqliteClient returns null when the file is absent and many supervisor/CLI tests silently relied on the repo store existing. Production sets neither variable, so its behaviour is byte-identical; the bun-test files that assert the git-root fallback are the proof and must stay green.

A peer message stating intent is not board state. I read 'I'm taking .55/.60' from a session and wrote it to the beads as an assignee, which moved a bead to IN_PROGRESS under a claim held by a read-only activation with no bd tooling — structurally incapable of owning it. Clearing it needed a scoped --force because bd correctly refused to overwrite what looked like a live claim. The severity is the point: an unowned bead gets picked up, an INCORRECTLY-owned one looks handled and strands silently, so a wrong assignee is worse than none. Also: a message from a session name may come from that session's coordinator OR from an activation running inside it, and those have very different capabilities — verify the sender can act before recording that it will.

pi beads commit-gate '<id>' placeholder bug: the pi extension (@jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions extensions/beads) claim_job_start handler can write the LITERAL string '<id>' as the value of bd kv key 'claimed:<pi-session-id>' (a templating bug — value shows as <id> not a real bead id). pi-claude-link is evidence of what pi-claude-link SENDS, never a specification of what Claude Code sends. Three measured instances in the specialists repo: (1) its procStart format is one of two in use on the real roster; (2) its protocol header comment claims Claude sends delivery/hold receipts, which its own code never exercises and which is false; (3) a real inbound frame carried a hop-chain envelope attribute its buildEnvelope does not emit and its stripEnvelope does not capture. Write any inbound parser against real frames read off a socket, not against that source. Related: reply-as-delivery needs FOUR boundaries, not three — kind predicate, inReplyTo-only correlation, no resurrection of refused, AND only a push the wire accepted may be upgraded; without the fourth, a failed send plus a polling-driven reply gets marked delivered.

pi 0.85.1 calls a custom tool's execute() with FIVE arguments: (toolCallId: string, args: object, ctx: object, callback: function, ...). The PARAMETERS OBJECT IS THE SECOND ARGUMENT, not the first. Declaring execute: async (args) => ... binds the tool-call id string to args, so every field read is undefined and the tool silently misbehaves — in this repo ask_coordinator refused every call as empty and the child reasoned that the harness was broken. Nothing catches it: the parameter is typed, it compiles, and a unit test calling tool.execute({...}) directly asserts the contract it wishes for. Test custom tools through a helper that supplies the tool-call id, and assert on the observable effect rather than on the arguments the test passed. Measured by instrumenting execute as (...all) and printing arity and each argument.

A pi 0.85.1 custom tool must return AgentToolResult { content: [{type:'text',text}], details } — NOT a bare string. pi normalises result.content ?? [] so a string becomes empty content and the child sees '(no tool output)'. In this repo that was the THIRD consecutive defect in ask-tool.ts, each hidden by the last: tools filtered out of the session by tools[] (.43.1), wrong execute signature — args is the SECOND argument (.43.2), wrong return shape (.43.3). All three were invisible to a unit test that called execute directly and asserted on its return value, because at that boundary each defect looked correct. Test custom tools by extracting the text from content[], i.e. assert what the CHILD sees, and get live evidence — every one of the three was found by a live run, never by reading code.

Pi event-stream cap should be on RETAINED state (assistant text + stderr + single line size), never raw pipe throughput. Raw-byte caps reject runs based on the volume of data we explicitly discard during streaming parse. The wrong knob causes legitimate large-range LLM runs to fail and tempts band-aid cap raises that risk downstream context overflow. Pattern: cap what you keep, not what you receive.

pi hook gotcha: Bash heredocs are scanned as raw command text by xtrm/pi gates. If generated documentation contains a literal beads close command inside a code block, the memory gate can block the whole Bash command before file writing. Workaround for docs generation: write a placeholder in the heredoc and replace it afterward with Python string concatenation, so the literal trigger is not present in the Bash command text.

pi 0.85.1 lets a session's own CREATOR guard tool calls without an extension. It exports the builtin tool factories individually — createEditTool, createWriteTool, createBashTool, createPowerShellTool, createReadTool, createGrepTool, createFindTool, createLsTool, plus *Definition variants and createCodingTools/createReadOnlyTools — and wrapRegisteredTool(registeredTool, runner)/wrapRegisteredTools show the wrapping shape, returning { ...tool, execute: async (toolCallId, params, signal, onUpdate) => ... }. So a host can construct the mutating builtins itself, wrap each execute with its own admission check, and pass them as customTools instead of naming pi's unguarded originals in tools[]. That makes the guard structurally unskippable rather than something each frontend must remember to call. AgentSession also exposes bindExtensions/extensionRunner/hasExtensionHandlers, but an extension tool_call veto is weaker: it does not cover AgentSession.executeBash() or pi.exec(). Caveat: a wrapped custom tool must ALSO be named in tools[], which is a hard filter.

pi install -l only adds a package to .pi/settings.json — it does NOT fetch/install from npm. To actually install, run pi install npm:<pkg> without -l (global). Listing in settings.json is declarative; the global install is what makes the extension available at runtime.

pi loads extensions from three scopes, not just global npm: (1) project-bundled at repo config/pi-extensions/, (2) global npm at $(npm root -g), (3) user-scope pi manifest at ~/.pi/agent/npm/package.json with its own node_modules tree. When asked 'what pi extension is installed', check all three — npm ls -g alone misses user-scope pi extensions like @gotgenes/pi-subagents.

Pi 0.84.3 model-availability gate, EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED: to reject an unavailable model before session creation you need BOTH halves — no 'no-match' diagnostic from resolveModelScopeWithDiagnostics AND modelRuntime.hasConfiguredAuth(provider). Neither alone is sufficient. Confirmed trap: with a KNOWN provider and an unknown model id (--provider nvidia --model no-such-model-at-all), resolveCliModel returns a FABRICATED model with error undefined and only a warning ('Using custom model id'), while hasConfiguredAuth('nvidia') returns true — so an auth-only gate accepts a model that does not exist. Only the no-match diagnostic catches that case. Conversely a real model under an unauthenticated provider resolves fine via resolveCliModel, so only the auth check catches that one. OPERATIONAL TRAP: ModelRuntime.create({refreshOnCreate:false}) returns zero configured-auth providers and an empty getAvailable(), which makes the gate reject everything; use {allowModelNetwork:false} instead and leave refreshOnCreate alone.

pi's ExtensionAPI exposes on('tool_call', handler) returning ToolCallEventResult { block?: boolean; reason?: string } — 'Fired before a tool executes. Can block.' So an extension CAN refuse the COORDINATOR's own tool calls per call, which is the shape a workspace fence needs and which setActiveToolsByName cannot provide. on('user_bash', ...) with UserBashEventResult exists too, so the operator bash path is enforceable rather than merely avoidable by discipline. pi.exec and direct node:fs inside extension code remain unhookable on 0.85.1. Read this from node_modules/@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts rather than inferring it — the typings ARE installed even though the repo has none of its own.

Pi 0.84.3 tool_call veto, EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED (not just source-read) at /tmp/xtrm-pi-veto-probe/: (1) The veto fires and actually prevents execution for all five LLM tool paths — built-in edit, write, bash, registerTool tools, and SDK customTools — proven by side effect with a veto-off control run. Blocked calls surface as isError=true carrying the reason string. (2) setActiveToolsByName CANNOT revoke a tool call already planned in the current batch: a real two-call parallel batch where handler #1 revoked call #2's tool still executed call #2. Only {block:true} stops it. (3) IMPORTANT POSITIVE: every tool_call handler in a parallel batch fires BEFORE any tool in that batch executes (prepare-all, then Promise.all — pi-agent-core agent-loop.js:332-374), so a lease acquired during call #1 CAN still block call #2 in the same batch via block. Mid-batch lease acquisition is enforceable. (4) Confirmed bypasses, handler fired ZERO times while the veto was active and blocking everything: AgentSession.executeBash() and pi.exec() called inside an extension handler. Both exited 0 and wrote their files. Any lease must gate these at their own call sites.

pi 0.85.1: createAgentSession's tools[] is a HARD FILTER that also applies to customTools. A session given customTools:[ask_coordinator] and tools:['read'] reports getAllTools()===['read'] — the custom tool is dropped silently, no error and no diagnostic. Custom tool names MUST also appear in tools[]. Omitting tools[] is not the alternative: that admits every builtin, measured at 50+ including bash/edit/write/powershell, which is fail-OPEN. Consequence in this repo: ask_coordinator and escalate_to_coordinator never reached any Specialist, so PRD Phase 6 (acceptances J, K, L and AX) was unreachable by construction while ask-tool.ts and interaction.ts were complete and unit-tested against doubles. Diagnosed by enumerating getAllTools() on a live session; the tempting wrong explanation was that a small model chose not to call the tool. Assert on the session's own tool set, never on the arguments passed to createAgentSession — those were always correct.

The pi SDK's tools[] is a hard filter that applies to customTools too: naming a custom tool in tools[] is necessary but not sufficient, and omitting tools[] entirely fails OPEN, admitting 50+ builtins including bash/edit/write. The ask_coordinator defect was three stacked defects, none visible by reading code: the allowlist filtered the custom tools out, execute's params are the SECOND argument of a 5-arity signature, and a bare string return normalises to empty so the child sees '(no tool output)'. All three were found by live probes.

pi-tui TUI integration gotchas (learned from chat.ts P0 fix unitAI-h1yst): (1) Input components don't render their cursor or accept keys until tui.setFocus(input) is called — without it, the box appears empty and inert. The resolution was WARN-not-refuse, because the ungated tool predates the gate and refusing breaks callers whose beads were never written to the contract. The load-bearing detail: the warning must ride the RESULT, not a log. A log nobody reads reproduces the original defect exactly — the operator takes the ungated path with no indication they took it.

Bead content is DATA, never template source. Template-origin tokens still resolve because the union map carries prompt/bead_context/bead_id/cwd/pre_script_output/lineage/caller vars.

sp merge conflict fallback pattern: when sp merge fails with 'Merge conflict', root causes are (1) stale .git/index.lock from a crashed merge attempt — fix: rm .git/index.lock, and (2) noise files staged from prior squash attempts. Use git branch -D (not -d) to delete squash-merged branches since --squash doesn't create a merge commit in the DAG.

spawnSync-stdin-block: spawnSync() without explicit stdio config inherits parent stdin. Specialist staleness STALE flag can't be cleared by a same-day metadata.updated bump (loader.ts:46-51). computeStaleness does updatedMs=new Date(metadata.updated).getTime() which parses a 'YYYY-MM-DD' string as MIDNIGHT UTC, then flags STALE when watched-file mtimeMs > updatedMs. A files_to_watch target touched later the SAME calendar day (e.g. 03:4x) has mtime > midnight, so it stays STALE until metadata.updated is a LATER date (or an ISO timestamp >= the file mtime). The mechanism is day-granular in intent (stale_threshold_days is in days) but the comparison is ms-granular — a real minor bug. Proper fix: compare date-granular (truncate mtimeMs to its date vs updated date). Workaround if you must clear it today: set updated to a full ISO timestamp after the file mtime (breaks the YYYY-MM-DD convention) or next day's date (inaccurate). Surfaced bumping specialists-creator.specialist.json to 1.4.1/2026-05-30 after the SKILL.md refresh (unitAI-tkl69).

Specialists runtime has 6 architectural asymmetries (docs/design/specialists-runtime-critique.md) all rooted in one shape error: jobs are first-class, chains are derived projections. Confirmed in chain-identity.ts:38-39 (chainId defaults to worktree_owner_job_id defaults to job's own id — no chain entity). The 6 asymmetries: (1) executor as privileged chain bootstrapper (--worktree and --job mutually exclusive forces first-dispatched role to own chain), (2) worktree owned by job not chain (orphan-on-death pattern, stale-base false positives), (3) chain has no entity row (workflow/scrutiny/budget/evidence-index have nowhere to live), (4) keep-alive paradox (pi session held alive because workspace handle bound to job_id), (5) --bead conflates work-contract with chain-key (R4 tracking-bead-vs-target confusion is structural), (6) reviewer-as-parasite cannot exist without executor --job (locks chain shape to executor-first). Substrate containers invert each: container opens BEFORE specialists, worktree lifetime = container lifetime, container row carries chain-level state, pi keep-alive becomes purely LLM-state convenience. Stage A/B/C/D rollout plan: containers table additive → worktree ownership migration → explicit container open → issue membership edges replace chain_root_bead_id. Substrate autonomy gradient — one pattern for three open questions (container nesting, node nesting, dispatch_mode). Pattern: 'allowed within policy → escalates at boundary → hard-blocked beyond which only operator can go' (same shape as §5.10 graded escalation + §5.8 emitter capability). Decisions: (a) container nesting soft-warn at depth 2, hard-cap at 4 (depth=live membership only, seeds don't count); (b) node nesting depth 1 via parent escalation + operator approval, depth 2 manual-only (sub-node coordinator cannot escalate for grandchild), depth 3+ hard-blocked unconditionally; (c) dispatch_mode = flat default string + optional matcher rules reusing seed invite_when / workflow applies_when syntax. All three are config + reuse of existing primitives — no new daemon machinery, no new SDK verbs.

Substrate chain_template + coordinator covers bounded adaptation via insert-step policy, but not open-ended self-organizing research loops that need external memory/artifact handoffs and runtime team formation.

Substrate close model elegantly removes 3 bd shim hooks (memory-ack, commit-gate, Stop) by making close a derivation not an imperative: issue closes when evidence satisfies acceptance AND container state permits AND close_reason recorded. Normal path: nobody runs sb issue close — container merge transactionally closes all members. memory-ack disappears because substrate auto-distills memory on failed-semantic close (curator pulled relevant memories at seed start, no end-of-issue lesson to ack). commit-gate disappears because issue cannot reach close_ready until diff evidence dual-written. Stop hook disappears because claims belong to participants (jobs) not sessions — pi keep-alive holds participant in waiting, no claim is left dangling. Eligibility table maps issue class × container kind × container state to allowed close_reason enum; refusal returns structured envelope matching channels.md §10.2 shape. close_reason deterministically drives done vs archived split. New work_state value 'close_ready' = eligible but awaiting container merge.

Substrate knowledge-scope principle (unifies rule conflict / cold-start context / memory pruning + promotion): 'facts with metadata; queries reconstruct the slice. Rules, curation, pruning are queries with different filters — not different stores or new entities.' Extends §10 'levels are queries not fields' to all 3. Decisions: (a) rule conflict impossible because owning-issue rules govern MY behavior, target-issue contract is MY rubric, referenced-issue evidence is MY input — three different surfaces, not one collapsed authority; (b) no session-level memory curator — orchestrator-as-participant gets context same as any participant, cold-start = explicit CLI Query (one store, two entry points); (c) pruning runs on stored metadata fields (in_container, in_project) not on tier-queries — preserve-and-demote, never delete on retirement (matches §5.10 closed:failed pattern); (d) promotion = automatic counter (≥3 distinct workgroups in 90d) + manual override; (e) identity scope = per-role-per-project (not per-role-global) to prevent cross-project surface leakage.

Token counts in 'sp ps' (e.g. tokens=90k) are RAW totals, not context-window percentages. Models like gpt-5.3-codex have ~200k windows. Wave/chain/job formal model LOCKED 2026-04-10 via 2 parallel overthinkers in unitAI-5osz. TAXONOMY: Job (atomic) | Chain (worktree lineage, seeded only by edit-capable specialist) | Wave (STAGE/BATCH label, speech only, zero code meaning) | Epic (top merge-gated identity with state machine). MULTI-AXIS not strict nesting: epic contains stages, chain contains jobs, jobs carry both associations. 'Wave' is reserved for human shorthand ('Wave 1', 'Wave 2b') — never persisted, never a code identity. The top merge container is 'epic' (reuses bead epic id). Epic lifecycle: open → resolving → merge_ready → merged/failed/abandoned. INVARIANT: an epic is not 'done' when its jobs finish; it is only complete when it reaches merge_ready and is closed through sp epic merge, even if that merge is a no-op. CLI split: sp merge <chain> (one-shot, refuses if chain ∈ unresolved epic), sp epic merge <epic> (the only legal publication path for wave-bound chains), sp end (must be epic-aware, refuses bypass). Chain owns worktree, provisioned at chain seed. Full locked design in unitAI-lzys notes.

Building inside an .xtrm worktree with incomplete node_modules produces a CORRUPT bundle with no error: bun silently resolves missing packages from the parent checkout and bakes ../../../node_modules paths into dist. The only signal was release-attestation failing, which reads as a defect in the changed code until you diff dist against HEAD. Threshold that separates real from benign: dist/ is one level down, so ../node_modules is this repo's own tree and correct, while TWO OR MORE ../ escapes the checkout. Guard added in scripts/postprocess-build.mjs, which runs on every build — it throws and names the leaked packages rather than stripping the comments, because a bundle linked against two dependency trees is wrong rather than untidy and stripping would hide it.

Worktree concurrency guard must NOT reuse ACTIVE_STATUSES from worktree-gc.ts — GC treats 'waiting' as active (don't delete), but the --job concurrency guard must treat 'waiting' as SAFE (reviewer enters idle executor). Different semantics require a separate BLOCKED_JOB_REUSE_STATUSES = Set(['starting', 'running']). Also: --job auto-bead resolution requires TWO changes — relaxing parseArgs() validation (currently rejects --job without --bead/--prompt before run() executes) AND adding post-resolution inference.

Building dist inside an .xtrm worktree can silently corrupt the bundle. The worktree's node_modules was missing zod, zod-to-json-schema and @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, so bun resolved them from the repo root and baked 248 '// ../../../node_modules/...' path comments into dist/index.js, failing tests/integration/release-attestation.test.ts. HEAD's dist had zero. Fix: run 'bun install' in the worktree BEFORE 'bun run build'. The attestation test is what catches it.

worktree-per-edit-agent: Any specialist with edit permission runs in its own worktree branch. Subsequent agents (reviewer, test-runner, etc.) must cd into that same worktree to see the files. Orchestrator merges branches in dependency order after each wave. Parallel executors only allowed if file sets are provably disjoint.

Worktree pi RPC startup fix: provisionWorktree() now symlinks <worktree>/.pi/npm -> <commonRoot>/.pi/npm. Prevents 30-60s npm install on first specialist run in new worktrees. symlinkPiNpmCache() is non-fatal: if symlink fails, pi still installs from scratch. The stdout corruption claim in notes was incorrect — takeOverStdout() is called before resourceLoader.reload() so npm output goes to stderr, not stdout. Real issue was slow startup (10s→30s timeout was band-aid, symlink is fix).

Worktree RPC timeout root cause: pi runs npm install in fresh worktrees, stdout output corrupts RPC JSON channel. Fix: symlink worktree .pi/npm/node_modules → main repo .pi/npm/node_modules. provisionWorktree() should do this automatically. Also: always run commands from main repo cwd, not worktree — cd into worktree loses beads DB connection.

writeGlobalUserConfig in src/specialist/global-config.ts uses atomic tmp+rename: writes to sibling tmp file (path+'.tmp.PID.cookie'), renameSync over dest. POSIX rename is atomic within same fs. On rename failure: cleans up tmp file, falls back to direct writeFileSync (last-resort persistence), then throws the rename error so the operator surface sees atomicity wasn't achieved. Regression test exercises EISDIR by placing a directory at dest.

xt pi forwards flags to the pi runtime ONLY after a bare '--'. Anything before it is xt-owned or silently dropped. Measured 2026-09-08: 'xt pi <name> --model M -e path/to/extension.mjs' starts a normal session with the extension NOT loaded, and the coordinator then misdiagnoses the missing tools as 'no MCP servers are connected' — a confident wrong explanation, because an extension surface is not MCP. Working form: 'xt pi <name> --model M -- -e config/pi-extensions/<name>/index.mjs'. Verify by checking pi's [Extensions] list in the TUI, not by the session starting.

xtrm-tools-pre-push-osv-vs-gitignored-lockfile-2026-05-23: xtrm-tools's pre-push osv-scanner reads cli/.pi/npm/package-lock.json from disk regardless of .gitignore status. When pushing to xtrm-tools origin/main, this lockfile may flag GHSA advisories for transitive deps (e.g. qs<6.15.2 GHSA-q8mj-m7cp-5q26 from body-parser/express) that have nothing to do with the commit. Fix: cd ~/dev/xtrm-tools/cli/.pi/npm && npm update <pkg> to bump the lockfile in place. No git commit needed since the file is gitignored; the osv-scanner picks up the disk state, hook passes, push proceeds. Verify by checking grep '"version":' on the lockfile after npm update before retrying the push.

xtrm-tools-skill-propagation-requires-npm-link-2026-05-23: To propagate skill changes from ~/dev/specialists/config/skills/* to consumer repos via xt update, xtrm-tools must be installed as an npm symlink (not a real-dir copy). Default xtrm-tools install via npm publish creates a real directory at /home/dawid/.nvm/.../lib/node_modules/xtrm-tools, breaking the symlink pattern that pi-extensions and specialists use. Symptom: xt update --apply reports 'refreshed' but the SKILL.md content doesn't change in consumer repos because xt reads the npm-installed xtrm-tools registry which has stale hashes baked in at install time. Fix: cd ~/dev/xtrm-tools && npm link (restores the global symlink), then re-run vendor-specialists-skills.mjs + gen-registry.mjs, then xt update --apply again. The first xt update WILL revert your vendor changes (because pre-link, it treats them as drift); only the second one after link+revendor propagates them. Verify with diff -q ~/projects/<repo>/.xtrm/skills/default/<skill>/SKILL.md ~/dev/specialists/config/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md returning identical.

yme9q-terminal-alive-orphan-reaper-2026-07-05: Fixed the class of orphan pi keep-alive sessions where the SQLite job row is terminal (done/error/cancelled) but the OS process (and its detached pi child) still runs. Three surfaces now cover it: (1) src/specialist/process-health.ts:collectStaleSpecialistJobs adds a second pass over terminal statuses whose PID is still alive past minTerminalAliveAgeMs (default 60s — pi's close backstop is 8s so anything past a minute is definitively leaked). New reason: 'terminal-alive'. This class does NOT require ppid==1 — deliberately different from 'orphaned-keep-alive', because the leak surfaces even with a live parent shell/tmux pane (that was exactly the class the old reaper missed). (2) src/cli/clean.ts:reapStaleSpecialistJobs kills the whole process group (SIGTERM to -pid, wait 500ms, SIGKILL to -pid) for terminal-alive — group kill catches the detached pi child + its MCP servers. Crucially, DO NOT call markSpecialistJobCancelled for terminal-alive; the DB row is correctly terminal, only the process leaked. (3) src/specialist/control.ts:stopJob now checks isProcessAlive(pid, started_at_ms) before returning 'already finalized'; when registry-terminal-but-PID-alive, emits stop_terminal_alive_reaped control event, SIGTERM the group, waits 3s, group-SIGKILL if still alive, kills tmux session, prints 'Reaped orphaned PID <pid> for job <id>'. Tests: process-health.test.ts + stop.test.ts. StatusFixture helper (Partial<SupervisorStatus>) in process-health.test.ts fixes long-standing tsc excess-property noise that pre-dated this fix.
